Y ahora que sabe usted que es la hija ilegítima de una bailarina francesa, acaso no le agrade tanto el cargo que ejerce con ella y venga cualquier día a notificarne que ha encontrado usted otro empleo, que me busque otra institutriz, etcétera.

"No: Adele is not answerable for either her mother's faults or yours: I have a regard for her; and now that I know she is, in a sense, parentless--forsaken by her mother and disowned by you, sir--I shall cling closer to her than before.

Adèle no es responsable de las faltas de su madre ni de las de usted. Yo tengo un deber respecto a ella y ahora que sé que es, hasta cierto punto, huérfana -ya que su madre la olvida y usted no la reconoce-, me siento más dispuesta a seguir cumpliéndolo.
How could I possibly prefer the spoilt pet of a wealthy family, who would hate her governess as a nuisance, to a lonely little orphan, who leans towards her as a friend?"
¿Cómo he de preferir ser institutriz en alguna familia donde constituya un enojo más que otra cosa, que ser la amiga de una huerfanita?
"Oh, that is the light in which you view it!
-Si lo ve usted así...
Well, I must go in now; and you too: it darkens."
Vaya, regresemos. Está oscureciendo ya.
But I stayed out a few minutes longer with Adele and Pilot--ran a race with her, and played a game of battledore and shuttlecock.
Yo me entretuve algunos minutos más con la niña y el perro, y corrí y jugué con ellos.

When we went in, and I had removed her bonnet and coat, I took her on my knee; kept her there an hour, allowing her to prattle as she liked: not rebuking even some little freedoms and trivialities into which she was apt to stray when much noticed, and which betrayed in her a superficiality of character, inherited probably from her mother, hardly congenial to an English mind.

Cuando volvimos a casa y la quité el sombrero y el abrigo, la hice sentar en mis rodillas y durante una hora charlé con ella de las cosas que le complacían y que eran, principalmente, frivolidades sin sustancia, probable herencia de su madre y difíciles de concebir para una mentalidad inglesa.
Still she had her merits; and I was disposed to appreciate all that was good in her to the utmost.
Con todo, la niña tenía algunos méritos y yo estaba dispuesta a reconocerlos.
I sought in her countenance and features a likeness to Mr. Rochester, but found none: no trait, no turn of expression announced relationship.
Busqué en sus facciones alguna semejanza con Mr. Rochester, pero no hallé ninguna.
It was a pity: if she could but have been proved to resemble him, he would have thought more of her.
Era lamentable, porque de haber podido probarle cierto parecido, él se hubiera preocupado más de la pequeña.
It was not till after I had withdrawn to my own chamber for the night, that I steadily reviewed the tale Mr. Rochester had told me.
Cuando me retiré a mi habitación, por la noche, pensé en la narración que Mr. Rochester me había hecho.

As he had said, there was probably nothing at all extraordinary in the substance of the narrative itself: a wealthy Englishman's passion for a French dancer, and her treachery to him, were every-day matters enough, no doubt, in society; but there was something decidedly strange in the paroxysm of emotion which had suddenly seized him when he was in the act of expressing the present contentment of his mood, and his newly revived pleasure in the old hall and its environs.

Como él dijera, nada había de extraordinario en tal historia: los amores de un inglés con una bailarina francesa y la traición de ella eran cosa muy corriente. Pero había algo extraño en la emoción que él experimentara cuando se refirió al viejo palacio.
I meditated wonderingly on this incident; but gradually quitting it, as I found it for the present inexplicable, I turned to the consideration of my master's manner to myself.
Gradualmente pasé, de meditar en aquel incidente, a pensar en la confianza que el dueño de la casa me manifestaba.
The confidence he had thought fit to repose in me seemed a tribute to my discretion: I regarded and accepted it as such.
Considerándola como un tributo a mi discreción, la acepté en tal sentido.
His deportment had now for some weeks been more uniform towards me than at the first.
Su comportamiento conmigo durante las últimas semanas era menos desigual que al principio. No mostraba altanería y cuando nos veíamos parecía alegrarse.

I never seemed in his way; he did not take fits of chilling hauteur: when he met me unexpectedly, the encounter seemed welcome; he had always a word and sometimes a smile for me: when summoned by formal invitation to his presence, I was honoured by a cordiality of reception that made me feel I really possessed the power to amuse him, and that these evening conferences were sought as much for his pleasure as for my benefit.

Siempre reservaba para mí una palabra amable y una sonrisa. Cuando me invitaba a reunirme con él, me acogía con una cordialidad que me llevaba a pensar que realmente debía de poseer la facultad de divertirle y que aquellas conversaciones durante las veladas debían de agradarle a él tanto como a mí.
I, indeed, talked comparatively little, but I heard him talk with relish.

Aunque yo solía hablar muy poco, le escuchaba con agrado. Él, por naturaleza, era comunicativo y le gustaba abrir ante mi espíritu ignorante del mundo muchos horizontes sobre sus costumbres y escenas.

It was his nature to be communicative; he liked to open to a mind unacquainted with the world glimpses of its scenes and ways (I do not mean its corrupt scenes and wicked ways, but such as derived their interest from the great scale on which they were acted, the strange novelty by which they were characterised); and I had a keen delight in receiving the new ideas he offered, in imagining the new pictures he portrayed, and following him in thought through the new regions he disclosed, never startled or troubled by one noxious allusion.

No precisamente escenas de corrupción y costumbres viciosas, sino cosas cuyo interés residía en la novedad que para mí presentaban. Yo experimentaba placer escuchando las ideas que él me sugería, imaginando los cuadros que él me pintaba, y siguiéndole con la imaginación a las nuevas regiones que extendía ante mi mente.
The ease of his manner freed me from painful restraint: the friendly frankness, as correct as cordial, with which he treated me, drew me to him.
La espontaneidad de sus maneras me libró de la molestia de sentirme cohibida, y la amistosa franqueza, tan correcta como cordial, con que me trataba, me impresionó.
I felt at times as if he were my relation rather than my master: yet he was imperious sometimes still; but I did not mind that; I saw it was his way.
Al poco tiempo experimentaba la impresión de que Rochester era más bien un amigo que un amo, aunque a veces me tratara con imperio. Pero no me molestaba, porque comprendía que tal era su costumbre.

So happy, so gratified did I become with this new interest added to life, that I ceased to pine after kindred: my thin crescent-destiny seemed to enlarge; the blanks of existence were filled up; my bodily health improved; I gathered flesh and strength.

Sintiéndome más feliz, más interesada en la vida, mejor tratada, me encontraba más a gusto de lo habitual. Los vacíos de mi vida se llenaban y, físicamente, también mejoré: estaba más gruesa y más fuerte.
And was Mr. Rochester now ugly in my eyes?
¿Me parecía feo ahora Mr. Rochester?
No, reader: gratitude, and many associations, all pleasurable and genial, made his face the object I best liked to see; his presence in a room was more cheering than the brightest fire.

No, lector, la gratitud, unida a cuanto veía en él, todo bueno y genial, hacían que su rostro se me figurara lo más agradable del mundo. Su presencia en una habitación parecía alegrar y caldear la atmósfera mejor que el más brillante fuego.
Yet I had not forgotten his faults; indeed, I could not, for he brought them frequently before me.
Ello no significaba que yo olvidase sus defectos, tanto más cuanto que los mostraba con frecuencia.
He was proud, sardonic, harsh to inferiority of every description: in my secret soul I knew that his great kindness to me was balanced by unjust severity to many others.
Era orgulloso y sarcástico y, en mi interior, yo reconocía que su mucha amabilidad hacia mí estaba compensada por su mucha severidad hacia los demás.

He was moody, too; unaccountably so; I more than once, when sent for to read to him, found him sitting in his library alone, with his head bent on his folded arms; and, when he looked up, a morose, almost a malignant, scowl blackened his features.
Estaba generalmente malhumorado. Con frecuencia, cuando me enviaba a buscar, le encontraba en la biblioteca, solo, con la cabeza apoyada sobre sus brazos cruzados.
But I believed that his moodiness, his harshness, and his former faults of morality (I say _former_, for now he seemed corrected of them) had their source in some cruel cross of fate.

Y cuando la levantaba, un gesto melancólico, casi maligno, ensombrecía sus facciones. Pero yo creía que su mal humor, su aspereza y sus anteriores vicios -anteriores, porque ahora parecía haberlos corregido- eran el resultado de alguna injusticia con que el destino le abrumara.
I believed he was naturally a man of better tendencies, higher principles, and purer tastes than such as circumstances had developed, education instilled, or destiny encouraged.
Yo entendía que, por naturaleza, Rochester era un hombre de buenas inclinaciones, elevados principios y delicados gestos, que las circunstancias, la educación y el destino habían desviado.

I thought there were excellent materials in him; though for the present they hung together somewhat spoiled and tangled. I cannot deny that I grieved for his grief, whatever that was, and would have given much to assuage it.
Su pena, cualquiera que fuese, me apenaba a mí y hubiera dado cualquier cosa por poder mitigarla.

Though I had now extinguished my candle and was laid down in bed, I could not sleep for thinking of his look when he paused in the avenue, and told how his destiny had risen up before him, and dared him to be happy at Thornfield.
Aquella noche, en mi lecho, con la luz ya apagada, no conseguía dormir pensando en la mirada que Rochester dirigiera a la casa, y me preguntaba si él no podría llegar a ser feliz en Thornfield.
"Why not?" I asked myself.
«¿Por qué no? -me preguntaba-.
"What alienates him from the house?
¿Qué le separa de este lugar?
Will he leave it again soon?
¿Por qué lo abandona siempre tan pronto?
Mrs. Fairfax said he seldom stayed here longer than a fortnight at a time; and he has now been resident eight weeks.
Fairfax dice que nunca pasa aquí más de quince días y ahora lleva, sin embargo, ocho semanas. Sería lamentable que se marchase.
If he does go, the change will be doleful. Suppose he should be absent spring, summer, and autumn: how joyless sunshine and fine days will seem!"
¡Qué tristes días, a pesar del sol radiante y el cielo despejado, me esperan en la primavera, en el verano y el otoño venideros, si él no está!»
I hardly know whether I had slept or not after this musing; at any rate, I started wide awake on hearing a vague murmur, peculiar and lugubrious, which sounded, I thought, just above me.
Después de este pensamiento, no sé si me dormí o no. Lo cierto es que desperté oyendo un vago murmullo, extraño y lúgubre, que me pareció sonar precisamente encima de mí.
I wished I had kept my candle burning: the night was drearily dark; my spirits were depressed.
Hubiese querido tener encendida la vela, porque la noche era terriblemente oscura. Me sentí deprimida y asustada.
I rose and sat up in bed, listening.
Me senté en el lecho y escuché.
The sound was hushed.
El murmullo se había apagado.
I tried again to sleep; but my heart beat anxiously: my inward tranquillity was broken.
Traté otra vez de dormirme, pero mi corazón latía tumultuosamente y mi serenidad había desaparecido.
The clock, far down in the hall, struck two.
El lejano reloj del vestíbulo dio las dos.
Just then it seemed my chamber-door was touched; as if fingers had swept the panels in groping a way along the dark gallery outside.
Creí percibir que unos dedos arañaban la puerta de mi dormitorio, como si buscasen a tientas una salida en la galería.
I said, "Who is there?"
Exclamé: -¿Quién es?
Nothing answered.
Nadie contestó.
I was chilled with fear.
Sentí un escalofrío de temor.

All at once I remembered that it might be Pilot, who, when the kitchen- door chanced to be left open, not unfrequently found his way up to the threshold of Mr. Rochester's chamber: I had seen him lying there myself in the mornings.
Recordé de pronto que, a veces, Piloto, cuando la puerta de la cocina quedaba abierta, salía y buscaba en la oscuridad el cuarto de su amor, en cuyo umbral le había visto durmiendo algunas mañanas.
The idea calmed me somewhat: I lay down.
Tal pensamiento me tranquilizó.
Silence composes the nerves; and as an unbroken hush now reigned again through the whole house, I began to feel the return of slumber. But it was not fated that I should sleep that night.
Me tendí en el lecho y ya comenzaba a dormirme otra vez cuando un nuevo incidente vino a desvelarme.
This was a demoniac laugh--low, suppressed, and deep--uttered, as it seemed, at the very keyhole of my chamber door.
Esta vez era una risa casi demoníaca: baja, reprimida y que sonaba, según me pareció, a través del agujero de la cerradura de mi puerta.

The head of my bed was near the door, and I thought at first the goblin-laugher stood at my bedside--or rather, crouched by my pillow: but I rose, looked round, and could see nothing; while, as I still gazed, the unnatural sound was reiterated: and I knew it came from behind the panels.
La cabecera de mi cama estaba próxima a la puerta. Al principio pensé que algún duendecillo burlón estaba al lado de mi lecho, o quizá en mi misma almohada.
My first impulse was to rise and fasten the bolt; my next, again to cry out,
Mi primer impulso fue echar el cerrojo. El segundo preguntar otra vez:
"Who is there?"
-¿Quién es?
Something gurgled and moaned.
Sentí una especie de gruñido.
Ere long, steps retreated up the gallery towards the third-storey staircase: a door had lately been made to shut in that staircase; I heard it open and close, and all was still.
Luego oí pasos en la escalera del tercer piso y el abrir y cerrar de una puerta que recientemente se había colocado al final de aquella escalera.
"Was that Grace Poole? and is she possessed with a devil?" thought I. Impossible now to remain longer by myself: I must go to Mrs. Fairfax.
«¿Será Grace Poole y estará poseída del diablo?», pensé. Imposible seguir más tiempo sola.
I hurried on my frock and a shawl; I withdrew the bolt and opened the door with a trembling hand.
Me puse un vestido y un chal y con temblorosa mano abrí la puerta.
There was a candle burning just outside, and on the matting in the gallery.
En la estera de la galería alguien había dejado una bujía encendida.

I was surprised at this circumstance: but still more was I amazed to perceive the air quite dim, as if filled with smoke; and, while looking to the right hand and left, to find whence these blue wreaths issued, I became further aware of a strong smell of burning.

Me sorprendió aquella circunstancia, y mi extrañeza creció cuando noté que había un humo sofocante. Mientras miraba a derecha e izquierda buscando el origen de aquella humareda, percibí también un fuerte olor a quemado.
Something creaked: it was a door ajar; and that door was Mr. Rochester's, and the smoke rushed in a cloud from thence.
De la puerta entornada del cuarto de Mr. Rochester salían espesas nubes de humo.
I thought no more of Mrs. Fairfax; I thought no more of Grace Poole, or the laugh: in an instant, I was within the chamber.
Ya no pensé más en el ama de llaves, ni en Grace Poole, ni en las extrañas risas.
Tongues of flame darted round the bed: the curtains were on fire.
En un instante me hallé dentro de la alcoba.
In the midst of blaze and vapour, Mr. Rochester lay stretched motionless, in deep sleep.
El lecho estaba envuelto en llamas, sus cortinas ardían y bajo ellas, profundamente dormido e inmóvil, reposaba Mr. Rochester.
"Wake! wake!"
-¡Despierte! -grité.
I cried. I shook him, but he only murmured and turned: the smoke had stupefied him.
Apenas se volvió y sólo murmuró algo ininteligible. El humo le había hecho desvanecerse.
Not a moment could be lost: the very sheets were kindling, I rushed to his basin and ewer; fortunately, one was wide and the other deep, and both were filled with water.
No se podía perder ni un segundo. Corrí hacia el lavabo: el jarro y la palangana estaban llenos de agua.

I heaved them up, deluged the bed and its occupant, flew back to my own room, brought my own water-jug, baptized the couch afresh, and, by God's aid, succeeded in extinguishing the flames which were devouring it.
Los vacié sobre el lecho y sobre su ocupante, corrí a mi alcoba, cogí mi jarro y mi jofaina, los vertí sobre el lecho y, con la ayuda de Dios, logré extinguir las llamas que lo devoraban.

The hiss of the quenched element, the breakage of a pitcher which I flung from my hand when I had emptied it, and, above all, the splash of the shower-bath I had liberally bestowed, roused Mr. Rochester at last.
El baño con que había obsequiado pródigamente a Mr. Rochester le hizo volver en sí.
Though it was now dark, I knew he was awake; because I heard him fulminating strange anathemas at finding himself lying in a pool of water.
Aunque, al apagarse el fuego la habitación estaba a oscuras, comprendí que se había despertado al oírle fulminar extraordinarias maldiciones contra quien le hiciera nadar en agua.
"Is there a flood?" he cried.
-¿Qué es esto, una inundación? -rugió.
"No, sir," I answered; "but there has been a fire: get up, do; you are quenched now; I will fetch you a candle."
-No, señor -repuse-, había estallado un incendio. Espere: voy a traer una vela.
"In the name of all the elves in Christendom, is that Jane Eyre?" he demanded.
-¡Por todos los diablos del infierno, que esa es Jane Eyre!
"What have you done with me, witch, sorceress?
¿Qué ha hecho usted conmigo, bruja?
Who is in the room besides you?
¿Quién está con usted en la habitación?
Have you plotted to drown me?"
¿Se proponían ahogarme?
"I will fetch you a candle, sir; and, in Heaven's name, get up.
-Voy por una luz, señor -insistí-.
Somebody has plotted something: you cannot too soon find out who and what it is."
No sé lo que ha pasado.
"There! I am up now; but at your peril you fetch a candle yet: wait two minutes till I get into some dry garments, if any dry there be--yes, here is my dressing-gown.
-Espere un minuto, a ver si encuentro alguna ropa seca si es que queda. ¡Sí!
Now run!"
Ya puede usted traer la vela.
I did run; I brought the candle which still remained in the gallery.
Cogí la luz que estaba en el suelo de la galería.
He took it from my hand, held it up, and surveyed the bed, all blackened and scorched, the sheets drenched, the carpet round swimming in water.
Él la tomó de mis manos, examinó el lecho quemado, las sábanas empapadas, la alfombra llena de agua.
"What is it? and who did it?" he asked.
-¿Qué ha ocurrido? -preguntó.

I briefly related to him what had transpired: the strange laugh I had heard in the gallery: the step ascending to the third storey; the smoke,--the smell of fire which had conducted me to his room; in what state I had found matters there, and how I had deluged him with all the water I could lay hands on.

Le relaté brevemente lo que sabía: la extraña risa en la galería, los pasos en la escalera del tercer piso, el olor a quemado que me condujo hasta su cuarto, el estado en que le había encontrado y cómo le anegara con cuanta agua pude hallar a mano.
He listened very gravely; his face, as I went on, expressed more concern than astonishment; he did not immediately speak when I had concluded.
Me atendió con más interés que sorpresa y cuando concluí permaneció callado.
"Shall I call Mrs. Fairfax?"
-¿Llamo a Mrs.
I asked.
Fairfax? -pregunté.
"Mrs. Fairfax? No; what the deuce would you call her for?
-¿Para qué diablo va usted a llamarla?
What can she do? Let her sleep unmolested."
No la moleste.
"Then I will fetch Leah, and wake John and his wife."
-¿Voy a buscar a Leah, o a John y a su mujer?
"Not at all: just be still. You have a shawl on.
-No hace falta. Siéntese en esa butaca y póngase mi abrigo si tiene frío con ese chal que lleva.
If you are not warm enough, you may take my cloak yonder; wrap it about you, and sit down in the arm-chair: there,--I will put it on.
Ahora coloque los pies en este taburete para no mojárselos.
Now place your feet on the stool, to keep them out of the wet. I am going to leave you a few minutes.
Me voy; vuelvo dentro de unos minutos.
I shall take the candle.
Me llevaré la luz.
Remain where you are till I return; be as still as a mouse.
Estese aquí, quietecita como una muerta, hasta que yo vuelva.
I must pay a visit to the second storey.
Tengo que hacer una visita al piso de arriba.
Don't move, remember, or call any one."
No se mueva ni llame a nadie.
He went: I watched the light withdraw.
Salió.
He passed up the gallery very softly, unclosed the staircase door with as little noise as possible, shut it after him, and the last ray vanished.
Se deslizó por la galería sin hacer ruido, abrió con sigilo la puerta de la escalera, la cerró tras sí y la luz que llevaba se desvaneció.
I was left in total darkness.
Quedé en absoluta oscuridad.
I listened for some noise, but heard nothing.
Puse oído atento, pero no percibí rumor alguno.
A very long time elapsed.
Pasó mucho tiempo.
I grew weary: it was cold, in spite of the cloak; and then I did not see the use of staying, as I was not to rouse the house.
Yo sentía frío a pesar del abrigo, y ya estaba a punto de desobedecer las órdenes de Mr.
I was on the point of risking Mr. Rochester's displeasure by disobeying his orders, when the light once more gleamed dimly on the gallery wall, and I heard his unshod feet tread the matting.
Rochester e irme, a riesgo de incurrir en su desagrado, cuando vi reaparecer la luz proyectándose en los muros de la galería y sentí pasos sobre la estera.
"I hope it is he," thought I, "and not something worse."
«Confiemos en que sea él y no algo peor», pensé.
He re-entered, pale and very gloomy.
Rochester entró, pálido y sombrío.
"I have found it all out," said he, setting his candle down on the washstand; "it is as I thought."
Puso la luz sobre el lavabo. -Ya sé de lo que se trata -murmuró-. Es lo que yo me había figurado.
"How, sir?"
-¿Qué era, señor?
He made no reply, but stood with his arms folded, looking on the ground.
No contestó. Permaneció con los brazos cruzados, mirando al suelo.
At the end of a few minutes he inquired in rather a peculiar tone--
Al cabo de algunos instantes me dijo:
"I forget whether you said you saw anything when you opened your chamber door."
-¿Vio usted algo de particular cuando abrió la puerta de su cuarto?
"No, sir, only the candlestick on the ground."
-No, señor. Sólo la bujía en el suelo.
"But you heard an odd laugh?
-¿Pero no oyó usted una risa rara?
You have heard that laugh before, I should think, or something like it?"
¿No la había oído antes de ahora?
"Yes, sir: there is a woman who sews here, called Grace Poole,--she laughs in that way. She is a singular person."
-Sí, señor, y quien se ríe así es Grace Poole, una mujer muy extraña.
"Just so. Grace Poole--you have guessed it. She is, as you say, singular--very.
-Exacto, Grace Poole es, como usted dice, muy extraña.
Well, I shall reflect on the subject.
Pensaré en el asunto.
Meantime, I am glad that you are the only person, besides myself, acquainted with the precise details of to-night's incident.
Me alegro mucho de que sólo usted y yo sepamos los detalles de este incidente.
You are no talking fool: say nothing about it.
No diga nada de ello a nadie.
I will account for this state of affairs" (pointing to the bed): "and now return to your own room.
Yo explicaré esto -añadió señalando el lecho quemado-. Ahora vuélvase a su cuarto.
I shall do very well on the sofa in the library for the rest of the night.
Yo puedo pasar muy bien la noche en el sofá de la biblioteca.
It is near four:--in two hours the servants will be up."
Son casi las cuatro y de aquí a dos horas los criados se levantarán.
"Good-night, then, sir," said I, departing.
-Entonces, buenas noches, señor-dije, saliendo.
He seemed surprised--very inconsistently so, as he had just told me to go.
Pareció sorprenderse, cosa asombrosa, porque él mismo me había dicho que me fuera.
"What!" he exclaimed, "are you quitting me already, and in that way?"
-¿Me deja usted de este modo? -exclamó.
"You said I might go, sir."
-Usted me lo ha mandado, señor.
"But not without taking leave; not without a word or two of acknowledgment and good-will: not, in short, in that brief, dry fashion.
-Pero no así; no sin una palabra de agradecimiento hacia usted, que me ha salvado de una muerte horrible...
Why, you have saved my life!--snatched me from a horrible and excruciating death! and you walk past me as if we were mutual strangers! At least shake hands."
Al menos, permítame estrecharle la mano.
He held out his hand; I gave him mine: he took it first in one, them in both his own.
Le tendí la mano y él la estrechó primero con una de las suyas y luego con ambas.
"You have saved my life: I have a pleasure in owing you so immense a debt.
-Me ha salvado usted la vida y me satisface tener con usted una deuda tan grande.
I cannot say more.
No puedo decir más.
Nothing else that has being would have been tolerable to me in the character of creditor for such an obligation: but you: it is different;--I feel your benefits no burden, Jane."
Con cualquier otra persona, semejante deuda representaría para mí una carga intolerable, pero con usted es distinto, Jane. Sus beneficios no se hacen abrumadores.
He paused; gazed at me: words almost visible trembled on his lips,--but his voice was checked.
Calló y me miró. Se notaba que sus labios querían proferir alguna palabra más, pero se contuvo.
"Good-night again, sir.
-Buenas noches, señor.
There is no debt, benefit, burden, obligation, in the case."
Y conste que no hay caso de deuda, beneficio, obligación ni peso alguno.

"I knew," he continued, "you would do me good in some way, at some time;--I saw it in your eyes when I first beheld you: their expression and smile did not"--(again he stopped)--"did not" (he proceeded hastily) "strike delight to my very inmost heart so for nothing.
-Experimento la sensación -continuó él- de que usted ejerce algún buen influjo sobre mí. Lo adiviné cuando la vi por vez primera...
People talk of natural sympathies; I have heard of good genii: there are grains of truth in the wildest fable.
La gente dice que hay simpatías espontáneas; también he oído hablar de buenos genios... En esa leyenda hay algunos puntos de verdad.
My cherished preserver, goodnight!"
Querida bienhechora mía: buenas noches.
Strange energy was in his voice, strange fire in his look.
En su voz vibraba una inusitada energía y en sus ojos ardía un insólito fuego.
"I am glad I happened to be awake," I said: and then I was going.
-Me alegro de haber estado despierta, señor -dije. Y traté de irme.
"What! you _will_ go?"
-¿Ya se va?
"I am cold, sir."
-Tengo frío, señor. -¿Frío?
"Cold? Yes,--and standing in a pool!
¡Claro: estamos en un charco!
Go, then, Jane; go!"
Bueno, váyase.. .
But he still retained my hand, and I could not free it.
Pero no soltaba mi mano.
I bethought myself of an expedient. "I think I hear Mrs. Fairfax move, sir," said I.
Tuve que imaginar un pretexto. -Me parece haber sentido moverse a Mrs. Fairfax -dije.
"Well, leave me:" he relaxed his fingers, and I was gone.
-Bien; váyase. Aflojó sus dedos y me dejó marchar.
I regained my couch, but never thought of sleep.
Volví a mi alcoba, pero no pude dormir.
Till morning dawned I was tossed on a buoyant but unquiet sea, where billows of trouble rolled under surges of joy.
Mi imaginación flotó hasta la mañana en un mar alegre, pero turbulento, en el que olas de turbación sucedían a otras de grato optimismo.

I thought sometimes I saw beyond its wild waters a shore, sweet as the hills of Beulah; and now and then a freshening gale, wakened by hope, bore my spirit triumphantly towards the bourne: but I could not reach it, even in fancy--a counteracting breeze blew off land, and continually drove me back.

A trechos, más allá de las hirvientes aguas, parecíame divisar una plácida orilla, hacia la que de vez en cuando me impulsaba una fresca brisa. Pero otro viento que soplaba desde tierra me hacía retroceder.
Sense would resist delirium: judgment would warn passion.
La sensatez trataba de oponerse al delirio, el criterio a la pasión.
Too feverish to rest, I rose as soon as day dawned.
Incapaz de seguir acostada, me levanté en cuanto alboreó el día.
I both wished and feared to see Mr. Rochester on the day which followed this sleepless night: I wanted to hear his voice again, yet feared to meet his eye.
Rochester. Ansiaba oír su voz de nuevo y me asustaba, sin embargo, presentarme ante él.

During the early part of the morning, I momentarily expected his coming; he was not in the frequent habit of entering the schoolroom, but he did step in for a few minutes sometimes, and I had the impression that he was sure to visit it that day.
Rochester, algunas veces, aunque pocas, solía entrar en el cuarto de estudio y permanecer en él, y yo estaba segura de que aquella mañana se presentaría.

But the morning passed just as usual: nothing happened to interrupt the quiet course of Adele's studies; only soon after breakfast, I heard some bustle in the neighbourhood of Mr. Rochester's chamber, Mrs. Fairfax's voice, and Leah's, and the cook's--that is, John's wife--and even John's own gruff tones.

Pero la mañana transcurrió sin que nada interrumpiese los estudios de Adèle. Únicamente oí, antes de desayunar, algunas voces cerca del cuarto de Rochester: las del ama de llaves, de Leah, de la cocinera -que era la mujer de John- y el áspero acento del propio John.
There were exclamations of "What a mercy master was not burnt in his bed!" "It is always dangerous to keep a candle lit at night."
Se percibían exclamaciones tales como: «¡Por poco se abrasa el señor en su cama!»
"How providential that he had presence of mind to think of the water-jug!"
«Es peligroso dejar la luz encendida por la noche.»
"I wonder he waked nobody!" "It is to be hoped he will not take cold with sleeping on the library sofa," &c.
«¿No se habrá enfriado durmiendo en el sofá?», etcétera.

To much confabulation succeeded a sound of scrubbing and setting to rights; and when I passed the room, in going downstairs to dinner, I saw through the open door that all was again restored to complete order; only the bed was stripped of its hangings.

A aquella conversación siguió algún movimiento en el cuarto y cuando pasé ante él para ir a comer, vi a través de la puerta abierta que todo había sido puesto en orden. Unicamente la cama carecía aún de cortinas.
Leah stood up in the window-seat, rubbing the panes of glass dimmed with smoke.
Leah estaba limpiando los cristales, empañados por el humo.

I was about to address her, for I wished to know what account had been given of the affair: but, on advancing, I saw a second person in the chamber--a woman sitting on a chair by the bedside, and sewing rings to new curtains. That woman was no other than Grace Poole.
Iba a hablarla para saber qué explicación se había dado del caso, cuando divisé, sentada en una silla y colocando las anillas de las nuevas cortinas del lecho, a Grace Poole.
There she sat, staid and taciturn-looking, as usual, in her brown stuff gown, her check apron, white handkerchief, and cap.
Permanecía taciturna como de costumbre, con su vestido oscuro, su delantal ceñido y su cofia.

She was intent on her work, in which her whole thoughts seemed absorbed: on her hard forehead, and in her commonplace features, was nothing either of the paleness or desperation one would have expected to see marking the countenance of a woman who had attempted murder, and whose intended victim had followed her last night to her lair, and (as I believed), charged her with the crime she wished to perpetrate.

Estaba absorta en su trabajo, al que parecía dedicar todas las energías de su mente. En sus vulgares rasgos no se percibía la palidez ni la desesperación que debían esperarse en una mujer que hacía poco intentara cometer un asesinato y cuya víctima debía, según mis suposiciones, haberle reprochado el crimen que tratara de perpetrar.
I was amazed--confounded.
Quedé perpleja.
She looked up, while I still gazed at her: no start, no increase or failure of colour betrayed emotion, consciousness of guilt, or fear of detection.
Ella me miró sin que su expresión se alterase y me dijo:
She said "Good morning, Miss," in her usual phlegmatic and brief manner; and taking up another ring and more tape, went on with her sewing.
«Buenos días, señorita», con tanta calma y flema como de costumbre. Luego continuó su labor.
"I will put her to some test," thought I: "such absolute impenetrability is past comprehension."
«Es preciso poner a prueba esa indiferencia», pensé.
"Good morning, Grace," I said.
-Buenos días, Grace -repuse en voz alta-.
"Has anything happened here?
¿Ha ocurrido algo?
I thought I heard the servants all talking together a while ago."
Me ha parecido oír hablar aquí hace un rato...

"Only master had been reading in his bed last night; he fell asleep with his candle lit, and the curtains got on fire; but, fortunately, he awoke before the bed-clothes or the wood-work caught, and contrived to quench the flames with the water in the ewer."
-El señor estuvo leyendo esta noche en la cama, se durmió con la luz encendida y las cortinas se incendiaron. Afortunadamente despertó a tiempo de apagar el fuego con el agua del jarro.
"A strange affair!" I said, in a low voice: then, looking at her fixedly
-¡Qué raro! -dije, en voz baja, mirándola fijamente-.
--"Did Mr. Rochester wake nobody?
¿No despertó Mr. Rochester a nadie?
Did no one hear him move?"
¿Ninguno le oyó moverse?
She again raised her eyes to me, and this time there was something of consciousness in their expression.
Me contempló de nuevo y ahora su expresión reflejaba un sentimiento distinto.
She seemed to examine me warily; then she answered--
Después de haberme examinado con recelo, contestó:
"The servants sleep so far off, you know, Miss, they would not be likely to hear.
-Ya sabe usted, señorita, que los criados duermen lejos.
Mrs. Fairfax's room and yours are the nearest to master's; but Mrs. Fairfax said she heard nothing: when people get elderly, they often sleep heavy."
Ella no ha oído nada. Las personas de cierta edad duermen muy pesadamente.

She paused, and then added, with a sort of assumed indifference, but still in a marked and significant tone--"But you are young, Miss; and I should say a light sleeper: perhaps you may have heard a noise?"
Se interrumpió, y luego agregó con afectada indiferencia, pero con significativo acento: -Usted es joven, señorita, y debe tener el sueño ligero. ¿No oyó nada?

"I did," said I, dropping my voice, so that Leah, who was still polishing the panes, could not hear me, "and at first I thought it was Pilot: but Pilot cannot laugh; and I am certain I heard a laugh, and a strange one."
-Sí -dije en voz baja, para que Leah no me oyese al principio creí que era Piloto. Pero es imposible que un perro ría, y estoy segura de haber oído una risa muy extraña.
She took a new needleful of thread, waxed it carefully, threaded her needle with a steady hand, and then observed, with perfect composure--
Ella reanudó su labor con perfecta calma y me dijo:
"It is hardly likely master would laugh, I should think, Miss, when he was in such danger: You must have been dreaming."
-Debía usted de estar soñando, señorita, porque es muy raro que el amo, en un caso así, se riera.
"I was not dreaming," I said, with some warmth, for her brazen coolness provoked me.
-No soñaba -repuse acaloradamente-. Su fingida frialdad me ofendía.
"You did not think of opening your door and looking out into the gallery?" she further asked.
-¿Cómo no abrió usted la puerta y miró? -repuso sin perder la calma-. Y ¿cómo no ha hablado al amo de esa risa extraña?
She appeared to be cross-questioning me, attempting to draw from me information unawares.
-No he tenido ocasión de verle esta mañana.
The idea struck me that if she discovered I knew or suspected her guilt, she would be playing of some of her malignant pranks on me; I thought it advisable to be on my guard.
Me pareció que tenía interés en interrogarme. Y como, si notaba que yo desconfiaba de ella, podía volver contra mí sus malignos propósitos, me pareció conveniente precaverme.
"Then you are not in the habit of bolting your door every night before you get into bed?"
-¿Así -continuó ella- que no tiene usted la costumbre de cerrar la puerta con cerrojo cuando se acuesta?
"Fiend! she wants to know my habits, that she may lay her plans accordingly!"
«¡La muy bruja quiere conocer mis costumbres para fraguar sus planes!», pensé. Y la indignación, superando mi prudencia, me hizo contestar:
Indignation again prevailed over prudence: I replied sharply, "Hitherto I have often omitted to fasten the bolt: I did not think it necessary.
-Con frecuencia he omitido esa precaución, por no creerla necesaria.

I was not aware any danger or annoyance was to be dreaded at Thornfield Hall: but in future" (and I laid marked stress on the words) "I shall take good care to make all secure before I venture to lie down."
No pensaba que en Thornfield Hall hubiera peligro de muerte violenta. Pero de aquí en adelante -y recalqué las palabras- tomaré mis precauciones antes de acostarme.

"It will be wise so to do," was her answer: "this neighbourhood is as quiet as any I know, and I never heard of the hall being attempted by robbers since it was a house; though there are hundreds of pounds' worth of plate in the plate-closet, as is well known.
-Será conveniente que lo haga -respondió Grace, aunque esta región es muy pacífica y yo no he oído nunca hablar de intentos de robo en esta casa.

And you see, for such a large house, there are very few servants, because master has never lived here much; and when he does come, being a bachelor, he needs little waiting on: but I always think it best to err on the safe side; a door is soon fastened, and it is as well to have a drawn bolt between one and any mischief that may be about.

Y eso que se sabe que aquí hay vajilla de plata por valor de varios cientos de libras y que, como el amo es soltero y está muy poco aquí, hay menos criados de los que corresponde a un edificio de esta importancia. De todos modos, me parece que la prudencia no sobra y que siempre es mejor tener echado el cerrojo de la puerta entre uno y cualquier peligro que pueda sobrevenir.
A deal of people, Miss, are for trusting all to Providence; but I say Providence will not dispense with the means, though He often blesses them when they are used discreetly."
Mucha gente confía en Dios, pero yo digo que debe uno ayudarse para que Dios le ayude.
And here she closed her harangue: a long one for her, and uttered with the demureness of a Quakeress.
Así concluyó su párrafo, muy largo para lo que ella acostumbraba, y pronunciado con el gazmoño acento de una cuáquera.
I still stood absolutely dumfoundered at what appeared to me her miraculous self-possession and most inscrutable hypocrisy, when the cook entered.
Quedé estupefacta ante lo que me parecía un increíble dominio de sí misma y una hipocresía refinada.
"Mrs. Poole," said she, addressing Grace, "the servants' dinner will soon be ready: will you come down?"
La cocinera entró en aquel momento. -Grace -dijo-: ¿baja usted a comer?
"No; just put my pint of porter and bit of pudding on a tray, and I'll carry it upstairs."
-No -repuso ella-; póngame mi jarro de cerveza y un trozo de pudding en una bandeja y me lo llevaré arriba.
"You'll have some meat?"
-¿No quiere carne?
"Just a morsel, and a taste of cheese, that's all."
-Un poco. Y también un trozo de queso.
"And the sago?" "Never mind it at present: I shall be coming down before teatime: I'll make it myself."
La cocinera se dirigió a mí para decirme que Mrs. Fairfax me esperaba, y salió.
The cook here turned to me, saying that Mrs. Fairfax was waiting for me: so I departed.
Apenas presté atención al relato que me hizo del incendio, mientras comíamos, el ama de llaves.

I hardly heard Mrs. Fairfax's account of the curtain conflagration during dinner, so much was I occupied in puzzling my brains over the enigmatical character of Grace Poole, and still more in pondering the problem of her position at Thornfield and questioning why she had not been given into custody that morning, or, at the very least, dismissed from her master's service.
No pensaba sino en el enigma del carácter y la posición de Grace Poole en la casa, ya que era raro que no la hubieran entregado a las autoridades o, al menos, la hubiesen despedido.
He had almost as much as declared his conviction of her criminality last night: what mysterious cause withheld him from accusing her?
Mr. Rochester me había declarado casi abiertamente que ella era la culpable: ¿Cómo, pues, no la acusaba?
Why had he enjoined me, too, to secrecy?
¿Por qué me había recomendado el secreto?

It was strange: a bold, vindictive, and haughty gentleman seemed somehow in the power of one of the meanest of his dependants; so much in her power, that even when she lifted her hand against his life, he dared not openly charge her with the attempt, much less punish her for it.

Era extraño que un propietario, hombre de mal carácter y bastante rencoroso, estuviese en cierto modo a merced de la más insignificante de sus sirvientas, hasta el punto de que pudiera atentar contra su vida sin que la castigase ni la culpase siquiera.

Had Grace been young and handsome, I should have been tempted to think that tenderer feelings than prudence or fear influenced Mr. Rochester in her behalf; but, hard-favoured and matronly as she was, the idea could not be admitted.

Si Grace hubiese sido joven y hermosa, yo me habría inclinado a pensar que algún dulce sentimiento influía en Rochester más que la prudencia y el temor, pero con una mujer de su edad y aspecto no cabía tal idea.
"Yet," I reflected, "she has been young once; her youth would be contemporary with her master's: Mrs. Fairfax told me once, she had lived here many years.
«Sin embargo -reflexioné-, por su edad ella debe ser contemporánea de su señor, y tal vez en su juventud... Mrs.
I don't think she can ever have been pretty; but, for aught I know, she may possess originality and strength of character to compensate for the want of personal advantages.
Fairfax me ha dicho que lleva aquí muchos años. No creo que haya sido bonita nunca, pero podría compensar con su carácter y otras cualidades sus defectos físicos.
Mr. Rochester is an amateur of the decided and eccentric: Grace is eccentric at least.
Mr. Rochester ama lo excéntrico, y Grace lo es.

What if a former caprice (a freak very possible to a nature so sudden and headstrong as his) has delivered him into her power, and she now exercises over his actions a secret influence, the result of his own indiscretion, which he cannot shake off, and dare not disregard?"
¿Quién sabe si algún antiguo capricho, muy posible en un carácter tan impetuoso y terco como el de Rochester, le tiene a merced de ella y hace que esa mujer influya en su vida?»

But, having reached this point of conjecture, Mrs. Poole's square, flat figure, and uncomely, dry, even coarse face, recurred so distinctly to my mind's eye, that I thought, "No; impossible! my supposition cannot be correct.
Pero en este punto de mis conjeturas, la maciza figura de la Poole acudió a mi mente con tal viveza que no pude por menos de pensar: «Es imposible. Mi suposición no tiene base.»

Yet," suggested the secret voice which talks to us in our own hearts, "you are not beautiful either, and perhaps Mr. Rochester approves you: at any rate, you have often felt as if he did; and last night--remember his words; remember his look; remember his voice!"
Mas esa secreta voz que a veces suena en el fondo de nuestras almas, me sugería: «Sin embargo, tú no eres hermosa tampoco y parece que no desagradas a Mr. Rochester.
I well remembered all; language, glance, and tone seemed at the moment vividly renewed.
Yo lo recordaba todo muy bien.
I was now in the schoolroom; Adele was drawing; I bent over her and directed her pencil.
En aquel momento estábamos en el cuarto de estudio. Adèle dibujaba.
She looked up with a sort of start. "Qu' avez-vous, mademoiselle?" said she.
Me miró con sobresalto. -¿Qué tiene usted, señorita? -dijo-.
"Vos doigts tremblent comme la feuille, et vos joues sont rouges: mais, rouges comme des cerises!"
Sus dedos tiemblan y sus mejillas están encarnadas como las cerezas...
"I am hot, Adele, with stooping!"
-Es que al inclinarme estoy en una posición incómoda, Adèle.
She went on sketching; I went on thinking.
Ella continuó dibujando y yo me sumí otra vez en mis pensamientos.
I hastened to drive from my mind the hateful notion I had been conceiving respecting Grace Poole; it disgusted me.
Me apresuré a eliminar de mi mente la desagradable idea que había formado a propósito de Grace Poole.
I compared myself with her, and found we were different.
Comparándome con ella, concluí que éramos muy diferentes.
Bessie Leaven had said I was quite a lady; and she spoke truth--I was a lady.
Bessie Leaven decía que yo era una señora, y tenía razón: lo era.
And now I looked much better than I did when Bessie saw me; I had more colour and more flesh, more life, more vivacity, because I had brighter hopes and keener enjoyments.
Y ahora yo estaba mucho mejor que cuando me viera Bessie: más gruesa, con mejor color, más viva, más animada, porque tenía más esperanzas y más satisfacciones.
"Evening approaches," said I, as I looked towards the window.
«Ya está oscureciendo -medité, acercándome a la ventana-, y en todo el día no he visto ni oído a Mr. Rochester.

"I have never heard Mr. Rochester's voice or step in the house to-day; but surely I shall see him before night: I feared the meeting in the morning; now I desire it, because expectation has been so long baffled that it is grown impatient."
Seguramente le veré antes de la noche. Por la mañana lo temía, pero ahora estoy impaciente por reunirme con él.»
When dusk actually closed, and when Adele left me to go and play in the nursery with Sophie, I did most keenly desire it.
Mi impaciencia se acrecentó cuando se hizo noche cerrada y Adèle se marchó a jugar con Sophie.

I listened for the bell to ring below; I listened for Leah coming up with a message; I fancied sometimes I heard Mr. Rochester's own tread, and I turned to the door, expecting it to open and admit him.
Yo esperaba oír sonar la campanilla, esperaba que Leah me avisase para que bajara, hasta esperaba que el propio Mr. Rochester llamase a mi puerta...
The door remained shut; darkness only came in through the window.
Pero la puerta seguía cerrada y nadie entraba, sino la oscuridad de la noche a través de la ventana.
Still it was not late; he often sent for me at seven and eight o'clock, and it was yet but six.
Aún no era muy tarde: sólo las seis, y él a veces no enviaba por mí hasta las siete o las ocho.
Surely I should not be wholly disappointed to-night, when I had so many things to say to him!
¡Era imposible que no me mandara a llamar una noche en que tenía tanto de que hablarle!

I wanted again to introduce the subject of Grace Poole, and to hear what he would answer; I wanted to ask him plainly if he really believed it was she who had made last night's hideous attempt; and if so, why he kept her wickedness a secret.

Era preciso preguntarle sobre Grace para ver lo que respondía; era preciso preguntarle francamente si creía que era la culpable del odioso atentado de la noche anterior y, en tal caso, por qué deseaba guardar el secreto.
A tread creaked on the stairs at last. Leah made her appearance; but it was only to intimate that tea was ready in Mrs. Fairfax's room.
Al fin se sintió un paso en las escaleras y Leah se presentó, pero sólo para anunciarme que el té estaba servido en el gabinete de Mrs. Fairfax.
Thither I repaired, glad at least to go downstairs; for that brought me, I imagined, nearer to Mr. Rochester's presence.
De todos modos, me alegré de bajar, pensando que ello me acercaba a la presencia de Mr. Rochester.
"You must want your tea," said the good lady, as I joined her; "you ate so little at dinner.
-Vaya, tome su té -dijo la buena señora cuando me vio-. Hoy ha comido usted muy poco.
I am afraid," she continued, "you are not well to- day: you look flushed and feverish."
Temo que no se encuentre usted bien. Parece un poco agitada.
"Oh, quite well! I never felt better."
-¡Oh, nunca me he sentido mejor! -Demuéstremelo con su buen apetito.
"Then you must prove it by evincing a good appetite; will you fill the teapot while I knit off this needle?"
¿Quiere servir el té mientras yo arreglo la labor?
Having completed her task, she rose to draw down the blind, which she had hitherto kept up, by way, I suppose, of making the most of daylight, though dusk was now fast deepening into total obscurity.
Cuando lo hubo hecho, corrió las cortinillas de la ventana, lo que sin duda no había efectuado antes para aprovechar lo más posible la luz del día.
"It is fair to-night," said she, as she looked through the panes, "though not starlight; Mr. Rochester has, on the whole, had a favourable day for his journey."
-La noche es clara, aunque no hay estrellas -dijo, mirando a través de los cristales-. Mr.
"Journey!--Is Mr. Rochester gone anywhere?
Rochester ha tenido buen tiempo para su viaje. -Pero ¿se ha marchado Mr.
I did not know he was out."
Rochester? No lo sabía.
"Oh, he set off the moment he had breakfasted!
-Se fue en seguida de desayunar.
He is gone to the Leas, Mr. Eshton's place, ten miles on the other side Millcote.
Ha ido a casa de Mr. Eshton, en Leas, diez millas más allá de Millcote.
I believe there is quite a party assembled there; Lord Ingram, Sir George Lynn, Colonel Dent, and others."
Creo que se reunirá allí con Lord Ingram, Sir Jorge Lynn, el coronel Dent y otros.
"Do you expect him back to-night?"
-¿Cree que volverá esta noche?

"No--nor to-morrow either; I should think he is very likely to stay a week or more: when these fine, fashionable people get together, they are so surrounded by elegance and gaiety, so well provided with all that can please and entertain, they are in no hurry to separate.
Pasará fuera una semana o más. Cuando esas gentes distinguidas se reúnen, se divierten tanto y están tan a gusto que no ven nunca la hora de separarse.

Gentlemen especially are often in request on such occasions; and Mr. Rochester is so talented and so lively in society, that I believe he is a general favourite: the ladies are very fond of him; though you would not think his appearance calculated to recommend him particularly in their eyes: but I suppose his acquirements and abilities, perhaps his wealth and good blood, make amends for any little fault of look."

Rochester es un hombre encantador en sociedad, y se hace el favorito de todos, sobre todo de las señoras, aunque usted crea que su aspecto no le favorece. Yo supongo que su inteligencia, su riqueza y su nacimiento compensan esos pequeños defectos físicos.
"Are there ladies at the Leas?"
-¿Habrá señoras en Leas?

"There are Mrs. Eshton and her three daughters--very elegant young ladies indeed; and there are the Honourable Blanche and Mary Ingram, most beautiful women, I suppose: indeed I have seen Blanche, six or seven years since, when she was a girl of eighteen.
Eshton y sus hijas, jóvenes muy elegantes, y las honorables Blanche y Mary Ingram, que deben de estar muy guapas. Yo no veo a Blanche desde hace seis o siete años, cuando tenía dieciocho.
She came here to a Christmas ball and party Mr. Rochester gave.
Vino con motivo de un baile de Navidad que dio Mrs. Rochester.
You should have seen the dining-room that day--how richly it was decorated, how brilliantly lit up!
¡Si hubiera visto usted el comedor ese día! Estaba decorado y alumbrado que no había más que pedir.
I should think there were fifty ladies and gentlemen present--all of the first county families; and Miss Ingram was considered the belle of the evening."
Asistieron unas cincuenta señoras y caballeros de las mejores familias del condado, y Miss Ingram fue considerada por todos como la más hermosa.
"You saw her, you say, Mrs. Fairfax: what was she like?"
-¿La vio usted, Mrs. Fairfax?
"Yes, I saw her.
-Sí.
The dining-room doors were thrown open; and, as it was Christmas-time, the servants were allowed to assemble in the hall, to hear some of the ladies sing and play.
La puerta del comedor estaba abierta, porque, en Navidad, los criados se reunían en el vestíbulo para oír a las señoras tocar y cantar.
Mr. Rochester would have me to come in, and I sat down in a quiet corner and watched them.
Mr. Rochester me hizo pasar y yo me senté en un rincón apartado y lo vi todo.
I never saw a more splendid scene: the ladies were magnificently dressed; most of them--at least most of the younger ones--looked handsome; but Miss Ingram was certainly the queen."
Nunca he presenciado espectáculo más espléndido. La mayoría de las señoras -por lo menos, de las jóvenes me parecieron muy hermosas, pero Miss Ingram era verdaderamente la reina entre todas.
"And what was she like?"
-¿Cómo es?
"Tall, fine bust, sloping shoulders; long, graceful neck: olive complexion, dark and clear; noble features; eyes rather like Mr. Rochester's: large and black, and as brilliant as her jewels.
-Alta, muy bien formada, con los hombros muy bien contorneados, el cuello largo y gracioso, la piel morena, las facciones muy delicadas y los ojos negros, grandes y brillantes como joyas.
And then she had such a fine head of hair; raven-black and so becomingly arranged: a crown of thick plaits behind, and in front the longest, the glossiest curls I ever saw.
Llevaba muy bien peinado el cabello, que era negro y lustroso, con las trenzas en forma de corona y los rizos más lindos que yo he visto en mi vida.
She was dressed in pure white; an amber-coloured scarf was passed over her shoulder and across her breast, tied at the side, and descending in long, fringed ends below her knee.

-La admirarían mucho, ¿no?

-Sí; y no sólo por su belleza, sino por sus habilidades.

Rochester supiera cantar.

-Tiene una excelente voz de bajo y mucho gusto para la música.

-Pero me asombra que no haya habido algún caballero acomodado que se enamore de ella. Mr.

Rochester, por ejemplo. Es rico, ¿no?

When once more alone, I reviewed the information I had got; looked into my heart, examined its thoughts and feelings, and endeavoured to bring back with a strict hand such as had been straying through imagination's boundless and trackless waste, into the safe fold of common sense.

Cuando me hallé de nuevo sola, pensé en los informes que se me dieran, sondeé mi corazón, examiné mis pensamientos y mis sentimientos y me esforcé en restablecer las cosas en el estado que aconsejaba el sentido común.

Arraigned at my own bar, Memory having given her evidence of the hopes, wishes, sentiments I had been cherishing since last night--of the general state of mind in which I had indulged for nearly a fortnight past; Reason having come forward and told, in her own quiet way a plain, unvarnished tale, showing how I had rejected the real, and rabidly devoured the ideal;--I pronounced judgment to this effect:--

Repasé mentalmente las esperanzas y deseos a que me entregara desde la noche anterior -y que en realidad había comenzado a experimentar hacía quince días- y, apelando a la razón para reducir el ideal a la realidad, llegué a la conclusión siguiente:
That a greater fool than Jane Eyre had never breathed the breath of life; that a more fantastic idiot had never surfeited herself on sweet lies, and swallowed poison as if it were nectar.
Que jamás había existido una loca mayor que Jane Eyre, y que nunca idiota alguno se entregara a más dulces y fantásticos sueños bebiendo el veneno de la quimera como si fuese néctar.
"_You_," I said, "a favourite with Mr. Rochester? _You_ gifted with the power of pleasing him? _You_ of importance to him in any way? Go! your folly sickens me.
«¿ Tú, predilecta de Rochester? -pensé-. ¿Tú, dotada de la facultad de complacerle?
And you have derived pleasure from occasional tokens of preference--equivocal tokens shown by a gentleman of family and a man of the world to a dependent and a novice.
¿Tú, teniendo alguna importancia a sus ojos?
How dared you?
¿Es posible que te hayas dejado llevar por unas pocas muestras de preferencia, propias de un caballero y de un hombre de mundo, hacia ti, que eres una inexperta y además dependes de él?
Poor stupid dupe!--Could not even self-interest make you wiser?
¿Cómo has pensado en eso, pobre tonta?
You repeated to yourself this morning the brief scene of last night?--Cover your face and be ashamed! He said something in praise of your eyes, did he?
¿No te avergüenzas pensando en la escena de esta última noche?

It does good to no woman to be flattered by her superior, who cannot possibly intend to marry her; and it is madness in all women to let a secret love kindle within them, which, if unreturned and unknown, must devour the life that feeds it; and, if discovered and responded to, must lead, _ignis-fatus_-like, into miry wilds whence there is no extrication.

Una mujer no debe dejarse galantear por su jefe, que no puede soñar en casarse con ella, y es una locura, por otra parte, que las mujeres experimenten un amor para conservarlo oculto, porque ello agotaría su vida.

"Listen, then, Jane Eyre, to your sentence: to-morrow, place the glass before you, and draw in chalk your own picture, faithfully, without softening one defect; omit no harsh line, smooth away no displeasing irregularity; write under it, 'Portrait of a Governess, disconnected, poor, and plain.'

»Escucha, pues, Jane Eyre, tu sentencia: colócate mañana ante un espejo y, tan fielmente como puedas, haz tu autorretrato, sin paliar un defecto, sin suavizar ninguna fealdad, y escribe al pie: "Retrato de una institutriz pobre, vulgar y huérfana."

"Afterwards, take a piece of smooth ivory--you have one prepared in your drawing-box: take your palette, mix your freshest, finest, clearest tints; choose your most delicate camel-hair pencils; delineate carefully the loveliest face you can imagine; paint it in your softest shades and sweetest lines, according to the description given by Mrs. Fairfax of Blanche Ingram; remember the raven ringlets, the oriental eye;--What! you revert to Mr. Rochester as a model!

»Después, toma la lámina de marfil pulido que tienes entre tus útiles de dibujo, mezcla tus más puros y delicados colores, elige tus más finos lápices y traza cuidadosamente el rostro más encantador que puedas imaginar, acordándote de la descripción que te han hecho de Blanche Ingram. Order!
Rochester...
No snivel!--no sentiment!--no regret!
Pero no; ¡alto! Nada de sentimentalismos.
I will endure only sense and resolution.
Sólo hace falta buen juicio y decisión.

Recall the august yet harmonious lineaments, the Grecian neck and bust; let the round and dazzling arm be visible, and the delicate hand; omit neither diamond ring nor gold bracelet; portray faithfully the attire, aerial lace and glistening satin, graceful scarf and golden rose; call it 'Blanche, an accomplished lady of rank.'

Dibuja las líneas armoniosas y gráciles que te imaginas, el cuello de corte griego, el busto, el brazo redondo y fino, la delicada mano, sin omitir el anillo con un diamante ni la pulsera de oro. Añádele los adornos adecuados y escribe al pie: "Blanche.

"Whenever, in future, you should chance to fancy Mr. Rochester thinks well of you, take out these two pictures and compare them: say, 'Mr. Rochester might probably win that noble lady's love, if he chose to strive for it; is it likely he would waste a serious thought on this indigent and insignificant plebeian?'"
Rochester te mira con buenos ojos, coge los dos retratos y compáralos diciendo: "Si Mr. Rochester quiere, puede conseguir el amor de esta aristócrata.
"I'll do it," I resolved: and having framed this determination, I grew calm, and fell asleep.
»"Así lo haré", resolví. Y, una vez adoptada tal determinación, me sentí tranquilizada y pude dormirme.»
I kept my word.
Cumplí mi palabra.
An hour or two sufficed to sketch my own portrait in crayons; and in less than a fortnight I had completed an ivory miniature of an imaginary Blanche Ingram.
Un par de horas me bastó para concluir mi autorretrato a lápiz, y en menos de quince días terminé la miniatura de marfil de una imaginaria Blanche Ingram.
It looked a lovely face enough, and when compared with the real head in chalk, the contrast was as great as self- control could desire.
Cuando comparé aquella encantadora cabeza con mi retrato, el efecto fue tan positivo como mi voluntad de autodominio deseaba.
I derived benefit from the task: it had kept my head and hands employed, and had given force and fixedness to the new impressions I wished to stamp indelibly on my heart.
El trabajo resultó doblemente beneficioso, ya que entretuvo mis manos y mis pensamientos y vigorizó las nuevas impresiones que yo deseaba estampar indeleblemente en mi corazón.
Ere long, I had reason to congratulate myself on the course of wholesome discipline to which I had thus forced my feelings to submit.
A la larga, tuve motivos para felicitarme de aquella disciplina que me impusiera. Gracias a ella pude soportar los inmediatos sucesos con serenidad.
Thanks to it, I was able to meet subsequent occurrences with a decent calm, which, had they found me unprepared, I should probably have been unequal to maintain, even externally.
Sin aquella preparación los hubiera tolerado más difícilmente, e incluso no hubiera sabido disimular ante los demás mis reacciones.
A week passed, and no news arrived of Mr. Rochester: ten days, and still he did not come.
Pasó una semana, pasaron diez días y no llegaban noticias de Mr. Rochester.

Mrs. Fairfax said she should not be surprised if he were to go straight from the Leas to London, and thence to the Continent, and not show his face again at Thornfield for a year to come; he had not unfrequently quitted it in a manner quite as abrupt and unexpected.
Mrs. Fairfax aseguraba que no le sorprendería que a lo mejor se marchara con sus amigos a Londres, e incluso al continente, y que no apareciera por Thornfield hasta dentro de un año.
When I heard this, I was beginning to feel a strange chill and failing at the heart.
Era muy frecuente en él desaparecer de aquel modo brusco e inesperado.

I was actually permitting myself to experience a sickening sense of disappointment; but rallying my wits, and recollecting my principles, I at once called my sensations to order; and it was wonderful how I got over the temporary blunder--how I cleared up the mistake of supposing Mr. Rochester's movements a matter in which I had any cause to take a vital interest.

Al oírla experimenté un extraño desfallecimiento en el corazón, pero dominando mis sentimientos logré enseguida superar mi momentáneo desvarío, recordando lo absurdo que era que considerase los movimientos de Mr. Rochester como cosa de vital interés para mí.

Not that I humbled myself by a slavish notion of inferiority: on the contrary, I just said-- "You have nothing to do with the master of Thornfield, further than to receive the salary he gives you for teaching his protegee, and to be grateful for such respectful and kind treatment as, if you do your duty, you have a right to expect at his hands.

Con esto no me situaba ante mí misma en una situación de inferioridad, sino que, al contrario, razonaba: «Tú no tienes nada que ver con el dueño de Thornfield, sino para cobrar el sueldo que te paga por enseñar a su protegida y para agradecerle el trato amable que te da, y el cual tienes derecho a esperar mientras cumplas tus deberes a conciencia.
Be sure that is the only tie he seriously acknowledges between you and him; so don't make him the object of your fine feelings, your raptures, agonies, and so forth.
Entre él y tú no pueden existir otras relaciones. Prescinde, pues, de consagrarle tus sentimientos, entusiasmos y cosas análogas.
He is not of your order: keep to your caste, and be too self-respecting to lavish the love of the whole heart, soul, and strength, where such a gift is not wanted and would be despised."
Él no es de tu clase; mantente en tu terreno y, por tu propio respeto, no ofrezcas tu amor a quien no te lo pide y acaso te lo despreciara.»

I went on with my day's business tranquilly; but ever and anon vague suggestions kept wandering across my brain of reasons why I should quit Thornfield; and I kept involuntarily framing advertisements and pondering conjectures about new situations: these thoughts I did not think to check; they might germinate and bear fruit if they could.
Me ocupé, pues, con calma en mi misión cerca de la niña, pero sin poderlo evitar bullían en mi cerebro ideas y conjeturas sobre la posibilidad de abandonar Thornfield y buscar nuevos horizontes.
Mr. Rochester had been absent upwards of a fortnight, when the post brought Mrs. Fairfax a letter.
Pensamientos de tal clase no había por qué reprimirlos; antes bien, podían desarrollarse libremente y fructificar si llegaba el caso.
"It is from the master," said she, as she looked at the direction.
Mr. Rochester llevaba ausente unos quince días, cuando Mr.
"Now I suppose we shall know whether we are to expect his return or not."
Fairfax recibió una carta. -Es del amo -dijo, mirando la dirección-. Ahora sabremos si vuelve o no.

And while she broke the seal and perused the document, I went on taking my coffee (we were at breakfast): it was hot, and I attributed to that circumstance a fiery glow which suddenly rose to my face.
Mientras abría el escrito, yo comencé a tomar mi café (porque nos hallábamos desayunando) y, como estaba muy caliente, atribuí a tal circunstancia el brusco arrebato que me coloreó de rojo la cara.
Why my hand shook, and why I involuntarily spilt half the contents of my cup into my saucer, I did not choose to consider.
Lo que ya no pude concretar a qué se debiera fue el temblor de mi mano, que me hizo derramar en el plato la mitad del contenido de mi taza.
"Well, I sometimes think we are too quiet; but we run a chance of being busy enough now: for a little while at least," said Mrs. Fairfax, still holding the note before her spectacles.

-Vaya -dijo Mrs. Fairfax, después de leer la carta-: yo, a veces, me quejo de que aquí estamos demasiado tranquilos, pero me parece que ahora vamos a andar demasiado ocupados, al menos por algún tiempo.

Ere I permitted myself to request an explanation, I tied the string of Adele's pinafore, which happened to be loose: having helped her also to another bun and refilled her mug with milk, I said, nonchalantly--
Me permití preguntar:
"Mr. Rochester is not likely to return soon, I suppose?"
-¿Es que vuelve pronto Mr. Rochester?
"Indeed he is--in three days, he says: that will be next Thursday; and not alone either.
-De aquí a tres días, según dice, y no solo. Yo no sé cuánta gente traerá consigo, pero ordena que se preparen los mejores dormitorios y que se limpien los salones y la biblioteca.

I don't know how many of the fine people at the Leas are coming with him: he sends directions for all the best bedrooms to be prepared; and the library and drawing-rooms are to be cleaned out; I am to get more kitchen hands from the George Inn, at Millcote, and from wherever else I can; and the ladies will bring their maids and the gentlemen their valets: so we shall have a full house of it."
Es necesario que yo busque alguna ayudante de cocina y alguna asistenta en la posada de George en Millcote y donde se pueda. Además, las señoras traen sus doncellas y los señores sus criados.
And Mrs. Fairfax swallowed her breakfast and hastened away to commence operations.
Mrs. Fairfax terminó, pues, su desayuno y se apresuró a preparar todo lo necesario.
The three days were, as she had foretold, busy enough.
Aquellos tres días hubo mucho ajetreo.
I had thought all the rooms at Thornfield beautifully clean and well arranged; but it appears I was mistaken.
Yo creía que todos los aposentos de Thornfield estaban arreglados y limpios, pero entonces descubrí que me engañaba.

Three women were got to help; and such scrubbing, such brushing, such washing of paint and beating of carpets, such taking down and putting up of pictures, such polishing of mirrors and lustres, such lighting of fires in bedrooms, such airing of sheets and feather-beds on hearths, I never beheld, either before or since.

Tres mujeres fueron contratadas para ayudar en las tareas, y hubo fregado, barrido, sacudido de alfombras, limpieza de espejos, preparación de chimeneas y lavado de ropas de cama, como no viera en mi vida.
Adele ran quite wild in the midst of it: the preparations for company and the prospect of their arrival, seemed to throw her into ecstasies.
Adèle estaba encantada con los preparativos y con la perspectiva de los invitados que iban a venir.
She would have Sophie to look over all her "toilettes," as she called frocks; to furbish up any that were "_passees_," and to air and arrange the new.
Hizo que Sophie reparase todas sus toilettes, según llamaba a los vestidos, para arreglar aquellos que estuvieran passées.

For herself, she did nothing but caper about in the front chambers, jump on and off the bedsteads, and lie on the mattresses and piled-up bolsters and pillows before the enormous fires roaring in the chimneys.
Por su parte no hizo nada, sino saltar en las alcobas, brincar en las camas, tenderse en los colchones y apilar almohadas ante las chimeneas.

From school duties she was exonerated: Mrs. Fairfax had pressed me into her service, and I was all day in the storeroom, helping (or hindering) her and the cook; learning to make custards and cheese-cakes and French pastry, to truss game and garnish desert-dishes.

Le dimos vacaciones, porque Mrs. Fairfax había requerido mi ayuda y yo pasaba el día en la despensa con ella y con la cocinera, aprendiendo a hacer flanes y natillas, a preparar empanadillas de queso y dulces a la francesa, a mechar carne y a guarnecer platos de postre.
The party were expected to arrive on Thursday afternoon, in time for dinner at six.
Se esperaba a los invitados la tarde del jueves, y se contaba que cenaran a las seis.
During the intervening period I had no time to nurse chimeras; and I believe I was as active and gay as anybody--Adele excepted.
Durante todo aquel período no tuve tiempo de imaginar quimeras y estuve más activa y alegre que nadie, excepto Adèle.
Still, now and then, I received a damping check to my cheerfulness; and was, in spite of myself, thrown back on the region of doubts and portents, and dark conjectures.
No obstante, de vez en cuando, a despecho de mí misma, me dejaba arrastrar con el pensamiento a la región que originaba mis dudas, suposiciones y conjeturas sombrías.

This was when I chanced to see the third-storey staircase door (which of late had always been kept locked) open slowly, and give passage to the form of Grace Poole, in prim cap, white apron, and handkerchief; when I watched her glide along the gallery, her quiet tread muffled in a list slipper; when I saw her look into the bustling, topsy-turvy bedrooms,--just say a word, perhaps, to the charwoman about the proper way to polish a grate, or clean a marble mantelpiece, or take stains from papered walls, and then pass on.

Esto sucedía cuando veía abrirse la puerta de la escalera del tercer piso y aparecer a Grace Poole, con su cofia almidonada y su delantal blanco, deslizándose por la galería con su paso tranquilo, mirando el interior de los revueltos dormitorios, y diciendo alguna palabra a los asistentes a propósito de la limpieza, del polvo de las chimeneas, del modo de quitar las manchas de las paredes empapeladas...

She would thus descend to the kitchen once a day, eat her dinner, smoke a moderate pipe on the hearth, and go back, carrying her pot of porter with her, for her private solace, in her own gloomy, upper haunt.
Grace bajaba a comer a la cocina una vez al día, fumaba una pipa junto al fogón y se marchaba llevándose a su guarida, para su solaz, una voluminosa jarra de cerveza.

Only one hour in the twenty-four did she pass with her fellow-servants below; all the rest of her time was spent in some low-ceiled, oaken chamber of the second storey: there she sat and sewed--and probably laughed drearily to herself,--as companionless as a prisoner in his dungeon.
Sólo una hora del día pasaba con los demás sirvientes; el resto estaba en su habitación del piso alto, acaso riendo con aquella terrible risa suya, y tan solitaria como un prisionero en su celda.

The strangest thing of all was, that not a soul in the house, except me, noticed her habits, or seemed to marvel at them: no one discussed her position or employment; no one pitied her solitude or isolation.
Lo más raro de todo era que nadie de la casa, excepto yo, parecía reparar en sus costumbres ni asombrarse de ellas. Nadie discutía cuál era su misión ni manifestaba compasión por su soledad.
I once, indeed, overheard part of a dialogue between Leah and one of the charwomen, of which Grace formed the subject.
Una vez, sin embargo, sorprendí una conversación entre Leah y una de las asistentas, a propósito de Grace.
Leah had been saying something I had not caught, and the charwoman remarked-- "She gets good wages, I guess?"
Leah había dicho algo que no pude oír, y la asistenta contestaba: -Debe ganar buen sueldo, ¿no?
"Yes," said Leah; "I wish I had as good; not that mine are to complain of,--there's no stinginess at Thornfield; but they're not one fifth of the sum Mrs. Poole receives.
No es que yo esté descontenta de lo que gano, porque no es poco, pero ¡ya quisiera tener el sueldo de Grace! El mío no llega ni a la quinta parte del suyo.
And she is laying by: she goes every quarter to the bank at Millcote.
Cada trimestre va al Banco de Millcote a guardar dinero.

I should not wonder but she has saved enough to keep her independent if she liked to leave; but I suppose she's got used to the place; and then she's not forty yet, and strong and able for anything. It is too soon for her to give up business."

No me asombraría que tuviese ya bastante para vivir si deseara dejar de trabajar, pero debe de estar acostumbrada a la casa, y como aún no tiene cuarenta años y está muy fuerte, seguramente piensa que todavía no es tiempo de retirarse...
"She is a good hand, I daresay," said the charwoman.
-¡Buenas tragaderas debe de tener! -dijo la sirvienta.
"Ah!--she understands what she has to do,--nobody better," rejoined Leah significantly; "and it is not every one could fill her shoes--not for all the money she gets."
-¡Y usted que lo diga! -replicó Leah, que sin duda entendía lo que la otra quería indicar con aquello-. No quisiera estar en su caso ni por todo lo que gana.
"That it is not!" was the reply.
-¡Claro que no!
"I wonder whether the master--"
Me asombra que el amo...
The charwoman was going on; but here Leah turned and perceived me, and she instantly gave her companion a nudge.
Leah se volvió en aquel momento y, al verme, hizo un guiño a la asistenta.
"Doesn't she know?" I heard the woman whisper.
-¿Es que no lo sabe? -oí cuchichear a la mujer.
Leah shook her head, and the conversation was of course dropped.
Leah movió la cabeza y la conversación se interrumpió.
All I had gathered from it amounted to this,--that there was a mystery at Thornfield; and that from participation in that mystery I was purposely excluded.
Cuanto pude sacar en limpio fue que en Thornfield había un misterio y que de él, deliberadamente, se me excluía a mí.

Thursday came: all work had been completed the previous evening; carpets were laid down, bed-hangings festooned, radiant white counterpanes spread, toilet tables arranged, furniture rubbed, flowers piled in vases: both chambers and saloons looked as fresh and bright as hands could make them.

La noche anterior se había concluido todo el trabajo: las alfombras estaban limpias y extendidas, los lechos preparados, dispuestos los tocadores, bruñida la vajilla, las flores colocadas en los jarrones. Alcobas y salones parecían tan flamantes como si fueran nuevos.

The hall, too, was scoured; and the great carved clock, as well as the steps and banisters of the staircase, were polished to the brightness of glass; in the dining-room, the sideboard flashed resplendent with plate; in the drawing-room and boudoir, vases of exotics bloomed on all sides.
Tanto el reloj como las escaleras y las barandillas había sido encerados y brillaban como espejos. Los aparadores, en el comedor, resplandecían de plata.
Afternoon arrived: Mrs. Fairfax assumed her best black satin gown, her gloves, and her gold watch; for it was her part to receive the company,--to conduct the ladies to their rooms, &c.
Por la tarde, Mrs. Fairfax se puso su mejor vestido de raso negro y su reloj de oro, a fin de recibir a los invitados, llevar a sus cuartos a las señoras, etc.
Adele, too, would be dressed: though I thought she had little chance of being introduced to the party that day at least.
Adèle quiso también que la vistiésemos, aunque yo pensaba que no era probable que la presentasen a los invitados, por lo menos aquel día.
However, to please her, I allowed Sophie to apparel her in one of her short, full muslin frocks.
Sin embargo, para complacerla, encargué a Sophie que la vistiese con un bonito traje de muselina, muy corto.
For myself, I had no need to make any change; I should not be called upon to quit my sanctum of the schoolroom; for a sanctum it was now become to me,--"a very pleasant refuge in time of trouble."

En cuanto a mí, no era necesario que cambiase de ropa. Nadie iba a ir a reclamarme a mi santuario del cuarto de estudio, que en santuario, en efecto, se había convertido para mí: en un verdadero «agradable refugio en los tiempos calamitosos»...
It had been a mild, serene spring day--one of those days which, towards the end of March or the beginning of April, rise shining over the earth as heralds of summer.
Era uno de esos serenos días de primavera, de fines de marzo o primeros de abril, tan llenos de sol que parecen heraldos del verano.
It was drawing to an end now; but the evening was even warm, and I sat at work in the schoolroom with the window open.
En aquel momento tocaba ya a su fin, pero el atardecer era agradable y tibio. Yo hacía labor al lado de la abierta ventana del cuarto de estudio.
"It gets late," said Mrs. Fairfax, entering in rustling state.
-Es bastante tarde -dijo Mrs. Fairfax, entrando, con gran crujido de faldas, en la habitación-.
"I am glad I ordered dinner an hour after the time Mr. Rochester mentioned; for it is past six now.
Me alegro de haber mandado preparar la comida para una hora después de la que Mr. Rochester indicaba, porque son más de las seis.
I have sent John down to the gates to see if there is anything on the road: one can see a long way from thence in the direction of Millcote."
He enviado a John a la verla, a ver si divisa llegar a los señores por el camino.
She went to the window.
Se acercó a la ventana.
"Here he is!" said she.
-¡Ahí está!
