"Well, John" (leaning out), "any news?"
¡John! -gritó asomándose-.
"They're coming, ma'am," was the answer.
¿Qué hay? -Ya vienen, señora -respondió él-.
"They'll be here in ten minutes."
Estarán aquí dentro de diez minutos.
Adele flew to the window.
Adèle se precipitó a la ventana.
I followed, taking care to stand on one side, so that, screened by the curtain, I could see without being seen.
Yo la seguí, colocándome tras la cortina de modo que pudiese ver sin ser vista.
The ten minutes John had given seemed very long, but at last wheels were heard; four equestrians galloped up the drive, and after them came two open carriages.

Los diez minutos que anunciara John me parecieron muy largos, más al fin se oyó rumor de ruedas y vimos aparecer cuatro jinetes seguidos de dos coches abiertos llenos de plumas y velos flotantes. Dos de los jinetes eran jóvenes y arrogantes; el tercero era Mr.

Fluttering veils and waving plumes filled the vehicles; two of the cavaliers were young, dashing-looking gentlemen; the third was Mr. Rochester, on his black horse, Mesrour, Pilot bounding before him; at his side rode a lady, and he and she were the first of the party.
Piloto corría a su lado. Rochester iba emparejado con una amazona, y ambos marchaban a la cabeza del grupo.
Her purple riding-habit almost swept the ground, her veil streamed long on the breeze; mingling with its transparent folds, and gleaming through them, shone rich raven ringlets.
Los vuelos del rojo traje de montar de la señora rozaban casi el suelo y el viento hacía ondear su velo, a cuyo través se transparentaban los brillantes rizos de su cabellera.
"Miss Ingram!" exclaimed Mrs. Fairfax, and away she hurried to her post below.
-¡Miss Ingam! -exclamó el ama de llaves. Y se precipitó a su puesto, en el piso bajo.
The cavalcade, following the sweep of the drive, quickly turned the angle of the house, and I lost sight of it.
La cabalgata, siguiendo las sinuosidades del camino, dio la vuelta a la casa. La perdí de vista.

Adele now petitioned to go down; but I took her on my knee, and gave her to understand that she must not on any account think of venturing in sight of the ladies, either now or at any other time, unless expressly sent for: that Mr. Rochester would be very angry, &c.

Adèle me pidió que le permitiese bajar, pero yo la senté sobre mis rodillas y traté de hacerle comprender que no debía aventurarse a aparecer ante las señoras antes de que Mr. Rochester la mandase a buscar, para no disgustarle.
"Some natural tears she shed" on being told this; but as I began to look very grave, she consented at last to wipe them.
Comenzó a verter lágrimas, como era presumible, pero la miré con severidad y acabó secando su llanto.

A joyous stir was now audible in the hall: gentlemen's deep tones and ladies' silvery accents blent harmoniously together, and distinguishable above all, though not loud, was the sonorous voice of the master of Thornfield Hall, welcoming his fair and gallant guests under its roof.
En el vestíbulo sonaba ya el alegre bullicio que producían los recién llegados. Las voces profundas de los caballeros y las argentinas de las señoras se confundían armoniosamente.
Then light steps ascended the stairs; and there was a tripping through the gallery, and soft cheerful laughs, and opening and closing doors, and, for a time, a hush.

Entre todas, destacaba la sonora del dueño de Thornfield, dando la bienvenida a los invitados que honraban su casa. Luego, ligeros pasos resonaron en la escalera y en la galería y se oyó un abrir y cerrar de puertas, risas, un murmullo confuso...
"Elles changent de toilettes," said Adele; who, listening attentively, had followed every movement; and she sighed.
-Se están cambiando de ropa -dijo Adèle, que había escuchado con atención. Y suspiró al añadir-:

"Chez maman," said she, "quand il y avait du monde, je le suivais partout, au salon et a leurs chambres; souvent je regardais les femmes de chambre coiffer et habiller les dames, et c'etait si amusant: comme cela on apprend."

En casa de mamá, cuando había visitas, yo la acompañaba a todas partes, en el salón y en las habitaciones, y muchas veces miraba a las doncellas vestir y peinar a las señoras. Es muy divertido, y, además, así se aprende...
"Don't you feel hungry, Adele?"
-¿No tienes apetito, Adèle? -interrumpí.
"Mais oui, mademoiselle: voila cinq ou six heures que nous n'avons pas mange."
-Sí, señorita. Hace cinco o seis horas que no hemos comido.
"Well now, while the ladies are in their rooms, I will venture down and get you something to eat."
-Bueno, pues mientras las señoras están en sus alcobas, intentaré traerte algo de comer.
And issuing from my asylum with precaution, I sought a back-stairs which conducted directly to the kitchen.
Y, saliendo de mi refugio con precaución, bajé la escalera de servicio que conducía a la cocina.
All in that region was fire and commotion; the soup and fish were in the last stage of projection, and the cook hung over her crucibles in a frame of mind and body threatening spontaneous combustion.

La sopa y el pescado estaban a punto de quedar listos y la cocinera se inclinaba sobre los hornillos en un estado de cuerpo y de ánimo que hacía temer que sufriese peligro de combustión personal. En el cuarto de estar de la servidumbre estaban sentados dos cocheros, y otros tres criados alrededor del fuego.

In the servants' hall two coachmen and three gentlemen's gentlemen stood or sat round the fire; the abigails, I suppose, were upstairs with their mistresses; the new servants, that had been hired from Millcote, were bustling about everywhere.
Las doncellas, a lo que imaginé, debían de hallarse ocupadas vistiendo a sus señoras. En cuanto a las nuevas sirvientas contratadas en Millcote, andaban de un lado para otro con gran estrépito.

Threading this chaos, I at last reached the larder; there I took possession of a cold chicken, a roll of bread, some tarts, a plate or two and a knife and fork: with this booty I made a hasty retreat.
Atravesando aquel caos, alcancé la despensa, donde me apoderé de un pollo frío, un trozo de pan, algunos dulces, un par de platos y un cubierto, con todo lo cual me retiré apresuradamente.
I had regained the gallery, and was just shutting the back-door behind me, when an accelerated hum warned me that the ladies were about to issue from their chambers.
Ya ganaba la galería y cerraba tras de mí la puerta de servicio, cuando un acelerado rumor me hizo comprender que las señoras salían de sus aposentos.

I could not proceed to the schoolroom without passing some of their doors, and running the risk of being surprised with my cargo of victualage; so I stood still at this end, which, being windowless, was dark: quite dark now, for the sun was set and twilight gathering.
No podía llegar al cuarto de estudio sin pasar ante algunas de las puertas, a riesgo de ser sorprendida en mi menester de avituallamiento.

Presently the chambers gave up their fair tenants one after another: each came out gaily and airily, with dress that gleamed lustrous through the dusk. For a moment they stood grouped together at the other extremity of the gallery, conversing in a key of sweet subdued vivacity: they then descended the staircase almost as noiselessly as a bright mist rolls down a hill.

Por fortuna, el cuarto se encontraba al extremo de la galería, la cual, por no tener ventana, estaba generalmente en penumbra y ahora en tinieblas completas porque ya se había puesto el sol y se apagaban las últimas claridades del crepúsculo.
Their collective appearance had left on me an impression of high- born elegance, such as I had never before received.

Se reunieron en un grupo, hablando con suave vivacidad, y luego descendieron la escalera con tan poco ruido como una masa de niebla por una colina. La aparición colectiva de aquellas mujeres dejó en mi mente una impresión de distinción y elegancia como nunca experimentara hasta entonces.
I found Adele peeping through the schoolroom door, which she held ajar.
Encontré a Adèle mirándolas a través de la puerta del cuarto de estudio, que la niña había abierto a medias.
"What beautiful ladies!" cried she in English.
-¡Qué señoras tan hermosas! -exclamó, en inglés-.
"Oh, I wish I might go to them!
¡Cuánto me gustaría bajar con ellas!
Do you think Mr. Rochester will send for us by-and-bye, after dinner?"
¿Cree usted que Mr. Rochester nos mandará a buscar después de que terminen de cenar?
"No, indeed, I don't; Mr. Rochester has something else to think about.
Mr. Rochester tiene ahora otras cosas en qué ocuparse.
Never mind the ladies to-night; perhaps you will see them to-morrow: here is your dinner."
Hoy no es fácil que te presenten a esas señoras. Acaso mañana...
She was really hungry, so the chicken and tarts served to divert her attention for a time.
Como la niña tenía verdadero apetito, el pollo y los dulces atrajeron su atención durante un rato.

It was well I secured this forage, or both she, I, and Sophie, to whom I conveyed a share of our repast, would have run a chance of getting no dinner at all: every one downstairs was too much engaged to think of us.
Mi previsión no fue desacertada, porque tanto Adèle como yo y como Sophie, a quien envié parte de las provisiones, corríamos el riesgo de quedarnos sin cenar, en medio del general ajetreo.
The dessert was not carried out till after nine and at ten footmen were still running to and fro with trays and coffee- cups.
Los postres no se sirvieron hasta las nueve, y a las diez aún los criados corrían de aquí para allá llevando bandejas y tazas de café.
I allowed Adele to sit up much later than usual; for she declared she could not possibly go to sleep while the doors kept opening and shutting below, and people bustling about.
Acosté a Adèle mucho más tarde que de costumbre, porque me aseguró que no podría dormirse mientras oyera aquel continuo abrir y cerrar de puertas.
Besides, she added, a message might possibly come from Mr. Rochester when she was undressed; "et alors quel dommage!"
Además, añadió, podía llegar un aviso de Mr. Rochester cuando ella estuviera ya acostada, «y sería lamentable...»
I told her stories as long as she would listen to them; and then for a change I took her out into the gallery.
La relaté cuantos cuentos quiso escucharme y luego, por cambiar un poco de ambiente, me la llevé a la galería.
The hall lamp was now lit, and it amused her to look over the balustrade and watch the servants passing backwards and forwards.
La gran lámpara del vestíbulo estaba encendida y a la niña la divertía asomarse a la barandilla y ver pasar los sirvientes.
When the evening was far advanced, a sound of music issued from the drawing-room, whither the piano had been removed; Adele and I sat down on the top step of the stairs to listen.
Y avanzada la noche, oímos sonar el piano en el salón. Adèle se sentó en el último peldaño de la escalera para escuchar.
Presently a voice blent with the rich tones of the instrument; it was a lady who sang, and very sweet her notes were.
Una dulce voz femenina comenzó una canción.
The solo over, a duet followed, and then a glee: a joyous conversational murmur filled up the intervals.
Al solo siguió un dúo. En los intervalos percibíase el murmullo de alegres conversaciones.

I listened long: suddenly I discovered that my ear was wholly intent on analysing the mingled sounds, and trying to discriminate amidst the confusion of accents those of Mr. Rochester; and when it caught them, which it soon did, it found a further task in framing the tones, rendered by distance inarticulate, into words.
Yo escuché también, y de pronto reparé que estaba intentando distinguir entre el rumor de la charla el acento peculiar de Mr. Rochester.
The clock struck eleven.
El reloj dio las once.
I looked at Adele, whose head leant against my shoulder; her eyes were waxing heavy, so I took her up in my arms and carried her off to bed.
La cabeza de Adèle se apoyaba en mi hombro y sus ojos se cerraban ya. La cogí en brazos y la llevé al lecho.
It was near one before the gentlemen and ladies sought their chambers.
Debía de ser sobre la una cuando los invitados se retiraron a sus habitaciones.
The next day was as fine as its predecessor: it was devoted by the party to an excursion to some site in the neighbourhood.
Al día siguiente también hizo buen tiempo. La reunión lo aprovechó para hacer una excursión a no sé qué lugar de las cercanías.
They set out early in the forenoon, some on horseback, the rest in carriages; I witnessed both the departure and the return.
Salieron temprano de mañana; unos a pie y otros en coches. Miss Ingram era la única amazona y Mr.
Miss Ingram, as before, was the only lady equestrian; and, as before, Mr. Rochester galloped at her side; the two rode a little apart from the rest.
Rochester cabalgaba a su lado, un poco separados ambos del resto de los excursionistas.
I pointed out this circumstance to Mrs. Fairfax, who was standing at the window with me--
Se lo hice notar a Mrs. Fairfax, que estaba sentada a mi lado, junto a la ventana.
"You said it was not likely they should think of being married," said I, "but you see Mr. Rochester evidently prefers her to any of the other ladies."
¡Observe cómo Mr. Rochester corteja a esa señorita entre todas! -comenté.
"Yes, I daresay: no doubt he admires her."
-Tiene usted razón: se ve que la admira.
"And she him," I added; "look how she leans her head towards him as if she were conversing confidentially; I wish I could see her face; I have never had a glimpse of it yet."
Mire cómo inclina la cabeza para hablarle confidencialmente. Me gustaría verla la cara.
"You will see her this evening," answered Mrs. Fairfax.
-La verá esta noche -repuso el ama de llaves-.

"I happened to remark to Mr. Rochester how much Adele wished to be introduced to the ladies, and he said: 'Oh! let her come into the drawing-room after dinner; and request Miss Eyre to accompany her.'"
He hablado a Mr. Rochester del interés que tenía Adèle en ser presentada a las señoras, y me ha dicho que fuera usted con ella al salón esta noche, después de cenar.
"Yes; he said that from mere politeness: I need not go, I am sure," I answered.
-Le aseguro que no me hace ninguna gracia ir.

"Well, I observed to him that as you were unused to company, I did not think you would like appearing before so gay a party--all strangers; and he replied, in his quick way--'Nonsense! If she objects, tell her it is my particular wish; and if she resists, say I shall come and fetch her in case of contumacy.'"

-Ya le indiqué que usted está poco acostumbrada a la sociedad y que no se divertirá en una reunión de desconocidos, pero me contestó que, si usted se oponía, la dijese que él tenía particular interés, agregando que, si aun así se negaba usted, vendría en persona a buscarla.
"I will not give him that trouble," I answered.
-No tiene por qué molestarse tanto -dije-.
"I will go, if no better may be; but I don't like it.
Iré yo, aunque preferiría no hacerlo.
Shall you be there, Mrs. Fairfax?"
¿Estará usted también?
"No; I pleaded off, and he admitted my plea.
-No. Le rogué que me excusara y consintió.
I'll tell you how to manage so as to avoid the embarrassment of making a formal entrance, which is the most disagreeable part of the business.
Voy a decirle lo que debe hacer para evitar una entrada aparatosa en el salón, que es la parte más desagradable de esas cosas.

You must go into the drawing- room while it is empty, before the ladies leave the dinner-table; choose your seat in any quiet nook you like; you need not stay long after the gentlemen come in, unless you please: just let Mr. Rochester see you are there and then slip away--nobody will notice you."

Usted entra cuando el salón esté vacío, es decir, mientras los invitados se hallen aún a la mesa, y elige un asiento en un rincón. Tampoco es preciso que esté mucho tiempo después de que entren los señores, a no ser que la agrade.
"Will these people remain long, do you think?"
-¿Cree que estarán mucho tiempo en Thornfield los invitados?
"Perhaps two or three weeks, certainly not more.
-No creo que más de dos o tres semanas.

After the Easter recess, Sir George Lynn, who was lately elected member for Millcote, will have to go up to town and take his seat; I daresay Mr. Rochester will accompany him: it surprises me that he has already made so protracted a stay at Thornfield."
Después de las vacaciones de Pascua, Sir George Lynn, que ha sido elegido representante de Millcote, tendrá que ir a la ciudad a ocupar su cargo y no me extrañaría que el señor le acompañase.
It was with some trepidation that I perceived the hour approach when I was to repair with my charge to the drawing-room.
Lo que me parece raro es que pase tanto tiempo en Thornfield. No sin emoción vi aproximarse la hora de mi entrada en el salón.

Adele had been in a state of ecstasy all day, after hearing she was to be presented to the ladies in the evening; and it was not till Sophie commenced the operation of dressing her that she sobered down.
Adèle, desde que oyera que iba a ser presentada a las señoras, se había sumido en éxtasis.

Then the importance of the process quickly steadied her, and by the time she had her curls arranged in well-smoothed, drooping clusters, her pink satin frock put on, her long sash tied, and her lace mittens adjusted, she looked as grave as any judge.

Una vez que Sophie la hubo vestido con todo cuidado, arreglado sus cabellos en lindos rizos y puesto el trajecito de seda rosa, adoptó un aire tan grave como el de un juez, se sentó con precaución en su sillita, procurando que el vestido no rozase, y esperó que yo estuviera preparada, lo que sucedió pronto.

This I quickly was: my best dress (the silver-grey one, purchased for Miss Temple's wedding, and never worn since) was soon put on; my hair was soon smoothed; my sole ornament, the pearl brooch, soon assumed.
Me puse mi mejor vestido (el gris que me hiciera para la boda de Miss Temple y que no había vuelto a usar más), me peiné rápidamente y me coloqué el prendedor, única joya que poseía.
We descended.
Luego bajamos.
Fortunately there was another entrance to the drawing-room than that through the saloon where they were all seated at dinner.
Afortunadamente el salón tenía otra entrada, además de la del comedor, en el que estaba congregada la concurrencia.
We found the apartment vacant; a large fire burning silently on the marble hearth, and wax candles shining in bright solitude, amid the exquisite flowers with which the tables were adorned.

La estancia se hallaba aún vacía. Un gran fuego ardía silenciosamente en la chimenea y muchas bujías de cera, dispuestas entre las exquisitas flores con que estaban adornadas las mesas, iluminaban la soledad.

The crimson curtain hung before the arch: slight as was the separation this drapery formed from the party in the adjoining saloon, they spoke in so low a key that nothing of their conversation could be distinguished beyond a soothing murmur.
El cortinón carmesí pendía ante el arco de acceso al comedor y, por ligera que fuese la separación, bastaba para que de las conversaciones no llegase más que un apagado murmullo.
Adele, who appeared to be still under the influence of a most solemnising impression, sat down, without a word, on the footstool I pointed out to her.
Adèle, que estaba muy impresionada, se sentó, sin decir palabra, en el taburete que la indiqué.
I retired to a window-seat, and taking a book from a table near, endeavoured to read.
Yo me coloqué en un asiento próximo a una ventana, cogí un libro de una mesa y empecé a leer.
Adele brought her stool to my feet; ere long she touched my knee. "What is it, Adele?"
Adèle acercó su escabel a mí y me tocó una rodilla. -¿Qué quieres, Adèle?
"Est-ce que je ne puis pas prendrie une seule de ces fleurs magnifiques, mademoiselle?
-¿Puedo coger una de esas magníficas flores, señorita?
Seulement pour completer ma toilette."
Así completaré mi tocado...
"You think too much of your 'toilette,' Adele: but you may have a flower."
-Piensas demasiado en tu tocado, Adèle... Pero, en fin, coge una flor...
And I took a rose from a vase and fastened it in her sash. She sighed a sigh of ineffable satisfaction, as if her cup of happiness were now full.
Tomó una rosa, se la puso en la cintura y exhaló un suspiro de profunda satisfacción, como si la copa de su felicidad estuviese ahora colmada.
I turned my face away to conceal a smile I could not suppress: there was something ludicrous as well as painful in the little Parisienne's earnest and innate devotion to matters of dress.
Volví el rostro para ocultar una sonrisa que no pude contener. Había algo tan doloroso como ridículo en la innata devoción de aquella minúscula parisiense a cuanto se refiriese a adornos y vestidos.

A soft sound of rising now became audible; the curtain was swept back from the arch; through it appeared the dining-room, with its lit lustre pouring down light on the silver and glass of a magnificent dessert-service covering a long table; a band of ladies stood in the opening; they entered, and the curtain fell behind them.
Corrieron la cortina de la arcada y apareció el comedor, esplendoroso con los servicios de postre, de plata y cristal. Un grupo de señoras entró en el salón y la cortina cayó otra vez tras ellas.
There were but eight; yet, somehow, as they flocked in, they gave the impression of a much larger number.
Aunque sólo fuesen ocho, la magnificencia de su aspecto daba la impresión de que eran muchas más.
Some of them were very tall; many were dressed in white; and all had a sweeping amplitude of array that seemed to magnify their persons as a mist magnifies the moon.
Algunas eran muy altas, varias vestían de blanco, y la esplendidez de los adornos de todas las embellecía como una neblina embellece la luna.
I rose and curtseyed to them: one or two bent their heads in return, the others only stared at me.
Me levanté cortésmente. Unas pocas correspondieron inclinando la cabeza; otras se limitaron a mirarme.
They dispersed about the room, reminding me, by the lightness and buoyancy of their movements, of a flock of white plumy birds.
Se esparcieron por el salón. La gracia y ligereza de sus movimientos las asemejaba a una bandada de pájaros blancos.

Some of them threw themselves in half-reclining positions on the sofas and ottomans: some bent over the tables and examined the flowers and books: the rest gathered in a group round the fire: all talked in a low but clear tone which seemed habitual to them.

Algunas se acomodaron en lánguidas posturas en los sofás y otomanas, y otras se inclinaron sobre las mesas para examinar los libros y las flores. Las demás se agruparon en torno al fuego y comenzaron a hablar en el tono de voz bajo y claro que parecía serles habitual.
I knew their names afterwards, and may as well mention them now.
Oyéndolas, me enteré de sus nombres.
She had evidently been a handsome woman, and was well preserved still.
Mrs. Eshton había sido sin duda hermosa y aún estaba muy bien conservada.
Of her daughters, the eldest, Amy, was rather little: naive, and child-like in face and manner, and piquant in form; her white muslin dress and blue sash became her well.
La mayor de sus hijas, Amy, era menuda, infantil de rostro y modales y de sugestivas formas.
The second, Louisa, was taller and more elegant in figure; with a very pretty face, of that order the French term _minois chiffone_: both sisters were fair as lilies.
La menor, Louisa era más alta y más elegante de tipo. Tenía una cara bonita, de esas que los franceses llaman minois chiffonné.

Lady Lynn was a large and stout personage of about forty, very erect, very haughty-looking, richly dressed in a satin robe of changeful sheen: her dark hair shone glossily under the shade of an azure plume, and within the circlet of a band of gems.
Representaba unos cuarenta años, erguida y altanera. Vestía un magnífico traje de raso, y su negro cabello estaba adornado con una pluma azul celeste y con una diadema incrustada de joyas.
Mrs. Colonel Dent was less showy; but, I thought, more lady-like.
La esposa del coronel Dent era menos brillante, pero me pareció más señorial.
She had a slight figure, a pale, gentle face, and fair hair.
Su rostro era agradable y pálido y tenía el cabello rubio.
Her black satin dress, her scarf of rich foreign lace, and her pearl ornaments, pleased me better than the rainbow radiance of the titled dame.
Su sobrio vestido de raso negro, con adornos de perlas, me agradó más que la opulencia de la anterior señora.
But the three most distinguished--partly, perhaps, because the tallest figures of the band--were the Dowager Lady Ingram and her daughters, Blanche and Mary.
Pero las más distinguidas entre todas -tal vez porque eran las más altas- resultaban la viuda Lady Ingram y sus hijas Blanche y Mary.
They were all three of the loftiest stature of women.
Para ser mujeres, tenían muy aventajada estatura.
The Dowager might be between forty and fifty: her shape was still fine; her hair (by candle-light at least) still black; her teeth, too, were still apparently perfect.
La viuda debía de contar de cuarenta a cincuenta años. Sus formas se mantenían aún proporcionadas, su cabello todavía negro (al menos a la luz de las bujías) y sus dientes perfectos.

Most people would have termed her a splendid woman of her age: and so she was, no doubt, physically speaking; but then there was an expression of almost insupportable haughtiness in her bearing and countenance.
La mayoría de los hombres hubiesen dicho de ella que era una espléndida mujer madura y, físicamente hablando, sin duda habrían acertado, pero emanaba de su aspecto una altivez casi insoportable.

She had Roman features and a double chin, disappearing into a throat like a pillar: these features appeared to me not only inflated and darkened, but even furrowed with pride; and the chin was sustained by the same principle, in a position of almost preternatural erectness.
Una amplia sotabarba se unía a una garganta robusta como una columna. Sus facciones rebosaban orgullo y su barbilla adoptaba una posición exageradamente erecta.

She had, likewise, a fierce and a hard eye: it reminded me of Mrs. Reed's; she mouthed her words in speaking; her voice was deep, its inflections very pompous, very dogmatical,--very intolerable, in short.
Sus ojos, orgullosos y duros, me recordaban los de mi tía Reed. Hablaba doctoralmente, con un tono de superioridad inaguantable.
A crimson velvet robe, and a shawl turban of some gold-wrought Indian fabric, invested her (I suppose she thought) with a truly imperial dignity.
Un vestido de terciopelo carmesí y un turbante-chal de manufactura india la investía (según imagino que ella se figuraba) de una dignidad casi imperial.
Blanche and Mary were of equal stature,--straight and tall as poplars.
Blanche y Mary eran de la misma estatura: altas y erguidas como álamos.
Mary was too slim for her height, but Blanche was moulded like a Dian.
Mary era demasiado delgada para su altura, pero Blanche, en cambio, tenía los perfectos contornos de una Diana.
I regarded her, of course, with special interest.
La miré con especial interés.

First, I wished to see whether her appearance accorded with Mrs. Fairfax's description; secondly, whether it at all resembled the fancy miniature I had painted of her; and thirdly--it will out!--whether it were such as I should fancy likely to suit Mr. Rochester's taste.
Deseaba ver si su aspecto respondía a la descripción de Mrs. Fairfax, si se asemejaba a la miniatura mía y si respondería al gusto que yo me imaginaba que debía ser el de Mr.

As far as person went, she answered point for point, both to my picture and Mrs. Fairfax's description. The noble bust, the sloping shoulders, the graceful neck, the dark eyes and black ringlets were all there;--but her face?
Su tipo respondía, en efecto, a la descripción del ama de llaves y a mi retrato: torso delicado, hombros bien contorneados, cuello gracioso, negros ojos y negros rizos.
Her face was like her mother's; a youthful unfurrowed likeness: the same low brow, the same high features, the same pride.
Pero su rostro era como el de su madre: idéntico ceño, idénticas facciones altaneras, idéntico orgullo, si bien no era un orgullo tan sombrío.
It was not, however, so saturnine a pride! she laughed continually; her laugh was satirical, and so was the habitual expression of her arched and haughty lip.
Por el contrario, reía continuamente, con una risa desdeñosa que parecía constituir la expresión habitual de sus labios arqueados y altivos.
Genius is said to be self-conscious.
Se asegura que el genio es orgulloso y consciente de sí mismo.
I cannot tell whether Miss Ingram was a genius, but she was self-conscious--remarkably self-conscious indeed.
Yo no. puedo asegurar si Miss Ingram era un genio, pero sí que estaba muy consciente y muy orgullosa de sí misma.
She entered into a discourse on botany with the gentle Mrs. Dent.
Inició una discusión sobre botánica con la gentil señora Dent.
It seemed Mrs. Dent had not studied that science: though, as she said, she liked flowers, "especially wild ones;" Miss Ingram had, and she ran over its vocabulary with an air.
Ésta parecía no haber estudiado semejante ciencia, limitándose a asegurar que le gustaban las flores, «y sobre todo las silvestres».
I presently perceived she was (what is vernacularly termed) _trailing_ Mrs. Dent; that is, playing on her ignorance--her _trail_ might be clever, but it was decidedly not good- natured.
En cambio, Miss Ingram entendía la materia y arrollaba a su interlocutora, gozándose en su ignorancia. Blanche podría ser inteligente, pero no era bondadosa.
She played: her execution was brilliant; she sang: her voice was fine; she talked French apart to her mamma; and she talked it well, with fluency and with a good accent.
Tocaba bien, tenía buena voz, hablaba francés en apartes con su madre, y lo hablaba excelentemente, con mucha naturalidad y apropiado acento.

Mary had a milder and more open countenance than Blanche; softer features too, and a skin some shades fairer (Miss Ingram was dark as a Spaniard)--but Mary was deficient in life: her face lacked expression, her eye lustre; she had nothing to say, and having once taken her seat, remained fixed like a statue in its niche.

Mary parecía ser más amable y sencilla que Blanche, así como era más suave de facciones y más blanca de tez (su hermana era morena como una española). Pero su rostro carecía de expresión y sus ojos de brillo.
The sisters were both attired in spotless white.
Una vez sentada, permanecía inmóvil como una estatua en su pedestal.
And did I now think Miss Ingram such a choice as Mr. Rochester would be likely to make?
Las dos hermanas vestían ropas blancas como la nieve. ¿Gustaría Blanche a Mr.
I could not tell--I did not know his taste in female beauty.
Yo no conocía su opinión en materia de belleza femenina.
If he liked the majestic, she was the very type of majesty: then she was accomplished, sprightly.
Si le agradaba lo majestuoso, necesariamente debía de agradarle Miss Ingram.
Most gentlemen would admire her, I thought; and that he _did_ admire her, I already seemed to have obtained proof: to remove the last shade of doubt, it remained but to see them together.
La mayoría de los hombres debían de admirar a Blanche, y de que él la admiraba también parecíame tener evidentes pruebas. Para disipar la última sombra de duda me faltaba verles juntos.

You are not to suppose, reader, that Adele has all this time been sitting motionless on the stool at my feet: no; when the ladies entered, she rose, advanced to meet them, made a stately reverence, and said with gravity-- "Bon jour, mesdames."
Ya habrás supuesto, lector, que Adèle no permaneció quieta ni muda. En cuanto entraron las señoras, avanzó hacia ellas, hizo una solemne reverencia y dijo con gravedad: -Buenas noches, señoras.
And Miss Ingram had looked down at her with a mocking air, and exclaimed, "Oh, what a little puppet!"
Miss Ingram la miró burlonamente y exclamó: -¡Uy, qué muñequita!
Lady Lynn had remarked, "It is Mr. Rochester's ward, I suppose--the little French girl he was speaking of."
Lady Lynn observó: -Debe de ser la niña que tiene a su cargo Mr. Rochester.
Mrs. Dent had kindly taken her hand, and given her a kiss.
Mrs. Dent tomó a Adèle por la mano y la dio un beso.
Amy and Louisa Eshton had cried out simultaneously--"What a love of a child!"
Amy y Louisa Eshton gritaron a la vez: -¡Qué encanto de niña!

And then they had called her to a sofa, where she now sat, ensconced between them, chattering alternately in French and broken English; absorbing not only the young ladies' attention, but that of Mrs. Eshton and Lady Lynn, and getting spoilt to her heart's content.

Y la llevaron a un sofá, donde la pequeña se sentó, charlando alternadamente en francés y en inglés chapurreado y atrayendo no sólo la atención de las jóvenes, sino también la de Lady Lynn y Mrs. Eshton.
At last coffee is brought in, and the gentlemen are summoned.
Fue servido el café y se llamó a los hombres.
I sit in the shade--if any shade there be in this brilliantly-lit apartment; the window-curtain half hides me. Again the arch yawns; they come.
Me senté a la relativa sombra de las cortinas de las ventanas, que me ocultaban a medias. La aparición en grupo de los caballeros fue tan imponente como la de las señoras.
The collective appearance of the gentlemen, like that of the ladies, is very imposing: they are all costumed in black; most of them are tall, some young.
Todos vestían de negro. La mayoría eran altos, y algunos muy jóvenes.
Henry and Frederick Lynn are very dashing sparks indeed; and Colonel Dent is a fine soldierly man.
Henry y Frederick Lynn eran dos muchachos elegantes, y el coronel Dent un hombre de aspecto marcial. Mr.
Mr. Eshton, the magistrate of the district, is gentleman-like: his hair is quite white, his eyebrows and whiskers still dark, which gives him something of the appearance of a "pere noble de theatre."
Eshton, magistrado del distrito, tenía un aspecto muy señorial. Sus cabellos, completamente blancos, y sus cejas y patillas, negras aún, le daban la apariencia de un pére noble de théàtre.

Lord Ingram, like his sisters, is very tall; like them, also, he is handsome; but he shares Mary's apathetic and listless look: he seems to have more length of limb than vivacity of blood or vigour of brain.

Lord Ingram, como sus hermanas, era muy alto y, como ellas, muy arrogante, mas parecía tener algo de la apatía de su hermana Mary, denotando más vigor muscular que ardor de sangre o vivacidad de mente.
He comes in last: I am not looking at the arch, yet I see him enter.
Mr. Rochester entró el último.

I try to concentrate my attention on those netting-needles, on the meshes of the purse I am forming--I wish to think only of the work I have in my hands, to see only the silver beads and silk threads that lie in my lap; whereas, I distinctly behold his figure, and I inevitably recall the moment when I last saw it; just after I had rendered him, what he deemed, an essential service, and he, holding my hand, and looking down on my face, surveyed me with eyes that revealed a heart full and eager to overflow; in whose emotions I had a part.

Al distinguir la figura de aquel hombre, recordé el momento en que le viera por última vez, cuando le acababa de prestar un inestimable servicio. Entonces él, cogiendo mi mano y mirándome, había revelado una tumultuosa emoción, de la que yo había participado.
How near had I approached him at that moment!
¡Qué próximo a él me había sentido en aquel momento!
What had occurred since, calculated to change his and my relative positions?
Ahora, en cambio, ¡qué lejanos estábamos el uno del otro!
Yet now, how distant, how far estranged we were!
Tanto, que ni siquiera esperaba que viniese a hablarme.

So far estranged, that I did not expect him to come and speak to me. I did not wonder, when, without looking at me, he took a seat at the other side of the room, and began conversing with some of the ladies.
No me asombró, pues, que sin mirarme, se sentara al otro extremo del salón y comenzase a conversar con algunas señoras.

No sooner did I see that his attention was riveted on them, and that I might gaze without being observed, than my eyes were drawn involuntarily to his face; I could not keep their lids under control: they would rise, and the irids would fix on him. I looked, and had an acute pleasure in looking,--a precious yet poignant pleasure; pure gold, with a steely point of agony: a pleasure like what the thirst-perishing man might feel who knows the well to which he has crept is poisoned, yet stoops and drinks divine draughts nevertheless.

Al observar que su atención estaba dedicada a ellas y que podía, por tanto, mirarle sin ser vista, le contemplé, experimentando un agudo y a la vez doloroso placer en hacerlo: el placer que pueda experimentar quien, sintiéndose envenenado, bebe, a sabiendas, el dulce veneno que le lleva a la tumba.
Most true is it that "beauty is in the eye of the gazer."
¡Qué verdadero es el aforismo de que «la belleza está en los ojos del que mira»!

My master's colourless, olive face, square, massive brow, broad and jetty eyebrows, deep eyes, strong features, firm, grim mouth,--all energy, decision, will,--were not beautiful, according to rule; but they were more than beautiful to me; they were full of an interest, an influence that quite mastered me,--that took my feelings from my own power and fettered them in his.

El moreno y cuadrado rostro de Rochester, sus espesas cejas, sus penetrantes ojos, sus rudas facciones, su boca voluntariosa, no eran bellos, según los cánones de la estética, pero para mí eran más que bellos: eran interesantes y estaban llenos de una sugestión que me dominaba.

I had not intended to love him; the reader knows I had wrought hard to extirpate from my soul the germs of love there detected; and now, at the first renewed view of him, they spontaneously arrived, green and strong!
Yo deseaba no amarle -el lector sabe el esfuerzo que realicé para extirpar mi amor- y, sin embargo, ahora que le veía, la pasión desbordaba, impetuosa y fuerte.
He made me love him without looking at me.
Aun sin mirarme, me obligaba a que le amase.
I compared him with his guests.
Le comparé con sus invitados.
What was the gallant grace of the Lynns, the languid elegance of Lord Ingram,--even the military distinction of Colonel Dent, contrasted with his look of native pith and genuine power?
¿Qué valían la gallarda gracia de los Lynn, la lánguida elegancia de Lord Ingram, la marcial distinción del coronel Dent, ante la energía innata que emanaba de Rochester?

I had no sympathy in their appearance, their expression: yet I could imagine that most observers would call them attractive, handsome, imposing; while they would pronounce Mr. Rochester at once harsh-featured and melancholy-looking.

En el aspecto de aquellos no veía nada sugestivo para mí, aun reconociendo que la mayoría de las gentes les hubieran considerado atractivos, elegantes y distinguidos, mientras que de Mr. Rochester hubiesen dicho que estaba mal formado y que tenía un aire sombrío.
I saw them smile, laugh--it was nothing; the light of the candles had as much soul in it as their smile; the tinkle of the bell as much significance as their laugh.
Pero yo, viendo sonreír y reír a los otros, pensaba que sus sonrisas no eran más brillantes que la llama de una bujía, ni sus risas más sonoras que el ruido de una campanilla.
I saw Mr. Rochester smile:--his stern features softened; his eye grew both brilliant and gentle, its ray both searching and sweet.
En cambio, cuando Rochester sonreía, sus duras facciones se suavizaban y sus ojos brillaban con destellos a la vez acerados y dulces.
He was talking, at the moment, to Louisa and Amy Eshton.
En aquel momento hablaba a Louisa y Amy Eshton, y a mí me maravillaba ver la ecuanimidad con que ellas oían lo que a mí me parecía tan interesante.

I wondered to see them receive with calm that look which seemed to me so penetrating: I expected their eyes to fall, their colour to rise under it; yet I was glad when I found they were in no sense moved.
Me alegré al ver que no entornaban los ojos ni se ruborizaban escuchándole. «No es para ellas lo que para mí -pensé-.
"He is not to them what he is to me," I thought: "he is not of their kind.
Él no es del corte de ellas, sino del mío.

I believe he is of mine;--I am sure he is--I feel akin to him--I understand the language of his countenance and movements: though rank and wealth sever us widely, I have something in my brain and heart, in my blood and nerves, that assimilates me mentally to him.
Yo comprendo la elocuencia de sus movimientos y de su rostro. Aunque otras causas nos separen, en mi cerebro y en mi corazón, en mi sangre y en mis nervios hay alguna cosa que me hace semejante a él.
Did I say, a few days since, that I had nothing to do with him but to receive my salary at his hands? Did I forbid myself to think of him in any other light than as a paymaster?
¿Cómo he podido imaginar, hace pocos días, que nada teníamos que ver los dos, sino a efectos de salario, y que no podía considerarle desde otro punto de vista que el de ser mi patrón?
Blasphemy against nature!
¡Qué blasfemia contra la naturaleza!
Every good, true, vigorous feeling I have gathers impulsively round him.
Cuanto hay de bueno, de sincero y de vigoroso en mí, gira impulsivamente en torno de él.
I know I must conceal my sentiments: I must smother hope; I must remember that he cannot care much for me.
Reconozco que debo ocultar mis sentimientos y que él no se preocupa de mí para nada.
For when I say that I am of his kind, I do not mean that I have his force to influence, and his spell to attract; I mean only that I have certain tastes and feelings in common with him.
Cuando digo que soy como él, no quiero decir que posea su poder de sugestión, ni su atractivo, sino sólo que tengo sentimientos e inclinaciones iguales a las suyas.
I must, then, repeat continually that we are for ever sundered:--and yet, while I breathe and think, I must love him."
Sé que hemos de vivir siempre distantes y, sin embargo, mientras yo sienta y aliente, le amaré.»
Coffee is handed.
Se tomó el café.
The ladies, since the gentlemen entered, have become lively as larks; conversation waxes brisk and merry.
Las mujeres, desde que entraron los caballeros, se habían vuelto repentinamente animadas y vivas como alondras. La conversación era alegre.
Colonel Dent and Mr. Eshton argue on politics; their wives listen.
Dent y Eshton hablaban de política, y sus mujeres les escuchaban.

The two proud dowagers, Lady Lynn and Lady Ingram, confabulate together. Sir George--whom, by-the-bye, I have forgotten to describe,--a very big, and very fresh-looking country gentleman, stands before their sofa, coffee- cup in hand, and occasionally puts in a word.

Sir George -a quien he omitido describir y que era un robusto y corpulento caballero campesino- se colocó ante el sofá de aquellos con su taza de café en la mano, y de vez en cuando intercalaba alguna palabra.
Mr. Frederick Lynn has taken a seat beside Mary Ingram, and is showing her the engravings of a splendid volume: she looks, smiles now and then, but apparently says little.
Frederick Lynn se había sentado junto a Mary Ingram y le enseñaba los grabados de un magnífico libro. Ella miraba y sonreía, pero apenas decía nada.

The tall and phlegmatic Lord Ingram leans with folded arms on the chair-back of the little and lively Amy Eshton; she glances up at him, and chatters like a wren: she likes him better than she does Mr. Rochester.
El alto y flemático Lord Ingram había apoyado los brazos en el respaldo de la silla de la menuda y vivaracha Amy Eshton, que le miraba gorjeando como un pájaro. Sin duda le gustaba más que Rochester.
Henry Lynn has taken possession of an ottoman at the feet of Louisa: Adele shares it with him: he is trying to talk French with her, and Louisa laughs at his blunders.
Henry Lynn había tomado posesión de una otomana junto a Louisa, Adèle estaba a su lado y él trataba de conversar en francés con la niña, mientras Louisa se burlaba de los disparates que decía.
With whom will Blanche Ingram pair? She is standing alone at the table, bending gracefully over an album.
En cuanto a Blanche Ingram, se había sentado, sola, a una mesa, y permanecía graciosamente inclinada sobre un álbum.
She seems waiting to be sought; but she will not wait too long: she herself selects a mate.
Parecía esperar que alguien le hiciese compañía, y no esperó largo rato, porque ella misma eligió un compañero.
Mr. Rochester, having quitted the Eshtons, stands on the hearth as solitary as she stands by the table: she confronts him, taking her station on the opposite side of the mantelpiece.

Rochester, dejando a las Eshton, se sentó ante el fuego, donde quedó por unos instantes tan solitario como la Ingram ante la mesa. Blanche lo notó y se acercó a él, colocándose también junto a la chimenea.
"Mr. Rochester, I thought you were not fond of children?"
-Yo creía, Mr. Rochester, que no le gustaban los niños.
"Nor am I."
-Y no me gustan.
"Then, what induced you to take charge of such a little doll as that?" (pointing to Adele). "Where did you pick her up?"
-Entonces, ¿por qué se ha encargado de esa muñequita? - dijo, señalando a Adèle-.
"I did not pick her up; she was left on my hands." "You should have sent her to school."
¿De dónde la ha sacado usted? -No la saqué de sitio alguno: me la confiaron. -Debía usted enviarla al colegio.
"I could not afford it: schools are so dear."
-Los colegios son caros.
"Why, I suppose you have a governess for her: I saw a person with her just now--is she gone?
-Bien, pero usted tiene una institutriz para la niña, según he visto... ¿Se ha ido ya?
Oh, no! there she is still, behind the window- curtain.
No; está allí, junto a la ventana.
You pay her, of course; I should think it quite as expensive,--more so; for you have them both to keep in addition."
Usted tiene que pagarla y eso le resulta más caro aún, porque, además de pagar a esa mujer, necesita mantenerla.
I feared--or should I say, hoped?--the allusion to me would make Mr. Rochester glance my way; and I involuntarily shrank farther into the shade: but he never turned his eyes.
Yo temía -mejor sería decir esperaba- que la alusión motivase que Mr. Rochester me dirigiera una mirada, pero no lo hizo.
"I have not considered the subject," said he indifferently, looking straight before him. "No, you men never do consider economy and common sense.
-No me he parado a pensarlo -dijo él con indiferencia. -Ustedes, los hombres, nunca tienen en cuenta la economía ni el sentido común.

You should hear mama on the chapter of governesses: Mary and I have had, I should think, a dozen at least in our day; half of them detestable and the rest ridiculous, and all incubi--were they not, mama?"
Mary y yo hemos tenido lo menos una docena durante nuestra vida. La mitad eran odiosas y la otra mitad ridículas, y todas resultaban muy gravosas.
"Did you speak, my own?"
-¿Qué me decías?
The young lady thus claimed as the dowager's special property, reiterated her question with an explanation.
La joven explicó con detalle su pregunta.
"My dearest, don't mention governesses; the word makes me nervous.
-Querida: ¡no me hables de institutrices! Sólo oír esa palabra me pone nerviosa.
I have suffered a martyrdom from their incompetency and caprice.
He sido mártir de su incapacidad y de sus caprichos.
I thank Heaven I have now done with them!"
¡Gracias a Dios que ya no tengo que tratar con ellas!
Mrs. Dent here bent over to the pious lady and whispered something in her ear; I suppose, from the answer elicited, it was a reminder that one of the anathematised race was present.
Dent se acercó a la viuda y le habló al oído. Supongo, juzgando por la respuesta, que se trataba de una indicación de que un miembro de aquella aborrecida raza se hallaba presente.
"Tant pis!" said her Ladyship, "I hope it may do her good!"
-Tant pis! -exclamó la viuda-.
Then, in a lower tone, but still loud enough for me to hear, "I noticed her; I am a judge of physiognomy, and in hers I see all the faults of her class."

Confío en que ello contribuya a hacerla mejor que las otras -y agregó, más bajo, aunque lo bastante alto para que yo la oyese-: Ya lo había notado. Soy muy buena fisonomista, y reconozco en ella todos los defectos de las de su clase.
"What are they, madam?" inquired Mr. Rochester aloud.
-¿Qué defectos son esos? -inquirió Rochester.
"I will tell you in your private ear," replied she, wagging her turban three times with portentous significancy.
-Se lo diré a solas -repuso la señora, moviendo significativamente su turbante.
"But my curiosity will be past its appetite; it craves food now."
-Pero entonces mi despierta curiosidad quizá se haya dormido...
"Ask Blanche; she is nearer you than I."
-Pregunte a Blanche, que está más cerca de usted que yo.
"Oh, don't refer him to me, mama!
-Podías dejarme tranquila, mamá.
I have just one word to say of the whole tribe; they are a nuisance.
Sólo una palabra tengo que decir respecto a esa tribu: que son unas fastidiosas.
Not that I ever suffered much from them; I took care to turn the tables.
No es que yo las haya tolerado mucho.
What tricks Theodore and I used to play on our Miss Wilsons, and Mrs. Greys, and Madame Jouberts!
¡La de burlas que hemos hecho Theodore y yo a nuestra Miss Wilson, y a nuestra Mrs. Greys, y a nuestra Madame Joubert!
Mary was always too sleepy to join in a plot with spirit.
Mary no solía estar lo bastante animada para colaborar en nuestras tretas.

The best fun was with Madame Joubert: Miss Wilson was a poor sickly thing, lachrymose and low- spirited, not worth the trouble of vanquishing, in short; and Mrs. Grey was coarse and insensible; no blow took effect on her.

Las mejores fueron las que gastamos a Madame Joubert, porque Miss Wilson era una infeliz apocada, siempre llorosa, que no merecía ni el trabajo de burlarse de ella, y Mrs. Greys era tan insensible que ningún golpe la afectaba.
But poor Madame Joubert!
¡Pero a la pobre Madame Joubert!

I see her yet in her raging passions, when we had driven her to extremities--spilt our tea, crumbled our bread and butter, tossed our books up to the ceiling, and played a charivari with the ruler and desk, the fender and fire-irons.

Aún me parece verla, enfurecida cuando derramábamos el té, manoseábamos el pan, tirábamos los libros y armábamos una charanga golpeando la regla sobre el pupitre y la badila, en el cierre de la chimenea...
Theodore, do you remember those merry days?"
¿Recuerdas aquellos felices días, Theodore?

"Yaas, to be sure I do," drawled Lord Ingram; "and the poor old stick used to cry out 'Oh you villains childs!'--and then we sermonised her on the presumption of attempting to teach such clever blades as we were, when she was herself so ignorant."

-¡Ya lo creo! -repuso Lord Ingram-. La pobre vieja gritaba: «¡Niños malos!», y nos sermoneaba creyendo impresionarnos a nosotros, que éramos unos muchachos inteligentes, mientras que ella era una ignorante.
"We did; and, Tedo, you know, I helped you in prosecuting (or persecuting) your tutor, whey-faced Mr. Vining--the parson in the pip, as we used to call him.
-¿Y te acuerdas, Theodore, de cuando yo te ayudaba a mortificar a tu preceptor, Mr. Vining, a quien solíamos poner apodos tan grotescos?

He and Miss Wilson took the liberty of falling in love with each other--at least Tedo and I thought so; we surprised sundry tender glances and sighs which we interpreted as tokens of 'la belle passion,' and I promise you the public soon had the benefit of our discovery; we employed it as a sort of lever to hoist our dead-weights from the house.

Él y Miss Wilson se permitieron enamorarse, o al menos Theodore y yo nos lo figuramos. Les sorprendimos miradas tiernas y suspiros, que interpretábamos como muestras de una belle passion, y yo te aseguré que en breve la noticia sería del dominio público.
Dear mama, there, as soon as she got an inkling of the business, found out that it was of an immoral tendency.
Mamá, en cuanto se informó del asunto, encontró que era una inmoralidad.
Did you not, my lady-mother?"
¿No es cierto, madrecita?
"Certainly, my best.
-Sí, querida.
And I was quite right: depend on that: there are a thousand reasons why liaisons between governesses and tutors should never be tolerated a moment in any well-regulated house; firstly--"
Y lo pensaba con razón. Existen muchos motivos para que no pueda tolerarse una relación amorosa entre una institutriz y un preceptor en una casa bien organizada; en primer lugar, porque...

"Oh, gracious, mama! Spare us the enumeration! _Au reste_, we all know them: danger of bad example to innocence of childhood; distractions and consequent neglect of duty on the part of the attached--mutual alliance and reliance; confidence thence resulting--insolence accompanying--mutiny and general blow-up.

-¡Por Dios, mamá, ahórranos la exposición de los motivos! Au reste, todos los conocemos: peligro de dar malos ejemplos a los inocentes niños, distracción y negligencia en el desempeño de los cargos, alianza tácita entre ambos profesores y, como consecuencia, actitudes insolentes y subversivas...
Am I right, Baroness Ingram, of Ingram Park?" "My lily-flower, you are right now, as always."
¿Tengo razón o no, señora baronesa de Ingram? -Tienes razón como siempre, florecita mía. -Entonces no hay más que hablar.
"Then no more need be said: change the subject."
Cambiemos de conversación.

Amy Eshton, not hearing or not heeding this dictum, joined in with her soft, infantine tone: "Louisa and I used to quiz our governess too; but she was such a good creature, she would bear anything: nothing put her out.
Amy Eshton no oyó esta última frase, e insistió en el tema, diciendo con su dulce tono infantil: -Louisa y yo solíamos burlarnos de nuestra institutriz, pero era tan buena que no se ofendía nunca.
She was never cross with us; was she, Louisa?"
¿Verdad que no, Louisa?
"No, never: we might do what we pleased; ransack her desk and her workbox, and turn her drawers inside out; and she was so good-natured, she would give us anything we asked for."
Nos dejaba hacer lo que queríamos: registrar su pupitre, revolver su cesto de labor y sus cajones... Era muy condescendiente y nos concedía cuanto le pedíamos.

"I suppose, now," said Miss Ingram, curling her lip sarcastically, "we shall have an abstract of the memoirs of all the governesses extant: in order to avert such a visitation, I again move the introduction of a new topic.
-Creo -dijo Miss Ingram, plegando los labios irónicamente- que hemos tratado ya bastante ese tema, y que deberíamos pasar a uno nuevo.
Mr. Rochester, do you second my motion?"
¿Apoya usted mi proposición, Mr. Rochester?
"Madam, I support you on this point, as on every other."
-Coincido con usted en eso y en todo.
"Then on me be the onus of bringing it forward.
-Entonces, yo me encargaré de elegir otra distracción.
Signior Eduardo, are you in voice to-night?"
¿Está usted en voz esta noche, Mr.
"Donna Bianca, if you command it, I will be."
Edward? -Lo estaré si usted lo manda, doña Bianca.
"Then, signior, I lay on you my sovereign behest to furbish up your lungs and other vocal organs, as they will be wanted on my royal service."
-Entonces, mi soberano deseo es que usted ponga sus órganos vocales a mi real servicio.
Miss Ingram, who had now seated herself with proud grace at the piano, spreading out her snowy robes in queenly amplitude, commenced a brilliant prelude; talking meantime.
Miss Ingram se sentó al piano con altanera gracia, ahuecó su níveo vestido hasta darle una majestuosa amplitud, y comenzó un brillante preludio.

She appeared to be on her high horse to-night; both her words and her air seemed intended to excite not only the admiration, but the amazement of her auditors: she was evidently bent on striking them as something very dashing and daring indeed.

Aquella noche parecía estar en su mejor forma, y tanto sus palabras como su aspecto suscitaban no sólo la admiración, sino incluso el éxtasis de los que la oían. Mientras tocaba, hablaba de esta suerte:
"Oh, I am so sick of the young men of the present day!" exclaimed she, rattling away at the instrument.
-Estoy harta de los jóvenes de hoy día.
"Poor, puny things, not fit to stir a step beyond papa's park gates: nor to go even so far without mama's permission and guardianship!
Parecen niños: no pueden salir del jardín sin permiso de papá, de mamá y del aya.
Creatures so absorbed in care about their pretty faces, and their white hands, and their small feet; as if a man had anything to do with beauty!
No piensan más que en cuidar sus bonitos rostros, sus blancas manos y sus pequeños pies... ¡Como si el hombre tuviese que preocuparse de la belleza!
As if loveliness were not the special prerogative of woman--her legitimate appanage and heritage!
¡Como si la hermosura no fuese cosa exclusiva de la mujer!

I grant an ugly _woman_ is a blot on the fair face of creation; but as to the _gentlemen_, let them be solicitous to possess only strength and valour: let their motto be:--Hunt, shoot, and fight: the rest is not worth a fillip.
Yo opino que una mujer fea es una mácula de la creación, pero un caballero no debe pensar sino en parecer fuerte y valeroso. Su lema debe ser: cazar, esgrimir y luchar.
Such should be my device, were I a man."
El resto no merece la pena.
"Whenever I marry," she continued after a pause which none interrupted, "I am resolved my husband shall not be a rival, but a foil to me.
Así opinaría yo si fuera hombre. Hizo una pausa, que todos respetaron, y continuó: -Yo aspiro a casarme no con un rival, sino con un rendido.
I will suffer no competitor near the throne; I shall exact an undivided homage: his devotions shall not be shared between me and the shape he sees in his mirror.
Yo no sufriría un competidor; exigiría de mi marido un homenaje exclusivo, no una devoción compartida entre mi persona y la imagen que él viera en su espejo...
Mr. Rochester, now sing, and I will play for you."
Vamos, Mr. Rochester: cante, y yo le acompañaré al piano.
"I am all obedience," was the response.
-Estoy dispuesto a obedecer.
"Here then is a Corsair-song.
-Aquí hay una canción pirata.
Know that I doat on Corsairs; and for that reason, sing it _con spirito_."
¡Me muero por los piratas! Cante, pues, con spirito.
"Commands from Miss Ingram's lips would put spirit into a mug of milk and water."
-Las órdenes de sus labios infundirían espíritu hasta a un vaso de leche aguada. -Bien.
"Take care, then: if you don't please me, I will shame you by showing how such things _should_ be done."
Pero ándese con cuidado. Si no canta como debe, le humillaré mostrándole cómo hay que entonar esta canción.
"That is offering a premium on incapacity: I shall now endeavour to fail."
-Eso es ofrecer un premio a la incapacidad. Ahora procuraré hacerlo mal adrede...
"Gardez-vous en bien!
-Gardez-vous en bien!
If you err wilfully, I shall devise a proportionate punishment."
Si usted lo hace mal a propósito, le castigaré.
"Miss Ingram ought to be clement, for she has it in her power to inflict a chastisement beyond mortal endurance."
-Debe usted ser piadosa, ya que tiene en su mano aplicar un castigo mayor del que un mortal pueda soportar. -Explíquese -dijo ella.
"Ha! explain!" commanded the lady.
-Es superflua la explicación.
"Pardon me, madam: no need of explanation; your own fine sense must inform you that one of your frowns would be a sufficient substitute for capital punishment."
Usted sabe muy bien que un simple enojo suyo es más doloroso que el mayor de los castigos.
"Sing!" said she, and again touching the piano, she commenced an accompaniment in spirited style.
-Vamos, cante... -repuso ella. Y comenzó a acompañarle al piano, tocando con exquisito gusto.
"Now is my time to slip away," thought I: but the tones that then severed the air arrested me.
«Éste es el momento de irme», pensé. Pero las notas de la canción me emocionaron tanto, que no me decidí.

Mrs. Fairfax had said Mr. Rochester possessed a fine voice: he did--a mellow, powerful bass, into which he threw his own feeling, his own force; finding a way through the ear to the heart, and there waking sensation strangely.
Rochester tenía una bella voz, y era cierto. Poseía una potente voz de bajo, a la que comunicaba todo su sentimiento, toda su energía personal.

I waited till the last deep and full vibration had expired--till the tide of talk, checked an instant, had resumed its flow; I then quitted my sheltered corner and made my exit by the side-door, which was fortunately near.
Su acento penetraba hasta lo último. Esperé a que la última nota de aquella canción expirase, y luego inicié mi retirada hacia la puerta de escape, que afortunadamente estaba próxima.
Thence a narrow passage led into the hall: in crossing it, I perceived my sandal was loose; I stopped to tie it, kneeling down for that purpose on the mat at the foot of the staircase.
Un estrecho pasillo conducía desde ella al vestíbulo. Al atravesarlo, reparé que había perdido una de mis sandalias y, para buscarla, me arrodillé al pie de la escalera.
I heard the dining-room door unclose; a gentleman came out; rising hastily, I stood face to face with him: it was Mr. Rochester.
Oí abrir la puerta del comedor. Me apresuré a incorporarme y me hallé cara a cara con Mr.
"How do you do?" he asked. "I am very well, sir."
Rochester. -¿Cómo está usted? -me preguntó. -Muy bien, señor.
"Why did you not come and speak to me in the room?"
-¿Por qué no me ha dirigido la palabra en el salón?
I thought I might have retorted the question on him who put it: but I would not take that freedom.
Yo pensaba que lo mismo podía preguntarse a él, pero no me tomé tal liberad y repuse:
I answered-- "I did not wish to disturb you, as you seemed engaged, sir."
-No deseaba molestarle viéndole entretenido, señor.
"What have you been doing during my absence?"
-¿Qué ha hecho usted durante mi ausencia?
"Nothing particular; teaching Adele as usual."
-Nada de particular: enseñar a Adèle como siempre.
"And getting a good deal paler than you were--as I saw at first sight.
-Y palidecer mucho, de paso. Está tan pálida como la primera vez que la vi.
What is the matter?"
¿Qué le ocurre?
"Nothing at all, sir."
-Nada, señor.
"Did you take any cold that night you half drowned me?"
-¿Acaso se acatarró usted la noche que estuvo a punto de ahogarme?
"Not the least."
-Nada de eso.
"Return to the drawing-room: you are deserting too early."
-Vuelva al salón. Es muy pronto.
"I am tired, sir."
-Estoy cansada, señor.
He looked at me for a minute.
Me miró un instante.
"And a little depressed," he said.
-Sí, ya lo veo.
"What about?
Y también un poco deprimida.
Tell me."
¿Qué le sucede?
"Nothing--nothing, sir.
-Nada, señor, nada.
I am not depressed."
No estoy deprimida.

"But I affirm that you are: so much depressed that a few more words would bring tears to your eyes--indeed, they are there now, shining and swimming; and a bead has slipped from the lash and fallen on to the flag.
-Lo está usted hasta el punto de que si hablásemos algunas palabras más, rompería usted a llorar...

If I had time, and was not in mortal dread of some prating prig of a servant passing, I would know what all this means. Well, to-night I excuse you; but understand that so long as my visitors stay, I expect you to appear in the drawing-room every evening; it is my wish; don't neglect it.
En fin, por esta noche la dispenso, pero es mi deseo que todas las noches acuda al salón.
Now go, and send Sophie for Adele.
Retírese y envíe a Sophie a buscar a Adèle.
Good-night, my--" He stopped, bit his lip, and abruptly left me.
Buenas noches, queri... Se interrumpió, apretó los labios y se fue bruscamente.
Merry days were these at Thornfield Hall; and busy days too: how different from the first three months of stillness, monotony, and solitude I had passed beneath its roof!
Los días en Thornfield Hall transcurrían bulliciosos y alegres. ¡Qué diferentes eran de los primeros tres meses de soledad y monotonía que yo pasara bajo aquel techo!
All sad feelings seemed now driven from the house, all gloomy associations forgotten: there was life everywhere, movement all day long.
Todas las impresiones tristes parecían haber huido de la casa, todas las ideas sombrías parecían haberse olvidado.
You could not now traverse the gallery, once so hushed, nor enter the front chambers, once so tenantless, without encountering a smart lady's-maid or a dandy valet.
Era imposible atravesar la galería, antes siempre desierta, sin encontrar la elegante doncella de una de las señoras o el presumido criado de uno de los caballeros.

The kitchen, the butler's pantry, the servants' hall, the entrance hall, were equally alive; and the saloons were only left void and still when the blue sky and halcyon sunshine of the genial spring weather called their occupants out into the grounds.

La cocina, la despensa, el cuarto de estar de los criados, el vestíbulo, se hallaban siempre animados, y los aposentos no quedaban vacíos más que cuando el cielo azul y el sol brillante invitaban a pasear a los huéspedes de la casa.

Even when that weather was broken, and continuous rain set in for some days, no damp seemed cast over enjoyment: indoor amusements only became more lively and varied, in consequence of the stop put to outdoor gaiety.

Cuando el tiempo cambió y se sucedieron días de continua lluvia, la jovialidad general no disminuyó por eso. Los entretenimientos de puertas adentro se intensificaron al disiparse la posibilidad de divertirse fuera.
I wondered what they were going to do the first evening a change of entertainment was proposed: they spoke of "playing charades," but in my ignorance I did not understand the term.
Yo ignoraba el significado de la frase «jugar a las adivinanzas» que oí sugerir una tarde a alguien que deseaba cambiar las distracciones habituales.
The servants were called in, the dining-room tables wheeled away, the lights otherwise disposed, the chairs placed in a semicircle opposite the arch.
Se llamó a los criados, se separaron las mesas del comedor, las luces se colocaron de otra forma y las sillas se situaron en semicírculo. Mientras Mr.
While Mr. Rochester and the other gentlemen directed these alterations, the ladies were running up and down stairs ringing for their maids.
Rochester y los demás caballeros dirigían estos arreglos, las damas corrían de un lado a otro llamando a sus doncellas.

Mrs. Fairfax was summoned to give information respecting the resources of the house in shawls, dresses, draperies of any kind; and certain wardrobes of the third storey were ransacked, and their contents, in the shape of brocaded and hooped petticoats, satin sacques, black modes, lace lappets, &c., were brought down in armfuls by the abigails; then a selection was made, and such things as were chosen were carried to the boudoir within the drawing-room.

Fairfax y se la interrogó sobre las existencias de chales, vestidos o telas de cualquier clase que se hallasen en la casa. Se registró el tercer piso y las doncellas bajaron con brazadas de viejos brocados, faldas, lazos y toda clase de antiguas telas.
Meantime, Mr. Rochester had again summoned the ladies round him, and was selecting certain of their number to be of his party.
Entretanto, Mr. Rochester reunió a las señoras a su alrededor y eligió cierto número de ellas y de caballeros.
"Miss Ingram is mine, of course," said he: afterwards he named the two Misses Eshton, and Mrs. Dent.
-Miss Ingram me pertenece, desde luego -dijo. Después nombró a las señoritas Eshton y a Mrs.
He looked at me: I happened to be near him, as I had been fastening the clasp of Mrs. Dent's bracelet, which had got loose.
Yo estaba cerca de él, ayudando a Mrs. Dent a sujetar un broche que se le había soltado. -¿Quiere usted jugar? -me preguntó Rochester.
"Will you play?" he asked.
Denegué con la cabeza y él no insistió.
I shook my head. He did not insist, which I rather feared he would have done; he allowed me to return quietly to my usual seat.
Satisfecha de haber obrado con acierto, volví tranquilamente a mi rincón. Rochester y sus auxiliares se retiraron más allá de la cortina.
He and his aids now withdrew behind the curtain: the other party, which was headed by Colonel Dent, sat down on the crescent of chairs.
Dent y los suyos se acomodaron en el grupo de sillas colocadas en forma de media luna. Uno de los caballeros, Mr.
One of the gentlemen, Mr. Eshton, observing me, seemed to propose that I should be asked to join them; but Lady Ingram instantly negatived the notion.
Eshton, cuchicheó al oído de los demás. Debía proponer que se me invitara a unirme a ellos, porque oí decir instantáneamente a Lady Ingram:
"No," I heard her say: "she looks too stupid for any game of the sort."
-No. Me parece que es lo bastante estúpida para no saber jugar a nada.
Ere long a bell tinkled, and the curtain drew up.
Sonó una campanilla y se corrió la cortina.

Within the arch, the bulky figure of Sir George Lynn, whom Mr. Rochester had likewise chosen, was seen enveloped in a white sheet: before him, on a table, lay open a large book; and at his side stood Amy Eshton, draped in Mr. Rochester's cloak, and holding a book in her hand.

Bajo la arcada apareció la corpulenta figura de Sir George Lynn envuelto en una sábana blanca. Ante él, en una mesa, había un libro grande, abierto, y a su lado se vía a Amy Eshton, vestida con un abrigo de Mr.

Somebody, unseen, rang the bell merrily; then Adele (who had insisted on being one of her guardian's party), bounded forward, scattering round her the contents of a basket of flowers she carried on her arm.

Alguien a quien no veíamos tocó otra vez la campanilla, y Adèle, que había insistido en ayudar a su protector, apareció esparciendo en su torno el contenido de una cesta de flores que llevaba al brazo.

Then appeared the magnificent figure of Miss Ingram, clad in white, a long veil on her head, and a wreath of roses round her brow; by her side walked Mr. Rochester, and together they drew near the table.
En seguida surgió la majestuosa figura de Miss Ingram, vestida de blanco, con un largo velo y una guirnalda de rosas en torno a la frente. Mr.
They knelt; while Mrs. Dent and Louisa Eshton, dressed also in white, took up their stations behind them.
Ambos avanzaron hasta la mesa y se arrodillaron, mientras Mrs. Dent y Louisa Eshton, también vestidas de blanco, les flanqueaban.
A ceremony followed, in dumb show, in which it was easy to recognise the pantomime of a marriage.
Siguió una pantomima muda, en la que era fácil reconocer un simulacro de matrimonio.
At its termination, Colonel Dent and his party consulted in whispers for two minutes, then the Colonel called out--
Cuando concluyó, el coronel Dent consultó a los que estaban con él, y tras un breve cuchicheo exclamó:
"Bride!"
-¡Matrimonio!
Mr. Rochester bowed, and the curtain fell.
Mr. Rochester se inclinó, asintiendo, y la cortina cayó.
A considerable interval elapsed before it again rose.
Transcurrió un largo intervalo.
Its second rising displayed a more elaborately prepared scene than the last.
Al alzarse el cortinaje, reveló una escena mejor preparada que la anterior.

The drawing- room, as I have before observed, was raised two steps above the dining- room, and on the top of the upper step, placed a yard or two back within the room, appeared a large marble basin--which I recognised as an ornament of the conservatory--where it usually stood, surrounded by exotics, and tenanted by gold fish--and whence it must have been transported with some trouble, on account of its size and weight.

Se veía en primer término un gran pilón de mármol, que reconocí como perteneciente al invernadero, donde solía hallarse rodeado de plantas exóticas y conteniendo algunos pececillos dorados. Sin duda debía de haber costado trabajo transportarlo, atendidos su volumen y peso.
Seated on the carpet, by the side of this basin, was seen Mr. Rochester, costumed in shawls, with a turban on his head.
Sentado en la alfombra junto a aquel pilón estaba Mr. Rochester, vestido con chales y tocado con un turbante.
His dark eyes and swarthy skin and Paynim features suited the costume exactly: he looked the very model of an Eastern emir, an agent or a victim of the bowstring.
Sus ojos negros y su piel morena concordaban a maravilla con aquel atuendo. Parecía un emir oriental.
Presently advanced into view Miss Ingram.
En seguida sobrevino Blanche Ingram.

She, too, was attired in oriental fashion: a crimson scarf tied sash-like round the waist: an embroidered handkerchief knotted about her temples; her beautifully-moulded arms bare, one of them upraised in the act of supporting a pitcher, poised gracefully on her head.

Vestía también a estilo asiático, con una faja carmesí a la cintura y un pañuelo bordado en torno a las sienes. Sus hermosos brazos estaban desnudos, y uno de ellos sostenía con mucha gracia un cantarillo sobre la cabeza.

Both her cast of form and feature, her complexion and her general air, suggested the idea of some Israelitish princess of the patriarchal days; and such was doubtless the character she intended to represent.
Su aspecto y sus atavíos sugerían la idea de una princesa israelita de los tiempos patriarcales, y tal era, sin duda, el papel que trataba de representar.
She approached the basin, and bent over it as if to fill her pitcher; she again lifted it to her head.
Se aproximó al pilón, se inclinó sobre él como para llenar el cantarillo y volvió a colocar éste sobre su cabeza.
The personage on the well-brink now seemed to accost her; to make some request:--"She hasted, let down her pitcher on her hand, and gave him to drink."
El personaje masculino le hizo entonces una petición: -¡Eh, apresurada! Dame el cantarillo y déjame beber.

From the bosom of his robe he then produced a casket, opened it and showed magnificent bracelets and earrings; she acted astonishment and admiration; kneeling, he laid the treasure at her feet; incredulity and delight were expressed by her looks and gestures; the stranger fastened the bracelets on her arms and the rings in her ears.

El, arrodillándose, colocó el tesoro a los pies de la mujer, que expresaba en sus gestos y ademanes el placer y la incredulidad que sentía. Entonces Rochester colocó las pulseras en las muñecas de la joven y los pendientes en sus orejas.
It was Eliezer and Rebecca: the camels only were wanting.
Era, evidentemente, una reproducción de la escena de Eliezer y Rebecca. No faltaban más que los camellos.
The divining party again laid their heads together: apparently they could not agree about the word or syllable the scene illustrated.
Los que debían adivinar el significado del cuadro cuchichearon un rato. Al parecer, no se ponían de acuerdo en lo que la escena representaba.
Colonel Dent, their spokesman, demanded "the tableau of the whole;" whereupon the curtain again descended.
Al fin el coronel Dent, su portavoz, dio la respuesta oportuna y volvió a caer la cortina.
On its third rising only a portion of the drawing-room was disclosed; the rest being concealed by a screen, hung with some sort of dark and coarse drapery.
Al levantarse por tercera vez, sólo era visible una parte del salón, quedando lo demás oculto tras un biombo del que colgaban lienzos oscuros y groseros.

The marble basin was removed; in its place, stood a deal table and a kitchen chair: these objects were visible by a very dim light proceeding from a horn lantern, the wax candles being all extinguished.
El pilón de mármol había desaparecido. En su lugar había una mesa y una silla de cocina iluminadas por la opaca luz de una linterna.
Amidst this sordid scene, sat a man with his clenched hands resting on his knees, and his eyes bent on the ground.
En aquel sórdido escenario estaba sentado un hombre, con las manos atadas y la vista fija en el suelo. Pese a sus ropas en desorden y a su ennegrecida faz, reconocí en él a Mr.

I knew Mr. Rochester; though the begrimed face, the disordered dress (his coat hanging loose from one arm, as if it had been almost torn from his back in a scuffle), the desperate and scowling countenance, the rough, bristling hair might well have disguised him.

Vestía una burda chaqueta, una de cuyas mangas, desgarrada, pendía de su hombro, dando al protagonista el aspecto de haber sostenido una reciente refriega. Tales detalles, unidos a su desgreñado cabello, le disfrazaban muy bien.
As he moved, a chain clanked; to his wrists were attached fetters.
Al hacer un movimiento se oyó ruido de cadenas y vimos que llevaba grilletes en los tobillos.
"Bridewell!" exclaimed Colonel Dent, and the charade was solved.
-¡Prisión! -exclamó el coronel Dent, resolviendo el acertijo.
A sufficient interval having elapsed for the performers to resume their ordinary costume, they re-entered the dining-room.
Pasado el tiempo necesario para que los actores se vistieran como de costumbre, volvieron al comedor.
Mr. Rochester led in Miss Ingram; she was complimenting him on his acting.
Blanche felicitaba a Mr. Rochester.
"Do you know," said she, "that, of the three characters, I liked you in the last best?
-¿Sabe -le decía- que de sus tres caracterizaciones me gusta la última más que ninguna?
Oh, had you but lived a few years earlier, what a gallant gentleman-highwayman you would have made!"
¡Oh! Si hubiera usted vivido hace algunos años, ¡qué magnífico salteador de carreteras habría hecho usted!
"Is all the soot washed from my face?" he asked, turning it towards her.
-¿No me queda nada de hollín en la cara? -preguntó Rochester, volviéndose hacia ella.
"Alas! yes: the more's the pity!
-Nada, desgraciadamente.
Nothing could be more becoming to your complexion than that ruffian's rouge."
¡Qué bien le sienta el disfraz de bandido!
"You would like a hero of the road then?"
-¿Le gustan esos héroes del camino real?
"An English hero of the road would be the next best thing to an Italian bandit; and that could only be surpassed by a Levantine pirate."
-Creo que un salteador inglés debe de ser la cosa más parecida.
"Well, whatever I am, remember you are my wife; we were married an hour since, in the presence of all these witnesses."
En todo caso, recuerde que somos mujer y marido, de lo que son testigos cuantos se hallan presentes. ¡No hace aún una hora que nos hemos casado!
She giggled, and her colour rose.
Ella rió y se ruborizó.
"Now, Dent," continued Mr. Rochester, "it is your turn."
-Ahora le toca a usted, Dent -dijo Mr. Rochester.
And as the other party withdrew, he and his band took the vacated seats.
Y, mientras el otro bando se retiraba, él, con el suyo, ocupó los asientos que quedaban vacantes.
Miss Ingram placed herself at her leader's right hand; the other diviners filled the chairs on each side of him and her.
Miss Ingram se colocó al lado de Rochester. Los demás, en sillas inmediatas, a ambos lados de ellos.

I did not now watch the actors; I no longer waited with interest for the curtain to rise; my attention was absorbed by the spectators; my eyes, erewhile fixed on the arch, were now irresistibly attracted to the semicircle of chairs.
Yo dejé de mirar a los actores; había perdido todo interés por los acertijos y, en cambio, mis ojos se sentían irresistiblemente atraídos por el círculo de espectadores.
