What charade Colonel Dent and his party played, what word they chose, how they acquitted themselves, I no longer remember; but I still see the consultation which followed each scene: I see Mr. Rochester turn to Miss Ingram, and Miss Ingram to him; I see her incline her head towards him, till the jetty curls almost touch his shoulder and wave against his cheek; I hear their mutual whisperings; I recall their interchanged glances; and something even of the feeling roused by the spectacle returns in memory at this moment.

Rochester inclinarse hacia Blanche para consultarla y a ella acercarse a él hasta que los rizos de la joven casi tocaban los hombros y las mejillas de su compañero. Yo escuchaba sus cuchicheos y notaba las miradas que cambiaban entre sí.

I have told you, reader, that I had learnt to love Mr. Rochester: I could not unlove him now, merely because I found that he had ceased to notice me--because I might pass hours in his presence, and he would never once turn his eyes in my direction--because I saw all his attentions appropriated by a great lady, who scorned to touch me with the hem of her robes as she passed; who, if ever her dark and imperious eye fell on me by chance, would withdraw it instantly as from an object too mean to merit observation.

Rochester. Y no podía dejar ahora de amarle, porque no reparase en mí; porque transcurrieran horas sin que sus ojos buscaran los míos; porque sus miradas estuvieran dedicadas exclusivamente a otra mujer; porque, si se fijaba casualmente en mí, se apresuraba a apartar la vista.

I could not unlove him, because I felt sure he would soon marry this very lady--because I read daily in her a proud security in his intentions respecting her--because I witnessed hourly in him a style of courtship which, if careless and choosing rather to be sought than to seek, was yet, in its very carelessness, captivating, and in its very pride, irresistible.

No me era posible dejar de amarle aunque comprendiera que había de casarse en breve con Blanche Ingram, como lo indicaba la orgullosa seguridad que ella parecía mostrar respecto a sus intenciones. Yo, a pesar de todo, hubiera deseado que Rochester me dedicase aquellas amabilidades que, aunque negligentes e indiferentes, encerraban para mí un cautivador e irresistible interés.

There was nothing to cool or banish love in these circumstances, though much to create despair. Much too, you will think, reader, to engender jealousy: if a woman, in my position, could presume to be jealous of a woman in Miss Ingram's.
Mi amor no se disipaba, no. Cabe suponer que se levantaran en mí una inmensa desesperación y furiosos celos, si es que una mujer de mi posición podía sentir celos de Blanche Ingram.
But I was not jealous: or very rarely;--the nature of the pain I suffered could not be explained by that word.
Sin embargo, yo, en realidad, no era celosa y el sentimiento que experimentaba no se expresa bien con tal palabra.
Miss Ingram was a mark beneath jealousy: she was too inferior to excite the feeling.
Blanche era demasiado inferior para excitar mis celos.
Pardon the seeming paradox; I mean what I say.
Perdóneseme la paradoja, porque sé lo que digo.

She was very showy, but she was not genuine: she had a fine person, many brilliant attainments; but her mind was poor, her heart barren by nature: nothing bloomed spontaneously on that soil; no unforced natural fruit delighted by its freshness.
Blanche deslumbraba, pero no era sincera; era muy brillante, pero muy pobre de mentalidad. Tenía el corazón mezquino por naturaleza, como una tierra en la que nada fructificara espontáneamente.

She was not good; she was not original: she used to repeat sounding phrases from books: she never offered, nor had, an opinion of her own. She advocated a high tone of sentiment; but she did not know the sensations of sympathy and pity; tenderness and truth were not in her.
No era benévola, no era original, repetía frases leídas en los libros, no emitía nunca una opinión propia.

Too often she betrayed this, by the undue vent she gave to a spiteful antipathy she had conceived against little Adele: pushing her away with some contumelious epithet if she happened to approach her; sometimes ordering her from the room, and always treating her with coldness and acrimony.
Desconocía toda sensación de simpatía y piedad, y carecía de naturalidad y de ternura.
Other eyes besides mine watched these manifestations of character--watched them closely, keenly, shrewdly.
Con frecuencia se traicionaba, como cuando exteriorizó la antipatía que sintiera ante la pequeña Adèle.

Yes; the future bridegroom, Mr. Rochester himself, exercised over his intended a ceaseless surveillance; and it was from this sagacity--this guardedness of his--this perfect, clear consciousness of his fair one's defects--this obvious absence of passion in his sentiments towards her, that my ever- torturing pain arose.

Si ésta se aproximaba a ella alguna vez, la rechazaba con algún epíteto despectivo, ordenándola incluso salir de la habitación, y demostrando siempre hacia la niña sequedad y acrimonia. Otros ojos -no sólo los míos- apreciaban estas manifestaciones: su futuro prometido, Rochester, la observaba sin cesar.

I saw he was going to marry her, for family, perhaps political reasons, because her rank and connections suited him; I felt he had not given her his love, and that her qualifications were ill adapted to win from him that treasure.

Y era lo bastante sagaz para, sin duda, saber percibir sus defectos. Dada su evidente falta de pasión por ella, dada su notoria comprensión de las malas cualidades de Miss Ingram, yo adivinaba que iba a desposarla por razones familiares y acaso prácticas, pero no por amor.
This was the point--this was where the nerve was touched and teased--this was where the fever was sustained and fed: _she could not charm him_.
Aquél era el punto neurálgico de la cuestión: no era posible que una mujer así le agradase.
If she had managed the victory at once, and he had yielded and sincerely laid his heart at her feet, I should have covered my face, turned to the wall, and (figuratively) have died to them.
Si ella hubiese conquistado a Rochester, si él sinceramente hubiese puesto su corazón a sus pies, yo habría simbólicamente - muerto para ellos.

If Miss Ingram had been a good and noble woman, endowed with force, fervour, kindness, sense, I should have had one vital struggle with two tigers--jealousy and despair: then, my heart torn out and devoured, I should have admired her--acknowledged her excellence, and been quiet for the rest of my days: and the more absolute her superiority, the deeper would have been my admiration--the more truly tranquil my quiescence.

Si Blanche hubiera sido una mujer buena, amable, sensible, apasionada, yo habría debido mantener una lucha a muerte con dos tigres: la desesperación y los celos, que hubiesen devorado mi corazón. Y, después, reconociendo la superioridad de Blanche, la hubiese admirado durante el resto de mis días, con tanta más admiración cuanto mayor fuera su superioridad.

But as matters really stood, to watch Miss Ingram's efforts at fascinating Mr. Rochester, to witness their repeated failure--herself unconscious that they did fail; vainly fancying that each shaft launched hit the mark, and infatuatedly pluming herself on success, when her pride and self-complacency repelled further and further what she wished to allure--to witness _this_, was to be at once under ceaseless excitation and ruthless restraint.

Pero la realidad era que los esfuerzos de la señorita Ingram para seducir a Mr. Rochester fallaban, aunque ella misma no lo notase, y que, si insistía en sus propósitos, lo hacía estimulada por su orgullo y por su amor propio.

Arrows that continually glanced off from Mr. Rochester's breast and fell harmless at his feet, might, I knew, if shot by a surer hand, have quivered keen in his proud heart--have called love into his stern eye, and softness into his sardonic face; or, better still, without weapons a silent conquest might have been won.

Yo presentía que si tales flechas lanzadas sobre Rochester hubieran sido arrojadas por mano más segura, habrían alcanzado su corazón, hecho asomar el amor a sus ojos, la dulzura a su sarcástico semblante y, en todo caso, aun sin estas manifestaciones externas, habrían ganado una batalla silenciosa pero segura.
"Why can she not influence him more, when she is privileged to draw so near to him?"
«¿Por qué no habría yo de poder influirle más, estando moralmente más cerca de él? -me pregunté-.
I asked myself. "Surely she cannot truly like him, or not like him with true affection!
Bien seguro es que ella no le ama o, al menos, le ama sin afecto profundo.

If she did, she need not coin her smiles so lavishly, flash her glances so unremittingly, manufacture airs so elaborate, graces so multitudinous. It seems to me that she might, by merely sitting quietly at his side, saying little and looking less, get nigher his heart.
De ser así, no precisaría dar tan artificiales muestras de interés.

I have seen in his face a far different expression from that which hardens it now while she is so vivaciously accosting him; but then it came of itself: it was not elicited by meretricious arts and calculated manoeuvres; and one had but to accept it--to answer what he asked without pretension, to address him when needful without grimace--and it increased and grew kinder and more genial, and warmed one like a fostering sunbeam. How will she manage to please him when they are married?
A mi juicio, sobran tantas manifestaciones externas; podría estar más tranquila: hablar y gesticular menos. Si ahora precisa esas malas artes para atraerle, ¿a qué apelará cuando estén casados?
I do not think she will manage it; and yet it might be managed; and his wife might, I verily believe, be the very happiest woman the sun shines on."
No creo que ella le haga feliz y, sin embargo, él podría serlo y sabría hacer a su esposa la más dichosa mujer del mundo.»
I have not yet said anything condemnatory of Mr. Rochester's project of marrying for interest and connections.
No formulaba censura alguna contra Mr. Rochester al considerar aquel probable matrimonio por interés.

It surprised me when I first discovered that such was his intention: I had thought him a man unlikely to be influenced by motives so commonplace in his choice of a wife; but the longer I considered the position, education, &c., of the parties, the less I felt justified in judging and blaming either him or Miss Ingram for acting in conformity to ideas and principles instilled into them, doubtless, from their childhood.

Al principio me extrañó suponer en él tal intención, ya que le creía un hombre ajeno a los prejuicios vulgares respecto a la elección de mujer, pero cuanto más consideraba la posición, educación, etc., de los interesados, menos censurable me parecía que realizasen un acto acorde con los principios que les fueran imbuidos desde la infancia y comunes a todos los de su clase, aunque yo no pudiera comprenderlos.
All their class held these principles: I supposed, then, they had reasons for holding them such as I could not fathom.

Me parecía que, si yo hubiese sido un hombre en el caso de Rochester, sólo me hubiera casado con una mujer a quien amase, pero a la vez admitía que las evidentes ventajas que en pro de la felicidad matrimonial debía ofrecer una determinación así podían estar contrapesadas por razones que yo ignoraba en absoluto, aun cuando hubiera deseado que todo el mundo obrase como yo pensaba.
But in other points, as well as this, I was growing very lenient to my master: I was forgetting all his faults, for which I had once kept a sharp look-out.
En estas reflexiones prescindía de los aspectos malos del carácter de Rochester.

The sarcasm that had repelled, the harshness that had startled me once, were only like keen condiments in a choice dish: their presence was pungent, but their absence would be felt as comparatively insipid.
Su desagradable sarcasmo, su dureza, me parecían picantes condimentos de un excelente manjar. Y si su presencia era en algún sentido ingrata, su ausencia hacia la vida insípida para mí.

And as for the vague something--was it a sinister or a sorrowful, a designing or a desponding expression?--that opened upon a careful observer, now and then, in his eye, and closed again before one could fathom the strange depth partially disclosed; that something which used to make me fear and shrink, as if I had been wandering amongst volcanic-looking hills, and had suddenly felt the ground quiver and seen it gape: that something, I, at intervals, beheld still; and with throbbing heart, but not with palsied nerves.

Consideraba dichosa a Miss Ingram, porque iba a poder asomarse a los abismos del carácter de aquel hombre y sondearlos. Mientras yo no tenía ojos más que para Rochester y su futura esposa, el resto de los invitados se ocupaban en sí mismos.

The Ladies Lynn and Ingram continued to consort in solemn conferences, where they nodded their two turbans at each other, and held up their four hands in confronting gestures of surprise, or mystery, or horror, according to the theme on which their gossip ran, like a pair of magnified puppets.

Las señoras Lynn e Ingram mantenían un grave debate. De vez en cuando movían sus turbantes, agitaban sus cuatro manos en análogos ademanes de asombro, secreto u horror, sin duda relativos al tema que trataban.
Mild Mrs. Dent talked with good-natured Mrs. Eshton; and the two sometimes bestowed a courteous word or smile on me.
La amable señora Dent hablaba con la bondadosa Mrs. Eshton, y a veces una y otra me dirigían una palabra o una sonrisa afectuosa.
Sir George Lynn, Colonel Dent, and Mr. Eshton discussed politics, or county affairs, or justice business.
Sir George Lynn, el coronel Dent y Mr. Eshton discutían de política, de asuntos del condado o de temas judiciales.
Lord Ingram flirted with Amy Eshton; Louisa played and sang to and with one of the Messrs. Lynn; and Mary Ingram listened languidly to the gallant speeches of the other.
Lord Ingram cortejaba a Amy Eshton. Louisa cantaba y tocaba con uno de los Lynn, y Mary Ingram escuchaba con languidez la galante conversación del otro.

Sometimes all, as with one consent, suspended their by-play to observe and listen to the principal actors: for, after all, Mr. Rochester and--because closely connected with him--Miss Ingram were the life and soul of the party.
De vez en vez, todos suspendían unánimemente su charla para escuchar y observar a los principales actores: Rochester y Blanche Ingram, que eran, en efecto, el cuerpo y alma de la reunión.
If he was absent from the room an hour, a perceptible dulness seemed to steal over the spirits of his guests; and his re-entrance was sure to give a fresh impulse to the vivacity of conversation.
Si él faltaba un rato del salón, su ausencia parecía producir cierto decaimiento en los ánimos de sus invitados, y tan pronto como entraba se reanimaba la vivacidad de la conversación.
The want of his animating influence appeared to be peculiarly felt one day that he had been summoned to Millcote on business, and was not likely to return till late.
La necesidad de aquella estimulante influencia suya se puso de relieve un día que hubo de ir a Millcote a arreglar unos asuntos y no volvió hasta muy tarde.
The afternoon was wet: a walk the party had proposed to take to see a gipsy camp, lately pitched on a common beyond Hay, was consequently deferred.
La tarde estuvo lluviosa, motivo que hizo suspender una proyectada visita a un campamento de gitanos que se habían establecido cerca de Hay.
Some of the gentlemen were gone to the stables: the younger ones, together with the younger ladies, were playing billiards in the billiard-room.
Algunos de los caballeros fueron a las cuadras, mientras los jóvenes de ambos sexos jugaban al billar.
The dowagers Ingram and Lynn sought solace in a quiet game at cards.
Las viudas Ingram y Lynn se entregaban a una plácida partida de naipes.

Blanche Ingram, after having repelled, by supercilious taciturnity, some efforts of Mrs. Dent and Mrs. Eshton to draw her into conversation, had first murmured over some sentimental tunes and airs on the piano, and then, having fetched a novel from the library, had flung herself in haughty listlessness on a sofa, and prepared to beguile, by the spell of fiction, the tedious hours of absence.

Blanche Ingram, tras repeler con orgullosa taciturnidad algunos intentos de las Eshton y Dent para entablar conversación, había tocado primero algunas romanzas sentimentales en el piano, y luego tomando una novela de la biblioteca, se había hundido en un sofá y se disponía a matar con la lectura las tediosas horas de ausencia.
The room and the house were silent: only now and then the merriment of the billiard-players was heard from above.
El salón y toda la casa estaban silenciosos. No se oía más que el choque de las bolas de billar.
It was verging on dusk, and the clock had already given warning of the hour to dress for dinner, when little Adele, who knelt by me in the drawing-room window-seat, suddenly exclaimed--
Oscurecía. Se acercaba la hora de vestirse para cenar, cuando la pequeña Adèle, que se hallaba arrodillada en el hueco de una ventana del salón, exclamó:
"Voila, Monsieur Rochester, qui revient!"
-¡Ya vuelve Mr. Rochester!

I turned, and Miss Ingram darted forwards from her sofa: the others, too, looked up from their several occupations; for at the same time a crunching of wheels and a splashing tramp of horse-hoofs became audible on the wet gravel.
Blanche Ingram se levantó del sofá y los demás abandonaron sus ocupaciones, al tiempo que se sentía sonar un ruido de ruedas y de cascos de caballos sobre la arena húmeda.
A post-chaise was approaching.
Una silla de posta se aproximaba.
"What can possess him to come home in that style?" said Miss Ingram.
-¡Qué raro es que vuelva a casa de este modo! -dijo Blanche-.
"He rode Mesrour (the black horse), did he not, when he went out? and Pilot was with him:--what has he done with the animals?"
Se fue montado en Mesrour y acompañado de Piloto.

As she said this, she approached her tall person and ample garments so near the window, that I was obliged to bend back almost to the breaking of my spine: in her eagerness she did not observe me at first, but when she did, she curled her lip and moved to another casement.
¿Qué habrá sido de esos animales? Mientras hablaba, aproximaba a la ventana de tal modo su alta figura, que tuve que echarme hacia atrás para dejarle sitio, a riesgo de romperme la espina dorsal.
The post-chaise stopped; the driver rang the door-bell, and a gentleman alighted attired in travelling garb; but it was not Mr. Rochester; it was a tall, fashionable-looking man, a stranger.
Entretanto, la silla de posta se detuvo y el viajero se apeó y tocó la campanilla. Era un hombre desconocido, alto, elegante, en traje de viaje.

"How provoking!" exclaimed Miss Ingram: "you tiresome monkey!" (apostrophising Adele), "who perched you up in the window to give false intelligence?" and she cast on me an angry glance, as if I were in fault.
Y apostrofó a Adèle-: Y tú, monicaca, ¿qué haces ahí, en la ventana, dedicándote a dar noticias tontas? Y lanzó sobre mí una mirada agria, como si yo hubiese cometido algún delito.
Some parleying was audible in the hall, and soon the new-comer entered.
Se oyó hablar en el vestíbulo y en breve apareció el recién llegado.
He bowed to Lady Ingram, as deeming her the eldest lady present.
Se inclinó ante Lady Ingram, considerándola, sin duda, la de más edad de las presentes.

"It appears I come at an inopportune time, madam," said he, "when my friend, Mr. Rochester, is from home; but I arrive from a very long journey, and I think I may presume so far on old and intimate acquaintance as to instal myself here till he returns."
-Creo que llego con inoportunidad, señora -dijo-, ya que mi amigo Rochester está fuera, pero soy lo bastante íntimo suyo para poder permitirme instalarme aquí en espera de su regreso.

His manner was polite; his accent, in speaking, struck me as being somewhat unusual,--not precisely foreign, but still not altogether English: his age might be about Mr. Rochester's,--between thirty and forty; his complexion was singularly sallow: otherwise he was a fine-looking man, at first sight especially.

Sus modales eran corteses y su voz me impresionó porque, sin tener precisamente acento extranjero, hablaba de un modo no corriente en Inglaterra. Su edad podía ser la de Rochester: entre treinta y cuarenta años.
On closer examination, you detected something in his face that displeased, or rather that failed to please.
Examinándole mejor, creí encontrar en su rostro algo desagradable o, más bien, no agradable.
His features were regular, but too relaxed: his eye was large and well cut, but the life looking out of it was a tame, vacant life--at least so I thought.
Sus rasgos eran correctos, sus facciones suaves y sus ojos, aunque grandes y de bella forma, carecían de vida, o al menos me lo pareció.
The sound of the dressing-bell dispersed the party.
El sonido de la campana que indicaba la hora de vestirse para comer dispersó la reunión.
It was not till after dinner that I saw him again: he then seemed quite at his ease.
No volví a ver a aquel hombre hasta después de comer, y me pareció que se hallaba en su centro.
But I liked his physiognomy even less than before: it struck me as being at the same time unsettled and inanimate.
Pero su fisonomía me agradó menos aún que antes por un lado me impresionaba y por otro me parecía inanimada.
His eye wandered, and had no meaning in its wandering: this gave him an odd look, such as I never remembered to have seen.
Sus ojos erraban de un lado a otro, sin expresión alguna, lo que le daba un curioso aspecto, tal como yo no viera nunca.

For a handsome and not an unamiable-looking man, he repelled me exceedingly: there was no power in that smooth-skinned face of a full oval shape: no firmness in that aquiline nose and small cherry mouth; there was no thought on the low, even forehead; no command in that blank, brown eye.

En aquel rostro ovalado de fino cutis no se apreciaba energía viril, ni masculina firmeza en su nariz aquilina. Su boca era pequeña y tras su frente no parecía caber pensamiento alguno, así como sus oscuros ojos apagados parecían carecer de todo poder de sugestión.

As I sat in my usual nook, and looked at him with the light of the girandoles on the mantelpiece beaming full over him--for he occupied an arm-chair drawn close to the fire, and kept shrinking still nearer, as if he were cold, I compared him with Mr. Rochester.
Mientras le contemplaba desde mi rincón de costumbre, a la luz de la chimenea -ya que estaba sentado en una butaca muy próxima al fuego, como si sintiera frío-, le comparaba con Rochester.
I think (with deference be it spoken) the contrast could not be much greater between a sleek gander and a fierce falcon: between a meek sheep and the rough-coated keen-eyed dog, its guardian.
Pensaba que no hubiera habido mayor diferencia entre ambos que entre un pato y un fiero halcón, entre un dulce cordero y el mastín de ardientes ojos que le guarda. Había hablado de Mr.
He had spoken of Mr. Rochester as an old friend.
Rochester como de un antiguo amigo.
A curious friendship theirs must have been: a pointed illustration, indeed, of the old adage that "extremes meet."
¡Curiosa amistad, me confirmaba el proverbio de que «los extremos se tocan»!
Two or three of the gentlemen sat near him, and I caught at times scraps of their conversation across the room.
Junto a él estaban sentados otros dos o tres señores, y de vez en cuando podía oír fragmentos de su conversación.
At first I could not make much sense of what I heard; for the discourse of Louisa Eshton and Mary Ingram, who sat nearer to me, confused the fragmentary sentences that reached me at intervals.
Al principio no les comprendí bien, porque la charla de Louisa Eshton y Mary Ingram, sentadas muy cerca de mí, me hacían confundir las aisladas frases que les escuchaba.
These last were discussing the stranger; they both called him "a beautiful man."
Les oía decir: «Es un hombre hermoso.»
Louisa said he was "a love of a creature," and she "adored him;" and Mary instanced his "pretty little mouth, and nice nose," as her ideal of the charming.
«Un encanto de muchacho», decía Louisa, agregando que «le gustaba con locura».
"And what a sweet-tempered forehead he has!" cried Louisa,--"so smooth--none of those frowning irregularities I dislike so much; and such a placid eye and smile!"
Mary indicó su boca y su bella nariz como el ideal de la belleza. -¡Qué frente tan lisa tiene, sin ninguna de esas protuberancias tan desagradables! -exclamó Louisa-. ¡Y qué sonrisa tan dulce!
And then, to my great relief, Mr. Henry Lynn summoned them to the other side of the room, to settle some point about the deferred excursion to Hay Common.
Con gran satisfacción mía, Henry Lynn las llevó a otro extremo de la sala para acordar no sé qué respecto a la aplazada excursión.

I was now able to concentrate my attention on the group by the fire, and I presently gathered that the new-comer was called Mr. Mason; then I learned that he was but just arrived in England, and that he came from some hot country: which was the reason, doubtless, his face was so sallow, and that he sat so near the hearth, and wore a surtout in the house.

Pude así concentrar mi atención en el grupo cercano al fuego, y entonces me informé de que el recién llegado se llamaba Mason, que acababa de desembarcar en Inglaterra y que venía de los países tropicales. Aquélla era, sin duda, la causa de que estuviese tan amarillo, de que se sentase junto a la chimenea y de que llevase un abrigo en casa.

Presently the words Jamaica, Kingston, Spanish Town, indicated the West Indies as his residence; and it was with no little surprise I gathered, ere long, that he had there first seen and become acquainted with Mr. Rochester.
Las palabras Jamaica, Kingston, Puerto España, indicaban que debía tener su residencia en las Antillas. No sin sorpresa supe que fue allí donde contrajo amistad con Mr.
He spoke of his friend's dislike of the burning heats, the hurricanes, and rainy seasons of that region.
Mencionó lo que disgustaban a su amigo el ardiente calor, los huracanes y las épocas lluviosas de aquellos países.

I knew Mr. Rochester had been a traveller: Mrs. Fairfax had said so; but I thought the continent of Europe had bounded his wanderings; till now I had never heard a hint given of visits to more distant shores.

Yo no ignoraba que Rochester había viajado mucho -me lo había dicho Mrs. Fairfax-, pero siempre había creído que sus viajes se limitaban al continente europeo, no habiendo oído relatar sus visitas a más lejanas regiones.
I was pondering these things, when an incident, and a somewhat unexpected one, broke the thread of my musings.
Reflexionaba en estas cosas, cuando un inesperado incidente vino a distraerme de mis pensamientos.
Mr. Mason, shivering as some one chanced to open the door, asked for more coal to be put on the fire, which had burnt out its flame, though its mass of cinder still shone hot and red.
Mr. Mason, que tiritaba cada vez que alguien abría la puerta, había pedido más leña para el fuego, aunque las cenizas estaban aún calientes y rojas.
The footman who brought the coal, in going out, stopped near Mr. Eshton's chair, and said something to him in a low voice, of which I heard only the words, "old woman,"--"quite troublesome."
El criado que llevó la leña se detuvo un instante junto a la silla de Mr. Eshton y le dijo unas palabras en voz baja, de las que sólo oí: Vieja y muy desagradable.
"Tell her she shall be put in the stocks if she does not take herself off," replied the magistrate.
-Dígale que la encerraremos en el calabozo si no se va -replicó el magistrado.
"No--stop!" interrupted Colonel Dent.
-¡No! -interrumpió el coronel Dent-.
"Don't send her away, Eshton; we might turn the thing to account; better consult the ladies."
No lo hagamos sin consultar a las señoras -y añadió-:

And speaking aloud, he continued--"Ladies, you talked of going to Hay Common to visit the gipsy camp; Sam here says that one of the old Mother Bunches is in the servants' hall at this moment, and insists upon being brought in before 'the quality,' to tell them their fortunes. Would you like to see her?"

Señoras, ¿no hablaban ustedes de visitar el campamento de los gitanos? Sam acaba de decir que en el cuarto de la servidumbre se halla una vieja gibosa que se empeña en decirnos la buenaventura. -¡Vamos, coronel!
"Surely, colonel," cried Lady Ingram, "you would not encourage such a low impostor?
Ingram-. ¿Cree que nos interesa una de esas impostoras?
Dismiss her, by all means, at once!"
Mándenla irse en seguida. -No logramos convencerla de que se vaya, señora - -dijo el criado-. ¡Ni yo ni ninguno!

"But I cannot persuade her to go away, my lady," said the footman; "nor can any of the servants: Mrs. Fairfax is with her just now, entreating her to be gone; but she has taken a chair in the chimney-corner, and says nothing shall stir her from it till she gets leave to come in here."
Mrs. Fairfax ha tratado de persuadirla, pero ella se ha sentado en un rincón junto a la chimenea y asegura que no se irá mientras no la permitan entrar aquí.
"What does she want?" asked Mrs. Eshton.
-¿Qué quiere? -preguntó Mrs. Eshton.
"'To tell the gentry their fortunes,' she says, ma'am; and she swears she must and will do it."
-Decir la buenaventura; jura que es necesario hacerlo y que lo hará.
"What is she like?" inquired the Misses Eshton, in a breath.
-¿Qué aspecto tiene?
"A shockingly ugly old creature, miss; almost as black as a crock."
-Es una vieja feísima y más negra que una sartén, señora.
"Why, she's a real sorceress!" cried Frederick Lynn.
-¡Una verdadera hechicera! -gritó Frederick-.
"Let us have her in, of course."
¡Tráigala, tráigala!
"To be sure," rejoined his brother; "it would be a thousand pities to throw away such a chance of fun."
-¡Naturalmente! -agregó su hermano-. Sería muy lamentable perder tal oportunidad.
"My dear boys, what are you thinking about?" exclaimed Mrs. Lynn.
-¿Qué locura estáis pensando, muchachos? -exclamó Mrs. Lynn.
"I cannot possibly countenance any such inconsistent proceeding," chimed in the Dowager Ingram.
-Verdaderamente, una locura es -asintió la viuda Ingram.
"Indeed, mama, but you can--and will," pronounced the haughty voice of Blanche, as she turned round on the piano-stool; where till now she had sat silent, apparently examining sundry sheets of music.
-Nada de eso, mamá -replicó Blanche, girando sobre el taburete del piano, donde se hallaba sentada en silencio, examinando partituras, al parecer-.
"I have a curiosity to hear my fortune told: therefore, Sam, order the beldame forward."
Quiero que me predigan mi suerte. Mándela entrar, Sam.
"My darling Blanche! recollect--"
-¡Pero, querida Blanche!...
"I do--I recollect all you can suggest; and I must have my will--quick, Sam!"
¡Comprende que...! -Yo comprendo todo lo que tú dices, pero quiero hacer lo que te digo. ¡Pronto, Sam!
"Yes--yes--yes!" cried all the juveniles, both ladies and gentlemen.
-¡Sí, sí, sí! -gritaron todos los jóvenes de ambos sexos-.
"Let her come--it will be excellent sport!"
Tráigala: nos divertiremos.
The footman still lingered. "She looks such a rough one," said he.
-Tiene una traza que... -indicó el criado, vacilando aún.
"Go!" ejaculated Miss Ingram, and the man went.
-¡Tráigala! -conminó Blanche.
Excitement instantly seized the whole party: a running fire of raillery and jests was proceeding when Sam returned.
La reunión estaba muy excitada y se cruzaban risas y chanzas entre todos. Sam volvió a aparecer. -Ahora no quiere venir -afirmó-.
"She won't come now," said he. "She says it's not her mission to appear before the 'vulgar herd' (them's her words).
Dice (son sus propias palabras) que no es su misión aparecer ante el vulgo, sino que debe ser llevada a un cuarto y dejada.
I must show her into a room by herself, and then those who wish to consult her must go to her one by one."
Entonces sola recibirá allí, pero únicamente uno a uno, a quienes quieran consultarla.
"You see now, my queenly Blanche," began Lady Ingram, "she encroaches.
-Ya lo ves, reina mía... -comenzó Lady Ingram-.
Be advised, my angel girl--and--"
¿Te das cuenta, ángel mío, de que...?
"Show her into the library, of course," cut in the "angel girl."
-Llévela a la biblioteca-atajó el ángel-.
"It is not my mission to listen to her before the vulgar herd either: I mean to have her all to myself.
Mi misión no es tampoco escuchar a esa mujer ante el vulgo. Deseo verla a solas.
Is there a fire in the library?"
¿Hay fuego en la biblioteca?
"Yes, ma'am--but she looks such a tinkler."
-Sí, señora. Pero esa mujer parece un...
"Cease that chatter, blockhead! and do my bidding."
-¡Basta de charla! Haga lo que le digo, y no sea cabezota.
Again Sam vanished; and mystery, animation, expectation rose to full flow once more.
Sam desapareció de nuevo y la expectación y la curiosidad aumentaron.
"She's ready now," said the footman, as he reappeared. "She wishes to know who will be her first visitor."
-Ya está allí -dijo el criado al volver- y desea saber quién será el primero que la consulte.
"I think I had better just look in upon her before any of the ladies go," said Colonel Dent. "Tell her, Sam, a gentleman is coming."
-Creo que será mejor que vaya yo antes que las señoras -indicó el coronel Dent. -Dígala que va a ir un caballero, Sam.
Sam went and returned.
Sam se fue y volvió.

"She says, sir, that she'll have no gentlemen; they need not trouble themselves to come near her; nor," he added, with difficulty suppressing a titter, "any ladies either, except the young, and single."

-Dice, señor, que no quiere ver a ningún caballero, que no desea que éstos se tomen la molestia de ir a verla, ni -añadió, reprimiendo la risa- tampoco las señoras, sino sólo las jovencitas y una a una.
"By Jove, she has taste!" exclaimed Henry Lynn.
-¡Por Júpiter, que tiene buen gusto! -exclamó Henry Lynn.
Miss Ingram rose solemnly: "I go first," she said, in a tone which might have befitted the leader of a forlorn hope, mounting a breach in the van of his men.
Blanche Ingram se levantó solemnemente y dijo, con el acento que hubiera empleado el jefe de un ejército lanzándose a la vanguardia de sus hombres cuando todo parecía estar perdido: -Yo iré.
"Oh, my best! oh, my dearest! pause--reflect!" was her mama's cry; but she swept past her in stately silence, passed through the door which Colonel Dent held open, and we heard her enter the library.
-¡Oh, cariño mío, espera, reflexiona... ! -gritó su madre. Pero en vano, ya que su hija pasó ante ella en orgulloso silencio, cruzó la puerta que Dent abrió y la sentimos entrar en la biblioteca.
A comparative silence ensued.
Siguió un relativo silencio.
Lady Ingram thought it "le cas" to wring her hands: which she did accordingly.
Mrs. Ingram se creyó obligada a retorcerse las manos con desesperación.
Miss Mary declared she felt, for her part, she never dared venture.
Mary declaró que ella no osaría aventurarse a tal cosa.
Amy and Louisa Eshton tittered under their breath, and looked a little frightened.
Amy y Louisa Eshton reían por lo bajo y parecían un tanto asustadas.
The minutes passed very slowly: fifteen were counted before the library- door again opened.
Los minutos pasaban lentamente: quince transcurrieron antes de que la puerta de la biblioteca tornara a abrirse.
Miss Ingram returned to us through the arch.
Blanche volvió al salón.
Would she laugh?
¿Se reiría?
Would she take it as a joke?
¿Consideraría aquello como un juego?
All eyes met her with a glance of eager curiosity, and she met all eyes with one of rebuff and coldness; she looked neither flurried nor merry: she walked stiffly to her seat, and took it in silence.
Los ojos convergieron en ella con curiosidad y ella correspondió con una mirada fría. No parecía contenta.
"Well, Blanche?" said Lord Ingram.
-¿Y qué, Blanche? -preguntó Lord Ingram.
"What did she say, sister?" asked Mary.
-¿Qué te ha dicho, hermana? -preguntó Mary. -¿Qué piensa usted?
"What did you think?
¿Qué le ha parecido?
How do you feel?--Is she a real fortune-teller?" demanded the Misses Eshton.
¿Es una verdadera adivina? -inquirió Mrs. Eshton.
"Now, now, good people," returned Miss Ingram, "don't press upon me.
-¡Voy, voy! -repuso Blanche-. ¡No me metan tanta prisa!

Really your organs of wonder and credulity are easily excited: you seem, by the importance of you all--my good mama included--ascribe to this matter, absolutely to believe we have a genuine witch in the house, who is in close alliance with the old gentleman.

Veo que sus instintos de credulidad y asombro se excitan fácilmente. Por la importancia que ustedes parecen dar a eso, se diría que tenemos en casa una auténtica bruja en combinación con el viejo señor del castillo.
I have seen a gipsy vagabond; she has practised in hackneyed fashion the science of palmistry and told me what such people usually tell.
No he visto más que a una gitana vagabunda, que me ha examinado la palma de la mano y que me ha dicho lo que tales gentes suelen decir siempre.
My whim is gratified; and now I think Mr. Eshton will do well to put the hag in the stocks to-morrow morning, as he threatened."
Y ahora que mi capricho ha sido satisfecho plenamente, creo que Mr. Eshton hará bien en meter en el calabozo a esa mujer mañana, como antes dijo.
Miss Ingram took a book, leant back in her chair, and so declined further conversation.
Cogió un libro, se recostó en su silla y renunció a toda conversación.
I watched her for nearly half-an-hour: during all that time she never turned a page, and her face grew momently darker, more dissatisfied, and more sourly expressive of disappointment.
La examiné durante media hora. En todo el tiempo no volvió ni una página y su rostro se puso gradualmente más sombrío, más desabrido, más disgustado.

She had obviously not heard anything to her advantage: and it seemed to me, from her prolonged fit of gloom and taciturnity, that she herself, notwithstanding her professed indifference, attached undue importance to whatever revelations had been made her.
Era notorio que no había oído predicciones satisfactorias. Me pareció que, a pesar de su aparente indiferencia, daba a las revelaciones que escuchara una importancia que no merecían.
{During all that time she never turned a page: p184.jpg} Meantime, Mary Ingram, Amy and Louisa Eshton, declared they dared not go alone; and yet they all wished to go.
Entretanto, Mary Ingram, Amy Eshton y su hermana Louisa declararon que no se atrevían a ir solas a ver a la adivina, aunque no les faltaban deseos.

A negotiation was opened through the medium of the ambassador, Sam; and after much pacing to and fro, till, I think, the said Sam's calves must have ached with the exercise, permission was at last, with great difficulty, extorted from the rigorous Sibyl, for the three to wait upon her in a body.
Se entablaron negociaciones, con Sam como mediador, y tras muchas idas y venidas, la sibila, no sin dificultades, autorizó la entrada de tres muchachas en un solo grupo.

Their visit was not so still as Miss Ingram's had been: we heard hysterical giggling and little shrieks proceeding from the library; and at the end of about twenty minutes they burst the door open, and came running across the hall, as if they were half-scared out of their wits. "I am sure she is something not right!" they cried, one and all.

La visita no transcurrió tan silenciosa como la de Blanche. Oíamos grititos y risas histéricas procedentes de la biblioteca, hasta que, al cabo de veinte minutos, las muchachas aparecieron corriendo en el vestíbulo, como si huyeran de la adivina. -¡Debe de ser un ente del otro mundo! -gritaban todas-.
"She told us such things!
¡Qué cosas nos ha dicho!
She knows all about us!" and they sank breathless into the various seats the gentlemen hastened to bring them.
¡Sabe todos nuestros secretos! Y cayeron, como abrumadas, en los asientos que los caballeros galantemente les ofrecían.

Pressed for further explanation, they declared she had told them of things they had said and done when they were mere children; described books and ornaments they had in their boudoirs at home: keepsakes that different relations had presented to them.

Incitadas a explicarse, dijeron que aquella vieja les había contado cosas que ellas habían dicho y hecho siendo niñas; descrito libros y adornos que tenían en sus gabinetes; recordado los amigos que conocían.

They affirmed that she had even divined their thoughts, and had whispered in the ear of each the name of the person she liked best in the world, and informed them of what they most wished for. Here the gentlemen interposed with earnest petitions to be further enlightened on these two last-named points; but they got only blushes, ejaculations, tremors, and titters, in return for their importunity.
Afirmaron también que había adivinado sus pensamientos y cuchicheado al oído de cada una el nombre de la persona a quien más quería en el mundo.

The matrons, meantime, offered vinaigrettes and wielded fans; and again and again reiterated the expression of their concern that their warning had not been taken in time; and the elder gentlemen laughed, and the younger urged their services on the agitated fair ones.

Los caballeros solicitaron mayores aclaraciones sobre este último extremo, pero sólo obtuvieron rubores, exclamaciones y risas contenidas. Las matronas ofrecieron a las chicas sus frascos de sales, reprendiéndolas por no haber atendido sus consejos.
In the midst of the tumult, and while my eyes and ears were fully engaged in the scene before me, I heard a hem close at my elbow: I turned, and saw Sam.
Los caballeros de edad rieron y los jóvenes ofrecieron su ayuda a las conmovidas beldades. En medio de aquel tumulto, Sam, parándose ante mí, me habló:
"If you please, miss, the gipsy declares that there is another young single lady in the room who has not been to her yet, and she swears she will not go till she has seen all.
-Perdón, señorita: la gitana dice que hay una joven más en este salón y que no se irá hasta que la haya visto.
I thought it must be you: there is no one else for it.
Debe de ser usted, ya que no hay otra.
What shall I tell her?"
¿Qué le digo?
"Oh, I will go by all means," I answered: and I was glad of the unexpected opportunity to gratify my much-excited curiosity.
-Iré -dije, satisfecha de hallar ocasión de satisfacer mi excitada curiosidad.
I slipped out of the room, unobserved by any eye--for the company were gathered in one mass about the trembling trio just returned--and I closed the door quietly behind me.
Me deslicé fuera de la estancia sin ser notada -ya que la atención general estaba atraída por el tembloroso trío que acababa de regresar- y cerré la puerta tras de mí.
"If you like, miss," said Sam, "I'll wait in the hall for you; and if she frightens you, just call and I'll come in."
-Si lo desea, señorita -dijo Sam-, esperaré en el vestíbulo y así, si la vieja le asusta, me llama usted y entro en seguida.
"No, Sam, return to the kitchen: I am not in the least afraid."
-No, Sam: vuélvase a la cocina. No tengo temor alguno.
Nor was I; but I was a good deal interested and excited.
Lo que sentía en realidad era mucho interés y excitación.
The library looked tranquil enough as I entered it, and the Sibyl--if Sibyl she were--was seated snugly enough in an easy-chair at the chimney- corner.
Reinaba profunda tranquilidad en la biblioteca. La sibila -si tal era- estaba cómodamente sentada en un magnífico sillón junto a la chimenea.
She had on a red cloak and a black bonnet: or rather, a broad- brimmed gipsy hat, tied down with a striped handkerchief under her chin.
Llevaba un vestido rojo y un gorro negro -más bien un deshilachado sombrero de gitana y un pañuelo anudado bajo la barbilla.

An extinguished candle stood on the table; she was bending over the fire, and seemed reading in a little black book, like a prayer-book, by the light of the blaze: she muttered the words to herself, as most old women do, while she read; she did not desist immediately on my entrance: it appeared she wished to finish a paragraph.
Había sobre la mesa una bujía apagada y la vieja parecía leer, a la luz de la lumbre, un tomito negro, parecido a un devocionario. Leía en voz alta, como la mayoría de las viejas.
I stood on the rug and warmed my hands, which were rather cold with sitting at a distance from the drawing-room fire.
Me senté en la alfombra y me calenté las manos, que se me habían quedado ateridas.
I felt now as composed as ever I did in my life: there was nothing indeed in the gipsy's appearance to trouble one's calm.
Me sentía tranquila como nunca. En el aspecto de la gitana no había nada de inquietante.
She shut her book and slowly looked up; her hat-brim partially shaded her face, yet I could see, as she raised it, that it was a strange one.
Cerró el libro y me miró. Su pañuelo y las alas de su sombrero cubrían en gran parte su extraño rostro.

It looked all brown and black: elf- locks bristled out from beneath a white band which passed under her chin, and came half over her cheeks, or rather jaws: her eye confronted me at once, with a bold and direct gaze.
Era oscuro y moreno; los bucles de su cabello colgaban sobre sus mejillas. Me examinó con escudriñadora mirada.
"Well, and you want your fortune told?" she said, in a voice as decided as her glance, as harsh as her features.
-¿Quiere que le diga la buenaventura? -preguntó con voz tan penetrante como sus ojos y tan dura como sus facciones.
"I don't care about it, mother; you may please yourself: but I ought to warn you, I have no faith."
-No me interesa nada, abuela: si usted quiere... Pero le confieso que no creo en ninguna de esas cosas.
"It's like your impudence to say so: I expected it of you; I heard it in your step as you crossed the threshold."
-Esperaba que tuviese usted ese descaro: lo he comprendido por el ruido de sus pies al cruzar el umbral.
"Did you?
-¿Sí?
You've a quick ear."
Tiene usted buen oído.
"I have; and a quick eye and a quick brain."
-Y buen ojo y buena cabeza.
"You need them all in your trade."
-Bastante falta le harán para su trato.
"I do; especially when I've customers like you to deal with.
-Especialmente cuando encuentro clientes como usted.
Why don't you tremble?"
¿Cómo no se estremece?
"I'm not cold."
-Porque no tengo frío.
"Why don't you turn pale?"
-¿Cómo no palidece?
"I am not sick."
-Porque no estoy mal.
"Why don't you consult my art?"
-¿Cómo no quería consultar mi ciencia?
"I'm not silly."
-Porque no soy una necia.
The old crone "nichered" a laugh under her bonnet and bandage; she then drew out a short black pipe, and lighting it began to smoke.
La vieja emitió una carcajada cavernosa. Luego sacó una corta pipa y empezó a fumar.

Having indulged a while in this sedative, she raised her bent body, took the pipe from her lips, and while gazing steadily at the fire, said very deliberately--"You are cold; you are sick; and you are silly."

Después de haberse entregado a este placer, irguió su encorvado cuerpo, se quitó la pipa de los labios y, mirando fijamente el fuego, dijo subrayando las palabras: -Usted tiene frío, usted está enferma y usted es una necia.
"Prove it," I rejoined.
-Pruébemelo -dije.
"I will, in few words. You are cold, because you are alone: no contact strikes the fire from you that is in you.
-Lo haré en pocas palabras.

You are sick; because the best of feelings, the highest and the sweetest given to man, keeps far away from you. You are silly, because, suffer as you may, you will not beckon it to approach, nor will you stir one step to meet it where it waits you."

Tiene usted frío porque está muy sola; está mal, porque le falta el mejor de los sentimientos, el mayor y más dulce que puede experimentar el hombre, y es usted necia porque, sufriendo como sufre, no da una muestra ni inicia un paso para reunirse con el que la espera.
She again put her short black pipe to her lips, and renewed her smoking with vigour.
Volvió a aplicarse la pipa a los labios y fumó con renovada energía.
"You might say all that to almost any one who you knew lived as a solitary dependent in a great house."
-Eso es fácil de aplicar a cualquiera que esté como yo empleada en una gran casa y no tenga familia.
"I might say it to almost any one: but would it be true of almost any one?"
-Me sería fácil aplicarlo a casi todos los que dice, pero ¿con verdad?
"In my circumstances."
-Para quienes estén en mis circunstancias, sí.
"Yes; just so, in _your_ circumstances: but find me another precisely placed as you are."
-Señáleme alguien que se encuentre precisamente en las circunstancias de usted.
"It would be easy to find you thousands."
-Los hay a millares.
"You could scarcely find me one.
-Difícilmente encontraríamos uno.
If you knew it, you are peculiarly situated: very near happiness; yes, within reach of it.
No sé si sabe usted lo especialmente que se encuentra situada en la vida. Tiene la felicidad al alcance de su mano.
The materials are all prepared; there only wants a movement to combine them.
Los elementos de ella están preparados; sólo es preciso un movimiento que los combine.
Chance laid them somewhat apart; let them be once approached and bliss results."
Usted procura apartar las posibilidades. Deles una ocasión de florecer y fructificarán.
"I don't understand enigmas.
-No sé adivinar enigmas.
I never could guess a riddle in my life."
En mi vida no he acertado a descifrar ni un jeroglífico.
"If you wish me to speak more plainly, show me your palm."
-Si quiere que le hable más claramente, muéstreme la palma de su mano.
"And I must cross it with silver, I suppose?"
-Supongo que tendré que darle una moneda de plata, ¿no?
"To be sure."
-Por supuesto.
I gave her a shilling: she put it into an old stocking-foot which she took out of her pocket, and having tied it round and returned it, she told me to hold out my hand.
La entregué un chelín. Lo colocó en una media que sacó de la faltriquera y enrolló en torno a la moneda y me dijo que le enseñase la mano.
I did. She approached her face to the palm, and pored over it without touching it.
Examinó la palma sin tocarla.
"It is too fine," said she.
-Es demasiado lisa -dijo-.
"I can make nothing of such a hand as that; almost without lines: besides, what is in a palm?
Nada se puede leer en una mano como ésta. Casi no tiene líneas.
Destiny is not written there."
Además, el destino no está escrito aquí.
"I believe you," said I.
-Lo creo -dije.
"No," she continued, "it is in the face: on the forehead, about the eyes, in the lines of the mouth.
-No; está escrito en el rostro; en la frente, en torno a los ojos, en los ojos mismos, en las líneas de la boca.
Kneel, and lift up your head."
Arrodíllese y déjeme examinar su cara.
"Ah! now you are coming to reality," I said, as I obeyed her.
-Ahora se aproxima usted a la realidad.
"I shall begin to put some faith in you presently."
Empiezo a confiar en usted.
I knelt within half a yard of her.
Me arrodillé a media vara de ella.
She stirred the fire, so that a ripple of light broke from the disturbed coal: the glare, however, as she sat, only threw her face into deeper shadow: mine, it illumined.
Atizó el fuego hasta que la claridad que brotó de la leña removida iluminó mi rostro. Ella procuraba esquivar el suyo.
"I wonder with what feelings you came to me to-night," she said, when she had examined me a while.
-Me extrañan los sentimientos que experimenta usted-dijo, mientras me examinaba-.

"I wonder what thoughts are busy in your heart during all the hours you sit in yonder room with the fine people flitting before you like shapes in a magic-lantern: just as little sympathetic communion passing between you and them as if they were really mere shadows of human forms, and not the actual substance."

Me maravillan las impresiones que ha sentido su corazón durante las horas que ha estado sentada en aquel cuarto, ante gentes que desfilaban frente a usted como siluetas proyectadas por una linterna mágica. Entre ellos y usted había tan poca simpatía como si ellos fueran meras sombras de formas humanas y no seres reales.
"I feel tired often, sleepy sometimes, but seldom sad."
-Me siento aburrida entre esas personas, y alguna vez hasta me da sueño, pero rara vez me encuentro a disgusto con ellas.
"Then you have some secret hope to buoy you up and please you with whispers of the future?"
-¿Confía usted en llegar a librarse en el porvenir de la vida que lleva?
"Not I. The utmost I hope is, to save money enough out of my earnings to set up a school some day in a little house rented by myself."
-Lo que más espero es llegar a ahorrar algún dinero para montar con él una escuela en alguna casa alquilada...
"A mean nutriment for the spirit to exist on: and sitting in that window- seat (you see I know your habits )--" "You have learned them from the servants."
-¿De modo que es en eso en lo que sueña cuando se sienta en su rincón junto a la ventana...? Ya ve que conozco sus costumbres.
"Ah! you think yourself sharp.
-Se habrá enterado de ellas por los criados.
Well, perhaps I have: to speak truth, I have an acquaintance with one of them, Mrs. Poole--"
Acaso haya acertado usted. A decir verdad, conozco a una sirviente de aquí: a Grace Poole.
I started to my feet when I heard the name.
Di un salto al oír aquel nombre.
"You have--have you?" thought I; "there is diablerie in the business after all, then!"
-¿Usted, usted..? -dije-. ¡Aquí hay alguna trama diabólica!
"Don't be alarmed," continued the strange being; "she's a safe hand is Mrs. Poole: close and quiet; any one may repose confidence in her.
-No se alarme -repuso-. Esa Poole es muy discreta y se puede confiar en ella...
But, as I was saying: sitting in that window-seat, do you think of nothing but your future school?
Pues como le iba diciendo, cuando se sienta usted en su rincón, ¿no piensa más que en su futura escuela?
Have you no present interest in any of the company who occupy the sofas and chairs before you?
¿No siente algún interés por los que están en el salón? ¿No suele usted contemplar el rostro de ninguno?
Is there not one face you study? one figure whose movements you follow with at least curiosity?"
¿No hay ni siquiera una figura cuyos movimientos siga usted, si no con otro interés, por curiosidad?
"I like to observe all the faces and all the figures."
-Miro todos los rostros; miro a todos los concurrentes.
"But do you never single one from the rest--or it may be, two?"
-Pero ¿a ninguno -o acaso a dos- con mayor interés? -Sí; lo hago.
"I do frequently; when the gestures or looks of a pair seem telling a tale: it amuses me to watch them."
Cuando las miradas o los ademanes de cierta pareja parece que me narran un cuento, me divierte mirarlos.
"What tale do you like best to hear?"
-¿Y qué cuento le narran?
"Oh, I have not much choice!
-No hay duda sobre el caso.
They generally run on the same theme--courtship; and promise to end in the same catastrophe--marriage."
El cuento se limita a un cortejo y el catastrófico desenlace que es de suponer: un matrimonio...
"And do you like that monotonous theme?"
-¿Y ello le parece aburrido?
"Positively, I don't care about it: it is nothing to me."
-Realmente, no tiene interés para mí.
"Nothing to you?
-¿De verdad?
When a lady, young and full of life and health, charming with beauty and endowed with the gifts of rank and fortune, sits and smiles in the eyes of a gentleman you--"
Cuando una señorita, llena de vida y salud, encantadora, adornada con todas las dotes del nacimiento elevado y de la riqueza, se sienta y sonríe a un caballero a quien usted...
"I what?"
-Yo, ¿qué?
"You know--and perhaps think well of."
-A quien usted conoce y quizá aprecia.
"I don't know the gentlemen here.
-Yo no conozco apenas a los caballeros que están aquí. Casi no he cambiado ni una sílaba con ninguno.

I have scarcely interchanged a syllable with one of them; and as to thinking well of them, I consider some respectable, and stately, and middle-aged, and others young, dashing, handsome, and lively: but certainly they are all at liberty to be the recipients of whose smiles they please, without my feeling disposed to consider the transaction of any moment to me."
A unos les considero demasiado graves y respetables y a otros demasiado guapos y jóvenes. Y todos están en condiciones de recibir cuantas sonrisas les plazcan, sin que tengan por qué ocuparse de mí.
"You don't know the gentlemen here?
-¿De modo que usted no conoce a los caballeros que hay en esta casa?
You have not exchanged a syllable with one of them?
¿No ha cambiado ni una palabra con ninguno de ellos?
Will you say that of the master of the house!"
¿Dirá usted lo mismo del dueño de la casa?
"He is not at home."
-No está ahora aquí.
"A profound remark!
-¡Profunda e ingeniosa observación!

A most ingenious quibble! He went to Millcote this morning, and will be back here to-night or to-morrow: does that circumstance exclude him from the list of your acquaintance--blot him, as it were, out of existence?"

Cierto que se ha ido esta mañana a Millcote y que no volverá hasta entrada la noche o hasta mañana por la mañana, pero ¿acaso tal circunstancia se excluye de la lista de los conocidos de usted? ¿Acaso deja de existir por eso?
"No; but I can scarcely see what Mr. Rochester has to do with the theme you had introduced."
Pero no comprendo qué tiene que ver Mr. Rochester con el tema que usted menciona.

"I was talking of ladies smiling in the eyes of gentlemen; and of late so many smiles have been shed into Mr. Rochester's eyes that they overflow like two cups filled above the brim: have you never remarked that?"
-Yo hablaba de las señoras que sonríen a los caballeros, y tantas sonrisas femeninas ha recibido Mr. Rochester, que creo que podría llenar un almacén con ellas...
"Mr. Rochester has a right to enjoy the society of his guests."
-Mr. Rochester tiene perfecto derecho a disfrutar del trato de sus invitados.
"No question about his right: but have you never observed that, of all the tales told here about matrimony, Mr. Rochester has been favoured with the most lively and the most continuous?"
-Nadie discute tal derecho, pero ¿ha reparado en que cuanto se ha hablado aquí a propósito de matrimonios concierne principalmente a Mr. Rochester?
"The eagerness of a listener quickens the tongue of a narrator."
-El interés del que escucha estimula la lengua del que habla -dije, más que para la gitana, para mí misma.
I said this rather to myself than to the gipsy, whose strange talk, voice, manner, had by this time wrapped me in a kind of dream.
La extraña voz de aquella mujer y sus modales me habían sumergido en una especie de extraño sueño.

One unexpected sentence came from her lips after another, till I got involved in a web of mystification; and wondered what unseen spirit had been sitting for weeks by my heart watching its workings and taking record of every pulse.
Inesperadas palabras brotaban de sus labios una tras otra, envolviéndome en un manto de cosas desconocidas y misteriosas.

"Eagerness of a listener!" repeated she: "yes; Mr. Rochester has sat by the hour, his ear inclined to the fascinating lips that took such delight in their task of communicating; and Mr. Rochester was so willing to receive and looked so grateful for the pastime given him; you have noticed this?"
Sí; Mr. Rochester se ha sentado a veces con el oído atento a los fascinadores labios que con tanto interés le hablan.
"Grateful!
-¿Agradecido?
I cannot remember detecting gratitude in his face."
No es precisamente gratitud lo que he creído ver en su rostro.
"Detecting! You have analysed, then.
-¿Así que le ha estado observando?
And what did you detect, if not gratitude?"
¿Y qué ha creído ver, si no gratitud?
I said nothing.
No contesté.
"You have seen love: have you not?--and, looking forward, you have seen him married, and beheld his bride happy?"
-Ha visto usted amor, ¿no es eso? Y luego ha creído ya verle casado y feliz en su matrimonio...
Not exactly. Your witch's skill is rather at fault sometimes."
No es eso precisamente.
"What the devil have you seen, then?"
-Entonces, ¿qué demonios ha visto usted?
"Never mind: I came here to inquire, not to confess.
-No interesa. Yo vengo a saber, no a confesar.
Is it known that Mr. Rochester is to be married?"
¿Se casará Mr. Rochester?
"Yes; and to the beautiful Miss Ingram."
-Sí: con la hermosa Miss Ingram.
"Shortly?"
-¿Pronto?
"Appearances would warrant that conclusion: and, no doubt (though, with an audacity that wants chastising out of you, you seem to question it), they will be a superlatively happy pair.
-Las apariencias conducen a esa conclusión. Y (pese a la reprensible audacia con que usted juzga estas cosas) probablemente será un matrimonio feliz.
He must love such a handsome, noble, witty, accomplished lady; and probably she loves him, or, if not his person, at least his purse.
Él debe de amar necesariamente a una señora tan bella, noble y cumplida, y ella probablemente le ama a él, y si no a su persona, al menos su bolsa...
I know she considers the Rochester estate eligible to the last degree; though (God pardon me!)
Estoy segura de que considera muy digno de ser su esposo a Mr.
I told her something on that point about an hour ago which made her look wondrous grave: the corners of her mouth fell half an inch.
Rochester, aunque (¡Dios me perdone!) yo la he dicho hace una hora algo que hizo ponerse seria su mirada y plegarse su boca...
I would advise her blackaviced suitor to look out: if another comes, with a longer or clearer rent-roll,--he's dished--"
La predije que si apareciese otro pretendiente más rico, ella despreciaría a Rochester.
"But, mother, I did not come to hear Mr. Rochester's fortune: I came to hear my own; and you have told me nothing of it."
-Bien, abuela, pero yo no he venido a saber la buenaventura de Mr. Rochester, sino la mía.
"Your fortune is yet doubtful: when I examined your face, one trait contradicted another.
-Su suerte está aún muy dudosa: algunos de los rasgos de su rostro contradicen los demás.
Chance has meted you a measure of happiness: that I know.
El destino le ofrece una posibilidad de dicha; eso es evidente.
I knew it before I came here this evening.
Yo lo sabía antes de venir aquí esta noche.
She has laid it carefully on one side for you. I saw her do it.
La suerte ha reservado un rinconcito para usted.
It depends on yourself to stretch out your hand, and take it up: but whether you will do so, is the problem I study.
De usted depende coger con la mano la fortuna que le ofrecen. Que lo haga o no, es discutible.
Kneel again on the rug."
Arrodíllese otra vez en la alfombra.
"Don't keep me long; the fire scorches me."
-Procure que no sea por mucho tiempo. Me molesta el fuego.
I knelt.
Volví a arrodillarme.
She did not stoop towards me, but only gazed, leaning back in her chair. She began muttering,--
No se inclinó hacia mí. Se limitó a mirarme, echándose hacia atrás en su silla, y comenzó a murmurar:

"The flame flickers in the eye; the eye shines like dew; it looks soft and full of feeling; it smiles at my jargon: it is susceptible; impression follows impression through its clear sphere; where it ceases to smile, it is sad; an unconscious lassitude weighs on the lid: that signifies melancholy resulting from loneliness.
En sus claras pupilas, las impresiones se suceden a las impresiones. Cuando dejan de sonreír, se entristecen y pesa sobre ellos una inconsciente laxitud, hija de la melancolía derivada de su soledad.

It turns from me; it will not suffer further scrutiny; it seems to deny, by a mocking glance, the truth of the discoveries I have already made,--to disown the charge both of sensibility and chagrin: its pride and reserve only confirm me in my opinion.

Ahora se separan de mí, incapaces de tolerar más escrutinios y parecen negar, con una mirada de burla, la verdad de los descubrimientos que yo acabo de hacer respeto a su sensibilidad y a su tristeza. Pero su orgullo y su reserva no hacen más que confirmarse en mi opinión.

"As to the mouth, it delights at times in laughter; it is disposed to impart all that the brain conceives; though I daresay it would be silent on much the heart experiences. Mobile and flexible, it was never intended to be compressed in the eternal silence of solitude: it is a mouth which should speak much and smile often, and have human affection for its interlocutor.

»En cuanto a la boca, le gusta a veces reír, para hacer sentir a los demás lo que su alma experimenta, aunque me parece muy reservada cuando se trata de ciertos sentimientos del corazón. »No veo obstáculos a que goce de una suerte feliz, sino en ese entrecejo, un entrecejo orgulloso, que parece querer decir: "Yo puedo vivir sola, si el respeto de mí misma y las circunstancias me obligaran a ello.
That feature too is propitious.
No necesito vender mi alma a un comprador de felicidad.
"I see no enemy to a fortunate issue but in the brow; and that brow professes to say,--'I can live alone, if self-respect, and circumstances require me so to do. I need not sell my soul to buy bliss.
Poseo un escondido e innato tesoro que me bastará para vivir si he de prescindir de todo placer ajeno a mí misma, en el caso de que hubiese de pagar por la dicha un precio demasiado caro."
I have an inward treasure born with me, which can keep me alive if all extraneous delights should be withheld, or offered only at a price I cannot afford to give.'
En la frente se lee: "Mi razón es sólida y no permitirá a los sentimientos entregarse a sus desordenadas pasiones.

The forehead declares, 'Reason sits firm and holds the reins, and she will not let the feelings burst away and hurry her to wild chasms. The passions may rage furiously, like true heathens, as they are; and the desires may imagine all sorts of vain things: but judgment shall still have the last word in every argument, and the casting vote in every decision.
Podrán las pasiones bramar y los deseos imaginar toda clase de cosas vanas, pero la sensatez dirá siempre la última palabra sobre el asunto y emitirá el voto decisivo en todas las determinaciones.
Strong wind, earthquake-shock, and fire may pass by: but I shall follow the guiding of that still small voice which interprets the dictates of conscience.'
Podrán producirse violentos huracanes, impetuosos temblores de tierra, ardorosas llamas, pero yo seguiré siempre los dictados de esa voz interior que interpreta los dictados de la conciencia."
"Well said, forehead; your declaration shall be respected.
»Bien pensado. Lo que se lee en su frente es digno de todo respeto.
I have formed my plans--right plans I deem them--and in them I have attended to the claims of conscience, the counsels of reason.
En cuanto a mí, he formado mis planes y los desarrollaré según los dictados de la conciencia y los consejos de la razón.

I know how soon youth would fade and bloom perish, if, in the cup of bliss offered, but one dreg of shame, or one flavour of remorse were detected; and I do not want sacrifice, sorrow, dissolution--such is not my taste.
Sé lo pronto que pasa la juventud y desaparece la lozanía cuando la vergüenza o el remordimiento los amargan.
I wish to foster, not to blight--to earn gratitude, not to wring tears of blood--no, nor of brine: my harvest must be in smiles, in endearments, in sweet--That will do.
Deseo consolar y no brillar, conseguir la gratitud de los demás y no crear lágrimas de sangre. No deseo poner hiel en las cosas, sino infundirlas dulzura, sonrisas, encanto...
I think I rave in a kind of exquisite delirium. I should wish now to protract this moment _ad infinitum_; but I dare not.
Me parece vivir un sueño inefable.
So far I have governed myself thoroughly. I have acted as I inwardly swore I would act; but further might try me beyond my strength.
Quisiera prolongar este momento ad infinitum, pero no es posible.
Rise, Miss Eyre: leave me; the play is played out'."
Y ahora, Miss Eyre, levántese y váyase. El juego ha terminado.
Where was I? Did I wake or sleep?
¿Dónde me encontraba?
Had I been dreaming? Did I dream still?
¿Soñaba o estaba despierta?
The old woman's voice had changed: her accent, her gesture, and all were familiar to me as my own face in a glass--as the speech of my own tongue.
La voz de la vieja había cambiado y sus ademanes y su voz me eran tan familiares como mi propia imagen en un espejo, como el sonido de mi propia voz.
I got up, but did not go.
Me incorporé, pero no me fui.
I looked; I stirred the fire, and I looked again: but she drew her bonnet and her bandage closer about her face, and again beckoned me to depart.
La miré. Ella se quitaba el gorro y el pañuelo y me ordenaba de nuevo que marchase.
The flame illuminated her hand stretched out: roused now, and on the alert for discoveries, I at once noticed that hand.
La llama iluminaba su mano y reconocí aquella mano, y hasta vi en su dedo meñique el anillo y la piedra preciosa que viera un centenar de veces.
Again I looked at the face; which was no longer turned from me--on the contrary, the bonnet was doffed, the bandage displaced, the head advanced.
Volví a mirar aquel rostro, que ya no se esquivaba. Al contrario, libre ya de sombrero y pañuelo, se inclinaba hacia el mío. -¿Me conoce ahora, Jane? -preguntó la voz familiar.
"Well, Jane, do you know me?" asked the familiar voice.
-Si se quita el vestido encarnado, señor...
"Only take off the red cloak, sir, and then--"
-Está muy fuerte el cordón.
"But the string is in a knot--help me."
Ayúdeme a soltarlo.
"Break it, sir."
-Rómpalo.
"There, then--'Off, ye lendings!'"
-¡Ea, ya está! -Y Mr.
And Mr. Rochester stepped out of his disguise.
Rochester se libró de su disfraz.
"Now, sir, what a strange idea!"
-¡Qué idea tan original ha tenido usted, señor!
"But well carried out, eh? Don't you think so?"
-Y creo que la he realizado felizmente, ¿no? -Con las señoras me parece que sí.
"But not with you?"
-¿Y con usted?
"You did not act the character of a gipsy with me."
-No procedió conmigo como una gitana.
"What character did I act? My own?"
-Pues ¿cómo procedí?
"No; some unaccountable one. In short, I believe you have been trying to draw me out--or in; you have been talking nonsense to make me talk nonsense.
-Usted ha hablado cosas absurdas para hacerme hablar a mí del mismo modo.
It is scarcely fair, sir."
Eso no está bien, señor.
"Do you forgive me, Jane?"
-¿Me perdona, Jane?
"I cannot tell till I have thought it all over.
-Primero tengo que pensarlo.
If, on reflection, I find I have fallen into no great absurdity, I shall try to forgive you; but it was not right."
Si pensándolo deduzco que no he cometido grandes absurdos, le perdonaré. Pero no está bien, señor, lo repito.
"Oh, you have been very correct--very careful, very sensible."
-¡Bah! Usted ha procedido muy correctamente, con mucha cautela, con mucha sensatez.
I reflected, and thought, on the whole, I had.
Reflexioné en efecto.
It was a comfort; but, indeed, I had been on my guard almost from the beginning of the interview.
Desde el principio había permanecido en guardia, sospechando alguna broma en todo aquello.

Something of masquerade I suspected. I knew gipsies and fortune-tellers did not express themselves as this seeming old woman had expressed herself; besides I had noted her feigned voice, her anxiety to conceal her features.
Sabía que las gitanas y las adivinas no se expresan en los términos que lo hiciera la supuesta vieja. Había notado, además, la voz fingida, el afán de ocultar las facciones.
But my mind had been running on Grace Poole--that living enigma, that mystery of mysteries, as I considered her.
Y pensé en Grace Poole, aquel enigma viviente, aquel misterio de misterios, según yo la consideraba.
I had never thought of Mr. Rochester.
Mas no se me había ocurrido pensar en Mr. Rochester.
"Well," said he, "what are you musing about?
-Bien -dijo él-. ¿Qué opina usted?
What does that grave smile signify?"
¿Qué significa esa sonrisa?
"Wonder and self-congratulation, sir.
-Asombro y satisfacción de mí misma, señor.
I have your permission to retire now, I suppose?"
¿Puedo retirarme?
"No; stay a moment; and tell me what the people in the drawing-room yonder are doing."
-No: quédese un momento y dígame lo que estaban haciendo en el salón los invitados.
"Discussing the gipsy, I daresay."
-Hablando de la gitana.
"Sit down!--Let me hear what they said about me."
-Siéntese y cuénteme lo que decían.
"I had better not stay long, sir; it must be near eleven o'clock.
-Ya es tarde; son cerca de las once.
Oh, are you aware, Mr. Rochester, that a stranger has arrived here since you left this morning?"
¿No sabe, Mr. Rochester, que ha venido un forastero?
"A stranger!--no; who can it be?
-¿Un forastero? ¿Quién puede ser?
I expected no one; is he gone?"
No espero a ninguno. ¿Se fue?
"No; he said he had known you long, and that he could take the liberty of installing himself here till you returned." "The devil he did!
-No. Indicó que le conocía a usted hace tiempo y que podía tomarse la libertad de esperar en esta casa hasta que volviera.
Did he give his name?"
-¿Dijo su nombre?
"His name is Mason, sir; and he comes from the West Indies; from Spanish Town, in Jamaica, I think."
-Se llama Mason, señor, y creo que viene de Puerto España.
Mr. Rochester was standing near me; he had taken my hand, as if to lead me to a chair.
Mr. Rochester había tomado mi mano como para conducirme a una silla.
As I spoke he gave my wrist a convulsive grip; the smile on his lips froze: apparently a spasm caught his breath.
Al oírme, me la apretó convulsivamente, la sonrisa despareció de sus labios y un estremecimiento recorrió su cuerpo.

"Mason!--the West Indies!" he said, in the tone one might fancy a speaking automaton to enounce its single words; "Mason!--the West Indies!" he reiterated; and he went over the syllables three times, growing, in the intervals of speaking, whiter than ashes: he hardly seemed to know what he was doing.
¡Mason, el indiano! -repitió. Se había puesto pálido como la ceniza, y reiteró hasta tres veces la misma frase, como sin darse cuenta de lo que decía.
"Do you feel ill, sir?" I inquired.
-¿Se siente mal, señor? -pregunté.
"Jane, I've got a blow; I've got a blow, Jane!" He staggered.
-Estoy anonadado, Jane.
"Oh, lean on me, sir."
Me tambaleo. -Apóyese en mí, señor.
"Jane, you offered me your shoulder once before; let me have it now."
-Es la segunda vez que me ofrece su brazo. Permítame. -Sí, sí, señor.
"Yes, sir, yes; and my arm."
Se sentó y me hizo sentar.
He sat down, and made me sit beside him. Holding my hand in both his own, he chafed it; gazing on me, at the same time, with the most troubled and dreary look.
Cogió mi mano entre las suyas y me contempló con turbados ojos.
"My little friend!" said he, "I wish I were in a quiet island with only you; and trouble, and danger, and hideous recollections removed from me."
-Amiguita mía -dijo-, quisiera estar solo con usted en una isla desierta, lejos de turbaciones, peligros y odiosos recuerdos.
"Can I help you, sir?--I'd give my life to serve you."
-¿Puedo servirle en algo, señor? Daría mi vida por ayudarle.
"Jane, if aid is wanted, I'll seek it at your hands; I promise you that."
-Si necesito su ayuda, Jane, la solicitaré. Se lo prometo.
"Thank you, sir.
-Gracias, señor.
Tell me what to do,--I'll try, at least, to do it."
Dígame lo que debo hacer.
"Fetch me now, Jane, a glass of wine from the dining-room: they will be at supper there; and tell me if Mason is with them, and what he is doing."
-En este momento, Jane, tráigame del comedor un vaso de vino. Deben de estar comiendo ya.
I went.
Dígame si Mason está con ellos y lo que hace.

I found all the party in the dining-room at supper, as Mr. Rochester had said; they were not seated at table,--the supper was arranged on the sideboard; each had taken what he chose, and they stood about here and there in groups, their plates and glasses in their hands.

Encontré a todos en el comedor, en efecto. La cena estaba colocada en el aparador y cada uno había tomado lo que se le antojara, colocándose aquí y allá en grupos, y sosteniendo en las manos platos y vasos.
Every one seemed in high glee; laughter and conversation were general and animated.
Reían alegremente y las conversaciones era muy animadas.
Mr. Mason stood near the fire, talking to Colonel and Mrs. Dent, and appeared as merry as any of them.
Mr. Mason estaba junto al fuego, hablando con Mr. y Mrs.
I filled a wine-glass (I saw Miss Ingram watch me frowningly as I did so: she thought I was taking a liberty, I daresay), and I returned to the library.
Blanche Ingram me contemplaba como si pensase que me tomaba una libertad increíble. Volví a la biblioteca.
Mr. Rochester's extreme pallor had disappeared, and he looked once more firm and stern.
La palidez de Mr. Rochester había desaparecido y se mostraba otra vez firme y tranquilo.
He took the glass from my hand.
Tomó el vaso.
"Here is to your health, ministrant spirit!" he said. He swallowed the contents and returned it to me.
-¡A la salud de usted, amable amiga! -dijo vaciando el vaso y devolviéndomelo-.
"What are they doing, Jane?"
¿Qué están haciendo, Jane?
"Laughing and talking, sir."
-Riendo y hablando, señor.
"They don't look grave and mysterious, as if they had heard something strange?"
-¿No tienen un aspecto grave y misterioso, como si hubiesen oído algo extraño?
"Not at all: they are full of jests and gaiety."
-No: están muy alegres.
"And Mason?"
-¿Y Mason?
"He was laughing too."
-Tan alegre como los demás.
"If all these people came in a body and spat at me, what would you do, Jane?"
-Si todas esas gentes me atacaran en masa, ¿qué haría usted?
"Turn them out of the room, sir, if I could."
-Arrojarlos de aquí, señor, si me era posible.
"But if I were to go to them, and they only looked at me coldly, and whispered sneeringly amongst each other, and then dropped off and left me one by one, what then? Would you go with them?"
-Y si yo fuera a su encuentro, y todos me acogieran con frialdad y luego, uno a uno, despreciativamente, se alejaran de mí, ¿les seguiría usted?-interrogó, con una ligera sonrisa.
"I rather think not, sir: I should have more pleasure in staying with you."
-Al contrario, señor: entonces me sería más grato quedarme con usted.
"To comfort me?"
-¿Para consolarme?
"Yes, sir, to comfort you, as well as I could."
-Sí, si estaba a mi alcance.
"And if they laid you under a ban for adhering to me?"
-¿Y si la vituperaran por quedarse conmigo?
"I, probably, should know nothing about their ban; and if I did, I should care nothing about it."
-Seguramente no me enteraría de sus vituperios, y de enterarme me tendría sin cuidado.
"Then, you could dare censure for my sake?"
-¿Así que arrostraría usted por mí incluso que la criticasen?
"I could dare it for the sake of any friend who deserved my adherence; as you, I am sure, do."
-Creo que lo haría por cualquier amigo a quien apreciara, como creo que usted lo haría también.
"Go back now into the room; step quietly up to Mason, and whisper in his ear that Mr. Rochester is come and wishes to see him: show him in here and then leave me."
-Bien. Vaya al comedor y diga a Mason en un aparte que el señor Rochester ha vuelto y desea hablarle.
"Yes, sir."
Tráigale aquí y márchese luego.
I did his behest.
-Sí, señor.
The company all stared at me as I passed straight among them.
Hice lo que deseaba. Al pasar entre ellos, todos me miraron.
I sought Mr. Mason, delivered the message, and preceded him from the room: I ushered him into the library, and then I went upstairs.
