Transmití el mensaje a Mr. Mason, le precedí hasta la biblioteca y luego subí las escaleras.
At a late hour, after I had been in bed some time, I heard the visitors repair to their chambers: I distinguished Mr. Rochester's voice, and heard him say, "This way, Mason; this is your room."
Una hora más tarde, cuando ya llevaba rato en el lecho, sentí a los invitados entrar en sus habitaciones. Oí la voz de Rochester diciendo: -Por aquí, Mason: ésta es su alcoba.
He spoke cheerfully: the gay tones set my heart at ease. I was soon asleep.
La voz era alegre y despreocupada. Sentí el corazón aliviado y me dormí en seguida.
I had forgotten to draw my curtain, which I usually did, and also to let down my window-blind.
Había olvidado correr las cortinillas y cerrar las contraventanas.

The consequence was, that when the moon, which was full and bright (for the night was fine), came in her course to that space in the sky opposite my casement, and looked in at me through the unveiled panes, her glorious gaze roused me.
La consecuencia fue que cuando la luna, llena y brillante en la noche serena, alcanzó determinada altura en el cielo, su espléndida luz, pasando a través de los cristales, me despertó.
Awaking in the dead of night, I opened my eyes on her disk--silver-white and crystal clear.
El disco plateado y cristalino de la luna era muy bello, pero me producía un efecto en exceso solemne.
It was beautiful, but too solemn; I half rose, and stretched my arm to draw the curtain.
Me incorporé y alargué el brazo para correr las cortinillas.
Good God! What a cry!
¡Dios mío, qué grito oí en aquel instante!
The night--its silence--its rest, was rent in twain by a savage, a sharp, a shrilly sound that ran from end to end of Thornfield Hall.
Un sonido agudo, salvaje, estremecedor, que rompió la calma de la noche, recorriendo de extremo a extremo Thornfiel Hall.
My pulse stopped: my heart stood still; my stretched arm was paralysed.
Mi pulso, mi corazón y mi brazo se paralizaron.

The cry died, and was not renewed. Indeed, whatever being uttered that fearful shriek could not soon repeat it: not the widest-winged condor on the Andes could, twice in succession, send out such a yell from the cloud shrouding his eyrie. The thing delivering such utterance must rest ere it could repeat the effort.
El grito se apagó y no se repitió.
It came out of the third storey; for it passed overhead.
Procedía sin duda del tercer piso.
And overhead--yes, in the room just above my chamber-ceiling--I now heard a struggle: a deadly one it seemed from the noise; and a half-smothered voice shouted--
Encima de mí se sentía ahora rumor de lucha. Una voz medio sofocada gritó tres veces:
"Help! help! help!" three times rapidly.
-¡Socorro! Oí nuevos ruidos sobre el techo y una voz clamó:
"Will no one come?" it cried; and then, while the staggering and stamping went on wildly, I distinguished through plank and plaster:-- "Rochester! Rochester! for God's sake, come!"
-¡Rochester: ven, por amor de Dios!
A chamber-door opened: some one ran, or rushed, along the gallery.
Se abrió una puerta, alguien corrió por la galería. Sentí nuevas pisadas en el piso alto y luego una caída.
Another step stamped on the flooring above and something fell; and there was silence.
El silencio se restableció. Acerté a ponerme alguna ropa, a pesar de que el horror paralizaba mis miembros.
I had put on some clothes, though horror shook all my limbs; I issued from my apartment.
Salí de mi dormitorio. Todos los invitados habían despertado.
The sleepers were all aroused: ejaculations, terrified murmurs sounded in every room; door after door unclosed; one looked out and another looked out; the gallery filled.
Se sentían exclamaciones y murmullos de horror en todos los cuartos, las puertas se abrían una tras otra y la galería se llenaba de gente.

Gentlemen and ladies alike had quitted their beds; and "Oh! what is it?"--"Who is hurt?"--"What has happened?"--"Fetch a light!"--"Is it fire?"--"Are there robbers?"--"Where shall we run?" was demanded confusedly on all hands.
Se oía decir: «¿Qué es?», «¿Qué pasa?», «Enciendan luz», «¿Hay fuego?», «¿Son ladrones?»
But for the moonlight they would have been in complete darkness.
Salvo la luz de la luna, que entraba por las ventanas, la oscuridad era completa.
They ran to and fro; they crowded together: some sobbed, some stumbled: the confusion was inextricable.
Todos corrían de un lado para otro, tropezándose, pisándose. Reinaba una confusión indescriptible.
"Where the devil is Rochester?" cried Colonel Dent.
-¿Dónde diablo está Rochester? -gritó el coronel Dent-.
"I cannot find him in his bed."
No le encuentro en su alcoba.
"Here! here!" was shouted in return.
-Aquí, aquí -se oyó contestar-.
"Be composed, all of you: I'm coming."
Tranquilícense; ya vuelvo.
And the door at the end of the gallery opened, and Mr. Rochester advanced with a candle: he had just descended from the upper storey.
La puerta del final de la galería se abrió y el dueño de la casa apareció llevando una bujía.
One of the ladies ran to him directly; she seized his arm: it was Miss Ingram.
Venía del piso alto. Miss Ingram corrió hacia él y le asió de un brazo.
"What awful event has taken place?" said she.
-¿Qué ha ocurrido?
"Speak! let us know the worst at once!"
Díganoslo en seguida, sea lo que fuere.
"But don't pull me down or strangle me," he replied: for the Misses Eshton were clinging about him now; and the two dowagers, in vast white wrappers, were bearing down on him like ships in full sail.

-¡Pero no me estrangulen! -repuso Rochester, viendo que las Eshton caían también sobre él y que las dos viudas, vestidas con sus amplias batas de noche, se dirigían también a su encuentro, como buques navegando a toda vela.
"All's right!--all's right!" he cried.
-No pasa nada, no pasa nada -agregó-.
"It's a mere rehearsal of Much Ado about Nothing.
Mucho ruido y pocas nueces.
Ladies, keep off, or I shall wax dangerous."
Sepárense, señoras: las voy a poner perdidas de cera.
And dangerous he looked: his black eyes darted sparks.
Ofrecía un aspecto terrible: sus ojos centelleaban.
Calming himself by an effort, he added--
Dominándose con visible esfuerzo continuó:
"A servant has had the nightmare; that is all.
Eso es todo. Se trata de una persona irritable y nerviosa.
She's an excitable, nervous person: she construed her dream into an apparition, or something of that sort, no doubt; and has taken a fit with fright.
Ha soñado con una aparición y el miedo le ha producido un ataque. Les ruego que vuelvan todos a sus cuartos.
Now, then, I must see you all back into your rooms; for, till the house is settled, she cannot be looked after.
Caballeros: den ejemplo a las señoras. Miss Ingram: estoy seguro que usted sabrá dominar ese inmotivado terror.
Gentlemen, have the goodness to set the ladies the example. Miss Ingram, I am sure you will not fail in evincing superiority to idle terrors.
Amy y Louisa: vuélvanse a sus nidos, como dos dóciles palomitas que son.
Amy and Louisa, return to your nests like a pair of doves, as you are. Mesdames" (to the dowagers), "you will take cold to a dead certainty, if you stay in this chill gallery any longer."
Y ustedes, señoras -dijo, dirigiéndose a las viudas-, se acatarrarán si siguen más tiempo así en esta galería helada.
And so, by dint of alternate coaxing and commanding, he contrived to get them all once more enclosed in their separate dormitories.
Alternando las órdenes y las palabras amables, logró que todos volviesen a sus lechos.
I did not wait to be ordered back to mine, but retreated unnoticed, as unnoticed I had left it.
Yo me retiré al mío tan silenciosamente como lo había abandonado.
Not, however, to go to bed: on the contrary, I began and dressed myself carefully.
Pero no me acosté: antes bien, me vestí por completo para prepararme a toda contingencia.

The sounds I had heard after the scream, and the words that had been uttered, had probably been heard only by me; for they had proceeded from the room above mine: but they assured me that it was not a servant's dream which had thus struck horror through the house; and that the explanation Mr. Rochester had given was merely an invention framed to pacify his guests.

Los ruidos y exclamaciones que yo oyera acaso no los hubiesen sentido los demás, ya que procedían del cuarto situado sobre el mío. Así, yo estaba segura de que lo de la pesadilla de una criada había sido mera invención para tranquilizar a los invitados.
I dressed, then, to be ready for emergencies. When dressed, I sat a long time by the window looking out over the silent grounds and silvered fields and waiting for I knew not what.
Una vez vestida, permanecí junto a la ventana, mirando los campos silenciosos iluminados por la luna, en espera no sabía de qué.
It seemed to me that some event must follow the strange cry, struggle, and call.
Suponía que seguiría algún acontecimiento al grito, la lucha y la petición de socorro.
No: stillness returned: each murmur and movement ceased gradually, and in about an hour Thornfield Hall was again as hushed as a desert.
La tranquilidad renació. Cesaron gradualmente movimientos y murmullos y Thornfield Hall quedó silencioso como un desierto.
It seemed that sleep and night had resumed their empire.
Dijérase que el sueño y la noche habían restablecido un imperio.
Meantime the moon declined: she was about to set. Not liking to sit in the cold and darkness, I thought I would lie down on my bed, dressed as I was.
Como estar sentada en la oscuridad y con el frío que hacía era poco agradable, resolví tenderme, vestida, sobre el lecho.
I left the window, and moved with little noise across the carpet; as I stooped to take off my shoes, a cautious hand tapped low at the door.
Me aparté de la ventana y me deslicé sin ruido sobre la alfombra. Cuando estaba descalzándome, una mano golpeó suavemente la puerta.
"Am I wanted?" I asked.
-¿Me necesitan? -pregunté.
"Are you up?" asked the voice I expected to hear, viz., my master's.
-¿Está usted levantada y vestida? -preguntó la voz de Rochester.
"Yes."
-Sí, señor.
"Come out, then, quietly."
-Entonces salga sin hacer ruido.
I obeyed.
Obedecí.
Mr. Rochester stood in the gallery holding a light.
Mr. Rochester estaba en la galería, llevando una luz.
"I want you," he said: "come this way: take your time, and make no noise."
-La necesito -dijo-. Sígame sin que nos sientan.
My slippers were thin: I could walk the matted floor as softly as a cat.
Gracias a mis zapatillas, pude recorrer la galería tan silenciosamente como un gato.
He glided up the gallery and up the stairs, and stopped in the dark, low corridor of the fateful third storey: I had followed and stood at his side.
Subimos las escaleras y nos detuvimos en el oscuro corredor del aciago tercer piso. Rochester me precedía.
"Have you a sponge in your room?" he asked in a whisper.
-¿Tiene usted sales? -cuchicheó-.
"Yes, sir."
¿Y una esponja?
"Have you any salts--volatile salts?"
-Sí, señor.
"Go back and fetch both."
-Tráigalos.
I returned, sought the sponge on the washstand, the salts in my drawer, and once more retraced my steps.
Bajé a mi cuarto, cogí la esponja y las sales y volví sobre mis pasos. Él me esperaba.
He still waited; he held a key in his hand: approaching one of the small, black doors, he put it in the lock; he paused, and addressed me again.
La introdujo en la cerradura de una de las puertecillas negras del pasillo, se detuvo un instante y me preguntó:
"You don't turn sick at the sight of blood?"
-¿No le asusta la sangre?
"I think I shall not: I have never been tried yet."
-Creo que no. Hasta ahora, nunca...
I felt a thrill while I answered him; but no coldness, and no faintness.
Me estremecí al contestarle, pero no era de frío ni por debilidad.
"Just give me your hand," he said: "it will not do to risk a fainting fit."
-Deme la mano -dijo-. Hay que prevenir un mareo...
I put my fingers into his.
Puse mis dedos en los suyos.
"Warm and steady," was his remark: he turned the key and opened the door.
Él murmuró «¡Ánimo!» y abrió la puerta.

I saw a room I remembered to have seen before, the day Mrs. Fairfax showed me over the house: it was hung with tapestry; but the tapestry was now looped up in one part, and there was a door apparent, which had then been concealed.
Fairfax me mostró la casa. Entonces tenía las paredes tapizadas, pero ahora habían desaparecido los tapices, permitiendo distinguir una puerta antes disimulada debajo de ellos.
This door was open; a light shone out of the room within: I heard thence a snarling, snatching sound, almost like a dog quarrelling.
La puerta estaba abierta y de ella salía luz. Oí un sonido semejante al quejido de un perro.
Mr. Rochester, putting down his candle, said to me, "Wait a minute," and he went forward to the inner apartment.
Mr. Rochester, dejando la bujía, me dijo: «Espere un minuto», y entró en el cuarto interior.
A shout of laughter greeted his entrance; noisy at first, and terminating in Grace Poole's own goblin ha! ha! _She_ then was there.
Una carcajada le acogió al entrar, terminando en el característico «¡Ja, ja!», de Grace Poole. Ella estaba, pues, allí.
He made some sort of arrangement without speaking, though I heard a low voice address him: he came out and closed the door behind him.
Oí una voz reprimida que le interpelaba. Luego salió y cerró la puerta tras de sí.
"Here, Jane!" he said; and I walked round to the other side of a large bed, which with its drawn curtains concealed a considerable portion of the chamber.
Y me condujo junto a un lecho cubierto con cortinas oscuras. Al lado de la cabecera había una butaca y en ella sentado estaba un hombre sin chaqueta.
An easy-chair was near the bed-head: a man sat in it, dressed with the exception of his coat; he was still; his head leant back; his eyes were closed.
Tenía los ojos cerrados y recostaba la cabeza en el respaldo del asiento.
Mr. Rochester held the candle over him; I recognised in his pale and seemingly lifeless face--the stranger, Mason: I saw too that his linen on one side, and one arm, was almost soaked in blood.
A la luz de la bujía de Rochester reconocí en aquella pálida faz la de Mason, el forastero. Uno de sus brazos y su camisa estaban empapados en sangre. -Tome la vela -dijo Rochester.
"Hold the candle," said Mr. Rochester, and I took it: he fetched a basin of water from the washstand: "Hold that," said he. I obeyed.
Le obedecí. Él cogió el jarro de agua del lavabo.
He took the sponge, dipped it in, and moistened the corpse-like face; he asked for my smelling-bottle, and applied it to the nostrils.
Humedeció la esponja y frotó con ella la cadavérica faz de Mr. Mason; luego me pidió el frasco de sales y lo aplicó a las narices del desvanecido.
Mr. Mason shortly unclosed his eyes; he groaned.
Mason abrió los ojos y se quejó.
Mr. Rochester opened the shirt of the wounded man, whose arm and shoulder were bandaged: he sponged away blood, trickling fast down.
Rochester desabotonó la camisa del herido, cuyo brazo y hombro estaban vendados. Con la esponja comenzó a restañar la sangre.
"Is there immediate danger?" murmured Mr. Mason.
-¿Es de peligro? -preguntó Mason.
"Pooh!
-¡Bah!
No--a mere scratch.
Un simple rasguño.
Don't be so overcome, man: bear up!
Ten ánimo.
I'll fetch a surgeon for you now, myself: you'll be able to be removed by morning, I hope.
Ahora voy a buscar un médico y confío que mañana estarás en estado de que te traslademos de aquí.
Jane," he continued.
Jane...
"Sir?"
-¿Señor?

"I shall have to leave you in this room with this gentleman, for an hour, or perhaps two hours: you will sponge the blood as I do when it returns: if he feels faint, you will put the glass of water on that stand to his lips, and your salts to his nose.
Usted le restañará la sangre si vuelve a tener hemorragia. Si se desmaya, le aplica agua a los labios y le da a oler las sales.
You will not speak to him on any pretext--and--Richard, it will be at the peril of your life if you speak to her: open your lips--agitate yourself--and I'll not answer for the consequences."
No le hable bajo pretexto alguno. En cuanto a ti, Ricardo, no respondo de tu vida si abres los labios, si te mueves...
Again the poor man groaned; he looked as if he dared not move; fear, either of death or of something else, appeared almost to paralyse him.
El pobre hombre volvió a quejarse, pero no se movió. Al parecer, el temor a la muerte o a lo que fuera le paralizaba.
Mr. Rochester put the now bloody sponge into my hand, and I proceeded to use it as he had done.
Rochester me entregó la esponja ensangrentada y yo comencé a usarla como le había visto hacer a él.
He watched me a second, then saying, "Remember!--No conversation," he left the room.
Me miró por un instante y diciéndome: «Acuérdese: nada de conversación», salió del cuarto.
I experienced a strange feeling as the key grated in the lock, and the sound of his retreating step ceased to be heard.
Experimenté una sensación extraña cuando la llave giró en la cerradura y el rumor de sus pasos se apagó en la escalera.

Here then I was in the third storey, fastened into one of its mystic cells; night around me; a pale and bloody spectacle under my eyes and hands; a murderess hardly separated from me by a single door: yes--that was appalling--the rest I could bear; but I shuddered at the thought of Grace Poole bursting out upon me.

Me hallaba en aquel fantástico tercer piso, encerrada en una de sus celdas en plena noche, sola con un hombre pálido y ensangrentado, y separada de una asesina, sólo por una puerta. Si lo demás era hasta cierto punto soportable, me estremecía al pensar en la posibilidad de que Grace Poole abriese y cayera sobre mí.
I must keep to my post, however.
Sin embargo, no podía moverme.

I must watch this ghastly countenance--these blue, still lips forbidden to unclose--these eyes now shut, now opening, now wandering through the room, now fixing on me, and ever glazed with the dulness of horror.
Debía cuidar de aquel hombre, cuyos labios estaban condenados al silencio, cuyos ojos se abrían y cerraban alternativamente, y ora erraban, temerosos, por la habitación, ora se fijaban en mí.
I must dip my hand again and again in the basin of blood and water, and wipe away the trickling gore.
De vez en cuando, humedecía la esponja para seguir restañando la sangre.

I must see the light of the unsnuffed candle wane on my employment; the shadows darken on the wrought, antique tapestry round me, and grow black under the hangings of the vast old bed, and quiver strangely over the doors of a great cabinet opposite--whose front, divided into twelve panels, bore, in grim design, the heads of the twelve apostles, each enclosed in its separate panel as in a frame; while above them at the top rose an ebon crucifix and a dying Christ.

A la luz de la vacilante bujía, veía las oscuras sombras de las tapicerías que me rodeaban, las más oscuras aún de las cortinas del vasto lecho antiguo y las puertas de un gran gabinete contiguo, divididas en doce paneles, en cada uno de los cuales estaba representada la cabeza de uno de los doce Apóstoles, coronándolos un crucifijo de ébano con un Cristo expirante.

According as the shifting obscurity and flickering gleam hovered here or glanced there, it was now the bearded physician, Luke, that bent his brow; now St. John's long hair that waved; and anon the devilish face of Judas, that grew out of the panel, and seemed gathering life and threatening a revelation of the arch-traitor--of Satan himself--in his subordinate's form.

La combinación de luces y sombras que producía la temblorosa llama de la vela me permitía ver, a intervalos, el barbado rostro de Lucas, la larga cabellera flotante de San Juan y hasta la diabólica faz de Judas el traidor, que parecía salirse de su marco y reproducir las formas mismas del propio Satán.
Amidst all this, I had to listen as well as watch: to listen for the movements of the wild beast or the fiend in yonder side den.
Yo escuchaba, tratando de percibir los movimientos de la fiera o demonio que se hallaba en la habitación interior.

But since Mr. Rochester's visit it seemed spellbound: all the night I heard but three sounds at three long intervals,--a step creak, a momentary renewal of the snarling, canine noise, and a deep human groan.
Pero desde que se fuera Mr. Rochester sólo oí, con grandes intervalos, tres sonidos: una pisada, una breve repetición de aquella especie de gruñido canino que a veces sintiera y un quejido humano.

Then my own thoughts worried me. What crime was this that lived incarnate in this sequestered mansion, and could neither be expelled nor subdued by the owner?--what mystery, that broke out now in fire and now in blood, at the deadest hours of night?

¿Qué clase de criminal -pensaba yo- era aquella que vivía en una casa cuyo propietario no podía expulsarla ni someterla? ¿Qué misterio, ora suelto en llamas, ora en sangre, acontecía en aquellas noches oscuras?
What creature was it, that, masked in an ordinary woman's face and shape, uttered the voice, now of a mocking demon, and anon of a carrion-seeking bird of prey?
¿Qué clase de ser era aquél?
And this man I bent over--this commonplace, quiet stranger--how had he become involved in the web of horror? and why had the Fury flown at him?
¿Y por qué aquel hombre, aquel extranjero de tan insignificante aspecto que se hallaba ante mí, había sido envuelto en la ola de horror? ¿Por qué la Furia había caído sobre él?
What made him seek this quarter of the house at an untimely season, when he should have been asleep in bed?
¿Qué hacía a deshora en tal lugar inusitado de la casa, cuando debía encontrarse en su alcoba?
I had heard Mr. Rochester assign him an apartment below--what brought him here!
¿Qué le había traído hasta aquí?
And why, now, was he so tame under the violence or treachery done him?
¿Y por qué se resignaba a la violencia de que fuera víctima?
Why did he so quietly submit to the concealment Mr. Rochester enforced?
¿Por qué se sometía a la ocultación a que Rochester le forzaba?
Why _did_ Mr. Rochester enforce this concealment?
¿Por qué Rochester toleraba aquello?
His guest had been outraged, his own life on a former occasion had been hideously plotted against; and both attempts he smothered in secrecy and sank in oblivion!
Su huésped había sido agredido, su propia vida había corrido peligro una vez y, sin embargo, guardaba en secreto ambos atentados.

Lastly, I saw Mr. Mason was submissive to Mr. Rochester; that the impetuous will of the latter held complete sway over the inertness of the former: the few words which had passed between them assured me of this.
Yo había visto a Mason aceptar la voluntad de Rochester: las pocas palabras cruzadas entre ellos me lo demostraban.

It was evident that in their former intercourse, the passive disposition of the one had been habitually influenced by the active energy of the other: whence then had arisen Mr. Rochester's dismay when he heard of Mr. Mason's arrival?

Era evidente que en las anteriores relaciones de ambos la pasiva disposición de ánimo de uno de ellos debía haber sido influida por la energía del otro. ¿Por qué, pues, aquel abatimiento de Rochester cuando supo la llegada de Mason?
Why had the mere name of this unresisting individual--whom his word now sufficed to control like a child--fallen on him, a few hours since, as a thunderbolt might fall on an oak? Oh!
¿Por qué la noticia de la llegada de aquel a quien dominaba como a un niño había caído sobre él como un rayo sobre un roble?
I could not forget his look and his paleness when he whispered: "Jane, I have got a blow--I have got a blow, Jane."
Imposible olvidar su mirada y su palidez al murmurar: «Estoy anonadado, Jane», ni el temblor de su brazo al apoyarse, entonces, en el mío.
I could not forget how the arm had trembled which he rested on my shoulder: and it was no light matter which could thus bow the resolute spirit and thrill the vigorous frame of Fairfax Rochester.
Es imposible también esclarecer lo que podía impresionar de tal modo el resuelto ánimo y la energía de Fairfax Rochester.
When will he come?" I cried inwardly, as the night lingered and lingered--as my bleeding patient drooped, moaned, sickened: and neither day nor aid arrived.

«¿Cuándo vendrá, cuándo vendrá?», me preguntaba, impaciente, a lo largo de aquella interminable noche, mientras mi ensangrentado compañero sangraba más y más, suspiraba y desfallecía. Pero no llegaba el día ni nadie venía en nuestro socorro.

I had, again and again, held the water to Mason's white lips; again and again offered him the stimulating salts: my efforts seemed ineffectual: either bodily or mental suffering, or loss of blood, or all three combined, were fast prostrating his strength.
Cada vez con más frecuencia había de aplicar agua a los exangües labios de Mason y hacerle oler las sales. Pero mis esfuerzos parecían estériles.
He moaned so, and looked so weak, wild, and lost, I feared he was dying; and I might not even speak to him.

Fuese la pérdida de sangre, el sufrimiento físico, el mental, o todo reunido, el caso era que aquel hombre estaba muy postrado. Se quejaba de un modo tal, parecía tan agotado y débil, que yo le suponía moribundo.
The candle, wasted at last, went out; as it expired, I perceived streaks of grey light edging the window curtains: dawn was then approaching.
La bujía se apagó. A través de las cortinas de la ventana distinguí una claridad gris: el alba se aproximaba.
Presently I heard Pilot bark far below, out of his distant kennel in the courtyard: hope revived.
Oí ladrar a Piloto y mi esperanza renació. Cinco minutos más tarde, la llave rechinó en la cerradura, y me sentí aliviada.
Nor was it unwarranted: in five minutes more the grating key, the yielding lock, warned me my watch was relieved. It could not have lasted more than two hours: many a week has seemed shorter.
La espera no debía de haber durado más de dos horas, pero muchas semanas de mi vida me parecieron más cortas que aquella noche.
Mr. Rochester entered, and with him the surgeon he had been to fetch.
Mr. Rochester entró y, con él, el médico que había ido a buscar.
"Now, Carter, be on the alert," he said to this last: "I give you but half-an-hour for dressing the wound, fastening the bandages, getting the patient downstairs and all."
-Escuche, Carter: sólo le doy media hora - dijo Mr. Rochester a su acompañante- para curar la herida, vendarla y poner a este hombre en condiciones de marcharse.
"But is he fit to move, sir?"
-¿Y si se desmaya al moverse?
"No doubt of it; it is nothing serious; he is nervous, his spirits must be kept up.
-No se trata de nada serio.
Come, set to work."
Es que es un hombre muy nervioso y...

Mr. Rochester drew back the thick curtain, drew up the holland blind, let in all the daylight he could; and I was surprised and cheered to see how far dawn was advanced: what rosy streaks were beginning to brighten the east.
Rochester descorrió las cortinas de la ventana. La luz del alba penetró y quedé extrañada y complacida al ver que la mañana estaba ya bastante avanzada.
Then he approached Mason, whom the surgeon was already handling.
Por Oriente comenzaba a brillar una claridad rosada. Rochester se aproximó a Mason.
"Now, my good fellow, how are you?" he asked.
-¿Cómo te encuentras? -preguntó.
"She's done for me, I fear," was the faint reply.
-Temo que muy mal -fue la desmayada respuesta.
"Not a whit!--courage!
-¡Animo, hombre! No es nada.
This day fortnight you'll hardly be a pin the worse of it: you've lost a little blood; that's all.
De aquí a quince días no te queda ni la señal. Has perdido algo de sangre y eso es todo.
Carter, assure him there's no danger."
Carter: asegúrele que no hay peligro.
"I can do that conscientiously," said Carter, who had now undone the bandages; "only I wish I could have got here sooner: he would not have bled so much--but how is this?
-Puedo hacerlo en conciencia, porque es verdad - dijo el médico-, pero es lástima que no me haya llamado antes.
The flesh on the shoulder is torn as well as cut.
¿Qué es esto?
This wound was not done with a knife: there have been teeth here!"
¡La carne del hombro ha sido arrancada!
"She bit me," he murmured.
-Me mordió -murmuró Mason-.
"She worried me like a tigress, when Rochester got the knife from her."
Se tiró a mí como una fiera cuando Rochester le quitó el cuchillo.
"You should not have yielded: you should have grappled with her at once," said Mr. Rochester.
-No debiste condescender en quedarte -dijo Rochester-. Debiste irte enseguida.
"But under such circumstances, what could one do?" returned Mason.
-Pero en circunstancias así, ¿qué iba a hacer? -repuso Mason-.
"Oh, it was frightful!" he added, shuddering.
Además, fue inesperado...
"And I did not expect it: she looked so quiet at first."
¡Estaba tan tranquila al principio!
"I warned you," was his friend's answer; "I said--be on your guard when you go near her.
-Ya te advertí que tuvieras cuidado cuando te acercases a ella -contestó su amigo-.
Besides, you might have waited till to-morrow, and had me with you: it was mere folly to attempt the interview to-night, and alone."
Además, debiste esperar hasta hoy a visitarla conmigo. Fue una verdadera locura realizar esa entrevista por la noche y solo.
"I thought I could have done some good."
-Creía acertar.
"You thought! you thought!
-¡Creía, creía!
Yes, it makes me impatient to hear you: but, however, you have suffered, and are likely to suffer enough for not taking my advice; so I'll say no more.
Me impacienta oírte y ver que sufres por no haberme hecho caso.
Carter--hurry!--hurry!
¡De prisa, Carter, de prisa!
The sun will soon rise, and I must have him off."
El sol va a salir ya y tenemos que llevarnos a este hombre.
"Directly, sir; the shoulder is just bandaged.
-Enseguida. El hombro está vendado ya.
I must look to this other wound in the arm: she has had her teeth here too, I think."
Ahora veamos la dentellada que tiene en el brazo.
"She sucked the blood: she said she'd drain my heart," said Mason.
-¡Ella bebía mi sangre y decía que deseaba devorar mi corazón! -murmuró Mason.
I saw Mr. Rochester shudder: a singularly marked expression of disgust, horror, hatred, warped his countenance almost to distortion; but he only said--
Rochester se estremeció. Una expresión de disgusto y horror contrajo su rostro.
"Come, be silent, Richard, and never mind her gibberish: don't repeat it."
Pero no dijo más que: -Calla, Richard; no recuerdes aquellas palabras. No las repitas...
"I wish I could forget it," was the answer.
-No desearía más que olvidarlas -contestó el herido.
"You will when you are out of the country: when you get back to Spanish Town, you may think of her as dead and buried--or rather, you need not think of her at all."
-Cuando te halles fuera de Inglaterra, en Puerto España, no pienses más en ella. Figúrate que está muerta y enterrada.
"Impossible to forget this night!"
-Me será imposible olvidar esta noche.
"It is not impossible: have some energy, man.
-No te será imposible. Ten energía.
You thought you were as dead as a herring two hours since, and you are all alive and talking now.
También hace dos horas pensabas que ibas a morir y ya ves que vives.
There!--Carter has done with you or nearly so; I'll make you decent in a trice.
Ahora que Carter termina, tenemos que vestirte.

Jane" (he turned to me for the first time since his re-entrance), "take this key: go down into my bedroom, and walk straight forward into my dressing-room: open the top drawer of the wardrobe and take out a clean shirt and neck-handkerchief: bring them here; and be nimble."
Jane -dijo, volviéndose hacia mí por primera vez desde que entrara-: tome esta llave, vaya a mi cuarto, saque del guardarropa una camisa limpia y una bufanda y tráigalas, pero pronto.
I went; sought the repository he had mentioned, found the articles named, and returned with them.
Fui, hice lo que se me indicaba y volví con lo ordenado.
"Now," said he, "go to the other side of the bed while I order his toilet; but don't leave the room: you may be wanted again."
-Ahora -me dijo- retírese al otro lado de la cama mientras le arreglo, pero no se vaya.
I retired as directed.
Quizá la necesitemos otra vez.
"Was anybody stirring below when you went down, Jane?" inquired Mr. Rochester presently.
¿Ha habido alguna novedad mientras he estado fuera? -agregó.
"No, sir; all was very still."
-Ninguna.
"We shall get you off cannily, Dick: and it will be better, both for your sake, and for that of the poor creature in yonder.
-Conviene que nos vayamos cuanto antes, Dick -dijo Rochester-, tanto por ti como por esa pobre...
I have striven long to avoid exposure, and I should not like it to come at last.
Hasta ahora he logrado evitar el escándalo y no deseo echarlo a perder.
Here, Carter, help him on with his waist-coat.
Carter: ayúdeme a ponerle el chaleco.
Where did you leave your furred cloak?
¿Dónde te has dejado el abrigo de piel?
You can't travel a mile without that, I know, in this damned cold climate.
No podrás andar ni una milla, dado el frío de este condenado clima, si no lo llevas. ¿En tu alcoba?
In your room?--Jane, run down to Mr. Mason's room,--the one next mine,--and fetch a cloak you will see there."
Jane: vaya al cuarto de Mr. Mason, que es el inmediato al mío, y traiga un abrigo que encontrará en él.
Again I ran, and again returned, bearing an immense mantle lined and edged with fur.
De nuevo corrí, y de nuevo regresé, llevando un enorme abrigo guarnecido de piel.
"Now, I've another errand for you," said my untiring master; "you must away to my room again.
-Aún tengo algo más que ordenarle, Jane -dijo él-. ¡Es magnífico que lleve usted esas zapatillas de terciopelo!
What a mercy you are shod with velvet, Jane!--a clod-hopping messenger would never do at this juncture.
No hubiéramos podido encontrar emisario más a propósito en esta ocasión.
You must open the middle drawer of my toilet-table and take out a little phial and a little glass you will find there,--quick!"
Abra el cajón de mi tocador y coja un frasquito y un vaso que verá.
I flew thither and back, bringing the desired vessels.
Fui y volví trayendo lo solicitado.
"That's well!
-Muy bien.
Now, doctor, I shall take the liberty of administering a dose myself, on my own responsibility.
Ahora, doctor, voy a tomarme la libertad de administrar al paciente una dosis de este preparado, bajo mi responsabilidad.
I got this cordial at Rome, of an Italian charlatan--a fellow you would have kicked, Carter.
Es un cordial que adquirí en Roma a un charlatán italiano, un tipo a quien usted hubiese dado de puntapiés con gusto...
It is not a thing to be used indiscriminately, but it is good upon occasion: as now, for instance.
No es cosa que pueda usarse a grandes dosis, pero es bueno en ciertas ocasiones, como ahora.
Jane, a little water."
Un poco de agua, Jane.
He held out the tiny glass, and I half filled it from the water-bottle on the washstand.
Llené el vaso hasta la mitad con agua de la botella del lavabo.
"That will do;--now wet the lip of the phial." I did so; he measured twelve drops of a crimson liquid, and presented it to Mason.
Rochester vertió en el vaso una docena de gotas de un líquido rojo y lo ofreció a Mason.
"Drink, Richard: it will give you the heart you lack, for an hour or so."
-Bebe, Richard. Esto te dará el ánimo que te falta, al menos por una hora.
"But will it hurt me?--is it inflammatory?"
-¿No me perjudicará?
"Drink! drink! drink!"
-¡Bebe, hombre, bebe!
Mr. Mason obeyed, because it was evidently useless to resist.
Mason bebió, considerando, sin duda, que era inútil toda resistencia.
He was dressed now: he still looked pale, but he was no longer gory and sullied.
Ya estaba vestido, y no quedaba rastro de su desaliño ni de su ensangrentado aspecto de poco antes, aunque estaba muy pálido aún.
Mr. Rochester let him sit three minutes after he had swallowed the liquid; he then took his arm--
Rochester le permitió permanecer sentado tres minutos más y después tomó su brazo.
"Now I am sure you can get on your feet," he said--"try."
-Ahora estoy seguro de que puedes sostenerte en pie -dijo.
The patient rose.
El paciente se levantó.
"Carter, take him under the other shoulder.
-Cójalo por el otro brazo, Carter.
Be of good cheer, Richard; step out--that's it!"
Ea, Richard, vamos. ¡Eso es!
"I do feel better," remarked Mr. Mason.
-Me siento mejor -observó Mason.
"I am sure you do.
-¡Ya lo sabía yo!

Now, Jane, trip on before us away to the backstairs; unbolt the side-passage door, and tell the driver of the post-chaise you will see in the yard--or just outside, for I told him not to drive his rattling wheels over the pavement--to be ready; we are coming: and, Jane, if any one is about, come to the foot of the stairs and hem."

Ahora, Jane, haga el favor de adelantarse, salga por la puerta trasera y diga al cochero de la silla de posta que verá usted en el patio -o mejor dicho fuera, porque le he indicado que no entre- que esté preparado. Nosotros vamos andando.
It was by this time half-past five, and the sun was on the point of rising; but I found the kitchen still dark and silent.
La cocina estaba aún oscura y silenciosa. Abrí la puerta trasera de la casa con el menor ruido posible.

The side-passage door was fastened; I opened it with as little noise as possible: all the yard was quiet; but the gates stood wide open, and there was a post-chaise, with horses ready harnessed, and driver seated on the box, stationed outside.
El patio estaba silencioso. Las verjas se hallaban abiertas y junto a ellas había una silla de posta, con el cochero encaramado en el pescante.
I approached him, and said the gentlemen were coming; he nodded: then I looked carefully round and listened.
Me acerqué, le dije que los señores iban a bajar ya, asintió y yo miré en torno mío y escuché. Aún dormía todo en la naciente mañana.

The stillness of early morning slumbered everywhere; the curtains were yet drawn over the servants' chamber windows; little birds were just twittering in the blossom-blanched orchard trees, whose boughs drooped like white garlands over the wall enclosing one side of the yard; the carriage horses stamped from time to time in their closed stables: all else was still.
Las ventanas de los cuartos de la servidumbre estaban cerradas todavía. Algunos pajarillos gorjeaban en los árboles del huerto, cuyas ramas asomaban sobre uno de los muros del patio.
The gentlemen now appeared.
Los tres caballeros se presentaron.
Mason, supported by Mr. Rochester and the surgeon, seemed to walk with tolerable ease: they assisted him into the chaise; Carter followed.
Mason, ayudado por Rochester y el médico, parecía andar con bastante facilidad. Le colocaron en la silla.
"Take care of him," said Mr. Rochester to the latter, "and keep him at your house till he is quite well: I shall ride over in a day or two to see how he gets on.
-Cuídele -dijo Rochester al último- y téngale en su casa hasta que esté bien del todo. Iré dentro de uno o dos días a ver cómo se encuentran.
Richard, how is it with you?"
¿Cómo te sientes, Richard?
"The fresh air revives me, Fairfax."
-El aire fresco me reanima, Fairfax.
"Leave the window open on his side, Carter; there is no wind--good-bye, Dick."
-Deje abierta la ventanilla, Carter. No hace viento.
"Fairfax--"
-Fairfax...
"Well what is it?"
-¿Qué quieres?
"Let her be taken care of; let her be treated as tenderly as may be: let her--" he stopped and burst into tears.
-Cuídala bien y trátala todo lo mejor que puedas. Procura que...
"I do my best; and have done it, and will do it," was the answer: he shut up the chaise door, and the vehicle drove away.
-Lo haré todo lo mejor posible, en efecto, como siempre lo he hecho y lo continuaré haciendo.
"Yet would to God there was an end of all this!" added Mr. Rochester, as he closed and barred the heavy yard-gates.
Cerró la puerta del coche y éste se puso en camino. -¡Hasta que Dios quiera poner fin a esto! -añadió Rochester, mientras cerraba las pesadas verjas.
This done, he moved with slow step and abstracted air towards a door in the wall bordering the orchard.
Y luego comenzó a andar con lento paso y abstraído aspecto hacia una puerta que se abría en el muro del huerto.
I, supposing he had done with me, prepared to return to the house; again, however, I heard him call "Jane!"
Yo me preparaba a volver a la casa, cuando le oí decir: -¡Jane!
He had opened feel portal and stood at it, waiting for me. "Come where there is some freshness, for a few moments," he said; "that house is a mere dungeon: don't you feel it so?"
Había abierto la puerta y estaba parado, esperándome. -Vamos a respirar un poco el aire puro -dijo-. Esa casa no es más que un calabozo.
"It seems to me a splendid mansion, sir."
¿No le parece? -A mí me parece magnífica.

"The glamour of inexperience is over your eyes," he answered; "and you see it through a charmed medium: you cannot discern that the gilding is slime and the silk draperies cobwebs; that the marble is sordid slate, and the polished woods mere refuse chips and scaly bark.

-Su inexperiencia la ciega -repuso- y todo lo ve usted a través de un falso aspecto encantador. No comprende usted que el oro es barro y las sedas telarañas; el mármol, grosera pizarra, y las maderas barnizadas, despreciable leña...
Now _here_" (he pointed to the leafy enclosure we had entered) "all is real, sweet, and pure."
En cambio, aquí -y señalaba el lugar en que habíamos entrado- todo es real, bello y puro. Avanzó por un sendero circundado de boj.

He strayed down a walk edged with box, with apple trees, pear trees, and cherry trees on one side, and a border on the other full of all sorts of old-fashioned flowers, stocks, sweet-williams, primroses, pansies, mingled with southernwood, sweet-briar, and various fragrant herbs.

De un lado, lo sombreaban manzanos, perales y cerezos. Al otro había un pénsil de flores: belloritas, trinitarias, escaramujos de olor, abrótano y hierbas aromáticas, todo ello fresco y lozano en la radiante mañana de primavera.

They were fresh now as a succession of April showers and gleams, followed by a lovely spring morning, could make them: the sun was just entering the dappled east, and his light illumined the wreathed and dewy orchard trees and shone down the quiet walks under them.
El sol apuntaba por Oriente y sus rayos besaban los árboles frutales y brillaban en los quietos muros.
"Jane, will you have a flower?"
-¿Quiere una flor, Jane?
He gathered a half-blown rose, the first on the bush, and offered it to me. "Thank you, sir."
Cortó una rosa y me la ofreció. -Gracias, señor.
"Do you like this sunrise, Jane?
-¿Le gusta ver nacer el sol, Jane?
That sky with its high and light clouds which are sure to melt away as the day waxes warm--this placid and balmly atmosphere?"
¿Este cielo donde flotan lejanas y brillantes nubes que se disiparán a medida que avance el día, esta atmósfera plácida y perfumada?
"I do, very much."
-Sí, me gusta mucho.
"You have passed a strange night, Jane."
-Ha pasado usted una noche muy mala, ¿no?
"And it has made you look pale--were you afraid when I left you alone with Mason?"
-Está usted muy pálida. ¿Tuvo miedo cuando la dejé sola con Mason?
"I was afraid of some one coming out of the inner room."
-Temía que saliese alguien del cuarto interior.
"But I had fastened the door--I had the key in my pocket: I should have been a careless shepherd if I had left a lamb--my pet lamb--so near a wolf's den, unguarded: you were safe."
-Ya había cerrado yo la puerta con llave. ¿Iba a dejar a mi oveja -a mi oveja favorita- al alcance del lobo?
"Will Grace Poole live here still, sir?"
-¿Cree que lo estaré mientras Grace Poole viva en la casa?
"Oh yes! don't trouble your head about her--put the thing out of your thoughts."
-No se asuste de Grace. No piense en ella siquiera, por favor.
"Yet it seems to me your life is hardly secure while she stays."
-Me parece que ni la vida de usted está segura mientras ella continúe aquí.
"Never fear--I will take care of myself."
-No tema. Ya me preocupo de mí también.
"Is the danger you apprehended last night gone by now, sir?"
-¿Se ha alejado el peligro que temía anoche, señor?
"I cannot vouch for that till Mason is out of England: nor even then.
-No respondo de ello mientras Mason no esté fuera de Inglaterra... y entonces tampoco.
To live, for me, Jane, is to stand on a crater-crust which may crack and spue fire any day." "But Mr. Mason seems a man easily led.
La vida para mí, Jane, consiste en permanecer sobre el cráter de un volcán dormido que puede cualquier día entrar en erupción. -Pero Mason me parece una persona dócil.
Your influence, sir, is evidently potent with him: he will never set you at defiance or wilfully injure you."
Usted influye mucho sobre él y no creo que le dañe o le perjudique en nada.
"Oh, no!
-¡Oh, no desconfío de Mason!
Mason will not defy me; nor, knowing it, will he hurt me--but, unintentionally, he might in a moment, by one careless word, deprive me, if not of life, yet for ever of happiness."
El peligro está en que, sin querer, pronuncie alguna palabra que me costara, si no la vida, al menos la felicidad.
"Tell him to be cautious, sir: let him know what you fear, and show him how to avert the danger."
-Dígale que sea precavido, hágale comprender los temores que usted siente y adviértale del peligro.
He laughed sardonically, hastily took my hand, and as hastily threw it from him.
Él rió sarcásticamente, tomó mi mano y la apretó contra su pecho.
"If I could do that, simpleton, where would the danger be? Annihilated in a moment.
-Si eso fuera posible, bobita, ¿dónde estaría el peligro?
Ever since I have known Mason, I have only had to say to him 'Do that,' and the thing has been done.
Desaparecería instantáneamente.
But I cannot give him orders in this case: I cannot say 'Beware of harming me, Richard;' for it is imperative that I should keep him ignorant that harm to me is possible.
A Mason, desde que le conozco, me basta decirle «Haz esto», para que lo haga en el acto. Pero en este caso, no cabe hacer nada.
Now you look puzzled; and I will puzzle you further.
Parece usted confundida y se confundirá más aún si...
You are my little friend, are you not?"
Usted es amiga mía, ¿no?
"I like to serve you, sir, and to obey you in all that is right." "Precisely: I see you do.
-Deseo serle útil y servirle en todo lo que sea razonable, señor. -Ya lo he visto.

I see genuine contentment in your gait and mien, your eye and face, when you are helping me and pleasing me--working for me, and with me, in, as you characteristically say, '_all that is right_:' for if I bid you do what you thought wrong, there would be no light-footed running, no neat-handed alacrity, no lively glance and animated complexion.

Me parece apreciar verdadera satisfacción en todo su aspecto cuando usted me ayuda en algo, trabaja para mí y me complace en cuanto, como usted dice, «es razonable». Estoy seguro de que si la pidiera algo que no fuese razonable, mi amiga no huiría de mí, ni sentiría alegría, ni se pondría encarnada y le brillarían los ojos.
My friend would then turn to me, quiet and pale, and would say, 'No, sir; that is impossible: I cannot do it, because it is wrong;' and would become immutable as a fixed star.
No; mi amiga, en un caso así, se volvería hacia mí, serena y pálida, y me diría: «No, señor, porque no es razonable».
Well, you too have power over me, and may injure me: yet I dare not show you where I am vulnerable, lest, faithful and friendly as you are, you should transfix me at once."
Y permanecería tan inmutable como una estrella fija... En fin: usted puede influir en mí y hasta herirme aunque no la mostrara mi lado vulnerable.
"If you have no more to fear from Mr. Mason than you have from me, sir, you are very safe."
-Si no tuviese usted que temer a Mr. Mason más que a mí, bien seguro estaría usted, señor.
"God grant it may be so!
-¡Ojalá fuera así!
Here, Jane, is an arbour; sit down."
Vamos a sentarnos en ese banco, Jane.
The arbour was an arch in the wall, lined with ivy; it contained a rustic seat.
Adosado a la tapia había un banco bajo un dosel de hiedra.
Mr. Rochester took it, leaving room, however, for me: but I stood before him.
Se sentó y me hizo sitio. Pero yo permanecí en pie.
"Sit," he said; "the bench is long enough for two.
-Siéntese -dijo-. El banco es suficiente para los dos.
You don't hesitate to take a place at my side, do you?
¿Acaso teme sentarse a mi lado?
Is that wrong, Jane?"
¿Se trata de una cosa irrazonable?
I answered him by assuming it: to refuse would, I felt, have been unwise.
Mi contestación fue sentarme. Comprendí que no había motivo para la negativa.

"Now, my little friend, while the sun drinks the dew--while all the flowers in this old garden awake and expand, and the birds fetch their young ones' breakfast out of the Thornfield, and the early bees do their first spell of work--I'll put a case to you, which you must endeavour to suppose your own: but first, look at me, and tell me you are at ease, and not fearing that I err in detaining you, or that you err in staying."

-Ahora, amiguita mía, mientras el sol bebe el rocío, mientras se abren las flores de este viejo jardín, mientras los pájaros levantan el vuelo a fin de buscar comida para sus crías, voy a exponer a usted un caso que..., pero antes míreme y dígame si encuentra mal que la retenga o no le agrada permanecer aquí. -No, señor.
"No, sir; I am content."
Estoy satisfecha.

"Well then, Jane, call to aid your fancy:--suppose you were no longer a girl well reared and disciplined, but a wild boy indulged from childhood upwards; imagine yourself in a remote foreign land; conceive that you there commit a capital error, no matter of what nature or from what motives, but one whose consequences must follow you through life and taint all your existence.

-Entonces, Jane, llame en su ayuda a su imaginación y suponga que no es usted una muchacha bien educada y disciplinada, sino una niña caprichosa y mimada desde la niñez. Imagínese viviendo en un lejano país extranjero y dé por hecho que hubiera cometido un gravísimo error, no importa de qué clase o por qué motivos, pero cuyas consecuencias la persiguen a lo largo de toda su vida y amargan toda su existencia.
Mind, I don't say a _crime_; I am not speaking of shedding of blood or any other guilty act, which might make the perpetrator amenable to the law: my word is _error_.
Note que no hablo de un crimen, esto es, de verter sangre u otra cosa análoga que pongan al que lo comete bajo la acción de la ley. No; me refiero a un error.
The results of what you have done become in time to you utterly insupportable; you take measures to obtain relief: unusual measures, but neither unlawful nor culpable.
Los resultados de lo que usted ha hecho acaban convirtiéndose en insoportables y usted adopta medidas para aliviarlos, medidas inusitadas, pero no ilegales.
Still you are miserable; for hope has quitted you on the very confines of life: your sun at noon darkens in an eclipse, which you feel will not leave it till the time of setting.
Usted sigue sintiéndose desgraciada; la esperanza la abandona, el sol y la luna de su vida se eclipsan.

Bitter and base associations have become the sole food of your memory: you wander here and there, seeking rest in exile: happiness in pleasure--I mean in heartless, sensual pleasure--such as dulls intellect and blights feeling.

Amargos y humillantes recuerdos son el único alimento de su memoria, y usted vagabundea de un sitio a otro buscando olvido en el destierro y felicidad en el placer, significando con esto el mero placer sensual.

Heart-weary and soul-withered, you come home after years of voluntary banishment: you make a new acquaintance--how or where no matter: you find in this stranger much of the good and bright qualities which you have sought for twenty years, and never before encountered; and they are all fresh, healthy, without soil and without taint.

Con el corazón cansado y el alma marchita, vuelve usted a su casa tras años de voluntario destierro y halla usted a alguien -quién y cómo no hace al caso- en quien halla las cualidades que en vano ha buscado usted durante veinte años; cualidades en plena lozanía, no acompasadas por corrupción de clase alguna.

Such society revives, regenerates: you feel better days come back--higher wishes, purer feelings; you desire to recommence your life, and to spend what remains to you of days in a way more worthy of an immortal being.
Su trato le hace revivir, le regenera, experimenta mejores sentimientos y deseos más puros. Desea usted volver a empezar su vida y terminarla de un modo más digno de un ser humano.
To attain this end, are you justified in overleaping an obstacle of custom--a mere conventional impediment which neither your conscience sanctifies nor your judgment approves?"
Para alcanzar este fin, ¿encontraría usted justificado saltar sobre un obstáculo, un impedimento meramente convencional, que ni la conciencia santifica ni la razón aprueba?
He paused for an answer:
Calló, esperando mi contestación.
and what was I to say?
¿Qué podía yo decir?
Oh, for some good spirit to suggest a judicious and satisfactory response!
En vano deseé que algún genio amigo me sugiriese una respuesta satisfactoria y sensata.

Vain aspiration! The west wind whispered in the ivy round me; but no gentle Ariel borrowed its breath as a medium of speech: the birds sang in the tree-tops; but their song, however sweet, was inarticulate.
El viento Oeste agitaba la hiedra, pero ningún amable Ariel le hacía servir de vehículo de sus consejos. Los pájaros cantaban en las ramas, pero su canto, aunque dulce, no me decía nada.
Again Mr. Rochester propounded his query:
Mr. Rochester insistió:

"Is the wandering and sinful, but now rest-seeking and repentant, man justified in daring the world's opinion, in order to attach to him for ever this gentle, gracious, genial stranger, thereby securing his own peace of mind and regeneration of life?"

-Si el vagabundo pecador, ahora quieto y arrepentido, desafiando la opinión del mundo, uniese a su vida la de la amable, bondadosa y gentil mujer a quien ama, ¿aseguraría la paz de su alma y la regeneración de su vida?
"Sir," I answered, "a wanderer's repose or a sinner's reformation should never depend on a fellow-creature.
-Señor -repuse-: creo que el reposo de un vagabundo y la reforma de un pecador no dependen de otro ser humano.

Men and women die; philosophers falter in wisdom, and Christians in goodness: if any one you know has suffered and erred, let him look higher than his equals for strength to amend and solace to heal."
El hombre puede corregirse por sí mismo, si reconoce que yerra. -Pero se necesita un instrumento.
"But the instrument--the instrument!
Dios, que impone el trabajo, da la herramienta.
God, who does the work, ordains the instrument.
Yo, se lo digo sin ambages, he sido un hombre disoluto, un vagabundo, un...
I have myself--I tell it you without parable--been a worldly, dissipated, restless man; and I believe I have found the instrument for my cure in--"
Creo haber hallado ahora el instrumento para mi salvación y...
He paused: the birds went on carolling, the leaves lightly rustling.
Se detuvo. Los pájaros cantaban y las hojas de los árboles se balanceaban impulsadas por el viento.
I almost wondered they did not check their songs and whispers to catch the suspended revelation; but they would have had to wait many minutes--so long was the silence protracted.
Me sorprendió que unos y otras no suspendieran sus cantos y sus movimientos para escuchar la interrumpida revelación. Pero hubieran tenido que esperar mucho, tanto como aquel silencio se prolongó...
At last I looked up at the tardy speaker: he was looking eagerly at me.
Cuando, al fin, osé mirar a mi interlocutor, él a su vez estaba mirándome a mí.

"Little friend," said he, in quite a changed tone--while his face changed too, losing all its softness and gravity, and becoming harsh and sarcastic--"you have noticed my tender penchant for Miss Ingram: don't you think if I married her she would regenerate me with a vengeance?"

-Amiguita mía -dijo, con tono totalmente distinto, ya sin dulzura ni gravedad algunas, sino con sarcasmo y dureza-: ¿ha notado usted la tierna inclinación que experimento hacia Blanche Ingram? ¿Cree que si me caso con ella me regenerará?
He got up instantly, went quite to the other end of the walk, and when he came back he was humming a tune.
Se levantó de pronto, se alejó hasta el extremo del sendero y volvió tarareando un cantar.
"Jane, Jane," said he, stopping before me, "you are quite pale with your vigils: don't you curse me for disturbing your rest?"
-Jane -dijo-: está usted palidísima. ¿No abomina de mí, que la he hecho pasar la noche en vela?
"Curse you? No, sir."
-No, señor.
"Shake hands in confirmation of the word.
-Confírmelo con un apretón de manos.
What cold fingers!
¡Qué frías las tiene!
They were warmer last night when I touched them at the door of the mysterious chamber.
Estaban mucho más cálidas esta noche, a la puerta de la habitación misteriosa.
Jane, when will you watch with me again?"
¿Cuándo volverá a velar conmigo otra vez?
"Whenever I can be useful, sir."
-Cuando pueda serle útil, señor.
"For instance, the night before I am married!
-Por ejemplo, la noche antes de mi boda.
I am sure I shall not be able to sleep.
Estoy seguro de que esa noche no podré dormir.
Will you promise to sit up with me to bear me company?
¿Me promete usted sentarse entonces a mi lado haciéndome compañía?
To you I can talk of my lovely one: for now you have seen her and know her."
A usted puedo hablarle de mi amada, puesto que la conoce.
"She's a rare one, is she not, Jane?"
-Blanche es admirable, ¿verdad?
"A strapper--a real strapper, Jane: big, brown, and buxom; with hair just such as the ladies of Carthage must have had.
-Robusta, alta, morena, con un cabello como debían tenerlo las mujeres de Cartago... ¡Caramba!
Bless me! there's Dent and Lynn in the stables!
Dent y Lynn están ya en las cuadras.
Go in by the shrubbery, through that wicket." As I went one way, he went another, and I heard him in the yard, saying cheerfully--
Se fue por un lado, yo me fui por otro y a poco le oí hablar diciendo tranquilamente:
"Mason got the start of you all this morning; he was gone before sunrise: I rose at four to see him off."
-Mason se ha ido hoy antes de salir el sol. Me levanté a las cuatro para despedirle.
Presentiments are strange things! and so are sympathies; and so are signs; and the three combined make one mystery to which humanity has not yet found the key.

¡Qué cosa tan extraña son los presentimientos! Ellos, como las simpatías espontáneas y los signos que se hallan en todas las cosas, constituyen un misterio del que la humanidad no ha encontrado la clave.
I never laughed at presentiments in my life, because I have had strange ones of my own.
Nunca me burlaré de los presentimientos, porque yo misma los he experimentado muchas veces.

Sympathies, I believe, exist (for instance, between far-distant, long-absent, wholly estranged relatives asserting, notwithstanding their alienation, the unity of the source to which each traces his origin) whose workings baffle mortal comprehension.
La simpatía espontánea existe también, como ocurre entre parientes que no se han visto jamás, y que simpatizan, no obstante, como demostración de su origen común.
And signs, for aught we know, may be but the sympathies of Nature with man.
En cuanto a los signos reveladores, quizá sean muestra de la simpatía de la naturaleza hacia el hombre.

When I was a little girl, only six years old, I one night heard Bessie Leaven say to Martha Abbot that she had been dreaming about a little child; and that to dream of children was a sure sign of trouble, either to one's self or one's kin. The saying might have worn out of my memory, had not a circumstance immediately followed which served indelibly to fix it there.

Teniendo apenas seis años, oí una noche comentar a Bessie Leaven y Martha Abbot que la primera había soñado con un niño pequeño y que soñar con niños es signo seguro de desgracia, o para uno mismo o para otros.
The next day Bessie was sent for home to the deathbed of her little sister.
A la mañana siguiente Bessie tuvo que ir a su casa, porque su hermana menor había muerto.

Of late I had often recalled this saying and this incident; for during the past week scarcely a night had gone over my couch that had not brought with it a dream of an infant, which I sometimes hushed in my arms, sometimes dandled on my knee, sometimes watched playing with daisies on a lawn, or again, dabbling its hands in running water.

Ahora yo llevaba una semana soñando constantemente con un niño a quien tenía en brazos o sobre las rodillas, o cuyos juegos vigilaba en un prado. Unas veces era un niño triste y otras riente; ora se refugiaba en mi regazo; ora huía de mi lado.
I did not like this iteration of one idea--this strange recurrence of one image, and I grew nervous as bedtime approached and the hour of the vision drew near.
El pensar en la reiteración de este sueño me ponía nerviosa en cuanto llegaba la hora de acostarme.

It was from companionship with this baby-phantom I had been roused on that moonlight night when I heard the cry; and it was on the afternoon of the day following I was summoned downstairs by a message that some one wanted me in Mrs. Fairfax's room.
Cuando el grito de aquella noche me despertó, soñaba estar en la fantástica compañía de aquel niño. La tarde del día siguiente me dijeron que en el gabinete de Mrs.
On repairing thither, I found a man waiting for me, having the appearance of a gentleman's servant: he was dressed in deep mourning, and the hat he held in his hand was surrounded with a crape band.
Me dirigí hacia allí y encontré a un hombre de aspecto de criado. Vestía de negro, con un crespón en el sombrero que tenía en la mano.

"I daresay you hardly remember me, Miss," he said, rising as I entered; "but my name is Leaven: I lived coachman with Mrs. Reed when you were at Gateshead, eight or nine years since, and I live there still."
Me llamo Leaven y era cochero en casa de Mrs. Reed cuando usted vivía allí hace ocho o nueve años.
"Oh, Robert! how do you do?
-¡Oh, Robert! ¿Cómo está usted?
I remember you very well: you used to give me a ride sometimes on Miss Georgiana's bay pony.
Le recuerdo muy bien. Solía usted montarme en la jaquita de Georgiana.
And how is Bessie?
¿Y Bessie?
You are married to Bessie?"
Porque es usted marido de Bessie, ¿verdad?
"Yes, Miss: my wife is very hearty, thank you; she brought me another little one about two months since--we have three now--and both mother and child are thriving."
Bessie está bien, gracias a Dios. Hace dos meses ha tenido otro pequeño.
"And are the family well at the house, Robert?"
Todos están bien. -¿Y mis parientes, Robert?
"I am sorry I can't give you better news of them, Miss: they are very badly at present--in great trouble."
¿Cómo se encuentran? -Siento decirle que mal. Sufren una gran desgracia.
"I hope no one is dead," I said, glancing at his black dress.
-Confío que no haya muerto ninguno -dije, dirigiendo una mirada al vestido negro del cochero.
He too looked down at the crape round his hat and replied-- "Mr. John died yesterday was a week, at his chambers in London."
-Mr. John ha muerto en Londres hace una semana.
"Mr. John?"
-¡John!
"And how does his mother bear it?"
-¿Y cómo está su madre?
"Why, you see, Miss Eyre, it is not a common mishap: his life has been very wild: these last three years he gave himself up to strange ways, and his death was shocking."
Mr. John hacía una vida muy extraña y su muerte lo ha sido más aún.
"I heard from Bessie he was not doing well."
-Bessie me dijo que no se comportaba bien. -¡Quia!
"Doing well! He could not do worse: he ruined his health and his estate amongst the worst men and the worst women.
Hacía una vida pésima, derrochando su dinero y su salud entre las peores gentes que podía encontrar.
He got into debt and into jail: his mother helped him out twice, but as soon as he was free he returned to his old companions and habits.
Dos veces ha estado preso por deudas. Su madre le ayudó a salir, pero en cuanto se halló libre volvió a sus vicios y a sus malas compañías.
His head was not strong: the knaves he lived amongst fooled him beyond anything I ever heard.
Creo que no estaba bien de la cabeza y las gentes con quienes trataba le acabaron de echar a perder.
He came down to Gateshead about three weeks ago and wanted missis to give up all to him.
Hace tres meses fue a casa y pidió a la señora que le diera todo cuanto poseía.
Missis refused: her means have long been much reduced by his extravagance; so he went back again, and the next news was that he was dead.
La señora se negó, porque sus bienes han mermado mucho como consecuencia de las locuras de su hijo.
How he died, God knows!--they say he killed himself."
Él se fue y ahora hemos sabido su muerte. ¡Y qué muerte!
I was silent: the things were frightful.
Yo estaba anonadada.

Robert Leaven resumed-- "Missis had been out of health herself for some time: she had got very stout, but was not strong with it; and the loss of money and fear of poverty were quite breaking her down.
Robert Leaven continuó. -La señora, a pesar de ser robusta, hace tiempo que no está bien de salud.
The information about Mr. John's death and the manner of it came too suddenly: it brought on a stroke.
Las pérdidas de dinero y el temor a la pobreza la han empeorado. Y la brusca noticia del suicidio del señorito le produjo un ataque.
She was three days without speaking; but last Tuesday she seemed rather better: she appeared as if she wanted to say something, and kept making signs to my wife and mumbling.
Durante tres días estuvo sin habla. El martes pasado parecía encontrarse mejor.
It was only yesterday morning, however, that Bessie understood she was pronouncing your name; and at last she made out the words, 'Bring Jane--fetch Jane Eyre: I want to speak to her.'
Hacía señas a mi mujer, como si quisiera decirle algo. Pero sólo ayer por la mañana pudo Bessie entender lo que le decía: «Tráigame a Jane, tengo que hablarla.»
Bessie is not sure whether she is in her right mind, or means anything by the words; but she told Miss Reed and Miss Georgiana, and advised them to send for you.
Aunque Bessie no tenía certeza de que la señora supiese lo que decía, habló a las señoritas, aconsejándolas que enviasen a buscarle a usted.
The young ladies put it off at first; but their mother grew so restless, and said, 'Jane, Jane,' so many times, that at last they consented.
Las jóvenes se indignaron, pero su madre repitió: «Jane, Jane», tantas veces, que acabaron consintiendo.
I left Gateshead yesterday: and if you can get ready, Miss, I should like to take you back with me early to-morrow morning."
Salí de Gateshead ayer y quisiera llevarla mañana por la mañana.
"Yes, Robert, I shall be ready: it seems to me that I ought to go."
-Iré, Robert. Creo que debo hacerlo.
"I think so too, Miss.
-También yo lo creo, señorita.
Bessie said she was sure you would not refuse: but I suppose you will have to ask leave before you can get off?"
Bessie decía que estaba segura de que usted no se negaría a ir. Tendrá que pedir permiso, ¿no?
"Yes; and I will do it now;" and having directed him to the servants' hall, and recommended him to the care of John's wife, and the attentions of John himself, I went in search of Mr. Rochester.
-Sí; ahora mismo voy a solicitarlo. Y dejando a Leaven al cuidado de John y de su mujer, fui en busca de Mr.
He was not in any of the lower rooms; he was not in the yard, the stables, or the grounds.
No le hallé ni en el salón, ni en el patio, ni en las cuadras. Pregunté por él a Mrs.
I asked Mrs. Fairfax if she had seen him;--yes: she believed he was playing billiards with Miss Ingram.
Fairfax y me dijo que debía de estar jugando al billar con Blanche Ingram.
To the billiard- room I hastened: the click of balls and the hum of voices resounded thence; Mr. Rochester, Miss Ingram, the two Misses Eshton, and their admirers, were all busied in the game.
Llegué al cuarto de billar. Oí las voces de Rochester, Blanche, las Eshton y sus admiradores, que estaban jugando.
It required some courage to disturb so interesting a party; my errand, however, was one I could not defer, so I approached the master where he stood at Miss Ingram's side.
Aunque me disgustaba interrumpirles, no tuve más remedio que abordar al dueño de la casa, porque mi viaje no se podía diferir.

She turned as I drew near, and looked at me haughtily: her eyes seemed to demand, "What can the creeping creature want now?" and when I said, in a low voice, "Mr. Rochester," she made a movement as if tempted to order me away.
Blanche me miró como preguntándose: «¿Qué querrá esta sabandija?», y cuando me acerqué a él y le dije en voz baja: «Mr. Rochester...», ella inició un movimiento como para mandarme salir.

I remember her appearance at the moment--it was very graceful and very striking: she wore a morning robe of sky-blue crape; a gauzy azure scarf was twisted in her hair. She had been all animation with the game, and irritated pride did not lower the expression of her haughty lineaments.
Recuerdo muy bien su aspecto de entonces. Vestía un vestido de crespón azul celeste y ceñía el cabello con una cinta de seda del mismo color.
"Does that person want you?" she inquired of Mr. Rochester; and Mr. Rochester turned to see who the "person" was.
-¿Qué quiere esta mujer? -preguntó a Mr. Rochester mientras éste se volvía para ver lo que yo deseaba.
He made a curious grimace--one of his strange and equivocal demonstrations--threw down his cue and followed me from the room.
Él hizo una de sus muecas características y me siguió fuera del cuarto.
"Well, Jane?" he said, as he rested his back against the schoolroom door, which he had shut.
-Y bien, Jane, ¿qué desea?
"If you please, sir, I want leave of absence for a week or two."
-Si no tiene inconveniente, señor, un permiso de una o dos semanas.
"What to do?--where to go?"
-¿Para que? ¿Adónde va?
"To see a sick lady who has sent for me."
-A visitar a una señora enferma, que ha enviado a buscarme.
"What sick lady?--where does she live?"
-¿Quién es? ¿Dónde vive?
"At Gateshead; in ---shire."
-En Gateshead, en el condado de...
"-shire? That is a hundred miles off!
-¿A cien millas de aquí?
Who may she be that sends for people to see her that distance?"
¿Para qué pueden querer que las visite gentes que viven a tanta distancia?
"Her name is Reed, sir--Mrs.
-Se llama Mrs.
Reed."
Reed y...
"Reed of Gateshead?
-¿Reed de Gasteshead?
There was a Reed of Gateshead, a magistrate."
Recuerdo un tal Reed de Gasteshead, un magistrado.
"It is his widow, sir."
-Es su viuda, señor.
"And what have you to do with her?
-¿Y qué tiene usted que ver con ella?
How do you know her?"
¿De qué la conoce? -Es tía mía.
"Mr. Reed was my uncle--my mother's brother."
Mr. Reed era hermano de mi madre. -¡Demonio!
"The deuce he was!
¿Por qué no me lo ha dicho antes?
You never told me that before: you always said you had no relations."
Siempre me ha manifestado usted que no tenía parientes.
"None that would own me, sir.
-Realmente no los tengo. Mi verdadero tío era Mr.
Mr. Reed is dead, and his wife cast me off."
Reed y, después de morir él, mi tía me envió fuera de su casa.
"Because I was poor, and burdensome, and she disliked me."
-Porque yo era pobre y la desagradaba.
"But Reed left children?--you must have cousins?
-Pero Reed creo que dejó hijos, primos de usted, por tanto...

Sir George Lynn was talking of a Reed of Gateshead yesterday, who, he said, was one of the veriest rascals on town; and Ingram was mentioning a Georgiana Reed of the same place, who was much admired for her beauty a season or two ago in London."

Sir Jorge Lynn me habló ayer de un Reed de Gateshead que es, por lo visto, uno de los mayores bribones de Londres, y de una Georgina Reed que causó mucha sensación en la capital hace una o dos temporadas.
"John Reed is dead, too, sir: he ruined himself and half-ruined his family, and is supposed to have committed suicide.
-John Reed ha muerto después de arruinarse y arruinar a su familia, y se supone que se ha suicidado.
The news so shocked his mother that it brought on an apoplectic attack."
La noticia ha producido a su madre un ataque de apoplejía.
"And what good can you do her? Nonsense, Jane!
-¿Y de qué va usted a servirla?
I would never think of running a hundred miles to see an old lady who will, perhaps, be dead before you reach her: besides, you say she cast you off."
Me parece un absurdo, Jane, que haga usted un viaje de cien millas para ver a una mujer que quizá haya muerto cuando usted llegue y que, para colmo, la echó a usted de su casa.
"Yes, sir, but that is long ago; and when her circumstances were very different: I could not be easy to neglect her wishes now."
-Sí, señor, pero eso ocurrió hace mucho y las circunstancias han variado. Mi deber ahora es complacerla.
"How long will you stay?"
-¿Cuánto tiempo estará fuera?
"As short a time as possible, sir."
-Lo menos posible, señor.
"Promise me only to stay a week--"
-¿Me promete no estar más de una semana?
"I had better not pass my word: I might be obliged to break it."
-Preferiría no darle palabra para no tener que incumplirla quizá.
"At all events you _will_ come back: you will not be induced under any pretext to take up a permanent residence with her?"
-En todo caso, ¿volverá usted y no se dejará inducir para quedarse allí?
"Oh, no!
-No.
I shall certainly return if all be well."
Volveré de todos modos. -Y ¿cómo nos arreglamos?
"And who goes with you? You don't travel a hundred miles alone."
¡No va usted a hacer sola un viaje de cien millas!
"No, sir, she has sent her coachman."
-Ha venido el cochero de mi tía para llevarme con él, señor.
"A person to be trusted?"
-¿Es persona de confianza?
"Yes, sir, he has lived ten years in the family."
-Sí. Lleva diez años en la casa.
Mr. Rochester meditated.
-¿Cuándo quiere irse? -dijo Mr.
"When do you wish to go?"
Rochester, después de meditar un momento.
"Early to-morrow morning, sir."
-Mañana por la mañana.
"Well, you must have some money; you can't travel without money, and I daresay you have not much: I have given you no salary yet.
-Supongo que necesitará usted dinero, porque presumo que no tendrá mucho y yo no le he pagado aún su salario.
How much have you in the world, Jane?" he asked, smiling.
¿Cuánto tiene para toda la vida, Jane? -me preguntó, sonriendo.
I drew out my purse; a meagre thing it was. "Five shillings, sir."
-Cinco chelines, señor -repuse, mostrándole mi flaca bolsa.
He took the purse, poured the hoard into his palm, and chuckled over it as if its scantiness amused him.
Vació el contenido en la palma de la mano y lo agitó, alegremente, como si fuera cosa que le agradase.
Soon he produced his pocket-book: "Here," said he, offering me a note; it was fifty pounds, and he owed me but fifteen.
Luego sacó su billetero y me ofreció un billete. Eran cincuenta libras y no me debía más que quince.
I told him I had no change.
Le dije que no tenía cambio.
"I don't want change; you know that.
-No necesito cambio. Ya lo sabe usted.
Take your wages."
Es su sueldo.
I declined accepting more than was my due.
Rehusé, manifestando que aquello era más de lo que me debía.
He scowled at first; then, as if recollecting something, he said-- "Right, right!
Pareció pensar de pronto en algo, y dijo: -Bueno, bueno.
Better not give you all now: you would, perhaps, stay away three months if you had fifty pounds.
Quizá sea mejor. De lo contrario, tal vez esté usted tres meses allí.
There are ten; is it not plenty?"
Tome entonces diez libras. ¿Basta?
"Yes, sir, but now you owe me five."
-Sí. Ahora me debe usted cinco.
"Come back for it, then; I am your banker for forty pounds."
Soy su banquero. Tiene usted conmigo cuenta corriente por cuarenta libras.
"Mr. Rochester, I may as well mention another matter of business to you while I have the opportunity."
-Mr. Rochester, quisiera de paso hablarle de negocios.
"Matter of business?
-¿De negocios?
I am curious to hear it."
Me muero de curiosidad.
"You have as good as informed me, sir, that you are going shortly to be married?"
Hable. -Usted ha tenido la amabilidad de informarme de que piensa casarse en breve.
"Yes; what then?"
-Sí; ¿y qué?
"In that case, sir, Adele ought to go to school: I am sure you will perceive the necessity of it."
-En tal caso, Adèle debe ir a un colegio. Estoy segura de que usted lo considerará necesario.
"To get her out of my bride's way, who might otherwise walk over her rather too emphatically?
-Desde luego, tendré que ponerla fuera del alcance de mi esposa que, si no, quizá se comportase demasiado altivamente con ella.
There's sense in the suggestion; not a doubt of it.
La sugerencia es razonable, sin duda.
Adele, as you say, must go to school; and you, of course, must march straight to--the devil?"
Como usted dice bien, Adèle tendrá que ir a un colegio. Y usted, ¿adónde irá?
"I hope not, sir; but I must seek another situation somewhere."
-Espero que no, señor, pero tendré que pensar en buscar otro empleo.
"In course!" he exclaimed, with a twang of voice and a distortion of features equally fantastic and ludicrous. He looked at me some minutes.
-Por supuesto -exclamó, contrayendo las facciones y con un extraño tono de chanza.
"And old Madam Reed, or the Misses, her daughters, will be solicited by you to seek a place, I suppose?"
Luego, agregó-: Supongo que pedirá usted a la vieja Reed y a sus primos que le busquen un puesto, ¿no?
"No, sir; I am not on such terms with my relatives as would justify me in asking favours of them--but I shall advertise."
-No, señor. No estoy con mis parientes en tan buenas relaciones como para pedirles que me proporcionen empleo.
"You shall walk up the pyramids of Egypt!" he growled.
-¡Veo que va usted a irse a parar lo menos a las pirámides de Egipto!
"At your peril you advertise!
Ha hecho usted mal en advertirme.
I wish I had only offered you a sovereign instead of ten pounds.
En vista de eso, sólo le doy un soberano.
Give me back nine pounds, Jane; I've a use for it."
Devuélvame nueve libras, Jane. Las tengo destinadas a...
"And so have I, sir," I returned, putting my hands and my purse behind me.
-También yo, señor -dije poniendo las manos sobre mi bolsillo-.
"I could not spare the money on any account."
No puedo ceder dinero en concepto alguno.
"Little niggard!" said he, "refusing me a pecuniary request!
-¡Qué avarienta! ¡Negarme una petición de dinero!
Give me five pounds, Jane."
Deme cinco libras siquiera, Jane.
"Not five shillings, sir; nor five pence."
-Ni cinco chelines, señor. Ni cinco peniques.
"Jane!"
-¡Jane!
"Promise me one thing."
-Prométame una cosa.
"Not to advertise: and to trust this quest of a situation to me.
Que cuando necesite esa nueva colocación me la pida.
I'll find you one in time."
Yo se la encontraré.
"I shall be glad so to do, sir, if you, in your turn, will promise that I and Adele shall be both safe out of the house before your bride enters it."
-Lo haré con gusto, si a su vez me promete que Adèle y yo saldremos de esta casa antes de que entre en ella su esposa.
"Very well! very well!
-Bueno, bueno.
I'll pledge my word on it.
Le doy palabra...
You go to-morrow, then?"
¿Se va mañana, pues?
"Yes, sir; early."
-Sí; muy temprano.
"Shall you come down to the drawing-room after dinner?"
-¿Bajará hoy al comedor después de cenar?
"No, sir, I must prepare for the journey."
-No, señor. Tengo que preparar mi equipaje.
"Then you and I must bid good-bye for a little while?"
-Entonces, ¿debemos despedirnos por algún tiempo?
"I suppose so, sir."
-Supongo que sí, señor.
