"And how do people perform that ceremony of parting, Jane?
-Y ¿cómo se verifica esa ceremonia de la despedida, Jane?
Teach me; I'm not quite up to it."
No estoy muy al corriente. Infórmeme.
"They say, Farewell, or any other form they prefer."
-Pues diciéndose adiós, u otra fórmula semejante, a elección.
"Then say it."
-¿Por ejemplo?
"Farewell, Mr. Rochester, for the present."
-Hasta la vista...
"What must I say?"
-Y yo, por mi parte, ¿qué debo decir?
"The same, if you like, sir."
-Lo mismo, si usted gusta.
"Farewell, Miss Eyre, for the present; is that all?"
Adiós, Miss Eyre, hasta la vista. ¿Nada más?
"Yes?"
-Nada mas.
"It seems stingy, to my notions, and dry, and unfriendly.
-A mí me parece esto muy frío y poco afectuoso.
I should like something else: a little addition to the rite.
Convendría añadir algún detalle a ese ritual.
If one shook hands, for instance; but no--that would not content me either.
Un apretón de manos, por ejemplo... Pero eso sería lo mismo.
So you'll do no more than say Farewell, Jane?"
¿Así que se limita usted a decirme adiós?
"It is enough, sir: as much good-will may be conveyed in one hearty word as in many."
-Es suficiente, señor. Tanto se puede decir con una palabra como con muchas.
"Very likely; but it is blank and cool--'Farewell.'"
-Pero esto es tan seco, tan glacial... «Adiós...»
"How long is he going to stand with his back against that door?" I asked myself; "I want to commence my packing."
-Tengo que hacer mi equipaje... -empecé a decir.
The dinner-bell rang, and suddenly away he bolted, without another syllable: I saw him no more during the day, and was off before he had risen in the morning.
Pero en aquel momento sonó la campana de la cena y él, sin añadir una sola sílaba más, se alejó. No le vi en todo el día y partí al día siguiente antes de que se levantara.
I reached the lodge at Gateshead about five o'clock in the afternoon of the first of May: I stepped in there before going up to the hall.
Llegué a Gateshead a las cinco de aquella tarde de principios de mayo. Me detuve en la portería antes de seguir a la casa.
It was very clean and neat: the ornamental windows were hung with little white curtains; the floor was spotless; the grate and fire-irons were burnished bright, and the fire burnt clear.
Las ventanas ostentaban blancas cortinillas. El suelo se hallaba escrupulosamente limpio.
Bessie sat on the hearth, nursing her last-born, and Robert and his sister played quietly in a corner.
Los dorados brillaban y en la chimenea ardía un excelente fuego. Bessie estaba junto a la lumbre amamantando a su pequeño y Robert y su hermana jugaban tranquilamente en un rincón.
"Bless you!--I knew you would come!" exclaimed Mrs. Leaven, as I entered.
-¡Bendito sea Dios! Ya sabía yo que vendría -dijo Bessie al verme entrar.
"Yes, Bessie," said I, after I had kissed her; "and I trust I am not too late.
-Sí, Bessie -dije, besándola-. He venido en cuanto me ha sido posible.
How is Mrs. Reed?--Alive still, I hope."
¿Y mi tía? Confío en que vivirá aún.
"Yes, she is alive; and more sensible and collected than she was.
-Vive, y hasta está más lúcida.
The doctor says she may linger a week or two yet; but he hardly thinks she will finally recover."
El doctor cree que resistirá aún una o dos semanas, pero dudo mucho que se restablezca.
"Has she mentioned me lately?"
-¿Ha vuelto a mencionarme?
"She was talking of you only this morning, and wishing you would come, but she is sleeping now, or was ten minutes ago, when I was up at the house.
-Esta mañana. Ahora -por lo menos hace diez minutos- está durmiendo.
She generally lies in a kind of lethargy all the afternoon, and wakes up about six or seven.
Suele pasar aletargada toda la tarde y despertar a las seis o las siete.
Will you rest yourself here an hour, Miss, and then I will go up with you?"
¿Quiere quedarse aquí una hora? Luego subiría yo con usted...

Robert here entered, and Bessie laid her sleeping child in the cradle and went to welcome him: afterwards she insisted on my taking off my bonnet and having some tea; for she said I looked pale and tired.
Entró Robert, y Bessie, dejando al niño en la cuna, fue a recibirle. Después insistió en que yo me quitase el sombrero y tomase el té, porque le parecía verme pálida y fatigada.
I was glad to accept her hospitality; and I submitted to be relieved of my travelling garb just as passively as I used to let her undress me when a child.
Acepté con satisfacción su hospitalidad y dejé que me quitase la ropa de viaje como cuando era niña y ella me desvestía.

Old times crowded fast back on me as I watched her bustling about--setting out the tea-tray with her best china, cutting bread and butter, toasting a tea-cake, and, between whiles, giving little Robert or Jane an occasional tap or push, just as she used to give me in former days.
Recordé los viejos tiempos al verla preparar el té, cortar pan con manteca, tostar los bollos y, entretanto, dar algún empujón o un cachete a Robert y Jane, como a mí cuando era niña.
Bessie had retained her quick temper as well as her light foot and good looks.
Bessie había conservado su genio vivo como conservaba su agilidad y su buen aspecto.

Tea ready, I was going to approach the table; but she desired me to sit still, quite in her old peremptory tones. I must be served at the fireside, she said; and she placed before me a little round stand with my cup and a plate of toast, absolutely as she used to accommodate me with some privately purloined dainty on a nursery chair: and I smiled and obeyed her as in bygone days.

Una vez preparado el té, me dispuse a sentarme a la mesa, pero ella, con el tono autoritario de los años antiguos, me conminó a instalarme junto a la lumbre y colocó ante mí una mesita redonda en la que puso el servicio, exactamente como en mi infancia. Y, como en mi infancia también, la obedecí, sonriendo.
She wanted to know if I was happy at Thornfield Hall, and what sort of a person the mistress was; and when I told her there was only a master, whether he was a nice gentleman, and if I liked him.
Me preguntó si estaba contenta en Thornfield Hall y cómo era la señora.
I told her he was rather an ugly man, but quite a gentleman; and that he treated me kindly, and I was content.
Contesté que no era señora, sino señor, y por cierto todo un caballero, que me trataba amablemente, y que estaba muy satisfecha.
Then I went on to describe to her the gay company that had lately been staying at the house; and to these details Bessie listened with interest: they were precisely of the kind she relished.
Luego le describí la clase de visitantes que había en la casa y Bessie me atendió con interés, porque tales detalles eran los que le encantaban.
In such conversation an hour was soon gone: Bessie restored to me my bonnet, &c., and, accompanied by her, I quitted the lodge for the hall.
Hablando, se nos fue una hora. Bessie volvió a ponerme el sombrero y demás adminículos y nos dirigimos a la casa.

It was also accompanied by her that I had, nearly nine years ago, walked down the path I was now ascending. On a dark, misty, raw morning in January, I had left a hostile roof with a desperate and embittered heart--a sense of outlawry and almost of reprobation--to seek the chilly harbourage of Lowood: that bourne so far away and unexplored.

También fui acompañada por ella como bajara yo, nueve años atrás, la escalera que ahora subía, en aquella oscura y brumosa mañana de enero en que abandoné una mansión hostil con el corazón amargado y desesperado, para buscar el frío refugio de Lowood, entonces lugar desconocido e inexplorado para mí.

The same hostile roof now again rose before me: my prospects were doubtful yet; and I had yet an aching heart. I still felt as a wanderer on the face of the earth; but I experienced firmer trust in myself and my own powers, and less withering dread of oppression.

El mismo techo hostil me acogía de nuevo y también ahora me parecía ser una peregrina errante a través de la tierra, pero me sentía más segura de mí misma y me asustaban menos las injusticias que pudieran cometer conmigo los demás.
The gaping wound of my wrongs, too, was now quite healed; and the flame of resentment extinguished.
La herida de los agravios recibidos hacía tiempo estaba curada y la llama de los rencores, extinguida.
"You shall go into the breakfast-room first," said Bessie, as she preceded me through the hall; "the young ladies will be there."
-Entre primero en el cuarto de desayunar -dijo Bessie-. Están allí las señoritas.
In another moment I was within that apartment.
Entré.
There was every article of furniture looking just as it did on the morning I was first introduced to Mr. Brocklehurst: the very rug he had stood upon still covered the hearth.
Todo estaba igual que la mañana en que me presentaran a Mr. Brock1ehurst.

Glancing at the bookcases, I thought I could distinguish the two volumes of Bewick's British Birds occupying their old place on the third shelf, and Gulliver's Travels and the Arabian Nights ranged just above.
La alfombra era la misma, idéntica la biblioteca y hasta en su tercer estante pude distinguir Los viajes de Gulliver, Las mil y una noches y los demás libros que leía en mi niñez.
The inanimate objects were not changed; but the living things had altered past recognition.
Los objetos inanimados no habían cambiado, pero los vivientes habían experimentado variación.
Two young ladies appeared before me; one very tall, almost as tall as Miss Ingram--very thin too, with a sallow face and severe mien.
Ante mí se hallaban dos jóvenes: una muy alta, casi tanto como Blanche Ingram, muy delgada, de faz severa y cetrina.

There was something ascetic in her look, which was augmented by the extreme plainness of a straight-skirted, black, stuff dress, a starched linen collar, hair combed away from the temples, and the nun-like ornament of a string of ebony beads and a crucifix.
Todo en su aspecto era ascético. Aumentaba esta impresión la extrema sencillez de su vestido negro con un cuello blanco almidonado, su cabello liso y el monjil adorno de un rosario y un crucifijo.
This I felt sure was Eliza, though I could trace little resemblance to her former self in that elongated and colourless visage.
Tuve la certeza de que era Eliza aunque se parecía muy poco a la Eliza de mis recuerdos.
The other was as certainly Georgiana: but not the Georgiana I remembered--the slim and fairy-like girl of eleven.
La otra era Georgiana pero no la Georgiana de once años, la linda y delgada muchachita que yo evocaba.
This was a full-blown, very plump damsel, fair as waxwork, with handsome and regular features, languishing blue eyes, and ringleted yellow hair.
La actual era una opulenta joven, de amplias líneas, blanca como la cera, de hermosas y correctas facciones, lánguidos ojos azules y dorados rizos.
The hue of her dress was black too; but its fashion was so different from her sister's--so much more flowing and becoming--it looked as stylish as the other's looked puritanical.
Su vestido era negro también, pero absolutamente distinto del de su hermana.

In each of the sisters there was one trait of the mother--and only one; the thin and pallid elder daughter had her parent's Cairngorm eye: the blooming and luxuriant younger girl had her contour of jaw and chin--perhaps a little softened, but still imparting an indescribable hardness to the countenance otherwise so voluptuous and buxom.
Una especie de luto estilizado.
Both ladies, as I advanced, rose to welcome me, and both addressed me by the name of "Miss Eyre."
Ambas se levantaron al entrar yo y me saludaron llamándome «Miss Eyre».
Eliza's greeting was delivered in a short, abrupt voice, without a smile; and then she sat down again, fixed her eyes on the fire, and seemed to forget me.
Eliza me dio la bienvenida con brusca, breve y cortada voz y sin una sonrisa, y luego dirigió la mirada al fuego y pareció olvidarse de mí.

Georgiana added to her "How d'ye do?" several commonplaces about my journey, the weather, and so on, uttered in rather a drawling tone: and accompanied by sundry side-glances that measured me from head to foot--now traversing the folds of my drab merino pelisse, and now lingering on the plain trimming of my cottage bonnet.

Georgiana añadió un «¿cómo está usted?», varios tópicos acerca de mi viaje y el tiempo que hacía y una mirada con la que me examinó de pies a cabeza, deteniéndose en mi pelliza, de merino de color pardo.

Young ladies have a remarkable way of letting you know that they think you a "quiz" without actually saying the words. A certain superciliousness of look, coolness of manner, nonchalance of tone, express fully their sentiments on the point, without committing them by any positive rudeness in word or deed.

Ambas muchachas tenían una curiosa manera de hacerle comprender a una que era una infeliz sin que una sola de sus palabras o actos lo exteriorizasen. Pero el desprecio, encubierto o no, ejercía poca influencia entonces sobre mí.

A sneer, however, whether covert or open, had now no longer that power over me it once possessed: as I sat between my cousins, I was surprised to find how easy I felt under the total neglect of the one and the semi- sarcastic attentions of the other--Eliza did not mortify, nor Georgiana ruffle me.
Hasta a mí me maravilló la naturalidad con que me senté entre mis dos primas, con absoluta indiferencia hacia el desprecio de la una y las irónicas amabilidades de la otra.

The fact was, I had other things to think about; within the last few months feelings had been stirred in me so much more potent than any they could raise--pains and pleasures so much more acute and exquisite had been excited than any it was in their power to inflict or bestow--that their airs gave me no concern either for good or bad.

Yo tenía otras cosas en qué pensar, placeres y dolores mucho mayores que experimentar y sufrir -sobre todo desde los últimos meses- y ellas no podían producirme ninguna impresión semejante, cualesquiera que fuesen sus propósitos en bien o en mal.
"How is Mrs. Reed?"
-¿Cómo está Mrs.
I asked soon, looking calmly at Georgiana, who thought fit to bridle at the direct address, as if it were an unexpected liberty.
Reed? -pregunté a Georgiana.
"Mrs. Reed?
-¿Mrs...? ¡Ah, quiere usted decir mamá!
Ah! mama, you mean; she is extremely poorly: I doubt if you can see her to-night."
Muy mal. Dudo mucho de que pueda usted verla esta noche.
"If," said I, "you would just step upstairs and tell her I am come, I should be much obliged to you."
-Si tiene usted la atención de manifestarla que he venido, se lo agradeceré mucho -dije.
Georgiana almost started, and she opened her blue eyes wild and wide.
Georgiana me miró con asombro.
"I know she had a particular wish to see me," I added, "and I would not defer attending to her desire longer than is absolutely necessary."
-Sé -proseguí- que tenía un particular interés en verme y no quiero aplazar el cumplimiento de su deseo más del tiempo imprescindible.
"Mama dislikes being disturbed in an evening," remarked Eliza.
-A mamá no le agradará que la molesten por la noche -intervino Eliza.

I soon rose, quietly took off my bonnet and gloves, uninvited, and said I would just step out to Bessie--who was, I dared say, in the kitchen--and ask her to ascertain whether Mrs. Reed was disposed to receive me or not to- night.
Me levanté, cogí el sombrero y los guantes y dije que iba a preguntar a Bessie si Mrs. Reed estaba dispuesta o no a recibirme aquella noche.
I went, and having found Bessie and despatched her on my errand, I proceeded to take further measures.
La despaché, pues, a averiguarlo y me preparé a adoptar ulteriores medidas.

It had heretofore been my habit always to shrink from arrogance: received as I had been to-day, I should, a year ago, have resolved to quit Gateshead the very next morning; now, it was disclosed to me all at once that that would be a foolish plan.
Si un año antes me hubiesen hecho una recepción de aquella clase en Gateshead, hubiera partido a la mañana siguiente. Pero ahora comprendía que ello, en esta ocasión, hubiese sido desacertado.

I had taken a journey of a hundred miles to see my aunt, and I must stay with her till she was better--or dead: as to her daughters' pride or folly, I must put it on one side, make myself independent of it.
Había hecho un viaje de cien millas para ver a mi tía y no debía separarme de su lado hasta que mejorase o muriera, sin preocuparme del orgullo y la insensatez de sus hijas.

So I addressed the housekeeper; asked her to show me a room, told her I should probably be a visitor here for a week or two, had my trunk conveyed to my chamber, and followed it thither myself: I met Bessie on the landing.
Me dirigí, pues, al ama de llaves y le pedí que me preparase un cuarto, advirtiéndola que quizá permaneciese allí una semana o dos. Llevaron mi equipaje a mi cuarto.
"Missis is awake," said she; "I have told her you are here: come and let us see if she will know you."
La he dicho que ha venido usted. Venga y veremos si la reconoce.

I did not need to be guided to the well-known room, to which I had so often been summoned for chastisement or reprimand in former days. I hastened before Bessie; I softly opened the door: a shaded light stood on the table, for it was now getting dark.

No me era necesario guía para llegar al bien conocido cuarto a que tantas veces me llamaran en los viejos tiempos para propinarme castigos o reprimendas. Precedí a Bessie y abrí la puerta con suavidad.

There was the great four-post bed with amber hangings as of old; there the toilet-table, the armchair, and the footstool, at which I had a hundred times been sentenced to kneel, to ask pardon for offences by me uncommitted.

Sobre la mesa había una bujía y a su luz vi el gran lecho con las mismas cortinas de antes, el tocador, la butaca y el taburete en que cien veces fui condenada a arrodillarme para pedir perdón de faltas que no había cometido.

I looked into a certain corner near, half-expecting to see the slim outline of a once dreaded switch which used to lurk there, waiting to leap out imp-like and lace my quivering palm or shrinking neck.
Incluso miré a cierto rincón esperando ver la varilla con que solían golpearme la palma de la mano.
I approached the bed; I opened the curtains and leant over the high-piled pillows.
Luego me acerqué al lecho y corrí las cortinillas que colgaban entre sus columnas.
Well did I remember Mrs. Reed's face, and I eagerly sought the familiar image.
Recordando muy bien el rostro de mi tía.
It is a happy thing that time quells the longings of vengeance and hushes the promptings of rage and aversion.
El tiempo tiene la virtud de disipar los afanes de venganza y extinguir los impulsos de aversión.

I had left this woman in bitterness and hate, and I came back to her now with no other emotion than a sort of ruth for her great sufferings, and a strong yearning to forget and forgive all injuries--to be reconciled and clasp hands in amity.

Yo me había separado de aquella mujer odiándola y ahora no experimentaba, sin embargo, más que conmiseración hacia sus grandes sufrimientos y un vivo deseo de perdonar y olvidar sus injurias y reconciliarme con ella.
The well-known face was there: stern, relentless as ever--there was that peculiar eye which nothing could melt, and the somewhat raised, imperious, despotic eyebrow.
Distinguí su rostro duro e inflexible, su entrecejo imperioso, despótico, sus inconfundibles ojos...
How often had it lowered on me menace and hate! and how the recollection of childhood's terrors and sorrows revived as I traced its harsh line now!
¡Cuántas veces me habían contemplado con odio y amenazadores, y cuántas tristezas y terrores de la niñez me recordaban!
And yet I stooped down and kissed her: she looked at me.
No obstante, me incliné y besé aquel rostro.
"Is this Jane Eyre?" she said.
Ella me miró. -¿Eres Jane Eyre? -dijo.
"Yes, Aunt Reed.
-Sí, lo soy.
How are you, dear aunt?"
¿Cómo está usted, querida tía?
I had once vowed that I would never call her aunt again: I thought it no sin to forget and break that vow now.
Aunque yo jurara una vez no volver a llamarla tía jamás, no consideré pecado quebrantar ahora este juramento.
My fingers had fastened on her hand which lay outside the sheet: had she pressed mine kindly, I should at that moment have experienced true pleasure.
Mis dedos buscaron su mano. Si ella la hubiese oprimido amistosamente, yo habría encontrado en ello verdadero placer.
But unimpressionable natures are not so soon softened, nor are natural antipathies so readily eradicated.
Pero las naturalezas insensibles no se ablandan con facilidad y las antipatías espontáneas no se desarraigan en un momento.
Mrs. Reed took her hand away, and, turning her face rather from me, she remarked that the night was warm.
Ella separó su mano y, volviendo la cara, comentó que la noche era calurosa.
Again she regarded me so icily, I felt at once that her opinion of me--her feeling towards me--was unchanged and unchangeable.
Cuando volvió a mirarme, con igual frialdad que siempre, comprendí que sus sentimientos respecto a mí no habían cambiado ni podían cambiar.

I knew by her stony eye--opaque to tenderness, indissoluble to tears--that she was resolved to consider me bad to the last; because to believe me good would give her no generous pleasure: only a sense of mortification.

Adiviné por sus duros ojos, impenetrables a la ternura, incapaces de lágrimas, que ella había resuelto considerarme mala hasta el fin, ya que creerme buena, en vez de producirla un generoso placer, le habría originado una mortificación.

I felt pain, and then I felt ire; and then I felt a determination to subdue her--to be her mistress in spite both of her nature and her will. My tears had risen, just as in childhood: I ordered them back to their source. I brought a chair to the bed-head: I sat down and leaned over the pillow.
Sentí pena y enojo, contuve mis lágrimas, a punto ya de brotar, como en la infancia, tomé una silla y me senté a la cabecera del lecho.
"You sent for me," I said, "and I am here; and it is my intention to stay till I see how you get on."
-Me ha enviado usted a buscar -dije- y he venido. No pienso irme antes de que me diga lo que deseaba.
"Oh, of course!
-Por supuesto.
You have seen my daughters?"
¿Has visto a mis hijas?
"Well, you may tell them I wish you to stay till I can talk some things over with you I have on my mind: to-night it is too late, and I have a difficulty in recalling them.
-Pues puedes decirlas que quiero que estés aquí hasta que pueda explicarte ciertas cosas que tengo en la cabeza. Ahora es demasiado tarde y no me es fácil recordar...
But there was something I wished to say--let me see--" The wandering look and changed utterance told what wreck had taken place in her once vigorous frame.
Pero deseaba decirte... espera. Su errante mirada y su alterado rostro demostraban que su antigua energía había desaparecido.
Turning restlessly, she drew the bedclothes round her; my elbow, resting on a corner of the quilt, fixed it down: she was at once irritated.
Trató de envolverse en las ropas de la cama. Mi codo, apoyado en la colcha, se lo dificultaba y se irritó.
"Sit up!" said she; "don't annoy me with holding the clothes fast.
-No me molestes sujetando las ropas -dijo-.
Are you Jane Eyre?"
¿Eres Jane Eyre?
"I am Jane Eyre."
-Sí.
"I have had more trouble with that child than any one would believe.
-Esa niña me ha dado más disgustos que lo que nadie puede imaginar.

Such a burden to be left on my hands--and so much annoyance as she caused me, daily and hourly, with her incomprehensible disposition, and her sudden starts of temper, and her continual, unnatural watchings of one's movements!
¡Cuántas complicaciones me produjo, cada día y cada hora, con su incomprensible carácter y con su brusquedad! ¡Y qué modo tenía de contemplarle a una!
I declare she talked to me once like something mad, or like a fiend--no child ever spoke or looked as she did; I was glad to get her away from the house.
Una vez me habló como lo hubiera hecho un demonio. Ningún niño habría dicho lo que ella.
What did they do with her at Lowood? The fever broke out there, and many of the pupils died. She, however, did not die: but I said she did--I wish she had died!"
¡Y luego, cuando se declaró la epidemia en Lowood y murieron tantas discípulas, ella no murió, a pesar de lo mucho que yo deseaba que muriese!
"A strange wish, Mrs. Reed; why do you hate her so?"
-¡Extraño deseo! ¿Por qué la odiaba así?

"I had a dislike to her mother always; for she was my husband's only sister, and a great favourite with him: he opposed the family's disowning her when she made her low marriage; and when news came of her death, he wept like a simpleton.
Era la única hermana de mi marido y él la quería mucho. Cuando se casó y murió al poco tiempo, mi esposo lloró como un tonto.
He would send for the baby; though I entreated him rather to put it out to nurse and pay for its maintenance.
Se empeñó en recoger a su hija, aunque yo le aconsejaba enviarla con una nodriza y pagar los gastos.
I hated it the first time I set my eyes on it--a sickly, whining, pining thing!
Odié a aquella pequeña desde que la vi, tan enfermiza, tan llorona...
It would wail in its cradle all night long--not screaming heartily like any other child, but whimpering and moaning.
No se durmió en su cuna como los demás niños, sino que pasó la noche lloriqueando.
Reed pitied it; and he used to nurse it and notice it as if it had been his own: more, indeed, than he ever noticed his own at that age.
Reed se compadecía de ella y no hacía más que informarse de su salud, como si fuera hija suya, o más aún, porque de sus hijos, a esa edad, casi no se preocupaba.
He would try to make my children friendly to the little beggar: the darlings could not bear it, and he was angry with them when they showed their dislike.
Se empeñaba en que mis niños tratasen bien a aquella mendiga y les reprendía si se negaban.
In his last illness, he had it brought continually to his bedside; and but an hour before he died, he bound me by vow to keep the creature.
Cuando enfermó mortalmente, no hacía más que llamar a la pequeña a su lado y me encargó antes de morir que la conservase bajo mi custodia.
I would as soon have been charged with a pauper brat out of a workhouse: but he was weak, naturally weak.
¡Encargarme de una hospiciana! Reed era débil, muy débil.
John does not at all resemble his father, and I am glad of it: John is like me and like my brothers--he is quite a Gibson.
John no se parece a su padre, gracias a Dios: es como mis hermanas y como yo.
Oh, I wish he would cease tormenting me with letters for money?
¡El vivo retrato de mi hermana Gibson!
I have no more money to give him: we are getting poor.
¡Sólo quisiera que dejase de atormentarme pidiéndome dinero!
I must send away half the servants and shut up part of the house; or let it off.
Ya no tengo nada que darle; estamos casi arruinados.
I can never submit to do that--yet how are we to get on?
Voy a tener que despedir a la mitad de la servidumbre y cerrar parte de la casa.
Two-thirds of my income goes in paying the interest of mortgages.
Dos tercios de las rentas se gastan en pagar los intereses de las hipotecas.
John gambles dreadfully, and always loses--poor boy!
John juega mucho y siempre pierde, el pobre... Vive rodeado de fulleros.
He is beset by sharpers: John is sunk and degraded--his look is frightful--I feel ashamed for him when I see him."
Y tiene un aspecto horroroso. Me avergüenza verle como le veo...
"I think I had better leave her now," said I to Bessie, who stood on the other side of the bed.
-Será mejor que salgamos -murmuré viendo tan excitada a mi tía.
"Perhaps you had, Miss: but she often talks in this way towards night--in the morning she is calmer."
Suele hablar así durante las noches. Por las mañanas está más tranquila -dijo Bessie, que estaba sentada al otro lado del lecho.
I rose.
Me levanté.
"Stop!" exclaimed Mrs. Reed, "there is another thing I wished to say.
-Esperad -exclamó la Reed-; tengo algo más que decir.
He threatens me--he continually threatens me with his own death, or mine: and I dream sometimes that I see him laid out with a great wound in his throat, or with a swollen and blackened face.
John me amenaza siempre con matarse o matarme. Muchas veces sueño que le veo tendido, con una enorme herida en la garganta o con el rostro negro, como los ahogados...
I am come to a strange pass: I have heavy troubles.
¡Oh, qué situación la mía!
What is to be done?
¿Qué haré?
How is the money to be had?"
¿De dónde sacaré dinero?
Bessie now endeavoured to persuade her to take a sedative draught: she succeeded with difficulty.
Bessie comenzó a persuadirla de que tomase un sedante y lo logró sin gran trabajo.
Soon after, Mrs. Reed grew more composed, and sank into a dozing state.
A poco, mi tía se tranquilizó y cayó en una especie de letargo.
I then left her.
Entonces me fui.
More than ten days elapsed before I had again any conversation with her.
Pasaron más de diez días antes de que pudiese reanudar mi conversación con ella.
She continued either delirious or lethargic; and the doctor forbade everything which could painfully excite her.
Estaba continuamente o delirando o amodorrada, y el médico prohibió hacer nada que pudiese impresionarla.
Meantime, I got on as well as I could with Georgiana and Eliza.
Entretanto me entendí lo mejor que pude con Georgiana y Eliza.
They were very cold, indeed, at first.
Ellas continuaban tan frías como al principio.
Eliza would sit half the day sewing, reading, or writing, and scarcely utter a word either to me or her sister.
Eliza estaba sentada casi todo el día, cosiendo, escribiendo o leyendo, y no nos dirigía la palabra ni a su hermana ni a mí.
Georgiana would chatter nonsense to her canary bird by the hour, and take no notice of me.
Georgiana pasaba horas y horas diciendo tonterías a su canario y no me hacía caso alguno.
But I was determined not to seem at a loss for occupation or amusement: I had brought my drawing materials with me, and they served me for both.
Pero yo no perdía mi tiempo. Había traído mis útiles de trabajo y los utilizaba.

Provided with a case of pencils, and some sheets of paper, I used to take a seat apart from them, near the window, and busy myself in sketching fancy vignettes, representing any scene that happened momentarily to shape itself in the ever-shifting kaleidoscope of imagination: a glimpse of sea between two rocks; the rising moon, and a ship crossing its disk; a group of reeds and water-flags, and a naiad's head, crowned with lotus- flowers, rising out of them; an elf sitting in a hedge-sparrow's nest, under a wreath of hawthorn-bloom.

Con mi caja de lápices y unas hojas de papel, me sentaba aparte de ellas, junto a la ventana, y me divertía en hacer los dibujos que se me ocurrían, las escenas que desfilaban por el quimérico calidoscopio de mi imaginación. Un trozo de mar entre las rocas, la luna elevándose sobre el mar y un navío cruzando ante su disco, la cabeza de una náyade coronada de flores de loto surgiendo entre olas, un enano sentado en un nido...
One morning I fell to sketching a face: what sort of a face it was to be, I did not care or know.
Una mañana comencé a dibujar un rostro, sin preocuparme de lo que pudiera resultar.
I took a soft black pencil, gave it a broad point, and worked away.
Tomé un lápiz blando, de punta ancha, y comencé a trabajar.
Soon I had traced on the paper a broad and prominent forehead and a square lower outline of visage: that contour gave me pleasure; my fingers proceeded actively to fill it with features.
A poco, había trazado una frente amplia y saliente, y el contorno de una cara cuadrada. El principio me agradó y comencé a completar las facciones.

Strongly-marked horizontal eyebrows must be traced under that brow; then followed, naturally, a well-defined nose, with a straight ridge and full nostrils; then a flexible-looking mouth, by no means narrow; then a firm chin, with a decided cleft down the middle of it: of course, some black whiskers were wanted, and some jetty hair, tufted on the temples, and waved above the forehead.

Bajo aquella frente se imponían unas cejas horizontales reciamente marcadas, a las que habían de seguir, naturalmente, una nariz enérgica, de amplias ventanas, una boca flexible y una firme barbilla con un bien definido hoyo en el centro. El conjunto necesitaba, evidentemente, patillas negras y cabello negro, formando dos tufos en las sienes y ondeado por arriba.
Now for the eyes: I had left them to the last, because they required the most careful working.
Los ojos habían quedado para lo último, por requerir un trabajo más esmerado.
I drew them large; I shaped them well: the eyelashes I traced long and sombre; the irids lustrous and large.
Los hice grandes, muy sombreados, con largas pestañas y pupila ancha y brillante.

"Good! but not quite the thing," I thought, as I surveyed the effect: "they want more force and spirit;" and I wrought the shades blacker, that the lights might flash more brilliantly--a happy touch or two secured success.
Necesita más fuerza, más alma.» Un par de toques, que dieron a las sombras más oscuridad y a las luces más brillo, completaron felizmente el trabajo.
There, I had a friend's face under my gaze; and what did it signify that those young ladies turned their backs on me?
Tenía el rostro de un amigo ante mis ojos. Por tanto, ¿qué importaba que aquellas dos jóvenes me volviesen la espalda?
I looked at it; I smiled at the speaking likeness: I was absorbed and content.
Me sentí absorta y contenta y sonreí contemplando el dibujo.
"Is that a portrait of some one you know?" asked Eliza, who had approached me unnoticed.
-¿Es el retrato de algún conocido suyo? -preguntó Eliza que se había acercado a mí sin que yo me diera cuenta.
I responded that it was merely a fancy head, and hurried it beneath the other sheets.
Respondí que era un dibujo caprichoso y lo coloqué entre los demás que tenía.
Of course, I lied: it was, in fact, a very faithful representation of Mr. Rochester.
Yo sabía, desde luego, que era una representación muy exacta de Mr.
But what was that to her, or to any one but myself?
Rochester, mas ¿qué le interesaba eso a nadie, sino a mí misma?
Georgiana also advanced to look.
Georgiana se acercó también para mirar.
The other drawings pleased her much, but she called that "an ugly man."
Los demás dibujos le gustaron mucho, pero aquél, según ella, era «un hombre muy feo».
They both seemed surprised at my skill.
Las dos parecieron sorprendidas de mi habilidad.
I offered to sketch their portraits; and each, in turn, sat for a pencil outline.
Entonces les ofrecí hacer sus retratos. Ambas se sentaron, ante mí, una después de otra, y obtuve de cada una un apunte de lápiz.
Then Georgiana produced her album.
Georgiana entonces sacó su álbum y le ofrecí contribuir a enriquecerlo con un dibujo a la aguada.
I promised to contribute a water-colour drawing: this put her at once into good humour.
Esto acabó por ponerla de buen humor.

She proposed a walk in the grounds. Before we had been out two hours, we were deep in a confidential conversation: she had favoured me with a description of the brilliant winter she had spent in London two seasons ago--of the admiration she had there excited--the attention she had received; and I even got hints of the titled conquest she had made.

Propuso dar un paseo por los alrededores y antes de dos horas estábamos entregadas a una conversación confidencial. Me describió la brillante temporada que había pasado en Londres dos años antes, la admiración que le produjera, las atenciones de que la hicieron objeto y aun la conquista que había realizado de un joven aristócrata.

In the course of the afternoon and evening these hints were enlarged on: various soft conversations were reported, and sentimental scenes represented; and, in short, a volume of a novel of fashionable life was that day improvised by her for my benefit.

En el curso de la tarde y de la noche, las confidencias se profundizaron, me fueron relatados varios dulces coloquios y algunas escenas sentimentales. En resumen, Georgiana improvisó en obsequio mío una verdadera novela sentimental.
The communications were renewed from day to day: they always ran on the same theme--herself, her loves, and woes.
Sus expansiones aumentaron de día en día, versando todas sobre el mismo tema: su amor y sus pesares.

It was strange she never once adverted either to her mother's illness, or her brother's death, or the present gloomy state of the family prospects. Her mind seemed wholly taken up with reminiscences of past gaiety, and aspirations after dissipations to come.

Era curioso que, en aquel sombrío momento de la vida de su familia, con su hermano muerto y su madre enferma, no pensara nunca en ello, limitándose a recrearse en el recuerdo de las pasadas alegrías y en imaginar las venturas que podría reservarle el porvenir.
She passed about five minutes each day in her mother's sick-room, and no more.
Pasaba diariamente cinco minutos en el cuarto de su madre, y no aparecía más por allí.
Eliza still spoke little: she had evidently no time to talk.
Eliza hablaba poco, sin duda por falta de tiempo.
I never saw a busier person than she seemed to be; yet it was difficult to say what she did: or rather, to discover any result of her diligence.
Jamás he visto persona más atareada de lo que ella parecía estar. Lo difícil era descubrir los resultados prácticos de su actividad.
She had an alarm to call her up early. I know not how she occupied herself before breakfast, but after that meal she divided her time into regular portions, and each hour had its allotted task.
No sé lo que hacía antes de desayunar, pero desde ese momento, todas sus horas estaban reguladas y dedicadas a una tarea diferente.
Three times a day she studied a little book, which I found, on inspection, was a Common Prayer Book.
Tres veces al día estudiaba un pequeño libro que, según averigüé mediante la oportuna inspección, era un devocionario corriente.
Three hours she gave to stitching, with gold thread, the border of a square crimson cloth, almost large enough for a carpet.
Tres horas al día trabajaba bordando en oro una tela cuadrada que, por su tamaño, parecía una alfombra.
In answer to my inquiries after the use of this article, she informed me it was a covering for the altar of a new church lately erected near Gateshead.
Preguntándole sobre su objeto, me dijo que estaba destinada a cubrir el altar de una iglesia recientemente erigida en las cercanías de Gateshead.
Two hours she devoted to her diary; two to working by herself in the kitchen-garden; and one to the regulation of her accounts.
Dedicaba otras dos horas a escribir su diario, una a trabajar en el huerto y otra a hacer sus cuentas.
She seemed to want no company; no conversation.
Al parecer, no necesitaba compañía ni conversación.
I believe she was happy in her way: this routine sufficed for her; and nothing annoyed her so much as the occurrence of any incident which forced her to vary its clockwork regularity.
Creo que era feliz a su modo y que aquella rutina la bastaba. Nada le disgustaba tanto como cualquier incidente que rompiese la monotonía de su vida regulada por el reloj.

She told me one evening, when more disposed to be communicative than usual, that John's conduct, and the threatened ruin of the family, had been a source of profound affliction to her: but she had now, she said, settled her mind, and formed her resolution.

Una noche en que se sentía más comunicativa que de costumbre, me dijo que la conducta de John y la ruina que amenazaba a su familia la habían afligido mucho, pero que al fin se había tranquilizado y adoptado su resolución.

Her own fortune she had taken care to secure; and when her mother died--and it was wholly improbable, she tranquilly remarked, that she should either recover or linger long--she would execute a long-cherished project: seek a retirement where punctual habits would be permanently secured from disturbance, and place safe barriers between herself and a frivolous world.

Habiendo tenido la precaución de salvar de la ruina sus propios bienes, cuando su madre muriera, ya que -según decía con toda tranquilidad- no era probable que curase ni que resistiese mucho, se proponía ejecutar un proyecto largo tiempo acariciado: retirarse a un lugar donde las costumbres rutinarias pudiesen asegurarse contra toda turbación exterior, y donde le fuese fácil establecer barreras entre ella y el frívolo mundo.
I asked if Georgiana would accompany her.
Le pregunté si Georgiana pensaba acompañarla.
"Of course not.
-Desde luego, no.
Georgiana and she had nothing in common: they never had had. She would not be burdened with her society for any consideration.
Georgiana y yo no nos parecemos en nada ni nos hemos parecido nunca.
Georgiana should take her own course; and she, Eliza, would take hers."
Georgiana seguirá su camino y yo el mío.

Georgiana, when not unburdening her heart to me, spent most of her time in lying on the sofa, fretting about the dulness of the house, and wishing over and over again that her aunt Gibson would send her an invitation up to town.

Georgiana, cuando no empleaba el tiempo en abrirme su corazón, pasaba el día tumbada en el sofá, esperando con ansia el momento en que su tía Gibson le enviase una invitación para ir una temporada a la ciudad.
"It would be so much better," she said, "if she could only get out of the way for a month or two, till all was over."
-Sería mejor -solía decir- que me marchara durante uno o dos meses, hasta que todo pasara.
I did not ask what she meant by "all being over," but I suppose she referred to the expected decease of her mother and the gloomy sequel of funeral rites.
Aquel «todo pasara» supongo, aunque nunca se lo pregunté, que quería decir hasta que su madre hubiera muerto y se efectuaran los funerales y demás solemnidades lúgubres.

Eliza generally took no more notice of her sister's indolence and complaints than if no such murmuring, lounging object had been before her. One day, however, as she put away her account-book and unfolded her embroidery, she suddenly took her up thus--
Eliza, generalmente, no solía hacer caso alguno de su hermana ni de sus quejas, pero un día, después de apartar su libro de cuentas y sus bordados, le habló de este modo:
"Georgiana, a more vain and absurd animal than you was certainly never allowed to cumber the earth.
-Georgiana; nunca ha existido en el mundo un ser más inútil y absurdo que tú.
You had no right to be born, for you make no use of life.
No tienes derecho a la vida, porque no sabes vivir.

Instead of living for, in, and with yourself, as a reasonable being ought, you seek only to fasten your feebleness on some other person's strength: if no one can be found willing to burden her or himself with such a fat, weak, puffy, useless thing, you cry out that you are ill-treated, neglected, miserable.

En vez de existir por ti y para ti, como debe hacer toda persona sensata, te es imposible prescindir de transmitir tus debilidades a otras personas de más energía que tú. Si no las encuentras, comienzas a lamentarte de que eres desgraciada, de que te tratan mal, de que no te hacen caso.

Then, too, existence for you must be a scene of continual change and excitement, or else the world is a dungeon: you must be admired, you must be courted, you must be flattered--you must have music, dancing, and society--or you languish, you die away.

Para ti, el mundo es una prisión si no hay en él continuos cambios y novedades, si no te admiran, te adulan y te cortejan. No sabes pasar sin el baile, la música, la compañía y por eso te aburres mortalmente.
Have you no sense to devise a system which will make you independent of all efforts, and all wills, but your own?
¿Quieres que te diga cómo puedes existir de un modo independiente, por ti misma, sin ayuda ajena?

Take one day; share it into sections; to each section apportion its task: leave no stray unemployed quarters of an hour, ten minutes, five minutes--include all; do each piece of business in its turn with method, with rigid regularity.
Divide tu día en partes y a cada una asígnale una tarea, sin dejar un cuarto de hora, diez minutos, ni cinco siquiera, sin algo que hacer.

The day will close almost before you are aware it has begun; and you are indebted to no one for helping you to get rid of one vacant moment: you have had to seek no one's company, conversation, sympathy, forbearance; you have lived, in short, as an independent being ought to do.
Cuando sea así, observarás que no necesitas compañía, conversación ni simpatía de nadie. Y lograrás vivir con la independencia a que todo ser humano debe aspirar.
Take this advice: the first and last I shall offer you; then you will not want me or any one else, happen what may.
Sigue mi consejo, primero y último que te doy, y verás cómo no necesitas de mí ni de nadie, suceda lo que quiera.
Neglect it--go on as heretofore, craving, whining, and idling--and suffer the results of your idiocy, however bad and insuperable they may be.
Si no lo atiendes, sufrirás los resultados de tu sandez, por malos que sean. Te lo digo francamente.
I tell you this plainly; and listen: for though I shall no more repeat what I am now about to say, I shall steadily act on it.
Escúchame bien, porque no volveré a hablarte así, sino que me limitaré a obrar.
After my mother's death, I wash my hands of you: from the day her coffin is carried to the vault in Gateshead Church, you and I will be as separate as if we had never known each other.
En cuanto mamá muera, yo me lavo las manos respecto a ti. El mismo día que la saquen de Gateshead, tú y yo nos separaremos para no volvernos a ver.

You need not think that because we chanced to be born of the same parents, I shall suffer you to fasten me down by even the feeblest claim: I can tell you this--if the whole human race, ourselves excepted, were swept away, and we two stood alone on the earth, I would leave you in the old world, and betake myself to the new."

No imagines que porque hayamos nacido de los mismos padres voy a estar tolerando siempre tus quejas y tus lamentaciones. Te digo más: si toda la raza humana fuera borrada del mapa y quedásemos tú y yo solas, te abandonaría en el Viejo Mundo y me marcharía al Nuevo.
"You might have spared yourself the trouble of delivering that tirade," answered Georgiana.

-Podías haberte ahorrado el sermón-dijo Georgiana cuando su hermana dejó de hablar-. Nadie ignora que eres el ser más egoísta y de menos corazón que existe en el mundo, y a mí me constan tu odio y tu envidia hacia mí.

"Everybody knows you are the most selfish, heartless creature in existence: and _I_ know your spiteful hatred towards me: I have had a specimen of it before in the trick you played me about Lord Edwin Vere: you could not bear me to be raised above you, to have a title, to be received into circles where you dare not show your face, and so you acted the spy and informer, and ruined my prospects for ever."

Ya me lo demostraste lo suficiente con el papel que te diste prisa a desempeñar en mis relaciones con Lord Edwin Vere. Te era insoportable que me elevase sobre ti, que obtuviera un título, que me recibiera en ambiente donde tú no te atreverías ni a asomar la cara.
Georgiana took out her handkerchief and blew her nose for an hour afterwards; Eliza sat cold, impassable, and assiduously industrious.
Y Georgiana sacando su pañuelo, lo aplicó a su rostro y así permaneció más de una hora. Eliza se sentó, fría y hermética, y se dedicó a su labor.

It was a wet and windy afternoon: Georgiana had fallen asleep on the sofa over the perusal of a novel; Eliza was gone to attend a saint's-day service at the new church--for in matters of religion she was a rigid formalist: no weather ever prevented the punctual discharge of what she considered her devotional duties; fair or foul, she went to church thrice every Sunday, and as often on week-days as there were prayers.

Practicaba con rigidez sus deberes religiosos, acudiendo a la iglesia tres veces cada domingo y los demás días de entre semana, si se celebraban plegarias, hiciera el tiempo que hiciese. Subí a la alcoba de la moribunda, sospechando que acaso se hallase desatendida, lo que ocurría con frecuencia, ya que los criados sólo le dedicaban una relativa atención.

I bethought myself to go upstairs and see how the dying woman sped, who lay there almost unheeded: the very servants paid her but a remittent attention: the hired nurse, being little looked after, would slip out of the room whenever she could. Bessie was faithful; but she had her own family to mind, and could only come occasionally to the hall.
La enfermera se marchaba del cuarto en cuanto podía, y Bessie, aunque muy fiel, tenía bastante quehacer con su propia familia y rara vez podía dirigirse a la casa.
I found the sick-room unwatched, as I had expected: no nurse was there; the patient lay still, and seemingly lethargic; her livid face sunk in the pillows: the fire was dying in the grate.
Como esperaba, hallé solitario el dormitorio de la enferma. La paciente parecía estar amodorrada, con la lívida faz sobre el almohadón; el fuego de la chimenea se estaba apagando.
I renewed the fuel, re-arranged the bedclothes, gazed awhile on her who could not now gaze on me, and then I moved away to the window.
Eché más leña, arreglé las ropas del lecho, contemplé a mi tía y me acerqué a la ventana.
The rain beat strongly against the panes, the wind blew tempestuously: "One lies there," I thought, "who will soon be beyond the war of earthly elements.
La lluvia batía violentamente los cristales y el viento aullaba con rabia.
Whither will that spirit--now struggling to quit its material tenement--flit when at length released?"
«¿Dónde irá -pensaba yo- el alma de esta mujer cuando abandone su cuerpo moribundo?»
In pondering the great mystery, I thought of Helen Burns, recalled her dying words--her faith--her doctrine of the equality of disembodied souls.
Mientras meditaba en tan gran misterio, recordaba a Helen Burns, sus últimas palabras, su fe, su creencia en la vida del más allá.

I was still listening in thought to her well-remembered tones--still picturing her pale and spiritual aspect, her wasted face and sublime gaze, as she lay on her placid deathbed, and whispered her longing to be restored to her divine Father's bosom--when a feeble voice murmured from the couch behind: "Who is that?"
Y me parecía escuchar su plácido tono, contemplar su rostro pálido y espiritual y su mirada sublime, verla luego tendida en su tranquilo lecho mortuorio...
I knew Mrs. Reed had not spoken for days: was she reviving?
De pronto, una débil voz murmuró: -¿Quién está ahí?
"It is I, Aunt Reed."
-Soy yo, tía.
"Who--I?" was her answer. "Who are you?" looking at me with surprise and a sort of alarm, but still not wildly.
-¿Quién -repuso con sorpresa y alarma-.
"You are quite a stranger to me--where is Bessie?"
No la conozco. ¿Dónde está Bessie?
"She is at the lodge, aunt."
-Está en la portería, tía.
"Aunt," she repeated.
-¡Tía!
"Who calls me aunt?
¿Por qué me llama tía?
You are not one of the Gibsons; and yet I know you--that face, and the eyes and forehead, are quiet familiar to me: you are like--why, you are like Jane Eyre!"
Usted no es ninguna de las Gibson, y aunque la creo reconocer... Sí; esa cara, esos ojos y esa frente me recuerdan algo.
I said nothing: I was afraid of occasioning some shock by declaring my identity.
No dije nada, temiendo producirla una impresión muy fuerte si la descubría mi identidad.
"Yet," said she, "I am afraid it is a mistake: my thoughts deceive me.
-Sin embargo -siguió-, debo de estar equivocada. Me engaña el corazón.
I wished to see Jane Eyre, and I fancy a likeness where none exists: besides, in eight years she must be so changed."
Quisiera ver a Jane Eyre y la imaginación me hace ver lo que no existe. En ocho años debe de haber cambiado mucho.

I now gently assured her that I was the person she supposed and desired me to be: and seeing that I was understood, and that her senses were quite collected, I explained how Bessie had sent her husband to fetch me from Thornfield.

Entonces le aseguré con amabilidad que yo era la persona que ella suponía y a quien deseaba ver. Notando que me comprendía y que estaba en sus cabales sentidos, le expliqué que el marido de Bessie había ido a buscarme a Thornfield.
"I am very ill, I know," she said ere long.
-Estoy muy enferma, lo sé-dijo ella-.
"I was trying to turn myself a few minutes since, and find I cannot move a limb.
Hace poco he querido volverme y he notado que no puedo ni mover los músculos.
It is as well I should ease my mind before I die: what we think little of in health, burdens us at such an hour as the present is to me.
Menos mal que recobro mi sentido antes de morir, porque cuando uno está sano piensa poco en lo que sucede en estos momentos...
Is the nurse here? or is there no one in the room but you?"
¿Está la enfermera ahí o estás tú sola?
I assured her we were alone.
Afirmé que estaba sola.
"Well, I have twice done you a wrong which I regret now.
-Bueno... En dos ocasiones me he portado mal contigo.
One was in breaking the promise which I gave my husband to bring you up as my own child; the other--" she stopped.
La primera, quebrantando la promesa que hice a mi marido de que te trataría como a mis propios hijos...
"After all, it is of no great importance, perhaps," she murmured to herself: "and then I may get better; and to humble myself so to her is painful."
La otra... -y se interrumpió-. Después de todo, acaso no tenga gran importancia -dijo como para sí- y podría prescindir de humillarme...
She made an effort to alter her position, but failed: her face changed; she seemed to experience some inward sensation--the precursor, perhaps, of the last pang.
La expresión de su faz se alteró. Parecía experimentar una sensación extraña: acaso la precursora del fin.
"Well, I must get it over.
-Haré mejor en hablar.
Eternity is before me: I had better tell her.--Go to my dressing-case, open it, and take out a letter you will see there."
Estoy al borde de la eternidad. Vete al cajón de mi armario y saca una carta que hallarás allí.
I obeyed her directions.
-Y cuando hube obedecido, ordenó-:
"Read the letter," she said.
Léela.
It was short, and thus conceived:--
La carta, muy breve, decía:
"Madam,--Will you have the goodness to send me the address of my niece, Jane Eyre, and to tell me how she is?
«Señora: ¿Tendrá usted la bondad de enviarme la dirección de mi sobrina Jane Eyre y decirme cómo está?
It is my intention to write shortly and desire her to come to me at Madeira.
Me propongo escribirla y traerla conmigo a Madera.

Providence has blessed my endeavours to secure a competency; and as I am unmarried and childless, I wish to adopt her during my life, and bequeath her at my death whatever I may have to leave.--I am, Madam, &c., &c.,
La Providencia ha favorecido mi trabajo y, como soy soltero y sin hijos, me propongo adoptar a mi sobrina y cederla a mi muerte cuanto poseo.
"JOHN EYRE, Madeira."
«De usted, atto. etc. -JAME EYRE, Madera.»
It was dated three years back.
La carta estaba fechada tres años antes.
"Why did I never hear of this?" I asked.
-¿Cómo no se me informó de eso? -pregunté.
"Because I disliked you too fixedly and thoroughly ever to lend a hand in lifting you to prosperity.
-Porque yo no deseaba mover una sola mano en favor tuyo.

I could not forget your conduct to me, Jane--the fury with which you once turned on me; the tone in which you declared you abhorred me the worst of anybody in the world; the unchildlike look and voice with which you affirmed that the very thought of me made you sick, and asserted that I had treated you with miserable cruelty.

Yo no podía olvidar tu comportamiento conmigo, Jane, la furia con que una vez te revolviste contra mí, el tono con que declaraste que me odiabas más que a nadie en el mundo, que todos mis pensamientos hacia ti eran de aversión y que te trataba con horrible crueldad.

I could not forget my own sensations when you thus started up and poured out the venom of your mind: I felt fear as if an animal that I had struck or pushed had looked up at me with human eyes and cursed me in a man's voice.--Bring me some water!

No podía olvidar tampoco lo que experimentaba cuando te volvías contra mí y comenzabas a increparme. Era como si un animal a quien hubiese golpeado me mirara con ojos humanos y me hablase para recriminarme.
Oh, make haste!"
¡Tráeme agua! Apresúrate.
"Dear Mrs. Reed," said I, as I offered her the draught she required, "think no more of all this, let it pass away from your mind.
-Querida tía -dije, al llevarle lo que pedía-, no piense más en eso. Perdone mi violento lenguaje.
Forgive me for my passionate language: I was a child then; eight, nine years have passed since that day."
Yo era entonces una niña. Han pasado ocho o nueve años desde entonces.
She heeded nothing of what I said; but when she had tasted the water and drawn breath, she went on thus--
No hizo caso de lo que decía. Después de beber y respirar profundamente, continuó:
"I tell you I could not forget it; and I took my revenge: for you to be adopted by your uncle, and placed in a state of ease and comfort, was what I could not endure.
-Te dije que no te perdonaría aquello y, en efecto, tomé mi desquite, porque la idea de que fueras adoptada por tu tío y vivieras bien era insoportable para mí.
I wrote to him; I said I was sorry for his disappointment, but Jane Eyre was dead: she had died of typhus fever at Lowood.
Le escribí diciéndole que sentía comunicárselo, pero que habías muerto de tifus en Lowood.
Now act as you please: write and contradict my assertion--expose my falsehood as soon as you like.
Ahora haz lo que quieras. Escribe desmintiéndome, si te parece.
You were born, I think, to be my torment: my last hour is racked by the recollection of a deed which, but for you, I should never have been tempted to commit."
Creo que has nacido para ser mi tormento; hasta en mi última hora he de ser torturada por el recuerdo de un mal que no debía cometer ni aun tratándose de ti.
"If you could but be persuaded to think no more of it, aunt, and to regard me with kindness and forgiveness"
-Quisiera que no pensase más en ello, tía, y que me mirase con afecto.

"You have a very bad disposition," said she, "and one to this day I feel it impossible to understand: how for nine years you could be patient and quiescent under any treatment, and in the tenth break out all fire and violence, I can never comprehend."
-Tienes muy malos instintos -repuso-, y aún hoy no comprendo cómo has sido capaz de permanecer nueve años en el colegio sin rebelarte.
"My disposition is not so bad as you think: I am passionate, but not vindictive.
-Mis instintos no son tan malos como usted piensa. Soy vehemente, pero no vengativa.
Many a time, as a little child, I should have been glad to love you if you would have let me; and I long earnestly to be reconciled to you now: kiss me, aunt."
Durante mucho tiempo, mientras fui niña, hubiera deseado quererla mucho, si usted me lo hubiera permitido, y ahora deseo reconciliarme con usted. Béseme, tía.
I approached my cheek to her lips: she would not touch it.
Aproximé mis mejillas a sus labios, pero no me tocó.
She said I oppressed her by leaning over the bed, and again demanded water.
Dijo que la ahogaba inclinándome así sobre la cama, y me pidió más agua.

As I laid her down--for I raised her and supported her on my arm while she drank--I covered her ice-cold and clammy hand with mine: the feeble fingers shrank from my touch--the glazing eyes shunned my gaze.
La incorporé para que bebiese y, al volverla a acostar, coloqué mis manos sobre las suyas, heladas, que se retiraron de mi contacto, mientras su apagada mirada esquivaba la mía.
"Love me, then, or hate me, as you will," I said at last, "you have my full and free forgiveness: ask now for God's, and be at peace."
-Quiérame u ódieme, como desee -dije, al fin-. En uno u otro caso, la perdono de corazón.
Poor, suffering woman! it was too late for her to make now the effort to change her habitual frame of mind: living, she had ever hated me--dying, she must hate me still.
Era demasiado tarde para que cambiase de carácter. Me había odiado en vida y era, al parecer, inevitable que me odiara en su agonía.
The nurse now entered, and Bessie followed.
Entró la enfermera, seguida de Bessie.
I yet lingered half-an-hour longer, hoping to see some sign of amity: but she gave none.
Permanecí en la estancia media hora más, esperando que mi tía diese algún indicio de alivio, pero no dio ninguno.
She was fast relapsing into stupor; nor did her mind again rally: at twelve o'clock that night she died.
Permaneció sumida en el habitual sopor y a medianoche falleció.
I was not present to close her eyes, nor were either of her daughters.
Ni sus hijas ni yo estuvimos presentes para cerrar sus ojos.
They came to tell us the next morning that all was over. She was by that time laid out.
A la mañana siguiente nos dijeron que todo había terminado.
Eliza and I went to look at her: Georgiana, who had burst out into loud weeping, said she dared not go.
Georgiana que estaba deshecha en llanto, dijo que no se atrevía. La antes robusta y enérgica Sarah Reed yacía rígida e inmóvil, con los párpados cerrados.
There was stretched Sarah Reed's once robust and active frame, rigid and still: her eye of flint was covered with its cold lid; her brow and strong traits wore yet the impress of her inexorable soul.
En su entrecejo y sus duras facciones estaba impreso aún el sello de la inflexibilidad de su alma.
A strange and solemn object was that corpse to me.
Aquel cadáver me produjo un efecto extraño y solemne.

I gazed on it with gloom and pain: nothing soft, nothing sweet, nothing pitying, or hopeful, or subduing did it inspire; only a grating anguish for _her_ woes--not _my_ loss--and a sombre tearless dismay at the fearfulness of death in such a form.
Le miré con espanto y tristeza. Nada había en él que sugiriese imágenes suaves, de piedad o de esperanza.
Eliza surveyed her parent calmly.
Eliza miró a su madre con serenidad.
After a silence of some minutes she observed--
Después de algunos minutos de silencio, comentó:
"With her constitution she should have lived to a good old age: her life was shortened by trouble."
-Tenía una constitución muy robusta y hubiera vivido mucho más a no haber abreviado su existencia los disgustos.
And then a spasm constricted her mouth for an instant: as it passed away she turned and left the room, and so did I. Neither of us had dropt a tear.
Luego salió del cuarto y yo la seguí. Ninguna de las dos habíamos vertido una sola lágrima.
Mr. Rochester had given me but one week's leave of absence: yet a month elapsed before I quitted Gateshead.
Mr. Rochester me había concedido una semana de permiso, pero pasó un mes antes de que yo abandonase Gateshead.

I wished to leave immediately after the funeral, but Georgiana entreated me to stay till she could get off to London, whither she was now at last invited by her uncle, Mr. Gibson, who had come down to direct his sister's interment and settle the family affairs.

Pretendí irme en seguida de los funerales, mas Georgiana me obligó a estar con ella hasta su marcha a Londres, donde al fin había sido invitada por su tía Gibson, que acudió para arreglar los asuntos familiares.

Georgiana said she dreaded being left alone with Eliza; from her she got neither sympathy in her dejection, support in her fears, nor aid in her preparations; so I bore with her feeble-minded wailings and selfish lamentations as well as I could, and did my best in sewing for her and packing her dresses.

Georgiana afirmaba que temía quedar sola con Eliza porque no podía contar para nada con su simpatía ni su ayuda. Soporté lo mejor que pude sus quejas egoístas y la auxilié con todas mis fuerzas a hacer su equipaje.
It is true, that while I worked, she would idle; and I thought to myself, "If you and I were destined to live always together, cousin, we would commence matters on a different footing.
Mientras yo trabajaba, ella permanecía inactiva, y yo pensaba para mí: «Si nosotras hubiéramos de vivir juntas, primita, las cosas se organizarían sobre una base diferente.

I should not settle tamely down into being the forbearing party; I should assign you your share of labour, and compel you to accomplish it, or else it should be left undone: I should insist, also, on your keeping some of those drawling, half-insincere complaints hushed in your own breast.
Ya me encargaría yo de marcarte tu tarea y te obligaría a cumplirla. También te persuadiría de que guardases parte de tus lamentaciones en el fondo de tu alma.
It is only because our connection happens to be very transitory, and comes at a peculiarly mournful season, that I consent thus to render it so patient and compliant on my part."
Si tengo tanta paciencia y soy tan complaciente contigo, se debe a la triste ocasión en que te hallas y a que se trata de una cosa pasajera.»
At last I saw Georgiana off; but now it was Eliza's turn to request me to stay another week.
Al fin Georgiana partió, pero entonces fue Eliza quien me pidió que me quedase otra semana.

Her plans required all her time and attention, she said; she was about to depart for some unknown bourne; and all day long she stayed in her own room, her door bolted within, filling trunks, emptying drawers, burning papers, and holding no communication with any one.

Sus proyectos absorbían todo su tiempo y su atención y, antes de partir para su desconocido destino, se pasaba el día cerrando baúles, vaciando cajones, quemando papeles, todo ello dentro de su cuarto y con el cerrojo echado.
She wished me to look after the house, to see callers, and answer notes of condolence.
Me necesitaba, pues, para que yo atendiese la casa, recibiese pésames y contestase cartas.
One morning she told me I was at liberty.
Al fin, una mañana me dijo que me dejaba en libertad, y añadió:
"And," she added, "I am obliged to you for your valuable services and discreet conduct!
-Le agradezco mucho su discreción y sus valiosos servicios.
There is some difference between living with such an one as you and with Georgiana: you perform your own part in life and burden no one.
¡Qué diferencia entre vivir con una persona como usted o con una como Georgiana! Usted sabe llenar su misión en la vida.
To-morrow," she continued, "I set out for the Continent.
Mañana -continuó- parto para el continente.
I shall take up my abode in a religious house near Lisle--a nunnery you would call it; there I shall be quiet and unmolested.
Me instalaré en una residencia de religiosas, cerca de Lisle, una especie de monasterio donde viviré tranquila y aislada.

I shall devote myself for a time to the examination of the Roman Catholic dogmas, and to a careful study of the workings of their system: if I find it to be, as I half suspect it is, the one best calculated to ensure the doing of all things decently and in order, I shall embrace the tenets of Rome and probably take the veil."

Quiero dedicar mi tiempo al examen de los dogmas catolicoromanos, y si, como casi supongo, encuentro que son los que mejor permiten hacer las cosas bien y ordenadamente, abrazaré la fe romana y probablemente me haré monja.
I neither expressed surprise at this resolution nor attempted to dissuade her from it.
No manifesté sorpresa por tal resolución ni intenté disuadirla de ella.
When we parted, she said: "Good-bye, cousin Jane Eyre; I wish you well: you have some sense."
Al despedirme, me dijo: -Adiós, prima Jane Eyre. Le deseo buena suerte.
I then returned: "You are not without sense, cousin Eliza; but what you have, I suppose, in another year will be walled up alive in a French convent.
-También usted, prima Eliza -repuse.
"You are in the right," said she; and with these words we each went our separate way.
Y con estas palabras nos despedimos.

As I shall not have occasion to refer either to her or her sister again, I may as well mention here, that Georgiana made an advantageous match with a wealthy worn-out man of fashion, and that Eliza actually took the veil, and is at this day superior of the convent where she passed the period of her novitiate, and which she endowed with her fortune.

Como no habrá ocasión de referirme de nuevo a ninguna de mis primas, me limitaré a mencionar que Georgiana hizo un buen matrimonio con un hombre rico y distinguido y que Eliza profesó como monja después de un año de noviciado y es actualmente superiora de su convento.
My journey seemed tedious--very tedious: fifty miles one day, a night spent at an inn; fifty miles the next day.
Mi viaje fue aburrido, muy aburrido. Una jornada de cincuenta millas, una noche en una posada y cincuenta millas más al día siguiente.
During the first twelve hours I thought of Mrs. Reed in her last moments; I saw her disfigured and discoloured face, and heard her strangely altered voice.
Durante las primeras horas del viaje pensé en los últimos momentos de mi tía: creía ver su desfigurada faz y escuchar su alterada voz.
I mused on the funeral day, the coffin, the hearse, the black train of tenants and servants--few was the number of relatives--the gaping vault, the silent church, the solemn service.
Recordaba el sepelio: el ataúd, el carruaje fúnebre, la comitiva de criados y colonos -parientes había muy pocos-, la cripta, la silente iglesia, el solemne oficio...

Then I thought of Eliza and Georgiana; I beheld one the cynosure of a ball-room, the other the inmate of a convent cell; and I dwelt on and analysed their separate peculiarities of person and character.
Pensé en Georgiana y en Eliza, figurándome a la una brillando en un salón de baile, y a la otra habitando una celda conventual, y analicé y comparé sus respectivos caracteres.
The evening arrival at the great town of--scattered these thoughts; night gave them quite another turn: laid down on my traveller's bed, I left reminiscence for anticipation.
La noche pasada en la gran ciudad de... desvaneció estos pensamientos. Acostada en mi cama de viajera, sustituí los recuerdos por cábalas sobre el porvenir.
I was going back to Thornfield: but how long was I to stay there?
Volvía a Thornfield, pero ¿cuánto tiempo pasaría allí?
Not long; of that I was sure.
Seguramente no mucho.
I had heard from Mrs. Fairfax in the interim of my absence: the party at the hall was dispersed; Mr. Rochester had left for London three weeks ago, but he was then expected to return in a fortnight.
Fairfax me escribió a Gateshead diciendo que los invitados se habían ido ya y que Mr. Rochester se había ido a Londres hacía tres semanas y se le esperaba dentro de quince días.

Mrs. Fairfax surmised that he was gone to make arrangements for his wedding, as he had talked of purchasing a new carriage: she said the idea of his marrying Miss Ingram still seemed strange to her; but from what everybody said, and from what she had herself seen, she could no longer doubt that the event would shortly take place.

Fairfax suponía que iba a arreglar asuntos relativos a su matrimonio, puesto que él habló de adquirir un coche nuevo. A la anciana le resultaba muy rara la idea de que su señor se casase con Blanche Ingram, pero según oyera a todos, la boda no debía dilatarse mucho.
"You would be strangely incredulous if you did doubt it," was my mental comment.
«¡Muy incrédula eres! -comenté mentalmente-.
"I don't doubt it."
¡Yo no experimento duda alguna!»
The question followed, "Where was I to go?"
La cuestión inmediata a estudiar era adónde iría yo. Soñé por la noche con Blanche, que me cerraba las puertas de Thornfield y me señalaba el camino.

I dreamt of Miss Ingram all the night: in a vivid morning dream I saw her closing the gates of Thornfield against me and pointing me out another road; and Mr. Rochester looked on with his arms folded--smiling sardonically, as it seemed, at both her and me.
Mr. Rochester nos miraba a las dos, cruzado de brazos, sonriendo sarcásticamente.
I had not notified to Mrs. Fairfax the exact day of my return; for I did not wish either car or carriage to meet me at Millcote.
No avisé a Mrs. Fairfax el día de mi regreso, porque no quería que enviasen coche alguno a buscarme a Millcote.

I proposed to walk the distance quietly by myself; and very quietly, after leaving my box in the ostler's care, did I slip away from the George Inn, about six o'clock of a June evening, and take the old road to Thornfield: a road which lay chiefly through fields, and was now little frequented.

Me proponía recorrer la distancia dando un paseo, y así, después de dejar mi equipaje al cuidado del dueño de la posada, a las seis de una tarde de junio eché a andar por el antiguo camino de Thornfield, que se deslizaba a través de los prados y era muy poco frecuentado entonces.

I felt glad as the road shortened before me: so glad that I stopped once to ask myself what that joy meant: and to remind reason that it was not to my home I was going, or to a permanent resting-place, or to a place where fond friends looked out for me and waited my arrival.

A medida que iba caminando me sentía más contenta, hasta el punto de que más de una vez me detuve para preguntarme el motivo de tal alegría, ya que, en realidad, no me dirigía a mi casa ni a un lugar donde me aguardasen con impaciencia amigos cariñosos.

"Mrs. Fairfax will smile you a calm welcome, to be sure," said I; "and little Adele will clap her hands and jump to see you: but you know very well you are thinking of another than they, and that he is not thinking of you."

«Mrs. Fairfax me acogerá con una tranquila sonrisa y Adèle me tomará las manos y comenzará a saltar cuando me vea -pensé-, pero la verdad es que ellas piensan en cosas distintas de mí, como yo pienso en cosas distintas de ellas.»
They are making hay, too, in Thornfield meadows: or rather, the labourers are just quitting their work, and returning home with their rakes on their shoulders, now, at the hour I arrive.
En las praderas de Thornfield los labradores comenzaban a abandonar el trabajo y volvían a sus casas con las herramientas al hombro.
I have but a field or two to traverse, and then I shall cross the road and reach the gates.
Sólo me faltaba atravesar un par de prados antes de llegar a las verjas.
How full the hedges are of roses!
Los setos de los bordes estaban llenos de rosas.
But I have no time to gather any; I want to be at the house.
Pero no me detuve a tomar ninguna, tanta era la prisa que sentía por llegar a la casa.
I passed a tall briar, shooting leafy and flowery branches across the path; I see the narrow stile with stone steps; and I see--Mr.
Pasé bajo un alto zarzal que abovedaba el sendero con sus ramas de blancas florecillas, distinguí el estrecho portillo con escalones de piedra y vi... a Mr.
Rochester sitting there, a book and a pencil in his hand; he is writing.
Rochester sentado en ellos, con un libro y un lápiz en la mano. Estaba escribiendo.
Well, he is not a ghost; yet every nerve I have is unstrung: for a moment I am beyond my own mastery.
No era ciertamente un fantasma, y, sin embargo, sentí un estremecimiento nervioso y estuve a punto de perder el dominio de mí misma.
What does it mean?
¿Qué hacer?
I did not think I should tremble in this way when I saw him, or lose my voice or the power of motion in his presence.
Nunca había pensado que pudiera temblar de aquel modo ante su presencia, que perdiera así la voz y hasta el movimiento al verle.
I will go back as soon as I can stir: I need not make an absolute fool of myself.
Me urgía retroceder, para no mostrarme ante él temblorosa como una tonta.
I know another way to the house.
Conocía otro camino para ir a la casa.
It does not signify if I knew twenty ways; for he has seen me.
Pero aunque hubiese conocido veinte, todo era inútil, porque él me vio antes de que pudiera retirarme.
"Hillo!" he cries; and he puts up his book and his pencil.
-¡Caramba! -exclamó-.
"There you are!
¿Conque está usted aquí?
Come on, if you please."
¡Venga, venga!

I suppose I do come on; though in what fashion I know not; being scarcely cognisant of my movements, and solicitous only to appear calm; and, above all, to control the working muscles of my face--which I feel rebel insolently against my will, and struggle to express what I had resolved to conceal.

Supongo que debí ir, en efecto, aunque no sé cómo, pues me hallaba inconsciente de mis movimientos y sólo me ocupaba en fingir tranquilidad y en dominar los músculos de mi rostro que, insolentemente rebeldes a mi voluntad, se obstinaban en revelar lo que debía permanecer oculto.
But I have a veil--it is down: I may make shift yet to behave with decent composure.
Pude, sin embargo, presentarme con la mayor compostura posible.
"And this is Jane Eyre?
-Conque Jane Eyre, ¿eh?
Are you coming from Millcote, and on foot?
De Millcote y a pie...

Yes--just one of your tricks: not to send for a carriage, and come clattering over street and road like a common mortal, but to steal into the vicinage of your home along with twilight, just as if you were a dream or a shade.
Es una de las peculiaridades de usted: no pedir un carruaje para venir por la carretera como una persona corriente, sino aparecer junto a su casa a la caída de la tarde, como una aparición...
What the deuce have you done with yourself this last month?"
¿Qué diablos ha estado haciendo todo este mes?
"I have been with my aunt, sir, who is dead."
-Estaba con mi tía, que ha muerto, señor.
"A true Janian reply! Good angels be my guard!
-¡Una contestación muy de Jane Eyre!
She comes from the other world--from the abode of people who are dead; and tells me so when she meets me alone here in the gloaming!
¡Los ángeles, me ayuden! ¡Lo primero que me dice al encontrarnos es que viene de estar con muertos, en el otro mundo!
If I dared, I'd touch you, to see if you are substance or shadow, you elf!--but I'd as soon offer to take hold of a blue _ignis fatuus_ light in a marsh.
Si me atreviera, la tocaría, a ver si es de carne y hueso, o bien una visión, que se disipara a mi contacto, como un fuego fatuo en los pantanos...
Truant! truant!" he added, when he had paused an instant.
¡Pícara! -añadió, después de un momento de silencio-.
"Absent from me a whole month, and forgetting me quite, I'll be sworn!"
¡Un mes ausente y olvidada de mí por completo, estoy seguro!

I knew there would be pleasure in meeting my master again, even though broken by the fear that he was so soon to cease to be my master, and by the knowledge that I was nothing to him: but there was ever in Mr. Rochester (so at least I thought) such a wealth of the power of communicating happiness, that to taste but of the crumbs he scattered to stray and stranger birds like me, was to feast genially.
Sentía verdadero placer en reunirme con Mr. Rochester, aunque acibarado por el pensamiento de que en breve dejaría de verle y de que, además, nada había de común entre él y yo.
His last words were balm: they seemed to imply that it imported something to him whether I forgot him or not.
Pero de sus palabras emanaba una sensación que me placía en extremo. Parecían indicar que le interesaba saber si yo me acordaba de él o no.
And he had spoken of Thornfield as my home--would that it were my home!
Y había hablado de Thornfield como de mi casa...
I inquired soon if he had not been to London.
Le pregunté si había estado en Londres.
"Yes; I suppose you found that out by second-sight."
-Sí. Y supongo que lo sabe usted gracias a su doble vista.
"Mrs. Fairfax told me in a letter."
-Me lo escribió Mrs. Fairfax.
