"And did she inform you what I went to do?"
-¿Y le informó de lo que fui a hacer?
"Oh, yes, sir!
-Sí, señor.
Everybody knew your errand."
Todos lo saben.
"You must see the carriage, Jane, and tell me if you don't think it will suit Mrs. Rochester exactly; and whether she won't look like Queen Boadicea, leaning back against those purple cushions.
-Tiene usted que ver el coche, Jane, y decirme si cree que es apropiado o no para Mrs. Rochester y si viajando en él parecerá una reina apoyada en sus rojos cojines.
I wish, Jane, I were a trifle better adapted to match with her externally.
Por cierto que sería mucho mejor que ella y yo hiciéramos mejor pareja, físicamente hablando.
Tell me now, fairy as you are--can't you give me a charm, or a philter, or something of that sort, to make me a handsome man?"
Usted, que es un hada, puede proporcionarme un filtro, realizar algún conjuro o cosa parecida, para convertirme en un hombre guapo.
"It would be past the power of magic, sir;" and, in thought, I added, "A loving eye is all the charm needed: to such you are handsome enough; or rather your sternness has a power beyond beauty."

-Eso no entra en las posibilidades de la magia, señor -respondí mientras pensaba: «Todo el conjuro que se necesita son los ojos de una enamorada. Para ella sería usted lo más hermoso que se pudiera desear.»

Mr. Rochester had sometimes read my unspoken thoughts with an acumen to me incomprehensible: in the present instance he took no notice of my abrupt vocal response; but he smiled at me with a certain smile he had of his own, and which he used but on rare occasions.
Rochester había leído a menudo mis pensamientos. Aquella vez no pareció atender mucho mis palabras.
He seemed to think it too good for common purposes: it was the real sunshine of feeling--he shed it over me now.
Me sonrió de un modo peculiar, que rara vez empleaba, quizá porque aquella sonrisa, a la que asomaba toda su alma, no le pareciese conveniente para ser aplicada a las situaciones vulgares de la vida.
"Pass, Janet," said he, making room for me to cross the stile: "go up home, and stay your weary little wandering feet at a friend's threshold."
-Pase, Jane -dijo, separándose a un lado del portillo-, pase y descanse sus piececitos fatigados en la casa de un amigo.
All I had now to do was to obey him in silence: no need for me to colloquise further.
Obedecí sin decirle nada; sobraba para mí todo diálogo ulterior.
I got over the stile without a word, and meant to leave him calmly. An impulse held me fast--a force turned me round. I said--or something in me said for me, and in spite of me--

No obstante, un impulso interior me hizo detenerme, una fuerza desconocida me hizo girar sobre mí misma y decirle, no sé si yo o algo que me hacía hablar a pesar mío: -Gracias por su mucha amabilidad, Mr.
"Thank you, Mr. Rochester, for your great kindness. I am strangely glad to get back again to you: and wherever you are is my home--my only home."
Rochester. Estoy muy satisfecha de volver a verle, y considero que dondequiera que usted esté está mi casa, mi única casa.
I walked on so fast that even he could hardly have overtaken me had he tried.
Y me alejé tan de prisa, que difícilmente hubiera podido él alcanzarme aunque se lo hubiera propuesto.
Little Adele was half wild with delight when she saw me.
Adèle se volvió casi loca de alegría al verme. Mrs.
Mrs. Fairfax received me with her usual plain friendliness.
Fairfax me acogió con su acostumbrada afabilidad.
Leah smiled, and even Sophie bid me "bon soir" with glee.
Aquello me resultó muy agradable.
This was very pleasant; there is no happiness like that of being loved by your fellow-creatures, and feeling that your presence is an addition to their comfort.
Nada complace más que sentirse amado por los que le rodean a uno y apreciar que la propia presencia aumenta su satisfacción.
I that evening shut my eyes resolutely against the future: I stopped my cars against the voice that kept warning me of near separation and coming grief.
Cerré, pues, mis ojos al porvenir y taponé mis oídos contra la voz que me aconsejaba ponerme en guardia previniendo la próxima separación. Cuando tomamos el té y Mrs.

When tea was over and Mrs. Fairfax had taken her knitting, and I had assumed a low seat near her, and Adele, kneeling on the carpet, had nestled close up to me, and a sense of mutual affection seemed to surround us with a ring of golden peace, I uttered a silent prayer that we might not be parted far or soon; but when, as we thus sat, Mr. Rochester entered, unannounced, and looking at us, seemed to take pleasure in the spectacle of a group so amicable--when he said he supposed the old lady was all right now that she had got her adopted daughter back again, and added that he saw Adele was "prete a croquer sa petite maman Anglaise"--I half ventured to hope that he would, even after his marriage, keep us together somewhere under the shelter of his protection, and not quite exiled from the sunshine of his presence.

Murmuré una plegaria sin palabras pidiendo a Dios que no nos separásemos nunca, y cuando Mr. Rochester entró sin anunciarse y nos miró, complacido ante el espectáculo de aquel grupo tan amistoso, cuando dijo que suponía que la anciana estaría satisfecha al ver que su hija adoptiva regresaba y añadió que Adèle le parecía préte a croques sa petite maman Anglaise, casi comencé a alimentar la esperanza de que él, aun después de casarse, nos conservaría bajo su protección y no nos privaría en absoluto de su presencia.
A fortnight of dubious calm succeeded my return to Thornfield Hall.
A mi vuelta a Thornfield Hall sucedió una quincena de tranquilidad absoluta.
Nothing was said of the master's marriage, and I saw no preparation going on for such an event.
No se hablaba nada del casamiento del dueño, ni yo veía preparativo alguno.
Almost every day I asked Mrs. Fairfax if she had yet heard anything decided: her answer was always in the negative.
Casi a diario preguntaba a Mrs. Fairfax si sabía que hubiera algo decidido y siempre recibía la misma negativa.

Once she said she had actually put the question to Mr. Rochester as to when he was going to bring his bride home; but he had answered her only by a joke and one of his queer looks, and she could not tell what to make of him.
Según dijo, sólo una vez preguntó sobre el asunto a Mr. Rochester, pero éste respondió con una broma y ella no pudo sacar nada en limpio.

One thing specially surprised me, and that was, there were no journeyings backward and forward, no visits to Ingram Park: to be sure it was twenty miles off, on the borders of another county; but what was that distance to an ardent lover?

Una cosa que me sorprendía mucho era que Rochester no visitaba Ingram Park. Si bien este lugar estaba sito a veinte millas, en los límites de otro condado, ¿qué era esa distancia para un enamorado ardiente?
To so practised and indefatigable a horseman as Mr. Rochester, it would be but a morning's ride.
Un jinete tan experto e infatigable como Rochester la recorrería en una mañana de cabalgar.
I began to cherish hopes I had no right to conceive: that the match was broken off; that rumour had been mistaken; that one or both parties had changed their minds.
Comencé a acariciar esperanzas que no tenía motivo alguno para concebir: que el enlace se hubiese roto, que el rumor hubiera sido infundado, que una de las dos partes hubiera rectificado su opinión.
I used to look at my master's face to see if it were sad or fierce; but I could not remember the time when it had been so uniformly clear of clouds or evil feelings.
Trataba de adivinar si en el rostro de Rochester se apreciaba alguna cosa desagradable o violenta, pero jamás me había parecido su cara tan límpida y exenta de malas inclinaciones.

If, in the moments I and my pupil spent with him, I lacked spirits and sank into inevitable dejection, he became even gay. Never had he called me more frequently to his presence; never been kinder to me when there--and, alas! never had I loved him so well.
Nunca me llamó a su presencia tan frecuentemente como entonces, nunca había sido más amable para conmigo y nunca, ¡ay!, le había amado yo más a él...

A splendid Midsummer shone over England: skies so pure, suns so radiant as were then seen in long succession, seldom favour even singly, our wave- girt land. It was as if a band of Italian days had come from the South, like a flock of glorious passenger birds, and lighted to rest them on the cliffs of Albion.

Hacía un tiempo espléndido, como de mediados de verano, con un cielo tan puro y un sol tan radiante, que se diría que una bandada de días italianos, a la manera de magníficos pájaros, hubiese venido desde el Sur hasta Inglaterra.

The hay was all got in; the fields round Thornfield were green and shorn; the roads white and baked; the trees were in their dark prime; hedge and wood, full-leaved and deeply tinted, contrasted well with the sunny hue of the cleared meadows between.
El heno había sido segado por completo. Los campos circundantes estaban verdes, los árboles en flor, los bosques pomposos y los setos magníficos de frutos y florecillas.
On Midsummer-eve, Adele, weary with gathering wild strawberries in Hay Lane half the day, had gone to bed with the sun. I watched her drop asleep, and when I left her, I sought the garden.

Una tarde de aquel verano, Adèle, que se había fatigado mucho cogiendo fresas silvestres por la tarde en el camino de Hay, se acostó en cuanto se puso el sol, y yo, después de asegurarme de que la niña dormía, bajé al jardín.
It was now the sweetest hour of the twenty-four:--"Day its fervid fires had wasted," and dew fell cool on panting plain and scorched summit.
Era la hora más grata de las veinticuatro del día.

Where the sun had gone down in simple state--pure of the pomp of clouds--spread a solemn purple, burning with the light of red jewel and furnace flame at one point, on one hill-peak, and extending high and wide, soft and still softer, over half heaven.

Por Occidente, donde el sol acababa de desaparecer, se extendía ahora una espléndida mancha de púrpura, ardiente como el rubí o como la llama, surgiendo tras lo alto de una colina, y extendiéndose más tenue a medida que se elevaba, hasta la mitad del cielo.
The east had its own charm or fine deep blue, and its own modest gem, a casino and solitary star: soon it would boast the moon; but she was yet beneath the horizon.
Por Oriente, el cielo ostentaba un suave azul y brillaba en él una estrella como una joya. En breve saldría la luna, pero ahora no asomaba todavía en el horizonte.

I walked a while on the pavement; but a subtle, well-known scent--that of a cigar--stole from some window; I saw the library casement open a handbreadth; I knew I might be watched thence; so I went apart into the orchard.
Primero paseé ante la casa, mas un bien conocido olor de cigarro que salía por la abierta ventana de la biblioteca me hizo comprender que podían verme, y entonces me interné en el huerto.

No nook in the grounds more sheltered and more Eden-like; it was full of trees, it bloomed with flowers: a very high wall shut it out from the court, on one side; on the other, a beech avenue screened it from the lawn.
Imposible encontrar un sitio más paradisíaco. Estaba lleno de árboles y flores, un alto muro lo separaba del patio y una avenida de hayas conducía al prado de frente al edificio.

At the bottom was a sunk fence; its sole separation from lonely fields: a winding walk, bordered with laurels and terminating in a giant horse-chestnut, circled at the base by a seat, led down to the fence.
Un seto aislaba el huerto de los solitarios campos, y un caminito bordeado de laureles y que terminaba en un gigantesco castaño rodeado de un asiento circular conducía al extremo del seto.

Here one could wander unseen. While such honey-dew fell, such silence reigned, such gloaming gathered, I felt as if I could haunt such shade for ever; but in threading the flower and fruit parterres at the upper part of the enclosure, enticed there by the light the now rising moon cast on this more open quarter, my step is stayed--not by sound, not by sight, but once more by a warning fragrance.
El silencio era absoluto, la sombra grata. Mas apenas había caminado algunos pasos me detuve al percibir cierta cálida fragancia en el ambiente.

Sweet-briar and southernwood, jasmine, pink, and rose have long been yielding their evening sacrifice of incense: this new scent is neither of shrub nor flower; it is--I know it well--it is Mr. Rochester's cigar.
No procedía de los rosales silvestres, ni de los abrótanos, jazmines, claveles y rosas que colmaban el jardín. No: aquel nuevo aroma era el del cigarro de Mr.
I look round and I listen.
Rochester. Miré a mi alrededor y escuché.
I see trees laden with ripening fruit. I hear a nightingale warbling in a wood half a mile off; no moving form is visible, no coming step audible; but that perfume increases: I must flee.
Vi árboles cargados de fruta y oí trinar a un ruiseñor, pero no distinguí ninguna forma humana ni sentí paso alguno. Sin embargo, el aroma se hacía más intenso.
I make for the wicket leading to the shrubbery, and I see Mr. Rochester entering.
Debía marcharme. Me dirigí a un portillo que daba al campo y en aquel momento divisé a Mr.
I step aside into the ivy recess; he will not stay long: he will soon return whence he came, and if I sit still he will never see me.
Mr. Rochester seguramente no estaría mucho tiempo allí y, si yo me quedaba donde estaba, podía pasar inadvertida.

But no--eventide is as pleasant to him as to me, and this antique garden as attractive; and he strolls on, now lifting the gooseberry-tree branches to look at the fruit, large as plums, with which they are laden; now taking a ripe cherry from the wall; now stooping towards a knot of flowers, either to inhale their fragrance or to admire the dew-beads on their petals.

Pero aquel antiguo jardín era tan agradable para él como para mí. Lo recorría lentamente, parándose de vez en cuando, ora para contemplar las parras cargadas de uvas grandes como ciruelas, ora para coger una cereza o para contemplar una flor.
A great moth goes humming by me; it alights on a plant at Mr. Rochester's foot: he sees it, and bends to examine it.
Una enorme libélula voló a mi lado, se detuvo en una planta a los pies de Rochester y éste se inclinó a fin de examinarla.
"Now, he has his back towards me," thought I, "and he is occupied too; perhaps, if I walk softly, I can slip away unnoticed."
«Ahora está de espaldas a mí -pensé-; acaso, si me deslizo en silencio, pueda irme sin que me oiga.»

I trode on an edging of turf that the crackle of the pebbly gravel might not betray me: he was standing among the beds at a yard or two distant from where I had to pass; the moth apparently engaged him.
Avancé sobre la hierba, queriendo evitar que mis pasos sobre la arena me traicionaran. Cuando pasé a una vara o dos de él, que parecía absorto en contemplar la libélula, dijo, sin volverse:
"Jane, come and look at this fellow."
-Venga a ver esto, Jane.
I had made no noise: he had not eyes behind--could his shadow feel?
No había hecho ruido, él no me dirigía la mirada. ¿Cómo sabía que yo me hallaba allí?
I started at first, and then I approached him.
Me detuve y al fin me acerqué a él.
"Look at his wings," said he, "he reminds me rather of a West Indian insect; one does not often see so large and gay a night-rover in England; there! he is flown."
Parece un insecto de las Antillas. Nunca he visto ninguno tan grande y hermoso en Inglaterra.
The moth roamed away.
La libélula se había ido.
I was sheepishly retreating also; but Mr. Rochester followed me, and when we reached the wicket, he said--
Yo inicié también la retirada, pero Rochester me siguió. Al llegar al portillo dijo:
"Turn back: on so lovely a night it is a shame to sit in the house; and surely no one can wish to go to bed while sunset is thus at meeting with moonrise."
Es lamentable permanecer en casa en una noche tan hermosa como ésta. ¿A quién puede complacerle acostarse a esta hora?

It is one of my faults, that though my tongue is sometimes prompt enough at an answer, there are times when it sadly fails me in framing an excuse; and always the lapse occurs at some crisis, when a facile word or plausible pretext is specially wanted to get me out of painful embarrassment.

Vea: mientras la última claridad del crepúsculo brilla a lo lejos, por el otro extremo del horizonte nace la luna. Uno de mis defectos es que, aunque habitualmente tengo la lengua pronta para cualquier respuesta, en ocasiones no sé encontrar palabras adecuadas con que negarme a algo, y ello coincide siempre con los momentos en que más precisaría un pretexto plausible.
I did not like to walk at this hour alone with Mr. Rochester in the shadowy orchard; but I could not find a reason to allege for leaving him.
No me agradaba pasear a solas a aquellas horas con Mr. Rochester por el huerto, pero no supe cómo excusarme.

I followed with lagging step, and thoughts busily bent on discovering a means of extrication; but he himself looked so composed and so grave also, I became ashamed of feeling any confusion: the evil--if evil existent or prospective there was--seemed to lie with me only; his mind was unconscious and quiet.
Le seguí con lentos pasos, pensando en el modo de librarme de aquella complicación. Pero él parecía tan sereno y grave, que me avergoncé de mis temores.
"Jane," he recommenced, as we entered the laurel walk, and slowly strayed down in the direction of the sunk fence and the horse-chestnut, "Thornfield is a pleasant place in summer, is it not?"
-Jane -comenzó cuando íbamos por el sendero entre laureles hacia el castaño rodeado de un banco-, ¿verdad que Thornfield es un sitio muy agradable en verano?
"You must have become in some degree attached to the house,--you, who have an eye for natural beauties, and a good deal of the organ of Adhesiveness?"
-Usted debe de sentir cierto cariño a la casa, porque tiene usted muy desarrollada su capacidad afectiva y sabe apreciar lo bello.
"I am attached to it, indeed."
-En efecto, experimento afecto hacia Thornfield.
"And though I don't comprehend how it is, I perceive you have acquired a degree of regard for that foolish little child Adele, too; and even for simple dame Fairfax?"
-Y hasta me parece que, no sé cómo, ha tomado usted cariño a esa tontita de Adèle y a esa pobre Mrs. Fairfax.
"Yes, sir; in different ways, I have an affection for both."
-Sí, señor: las aprecio, a cada una en un sentido.
"And would be sorry to part with them?"
-¿Le disgustaría separarse de ellas?
"Pity!" he said, and sighed and paused.
-Es lástima -se interrumpió y suspiró. Luego siguió diciendo-:

"It is always the way of events in this life," he continued presently: "no sooner have you got settled in a pleasant resting-place, than a voice calls out to you to rise and move on, for the hour of repose is expired."
Siempre sucede en la vida que, cuando uno encuentra un sitio donde se halla a gusto, se ve en la precisión de abandonarlo...
"Must I move on, sir?" I asked. "Must I leave Thornfield?"
-¿Es necesario que me vaya de Thornfield? -pregunté.
"I believe you must, Jane. I am sorry, Janet, but I believe indeed you must."
-Lo siento, Jane, pero creo que sí.
This was a blow: but I did not let it prostrate me.
Me sentí anonadada, mas lo disimulé.
"Well, sir, I shall be ready when the order to march comes."
-Bien, señor. Me preparé para cuando usted me dé la orden de irme.
"It is come now--I must give it to-night."
-Esta misma noche.
"Then you _are_ going to be married, sir?"
-¿Es que va a casarse?
"Ex-act-ly--pre-cise-ly: with your usual acuteness, you have hit the nail straight on the head."
-E-xac-ta-men-te -silabeó-. Se muestra usted tan sagaz como de costumbre. -¿Pronto señor?
"Soon, sir?"
-Tan pronto que...

"Very soon, my--that is, Miss Eyre: and you'll remember, Jane, the first time I, or Rumour, plainly intimated to you that it was my intention to put my old bachelor's neck into the sacred noose, to enter into the holy estate of matrimony--to take Miss Ingram to my bosom, in short (she's an extensive armful: but that's not to the point--one can't have too much of such a very excellent thing as my beautiful Blanche): well, as I was saying--listen to me, Jane!
Miss Eyre: usted recordará que cuando yo, o la voz pública, le informaron de mi intención de ofrecer mi cerviz de soltero al sagrado yugo del matrimonio, de acoger en mi amante pecho a Miss Ingram...
You're not turning your head to look after more moths, are you? That was only a lady-clock, child, 'flying away home.'
Pero escúcheme, Jane, y no vuelva la cabeza para mirar las mariposas...

I wish to remind you that it was you who first said to me, with that discretion I respect in you--with that foresight, prudence, and humility which befit your responsible and dependent position--that in case I married Miss Ingram, both you and little Adele had better trot forthwith.

Usted recordará que fue la primera en decirme, con toda discreción y respeto, como conviene a su posición, que en caso de que yo me casara con Miss Ingram, era preferible que usted y Adèle se fueran de la casa.

I pass over the sort of slur conveyed in this suggestion on the character of my beloved; indeed, when you are far away, Janet, I'll try to forget it: I shall notice only its wisdom; which is such that I have made it my law of action.

Prescindo de la calumniosa mancha que esa sugerencia arroja sobre el angelical carácter de mi adorada y me limito, mi dulce Jane, a apreciar lo que en su indicación hay de prudente y a convertirla en mi línea de conducta.
Adele must go to school; and you, Miss Eyre, must get a new situation."
Adèle será enviada al colegio y usted, Miss Eyre, no tiene más salida que buscar otro empleo.

"Yes, sir, I will advertise immediately: and meantime, I suppose--" I was going to say, "I suppose I may stay here, till I find another shelter to betake myself to:" but I stopped, feeling it would not do to risk a long sentence, for my voice was not quite under command.
Iba a concluir: «que podría continuar aquí hasta que hallase otro puesto»; pero callé. No me atrevía a hablar mucho, temiendo que mi voz delatara lo que sentía.
"In about a month I hope to be a bridegroom," continued Mr. Rochester; "and in the interim, I shall myself look out for employment and an asylum for you."
-La boda se celebrará de aquí a un mes -siguió Rochester-, y he buscado ya otro empleo para usted. -Gracias, señor: siento que... -No, no; nada de gracias.
"Thank you, sir; I am sorry to give--" "Oh, no need to apologise!
Entiendo que cuando un empleado cumple su deber tan bien como usted lo ha cumplido, tiene derecho a que su patrón le ayude.

I consider that when a dependent does her duty as well as you have done yours, she has a sort of claim upon her employer for any little assistance he can conveniently render her; indeed I have already, through my future mother-in-law, heard of a place that I think will suit: it is to undertake the education of the five daughters of Mrs. Dionysius O'Gall of Bitternutt Lodge, Connaught, Ireland.
Mi futura suegra me ha hablado de una plaza que seguramente le convendrá: se trata de encargarse de la educación de las cinco hijas de Mr. Dionysius O'Gall, de Bitternutt Lodge, en Connaught.
You'll like Ireland, I think: they're such warm-hearted people there, they say."
Le gustará Irlanda. Según dicen, los irlandeses son muy afectuosos.
"It is a long way off, sir."
-Está muy lejos, señor.
"No matter--a girl of your sense will not object to the voyage or the distance."
-¿Qué importa? A una muchacha como usted no creo que le asuste un viaje largo.
"Not the voyage, but the distance: and then the sea is a barrier--"
-No es el viaje, sino la distancia y el mar, que es una barrera que me separaría de...
"From what, Jane?"
-¿De qué?
"From England and from Thornfield: and--"
-De Inglaterra, y de Thornfield, y de...
"Well?"
"From _you_, sir."
-De usted, señor...
I said this almost involuntarily, and, with as little sanction of free will, my tears gushed out. I did not cry so as to be heard, however; I avoided sobbing.
Lo dije casi involuntariamente, mientras lágrimas silenciosas bañaban mi rostro.

The thought of Mrs. O'Gall and Bitternutt Lodge struck cold to my heart; and colder the thought of all the brine and foam, destined, as it seemed, to rush between me and the master at whose side I now walked, and coldest the remembrance of the wider ocean--wealth, caste, custom intervened between me and what I naturally and inevitably loved.

La mención del señor O'Gall, de Bitternutt Lodge, había dejado frío mi corazón, y más aún el pensamiento del mar, del mar inmenso, revuelto y espumoso, que había de interponerse entre mi persona y aquel hombre a cuyo lado paseaba y a quien amaba de un modo espontáneo, superior a mi voluntad.
"It is a long way," I again said.
-Es muy lejos -repetí.
"It is, to be sure; and when you get to Bitternutt Lodge, Connaught, Ireland, I shall never see you again, Jane: that's morally certain.
-Desde luego. Y cuando usted esté en Bitternutt Lodge, no volveremos a vernos más.
I never go over to Ireland, not having myself much of a fancy for the country.
Me parece indudable. No creo ir nunca a Irlanda; no es un país que me atraiga en exceso...
We have been good friends, Jane; have we not?"
Hemos sido buenos amigos, ¿verdad,Jane?
"Yes, sir."
-Sí. -Bien.
"And when friends are on the eve of separation, they like to spend the little time that remains to them close to each other.
Pues cuando dos buenos amigos se separan, emplean el corto tiempo que les queda de estar juntos en hablar un poco de sí mismos.

Come! we'll talk over the voyage and the parting quietly half-an-hour or so, while the stars enter into their shining life up in heaven yonder: here is the chestnut tree: here is the bench at its old roots.
Ea, hablemos tranquilamente durante media hora, mientras las estrellas brillan en el cielo que nos cubre...
Come, we will sit there in peace to-night, though we should never more be destined to sit there together."
Sentémonos en este banco del castaño, ya que nuestro destino es no volver a sentarnos juntos más.
He seated me and himself.
Cuando nos hubimos acomodado, continuó:
"It is a long way to Ireland, Janet, and I am sorry to send my little friend on such weary travels: but if I can't do better, how is it to be helped?
-En efecto, Jane: el viaje a Irlanda es largo y la travesía incómoda y siento que mi amiguita haya de verse obligada a... Pero ¿cómo ayudarla si no?
Are you anything akin to me, do you think, Jane?"
¿Experimenta usted algún sentimiento respecto a mí, Jane?
I could risk no sort of answer by this time: my heart was still.
No pude contestar. Mi corazón desbordaba.

"Because," he said, "I sometimes have a queer feeling with regard to you--especially when you are near me, as now: it is as if I had a string somewhere under my left ribs, tightly and inextricably knotted to a similar string situated in the corresponding quarter of your little frame.

-Porque yo lo experimento por usted -continuó-, sobre todo cuando estamos juntos, como ahora. Es como si en el lado izquierdo de mi pecho tuviese una cuerda que vibrara al mismo ritmo que otra que usted tuviese en análogo lugar y se uniera de un modo invisible a la mía.

And if that boisterous Channel, and two hundred miles or so of land come broad between us, I am afraid that cord of communion will be snapt; and then I've a nervous notion I should take to bleeding inwardly.

Y si ese endiablado canal y doscientas millas de tierra van a separarnos, temo que ese lazo que nos une se rompa. Por lo qué a mí concierne, estoy seguro de que la rotura va a producirme una incontenible hemorragia.
"That I _never_ should, sir: you know--" Impossible to proceed.
Y usted... -Yo nunca, señor, usted sabe... No pude continuar.
"Jane, do you hear that nightingale singing in the wood?
-¿Oye cómo canta ese ruiseñor, Jane?
Listen!"
Escuche.
In listening, I sobbed convulsively; for I could repress what I endured no longer; I was obliged to yield, and I was shaken from head to foot with acute distress.
Escuché y de pronto rompí a llorar convulsivamente, estremeciéndome de pies a cabeza. Imposible soportar más lo que sufría.
When I did speak, it was only to express an impetuous wish that I had never been born, or never come to Thornfield.
Cuando pude hablar, fue para expresar con vehemencia el deseo de no haber nacido nunca o no haber ido jamás a Thornfield. -¿Cómo?
"Because you are sorry to leave it?"
¿Le disgusta tanto irse de aquí?

The vehemence of emotion, stirred by grief and love within me, was claiming mastery, and struggling for full sway, and asserting a right to predominate, to overcome, to live, rise, and reign at last: yes,--and to speak.

-Me disgusta irme de Thornfield. Amo este lugar, y lo amo porque en él he vivido una vida agradable y plena, momentáneamente al menos, porque no he sido rebajada a vivir entre seres inferiores ni excluida de toda relación con cuanto es superior y dinámico.
"I grieve to leave Thornfield: I love Thornfield:--I love it, because I have lived in it a full and delightful life,--momentarily at least. I have not been trampled on.
He podido hablar con alguien a quien admiro, en cuyo trato me complazco...
I have not been petrified. I have not been buried with inferior minds, and excluded from every glimpse of communion with what is bright and energetic and high.
Un cerebro poderoso, amplio, original...
I have talked, face to face, with what I reverence, with what I delight in,--with an original, a vigorous, an expanded mind.
En una palabra, le he conocido a usted, Mr.
I have known you, Mr. Rochester; and it strikes me with terror and anguish to feel I absolutely must be torn from you for ever.
Rochester, y me asusta pensar en irme de su lado.
I see the necessity of departure; and it is like looking on the necessity of death."
Reconozco que debo marchar, pero lo reconozco como podría reconocer la necesidad de morir.
"Where do you see the necessity?" he asked suddenly.
-¿Y qué necesidad tiene de irse? -preguntó de pronto.
"Where? You, sir, have placed it before me."
-Usted mismo me lo ha dicho, señor.
"In what shape?"
-¿A propósito de qué?
"In the shape of Miss Ingram; a noble and beautiful woman,--your bride."
-De Miss Ingram, su noble y bella prometida...
"My bride!
-¿Qué prometida? Yo no tengo prometida.
"But you will have."
-Pero se propone tenerla...
"Yes;--I will!--I will!" He set his teeth.
-Sí, me lo propongo... -masculló.
"Then I must go:--you have said it yourself."
-De modo que debo irme. Usted lo ha dicho.
"No: you must stay!
-No: usted se quedará.
I swear it--and the oath shall be kept."
Se lo juro y cumpliré el juramento.
"I tell you I must go!" I retorted, roused to something like passion.
-¡Y yo le digo que me iré! -exclamé con vehemencia-.

"Do you think I can stay to become nothing to you? Do you think I am an automaton?--a machine without feelings? and can bear to have my morsel of bread snatched from my lips, and my drop of living water dashed from my cup?
¿Piensa que me es posible vivir a su lado sin ser nada para usted? ¿Cree que soy una autómata, una máquina sin sentimientos humanos?
Do you think, because I am poor, obscure, plain, and little, I am soulless and heartless?
¿Piensa que porque soy pobre y oscura carezco de alma y de corazón?
You think wrong!--I have as much soul as you,--and full as much heart!
¡Se equivoca! ¡Tengo tanto corazón y tanta alma como usted!
And if God had gifted me with some beauty and much wealth, I should have made it as hard for you to leave me, as it is now for me to leave you.
Y si Dios me hubiese dado belleza y riquezas, le sería a usted tan amargo separarse de mí como lo es a mí separarme de usted.

I am not talking to you now through the medium of custom, conventionalities, nor even of mortal flesh;--it is my spirit that addresses your spirit; just as if both had passed through the grave, and we stood at God's feet, equal,--as we are!"
Le hablo prescindiendo de convencionalismos, como si estuviésemos más allá de la tumba, ante Dios, y nos hallásemos en un plano de igualdad, ya que en espíritu lo somos.
"As we are!" repeated Mr. Rochester--"so," he added, enclosing me in his arms.
-¡Lo somos! -repitió Rochester.
Gathering me to his breast, pressing his lips on my lips: "so, Jane!"
Y tomándome en sus brazos me oprimió contra su pecho y unió sus labios a los míos-. ¡Sí, Jane!

"Yes, so, sir," I rejoined: "and yet not so; for you are a married man--or as good as a married man, and wed to one inferior to you--to one with whom you have no sympathy--whom I do not believe you truly love; for I have seen and heard you sneer at her.
-O tal vez no -repuse, tratando de soltarme-, porque usted va a casarse con una mujer con quien no simpatiza, a quien no puedo creer que ame.
I would scorn such a union: therefore I am better than you--let me go!"
Yo rechazaría una unión así. Luego yo soy mejor que usted.
"Where, Jane?
-¿Adónde, Jane?
To Ireland?"
¡A Irlanda!
"Yes--to Ireland.
-Sí, a Irlanda.
I have spoken my mind, and can go anywhere now."
Lo he pensado bien y ahora creo que debo irme.
"Jane, be still; don't struggle so, like a wild frantic bird that is rending its own plumage in its desperation."
-Quédese, Jane. No luche consigo misma como un ave que, en su desesperación, despedaza su propio plumaje.
"I am no bird; and no net ensnares me; I am a free human being with an independent will, which I now exert to leave you."
-No soy un ave, sino un ser humano con voluntad personal, que ejercitaré alejándome de usted.
Another effort set me at liberty, and I stood erect before him.
Haciendo un esfuerzo, logré soltarme y permanecí en pie ante él.
"And your will shall decide your destiny," he said: "I offer you my hand, my heart, and a share of all my possessions."
También su voluntad va a decidir de su destino -repuso-. Le ofrezco mi mano, mi corazón y cuanto poseo.
"You play a farce, which I merely laugh at."
-Se burla usted, pero yo me río de su oferta.
"I ask you to pass through life at my side--to be my second self, and best earthly companion."
-La pido, que viva siempre a mi lado, que sea mi mujer.
"For that fate you have already made your choice, and must abide by it."
-Respecto a eso, ya tiene usted hecha su elección.
"Jane, be still a few moments: you are over-excited: I will be still too."
-Espere un poco, Jane. Está usted muy excitada.
A waft of wind came sweeping down the laurel-walk, and trembled through the boughs of the chestnut: it wandered away--away--to an indefinite distance--it died.
Una ráfaga de viento recorrió el sendero bordeado de laureles, agitó las ramas del castaño y se extinguió a lo lejos.
The nightingale's song was then the only voice of the hour: in listening to it, I again wept.
No se percibía otro ruido que el canto del ruiseñor. Al oírlo, volví a llorar.
Mr. Rochester sat quiet, looking at me gently and seriously.
Rochester, sentado, me contemplaba en silencio, con serenidad, grave y amablemente.
Some time passed before he spoke; he at last said--
Cuando habló al fin, dijo:
"Come to my side, Jane, and let us explain and understand one another."
-Siéntese a mi lado, Jane, y expliquémonos.
"I will never again come to your side: I am torn away now, and cannot return."
-No volveré más a su lado.
"But, Jane, I summon you as my wife: it is you only I intend to marry."
-Jane, ¿no oye que deseo hacerla mi mujer? Es con usted con quien quiero casarme.
I was silent: I thought he mocked me.
Callé, suponiendo que se burlaba.
"Come, Jane--come hither."
-Venga, Jane.
"Your bride stands between us."
-No. Su novia nos separa.
He rose, and with a stride reached me.
Se puso en pie y me alcanzó de un salto.
"My bride is here," he said, again drawing me to him, "because my equal is here, and my likeness.
-Mi novia está aquí -dijo, atrayéndome hacia sí-: es mi igual y me gusta.
Jane, will you marry me?"
¿Quiere casarse conmigo, Jane?
Still I did not answer, and still I writhed myself from his grasp: for I was still incredulous.
No le contesté; luchaba para librarme de él. No le creía.
"Do you doubt me, Jane?"
-¿Duda de mí, Jane?
"Entirely."
-En absoluto.
"You have no faith in me?"
-¿No tiene fe en mí?
"Not a whit."
-Ni una gota.
"Am I a liar in your eyes?" he asked passionately.
-Entonces, ¿me considera usted un bellaco? -dijo con vehemencia-.
"Little sceptic, you _shall_ be convinced.
Usted se convencerá, incrédula.
What love have I for Miss Ingram?
¿Acaso amo a Blanche Ingram?
None: and that you know.
No, y usted lo sabe.
What love has she for me?
¿Acaso me ama ella a mí?

None: as I have taken pains to prove: I caused a rumour to reach her that my fortune was not a third of what was supposed, and after that I presented myself to see the result; it was coldness both from her and her mother.
No, y me he preocupado de comprobarlo. He hecho llegar hasta ella el rumor de que mi fortuna no era ni la tercera parte de lo que se suponía, y luego me he presentado a Blanche y a su madre.
I would not--I could not--marry Miss Ingram.
Las dos me han acogido con frialdad. No puedo, ni debo, casarme con Blanche Ingram.
You--you strange, you almost unearthly thing!--I love as my own flesh. You--poor and obscure, and small and plain as you are--I entreat to accept me as a husband."
A usted, tan rara, tan insignificante, tan vulgar, es a quien quiero como a mi propia carne, y a quien ruego que me acepte por esposo.

"What, me!" I ejaculated, beginning in his earnestness--and especially in his incivility--to credit his sincerity: "me who have not a friend in the world but you--if you are my friend: not a shilling but what you have given me?"

-¿A mí? -exclamé, empezando a creerle, en vista de su apasionamiento y, sobre todo, de su ruda franqueza-. ¡A mí, que no tengo en el mundo otro amigo que usted, si es que usted se considera amigo mío, y que no poseo un chelín, no siendo los que usted me paga!
"You, Jane, I must have you for my own--entirely my own.
-A usted, Jane. Quiero que sea mía, únicamente mía.
Will you be mine?
¿Acepta? ¡Diga inmediatamente que sí!
Say yes, quickly."
-Mr.
"Mr. Rochester, let me look at your face: turn to the moonlight."
Rochester, déjeme mirarle la cara. Vuélvase de modo que le ilumine la luna.
"Why?"
-¿Para qué?
"Because I want to read your countenance--turn!"
-Porque quiero leer en su rostro.
"There! you will find it scarcely more legible than a crumpled, scratched page. Read on: only make haste, for I suffer."
-Bien; ya está. Creo que mi rostro no le va a parecer más legible que una hoja tachada, pero en fin, lea lo que quiera, con tal de que sea pronto.
His face was very much agitated and very much flushed, and there were strong workings in the features, and strange gleams in the eyes.
Su faz estaba muy agitada. Tenía las facciones contraídas y una extraña luz brillaba en sus ojos.
"Oh, Jane, you torture me!" he exclaimed.
-¡Me tortura usted, Jane! -exclamó-.
"With that searching and yet faithful and generous look, you torture me!"
Por muy franca y bondadosa que sea su mirada, me escudriña de un modo...
"How can I do that?
-¿Cómo voy a torturarle?
If you are true, and your offer real, my only feelings to you must be gratitude and devotion--they cannot torture."
Si dice usted la verdad y su oferta es sincera, mis sentimientos no pueden ser otros que los de una gratitud infinita. ¿Cómo voy a torturarle con ella?
"Gratitude!" he ejaculated; and added wildly--"Jane accept me quickly.
-¿Gratitud?
Say, Edward--give me my name--Edward--I will marry you." "Are you in earnest?
Jane -ordenó, perentoriamente-, dígame así: «Edward, quiero casarme contigo.»
Do you sincerely wish me to be your wife?"
-¿Es posible que me quiera usted de verdad?
"I do; and if an oath is necessary to satisfy you, I swear it."
¿Qué se propone hacerme su mujer? -Sí; se lo juro, si lo desea.
"Then, sir, I will marry you."
-Entonces, señor, sí quiero casarme con usted.
"Edward--my little wife!"
-Señor, no. Di Edward, mujercita mía.
"Dear Edward!"
-¡Oh, querido Edward!
"Come to me--come to me entirely now," said he; and added, in his deepest tone, speaking in my ear as his cheek was laid on mine, "Make my happiness--I will make yours."
-Ven, ven conmigo -y rozando mis mejillas con las suyas y hablándome al oído, murmuró-: Hazme feliz y yo te haré feliz a ti.

And if I had loved him less I should have thought his accent and look of exultation savage; but, sitting by him, roused from the nightmare of parting--called to the paradise of union--I thought only of the bliss given me to drink in so abundant a flow.

De haberle amado menos, hubiese pensado que su aspecto y su mirada mostraban una alegría casi salvaje, pero libre de la pesadilla de la marcha, abriéndose ante mí el paraíso de la dicha que se me ofrecía, sólo pensaba en beber hasta la última gota de aquel néctar.
Again and again he said, "Are you happy, Jane?" And again and again I answered, "Yes."
Una y otra vez, Rochester me preguntaba: «¿Te sientes feliz, Jane?»
After which he murmured, "It will atone--it will atone.
Y una y otra vez le respondía: «Sí.»
I know my Maker sanctions what I do. For the world's judgment--I wash my hands thereof.
Le oí murmurar para sí: -Sé que Dios no deja de aprobar lo que hago.
For man's opinion--I defy it."
La opinión del mundo me es indiferente, y desafío la crítica de los hombres.
But what had befallen the night? The moon was not yet set, and we were all in shadow: I could scarcely see my master's face, near as I was.
La luna ya no brillaba, estábamos en sombras y yo no podía ver apenas el rostro de Rochester, a pesar de lo cerca que me hallaba de él.
And what ailed the chestnut tree? it writhed and groaned; while wind roared in the laurel walk, and came sweeping over us.
El viento soplaba entre los laureles y movía, con sordo rumor, las ramas del castaño. -Tenemos que entrar -dijo Rochester-: el tiempo cambia.
"We must go in," said Mr. Rochester: "the weather changes.
Quisiera estar contigo hasta mañana, Jane.
I could have sat with thee till morning, Jane."
«Y yo contigo», pensé.

"And so," thought I, "could I with you." I should have said so, perhaps, but a livid, vivid spark leapt out of a cloud at which I was looking, and there was a crack, a crash, and a close rattling peal; and I thought only of hiding my dazzled eyes against Mr. Rochester's shoulder.
Y quizá lo hubiese dicho si en aquel momento un relámpago no me hubiera dejado deslumbrada, obligándome a ocultar mis ofuscados ojos contra el hombro de Rochester. Comenzó a llover con furia.
The rain rushed down. He hurried me up the walk, through the grounds, and into the house; but we were quite wet before we could pass the threshold.
Él me arrastró velozmente por el sendero hacia la casa, pero antes de que cruzásemos el umbral estábamos empapados.
He was taking off my shawl in the hall, and shaking the water out of my loosened hair, when Mrs. Fairfax emerged from her room.
Mientras Rochester me quitaba el chal y alisaba mi cabello despeinado por el agua, Mrs. Fairfax salió de su cuarto.
I did not observe her at first, nor did Mr. Rochester.
Ni él ni yo reparamos en ella.
The lamp was lit.
La lámpara estaba encendida.
The clock was on the stroke of twelve.
El reloj daba en aquellos momentos las doce.
"Hasten to take off your wet things," said he; "and before you go, good- night--good-night, my darling!"
-Quítate en seguida la ropa, ¡Estás calada! Buenas noches, queridita -dijo Rochester.
He kissed me repeatedly.
Me besó repetidas veces.
When I looked up, on leaving his arms, there stood the widow, pale, grave, and amazed.
Al separarme de él distinguí a la viuda, mirándonos, grave, pálida y asombrada.
I only smiled at her, and ran upstairs.
La sonreí y corrí escaleras arriba.

"Explanation will do for another time," thought I. Still, when I reached my chamber, I felt a pang at the idea she should even temporarily misconstrue what she had seen. But joy soon effaced every other feeling; and loud as the wind blew, near and deep as the thunder crashed, fierce and frequent as the lightning gleamed, cataract-like as the rain fell during a storm of two hours' duration, I experienced no fear and little awe.

«Dejemos la explicación para otra vez», pensé. No obstante, ya en mi cuarto me turbó algo la idea de suponer lo que ella podría pensar de lo que había visto, pero mi alegría borró pronto los demás sentimientos y pese a la violencia con que soplaba el viento, a la frecuencia y fragor con que sonaba el trueno, a los lívidos relámpagos y a la lluvia que cayó a torrentes durante dos horas, no sentía ni el más pequeño temor.
Mr. Rochester came thrice to my door in the course of it, to ask if I was safe and tranquil: and that was comfort, that was strength for anything.
Mientras persistió la tormenta, Rochester llamó tres veces a mi puerta para preguntarme si necesitaba algo.

Before I left my bed in the morning, little Adele came running in to tell me that the great horse-chestnut at the bottom of the orchard had been struck by lightning in the night, and half of it split away.
A la mañana siguiente, antes de levantarme, Adèle vino corriendo a decirme que por la noche había caído un rayo en el castaño del huerto y lo había medio destruido.
As I rose and dressed, I thought over what had happened, and wondered if it were a dream.
Una vez levantada y vestida, pensé en lo sucedido y me pareció un sueño.
I could not be certain of the reality till I had seen Mr. Rochester again, and heard him renew his words of love and promise.
No estaba segura de su realidad hasta que viese a Rochester y le oyese renovar sus promesas y sus frases de amor.

While arranging my hair, I looked at my face in the glass, and felt it was no longer plain: there was hope in its aspect and life in its colour; and my eyes seemed as if they had beheld the fount of fruition, and borrowed beams from the lustrous ripple.
Brillaban en él una expresión de esperanza y un vivido color. Mis ojos parecían haberse bañado en la fuente de la dicha y adquirido en ella un esplendor inusitado.
I had often been unwilling to look at my master, because I feared he could not be pleased at my look; but I was sure I might lift my face to his now, and not cool his affection by its expression.
Con frecuencia había temido que Rochester se sintiera desagradado por mi aspecto, pero ahora me sentía segura de que mi semblante, tal como estaba hoy, no enfriaría su afecto.
I took a plain but clean and light summer dress from my drawer and put it on: it seemed no attire had ever so well become me, because none had I ever worn in so blissful a mood.
Saqué del cajón un sencillo y limpio vestido de verano y me lo puse.

I was not surprised, when I ran down into the hall, to see that a brilliant June morning had succeeded to the tempest of the night; and to feel, through the open glass door, the breathing of a fresh and fragrant breeze.
Me pareció que nunca me había sentado tan bien. No me sorprendió al bajar al vestíbulo que una bella mañana de verano hubiera sucedido a la tempestad.
Nature must be gladsome when I was so happy.
Aspiré la brisa, fresca y fragante.

A beggar-woman and her little boy--pale, ragged objects both--were coming up the walk, and I ran down and gave them all the money I happened to have in my purse--some three or four shillings: good or bad, they must partake of my jubilee.
Una mendiga con un niño avanzada por el camino y corrí a darles cuanto llevaba: tres o cuatro chelines. Quería que todos y todo participaran de mi júbilo, de un modo u otro.
The rooks cawed, and blither birds sang; but nothing was so merry or so musical as my own rejoicing heart.
Graznaban las cornejas y cantaban los pájaros, pero nada me era tan grato como la alegría de mi corazón.
Mrs. Fairfax surprised me by looking out of the window with a sad countenance, and saying gravely--"Miss Eyre, will you come to breakfast?"
Fairfax se asomó a la ventana y con grave acento me dijo: -Miss Eyre, ¿viene a desayunar? Mientras desayunábamos, se mantuvo fría y silenciosa.
During the meal she was quiet and cool: but I could not undeceive her then.
Pero yo no podía explicarme con ella aún.
I must wait for my master to give explanations; and so must she.
Necesitaba que Rochester me repitiese lo que me dijera la noche antes.
I ate what I could, and then I hastened upstairs. I met Adele leaving the schoolroom.
Desayuné todo lo de prisa que pude, subí y encontré a Adèle que salía del cuarto de estudio.
"Where are you going?
-¿Adónde vas? Es hora de dar la lección.
It is time for lessons."
-Mrs.
"Mr. Rochester has sent me away to the nursery."
Rochester me ha dicho que vaya a jugar.
"Where is he?"
-¿Dónde está?
"In there," pointing to the apartment she had left; and I went in, and there he stood.
-Allí -contestó señalando el cuarto del que salía.
"Come and bid me good-morning," said he.
-Saludémonos -me dijo.
I gladly advanced; and it was not merely a cold word now, or even a shake of the hand that I received, but an embrace and a kiss.
Avancé hacia él, que me acogió no con una simple palabra o con un apretón de manos, sino con un abrazo y un beso.
It seemed natural: it seemed genial to be so well loved, so caressed by him.
Me parecía natural y admirable que me quisiera y me acariciara tanto.
"Jane, you look blooming, and smiling, and pretty," said he: "truly pretty this morning.
-Jane -me dijo-: esta mañana estás agradable, sonriente, bonita...
Is this my pale, little elf? Is this my mustard- seed?
No pareces el duendecillo de otras veces.
This little sunny-faced girl with the dimpled cheek and rosy lips; the satin-smooth hazel hair, and the radiant hazel eyes?"
¿Es posible que sea la misma esa muchachita de radiante rostro, rosadas mejillas, rojos labios, sedosa cabellera y brillantes ojos castaños?
(I had green eyes, reader; but you must excuse the mistake: for him they were new-dyed, I suppose.)
Yo tenía ojos verdes, lector; pero debes perdonar el error: supongo que para él mostraban un nuevo reflejo.
"It is Jane Eyre, sir."
-Soy la misma Jane Eyre.
"Soon to be Jane Rochester," he added: "in four weeks, Janet; not a day more.
-Pronto serás Jane Rochester. De aquí a cuatro semanas.
Do you hear that?"
¡Ni un día más! ¿Lo oyes?
I did, and I could not quite comprehend it: it made me giddy.
Lo oía sí, pero apenas lo comprendía.
The feeling, the announcement sent through me, was something stronger than was consistent with joy--something that smote and stunned. It was, I think almost fear.
Aquella noticia me causaba una sensación tal, que más que alegría rayaba en estupefacción, casi en miedo.
"You blushed, and now you are white, Jane: what is that for?"
-Te has puesto pálida, Jane. ¿Qué te pasa?
"Because you gave me a new name--Jane Rochester; and it seems so strange."
-Me da usted un nombre que me resulta tan extraño...
"Yes, Mrs. Rochester," said he; "young Mrs. Rochester--Fairfax Rochester's girl-bride."
Rochester-contestó-, la joven Mrs. Rochester; la esposa de Fairfax Rochester.
"It can never be, sir; it does not sound likely.
-Me parece imposible.
Human beings never enjoy complete happiness in this world. I was not born for a different destiny to the rest of my species: to imagine such a lot befalling me is a fairy tale--a day-dream."
Semejante felicidad se me figura un sueño, un cuento de hadas.
"Which I can and will realise. I shall begin to-day.
-Que yo convertiré en realidad.
This morning I wrote to my banker in London to send me certain jewels he has in his keeping,--heirlooms for the ladies of Thornfield.
Hoy he escrito a mi banquero para que envíe ciertas joyas que tiene en custodia: las joyas de la familia.
In a day or two I hope to pour them into your lap: for every privilege, every attention shall be yours that I would accord a peer's daughter, if about to marry her."
Espero poder dártelas dentro de un par de días. Quiero que disfrutes de todas las atenciones, de todas las delicadezas que merecería la hija de un par si me casara con ella.
"Oh, sir!--never rain jewels!
-No hablemos de joyas.
I don't like to hear them spoken of.
¡Joyas para Jane Eyre!
Jewels for Jane Eyre sounds unnatural and strange: I would rather not have them."
Vale más no tenerlas.

"I will myself put the diamond chain round your neck, and the circlet on your forehead,--which it will become: for nature, at least, has stamped her patent of nobility on this brow, Jane; and I will clasp the bracelets on these fine wrists, and load these fairy-like fingers with rings."

-Yo mismo te pondré al cuello el collar de diamantes y la diadema en esa frente que tiene por naturaleza un aspecto tan noble. Yo mismo ceñiré con pulseras tus finas muñecas y con anillos tus deditos de hada.
"No, no, sir! think of other subjects, and speak of other things, and in another strain.
-Pensemos y hablemos de otras cosas, no de esas que me resultan extrañas.
Don't address me as if I were a beauty; I am your plain, Quakerish governess."
No se dirija a mí como si fuera una belleza. No soy más que una vulgar institutriz.
"You are a beauty in my eyes, and a beauty just after the desire of my heart,--delicate and aerial."
-A mis ojos eres una belleza tal como me gusta: vaporosa, delicada...
"Puny and insignificant, you mean.
-Quiere usted decir mezquina e insignificante.
You are dreaming, sir,--or you are sneering.
O sueña usted o se burla de mí...
For God's sake don't be ironical!"
¡No se chancee, por Dios!
"I will make the world acknowledge you a beauty, too," he went on, while I really became uneasy at the strain he had adopted, because I felt he was either deluding himself or trying to delude me.
-Yo haré que todo el mundo reconozca tu belleza -dijo. Yo me sentía realmente contrariada de la actitud que había adoptado, porque comprendía que él trataba de ilusionarme o de ilusionarse-.
"I will attire my Jane in satin and lace, and she shall have roses in her hair; and I will cover the head I love best with a priceless veil."
Cubriré a mi Jane de rasos y blondas, pondré flores en sus cabellos, adornaré la cabeza que amo...
"And then you won't know me, sir; and I shall not be your Jane Eyre any longer, but an ape in a harlequin's jacket--a jay in borrowed plumes.
-Y no me conocerá usted entonces ni seré su Jane Eyre, sino un arlequín, un grajo con plumas de pavo real. Prefería que no se empeñase en considerarme como una bella dama.

I would as soon see you, Mr. Rochester, tricked out in stage-trappings, as myself clad in a court-lady's robe; and I don't call you handsome, sir, though I love you most dearly: far too dearly to flatter you. Don't flatter me."
Así como yo no le llamo hermoso, a pesar de lo mucho que le amo, para no adularle, tampoco debe usted adularme a mí.
He pursued his theme, however, without noticing my deprecation.
Pero él continuó hablando sin hacer caso alguno de mi opinión.
"This very day I shall take you in the carriage to Millcote, and you must choose some dresses for yourself.
-Voy a llevarte en coche a Millcote hoy mismo para que elijas los vestidos que gustes.
I told you we shall be married in four weeks.
Te digo que nos casaremos dentro de cuatro semanas.
The wedding is to take place quietly, in the church down below yonder; and then I shall waft you away at once to town.

Celebraremos la boda en la intimidad, en esa iglesita cercana, y luego iremos a Londres. Estaremos allí unos días y luego conduciré a mi tesoro a países más soleados: Francia, con sus viñedos; Italia, con sus llanuras.

After a brief stay there, I shall bear my treasure to regions nearer the sun: to French vineyards and Italian plains; and she shall see whatever is famous in old story and in modern record: she shall taste, too, of the life of cities; and she shall learn to value herself by just comparison with others."

Y mi tesorito conocerá cuanto hay digno de verse: los recuerdos de la Antigüedad, las cosas modernas... Se acostumbrará a vivir en las ciudades y aprenderá a estimarse en lo que merece comparándose con las demás.
"Shall I travel?--and with you, sir?"
-¿Viajaré con usted?

"You shall sojourn at Paris, Rome, and Naples: at Florence, Venice, and Vienna: all the ground I have wandered over shall be re-trodden by you: wherever I stamped my hoof, your sylph's foot shall step also.
-Iremos a París, a Roma, a Nápoles, a Florencia, a Venecia y a Viena. Recorreré contigo todos los países que he recorrido solo y tu pie pisará donde antes he pisado yo.
Ten years since, I flew through Europe half mad; with disgust, hate, and rage as my companions: now I shall revisit it healed and cleansed, with a very angel as my comforter."
Desde hace diez años he recorrido Europa medio loco, con el odio, la furia y el disgusto reinando en mi corazón. Ahora la recorreré sereno y purificado, acompañado de un ángel que me consolará...
I laughed at him as he said this.
Reí y le dije:
"I am not an angel," I asserted; "and I will not be one till I die: I will be myself.
-No soy un ángel ni lo seré hasta que muera. Seré como soy, Mr.
Mr. Rochester, you must neither expect nor exact anything celestial of me--for you will not get it, any more than I shall get it of you: which I do not at all anticipate."
No espere usted de mí nada celestial, porque no lo encontrará. Además, presumo que usted...
"What do you anticipate of me?"
-¿Qué presumes?

"For a little while you will perhaps be as you are now,--a very little while; and then you will turn cool; and then you will be capricious; and then you will be stern, and I shall have much ado to please you: but when you get well used to me, you will perhaps like me again,--_like_ me, I say, not _love_ me.

-Presumo que durante algún tiempo quizá siga usted como ahora, pero luego se enfriará, se hará malhumorado y antojadizo y yo tendré que esforzarme mucho para agradarle. Creo, no obstante, que cuando esté bien acostumbrado a mí me apreciará.
I suppose your love will effervesce in six months, or less.
Supongo que la vehemencia de su amor durará seis meses o quizá menos.
I have observed in books written by men, that period assigned as the farthest to which a husband's ardour extends.
Es el plazo que en los libros se asigna al amor del más ardoroso marido.
Yet, after all, as a friend and companion, I hope never to become quite distasteful to my dear master."
Ahora bien, como compañera y amiga, espero no resultar desagradable a mi querido dueño.
"Distasteful! and like you again!
-¿Desagradable? ¿Volver a apreciarte?
I think I shall like you again, and yet again: and I will make you confess I do not only _like_, but _love_ you--with truth, fervour, constancy."
¡No te dejaré de apreciar nunca! No sólo te apreciaré, sino que he de amarte con sinceridad, fervor y constancia.
"Yet are you not capricious, sir?"
-¿No es usted caprichoso?

"To women who please me only by their faces, I am the very devil when I find out they have neither souls nor hearts--when they open to me a perspective of flatness, triviality, and perhaps imbecility, coarseness, and ill-temper: but to the clear eye and eloquent tongue, to the soul made of fire, and the character that bends but does not break--at once supple and stable, tractable and consistent--I am ever tender and true."

-Con las mujeres que sólo me gustan por su aspecto, soy un verdadero demonio cuando descubro que no tienen alma ni corazón, cuando abren ante mí las perspectivas de su mal carácter, su vulgaridad y su estupidez. Pero para una mujer de límpidos ojos, de lengua elocuente, de alma ardorosa, de carácter flexible y firme, dócil y enérgico a la vez, seré siempre fiel y afectuoso.
"Had you ever experience of such a character, sir?
-¿Ha conocido usted a alguien así?
Did you ever love such an one?"
¿Ha amado a alguien que fuera de tal modo?
"I love it now."
-Amo ahora a una persona así.
"But before me: if I, indeed, in any respect come up to your difficult standard?"
-Pero, antes que a mí, ¿no ha amado a nadie que encarnara un tipo tan difícil de encontrar?
"I never met your likeness.
-Jane: nunca he hallado a nadie como tú.

Jane, you please me, and you master me--you seem to submit, and I like the sense of pliancy you impart; and while I am twining the soft, silken skein round my finger, it sends a thrill up my arm to my heart.
Nadie me ha sometido, nadie ha influido tan dulcemente como tú lo has hecho.
I am influenced--conquered; and the influence is sweeter than I can express; and the conquest I undergo has a witchery beyond any triumph I can win.
Esta influencia que ejerces sobre mí es mucho más encantadora de cuanto se pueda expresar.
Why do you smile, Jane?
Pero ¿por qué sonríes, Jane?
"I was thinking, sir (you will excuse the idea; it was involuntary), I was thinking of Hercules and Samson with their charmers--"
-Estaba pensando (y perdóneme, porque la idea ha acudido involuntariamente a mi mente) en Hércules y Sansón y en sus respectivas amadas.
"You were, you little elfish--"
-¿Y en qué más, duendecillo mío?

You don't talk very wisely just now; any more than those gentlemen acted very wisely. However, had they been married, they would no doubt by their severity as husbands have made up for their softness as suitors; and so will you, I fear.
-Pensaba que si aquellos caballeros se hubiesen casado, su severidad como maridos hubiera superado en mucho a su dulzura de enamorados. Y sospecho que a usted le pasará igual.
I wonder how you will answer me a year hence, should I ask a favour it does not suit your convenience or pleasure to grant."
Me agradaría saber cómo contestará cuando de aquí a un año le pida cualquier favor que usted no juzgue oportuno concederme.
"Ask me something now, Jane,--the least thing: I desire to be entreated--"
-Pídemelo ahora, Jane. ¿Qué más da?
"Indeed I will, sir; I have my petition all ready."
-Lo haré así.
"Speak!
-Habla.
But if you look up and smile with that countenance, I shall swear concession before I know to what, and that will make a fool of me."
Pero si me miras y sonríes de ese modo, te prometeré hacer lo que me solicites antes de saber lo que es, y quizá con ello haga una tontería.
"Not at all, sir; I ask only this: don't send for the jewels, and don't crown me with roses: you might as well put a border of gold lace round that plain pocket handkerchief you have there."
Sólo quiero que no haga traer las joyas y que no me corone de rosas. Sería tan ilógico como si mandara bordar en oro ese sencillo pañuelo que lleva usted.
"I might as well 'gild refined gold.'
-Más bien querrás decir que sería como dorar el oro...
I know it: your request is granted then--for the time.
Bien: se te concede por ahora lo que pides.
I will remand the order I despatched to my banker.
Rectificaré la orden que he enviado a mi banquero.
But you have not yet asked for anything; you have prayed a gift to be withdrawn: try again."
Pero esto no es pedir, sino obtener que se te deje de hacer un don. Pídeme otra cosa, pues.
"Well then, sir, have the goodness to gratify my curiosity, which is much piqued on one point."
-Entonces, señor, le ruego que satisfaga mi curiosidad sobre cierto extremo.
He looked disturbed.
-¿Cómo? -dijo, con alguna turbación-.
"What? what?" he said hastily. "Curiosity is a dangerous petition: it is well I have not taken a vow to accord every request--"
Las peticiones que hace la curiosidad son arriesgadas. Celebro no haber prometido complacerte en todo.
"But there can be no danger in complying with this, sir."
-Ningún riesgo puede haber en satisfacer esa curiosidad.
"Utter it, Jane: but I wish that instead of a mere inquiry into, perhaps, a secret, it was a wish for half my estate." "Now, King Ahasuerus!
-¿Tú qué sabes, Jane? Acaso, a hacerme preguntas sobre algo que convenga mantener en secreto, prefiriera que me pidieses la mitad de mis bienes.
Do you think I am a Jew-usurer, seeking good investment in land?
-¿Y para qué necesito la mitad de sus bienes? ¿Acaso se figura que soy un judío usurero?
I would much rather have all your confidence.
Prefiero conseguir las confidencias de usted.
You will not exclude me from your confidence if you admit me to your heart?"
¿Va usted a excluirme de sus confidencias cuando me acepta en su corazón?
"You are welcome to all my confidence that is worth having, Jane; but for God's sake, don't desire a useless burden! Don't long for poison--don't turn out a downright Eve on my hands!"
-No te rehusaré ninguna confidencia confesable, Jane; pero, por amor de Dios, no te obstines en que te haga confidencias inútiles.
"Why not, sir?
-¿Por qué no obstinarme?
You have just been telling me how much you liked to be conquered, and how pleasant over-persuasion is to you.
Usted mismo me ha dicho que lo que le place de mí es mi fuerza de persuasión.
This is what I have to ask,--Why did you take such pains to make me believe you wished to marry Miss Ingram?"
En resumen, ¿por qué se empeña usted en hacerme sufrir dándome a entender que iba a casarse con Blanche Ingram?
"Is that all?
-¿No es más que eso?
Thank God it is no worse!"
¡Menos mal!
And now he unknit his black brows; looked down, smiling at me, and stroked my hair, as if well pleased at seeing a danger averted.
-y sonrió, desarrugó el entrecejo y pasó la mano por mi cabellera, con la satisfecha expresión de quien ha visto alejarse el peligro-.

"Well, I feigned courtship of Miss Ingram, because I wished to render you as madly in love with me as I was with you; and I knew jealousy would be the best ally I could call in for the furtherance of that end."
He fingido cortejar a Blanche Ingram porque deseaba que te enamoraras tan locamente de mí como yo lo estaba de ti. Sabía que los celos eran el mejor modo de conseguir lo que me proponía.
"Excellent!
-¡Admirable!
Now you are small--not one whit bigger than the end of my little finger.
Es usted más pequeñito que la punta de mi meñique.
It was a burning shame and a scandalous disgrace to act in that way.
¿No le daba vergüenza?
Did you think nothing of Miss Ingram's feelings, sir?"
¿Cómo jugaba así con los sentimientos de Blanche?
"Her feelings are concentrated in one--pride; and that needs humbling.
-Todos sus sentimientos se reducen a uno: el orgullo. Y conviene humillarlo.
Were you jealous, Jane?"
¿Estabas celosa, Jane?
"Never mind, Mr. Rochester: it is in no way interesting to you to know that.
-Eso no le interesa.
Answer me truly once more. Do you think Miss Ingram will not suffer from your dishonest coquetry?
¿Cree que Blanche Ingram no sufrirá con el proceder de usted?
Won't she feel forsaken and deserted?"
¿No piensa que se considerará abandonada y desairada?
"Impossible!--when I told you how she, on the contrary, deserted me: the idea of my insolvency cooled, or rather extinguished, her flame in a moment."
-Ya te he dicho que es ella quien me ha abandonado a mí. El pensar en mi insolvencia enfrió o, mejor dicho, extinguió su ardor instantáneamente.
"You have a curious, designing mind, Mr. Rochester.
-Es usted original, Mr. Rochester.
I am afraid your principles on some points are eccentric."
Tiene usted principios muy extraños.
"My principles were never trained, Jane: they may have grown a little awry for want of attention."
-Si hubiesen sido encauzados cuando empezaban a desarrollarse, mis principios no serían como son.
"Once again, seriously; may I enjoy the great good that has been vouchsafed to me, without fearing that any one else is suffering the bitter pain I myself felt a while ago?"
-En serio: ¿cree que puedo gozar de esta gran alegría sin amargármela con el pensamiento de que otra mujer sufre lo que yo sufría antes?
"That you may, my good little girl: there is not another being in the world has the same pure love for me as yourself--for I lay that pleasant unction to my soul, Jane, a belief in your affection."
No hay nadie en el mundo que me quiera como tú. Ya ves, Jane, que tengo el consuelo de creer que me quieres.
I turned my lips to the hand that lay on my shoulder.
Puse mis labios sobre su mano, que estaba apoyada en mi hombro.
I loved him very much--more than I could trust myself to say--more than words had power to express.
Le amaba mucho, en efecto, más de lo que yo pudiera decir, más de cuanto las palabras pueden expresar.
"Ask something more," he said presently; "it is my delight to be entreated, and to yield."
-Pídeme algo más -dijo-. Mi mayor placer es complacerte.
"Communicate your intentions to Mrs. Fairfax, sir: she saw me with you last night in the hall, and she was shocked.
-Entonces manifieste usted sus propósitos a Mrs. Fairfax antes de que yo la vea.
Give her some explanation before I see her again.
Ayer nos sorprendió en el vestíbulo y se extrañó.
It pains me to be misjudged by so good a woman."
Me disgusta que una mujer tan bondadosa como ella me juzgue mal.
"Go to your room, and put on your bonnet," he replied.
-Vete a tu cuarto y ponte el sombrero -dijo-.
"I mean you to accompany me to Millcote this morning; and while you prepare for the drive, I will enlighten the old lady's understanding.
Tienes que acompañarme a Millcote. Entretanto, yo hablaré a la buena señora.
I was soon dressed; and when I heard Mr. Rochester quit Mrs. Fairfax's parlour, I hurried down to it.
Me vestí rápidamente y, cuando sentí a Mr. Rochester salir del gabinete de Mrs.
The old lady, had been reading her morning portion of Scripture--the Lesson for the day; her Bible lay open before her, and her spectacles were upon it.
La anciana había estado leyendo la Biblia; el tomo se hallaba abierto y tenía las gafas puestas sobre él.
Her occupation, suspended by Mr. Rochester's announcement, seemed now forgotten: her eyes, fixed on the blank wall opposite, expressed the surprise of a quiet mind stirred by unwonted tidings.

Parecía haber olvidado su ocupación, interrumpida por la noticia que Rochester le diera, y sus ojos, fijos en la blanca pared, expresaban la sorpresa propia de un cerebro sensato que asiste al desarrollo de cosas insólitas.
Seeing me, she roused herself: she made a sort of effort to smile, and framed a few words of congratulation; but the smile expired, and the sentence was abandoned unfinished.
Al verme se levantó, hizo un esfuerzo para sonreír y me dijo algunas palabras de felicitación. Pero su sonrisa expiró y hasta acabó interrumpiendo su enhorabuena.
She put up her spectacles, shut the Bible, and pushed her chair back from the table.
Cerró la Biblia, apartó las gafas y retiró su silla un poco hacia atrás.
"I feel so astonished," she began, "I hardly know what to say to you, Miss Eyre.
-Estoy asombrada -confesó-. Casi no sé qué decirla.
I have surely not been dreaming, have I?
¿No habré estado soñando?
Sometimes I half fall asleep when I am sitting alone and fancy things that have never happened.
A veces me adormezco cuando estoy sentada a solas, imagino cosas que no han ocurrido jamás.

It has seemed to me more than once when I have been in a doze, that my dear husband, who died fifteen years since, has come in and sat down beside me; and that I have even heard him call me by my name, Alice, as he used to do.
Una vez me pareció que mi difunto marido, muerto hace quince años, se sentaba a mi lado y me llamaba por mi nombre, Alice, como acostumbraba.
Now, can you tell me whether it is actually true that Mr. Rochester has asked you to marry him?
Dígame: ¿es cierto que el señor le ha pedido relaciones?
Don't laugh at me.
No se ría de mí.
But I really thought he came in here five minutes ago, and said that in a month you would be his wife."
Pero me ha parecido que él ha estado aquí hace cinco minutos y me ha dicho que dentro de un mes será usted su esposa.
"He has said the same thing to me," I replied.
-Lo mismo me ha dicho a mí -repliqué.
Do you believe him?
-¿Y le cree usted?
Have you accepted him?"
¿Ha aceptado?
She looked at me bewildered.
Me miró, turbada.
"I could never have thought it.
-¡Nunca se me hubiera ocurrido semejante cosa!
He is a proud man: all the Rochesters were proud: and his father, at least, liked money. He, too, has always been called careful.
Él, que es un hombre orgulloso, como todos los Rochester...
He means to marry you?"
¿Es posible que quiera casarse con usted?
"He tells me so."
-Así me lo ha dicho.
She surveyed my whole person: in her eyes I read that they had there found no charm powerful enough to solve the enigma.
Me miró de pies a cabeza, y leí en sus ojos que no veía en mí hechizos tales que justificaran aquel misterio.
"It passes me!" she continued; "but no doubt, it is true since you say so.
-Me parece increíble -dijo, al fin-, pero no lo dudo, puesto que usted lo dice.
How it will answer, I cannot tell: I really don't know.
Cómo resultará todo, no me atrevo a predecirlo.
Equality of position and fortune is often advisable in such cases; and there are twenty years of difference in your ages.
Es muy aconsejable en estos casos que la fortuna y la edad sean análogos, y él le lleva veinte años.
He might almost be your father."
Podría casi ser su padre.
"No, indeed, Mrs. Fairfax!" exclaimed I, nettled; "he is nothing like my father!
-Nada de eso, Mrs. Fairfax -protesté-.
No one, who saw us together, would suppose it for an instant.
Nadie que nos viera juntos diría que puede ser mi padre.
Mr. Rochester looks as young, and is as young, as some men at five-and- twenty."
Mr. Rochester parece y es tan joven como un hombre de veinticinco años.
"Is it really for love he is going to marry you?" she asked.
-¿Se casa con usted por amor, en realidad? -preguntó.
I was so hurt by her coldness and scepticism, that the tears rose to my eyes.
Me sentí tan herida por su frío escepticismo, que las lágrimas acudieron a mis ojos.
"I am sorry to grieve you," pursued the widow; "but you are so young, and so little acquainted with men, I wished to put you on your guard.
-Siento haberla disgustado -dijo la viuda-, pero usted es muy joven, no está acostumbrada a tratar con los hombres y quisiera ponerla en guardia.
It is an old saying that 'all is not gold that glitters;' and in this case I do fear there will be something found to be different to what either you or I expect."
Ya sabe que no es oro todo lo que reluce. En este caso, temo que todo termine de un modo que ni usted ni yo desearíamos.
"Why?--am I a monster?"
-¿Acaso soy un monstruo? -pregunté-.
I said: "is it impossible that Mr. Rochester should have a sincere affection for me?"
¿Es imposible que Mr. Rochester sienta algún afecto por mí?
"No: you are very well; and much improved of late; and Mr. Rochester, I daresay, is fond of you.
-No. Es usted agradable y mejorará con el tiempo, y reconozco que Mr.
I have always noticed that you were a sort of pet of his.
Rochester parece apreciarla. Vengo observando hace tiempo su predilección por usted.
There are times when, for your sake, I have been a little uneasy at his marked preference, and have wished to put you on your guard: but I did not like to suggest even the possibility of wrong.

Ha habido ocasiones en que he estado a punto de advertirla que se pusiera en guardia contra esa excesiva preferencia, pero temía ofenderla, porque es usted tan modesta, tan discreta y tan prudente, que pensaba que sabría guardarse por sí misma.
Last night I cannot tell you what I suffered when I sought all over the house, and could find you nowhere, nor the master either; and then, at twelve o'clock, saw you come in with him."
No puede usted imaginar lo que sufrí anoche cuando la busqué por toda la casa sin encontrarla y cuando la vi volver con él tan tarde...
"Well, never mind that now," I interrupted impatiently; "it is enough that all was right."
-Todo eso no importa -interrumpí, con impaciencia-. Ya ve que todo va bien.
"I hope all will be right in the end," she said: "but believe me, you cannot be too careful.
-Espero que vaya bien hasta el fin, mas, créame, toda precaución es poca.
Try and keep Mr. Rochester at a distance: distrust yourself as well as him.
Procure mantenerse a cierta distancia del señor. No confíe en él ni en usted misma.
Gentlemen in his station are not accustomed to marry their governesses."
Caballeros de la clase de Mr. Rochester no suelen casarse con institutrices.
I was growing truly irritated: happily, Adele ran in.
Mi irritación crecía. Afortunadamente, Adèle apareció en aquel momento.
"Let me go,--let me go to Millcote too!" she cried.
-¡Lléveme a Millcote! -exclamó-.
"Mr. Rochester won't: though there is so much room in the new carriage.
En el coche hay bastante sitio. Pida a Mr.
Beg him to let me go mademoiselle."
Rochester que me lleve. Él dice que no...
"That I will, Adele;" and I hastened away with her, glad to quit my gloomy monitress.
-Se lo diré, Adèle -repuse-. Y la saqué de la habitación, sintiéndome satisfecha de separarme de la anciana.
The carriage was ready: they were bringing it round to the front, and my master was pacing the pavement, Pilot following him backwards and forwards.
El coche estaba listo y Rochester paseaba ante la fachada de la casa, seguido de Piloto.
"Adele may accompany us, may she not, sir?"
-¿No quiere que nos acompañe Adèle? -pregunté.
"I told her no.
-Ya le he dicho a ella que no.
I'll have no brats!--I'll have only you."
No quiero llevar chiquillos.
"Do let her go, Mr. Rochester, if you please: it would be better."
-Llevémosla, Mr. Rochester.
"Not it: she will be a restraint."
-No: que se quede.
He was quite peremptory, both in look and voice.
Su acento y su mirada eran tan autoritarios que, sin poderlo evitar, los consejos de Mrs.
The chill of Mrs. Fairfax's warnings, and the damp of her doubts were upon me: something of unsubstantiality and uncertainty had beset my hopes. I half lost the sense of power over him.
Fairfax acudieron a mi cerebro y la dudas que ella experimentaba se me comunicaron, empañando mis esperanzas con una sombra de incertidumbre.
I was about mechanically to obey him, without further remonstrance; but as he helped me into the carriage, he looked at my face.
Le obedecí maquinalmente sin replicar. Al ayudarme a subir al coche me miró.
"What is the matter?" he asked; "all the sunshine is gone.
-¿Qué pasa? -preguntó-.
Do you really wish the bairn to go?
Toda tu alegría se ha desvanecido.
Will it annoy you if she is left behind?"
¿Quieres realmente llevar a la pequeña?
"I would far rather she went, sir."
-Lo preferiría.
"Then off for your bonnet, and back like a flash of lightning!" cried he to Adele.
-Entonces corre a buscar tu sombrero y vuelve como un relámpago -ordenó a Adèle.
She obeyed him with what speed she might.
Ella obedeció tan deprisa como pudo.
"After all, a single morning's interruption will not matter much," said he, "when I mean shortly to claim you--your thoughts, conversation, and company--for life."

-Después de todo -dijo él-, no es mucho sufrir una interrupción de una mañana cuando de aquí a poco voy a poder reclamarte íntegramente tus pensamientos, tu compañía y tu conversación para toda la vida.
Adele, when lifted in, commenced kissing me, by way of expressing her gratitude for my intercession: she was instantly stowed away into a corner on the other side of him.
Adèle, al subir al coche, comenzó a besarme en muestra de gratitud, pero él la hizo inmediatamente sentarse en un ángulo del asiento, en el lado opuesto al mío.
She then peeped round to where I sat; so stern a neighbour was too restrictive to him, in his present fractious mood, she dared whisper no observations, nor ask of him any information.
Adèle me miraba a hurtadillas, ya que su vecino de asiento se mostraba tan poco agradable para ella que no se atrevía a decirle ni preguntarle nada.
"Let her come to me," I entreated: "she will, perhaps, trouble you, sir: there is plenty of room on this side."
-Déjela venir a mi lado -dije-. Ahí quizá le moleste y aquí sobra sitio.
