He handed her over as if she had been a lapdog. "I'll send her to school yet," he said, but now he was smiling.
La cogió como si hubiera sido un perrito faldero y la cambió de lugar mientras decía, aunque ahora sonriendo: -Acabaré mandándola al colegio.
Adele heard him, and asked if she was to go to school "sans mademoiselle?"
Adèle que le oyó, se apresuró a preguntar si iba a ir al colegio sans mademoiselle.

"Yes," he replied, "absolutely sans mademoiselle; for I am to take mademoiselle to the moon, and there I shall seek a cave in one of the white valleys among the volcano-tops, and mademoiselle shall live with me there, and only me."
Me la voy a llevar a la Luna. La meteré en una cueva, en uno de los blancos valles que se extienden entre las cumbres de los volcanes, y allí vivirá conmigo, sólo conmigo.
"She will have nothing to eat: you will starve her," observed Adele.
-Pero no tendrá nada que comer y se morirá -observó Adèle.
"I shall gather manna for her morning and night: the plains and hillsides in the moon are bleached with manna, Adele."
-Yo recogeré maná para ella dos veces al día. Las llanuras y montes de la Luna están llenos de maná.
"She will want to warm herself: what will she do for a fire?"
-Tendrá que calentarse. ¿Cómo encenderá fuego?
"Fire rises out of the lunar mountains: when she is cold, I'll carry her up to a peak, and lay her down on the edge of a crater."
-Las montañas de la Luna arrojan fuego por los cráteres de sus volcanes. Cuando Jane tenga frío la colocaré en uno de ellos.
"Oh, qu' elle y sera mal--peu comfortable!
-Oh, qu'elle y será mal... peu confortable!
And her clothes, they will wear out: how can she get new ones?"
Y cuando se le estropee la ropa, ¿dónde comprará otra nueva?
Mr. Rochester professed to be puzzled.
Rochester estaba empeñado en maravillarla.
How would a white or a pink cloud answer for a gown, do you think?
-Para eso están las nubes, mujer. ¿No crees que de una nube blanca o rosada se puede cortar un buen vestido?
And one could cut a pretty enough scarf out of a rainbow."
Y con el arco iris puede muy bien hacerse un lindo chal.
"She is far better as she is," concluded Adele, after musing some time: "besides, she would get tired of living with only you in the moon.
-Mademoiselle está mejor como ahora -dijo Adèle, agregando-: Además se aburriría de vivir sola con usted en la Luna.
If I were mademoiselle, I would never consent to go with you."
Si yo fuera ella, no consentiría en irme allí con usted.
"She has consented: she has pledged her word."
-Pues ella me ha dado su palabra de acompañarme.
"But you can't get her there; there is no road to the moon: it is all air; and neither you nor she can fly."
-No sé cómo va a llevarla. A la Luna no hay caminos, no siendo el aire, y ni usted ni ella saben volar.
"Adele, look at that field."
-Mira ese prado, Adèle. ¿Lo ves?

"In that field, Adele, I was walking late one evening about a fortnight since--the evening of the day you helped me to make hay in the orchard meadows; and, as I was tired with raking swaths, I sat down to rest me on a stile; and there I took out a little book and a pencil, and began to write about a misfortune that befell me long ago, and a wish I had for happy days to come: I was writing away very fast, though daylight was fading from the leaf, when something came up the path and stopped two yards off me.
Pues en él, hace dos semanas, estaba yo sentado en un portillo, con un lápiz y un libro, cuando de pronto, noté que una figura llegaba por el sendero y se detenía a dos pasos de mí.
I looked at it. It was a little thing with a veil of gossamer on its head.
Miré y vi una cosa pequeñita, con un velo de telarañas en la cabeza.
I beckoned it to come near me; it stood soon at my knee.
Se acercó y se sentó en mis rodillas.
I never spoke to it, and it never spoke to me, in words; but I read its eyes, and it read mine; and our speechless colloquy was to this effect--
No nos dijimos nada, pero yo leía en sus ojos y ella en los míos y nuestras miradas mantuvieron un coloquio.

"It was a fairy, and come from Elf-land, it said; and its errand was to make me happy: I must go with it out of the common world to a lonely place--such as the moon, for instance--and it nodded its head towards her horn, rising over Hay-hill: it told me of the alabaster cave and silver vale where we might live.

Me dijo que era un hada que venía del país de la Fantasía a fin de hacerme dichoso, asegurándome que para ello era necesario abandonar la Tierra y buscar un sitio solitario, como por ejemplo, la Luna. Me indicó que en ella había un valle de plata y una cueva de alabastro donde yo podría estar muy contento.
I said I should like to go; but reminded it, as you did me, that I had no wings to fly.
Le dije que me gustaría ir, pero que no tenía alas para volar.
"'Oh,' returned the fairy, 'that does not signify! Here is a talisman will remove all difficulties;' and she held out a pretty gold ring.
«Eso no ofrece dificultad -contestó el hada- Toma este anillo de oro. Es un talismán.
'Put it,' she said, 'on the fourth finger of my left hand, and I am yours, and you are mine; and we shall leave earth, and make our own heaven yonder.'
Ponlo en el anular de mi mano izquierda y tú te convertirás en mío y yo en tuya. Entonces podremos abandonar la Tierra y volar al cielo.»
The ring, Adele, is in my breeches-pocket, under the disguise of a sovereign: but I mean soon to change it to a ring again."
Llevo el anillo en el bolsillo, Adèle. Ahora tiene la forma de una moneda, pero pienso convertirlo muy pronto en anillo.
"But what has mademoiselle to do with it?
-¿Qué tiene que ver Mademoiselle con todo eso?
I don't care for the fairy: you said it was mademoiselle you would take to the moon?"
Usted ha dicho que iba a llevar a Mademoiselle a la Luna...
"Mademoiselle is a fairy," he said, whispering mysteriously.
-Mademoiselle es un hada -cuchicheó al oído de la niña.

Whereupon I told her not to mind his badinage; and she, on her part, evinced a fund of genuine French scepticism: denominating Mr. Rochester "un vrai menteur," and assuring him that she made no account whatever of his "contes de fee," and that "du reste, il n'y avait pas de fees, et quand meme il y en avait:" she was sure they would never appear to him, nor ever give him rings, or offer to live with him in the moon.

Ella, con su escepticismo francés, no le creyó, en efecto. Trató a Rochester de un vrai menteur y le aseguró que ella no creía en sus conies de fées, que du reste, il n'y avrait pas de fées, et quand méme il y en avait, no se aparecerían a él ni le darían anillos ni se ofrecerían a vivir con él en la Luna.
The hour spent at Millcote was a somewhat harassing one to me.
La hora que pasamos en Millcote fue muy embarazosa para mí.
Mr. Rochester obliged me to go to a certain silk warehouse: there I was ordered to choose half-a-dozen dresses.
Rochester me obligó a entrar en un almacén donde me ordenó que eligiera media docena de vestidos.
I hated the business, I begged leave to defer it: no--it should be gone through with now.
Yo aborrecía el ir de compras y le rogué que lo aplazase, pero no lo conseguí.
By dint of entreaties expressed in energetic whispers, I reduced the half-dozen to two: these however, he vowed he would select himself.
Logré, mediante enérgicos cuchicheos, que la media docena se redujese a dos, pero puso la condición de elegirlos él mismo.
With anxiety I watched his eye rove over the gay stores: he fixed on a rich silk of the most brilliant amethyst dye, and a superb pink satin.
Sus miradas se detuvieron sobre una rica seda color amatista y un soberbio raso color de rosa.

I told him in a new series of whispers, that he might as well buy me a gold gown and a silver bonnet at once: I should certainly never venture to wear his choice. With infinite difficulty, for he was stubborn as a stone, I persuaded him to make an exchange in favour of a sober black satin and pearl-grey silk.

A través de una nueva serie de cuchicheos le dije que lo mismo podía haber elegido un vestido de oro y una corona de plata y, con grandes dificultades, porque se empeñaba en ser duro como el granito, logré convencerle de que optase por un satén negro y una seda color gris perla más modestos.
"It might pass for the present," he said; "but he would yet see me glittering like a parterre."
Convino, al fin, en ello, advirtiéndome que sólo cedía por aquella vez, pero que en lo sucesivo quería verme vestida con más colores que un pénsil florido.
Glad was I to get him out of the silk warehouse, and then out of a jewellers shop: the more he bought me, the more my cheek burned with a sense of annoyance and degradation.
Salí con la satisfacción del almacén, si bien para entrar en la joyería. Cuantas más cosas compraba, más me ruborizaba yo, sintiéndome humillada y a disgusto.

As we re-entered the carriage, and I sat back feverish and fagged, I remembered what, in the hurry of events, dark and bright, I had wholly forgotten--the letter of my uncle, John Eyre, to Mrs. Reed: his intention to adopt me and make me his legatee.
Entonces me acordé de la carta de mi tío John Eyre, olvidada en el torbellino de los sucesos de aquellos días, en la que anunciaba su propósito de adoptarme.

"It would, indeed, be a relief," I thought, "if I had ever so small an independency; I never can bear being dressed like a doll by Mr. Rochester, or sitting like a second Danae with the golden shower falling daily round me.
Me sería insoportable verme vestida siempre por Mr. Rochester como una muñeca, vivir como una segunda Dánae, bajo una lluvia de oro.

I will write to Madeira the moment I get home, and tell my uncle John I am going to be married, and to whom: if I had but a prospect of one day bringing Mr. Rochester an accession of fortune, I could better endure to be kept by him now."

En cuanto vuelva a casa escribiré a mi tío John diciéndole que voy a casarme y con quién. Si tengo la esperanza de proporcionar algún día a Rochester algún aumento de sus bienes, sobrellevaré mejor estas cosas.»

And somewhat relieved by this idea (which I failed not to execute that day), I ventured once more to meet my master's and lover's eye, which most pertinaciously sought mine, though I averted both face and gaze.
Algo tranquilizada por mi propósito -que, no obstante, no debía aquel día llevar a la práctica-, miré a mi señor y enamorado.

He smiled; and I thought his smile was such as a sultan might, in a blissful and fond moment, bestow on a slave his gold and gems had enriched: I crushed his hand, which was ever hunting mine, vigorously, and thrust it back to him red with the passionate pressure.

Le vi sonreír y me pareció que aquella sonrisa era la de un sultán en el agradable momento de cubrir de joyas y oro a una de sus esclavas. Cogí su mano, y mientras él estrechaba con fuerza la mía, le dije:
"You need not look in that way," I said; "if you do, I'll wear nothing but my old Lowood frocks to the end of the chapter.
-No me mire de ese modo. De lo contrario, no llevaré en lo sucesivo otras ropas que las que usaba en Lowood.

I'll be married in this lilac gingham: you may make a dressing-gown for yourself out of the pearl-grey silk, and an infinite series of waistcoats out of the black satin." He chuckled; he rubbed his hands.
Me casaré con este mismo vestidillo que llevo y usted podrá emplear para hacerse chalecos la tela que ha comprado.
"Oh, it is rich to see and hear her?" he exclaimed.
-¡Qué gracia me hace verte y oírte! -exclamó él-.
"Is she original?
¡Qué original eres!
Is she piquant? I would not exchange this one little English girl for the Grand Turk's whole seraglio, gazelle- eyes, houri forms, and all!"
¡No cambiaría esta inglesita por todo el serrallo del Gran Turco, con sus ojos de gacela, sus formas de hurí y demás encantos!
The Eastern allusion bit me again.
Esta alusión oriental me hirió de nuevo.
"I'll not stand you an inch in the stead of a seraglio," I said; "so don't consider me an equivalent for one.
Dije: -No hablemos de serrallos.

If you have a fancy for anything in that line, away with you, sir, to the bazaars of Stamboul without delay, and lay out in extensive slave- purchases some of that spare cash you seem at a loss to spend satisfactorily here."
Si usted me considerase como equivalente de una de esas hermosas de los harenes y me tomara en tal sentido, haría mejor en ir a adquirir esclavas en los bazares de Estambul.
"And what will you do, Janet, while I am bargaining for so many tons of flesh and such an assortment of black eyes?"
-¿Y qué harías tú mientras tanto?
"I'll be preparing myself to go out as a missionary to preach liberty to them that are enslaved--your harem inmates amongst the rest.
-Me prepararía para ser misionera e iría a predicar la abolición de la esclavitud, incluyendo la de las esclavas de su harén.

I'll get admitted there, and I'll stir up mutiny; and you, three-tailed bashaw as you are, sir, shall in a trice find yourself fettered amongst our hands: nor will I, for one, consent to cut your bonds till you have signed a charter, the most liberal that despot ever yet conferred."

Me introduciría en él y las amotinaría. Caería usted en nuestras manos y, por muy vigoroso que usted sea, no saldría de ellas hasta que hubiera devuelto a sus mujeres su albedrío, otorgándoles una constitución tan liberal como jamás déspota alguno haya concedido.
"I would consent to be at your mercy, Jane."
-Me confiaría entonces a tu clemencia, Jane.

"I would have no mercy, Mr. Rochester, if you supplicated for it with an eye like that. While you looked so, I should be certain that whatever charter you might grant under coercion, your first act, when released, would be to violate its conditions."

-Yo no tendría clemencia para usted si me miraba como me mira ahora, porque estaría segura de que su primer acto sería violar las cláusulas de la Constitución que nos concediese, tan pronto como le dejásemos en libertad.
We were now approaching Thornfield.
Entretanto, habíamos llegado a Thornfield.
He said this as he helped me to alight from the carriage, and while he afterwards lifted out Adele, I entered the house, and made good my retreat upstairs.
Rochester me ayudó a apearme y, mientras bajaba a Adèle yo me apresuré a subir las escaleras.
He duly summoned me to his presence in the evening.
Cuando me invitó a reunirme con él aquella noche,
I had prepared an occupation for him; for I was determined not to spend the whole time in a _tete-a-tete_ conversation.
yo había resuelto que se ocupase en algo, porque no estaba dispuesta a pasar todo el tiempo en una conversación íntima téte-à-téte.
I remembered his fine voice; I knew he liked to sing--good singers generally do.
Recordaba la buena voz de Rochester y sabía que le gustaba cantar como a casi todos los que tienen una hermosa voz.
I was no vocalist myself, and, in his fastidious judgment, no musician, either; but I delighted in listening when the performance was good.
En cuanto a mí, aunque no fuese buena cantante -ni, según él, buena música-, me deleitaba oír cantar bien.
No sooner had twilight, that hour of romance, began to lower her blue and starry banner over the lattice, than I rose, opened the piano, and entreated him, for the love of heaven, to give me a song.
Así, tan pronto como el anochecer comenzó a desplegar su azul y estrellada bandera más allá de las ventanas, abrí el piano y rogué a Rochester que cantara en obsequio mío.
"Did I like his voice?" he asked.
-¿Te gusta mi voz? -preguntó.
"Very much."
-Mucho -repuse.
I was not fond of pampering that susceptible vanity of his; but for once, and from motives of expediency, I would e'en soothe and stimulate it.
No deseaba halagar su vanidad, pero por una vez y dado el caso de que se trataba, me pareció oportuno hacerlo.
"Then, Jane, you must play the accompaniment."
-Entonces, Jane, tendrás que acompañarme al piano.
"Very well, sir, I will try."
-Con mucho gusto.
I did try, but was presently swept off the stool and denominated "a little bungler."
Comencé, si bien casi en seguida fui arrojada del taburete sin ceremonias y calificada de chapucerilla.
Being pushed unceremoniously to one side--which was precisely what I wished--he usurped my place, and proceeded to accompany himself: for he could play as well as sing.
Él se sentó en mi lugar y comenzó a acompañar su melodía con la música. Tocaba tan bien como cantaba.
I hied me to the window-recess. And while I sat there and looked out on the still trees and dim lawn, to a sweet air was sung in mellow tones the following strain:--
Yo me senté junto a una ventana y, mientras miraba los árboles y el campo oscuro, le oí cantar la siguiente tonada:
"The truest love that ever heart Felt at its kindled core, Did through each vein, in quickened start, The tide of being pour.
El más verdadero amor que nadie ha jamás sentido inflama mi corazón y acelera sus latidos.
Her coming was my hope each day, Her parting was my pain; The chance that did her steps delay Was ice in every vein.
Soy feliz cuando la veo e infeliz cuando ha partido. Si tarda en llegar, inquieto, se hiela en mi sangre el ritmo.
I dreamed it would be nameless bliss, As I loved, loved to be; And to this object did I press As blind as eagerly.
Por la indecible ventura de verme correspondido, yo haría lo que no haría ningún otro ser nacido.
But wide as pathless was the space That lay our lives between, And dangerous as the foamy race Of ocean-surges green.

Por ese amor cruzaré los infinitos abismos que nos separan; del mar los hirvientes remolinos; como un salteador, yo me arrojaré al camino y atropellaré por todo lo que pueda desunirnos; obstáculos venceré; desafiaré peligros; con razón o sin razón, sin miedo a premio o castigo.
I dangers dared; I hindrance scorned; I omens did defy: Whatever menaced, harassed, warned, I passed impetuous by.
Pese a la saña y al odio de todos mis enemigos, alcanzaré el arco iris detrás del que peregrino.
On sped my rainbow, fast as light; I flew as in a dream; For glorious rose upon my sight That child of Shower and Gleam.
Combatiré contra todo, sin que humanos ni divinos logren oponer barreras al triunfo de mis designios.
Still bright on clouds of suffering dim Shines that soft, solemn joy; Nor care I now, how dense and grim Disasters gather nigh.
Hasta que de mi adorada los delicados deditos enlacen mi ruda mano con eslabones de lirios, mientras con un beso selle el juramento ofrecido de acompañarme si muero y acompañarme si vivo.
He rose and came towards me, and I saw his face all kindled, and his full falcon-eye flashing, and tenderness and passion in every lineament.
Se levantó y avanzó hacia mí. Vi en su rostro pintada tal emoción y en sus ojos relampaguear tan ardiente llama, que me sentí desasosegada por un momento.
I quailed momentarily--then I rallied.
Pero reaccioné.

Soft scene, daring demonstration, I would not have; and I stood in peril of both: a weapon of defence must be prepared--I whetted my tongue: as he reached me, I asked with asperity, "whom he was going to marry now?"
Eran de temer peligrosas escenas de ternura y debía precaverme contra ellas. Así, al acercarse, le pregunté con aspereza que con quién pensaba casarse ahora.
"That was a strange question to be put by his darling Jane."
-¡Vaya una pregunta que me haces, Jane!
"Indeed!
-Nada de eso.
I considered it a very natural and necessary one: he had talked of his future wife dying with him.
Es muy natural. ¿No ha hablado de que su futura esposa le acompañe si muere?
What did he mean by such a pagan idea? _I_ had no intention of dying with him--he might depend on that."
No tengo propósito alguno de llevar a la práctica esa idea pagana de morir con usted.
"Oh, all he longed, all he prayed for, was that I might live with him! Death was not for such as I."
-Desde luego: me basta con que me acompañes en la vida.
"Indeed it was: I had as good a right to die when my time came as he had: but I should bide that time, and not be hurried away in a suttee."
La muerte no se ha hecho para un ser como tú. -Sí se ha hecho, pero cuando llegue mi hora y no antes.
"Would I forgive him for the selfish idea, and prove my pardon by a reconciling kiss?"
-Bien: ¿me perdonas ese egoísta pensamiento y me demuestras tu perdón besándome?
"No: I would rather be excused."
-Prefiero no hacerlo.
Here I heard myself apostrophised as a "hard little thing;" and it was added, "any other woman would have been melted to marrow at hearing such stanzas crooned in her praise."
Me apostrofó, acusándome de ser más dura que una piedra y afirmó que «cualquier otra mujer se hubiera emocionado profundamente escuchando aquellos versos entonados en alabanza suya.»

I assured him I was naturally hard--very flinty, and that he would often find me so; and that, moreover, I was determined to show him divers rugged points in my character before the ensuing four weeks elapsed: he should know fully what sort of a bargain he had made, while there was yet time to rescind it.

Le aseguré que mi carácter era duro como el pedernal y que estaba dispuesta a mostrarle todos los aspectos malos de mi modo de ser durante las próximas cuatro semanas, a fin de que supiese qué clase de compromiso iba a contraer mientras estuviese aún a tiempo de rescindirlo.
"Would I be quiet and talk rationally?"
-¿Quieres callarte o hablar con sentido común?
"I would be quiet if he liked, and as to talking rationally, I flattered myself I was doing that now."
-Me callaré, si quiere, pero en cuanto a hablar con sentido común, perdone que le diga que eso es lo que estaba haciendo ahora.
He fretted, pished, and pshawed.
Se irritó, bramó y pateó, pero yo me mantuve inflexible.
"Very good," I thought; "you may fume and fidget as you please: but this is the best plan to pursue with you, I am certain.
«Haz lo que te parezca -pensaba-, porque estoy segura de que este sistema es el mejor que puedo seguir contigo.

I like you more than I can say; but I'll not sink into a bathos of sentiment: and with this needle of repartee I'll keep you from the edge of the gulf too; and, moreover, maintain by its pungent aid that distance between you and myself most conducive to our real mutual advantage."

Te quiero más de lo que te imaginas, pero no deseo caer en las complicaciones que produce no refrenar el sentimiento. Cuanto mayor distancia exista ahora entre tú y yo, mejor será después para ambos.»

From less to more, I worked him up to considerable irritation; then, after he had retired, in dudgeon, quite to the other end of the room, I got up, and saying, "I wish you good-night, sir," in my natural and wonted respectful manner, I slipped out by the side-door and got away.
Cada vez más irritado, Rochester se retiró á un rincón del cuarto. Yo entonces me levanté tranquilamente, dije con la expresión respetuosa habitual en mí: «Buenas noches, señor», y salí.
The system thus entered on, I pursued during the whole season of probation; and with the best success.
Perseveré durante todo el tiempo que faltaba en la actitud adoptada, con excelentes resultados.

He was kept, to be sure, rather cross and crusty; but on the whole I could see he was excellently entertained, and that a lamb-like submission and turtle-dove sensibility, while fostering his despotism more, would have pleased his judgment, satisfied his common-sense, and even suited his taste less.
Porque, si bien mi sistema contrariaba el despotismo y los arranques de Rochester, por otro lado concordaba con su razón, su sentido común y, en el fondo, creo que hasta con sus gustos.
In other people's presence I was, as formerly, deferential and quiet; any other line of conduct being uncalled for: it was only in the evening conferences I thus thwarted and afflicted him.
En presencia de extraños yo me manifestaba, como antes, deferente e impasible, y sólo en nuestras veladas a solas me permitía contrariarle y zaherirle.

He continued to send for me punctually the moment the clock struck seven; though when I appeared before him now, he had no such honeyed terms as "love" and "darling" on his lips: the best words at my service were "provoking puppet," "malicious elf," "sprite," "changeling," &c.

Cada tarde, a las siete en punto, enviaba a por mí y, cuando yo me presentaba, las dulces frases de «amor mío», «querida» y otras análogas estaban ausentes de sus labios. Las mejores que me dedicaba eran «muñeca deslenguada», «espíritu maligno», «bruja», «veleta», etc.
For caresses, too, I now got grimaces; for a pressure of the hand, a pinch on the arm; for a kiss on the cheek, a severe tweak of the ear.
En vez de caricias, me hacía muecas; en vez de apretarme la mano, me daba pellizcos; en vez de besarme, me aplicaba severos tirones de orejas.
It was all right: at present I decidedly preferred these fierce favours to anything more tender.
Pero yo prefería estas muestras de afecto a otras más íntimas.
Mrs. Fairfax, I saw, approved me: her anxiety on my account vanished; therefore I was certain I did well.
Noté que Mrs. Fairfax aprobaba mi actitud y que sus temores se desvanecían.
Meantime, Mr. Rochester affirmed I was wearing him to skin and bone, and threatened awful vengeance for my present conduct at some period fast coming.
Rochester afirmaba que yo le estaba quemando la sangre y me amenazaba con fieras venganzas en lo futuro.
I laughed in my sleeve at his menaces.
Pero me reía de sus amenazas, creía obrar con acierto y pensaba que después sabría obrar lo mismo, ya que si el procedimiento de ahora no resultaba adecuado después, otro se encontraría.
"I can keep you in reasonable check now," I reflected; "and I don't doubt to be able to do it hereafter: if one expedient loses its virtue, another must be devised."
Mi tarea, sin embargo, no era fácil. Muchas veces hubiese preferido complacer a Rochester en vez de atormentarle.
Yet after all my task was not an easy one; often I would rather have pleased than teased him.
Mi futuro esposo se había convertido para mí en la única cosa importante de este mundo, y creo que aun del otro.

My future husband was becoming to me my whole world; and more than the world: almost my hope of heaven. He stood between me and every thought of religion, as an eclipse intervenes between man and the broad sun.
Él se había interpuesto entre mis sentimientos religiosos y yo como un eclipse se interpone entre el Sol y la Tierra.
I could not, in those days, see God for His creature: of whom I had made an idol.
En aquella época, el hombre de quien había hecho un ídolo me impedía ver otra cosa que no fuera él.
The month of courtship had wasted: its very last hours were being numbered.
Los últimos momentos del mes estipulado estaban a punto de expirar.

There was no putting off the day that advanced--the bridal day; and all preparations for its arrival were complete. _I_, at least, had nothing more to do: there were my trunks, packed, locked, corded, ranged in a row along the wall of my little chamber; to-morrow, at this time, they would be far on their road to London: and so should I (D.V.),--or rather, not I, but one Jane Rochester, a person whom as yet I knew not.
Mis equipajes estaban listos, atados, dispuestos para ser enviados a Londres al siguiente día. También entonces debía salir yo, o mejor dicho, Jane Rochester, una persona a quien no conocía aún.
Mr. Rochester had himself written the direction, "Mrs. Rochester, --- Hotel, London," on each: I could not persuade myself to affix them, or to have them affixed.
El propio Edward había escrito las etiquetas de mis equipajes. «Mrs.
Mrs. Rochester!
¡Mrs. Rochester!

She did not exist: she would not be born till to-morrow, some time after eight o'clock a.m.; and I would wait to be assured she had come into the world alive before I assigned to her all that property.
Semejante ser no comenzaría a existir hasta la mañana siguiente, poco después de las ocho, y me parecía mejor esperar a que naciese para asignarle con entera propiedad aquellos objetos.

It was enough that in yonder closet, opposite my dressing-table, garments said to be hers had already displaced my black stuff Lowood frock and straw bonnet: for not to me appertained that suit of wedding raiment; the pearl-coloured robe, the vapoury veil pendent from the usurped portmanteau.

Entretanto, no podía concebir que me perteneciesen las prendas que sustituirían mi negro vestido y mi sombrero lowoodianos: el traje de boda, el vestido color perla, el vaporoso velo que se hallaban colocados en el guardarropa que había en mi dormitorio.
I shut the closet to conceal the strange, wraith-like apparel it contained; which, at this evening hour--nine o'clock--gave out certainly a most ghostly shimmer through the shadow of my apartment.

«Os dejo solos», murmuré al cerrar el guardarropa para evitar la extraña apariencia, casi fantasmal, que a aquella hora, nueve de la noche, ofrecían los ropajes blancos entre las sombras de la habitación.
"I am feverish: I hear the wind blowing: I will go out of doors and feel it."
Tenía fiebre; fuera soplaba el viento y quería aspirar el aire puro.

It was not only the hurry of preparation that made me feverish; not only the anticipation of the great change--the new life which was to commence to-morrow: both these circumstances had their share, doubtless, in producing that restless, excited mood which hurried me forth at this late hour into the darkening grounds: but a third cause influenced my mind more than they.
No eran sólo el ajetreo de los preparativos ni la espera del gran cambio que iba a producirse en mi vida lo que me hacía sentirme febril.
I had at heart a strange and anxious thought. Something had happened which I could not comprehend; no one knew of or had seen the event but myself: it had taken place the preceding night.
Existía para ello una tercera causa que nadie sino yo conocía, y que había sucedido la noche antes.

Mr. Rochester that night was absent from home; nor was he yet returned: business had called him to a small estate of two or three farms he possessed thirty miles off--business it was requisite he should settle in person, previous to his meditated departure from England.
Mr. Rochester se hallaba en unas propiedades situadas a una distancia de treinta millas, donde fue a arreglar ciertos asuntos antes de su viaje.
I waited now his return; eager to disburthen my mind, and to seek of him the solution of the enigma that perplexed me.
Y yo, al presente, esperaba su regreso, confiando encontrar en él la solución del enigma que me inquietaba.
I sought the orchard, driven to its shelter by the wind, which all day had blown strong and full from the south, without, however, bringing a speck of rain.
Bajé al huerto. Todo el día había soplado viento del Sur, trayendo, de vez en cuando, algunos ramalazos de lluvia.

Instead of subsiding as night drew on, it seemed to augment its rush and deepen its roar: the trees blew steadfastly one way, never writhing round, and scarcely tossing back their boughs once in an hour; so continuous was the strain bending their branchy heads northward--the clouds drifted from pole to pole, fast following, mass on mass: no glimpse of blue sky had been visible that July day.
Las nubes cubrían el cielo en masas compactas, sin que un solo trocito de cielo azul hubiese brillado durante todo aquel día de julio.
It was not without a certain wild pleasure I ran before the wind, delivering my trouble of mind to the measureless air-torrent thundering through space.
Experimenté cierto violento placer sintiendo el azote del aire que refrescaba mi turbada mente.
Descending the laurel walk, I faced the wreck of the chestnut-tree; it stood up black and riven: the trunk, split down the centre, gasped ghastly.
Por el camino bordeado de laureles, llegué hasta el gran castaño medio destrozado por el rayo.

"I think, scathed as you look, and charred and scorched, there must be a little sense of life in you yet, rising out of that adhesion at the faithful, honest roots: you will never have green leaves more--never more see birds making nests and singing idyls in your boughs; the time of pleasure and love is over with you: but you are not desolate: each of you has a comrade to sympathise with him in his decay."
En aquel momento, una luna color de sangre apareció momentáneamente entre las nubes para volver a ocultarse tras ellas después.
The wind fell, for a second, round Thornfield; but far away over wood and water, poured a wild, melancholy wail: it was sad to listen to, and I ran off again.
Por un segundo, el viento pareció quedar inmóvil en torno a Thornfield. Luego volvió a soplar con fuerza.

Here and there I strayed through the orchard, gathered up the apples with which the grass round the tree roots was thickly strewn; then I employed myself in dividing the ripe from the unripe; I carried them into the house and put them away in the store-room.
La hierba, en torno a los manzanos, estaba cubierta de manzanas caídas. Comencé a recogerlas, separando las verdes de las maduras.

Then I repaired to the library to ascertain whether the fire was lit, for, though summer, I knew on such a gloomy evening Mr. Rochester would like to see a cheerful hearth when he came in: yes, the fire had been kindled some time, and burnt well.

Llevé éstas a la casa y las coloqué en la despensa, de donde fui a la biblioteca para asegurarme de que el fuego estaba encendido. Aunque era verano, sabía que, dado lo sombrío del tiempo, a Rochester le agradaría encontrar una buena lumbre.
I placed his arm-chair by the chimney-corner: I wheeled the table near it: I let down the curtain, and had the candles brought in ready for lighting.
Acerqué su sillón a la chimenea y la mesa al sillón y coloqué en ella las bujías.

More restless than ever, when I had completed these arrangements I could not sit still, nor even remain in the house: a little time-piece in the room and the old clock in the hall simultaneously struck ten.

Una vez hechos aquellos preparativos, no sabía si salir o quedarme en casa, porque me sentía muy inquieta. Un pequeño reloj que había en el aposento y el viejo reloj del vestíbulo dieron simultáneamente las diez.
"How late it grows!"
«¡Qué tarde es! -pensé-.
I said. "I will run down to the gates: it is moonlight at intervals; I can see a good way on the road.
Voy a acercarme hasta las verjas. La luna sale a ratos y puedo otear el camino.
He may be coming now, and to meet him will save some minutes of suspense."
Si me reúno con Edward en cuanto lo vea, evitaré algunos minutos de espera.»

The wind roared high in the great trees which embowered the gates; but the road as far as I could see, to the right hand and the left, was all still and solitary: save for the shadows of clouds crossing it at intervals as the moon looked out, it was but a long pale line, unvaried by one moving speck.
El camino, a izquierda y derecha, en cuanto alcanzaba la vista, estaba solitario. Sólo se veían sobre él, a intervalos, las pálidas sombras de las nubes cuando, por unos segundos, brillaba la luna.
A puerile tear dimmed my eye while I looked--a tear of disappointment and impatience; ashamed of it, I wiped it away.
Una lágrima pueril, lágrima de impaciencia y disgusto, acudió a mis ojos.
I lingered; the moon shut herself wholly within her chamber, and drew close her curtain of dense cloud: the night grew dark; rain came driving fast on the gale.
La luna parecía haberse encerrado herméticamente en su celeste estancia, porque no había vuelto a aparecer. La noche se hacía cada vez más oscura y la lluvia iba en aumento.
"I wish he would come! I wish he would come!" I exclaimed, seized with hypochondriac foreboding.
«¡Quiero que venga, quiero que venga!», deseé con un ansia casi histérica.
I had expected his arrival before tea; now it was dark: what could keep him?
Le esperaba antes del té y era ya noche cerrada.
Had an accident happened?
¿Le había sucedido algún accidente?
The event of last night again recurred to me.
Recordé el suceso de la noche anterior y lo interpreté como un presagio de desventura.

I interpreted it as a warning of disaster. I feared my hopes were too bright to be realised; and I had enjoyed so much bliss lately that I imagined my fortune had passed its meridian, and must now decline.

Presentía que mis esperanzas eran demasiado hermosas para que se realizasen y hasta pensé que había sido tan dichosa últimamente que mi fortuna, después de llegar a su cenit, debía comenzar indefectiblemente a declinar.
"Well, I cannot return to the house," I thought; "I cannot sit by the fireside, while he is abroad in inclement weather: better tire my limbs than strain my heart; I will go forward and meet him."
«No puedo volver a casa -reflexioné- y estar al lado del fuego, mientras él soporta fuera la inclemencia de la noche. Prefiero tener los miembros fatigados antes que el corazón oprimido.
I set out; I walked fast, but not far: ere I had measured a quarter of a mile, I heard the tramp of hoofs; a horseman came on, full gallop; a dog ran by his side.
No había recorrido aún un cuarto de milla cuando sentí ruido de cascos. Un caballo, seguido por un perro, llegaba a todo galope.
Away with evil presentiment!
¡Enhoramala todos los presentimientos!
It was he: here he was, mounted on Mesrour, followed by Pilot.
Allí estaba él, montado en Mesrour y acompañado por Piloto.
He saw me; for the moon had opened a blue field in the sky, and rode in it watery bright: he took his hat off, and waved it round his head.
Me vio a la luz de la luna que había salido otra vez, se quitó el sombrero y lo agitó en torno a su cabeza.
I now ran to meet him.
Corrí a reunirme con él.
"There!" he exclaimed, as he stretched out his hand and bent from the saddle: "You can't do without me, that is evident.
-¡Está visto que no puedes vivir sin mí! -exclamó-.
Step on my boot-toe; give me both hands: mount!"
Pon el pie sobre mi bota, dame las manos y ¡arriba!
I obeyed: joy made me agile: I sprang up before him.
Obedecí. La alegría me prestaba agilidad.
A hearty kissing I got for a welcome, and some boastful triumph, which I swallowed as well as I could.
Monté en la delantera del arzón. Un ardiente beso fue el saludo que cambiamos.
He checked himself in his exultation to demand, "But is there anything the matter, Janet, that you come to meet me at such an hour? Is there anything wrong?"
Él preguntó en seguida: -¿Qué pasa, Jane, para que hayas venido a buscarme a estas horas?
"No, but I thought you would never come.
-Creí que no llegaba usted nunca.
I could not bear to wait in the house for you, especially with this rain and wind."
Me era insoportable esperarle en casa con esta lluvia y este huracán. -Estás mojada como una sirena.
"Rain and wind, indeed!
Cúbrete con mi abrigo.
Yes, you are dripping like a mermaid; pull my cloak round you: but I think you are feverish, Jane: both your cheek and hand are burning hot.
Pero creo que tienes fiebre, Jane. Te arden las manos y las mejillas.
I ask again, is there anything the matter?"
Si ha pasado algo, dímelo. -Ahora no me pasa nada.
"Nothing now; I am neither afraid nor unhappy."
No tengo temor ni me siento infeliz.
"Then you have been both?"
-Entonces, ¿lo has sentido antes?
"Rather: but I'll tell you all about it by-and-bye, sir; and I daresay you will only laugh at me for my pains."
-Luego le explicaré. Seguramente se reirá de mí...
"I'll laugh at you heartily when to-morrow is past; till then I dare not: my prize is not certain.
-Mañana reiré todo lo que quieras. Antes no: no tengo aún segura mi presa...
This is you, who have been as slippery as an eel this last month, and as thorny as a briar-rose?
Me refiero a ti, que durante este mes último has sido para mí tan escurridiza como una anguila y más espinosa que una rosa silvestre.
I could not lay a finger anywhere but I was pricked; and now I seem to have gathered up a stray lamb in my arms.
No podía tocarte ni con un dedo sin que me pincharas. ¡Y ahora en cambio te tengo en mis brazos como una mansa cordera!
You wandered out of the fold to seek your shepherd, did you, Jane?"
¿Cómo es que has salido del redil para venir a buscar a tu pastor, Jane?
"I wanted you: but don't boast.
-Deseaba verle. Pero no cante victoria...
Here we are at Thornfield: now let me get down."
Ya estamos en Thornfield. Ayúdeme a apearme.
He landed me on the pavement.
Me puso en tierra.

As John took his horse, and he followed me into the hall, he told me to make haste and put something dry on, and then return to him in the library; and he stopped me, as I made for the staircase, to extort a promise that I would not be long: nor was I long; in five minutes I rejoined him.
John se llevó el caballo y él me siguió a la casa. Me indicó que fuese a cambiarme de ropa, lo que hice a toda prisa.
I found him at supper.
Cinco minutos después, volvía y le hallaba cenando.
"Take a seat and bear me company, Jane: please God, it is the last meal but one you will eat at Thornfield Hall for a long time."
-Siéntate y come conmigo, Jane. Es la última vez que comerás en Thornfield durante mucho tiempo.
I sat down near him, but told him I could not eat.
Me senté junto a él, pero no comí.
"Is it because you have the prospect of a journey before you, Jane? Is it the thoughts of going to London that takes away your appetite?"
-¿Acaso el pensamiento del largo viaje que hemos de hacer a Londres te quita el apetito?
"I cannot see my prospects clearly to-night, sir; and I hardly know what thoughts I have in my head.
-Hoy veo todas las cosas confusas y casi no sé ni lo que tengo en el cerebro.
Everything in life seems unreal."
Todo lo que me rodea me parece fantástico.
"Except me: I am substantial enough--touch me."
Yo soy absolutamente real. Tócame y lo verás.
"You, sir, are the most phantom-like of all: you are a mere dream."
-Usted me parece lo más fantástico de todo, casi una cosa soñada...
He had a rounded, muscular, and vigorous hand, as well as a long, strong arm.
Alargó su brazo musculoso, recio, lo puso ante mis ojos y dijo, riendo:
"Yes; though I touch it, it is a dream," said I, as I put it down from before my face.
-¿Es esto un sueño acaso? -Aunque sea tangible, es un sueño -dije-.
"Sir, have you finished supper?"
¿Ha terminado usted?
"Yes, Jane."
-Sí, Jane.
I rang the bell and ordered away the tray.
Toqué la campanilla y mandé quitar el servicio.
When we were again alone, I stirred the fire, and then took a low seat at my master's knee.
Cuando quedamos solos, aticé el fuego y luego me senté ante Rochester en un asiento bajo.
"It is near midnight," I said.
-Es casi medianoche -dije.
"Yes: but remember, Jane, you promised to wake with me the night before my wedding."
-Sí, Jane, pero recuerda que me prometiste velar conmigo la noche antes de mi boda.
"I did; and I will keep my promise, for an hour or two at least: I have no wish to go to bed."
-Y lo cumpliré, al menos por una hora o dos. No tengo ganas de acostarme.
"Are all your arrangements complete?"
-¿Tienes todas las cosas arregladas?
"All, sir."
-Todas.
"And on my part likewise," he returned, "I have settled everything; and we shall leave Thornfield to-morrow, within half-an-hour after our return from church."
-Por mi parte también -repuso él- y nos iremos de Thornfield mañana mismo, media hora después de volver de la iglesia.
"Very well, sir."
-Bueno...
"With what an extraordinary smile you uttered that word--'very well,' Jane!
-¡De qué modo tan raro lo has dicho!
What a bright spot of colour you have on each cheek! and how strangely your eyes glitter!
¡Cómo brillan tus mejillas y tus ojos!
Are you well?"
¿Te encuentras bien, Jane?
"I believe I am."
-Creo que sí.
"Believe!
-¡Crees!
What is the matter?
Vamos, dime qué te pasa.
Tell me what you feel."
-No sabría explicarme.
"I could not, sir: no words could tell you what I feel.
Quisiera que nunca se acabaran estos momentos.
I wish this present hour would never end: who knows with what fate the next may come charged?"
¿Quién sabe lo que nos reserva el destino?
"This is hypochondria, Jane.
-Todo eso son nervios, Jane.
You have been over-excited, or over-fatigued."
Estás sobreexcitada o acaso muy fatigada.
"Do you, sir, feel calm and happy?"
-¿Y usted se siente tranquilo y feliz?
"Calm?--no: but happy--to the heart's core."
-Feliz, sí; tranquilo, no.
I looked up at him to read the signs of bliss in his face: it was ardent and flushed.
Le miré, tratando de descubrir en su rostro la expresión de su dicha. Estaba arrebatado. -Vamos, confía en mí, Jane -continuó-.
"Give me your confidence, Jane," he said: "relieve your mind of any weight that oppresses it, by imparting it to me.
Alivia tu pecho confiándome el peso que lo oprime. ¿Qué temes?
What do you fear?--that I shall not prove a good husband?"
¿Sospechas que no voy a ser un buen esposo?
"It is the idea farthest from my thoughts."
-Nada más lejos de mis pensamientos.
"Are you apprehensive of the new sphere you are about to enter?--of the new life into which you are passing?"
-¿Te asustan los nuevos ambientes en que vas a vivir, la nueva existencia que vas a llevar?
"You puzzle me, Jane: your look and tone of sorrowful audacity perplex and pain me.
-Me asombras, Jane. Tu aspecto y tu acento me dejan perplejo y me entristecen.
I want an explanation."
Explícate.
"Then, sir, listen.
-Entonces, escuche.
You were from home last night?"
Usted no estuvo en casa la noche de ayer...
"I was: I know that; and you hinted a while ago at something which had happened in my absence:--nothing, probably, of consequence; but, in short, it has disturbed you. Let me hear it.
-Ya, ya sé que no estuve... Y adivino que ha sucedido algo en mi ausencia, y que me lo ocultas.
Mrs. Fairfax has said something, perhaps? or you have overheard the servants talk?--your sensitive self-respect has been wounded?"
Algo que te ha disgustado, aunque seguramente no tendrá importancia. ¿Te ha dicho algo Mrs.
"No, sir."
-No -repuse.
It struck twelve--I waited till the time-piece had concluded its silver chime, and the clock its hoarse, vibrating stroke, and then I proceeded.
Era medianoche. Esperé a que el argentino timbre del relojito del aposento y la pesada campana del gran reloj del vestíbulo hubiesen terminado de dar la hora, y continué-:

"All day yesterday I was very busy, and very happy in my ceaseless bustle; for I am not, as you seem to think, troubled by any haunting fears about the new sphere, et cetera: I think it a glorious thing to have the hope of living with you, because I love you.

Todo el día de ayer estuve muy ocupada arreglando mis cosas y sintiéndome feliz con esa ocupación, porque no estoy, como usted se figura, asustada de vivir en un nuevo ambiente, etcétera. Lo que pienso es en lo magnífico que ha de serme vivir con usted, porque le amo.

Yesterday I trusted well in Providence, and believed that events were working together for your good and mine: it was a fine day, if you recollect--the calmness of the air and sky forbade apprehensions respecting your safety or comfort on your journey.
Ayer yo creía en la Providencia y esperaba que todo se desenlazaría en bien de usted y mío. Hacía un día excelente y por ello no sentía inquietud alguna respecto a su viaje.
I walked a little while on the pavement after tea, thinking of you; and I beheld you in imagination so near me, I scarcely missed your actual presence.
Después de tomar el té, salí a pasear un poco ante la casa, y con tal intensidad pensaba en usted, que casi me parecía tenerle presente.
I wondered why moralists call this world a dreary wilderness: for me it blossomed like a rose.
Me asombraba de que los moralistas llamen a este mundo un valle de lágrimas, porque a mí me parecía un jardín de rosas.

Just at sunset, the air turned cold and the sky cloudy: I went in, Sophie called me upstairs to look at my wedding-dress, which they had just brought; and under it in the box I found your present--the veil which, in your princely extravagance, you sent for from London: resolved, I suppose, since I would not have jewels, to cheat me into accepting something as costly.

Sophie me llamó para que examinara mi vestido de boda, que acababa de traer en aquel momento. Encontré el velo que usted me regala y que, en su principesca extravagancia, ha hecho que me traigan de Londres, sin duda con objeto de chasquearme en mi propósito de no aceptar objetos costosos, como hice cuando me negué a aceptar las joyas.
I smiled as I unfolded it, and devised how I would tease you about your aristocratic tastes, and your efforts to masque your plebeian bride in the attributes of a peeress.
Sonreí al apreciar el empeño de usted en enmascarar a su humilde prometida con el disfraz de una gran señora.

I thought how I would carry down to you the square of unembroidered blond I had myself prepared as a covering for my low-born head, and ask if that was not good enough for a woman who could bring her husband neither fortune, beauty, nor connections.

Estaba meditando sobre el modo de presentarle el retazo de blonda sin bordar que había preparado para cubrir mi humilde cabeza el día de la boda, y proyectaba decirle que era bastante para una mujer que no le aporta ni fortuna, ni belleza, ni una alianza ilustre.

I saw plainly how you would look; and heard your impetuous republican answers, and your haughty disavowal of any necessity on your part to augment your wealth, or elevate your standing, by marrying either a purse or a coronet."
Imaginaba mentalmente las democráticas contestaciones de usted, y su perversa insistencia en afirmar que no necesitaba ni aumento de riqueza ni unirse a nadie que le dé el brillo de sus blasones...
"How well you read me, you witch!" interposed Mr. Rochester: "but what did you find in the veil besides its embroidery?
-¡Cómo adivinas mis pensamientos, brujilla! -interrumpió Rochester-. Pero ¿qué has hallado en ese velo, aparte de sus bordados?
Did you find poison, or a dagger, that you look so mournful now?"
¿Un puñal, un veneno? Porque, a juzgar por tu modo de...
"No, no, sir; besides the delicacy and richness of the fabric, I found nothing save Fairfax Rochester's pride; and that did not scare me, because I am used to the sight of the demon.
-No, no, no halle más que su riqueza y su delicada manufactura.
But, sir, as it grew dark, the wind rose: it blew yesterday evening, not as it blows now--wild and high--but 'with a sullen, moaning sound' far more eerie. I wished you were at home.
Pero entretanto oscurecía, arreciaba el viento y yo hubiera deseado que usted estuviese en casa.
I came into this room, and the sight of the empty chair and fireless hearth chilled me.
Vine a esta habitación y me impresionó el espectáculo de este sillón vacío y esta chimenea apagada.
For some time after I went to bed, I could not sleep--a sense of anxious excitement distressed me.
No podía dormir. Me sentía desasosegada y nerviosa.

The gale still rising, seemed to my ear to muffle a mournful under-sound; whether in the house or abroad I could not at first tell, but it recurred, doubtful yet doleful at every lull; at last I made out it must be some dog howling at a distance.
Creí oír de pronto, no sabía si dentro o fuera de la casa, un extraño sonido, algo triste y lúgubre, al parecer lejano.
I was glad when it ceased.
Cesó, al fin, con mucha satisfacción mía.
On sleeping, I continued in dreams the idea of a dark and gusty night. I continued also the wish to be with you, and experienced a strange, regretful consciousness of some barrier dividing us.
Al dormirme soñé que era de noche, una noche oscura, y que yo deseaba estar con usted, pero que entre ambos surgía una barrera que, no sé cómo, nos separaba.

During all my first sleep, I was following the windings of an unknown road; total obscurity environed me; rain pelted me; I was burdened with the charge of a little child: a very small creature, too young and feeble to walk, and which shivered in my cold arms, and wailed piteously in my ear.

Durante este primer sueño yo seguía un camino desconocido rodeada de una oscuridad absoluta. La lluvia me calaba y yo iba cargada con un niñito, demasiado pequeño para andar solo y cuyo llanto sonaba de un modo lastimero en mis oídos.

I thought, sir, that you were on the road a long way before me; and I strained every nerve to overtake you, and made effort on effort to utter your name and entreat you to stop--but my movements were fettered, and my voice still died away inarticulate; while you, I felt, withdrew farther and farther every moment."

Usted seguía aquel camino, muy lejos de mí, y yo me esforzaba en alcanzarle y en hacerle pararse a esperar tratando de pronunciar su nombre tan alto como podía. Pero mis movimientos y mi voz estaban como paralizados y experimentaba la impresión de que usted se alejaba más cada vez.
"And these dreams weigh on your spirits now, Jane, when I am close to you?
-¿De modo que era eso lo que tenías cuando te he encontrado? ¿Un mero sueño?
Little nervous subject!
¡Qué nerviosilla eres!
Forget visionary woe, and think only of real happiness!
Déjate de visiones y piensa en la felicidad real que nos aguarda.
You say you love me, Janet: yes--I will not forget that; and you cannot deny it. _Those_ words did not die inarticulate on your lips.
Vamos; dime que me quieres, Jane.
I heard them clear and soft: a thought too solemn perhaps, but sweet as music--
Esas palabras me suenan tan dulces como la música...
Do you love me, Jane?--repeat it."
¿Me amas, Jane?
"I do, sir--I do, with my whole heart."
-Sí; con todo mi corazón.
"Well," he said, after some minutes' silence, "it is strange; but that sentence has penetrated my breast painfully.
-Bien -dijo él, tras unos minutos de silencio-. Es raro, pero tus palabras me han producido una sensación casi dolorosa.
Why?
¿Por qué será?

I think because you said it with such an earnest, religious energy, and because your upward gaze at me now is the very sublime of faith, truth, and devotion: it is too much as if some spirit were near me.
Acaso por la afectuosa energía con que las has pronunciado, por la mirada de fe, de lealtad y de confianza que las acompañaba. Me ha parecido que había un espíritu junto a mí...

Look wicked, Jane: as you know well how to look: coin one of your wild, shy, provoking smiles; tell me you hate me--tease me, vex me; do anything but move me: I would rather be incensed than saddened."
Mientras me mires como me miras ahora, Jane, mientras sonrías como sabes sonreírme, aunque me digas que me odias, aunque me injuries y me atormentes, no podré renegar de ti, te amaré y...
"I will tease you and vex you to your heart's content, when I have finished my tale: but hear me to the end."
-Temo disgustarle al final de mi relato. Escúcheme. -Creí que ya me lo habías dicho todo.
"I thought, Jane, you had told me all. I thought I had found the source of your melancholy in a dream."
Pensaba que la causa de tu tristeza estaba en ese sueño.
I shook my head.
Moví la cabeza.
"What! is there more?
-¿Cómo? ¿Hay algo más?
But I will not believe it to be anything important. I warn you of incredulity beforehand.
Espero que no sea nada importante.
Go on."
Sigue.
The disquietude of his air, the somewhat apprehensive impatience of his manner, surprised me: but I proceeded.
La inquietud de su aspecto, cierta impaciencia de sus ademanes, me extrañaron. Continué:
"I dreamt another dream, sir: that Thornfield Hall was a dreary ruin, the retreat of bats and owls.
-Aún soñé otra cosa: que Thornfield estaba en ruinas y era guarida de búhos y murciélagos.
I thought that of all the stately front nothing remained but a shell-like wall, very high and very fragile-looking.
De toda la fachada sólo quedaba en pie un frágil lienzo de pared.
I wandered, on a moonlight night, through the grass- grown enclosure within: here I stumbled over a marble hearth, and there over a fallen fragment of cornice.
Yo erraba, a la luz de la luna, entre las ruinas en las que crecía la hierba, tropezando, ora con un trozo de mármol, ora con un caído fragmento de cornisa.
Wrapped up in a shawl, I still carried the unknown little child: I might not lay it down anywhere, however tired were my arms--however much its weight impeded my progress, I must retain it.
Seguía llevando al niñito desconocido, envuelto en un chal. Me era imposible ponerle en el suelo, y por mucho que su peso me fatigase, había de continuar llevándole.
I heard the gallop of a horse at a distance on the road; I was sure it was you; and you were departing for many years and for a distant country.
A lo lejos, en el camino, oía las pisadas de un caballo y estaba segura de que era el de usted, que partía para un lejano país, donde permanecería muchos años.

I climbed the thin wall with frantic perilous haste, eager to catch one glimpse of you from the top: the stones rolled from under my feet, the ivy branches I grasped gave way, the child clung round my neck in terror, and almost strangled me; at last I gained the summit.

Traté de escalar el muro a toda prisa, para poder verle desde arriba. Las piedras se desmoronaban bajo mis pies, la hiedra a que trataba de asirme cedía; el niño, abrazado a mi cuello y aterrorizado, casi me estrangulaba.
I saw you like a speck on a white track, lessening every moment.
Pero al fin llegué. Usted era ya un punto en la distancia y se alejaba por momentos.
The blast blew so strong I could not stand.
Soplaba un viento tan fuerte que no me podía sostener.

I sat down on the narrow ledge; I hushed the scared infant in my lap: you turned an angle of the road: I bent forward to take a last look; the wall crumbled; I was shaken; the child rolled from my knee, I lost my balance, fell, and woke."

Me senté en el estrecho borde del muro, colocando al niño sobre mi regazo. Usted dobló una curva del camino y, cuando yo le dirigía una última mirada, la pared se derrumbó, el niño cayó de mis rodillas, perdí el equilibrio y me desperté.
"Now, Jane, that is all."
-¿Eso es todo, Jane?
"All the preface, sir; the tale is yet to come.
-Todo el prólogo. Ahora falta el relato.
On waking, a gleam dazzled my eyes; I thought--Oh, it is daylight!
Al despertarme, una luz hirió mis ojos. Pensé que ya era de día.
But I was mistaken; it was only candlelight.
Pero no era más que el resplandor de una vela. Supuse que Sophie estaba en la alcoba.

Sophie, I supposed, had come in. There was a light in the dressing-table, and the door of the closet, where, before going to bed, I had hung my wedding-dress and veil, stood open; I heard a rustling there.
Alguien había dejado una bujía en la mesa, y el cuartito guardarropa, donde yo colocara mi velo y mi vestido de boda, se hallaba abierto.
I asked, 'Sophie, what are you doing?'
«¿Qué hace usted, Sophie?», pregunté.
No one answered; but a form emerged from the closet; it took the light, held it aloft, and surveyed the garments pendent from the portmanteau. 'Sophie!
Nadie contestó, pero una figura surgió del ropero, cogió la vela y empezó a examinar los vestidos.
Sophie!' I again cried: and still it was silent.
«¡Sophie!», volví a exclamar.
I had risen up in bed, I bent forward: first surprise, then bewilderment, came over me; and then my blood crept cold through my veins.
La figura seguía en silencio. Me incorporé en la cama, me incliné hacia delante y sentí que se me helaba la sangre en las venas.
Mr. Rochester, this was not Sophie, it was not Leah, it was not Mrs. Fairfax: it was not--no, I was sure of it, and am still--it was not even that strange woman, Grace Poole."
Porque aquella mujer no era ninguna de las que en esta casa conozco; no era Sophie, ni Leah, ni Mrs. Fairfax, ni siquiera -estoy segura de ello- Grace Poole.
"It must have been one of them," interrupted my master.
-Forzosamente había de ser una de ellas -interrumpió Rochester.
The shape standing before me had never crossed my eyes within the precincts of Thornfield Hall before; the height, the contour were new to me."
La mujer que yo tenía ante mí no ha cruzado jamás sus miradas con las mías desde que vivo en Thornfield. Todo en su aspecto era nuevo para mí.
"Describe it, Jane."
-Descríbemela, Jane.
"It seemed, sir, a woman, tall and large, with thick and dark hair hanging long down her back.
-Me pareció alta y corpulenta, con una negra cabellera cayéndole sobre la espalda.
I know not what dress she had on: it was white and straight; but whether gown, sheet, or shroud, I cannot tell."
No me fijé en cómo iba vestida; sólo sé que llevaba un traje blanco.
"Did you see her face?"
-¿Le viste la cara?
"Not at first.
-Primero no.
But presently she took my veil from its place; she held it up, gazed at it long, and then she threw it over her own head, and turned to the mirror.
Pero luego cogió el velo, lo examinó largamente, se lo puso y se miró el espejo.
At that moment I saw the reflection of the visage and features quite distinctly in the dark oblong glass."
Entonces distinguí su rostro en el cristal.
"And how were they?"
-¿Cómo era?
"Fearful and ghastly to me--oh, sir, I never saw a face like it!
-Me pareció horrible. Nunca he visto cara como aquella: una cara descolorida, espantosa.
It was a discoloured face--it was a savage face. I wish I could forget the roll of the red eyes and the fearful blackened inflation of the lineaments!"
Quisiera poder olvidar aquel desorbitado movimiento de sus ojos inyectados en sangre, y sus facciones hinchadas como si fuesen a estallar.
"Ghosts are usually pale, Jane."
-Los fantasmas son pálidos, por regla general.
"This, sir, was purple: the lips were swelled and dark; the brow furrowed: the black eyebrows widely raised over the bloodshot eyes.
-Pues éste no lo era. Tenía los labios protuberantes y amoratados, arrugado el entrecejo, los párpados muy abiertos sobre sus ojos enrojecidos.
Shall I tell you of what it reminded me?"
¿Sabe lo que me recordaba?
"You may."
-¿El qué?
"Of the foul German spectre--the Vampyre."
-La aparición de las leyendas germanas: el vampiro...
"Ah!--what did it do?"
-¡Ah! ¿Y qué hizo?
"Sir, it removed my veil from its gaunt head, rent it in two parts, and flinging both on the floor, trampled on them."
-Se quitó el velo de la cabeza, lo rasgó en dos, lo tiró al suelo y lo pisoteó.
"Afterwards?"
-¿Y luego?
"It drew aside the window-curtain and looked out; perhaps it saw dawn approaching, for, taking the candle, it retreated to the door.
-Descorrió las cortinas de la ventana y miró hacia fuera.
Just at my bedside, the figure stopped: the fiery eyes glared upon me--she thrust up her candle close to my face, and extinguished it under my eyes.
En seguida cogió la vela y se dirigió a la puerta. Se paró junto a mi lecho, apagó la bujía y se inclinó sobre mí.
I was aware her lurid visage flamed over mine, and I lost consciousness: for the second time in my life--only the second time--I became insensible from terror."
Tuve la sensación de que su rostro tocaba casi el mío y perdí el conocimiento. Es la segunda vez en mi vida -sólo la segunda- en que el terror me ha hecho desmayarme.
"Who was with you when you revived?"
-¿Y había alguien contigo cuando te recobraste?
"No one, sir, but the broad day.
-Nadie. Era de día ya.
I rose, bathed my head and face in water, drank a long draught; felt that though enfeebled I was not ill, and determined that to none but you would I impart this vision.
Sumergí la cabeza en agua, bebí, comprobé que, aunque débil, no me encontraba enferma y determiné no comunicar a nadie aquella visión.
Now, sir, tell me who and what that woman was?"
Ahora dígame: ¿quién es esa mujer?
"The creature of an over-stimulated brain; that is certain.
-Una creación de tu mente.
I must be careful of you, my treasure: nerves like yours were not made for rough handling."
Tienes que cuidarte. Eres demasiado nerviosa.
"Sir, depend on it, my nerves were not in fault; the thing was real: the transaction actually took place."
-No fue cosa de mis nervios. Todo lo que digo ocurrió en realidad.
"And your previous dreams, were they real too?
-¿También los sueños anteriores?
Is Thornfield Hall a ruin?
¿Acaso Thornfield Hall es una ruina?
Am I severed from you by insuperable obstacles?
¿Estoy separado de ti por insuperables obstáculos?
Am I leaving you without a tear--without a kiss--without a word?"
¿Te he abandonado sin una lágrima, sin un beso, sin una palabra?
"Not yet."
-Aún no.
"Am I about to do it?
-¿Y parezco inclinado a hacerlo?
Why, the day is already commenced which is to bind us indissolubly; and when we are once united, there shall be no recurrence of these mental terrors: I guarantee that."
Porque ya estamos en el día en que nos uniremos con un lazo indisoluble. Y una vez unidos, no se repetirán esas terroríficas alucinaciones, te lo aseguro...
"Mental terrors, sir!
-¡Alucinaciones!
I wish I could believe them to be only such: I wish it more now than ever; since even you cannot explain to me the mystery of that awful visitant."
¡Qué más quisiera yo que lo fuesen! Y lo desearía ahora más que nunca, en vista de que usted no puede aclararme la personalidad de esa para mí extraña visitante.
"And since I cannot do it, Jane, it must have been unreal."
-Puesto que no puedo decírtelo, es que no ha existido, esto es seguro.

"But, sir, when I said so to myself on rising this morning, and when I looked round the room to gather courage and comfort from the cheerful aspect of each familiar object in full daylight, there--on the carpet--I saw what gave the distinct lie to my hypothesis,--the veil, torn from top to bottom in two halves!"
-Cuando me he levantado esta mañana y he ido al ropero para asegurarme de que todo estaba en orden, he encontrado la prueba de que no había soñado: el velo, tirado en el suelo y partido en dos...
I felt Mr. Rochester start and shudder; he hastily flung his arms round me.
Rochester se estremeció. Me abrazó por la cintura, exclamando:
"Thank God!" he exclaimed, "that if anything malignant did come near you last night, it was only the veil that was harmed.
-¡Gracias a Dios que ese velo ha sido lo único que ha sufrido daño!
Oh, to think what might have happened!"
¡Oh, cuando pienso en lo que pudo haber sucedido!
He drew his breath short, and strained me so close to him, I could scarcely pant.
Me apretó con tal fuerza contra su pecho, que casi no me dejaba respirar.
After some minutes' silence, he continued, cheerily--
Continuó, tras una pausa:
"Now, Janet, I'll explain to you all about it.
-Te lo explicaré todo, Jane.
It was half dream, half reality.
Ha sido medio sueño y medio realidad.
A woman did, I doubt not, enter your room: and that woman was--must have been--Grace Poole.
Sin duda una mujer entró en tu cuarto. Y no fue -no pudo ser- otra que Grace Poole.
You call her a strange being yourself: from all you know, you have reason so to call her--what did she do to me? what to Mason?
Te parece un ser extraño, y no te falta razón, si consideramos lo que nos hizo a Mason y a mí.

In a state between sleeping and waking, you noticed her entrance and her actions; but feverish, almost delirious as you were, you ascribed to her a goblin appearance different from her own: the long dishevelled hair, the swelled black face, the exaggerated stature, were figments of imagination; results of nightmare: the spiteful tearing of the veil was real: and it is like her.

Sin duda encontrándote medio dormida y algo febril, la viste entrar y le atribuiste una forma fantástica distinta a la que tiene en realidad: el largo cabello desmelenado, la faz oscura e hinchada, la exagerada estatura. Todo ello son ficciones de pesadilla.
I see you would ask why I keep such a woman in my house: when we have been married a year and a day, I will tell you; but not now.
Ya veo que deseas preguntarme por qué conservo en mi casa a una persona así... Pues bien, te lo diré cuando llevemos casados un año y un día, pero no ahora
Are you satisfied, Jane?
¿Estas satisfecha, Jane?
Do you accept my solution of the mystery?"
¿Aceptas esta solución del misterio?

I reflected, and in truth it appeared to me the only possible one: satisfied I was not, but to please him I endeavoured to appear so--relieved, I certainly did feel; so I answered him with a contented smile.
No me sentía satisfecha, pero por complacerle traté de parecerlo. Le correspondí, pues, con una sonrisa de aquiescencia.
And now, as it was long past one, I prepared to leave him.
Y como era bastante más de la una, me dispuse a dejarle.
"Does not Sophie sleep with Adele in the nursery?" he asked, as I lit my candle.
-¿No duerme Sophie con Adèle? -me preguntó cuando cogí mi bujía.
"And there is room enough in Adele's little bed for you.
-En el cuarto de Adèle hay sitio suficiente para ti. Debes dormir allí esta noche, Jane.
You must share it with her to-night, Jane: it is no wonder that the incident you have related should make you nervous, and I would rather you did not sleep alone: promise me to go to the nursery."
No me extraña que el incidente que me has relatado te haya puesto nerviosa, y si pasas la noche sola no podrás dormir. Prométeme acostarte en la alcoba de Adèle.
"I shall be very glad to do so, sir."
-Lo haré con gusto.
"And fasten the door securely on the inside.
-Y cierra la puerta por dentro.
Wake Sophie when you go upstairs, under pretence of requesting her to rouse you in good time to- morrow; for you must be dressed and have finished breakfast before eight.
Despierta a Sophie cuando entres, con el pretexto de que te llame mañana temprano, para vestirte y desayunarte antes de las ocho.
And now, no more sombre thoughts: chase dull care away, Janet.
Y ahora basta de pensamientos sombríos. Olvida tus preocupaciones, Jane.
Don't you hear to what soft whispers the wind has fallen? and there is no more beating of rain against the window-panes: look here" (he lifted up the curtain)--"it is a lovely night!"
Tampoco la lluvia bate ya los cristales. Mira qué noche tan hermosa -concluyó, corriendo el visillo para que yo mirara.
It was.
Era cierto.
Half heaven was pure and stainless: the clouds, now trooping before the wind, which had shifted to the west, were filing off eastward in long, silvered columns.
La mitad del cielo estaba azul y límpido. Las nubes, impulsadas por el viento, desaparecían, formando grandes y argentadas masas, en el horizonte.
The moon shone peacefully.
La luna brillaba, serena.
"Well," said Mr. Rochester, gazing inquiringly into my eyes, "how is my Janet now?"
-¿Cómo se siente ahora mi Jane? -preguntó mirándome a los ojos.
"The night is serene, sir; and so am I."
-La noche es serena y yo también lo estoy.
"And you will not dream of separation and sorrow to-night; but of happy love and blissful union."
-Nada de soñar esta noche con terrores y pesadillas, sino con dulces sueños de amor y de felicidad.
This prediction was but half fulfilled: I did not indeed dream of sorrow, but as little did I dream of joy; for I never slept at all.
Su deseo se cumplió a medias, porque no tuve ni pesadillas ni sueños agradables, ya que no dormí nada.

With little Adele in my arms, I watched the slumber of childhood--so tranquil, so passionless, so innocent--and waited for the coming day: all my life was awake and astir in my frame: and as soon as the sun rose I rose too.
Con Adèle entre los brazos velé su sueño -e1 sueño tranquilo, despreocupado y puro de la infancia- y así esperé que alborease el día. En cuanto el sol salió, me levanté.

I remember Adele clung to me as I left her: I remember I kissed her as I loosened her little hands from my neck; and I cried over her with strange emotion, and quitted her because I feared my sobs would break her still sound repose.
Recuerdo cuando me separé de Adèle abrazada a mí, cómo separé sus bracitos de mi cuello y cómo lloré, mirándola, con emoción reprimida, para que mis sollozos no turbaran su sueño.
She seemed the emblem of my past life; and here I was now to array myself to meet, the dread, but adored, type of my unknown future day.
Ella simbolizaba para mí la vida pasada, como mi prometido, al que iba ahora a reunirme, simbolizaba mi ignorado porvenir, temido, pero adorado.
Sophie came at seven to dress me: she was very long indeed in accomplishing her task; so long that Mr. Rochester, grown, I suppose, impatient of my delay, sent up to ask why I did not come.
Sophie vino a las siete a vestirme, en lo que tardó bastante, hasta el punto de que Rochester, impaciente, sin duda, por mi tardanza, envió a preguntar el motivo de que yo no acudiera.
She was just fastening my veil (the plain square of blond after all) to my hair with a brooch; I hurried from under her hands as soon as I could.
En aquel momento ella estaba colocando sobre mi cabeza el velo -que al fin había tenido que ser mi liso velo de blonda- y sujetándolo con un broche. Me escapé de entre sus manos en cuanto pude.
"Stop!" she cried in French.
-¡Espere! -exclamó ella, en francés-.
"Look at yourself in the mirror: you have not taken one peep."
¡No se ha mirado aún al espejo!
So I turned at the door: I saw a robed and veiled figure, so unlike my usual self that it seemed almost the image of a stranger.
Me volví desde la puerta y vi en el cristal una figura tan distinta, con su velo y sus ropas, de la mía, que casi me pareció otra persona.
"Jane!" called a voice, and I hastened down.
-¡Jane! -gritó una voz. Bajé apresuradamente.
I was received at the foot of the stairs by Mr. Rochester.
Rochester me recibió al pie de la escaleras.
"Lingerer!" he said, "my brain is on fire with impatience, and you tarry so long!"
-Vamos -dijo-. Estoy ardiendo de impaciencia; ¡hay que ver lo que tardabas!

He took me into the dining-room, surveyed me keenly all over, pronounced me "fair as a lily, and not only the pride of his life, but the desire of his eyes," and then telling me he would give me but ten minutes to eat some breakfast, he rang the bell.
Me condujo al comedor, me examinó y dijo que yo era «tan bonita como un lirio, y no sólo el orgullo de su vida, sino el encanto de sus ojos».
One of his lately hired servants, a footman, answered it.
Luego agregó que me concedía diez minutos para desayunar y tocó la campanilla.
"Is John getting the carriage ready?"
-¿Ha enganchado John el coche?
"Is the luggage brought down?"
-¿Y el equipaje?
"They are bringing it down, sir."
-Están sacándolo.
"Go you to the church: see if Mr. Wood (the clergyman) and the clerk are there: return and tell me."
-Vaya a la iglesia, vea si está el Padre Wood y el sacristán y vuelva a decírmelo.
The church, as the reader knows, was but just beyond the gates; the footman soon returned.
Como no ignora el lector, la iglesia estaba muy cerca. El criado, pues, regresó enseguida.
"Mr. Wood is in the vestry, sir, putting on his surplice."
-El Padre Wood, señor, estaba poniéndose la sobrepelliz.
"And the carriage?"
-¿Y el coche?
"The horses are harnessing."
-Ya está.
"We shall not want it to go to church; but it must be ready the moment we return: all the boxes and luggage arranged and strapped on, and the coachman in his seat."
-No iremos en él a la iglesia, pero necesitamos que esté listo para cuando regresemos, con el equipaje colocado y el cochero en el pescante.
"Yes, sir."
-Bien, señor.
"Jane, are you ready?"
-¿Estás ya, Jane?
There were no groomsmen, no bridesmaids, no relatives to wait for or marshal: none but Mr. Rochester and I. Mrs. Fairfax stood in the hall as we passed.
Sólo Mrs. Fairfax estaba en el vestíbulo cuando pasamos.

I would fain have spoken to her, but my hand was held by a grasp of iron: I was hurried along by a stride I could hardly follow; and to look at Mr. Rochester's face was to feel that not a second of delay would be tolerated for any purpose.

Hubiera querido hablarla, pero una mano de hierro asió mi brazo y me vi obligada a caminar a un paso que apenas me era posible mantener. Una mirada al rostro de Rochester me indicó que él no quería perder ni un segundo.
I know not whether the day was fair or foul; in descending the drive, I gazed neither on sky nor earth: my heart was with my eyes; and both seemed migrated into Mr. Rochester's frame.
No sé si el día era bueno o malo, porque, mientras nos dirigíamos a la iglesia, yo no miraba ni la tierra ni el cielo.
I wanted to see the invisible thing on which, as we went along, he appeared to fasten a glance fierce and fell. I wanted to feel the thoughts whose force he seemed breasting and resisting.
Mi corazón estaba todo en mis ojos, y éstos contemplaban, estáticos, a Rochester, buscando en su apariencia la exteriorización de los sentimientos que parecía reprimir con dificultad.
At the churchyard wicket he stopped: he discovered I was quite out of breath.
Se paró ante la puerta del cementerio al notar que yo no podía ya ni respirar, y me dijo:
"Am I cruel in my love?" he said.
-Mi amor es un poco cruel...
"Delay an instant: lean on me, Jane."
Descansa un momento, Jane.
And now I can recall the picture of the grey old house of God rising calm before me, of a rook wheeling round the steeple, of a ruddy morning sky beyond.
Y entonces pude distinguir la parda y antigua casa de Dios alzándose ante mí. Una corneja volaba en torno al campanario bajo el cielo carmesí de la mañana.

I remember something, too, of the green grave-mounds; and I have not forgotten, either, two figures of strangers straying amongst the low hillocks and reading the mementoes graven on the few mossy head-stones.
Entre los verdes montículos de las tumbas vi las figuras de dos forasteros que se detenían entre ellas para leer los epitafios de sus lápidas.
I noticed them, because, as they saw us, they passed round to the back of the church; and I doubted not they were going to enter by the side-aisle door and witness the ceremony.
Noté que, al atisbarnos, desaparecieron detrás de la iglesia y no dudé de que iban a asistir a la ceremonia.
By Mr. Rochester they were not observed; he was earnestly looking at my face from which the blood had, I daresay, momentarily fled: for I felt my forehead dewy, and my cheeks and lips cold.
Pero Rochester no les observó, porque su mirada se concentraba en mi rostro, del que me parece que habían huido todos los colores. Yo tenía la frente húmeda y los labios fríos.
When I rallied, which I soon did, he walked gently with me up the path to the porch.
Cuando hube descansado, él me condujo lentamente hasta el pórtico.
We entered the quiet and humble temple; the priest waited in his white surplice at the lowly altar, the clerk beside him.
Entramos en el silencioso y humilde templo. El sacerdote, revestido con su blanca sobrepelliz, estaba ante el altar y el sacristán a su lado.
All was still: two shadows only moved in a remote corner.
No había nadie más, excepto dos sombras que se agitaban en un remoto rincón.

My conjecture had been correct: the strangers had slipped in before us, and they now stood by the vault of the Rochesters, their backs towards us, viewing through the rails the old time-stained marble tomb, where a kneeling angel guarded the remains of Damer de Rochester, slain at Marston Moor in the time of the civil wars, and of Elizabeth, his wife.

Mi suposición había sido acertada. Los dos desconocidos, entrando antes que nosotros, se hallaban dentro inclinados ahora sobre la cripta que guardaba los restos de los Rochester, y contemplando las tumbas de mármol en las que un ángel arrodillado custodiaba los restos de Damer de Rochester, muerto en Marston Moor durante las guerras civiles, y de Elizabeth, su mujer.
Our place was taken at the communion rails.
Nos arrodillamos ante la barandilla donde los fieles se posternaban para comulgar.
Hearing a cautious step behind me, I glanced over my shoulder: one of the strangers--a gentleman, evidently--was advancing up the chancel.
Oí un paso cauteloso a mis espaldas y, volviendo un poco el rostro, vi a uno de los dos forasteros, un caballero por las apariencias, que se aproximaba al presbiterio.
The service began.
Comenzó el servicio.
