The explanation of the intent of matrimony was gone through; and then the clergyman came a step further forward, and, bending slightly towards Mr. Rochester, went on.
Se hizo primero la manifestación de nuestro propósito de contraer matrimonio y después el sacerdote avanzó hacia nosotros y dijo:

"I require and charge you both (as ye will answer at the dreadful day of judgment, when the secrets of all hearts shall be disclosed), that if either of you know any impediment why ye may not lawfully be joined together in matrimony, ye do now confess it; for be ye well assured that so many as are coupled together otherwise than God's Word doth allow, are not joined together by God, neither is their matrimony lawful."

-Os pido que ambos declaréis (como si contestarais cuando, el Día del Juicio, los secretos de todos los corazones sean declarados íntegramente) si cualquiera de vosotros tiene o cree tener impedimentos de cualquier clase que os impidan uniros en matrimonio legal, porque, de existir, aunque os unierais, vuestro matrimonio no sería válido ante Dios ni, por tanto, legal.
He paused, as the custom is.
Calló, según costumbre.
When is the pause after that sentence ever broken by reply?
¿Hay acaso alguna ocasión en que ese silencio formulario sea roto?
Not, perhaps, once in a hundred years.
Quizá no suceda ni una vez en cien años.

And the clergyman, who had not lifted his eyes from his book, and had held his breath but for a moment, was proceeding: his hand was already stretched towards Mr. Rochester, as his lips unclosed to ask, "Wilt thou have this woman for thy wedded wife?"--when a distinct and near voice said--

El sacerdote, que no había separado los ojos de su libro, y que sólo se había interrumpido por un momento, iba a continuar. Ya su mano se dirigía a Rochester y sus labios se abrían para preguntarle si me tomaba por legítima esposa, cuando una voz clara y muy próxima dijo:
"The marriage cannot go on: I declare the existence of an impediment."
-Ese matrimonio no puede efectuarse. Afirmo que existe un impedimento.

The clergyman looked up at the speaker and stood mute; the clerk did the same; Mr. Rochester moved slightly, as if an earthquake had rolled under his feet: taking a firmer footing, and not turning his head or eyes, he said, "Proceed."
Rochester dio un salto, como si hubiera sentido temblar la tierra bajo sus pies. En seguida recuperó su serenidad y, sin volver la cabeza, dijo: -Continúe.
Profound silence fell when he had uttered that word, with deep but low intonation.
A su palabra, pronunciada en voz baja y clara, siguió un profundo silencio.
Presently Mr. Wood said--
El padre Wood repuso:
"I cannot proceed without some investigation into what has been asserted, and evidence of its truth or falsehood."
-No puedo continuar antes de que se investigue la certeza o falsedad de lo que acaba de asegurarse.
"The ceremony is quite broken off," subjoined the voice behind us.
No debe celebrarse la ceremonia -repitió la voz de antes-.
"I am in a condition to prove my allegation: an insuperable impediment to this marriage exists."
Puedo probar que existe un insuperable impedimento.
Mr. Rochester heard, but heeded not: he stood stubborn and rigid, making no movement but to possess himself of my hand.
Permanecía obstinado y rígido. Su mano asía la mía, y aquella mano ardiente parecía de hierro.
What a hot and strong grasp he had! and how like quarried marble was his pale, firm, massive front at this moment!
En cambio, su rostro cuadrado, su frente enérgica, estaban pálidos como el mármol.
How his eye shone, still watchful, and yet wild beneath!
Sus ojos brillaban, atentos, inmóviles y, sin embargo, con una expresión casi feroz.
Mr. Wood seemed at a loss. "What is the nature of the impediment?" he asked.
-¿De qué clase es ése impedimento? -preguntó el turbado padre Wood-.
"Perhaps it may be got over--explained away?"
Acaso sea hacedero eliminarlo...
"Hardly," was the answer.
-Difícilmente -dijo la voz de antes-.
"I have called it insuperable, and I speak advisedly."
He dicho que era insuperable y he hablado sabiendo lo que decía.
The speaker came forward and leaned on the rails. He continued, uttering each word distinctly, calmly, steadily, but not loudly--
El desconocido se acercó a la barandilla y siguió, con energía y claridad, pero sin alzar la voz:
"It simply consists in the existence of a previous marriage.
-El impedimento consiste en que Mr.
Mr. Rochester has a wife now living."
Rochester está casado y su mujer vive aún.

My nerves vibrated to those low-spoken words as they had never vibrated to thunder--my blood felt their subtle violence as it had never felt frost or fire; but I was collected, and in no danger of swooning.

Aquellas palabras, pronunciadas en voz baja, hicieron vibrar mis nervios cual si hubieran sonado fuertes como el trueno. Mi sangre sintió una impresión tal como el fuego o el hielo no hubieran sido capaces de producir.
I looked at Mr. Rochester: I made him look at me. His whole face was colourless rock: his eye was both spark and flint. He disavowed nothing: he seemed as if he would defy all things.
Miré a Rochester y él me miró: sus ojos permanecían fijos y duros, en actitud de desafiar al mundo entero.
Without speaking, without smiling, without seeming to recognise in me a human being, he only twined my waist with his arm and riveted me to his side.
Sin hablar, sin sonreír, sin indicio alguno de que me considerase como un ser viviente, ciñó mi talle con la mano y me atrajo hacia sí.
"Who are you?" he asked of the intruder.
-¿Quién es usted? -preguntó al intruso.
"My name is Briggs, a solicitor of --- Street, London."
-Me llamo Briggs, procurador de Londres.
"And you would thrust on me a wife?"
-¿Y asegura usted que soy casado?
"I would remind you of your lady's existence, sir, which the law recognises, if you do not."
-Puedo asegurar la existencia de su mujer. La ley lo reconocerá, si usted lo niega.
"Favour me with an account of her--with her name, her parentage, her place of abode."
-Hágame el favor de decirme su nombre, quiénes eran sus padres, dónde nació...
"Certainly."
-Con mucho gusto.
Mr. Briggs calmly took a paper from his pocket, and read out in a sort of official, nasal voice:--
El señor Briggs sacó un papel de su bolsillo y leyó con una voz nasal, protocolaria:

"'I affirm and can prove that on the 20th of October A.D. --- (a date of fifteen years back), Edward Fairfax Rochester, of Thornfield Hall, in the county of ---, and of Ferndean Manor, in ---shire, England, was married to my sister, Bertha Antoinetta Mason, daughter of Jonas Mason, merchant, and of Antoinetta his wife, a Creole, at --- church, Spanish Town, Jamaica.

-«Afirmo y puedo probar que el 20 de octubre de... (una fecha de quince años antes), Edward Fairfax Rochester, de Thornfield Hall, en el condado de... y de Ferndean Manor, en... (Inglaterra), casó con mi hermana Bertha Antoinette en Puerto España (Jamaica), en la iglesia de...
The record of the marriage will be found in the register of that church--a copy of it is now in my possession.
Poseo una copia del certificado de su partida de casamiento.
Signed, Richard Mason.'"
Firmado: Richard Mason.»
"That--if a genuine document--may prove I have been married, but it does not prove that the woman mentioned therein as my wife is still living."
-Aun suponiendo que se tratara de un documento auténtico eso probaría que he estado casado, pero no que mi mujer viva aún.
"She was living three months ago," returned the lawyer.
-Vivía hace tres meses -replicó el procurador.
"How do you know?"
-¿Cómo lo sabe?
"I have a witness to the fact, whose testimony even you, sir, will scarcely controvert."
-Tengo un testigo del hecho.
"Produce him--or go to hell."
-Preséntelo o váyase al infierno, si no...
"I will produce him first--he is on the spot.
-Prefiero presentarlo. Está aquí Mr.
Mr. Mason, have the goodness to step forward."
Mason: tenga la bondad.

Mr. Rochester, on hearing the name, set his teeth; he experienced, too, a sort of strong convulsive quiver; near to him as I was, I felt the spasmodic movement of fury or despair run through his frame. The second stranger, who had hitherto lingered in the background, now drew near; a pale face looked over the solicitor's shoulder--yes, it was Mason himself.

Rochester, al oír tal nombre, rechinó los dientes y experimentó un estremecimiento convulsivo El otro forastero, que hasta entonces permaneciera retirado, avanzó y la pálida faz de Mason en persona apareció sobre el hombro del procurador.
Mr. Rochester turned and glared at him.
Rochester se volvió y le miró.

His eye, as I have often said, was a black eye: it had now a tawny, nay, a bloody light in its gloom; and his face flushed--olive cheek and hueless forehead received a glow as from spreading, ascending heart-fire: and he stirred, lifted his strong arm--he could have struck Mason, dashed him on the church-floor, shocked by ruthless blow the breath from his body--but Mason shrank away, and cried faintly, "Good God!"
Una sombría luz brilló en sus ojos, la sangre afluyó a sus morenas mejillas y su fuerte brazo se distendió. Hubiera podido aplastar a Mason, de un golpe, sin duda.
Contempt fell cool on Mr. Rochester--his passion died as if a blight had shrivelled it up: he only asked--"What have _you_ to say?"
Limitóse a preguntarle: -¿Qué tienes que decir?
An inaudible reply escaped Mason's white lips.
De los pálidos labios de Mason escapó una réplica inaudible.
"The devil is in it if you cannot answer distinctly.
-El diablo te lleve si no contestas con más claridad.
I again demand, what have you to say?"
¿Qué tienes que decir, repito?
"Sir--sir," interrupted the clergyman, "do not forget you are in a sacred place."
-Señor -interrumpió el sacerdote-, no olvide que está usted en un sitio sagrado
Then addressing Mason, he inquired gently, "Are you aware, sir, whether or not this gentleman's wife is still living?"
-y dirigiéndose a Mason le preguntó con amabilidad-: ¿Le consta a usted que la esposa de este caballero vive realmente?
"Courage," urged the lawyer,--"speak out."
-¡Ánimo! -intervino el procurador-.
"She is now living at Thornfield Hall," said Mason, in more articulate tones: "I saw her there last April.
Hable. -Vive en Thornfield Hall -dijo Mason, más claramente-. La vi en abril pasado.
I am her brother."
Soy su hermano.
"At Thornfield Hall!" ejaculated the clergyman.
-¡En Thornfield Hall! -exclamó el sacerdote-.
"Impossible!
Es imposible.
I am an old resident in this neighbourhood, sir, and I never heard of a Mrs. Rochester at Thornfield Hall."
Hace mucho que habito en la vecindad y jamás he oído hablar de ninguna Mrs. Rochester en esa casa.
I saw a grim smile contort Mr. Rochester's lips, and he muttered--
Una horrible sonrisa contrajo la boca de Rochester al contestar:
"No, by God! I took care that none should hear of it--or of her under that name."
-Ya me preocupé bastante de que nadie supiera nada de ella, al menos como mi mujer.
He mused--for ten minutes he held counsel with himself: he formed his resolve, and announced it-- "Enough! all shall bolt out at once, like the bullet from the barrel.
Calló, reflexionó durante unos minutos y, al fin, como si hubiese adoptado una resolución, habló: -Basta, acabemos de una vez.
Wood, close your book and take off your surplice; John Green (to the clerk), leave the church: there will be no wedding to-day."
Wood, cierre el libro y quítese la sobrepelliz. Usted, John Green -se dirigía al sacristán-, puede irse.
The man obeyed.
El hombre obedeció.
Mr. Rochester continued, hardily and recklessly: "Bigamy is an ugly word!--I meant, however, to be a bigamist; but fate has out-manoeuvred me, or Providence has checked me,--perhaps the last.
Rochester siguió diciendo: -Ciertamente, la palabra bigamia suena muy mal. Sin embargo, yo iba a convertirme en bígamo, de no habérmelo impedido el destino o la Providencia.
I am little better than a devil at this moment; and, as my pastor there would tell me, deserve no doubt the sternest judgments of God, even to the quenchless fire and deathless worm.
Quizá esta última... Reconozco que he obrado diabólicamente...
Gentlemen, my plan is broken up:--what this lawyer and his client say is true: I have been married, and the woman to whom I was married lives!
Lo que este procurador y su cliente aseguran es verdad. Estoy casado y mi mujer vive aún.
You say you never heard of a Mrs. Rochester at the house up yonder, Wood; but I daresay you have many a time inclined your ear to gossip about the mysterious lunatic kept there under watch and ward.
Es verdad que usted no ha oído hablar de mi mujer, Wood, pero sí le habrán mencionado una loca que albergo en mi casa.
Some have whispered to you that she is my bastard half-sister: some, my cast-off mistress.
Algunos le dirían que se trata de una hermana bastarda, otros le afirmarán que es una antigua amante.

I now inform you that she is my wife, whom I married fifteen years ago,--Bertha Mason by name; sister of this resolute personage, who is now, with his quivering limbs and white cheeks, showing you what a stout heart men may bear.

Pero declaro ahora que es mi mujer, con la que me casé hace quince años. Se llama Bertha Mason y es hermana de este atrevido personaje, que con su temblor y su palidez les demuestra lo que un bravo corazón masculino es capaz de afrontar.
Cheer up, Dick!--never fear me!--I'd almost as soon strike a woman as you.
Tranquilízate, Dick, no temas; no te pegaré. ¡Casi sería capaz de pegar a una mujer antes que a ti!
Bertha Mason is mad; and she came of a mad family; idiots and maniacs through three generations!
Bertha Mason está loca y desciende de una familia cuyos miembros han sido locos o maniáticos a lo largo de tres generaciones.
Her mother, the Creole, was both a madwoman and a drunkard!--as I found out after I had wed the daughter: for they were silent on family secrets before.
La madre de mi mujer estaba loca y alcohólica. Lo supe después de casado, porque, desde luego, me ocultaron antes tales secretos de familia.
Bertha, like a dutiful child, copied her parent in both points.
Bertha, como buena hija, imitaba a su genitora en ambos aspectos.
I had a charming partner--pure, wise, modest: you can fancy I was a happy man. I went through rich scenes!
Tuve una encantadora compañera. ¡No pueden imaginarse lo admirable que era y lo feliz que fui yo con aquella mujer pura, prudente y modesta... !
Oh! my experience has been heavenly, if you only knew it!
¡Oh, qué escenas hubo entre nosotros! ¡Una cosa celestial!
But I owe you no further explanation.
Pero sobra entrar en más explicaciones.
Briggs, Wood, Mason, I invite you all to come up to the house and visit Mrs. Poole's patient, and _my wife_!
Briggs, Wood, Mason: les invito a venir a mi casa a conocer a la paciente de Grace Poole y esposa mía.
You shall see what sort of a being I was cheated into espousing, and judge whether or not I had a right to break the compact, and seek sympathy with something at least human.
Así verán ustedes con qué clase de ser me casé y si tengo o no derecho a romper el pacto matrimonial y buscar consuelo en un ser que ni siquiera pueda llamarse humano.

This girl," he continued, looking at me, "knew no more than you, Wood, of the disgusting secret: she thought all was fair and legal and never dreamt she was going to be entrapped into a feigned union with a defrauded wretch, already bound to a bad, mad, and embruted partner!

Esta muchacha, Wood -agregó, mirándome-, no conocía el secreto más que usted mismo, y creía que todo era limpio y legal. Jamás pudo ocurrírsele que iba a unirse a un hombre ligado a una compañera malvada, loca y embrutecida.
Come all of you--follow!"
¡Ea, óiganme!
Still holding me fast, he left the church: the three gentlemen came after.
Salió de la iglesia arrastrándome consigo. Los tres hombres nos seguían.
At the front door of the hall we found the carriage.
Ante la casa encontramos el coche.
"Take it back to the coach-house, John," said Mr. Rochester coolly; "it will not be wanted to-day."
-Llévelo a la cochera, John -dijo fríamente Rochester-. Hoy no nos hace falta.
At our entrance, Mrs. Fairfax, Adele, Sophie, Leah, advanced to meet and greet us.
Al entrar, Mr. Fairfax, Adèle, Sophie y Leah avanzaron a nuestro encuentro.
"To the right-about--every soul!" cried the master; "away with your congratulations!
-¡Alto! -gritó Rochester-. Nada de felicitaciones.
Who wants them?
¿Para qué las quiero?
Not I!--they are fifteen years too late!"
¡Llegan con quince años de retraso!
He passed on and ascended the stairs, still holding my hand, and still beckoning the gentlemen to follow him, which they did.
Subió las escaleras, siempre llevándome tomada del brazo y siempre seguidos los dos de los hombres.

We mounted the first staircase, passed up the gallery, proceeded to the third storey: the low, black door, opened by Mr. Rochester's master-key, admitted us to the tapestried room, with its great bed and its pictorial cabinet.
Cruzamos la galería y ascendimos al tercer piso. La llave maestra que llevaba Rochester nos abrió paso al cuarto tapizado, con su enorme lecho y su gabinete de puertas pintadas.
"You know this place, Mason," said our guide; "she bit and stabbed you here."
-Tú ya conoces el sitio -dijo Rochester a Mason-. Aquí es donde ella te mordió.
He lifted the hangings from the wall, uncovering the second door: this, too, he opened.
Corrió las tapicerías que cubrían la pared, descubriendo otra puerta, que abrió seguidamente.
In a room without a window, there burnt a fire guarded by a high and strong fender, and a lamp suspended from the ceiling by a chain.
Nos hallamos en una habitación sin ventanas, en la que ardía una lumbre protegida por un alto y fuerte guardafuegos. Del techo pendía una lámpara sostenida por una cadena.
Grace Poole bent over the fire, apparently cooking something in a saucepan.
Grace Poole, inclinada sobre el fuego, parecía cocinar algo en una cacerola.
In the deep shade, at the farther end of the room, a figure ran backwards and forwards.
En el fondo del cuarto se veía una figura que se movía de un lado para otro.

What it was, whether beast or human being, one could not, at first sight, tell: it grovelled, seemingly, on all fours; it snatched and growled like some strange wild animal: but it was covered with clothing, and a quantity of dark, grizzled hair, wild as a mane, hid its head and face.

No era fácil, a primera vista, percibir si se trataba de un ser humano o no, ya que en aquel momento se arrastraba en cuatro pies y gruñía como un animal feroz, pero iba vestida y una oscura cabellera cubría su cabeza y su rostro.
"Good-morrow, Mrs. Poole!" said Mr. Rochester.
-Buenos días, Grace -dijo Rochester-: ¿Cómo está usted?
"How are you? and how is your charge to-day?"
¿Y la persona que tiene a su cargo?
"We're tolerable, sir, I thank you," replied Grace, lifting the boiling mess carefully on to the hob: "rather snappish, but not 'rageous."
-No vamos mal, señor-replicó Grace, dejando cuidadosamente la cazuela a un lado de la lumbre-. Está algo arisca, pero no furiosa.
A fierce cry seemed to give the lie to her favourable report: the clothed hyena rose up, and stood tall on its hind-feet.
En aquel momento, un grito penetrante pareció desmentir aquella aserción. La hiena vestida se puso en pie, mostrándose en toda su elevada estatura.
"Ah! sir, she sees you!" exclaimed Grace: "you'd better not stay."
-¡Les ha visto, señor! -exclamó Grace-. Vale más que se vayan.
"Only a few moments, Grace: you must allow me a few moments."
-Sólo estaremos unos momentos, Grace. Tráigala.
"Take care then, sir!--for God's sake, take care!"
-Tenga cuidado, señor. ¡Por amor de Dios, tenga cuidado!
The maniac bellowed: she parted her shaggy locks from her visage, and gazed wildly at her visitors.
La loca avanzó, separó de su rostro el cabello que lo cubría y miró con fiereza a sus visitantes.
I recognised well that purple face,--those bloated features.
Reconocí bien aquel rostro encendido, aquellas facciones hinchadas.
Mrs. Poole advanced.
Grace se adelantó. -Sepárense -dijo Rochester, apartándola-.
"Keep out of the way," said Mr. Rochester, thrusting her aside: "she has no knife now, I suppose, and I'm on my guard."
Ya estoy prevenido. Supongo que ahora no tendrá un cuchillo, ¿eh?
"One never knows what she has, sir: she is so cunning: it is not in mortal discretion to fathom her craft."
-Nunca se sabe lo que puede tener, señor. Es tan astuta, que con ella no hay precaución que valga.
"We had better leave her," whispered Mason.
-Valdrá más que nos vayamos -murmuró Mason.
"Go to the devil!" was his brother-in-law's recommendation.
-¡Vete al diablo! -contestó su cuñado.
"'Ware!" cried Grace.
-¡Cuidado! -gritó Grace.
The three gentlemen retreated simultaneously.
Los tres visitantes retrocedieron a la vez. Rochester se puso delante de mí.
Mr. Rochester flung me behind him: the lunatic sprang and grappled his throat viciously, and laid her teeth to his cheek: they struggled.
La loca cayó sobre él y asió rabiosamente su garganta, mientras trataba de morderle el rostro. Ambos forcejearon.
She was a big woman, in stature almost equalling her husband, and corpulent besides: she showed virile force in the contest--more than once she almost throttled him, athletic as he was.
Ella era alta y corpulenta, tanto como su marido, y estaba dotada de una fuerza tremenda. Varias veces estuvo a punto de derribar a Rochester, a pesar de lo vigoroso que éste era.
He could have settled her with a well-planted blow; but he would not strike: he would only wrestle.
Cierto que él hubiera podido inmovilizarla, descargándole un golpe violento, pero no intentaba más que sujetarla. Al fin logró tomarla por los brazos.
At last he mastered her arms; Grace Poole gave him a cord, and he pinioned them behind her: with more rope, which was at hand, he bound her to a chair.
Grace Poole le tendió una cuerda y Rochester ató a la espalda las muñecas de la loca, lo que realizó a despecho de las sacudidas y empellones que ella daba.
The operation was performed amidst the fiercest yells and the most convulsive plunges. Mr. Rochester then turned to the spectators: he looked at them with a smile both acrid and desolate.
Entonces, Rochester se volvió a los espectadores y les contempló con una sonrisa triste y amarga. -¡Esta es mi mujer! -exclamó-.
"That is _my wife_," said he.
Tales son las únicas relaciones que puedo mantener con ella.

"Such is the sole conjugal embrace I am ever to know--such are the endearments which are to solace my leisure hours! And _this_ is what I wished to have" (laying his hand on my shoulder): "this young girl, who stands so grave and quiet at the mouth of hell, looking collectedly at the gambols of a demon, I wanted her just as a change after that fierce ragout.

¡Y ésta -añadió, poniendo su mano en mi hombro-, esta muchacha es la que yo deseaba tener, ésta que veis, grave y silenciosa en la misma boca del Infierno, contemplando sin perder la serenidad las gesticulaciones de ese demonio!
Wood and Briggs, look at the difference!
¡Aprecien la diferencia, Wood y Briggs!

Compare these clear eyes with the red balls yonder--this face with that mask--this form with that bulk; then judge me, priest of the gospel and man of the law, and remember with what judgment ye judge ye shall be judged!

Comparen estos ojos límpidos con esos ojos inyectados en sangre, este rostro con esa máscara, y júzguenme, usted, sacerdote de Dios, y usted, hombre de leyes. Júzguenme y recuerden que como juzguen serán juzgados.
Off with you now.
Y ahora vámonos.
I must shut up my prize."
Todos nos retiramos.
We all withdrew. Mr. Rochester stayed a moment behind us, to give some further order to Grace Poole.
Rochester se detuvo unos momentos más, dando órdenes a Grace.
The solicitor addressed me as he descended the stair.
El procurador me habló cuando bajábamos la escalera.
"You, madam," said he, "are cleared from all blame: your uncle will be glad to hear it--if, indeed, he should be still living--when Mr. Mason returns to Madeira."
-Su tío, señorita -dijo-, celebrará saber que la hemos evitado un grave disgusto, si vive aún cuando Mr. Mason pase por Madera.
"My uncle!
-¿Mi tío?
What of him? Do you know him?"
¿Lo conoce usted?
"Mr. Mason does.
-Le conoce Mr. Mason.
Mr. Eyre has been the Funchal correspondent of his house for some years.
Mr. Eyre ha sido su corresponsal en Funchal durante varios años.

When your uncle received your letter intimating the contemplated union between yourself and Mr. Rochester, Mr. Mason, who was staying at Madeira to recruit his health, on his way back to Jamaica, happened to be with him.
Rochester, Mr. Mason se hallaba en Madera para mejorar su salud antes de continuar a Jamaica.
Mr. Eyre mentioned the intelligence; for he knew that my client here was acquainted with a gentleman of the name of Rochester.
Mr. Eyre le habló del asunto, porque sabía que mi cliente era pariente de una persona llamada Rochester.
Mr. Mason, astonished and distressed as you may suppose, revealed the real state of matters.
Mr. Mason, tan asombrado y disgustado como usted puede suponer, le reveló cuál era el verdadero estado de cosas.
Your uncle, I am sorry to say, is now on a sick bed; from which, considering the nature of his disease--decline--and the stage it has reached, it is unlikely he will ever rise.
Siento decirla que su tío padece ahora una enfermedad que, desgraciadamente, deja pocas esperanzas de curación.
He could not then hasten to England himself, to extricate you from the snare into which you had fallen, but he implored Mr. Mason to lose no time in taking steps to prevent the false marriage.
No podía, pues, venir a Inglaterra para impedir que usted cayese en la trampa que se le tendía, pero rogó a Mr. Mason que volviese y evitara el ilegal matrimonio.
He referred him to me for assistance.
Mr.
I used all despatch, and am thankful I was not too late: as you, doubtless, must be also.
Mason consultó conmigo, que he puesto en el asunto todo interés. Celebro haber llegado a tiempo.

Were I not morally certain that your uncle will be dead ere you reach Madeira, I would advise you to accompany Mr. Mason back; but as it is, I think you had better remain in England till you can hear further, either from or of Mr. Eyre.

Si no tuviera la certeza íntima de que su tío habrá fallecido, antes de que usted pudiera llegar a Madera, la aconsejaría que fuese allí con Mr. Mason, pero en el estado actual de cosas, creo que vale más que se quede en Inglaterra hasta que reciba noticias acerca de su tío.
Have we anything else to stay for?" he inquired of Mr. Mason.
-Y preguntó a Mason-: ¿Tenemos algo más. que hacer aquí?
"No, no--let us be gone," was the anxious reply; and without waiting to take leave of Mr. Rochester, they made their exit at the hall door.
-No, no, vámonos -contestó Mason apresuradamente. Sin despedirse de Rochester, ganaron la puerta de la casa.
The clergyman stayed to exchange a few sentences, either of admonition or reproof, with his haughty parishioner; this duty done, he too departed.
El sacerdote se detuvo algo más para dirigir algunas palabras, de reproche o reprimenda, a su perverso feligrés, y cumplido tal deber, se marchó.
I heard him go as I stood at the half-open door of my own room, to which I had now withdrawn.
Le sentí bajar a través de la entornada puerta de mi habitación, a la que me había retirado.

The house cleared, I shut myself in, fastened the bolt that none might intrude, and proceeded--not to weep, not to mourn, I was yet too calm for that, but--mechanically to take off the wedding dress, and replace it by the stuff gown I had worn yesterday, as I thought, for the last time.
Corrí el cerrojo y procedí -sin lágrimas ni lamentos- a sustituir en mis maletas las ropas de boda por mis antiguos vestidos.
I then sat down: I felt weak and tired.
Una vez hecho esto, me senté. Sentíame febril y fatigada.
I leaned my arms on a table, and my head dropped on them.
Apoyé los brazos en la mesa y descansé la cabeza sobre mis brazos.
And now I thought: till now I had only heard, seen, moved--followed up and down where I was led or dragged--watched event rush on event, disclosure open beyond disclosure: but _now_, _I thought_.
Ahora comenzaba a sentir. Hasta entonces había visto, oído y actuado, pero ahora sentía y pensaba.

The morning had been a quiet morning enough--all except the brief scene with the lunatic: the transaction in the church had not been noisy; there was no explosion of passion, no loud altercation, no dispute, no defiance or challenge, no tears, no sobs: a few words had been spoken, a calmly pronounced objection to the marriage made; some stern, short questions put by Mr. Rochester; answers, explanations given, evidence adduced; an open admission of the truth had been uttered by my master; then the living proof had been seen; the intruders were gone, and all was over.

No hubo amenazas, desafíos, lágrimas ni sollozos. Alguien alegó serenamente un impedimento al matrimonio, se cambiaron breves preguntas y respuestas, mi prometido reconoció la verdad, se vio la prueba viviente de ella, los intrusos se fueron y todo quedaba en paz.
I was in my own room as usual--just myself, without obvious change: nothing had smitten me, or scathed me, or maimed me.
Yo me hallaba en mi cuarto, como de costumbre, sin que nada hubiese cambiado en mí.
And yet where was the Jane Eyre of yesterday?--where was her life?--where were her prospects?
Sin embargo, ¿qué era de la Jane Eyre de la víspera? ¿Qué de sus perspectivas y esperanzas?
Jane Eyre, who had been an ardent, expectant woman--almost a bride, was a cold, solitary girl again: her life was pale; her prospects were desolate.

Jane Eyre, que era el día anterior una mujer llena de dulces anhelos, una casi desposada, se había convertido otra vez en una muchacha desamparada y sola, con una vida gris, llena de desoladas perspectivas ante ella.

A Christmas frost had come at midsummer; a white December storm had whirled over June; ice glazed the ripe apples, drifts crushed the blowing roses; on hayfield and cornfield lay a frozen shroud: lanes which last night blushed full of flowers, to-day were pathless with untrodden snow; and the woods, which twelve hours since waved leafy and flagrant as groves between the tropics, now spread, waste, wild, and white as pine-forests in wintry Norway.

La nieve de diciembre había caído en medio del verano, el hielo helaba las manzanas maduras, un viento invernal arrancaba de sus tallos las rosas. Los bosques, que doce horas antes mostrábanse fragantes y espléndidos como tropicales árboles, eran ahora inmensos, solitarios, glaciales como los bosques de pinos en el invierno de Noruega...
My hopes were all dead--struck with a subtle doom, such as, in one night, fell on all the first-born in the land of Egypt.
Mis esperanzas habían muerto de repente; mis deseos, el día anterior rebosantes de vida, estaban convertidos en lívidos cadáveres.

I looked at my love: that feeling which was my master's--which he had created; it shivered in my heart, like a suffering child in a cold cradle; sickness and anguish had seized it; it could not seek Mr. Rochester's arms--it could not derive warmth from his breast.

Y mi amor, aquel sentimiento que Rochester había despertado en mí, yacía, angustiado, en mi corazón, como un niño en una cuna fría. Ya no podía buscar el brazo de Rochester ni encontrar calor en su pecho.
Oh, never more could it turn to him; for faith was blighted--confidence destroyed!
Mi fe y mi confianza quedaban destruidas.
Mr. Rochester was not to me what he had been; for he was not what I had thought him.
Rochester no volvería a ser para mí lo que fue, porque resultaba distinto a como yo le había imaginado.
I would not ascribe vice to him; I would not say he had betrayed me; but the attribute of stainless truth was gone from his idea, and from his presence I must go: _that_ I perceived well.
No deseaba increparle ni quería reprocharle su traición, pero se me aparecía privado de la sinceridad que yo le atribuyese. Debía marchar de su lado.
When--how--whither, I could not yet discern; but he himself, I doubted not, would hurry me from Thornfield.
Cuándo y cómo, no lo sabía, pero adivinaba que él mismo me aconsejaría partir de Thornfield.
Real affection, it seemed, he could not have for me; it had been only fitful passion: that was balked; he would want me no more.
Era imposible, a mi juicio, que hubiese sentido hacia mí verdadero afecto; sólo fue, sin duda, un capricho momentáneo.
I should fear even to cross his path now: my view must be hateful to him.
Debía procurar no cruzarme en su camino, porque ahora mi presencia había de resultarle odiosa, sin duda.
Oh, how blind had been my eyes!
¡Oh, qué ciega había estado!
How weak my conduct!
¡Qué débil había sido! Cerré los ojos.
My eyes were covered and closed: eddying darkness seemed to swim round me, and reflection came in as black and confused a flow.
La oscuridad me rodeó. Sentí una inmensa lasitud y parecióme yacer en el lecho de un río seco, sintiendo retumbar entre las lejanas montañas el rumor del torrente que se aproximaba por el cauce.

Self-abandoned, relaxed, and effortless, I seemed to have laid me down in the dried-up bed of a great river; I heard a flood loosened in remote mountains, and felt the torrent come: to rise I had no will, to flee I had no strength.
Pero no deseaba incorporarme ni tenía fuerzas para huir de la riada.
I lay faint, longing to be dead.
Al contrario: ansiaba la muerte.

One idea only still throbbed life-like within me--a remembrance of God: it begot an unuttered prayer: these words went wandering up and down in my rayless mind, as something that should be whispered, but no energy was found to express them--
En aquel momento pensé en Dios, y mentalmente le dirigí una plegaria:
"Be not far from me, for trouble is near: there is none to help."
«Ayúdame, ya que nadie me ayudará, en la turbación que me amenaza.»
It was near: and as I had lifted no petition to Heaven to avert it--as I had neither joined my hands, nor bent my knees, nor moved my lips--it came: in full heavy swing the torrent poured over me.
Y la turbación cayó sobre mí. Todo el peso de aquel torrente que oía avanzar, gravitó sobre mi corazón.
The whole consciousness of my life lorn, my love lost, my hope quenched, my faith death-struck, swayed full and mighty above me in one sullen mass.
La conciencia de mi vida rota, de mi amor perdido, de mi esperanza deshecha, me abrumó como una inmensa masa. Imposible describir la amargura de aquel momento.
That bitter hour cannot be described: in truth, "the waters came into my soul; I sank in deep mire: I felt no standing; I came into deep waters; the floods overflowed me."
Bien puede decirse que «las olas inundaron mi alma, me sentí hundir en el légamo, en el seno de las aguas profundas, y las ondas pasaron sobre mi cabeza».
Some time in the afternoon I raised my head, and looking round and seeing the western sun gilding the sign of its decline on the wall, I asked, "What am I to do?"
Varias veces durante la tarde, mientras el sol declinaba, me pregunté: «¿Qué haré?»
But the answer my mind gave--"Leave Thornfield at once"--was so prompt, so dread, that I stopped my ears. I said I could not bear such words now.

Pero la respuesta que me daba la razón: «Vete en seguida de Thornfield», me era tan dura de oír, que procuraba tapar los oídos a tal consejo, y me decía: «Lo peor no es que haya dejado de ser la prometida de Edward Rochester.

"That I am not Edward Rochester's bride is the least part of my woe," I alleged: "that I have wakened out of most glorious dreams, and found them all void and vain, is a horror I could bear and master; but that I must leave him decidedly, instantly, entirely, is intolerable.

Este brusco despertar del más bello sueño, este hallar que cuanto imaginara era falso y vano, puedo soportarlo por horroroso que sea. Pero la idea de abandonarle es, resuelta, indudable y enteramente imposible.
I cannot do it."
No puedo hacerlo.»
But, then, a voice within me averred that I could do it and foretold that I should do it.
Una voz interior me objetaba que sí podía y debía hacerlo.

I wrestled with my own resolution: I wanted to be weak that I might avoid the awful passage of further suffering I saw laid out for me; and Conscience, turned tyrant, held Passion by the throat, told her tauntingly, she had yet but dipped her dainty foot in the slough, and swore that with that arm of iron he would thrust her down to unsounded depths of agony.
La conciencia, inexorable, asió la pasión por el cuello, la vituperó, la pisoteó bajo sus pies.
"Let me be torn away," then I cried. "Let another help me!"
«Déjame buscar la ayuda de alguien», gemí.

"No; you shall tear yourself away, none shall help you: you shall yourself pluck out your right eye; yourself cut off your right hand: your heart shall be the victim, and you the priest to transfix it."
«No; tú sola debes ayudarte; tú debes arrancar, si es necesario, tu ojo derecho y cortar tu propia mano. Sólo tu corazón debe ser la víctima de tu error.»
I rose up suddenly, terror-struck at the solitude which so ruthless a judge haunted,--at the silence which so awful a voice filled. My head swam as I stood erect.
Me incorporé, aterrorizada de aquella soledad en la que oía pronunciar tan despiadado juicio y del silencio que llenaba aquella inexorable voz.
I perceived that I was sickening from excitement and inanition; neither meat nor drink had passed my lips that day, for I had taken no breakfast.
Al ponerme en pie sentí que se me iba la cabeza. No sólo estaba agotada por la excitación, sino extenuada, ya que no había comido ni bebido nada en todo el día.

And, with a strange pang, I now reflected that, long as I had been shut up here, no message had been sent to ask how I was, or to invite me to come down: not even little Adele had tapped at the door; not even Mrs. Fairfax had sought me.
Y entonces reparé en que nadie había venido a verme, ni preguntado por mí. Ni Adéle había llamado a mi puerta, ni Mrs.
"Friends always forget those whom fortune forsakes," I murmured, as I undrew the bolt and passed out.
«Los amigos siempre olvidan a quienes olvida la fortuna», pensé. Descorrí el cerrojo y salí.
I stumbled over an obstacle: my head was still dizzy, my sight was dim, and my limbs were feeble.
Tropecé con un obstáculo y estuve a punto de caer.
I could not soon recover myself.
Me sentía débil y mareada.
I fell, but not on to the ground: an outstretched arm caught me.
Un brazo vigoroso me sujetó.
I looked up--I was supported by Mr. Rochester, who sat in a chair across my chamber threshold. "You come out at last," he said.
Rochester, sentado en una silla, se hallaba ante el umbral de mi habitación.
"Well, I have been waiting for you long, and listening: yet not one movement have I heard, nor one sob: five minutes more of that death-like hush, and I should have forced the lock like a burglar.
Ni un movimiento, ni un solo sollozo he sentido. ¡Cinco minutos más de esta espera intolerable y habría forzado la puerta, como un ladrón!
So you shun me?--you shut yourself up and grieve alone! I would rather you had come and upbraided me with vehemence. You are passionate. I expected a scene of some kind.
¡Oh, preferiría que me apostrofases de vehemencia, que tus lágrimas manaran sobre mi pecho!
But I err: you have not wept at all!
Pero me he equivocado. ¡No lloras!
I see a white cheek and a faded eye, but no trace of tears.
Tu rostro está pálido y tus ojos marchitos, pero en ellos no hay huellas de lágrimas.
I suppose, then, your heart has been weeping blood?"
Temo que sea tu corazón el que haya vertido lágrimas de sangre...
"Well, Jane! not a word of reproach?
Dime algo, Jane. ¿No me reprochas?
Nothing bitter--nothing poignant?
¿No se te ocurre nada ofensivo que decirme?
You sit quietly where I have placed you, and regard me with a weary, passive look."
Te veo inmóvil, pasiva, mirándome con serenidad...
"Jane, I never meant to wound you thus.
No me propuse herirte, Jane.

If the man who had but one little ewe lamb that was dear to him as a daughter, that ate of his bread and drank of his cup, and lay in his bosom, had by some mistake slaughtered it at the shambles, he would not have rued his bloody blunder more than I now rue mine.

Estoy en la situación del pastor que tuviera una oveja, a la que quisiera como si fuera su hija, con quien compartiera su pan y su agua, y a la que un día degollara por error. Sí, ése es mi estado de alma...
Will you ever forgive me?"
¿No me perdonarás nunca?
Reader, I forgave him at the moment and on the spot.
¡Le perdoné en aquel mismo momento, lector!

There was such deep remorse in his eye, such true pity in his tone, such manly energy in his manner; and besides, there was such unchanged love in his whole look and mien--I forgave him all: yet not in words, not outwardly; only at my heart's core.

¡Había tan profundo remordimiento en sus ojos, tan sincera compasión en su acento y, sobre todo, tan inalterable amor en él y en mí! Sí; le perdoné con todo mi corazón, aunque no lo expresase con palabras.
"You know I am a scoundrel, Jane?" ere long he inquired wistfully--wondering, I suppose, at my continued silence and tameness, the result rather of weakness than of will.
-¿Sabes que soy un canalla, Jane? -me preguntó, tras un largo silencio, atribuyendo, sin duda, mi silencio y mi calma más al abatimiento que a mi propia voluntad.
"Then tell me so roundly and sharply--don't spare me."
-Dímelo, pues, con franqueza, con dureza. No calles nada.
"I cannot: I am tired and sick.
-No puedo.
I want some water."
Me siento muy enferma y cansada.
He heaved a sort of shuddering sigh, and taking me in his arms, carried me downstairs.
Tengo sed... Emitió un profundo suspiro y, tomándome en sus brazos, me hizo bajar las escaleras.
At first I did not know to what room he had borne me; all was cloudy to my glazed sight: presently I felt the reviving warmth of a fire; for, summer as it was, I had become icy cold in my chamber.
Luego sentí el estimulante calor del fuego. A pesar de estar en verano, me sentía fría como el hielo.
He put wine to my lips; I tasted it and revived; then I ate something he offered me, and was soon myself.
Me ofreció una copa de vino y me sentí revivir. Comí algo que me dio y recuperé totalmente mis energías.
I was in the library--sitting in his chair--he was quite near.
Me encontré en la biblioteca, sentada en el sillón donde él solía sentarse.

"If I could go out of life now, without too sharp a pang, it would be well for me," I thought; "then I should not have to make the effort of cracking my heart-strings in rending them from among Mr. Rochester's.
Rochester estaba a mi lado. Pensé que me valdría más morir en aquel momento.
I must leave him, it appears. I do not want to leave him--I cannot leave him." "How are you now, Jane?"
Sabía que debía abandonarle, y, sin embargo, no quería, no podía hacerlo. -¿Cómo estás ahora, Jane?
"Much better, sir; I shall be well soon."
-Mucho mejor.
"Taste the wine again, Jane."
-Toma más vino.
I obeyed him; then he put the glass on the table, stood before me, and looked at me attentively.
Le obedecí. Dejé el vaso en la mesa y me miró con detenimiento.

Suddenly he turned away, with an inarticulate exclamation, full of passionate emotion of some kind; he walked fast through the room and came back; he stooped towards me as if to kiss me; but I remembered caresses were now forbidden. I turned my face away and put his aside.

Se volvió de repente, lanzando una vehemente exclamación, comenzó a pasear por el cuarto y al fin se inclinó hacia mí como para besarme. Recordando que ahora las caricias estaban prohibidas entre nosotros, aparté el rostro.
"What!--How is this?" he exclaimed hastily.
-¡Cómo! -exclamó Rochester.
"Oh, I know! you won't kiss the husband of Bertha Mason?
Y agregó amargamente-: Ya: no quieres besar al marido de Bertha Mason.
You consider my arms filled and my embraces appropriated?"
Supongo que consideras que con las caricias de ella tengo bastante.

"If you think so, you must have a strange opinion of me; you must regard me as a plotting profligate--a base and low rake who has been simulating disinterested love in order to draw you into a snare deliberately laid, and strip you of honour and rob you of self-respect.
Me tienes sin duda por un odioso intrigante que me preparaba a hacerte perder el honor y el decoro.

What do you say to that? I see you can say nothing in the first place, you are faint still, and have enough to do to draw your breath; in the second place, you cannot yet accustom yourself to accuse and revile me, and besides, the flood-gates of tears are opened, and they would rush out if you spoke much; and you have no desire to expostulate, to upbraid, to make a scene: you are thinking how _to act_--_talking_ you consider is of no use.

Si no lo dices es: primero porque te faltan las fuerzas, segundo porque no te acostumbras a la idea de acusarme e increparme y, en fin, porque las puertas de tus lágrimas están abiertas y si hablases mucho romperías en llanto. Sé que no quieres llorar, explicarte, hacer una escena, sino que te propones, en vez de hablar, actuar.
I know you--I am on my guard."
Lo sé. Estoy preparado a ello.
"Sir, I do not wish to act against you," I said; and my unsteady voice warned me to curtail my sentence.
-No deseo proceder contra usted -dije con entrecortada voz.
"Not in your sense of the word, but in mine you are scheming to destroy me.
-En el sentido que tú das a las palabras, no; pero en el que yo le doy, sí.
You have as good as said that I am a married man--as a married man you will shun me, keep out of my way: just now you have refused to kiss me.
Piensas que, puesto que soy un hombre casado, debes apartarte de mi camino. Por eso ahora no has querido besarme.

You intend to make yourself a complete stranger to me: to live under this roof only as Adele's governess; if ever I say a friendly word to you, if ever a friendly feeling inclines you again to me, you will say,--'That man had nearly made me his mistress: I must be ice and rock to him;' and ice and rock you will accordingly become."
Te propones convertirte para mí en una extraña, vivir bajo mi mismo techo exclusivamente como institutriz de Adèle, rechazando mis palabras y mis aproximaciones como si fueras de piedra y de hielo.

I cleared and steadied my voice to reply: "All is changed about me, sir; I must change too--there is no doubt of that; and to avoid fluctuations of feeling, and continual combats with recollections and associations, there is only one way--Adele must have a new governess, sir."
-Señor -repuse-: todo ha cambiado para mí de tal forma que, para evitar enojosos recuerdos e ideas tristes, es preciso que busque usted una nueva institutriz para Adèle.

"Oh, Adele will go to school--I have settled that already; nor do I mean to torment you with the hideous associations and recollections of Thornfield Hall--this accursed place--this tent of Achan--this insolent vault, offering the ghastliness of living death to the light of the open sky--this narrow stone hell, with its one real fiend, worse than a legion of such as we imagine.
-Adèle irá a un colegio.
Jane, you shall not stay here, nor will I. I was wrong ever to bring you to Thornfield Hall, knowing as I did how it was haunted.
No deseo atormentarte reteniéndote en Thornfield Hall.

I charged them to conceal from you, before I ever saw you, all knowledge of the curse of the place; merely because I feared Adele never would have a governess to stay if she knew with what inmate she was housed, and my plans would not permit me to remove the maniac elsewhere--though I possess an old house, Ferndean Manor, even more retired and hidden than this, where I could have lodged her safely enough, had not a scruple about the unhealthiness of the situation, in the heart of a wood, made my conscience recoil from the arrangement.

Y ahora debo decirte que, si al principio oculté la existencia de una perturbada aquí, era porque temía que ninguna institutriz hubiera querido residir en una casa en esas condiciones. Cierto que yo podía haber llevado a la loca a otro sitio aún más escondido que poseo: Ferndean Manor, cuya insalubre situación en el corazón de un bosque tal vez me hubiera librado tan pronto de esa carga que arrastro.
Probably those damp walls would soon have eased me of her charge: but to each villain his own vice; and mine is not a tendency to indirect assassination, even of what I most hate.
Pero por perversas que sean mis inclinaciones, la de acometer un asesinato indirecto no figura entre ellas.
"Concealing the mad-woman's neighbourhood from you, however, was something like covering a child with a cloak and laying it down near a upas-tree: that demon's vicinage is poisoned, and always was.
Ocultarte la existencia de esa loca era inútil, lo reconozco... Toda la casa, toda la vecindad, está emponzoñada con su presencia.

But I'll shut up Thornfield Hall: I'll nail up the front door and board the lower windows: I'll give Mrs. Poole two hundred a year to live here with _my wife_, as you term that fearful hag: Grace will do much for money, and she shall have her son, the keeper at Grimsby Retreat, to bear her company and be at hand to give her aid in the paroxysms, when _my wife_ is prompted by her familiar to burn people in their beds at night, to stab them, to bite their flesh from their bones, and so on--"

Pago doscientas libras al año a Grace Poole para que custodie a esa bruja infernal que tú llamas mi mujer. Y dentro de poco, su hijo, que es celador en el asilo de Grimsby, vendrá a ayudarle en su tarea de vigilar a mi mujer cuando sufre esos paroxismos en cuyo curso incendia camas, muerde y...
"Sir," I interrupted him, "you are inexorable for that unfortunate lady: you speak of her with hate--with vindictive antipathy. It is cruel--she cannot help being mad."
-Es usted implacable con esa desventurada señora -interrumpí-. La menciona usted con aversión y odio, como si ella tuviese la culpa de su locura.
"Jane, my little darling (so I will call you, for so you are), you don't know what you are talking about; you misjudge me again: it is not because she is mad I hate her.
-Jane, queridita (y perdona que te llame así, porque para mí lo eres), me juzgas mal.
If you were mad, do you think I should hate you?"
¿Crees que yo te odiaría si tú estuvieses loca?
"I do indeed, sir."
-Sin duda.
"Then you are mistaken, and you know nothing about me, and nothing about the sort of love of which I am capable.
-Te engañas. Ignoras cómo soy, la clase de amor que soy capaz de experimentar.
Every atom of your flesh is as dear to me as my own: in pain and sickness it would still be dear.
Te quiero más que a mí mismo, y si sufrieses, te querría más aún.

Your mind is my treasure, and if it were broken, it would be my treasure still: if you raved, my arms should confine you, and not a strait waistcoat--your grasp, even in fury, would have a charm for me: if you flew at me as wildly as that woman did this morning, I should receive you in an embrace, at least as fond as it would be restrictive.
Aunque enloquecieses, aunque te lanzases sobre mí como esa mujer esta mañana, te recibiría con un abrazo. No me apartaría de ti con horror, como de ella, y nadie te cuidaría más que yo mismo.

I should not shrink from you with disgust as I did from her: in your quiet moments you should have no watcher and no nurse but me; and I could hang over you with untiring tenderness, though you gave me no smile in return; and never weary of gazing into your eyes, though they had no longer a ray of recognition for me.
Y no sería menos tierno para ti aunque no me dedicases una sonrisa ni me reconocieran tus ojos. Pero no sigamos hablando de eso.
I was talking of removing you from Thornfield.
Yo me refería a hacerte partir de Thornfield.
All, you know, is prepared for prompt departure: to-morrow you shall go.
Todo está preparado para tu marcha. Mañana puedes irte.
I only ask you to endure one more night under this roof, Jane; and then, farewell to its miseries and terrors for ever!
Sólo te pido que pases una noche más bajo este techo y luego ¡adiós miserias y terrores!
I have a place to repair to, which will be a secure sanctuary from hateful reminiscences, from unwelcome intrusion--even from falsehood and slander."
No faltará un lugar que sea como un santuario donde refugiarse y olvidar los resultados odiosos...
"And take Adele with you, sir," I interrupted; "she will be a companion for you."
-Quédese con Adèle -interrumpí-: será una compañera para usted.
I told you I would send Adele to school; and what do I want with a child for a companion, and not my own child,--a French dancer's bastard?
-Ya te he dicho que la enviaré a un colegio. ¿Para qué me sirve la compañía de una niña?
Why do you importune me about her!
¡Y ni siquiera mi propia hija, sino la bastarda de una bailarina francesa!
I say, why do you assign Adele to me for a companion?"
¿Por qué me importunas aconsejándome que la conserve en mi compañía?
"You spoke of a retirement, sir; and retirement and solitude are dull: too dull for you."
-Porque hablaba usted de retirarse, y la soledad y el retiro no serán beneficiosos para usted.
"Solitude! solitude!" he reiterated with irritation.
-¡Soledad! -repitió él, con irritación-.
"I see I must come to an explanation.
Es preciso que nos expliquemos.
I don't know what sphynx-like expression is forming in your countenance.
No sé lo que significa la expresión enigmática de tu rostro, pero lo que yo me propongo, sí lo sé.
You are to share my solitude. Do you understand?"
Tú compartirás mi soledad.
I shook my head: it required a degree of courage, excited as he was becoming, even to risk that mute sign of dissent.
Moví negativamente la cabeza. Hacía falta cierto valor para manifestar aquella oposición, dado lo excitado que él se encontraba.
He had been walking fast about the room, and he stopped, as if suddenly rooted to one spot.
Interrumpió sus paseos, se detuvo ante mí y me miró.
He looked at me long and hard: I turned my eyes from him, fixed them on the fire, and tried to assume and maintain a quiet, collected aspect.
Separé mis ojos de los suyos y los fijé en el fuego, esforzándome en adoptar un aspecto sereno y recogido.
"Now for the hitch in Jane's character," he said at last, speaking more calmly than from his look I had expected him to speak.
-Ya hemos tropezado con una dificultad de tu temperamento -dijo con más calma de la que cabía esperar de su aspecto-.
"The reel of silk has run smoothly enough so far; but I always knew there would come a knot and a puzzle: here it is.
Hasta ahora tu carácter iba devanándose suavemente como un carrete de seda, pero yo sabía que alguna vez habríamos de encontrar un nudo...
Now for vexation, and exasperation, and endless trouble!
¡Y ya lo tenemos aquí!
He recommenced his walk, but soon again stopped, and this time just before me.
Volvió a pasear, se paró en seguida y me habló acercando su boca a mi oído.
"Jane! will you hear reason?" (he stooped and approached his lips to my ear); "because, if you won't, I'll try violence."
-Jane, ¿quieres oír la voz de la razón? ¡Porque, si no, emplearé la violencia!
His voice was hoarse; his look that of a man who is just about to burst an insufferable bond and plunge headlong into wild license.
Su voz, su aspecto, eran los de un hombre que ha llegado al límite de lo que puede soportar y está dispuesto a entregarse a cualquier exceso.
I saw that in another moment, and with one impetus of frenzy more, I should be able to do nothing with him.
En otro momento, no hubiera estado en mi mano dominarle.
The present--the passing second of time--was all I had in which to control and restrain him--a movement of repulsion, flight, fear would have sealed my doom,--and his.
Ahora comprendí que un movimiento cualquiera, fuese de temor, de repulsión, o de huida, hubiese producido consecuencias irreparables. Yo no le temía.
But I was not afraid: not in the least.
Me sentía fortalecida por una fuerza misteriosa.
I felt an inward power; a sense of influence, which supported me. The crisis was perilous; but not without its charm: such as the Indian, perhaps, feels when he slips over the rapid in his canoe.
La situación era expuesta, pero no dejaba de tener cierto atractivo, análogo a la emoción que deben experimentar los indios cuando remontan una torrentera en sus frágiles canoas.
I took hold of his clenched hand, loosened the contorted fingers, and said to him, soothingly--
Cogí la mano de Rochester, y le dije, suavemente:
"Sit down; I'll talk to you as long as you like, and hear all you have to say, whether reasonable or unreasonable."
-Siéntese, hable lo que quiera y diga cuanto le plazca, sea razonable o no.
He sat down: but he did not get leave to speak directly.
Se sentó, mas no habló inmediatamente.

I had been struggling with tears for some time: I had taken great pains to repress them, because I knew he would not like to see me weep. Now, however, I considered it well to let them flow as freely and as long as they liked. If the flood annoyed him, so much the better.
Hasta entonces yo había reprimido mis lágrimas, temiendo que le disgustasen, pero ahora no tenía por qué contenerlas.
So I gave way and cried heartily. Soon I heard him earnestly entreating me to be composed.
Si le desagradaban, tanto mejor.
I said I could not while he was in such a passion.
Oí su voz diciéndome que no sollozara.
"But I am not angry, Jane: I only love you too well; and you had steeled your little pale face with such a resolute, frozen look, I could not endure it.

Repuse que no me era posible dejar de llorar mientras le viera en aquel estado. -No estoy furioso contra ti, Jane. Como te quiero mucho no he podido soportar la expresión resuelta y helada de tu rostro.
Hush, now, and wipe your eyes."
Vamos, sécate las lágrimas.
His softened voice announced that he was subdued; so I, in my turn, became calm.
La aumentada dulzura de su voz me hizo comprender que se había tranquilizado.
Now he made an effort to rest his head on my shoulder, but I would not permit it.
Me tranquilicé, pues, a mi vez. Él trató de apoyar su cabeza sobre mi hombro, pero no se lo permití.
Then he would draw me to him: no.
Trató de atraerme hacia sí. Me negué.
"Jane! Jane!" he said, in such an accent of bitter sadness it thrilled along every nerve I had; "you don't love me, then?
-Jane, Jane -dijo con tan amarga tristeza que me hizo estremecer hasta el fondo de mi alma-, no me quieres ¿verdad?
It was only my station, and the rank of my wife, that you valued?
No deseabas ser mi mujer sino por las ventajas que te traía, ¿eh?
Now that you think me disqualified to become your husband, you recoil from my touch as if I were some toad or ape."
Ahora que me consideras imposible como marido, te repugna mi contacto como el de un sapo o un mono.
These words cut me: yet what could I do or I say?
Aquellas palabras me hirieron.
I ought probably to have done or said nothing; but I was so tortured by a sense of remorse at thus hurting his feelings, I could not control the wish to drop balm where I had wounded.
¿Qué podía contestarle? Probablemente lo mejor hubiera sido no decir ni hacer nada, pero no pude contener el deseo de calmar su dolor:
"I _do_ love you," I said, "more than ever: but I must not show or indulge the feeling: and this is the last time I must express it."
-Le quiero -dije- más que nunca. Se lo digo por última vez, porque no puedo permitirme ese sentimiento.
"The last time, Jane!
-¡Por última vez, Jane!
What! do you think you can live with me, and see me daily, and yet, if you still love me, be always cold and distant?"
¿Es posible que pienses vivir a mi lado, verme a diario y mantenerte siempre fría y distante de mí?
"No, sir; that I am certain I could not; and therefore I see there is but one way: but you will be furious if I mention it."
-No, eso no sería posible. Sólo cabe una solución, pero temo enfurecerle si la menciono.
"Oh, mention it!
-¡Menciónala!
If I storm, you have the art of weeping."
Tú sabes calmar mis exaltaciones.
"Mr. Rochester, I must leave you."
-Mr. Rochester, es preciso que me separe de usted.
"For how long, Jane?
-¿Por cuánto tiempo?
For a few minutes, while you smooth your hair--which is somewhat dishevelled; and bathe your face--which looks feverish?"
Supongo que por el preciso para peinarte, porque estás desmelenada, y para lavarte, porque tienes la cara ardiendo.
"I must leave Adele and Thornfield. I must part with you for my whole life: I must begin a new existence among strange faces and strange scenes."
-Tengo que irme de Thornfield, separarme de usted para siempre, y empezar una nueva vida en otro ambiente y entre otras personas.
"Of course: I told you you should.
-Lo mismo creo, prescindiendo a la locura de alejarte de mí.
I pass over the madness about parting from me. You mean you must become a part of me.
Iremos a sitios donde no nos conozcan y serás, de hecho y ante el mundo, mi mujer.
As to the new existence, it is all right: you shall yet be my wife: I am not married. You shall be Mrs. Rochester--both virtually and nominally.
Te tendré a mi lado y no me separaré de ti mientras viva.
I shall keep only to you so long as you and I live. You shall go to a place I have in the south of France: a whitewashed villa on the shores of the Mediterranean.
Iremos a algún sitio del sur de Francia; viviremos en una villa blanca, frente al Mediterráneo.
There you shall live a happy, and guarded, and most innocent life.
Y allí llevaremos una vida honorable, segura y feliz.
Never fear that I wish to lure you into error--to make you my mistress.
No veas egoísmo en mí, no creas que trato de hacerte mi amante.
Why did you shake your head?
¿Por qué mueves la cabeza, Jane?
Jane, you must be reasonable, or in truth I shall again become frantic."
Debes ser razonable. De lo contrario, volveré a ponerme frenético.
His voice and hand quivered: his large nostrils dilated; his eye blazed: still I dared to speak.
Temblaban su voz y sus dedos, las aletas de su nariz se dilataban, sus ojos despedían lumbre. Sin embargo, me atrevía a contestar:
"Sir, your wife is living: that is a fact acknowledged this morning by yourself. If I lived with you as you desire, I should then be your mistress: to say otherwise is sophistical--is false."
-Su mujer existe, como usted mismo ha reconocido, y si yo viviese con usted en la forma que se indica, no sería más que su amante.
"Jane, I am not a gentle-tempered man--you forget that: I am not long- enduring; I am not cool and dispassionate.
-Jane: no soy un hombre de buen carácter; no soy capaz de soportar mucho; no soy desapasionado y frío.
Out of pity to me and yourself, put your finger on my pulse, feel how it throbs, and--beware!"
Toca mi pulso. Me presentó la muñeca.
He bared his wrist, and offered it to me: the blood was forsaking his cheek and lips, they were growing livid; I was distressed on all hands.
La sangre había huido de sus mejillas y sus labios, lívidos a la sazón,.y parecía afluir en tumulto a sus manos.
To agitate him thus deeply, by a resistance he so abhorred, was cruel: to yield was out of the question.
Hacerle sufrir con una negativa implacable era cruel, tratar de tranquilizarle era imposible, y complacerle, más aún.
I did what human beings do instinctively when they are driven to utter extremity--looked for aid to one higher than man: the words "God help me!" burst involuntarily from my lips.
Hice, pues, lo que todos los seres humanos en tales extremos. Las palabras «¡Dios me ayude!» brotaron, casi voluntariamente, de mis labios.
"I am a fool!" cried Mr. Rochester suddenly. "I keep telling her I am not married, and do not explain to her why.
-¡Qué necio soy! -exclamó Rochester súbitamente-.
I forget she knows nothing of the character of that woman, or of the circumstances attending my infernal union with her.
No te he explicado aún las circunstancias en que me uní a esa infernal mujer ni su carácter.
Oh, I am certain Jane will agree with me in opinion, when she knows all that I know!
Cuando lo sepas todo, Jane, estoy seguro de que concordarás conmigo.
Just put your hand in mine, Janet--that I may have the evidence of touch as well as sight, to prove you are near me--and I will in a few words show you the real state of the case.
Pon tu mano en la mía para sentirme seguro de tu proximidad y en pocas palabras te lo explicaré todo.
Can you listen to me?"
¿Me escucharás?
"Yes, sir; for hours if you will."
-Le escucharé cuanto quiera, aunque sea varias horas.
"I ask only minutes.
-Bastan unos minutos.
Jane, did you ever hear or know that I was not the eldest son of my house: that I had once a brother older than I?"
¿Has oído decir, Jane, que yo no era el primogénito de mi familia, sino que tenía un hermano mayor?
"I remember Mrs. Fairfax told me so once."
-Mrs. Fairfax me lo dijo una vez.
"And did you ever hear that my father was an avaricious, grasping man?"
-¿Y sabes también que mi padre era un hombre avaro, sórdido?
"I have understood something to that effect."
-Algo de eso he oído.

"Well, Jane, being so, it was his resolution to keep the property together; he could not bear the idea of dividing his estate and leaving me a fair portion: all, he resolved, should go to my brother, Rowland.
-Bien: entonces no te extrañará saber que no quería distribuir sus propiedades dándome una parte a mí.
Yet as little could he endure that a son of his should be a poor man. I must be provided for by a wealthy marriage.
Como, por otro lado, tampoco querría que un hijo suyo fuese un pordiosero, arregló para mí un matrimonio con una mujer rica.
Mr. Mason, a West India planter and merchant, was his old acquaintance.
Tenía en las Antillas un antiguo amigo: Mason, un plantador de Jamaica.
He was certain his possessions were real and vast: he made inquiries.
Mi padre sabía que sus posesiones eran muy importantes.
Mr. Mason, he found, had a son and daughter; and he learned from him that he could and would give the latter a fortune of thirty thousand pounds: that sufficed.
Mason tenía un hijo y una hija y dotaba a ésta con treinta mil libras. A mi padre le pareció bastante.
When I left college, I was sent out to Jamaica, to espouse a bride already courted for me.
Cuando salí del colegio me enviaron a Jamaica.
My father said nothing about her money; but he told me Miss Mason was the boast of Spanish Town for her beauty: and this was no lie.
Mi padre no me había hablado de la fortuna de mi futura mujer, pero me había dicho que era la beldad más cortejada de la isla, y en eso no mentía.
I found her a fine woman, in the style of Blanche Ingram: tall, dark, and majestic.
A mí me pareció una bella mujer, alta, morena, majestuosa, por el estilo de Blanche Ingram.
Her family wished to secure me because I was of a good race; and so did she.
Su familia deseaba asegurarme, porque yo pertenecía a una casta ilustre, y lo consiguieron.
They showed her to me in parties, splendidly dressed. I seldom saw her alone, and had very little private conversation with her.
Me invitaban, me hacían ver a Bertha Mason en reuniones en las que descollaba por sus espléndidos atavíos. Raras veces hablábamos a solas.
She flattered me, and lavishly displayed for my pleasure her charms and accomplishments.
Bertha me lisonjeaba todo lo que podía.
All the men in her circle seemed to admire her and envy me.
Cuantos hombres giraban en torno suyo la admiraban a ella y me envidiaban a mí.
I was dazzled, stimulated: my senses were excited; and being ignorant, raw, and inexperienced, I thought I loved her.
Excitado por su atractivo, inexperto como era entonces, pensé estar enamorado de ella.
There is no folly so besotted that the idiotic rivalries of society, the prurience, the rashness, the blindness of youth, will not hurry a man to its commission.
Las estúpidas rivalidades juveniles, la ceguera de la poca edad, son lo que más influye en estos casos.
Her relatives encouraged me; competitors piqued me; she allured me: a marriage was achieved almost before I knew where I was.
Su familia me alentaba, los competidores que tenía aguijoneaban mi amor propio, y, en resumen, me casé con ella sin conocerla casi.
Oh, I have no respect for myself when I think of that act!--an agony of inward contempt masters me.
¡Cuánto me desprecio a mí mismo al pensarlo!

I never loved, I never esteemed, I did not even know her. I was not sure of the existence of one virtue in her nature: I had marked neither modesty, nor benevolence, nor candour, nor refinement in her mind or manners--and, I married her:--gross, grovelling, mole-eyed blockhead that I was!
Yo no la amaba, ignoraba si era virtuosa o no, no había apreciado en su carácter ni bondad, ni modestia, ni candor, ni delicadeza... ¡y, sin embargo, me casé!
With less sin I might have--But let me remember to whom I am speaking."
¡Oh, qué estúpido fui!
"My bride's mother I had never seen: I understood she was dead.
»No había visto nunca a la madre de mi novia, y la creía muerta.
The honeymoon over, I learned my mistake; she was only mad, and shut up in a lunatic asylum.
Cuando transcurrió la luna de miel, comprendí mi error: mi suegra estaba loca, en un manicomio.
There was a younger brother, too--a complete dumb idiot.
Mi mujer tenía un hermano menor completamente idiota.

The elder one, whom you have seen (and whom I cannot hate, whilst I abhor all his kindred, because he has some grains of affection in his feeble mind, shown in the continued interest he takes in his wretched sister, and also in a dog-like attachment he once bore me), will probably be in the same state one day.

El mayor es el que conoces, y a quien no puedo odiar, aunque abomine de toda su casta, porque en su débil cerebro hay algunos elementos afectuosos, que prueba con su cariño a su hermana y con la adhesión, casi de perro leal, que siente hacia mí. No obstante, probablemente acabará perdiendo la razón por completo.
My father and my brother Rowland knew all this; but they thought only of the thirty thousand pounds, and joined in the plot against me."
Mi padre y mi hermano Rowland conocían todo esto, pero no pensaron más que en las treinta mil libras y se pusieron de acuerdo para hacerme contraer aquel matrimonio.

"These were vile discoveries; but except for the treachery of concealment, I should have made them no subject of reproach to my wife, even when I found her nature wholly alien to mine, her tastes obnoxious to me, her cast of mind common, low, narrow, and singularly incapable of being led to anything higher, expanded to anything larger--

»Aun descubiertas estas cosas, yo, pese a la ocultación que representaban, no había reprochado nada a mi mujer. Pero su carácter era absolutamente opuesto al mío, sus gustos discrepantes de los que yo tenía.

when I found that I could not pass a single evening, nor even a single hour of the day with her in comfort; that kindly conversation could not be sustained between us, because whatever topic I started, immediately received from her a turn at once coarse and trite, perverse and imbecile--when I perceived that I should never have a quiet or settled household, because no servant would bear the continued outbreaks of her violent and unreasonable temper, or the vexations of her absurd, contradictory, exacting orders--even then I restrained myself: I eschewed upbraiding, I curtailed remonstrance; I tried to devour my repentance and disgust in secret; I repressed the deep antipathy I felt.

A cuanto yo hablaba respondía con contestaciones groseras y chabacanas, perversas y estúpidas. Ningún criado paraba en la casa, porque no podían soportar los arrebatos de mal carácter de mi mujer, sus abusos ni sus órdenes absurdas y contradictorias.
"Jane, I will not trouble you with abominable details: some strong words shall express what I have to say.
»No quiero disgustarte con detalles odiosos, Jane; vale más resumir.

I lived with that woman upstairs four years, and before that time she had tried me indeed: her character ripened and developed with frightful rapidity; her vices sprang up fast and rank: they were so strong, only cruelty could check them, and I would not use cruelty.
Viví con esa mujer más de cuatro años y en tal lapso su perverso carácter y sus malas inclinaciones se desarrollaron con increíble rapidez.
Bertha Mason, the true daughter of an infamous mother, dragged me through all the hideous and degrading agonies which must attend a man bound to a wife at once intemperate and unchaste.
Bertha Mason, digna hija de una madre degenerada, me hizo sufrir todas las torturas, todas las agonías que cabía esperar de su temperamento inmoderado y vicioso.
"My brother in the interval was dead, and at the end of the four years my father died too.
»Mi hermano había muerto entre tanto y, al final de aquellos cuatro años, mi padre murió también.
I was rich enough now--yet poor to hideous indigence: a nature the most gross, impure, depraved I ever saw, was associated with mine, and called by the law and by society a part of me.
Yo era rico, aunque espiritualmente pobre, puesto que sufría la odiosa miseria de soportar la compañía del ser más degradado y abominable que conociera jamás, y que era mi esposa ante la ley.
And I could not rid myself of it by any legal proceedings: for the doctors now discovered that _my wife_ was mad--her excesses had prematurely developed the germs of insanity.
Ni siquiera podía librarme de ella por procedimientos legales, porque los médicos acababan de descubrir que estaba loca. Sus excesos habían acelerado su insania...
Jane, you don't like my narrative; you look almost sick--shall I defer the rest to another day?"
Pero veo, Jane, que mi narración te deprime. ¿Prefieres que la terminemos otro día?
"No, sir, finish it now; I pity you--I do earnestly pity you."
-No, terminemos ahora.

"Pity, Jane, from some people is a noxious and insulting sort of tribute, which one is justified in hurling back in the teeth of those who offer it; but that is the sort of pity native to callous, selfish hearts; it is a hybrid, egotistical pain at hearing of woes, crossed with ignorant contempt for those who have endured them.

Me da usted mucha lástima. -Algunas personas, Jane, consideran ofensivo que les tengan lástima, porque cierta clase de compasión -la que experimentan los corazones endurecidos y egoístas- es una híbrida mezcla de disgusto por lo que les disgusta y de satisfacción por el mal ajeno.

But that is not your pity, Jane; it is not the feeling of which your whole face is full at this moment--with which your eyes are now almost overflowing--with which your heart is heaving--with which your hand is trembling in mine.
Pero tu piedad no es de esa especie: lo siento en la expresión de tus ojos, en el temblor de tus manos, en los latidos de tu corazón.
Your pity, my darling, is the suffering mother of love: its anguish is the very natal pang of the divine passion. I accept it, Jane; let the daughter have free advent--my arms wait to receive her."
Tu compasión hacia mí, querida, es hija de tu amor y la acepto con los brazos abiertos.
"Now, sir, proceed; what did you do when you found she was mad?"
-Continúe. ¿Qué hizo usted cuando supo que su mujer estaba loca?
"Jane, I approached the verge of despair; a remnant of self-respect was all that intervened between me and the gulf.
-Me hallaba al borde de la desesperación.

In the eyes of the world, I was doubtless covered with grimy dishonour; but I resolved to be clean in my own sight--and to the last I repudiated the contamination of her crimes, and wrenched myself from connection with her mental defects.
A los ojos del mundo yo estaba evidentemente cubierto de deshonor, pero resolví absolverme ante mí mismo rompiendo todo lazo con ella.

Still, society associated my name and person with hers; I yet saw her and heard her daily: something of her breath (faugh!) mixed with the air I breathed; and besides, I remembered I had once been her husband--that recollection was then, and is now, inexpressibly odious to me; moreover, I knew that while she lived I could never be the husband of another and better wife; and, though five years my senior (her family and her father had lied to me even in the particular of her age), she was likely to live as long as I, being as robust in frame as she was infirm in mind.

La sociedad unía mi nombre al suyo, yo la veía a diario, respiraba el aire que su aliento contaminaba y, además, era su esposo -lo que me resultaba más odioso que nada- y sabía que mientras viviera, no podría unirme a una mujer mejor que ella. Tenía cinco años más que yo -su familia me había ocultado ese detalle-, pero físicamente estaba tan robusta como mentalmente enferma.
Thus, at the age of twenty-six, I was hopeless.
De modo que, a los veintiséis años de edad, yo era un hombre desesperado.

"One night I had been awakened by her yells--(since the medical men had pronounced her mad, she had, of course, been shut up)--it was a fiery West Indian night; one of the description that frequently precede the hurricanes of those climates.
(Desde que fuera declarada loca la teníamos encerrada, naturalmente.) Era una bochornosa noche antillana, y se sentía en el ambiente caliginoso la proximidad de un huracán.
Being unable to sleep in bed, I got up and opened the window.
No pudiendo dormir, me levanté y abrí la ventana.
The air was like sulphur-steams--I could find no refreshment anywhere.
El aire tormentoso olía a azufre.

Mosquitoes came buzzing in and hummed sullenly round the room; the sea, which I could hear from thence, rumbled dull like an earthquake--black clouds were casting up over it; the moon was setting in the waves, broad and red, like a hot cannon-ball--she threw her last bloody glance over a world quivering with the ferment of tempest.

Se oía el rumor del mar como un terremoto, negras nubes cubrían el cielo y la luna, roja y enorme como una ardiente bala de cañón, se reflejaba en las olas. El ambiente y la atmósfera pesada influían en mi ánimo.

I was physically influenced by the atmosphere and scene, and my ears were filled with the curses the maniac still shrieked out; wherein she momentarily mingled my name with such a tone of demon-hate, with such language!--no professed harlot ever had a fouler vocabulary than she: though two rooms off, I heard every word--the thin partitions of the West India house opposing but slight obstruction to her wolfish cries.

Súbitamente la oí pronunciar mi nombre con demoníaco acento de odio y percibí su abominable lenguaje. Aunque dormía dos cuartos más allá del mío, el estilo de construcción de las casas de aquel país no permitía ahogar sus aullidos de loba.
"'This life,' said I at last, 'is hell: this is the air--those are the sounds of the bottomless pit!
»Pensé que aquella vida era un infierno y aquellos gritos los lamentos terroríficos de los condenados.
I have a right to deliver myself from it if I can.
Tengo derecho a librarme de esto, si puedo -reflexioné-.
The sufferings of this mortal state will leave me with the heavy flesh that now cumbers my soul.
Y sin duda me libraré si abandono mi carne mortal.
Of the fanatic's burning eternity I have no fear: there is not a future state worse than this present one--let me break away, and go home to God!'
No temo a los castigos del más allá, porque no pueden ser más horribles que los que sufro aquí. ¡Rompamos la cadena y entreguémonos en manos de Dios!
"I said this whilst I knelt down at, and unlocked a trunk which contained a brace of loaded pistols: I mean to shoot myself.
»Y pensando así, abrí un baúl que contenía un par de pistolas con el propósito de suicidarme.
