You, penniless! Famous equality and fraternisation!
¿Yo rica, con una riqueza que no he ganado ni merecido, y ustedes pobres?
Close union! Intimate attachment!"
¡Vaya una fraternidad y vaya una unión!
"But, Jane, your aspirations after family ties and domestic happiness may be realised otherwise than by the means you contemplate: you may marry."
-Sus deseos de tener una familia pueden realizarse cuando se case.
"Nonsense, again!
-¡Tontería!
Marry! I don't want to marry, and never shall marry."
No quiero casarme y no me casaré nunca.
"That is saying too much: such hazardous affirmations are a proof of the excitement under which you labour."
-Eso es mucho decir, y sólo prueba lo muy excitada que está.
"It is not saying too much: I know what I feel, and how averse are my inclinations to the bare thought of marriage.
-No es mucho decir. Sé lo que siento y lo poco inclinada que me encuentro al matrimonio.
No one would take me for love; and I will not be regarded in the light of a mere money speculation.
Nadie se enamorará de mí, y si alguien se casara conmigo sería por mi dinero.
And I do not want a stranger--unsympathising, alien, different from me; I want my kindred: those with whom I have full fellow- feeling.
Y no deseo a mi lado un ser ajeno a mi alma. Quiero convivir con aquellos que comparten mis sentimientos.
Say again you will be my brother: when you uttered the words I was satisfied, happy; repeat them, if you can, repeat them sincerely."
Dígame otra vez que es mi hermano; dígalo, si puede, con sinceridad y me sentiré feliz.
"I think I can.
-Puedo.
I know I have always loved my own sisters; and I know on what my affection for them is grounded,--respect for their worth and admiration of their talents.
Sé que si he querido a mis hermanas ha sido porque estimo sus virtudes y admiro sus méritos.

You too have principle and mind: your tastes and habits resemble Diana's and Mary's; your presence is always agreeable to me; in your conversation I have already for some time found a salutary solace.
Usted es inteligente y virtuosa, tiene los mismos gustos que Diana y Mary, su presencia y su conversación me son agradables.
I feel I can easily and naturally make room in my heart for you, as my third and youngest sister."
Creo que puedo reservar un sitio para usted en mi corazón, como una hermana mía.
"Thank you: that contents me for to-night.
-Gracias. Eso me basta por hoy.
Now you had better go; for if you stay longer, you will perhaps irritate me afresh by some mistrustful scruple."
Y ahora vale más que se vaya, John, porque si se queda tal vez me haga enfadar otra vez con sus escrúpulos.
"And the school, Miss Eyre?
¿Y la escuela, Jane?
It must now be shut up, I suppose?"
¿Habrá que cerrarla?
"No. I will retain my post of mistress till you get a substitute."
-Seguiré en el cargo hasta que se encuentre una sustituta.
He smiled approbation: we shook hands, and he took leave.
Sonrió, aprobatorio. Nos estrechamos la mano y se fue.
I need not narrate in detail the further struggles I had, and arguments I used, to get matters regarding the legacy settled as I wished.
No es preciso detallar los ulteriores esfuerzos y argumentos que empleé para convencer a mis primos.

My task was a very hard one; but, as I was absolutely resolved--as my cousins saw at length that my mind was really and immutably fixed on making a just division of the property--as they must in their own hearts have felt the equity of the intention; and must, besides, have been innately conscious that in my place they would have done precisely what I wished to do--they yielded at length so far as to consent to put the affair to arbitration.
Mi tarea fue difícil, pero como estaba absolutamente resuelta a imponer mi voluntad y ellos comprendieron la sinceridad con que lo hacía, acordaron finalmente someter el asunto a arbitraje.
The judges chosen were Mr. Oliver and an able lawyer: both coincided in my opinion: I carried my point.
Los árbitros fueron Mr. Oliver y un inteligente abogado, que coincidieron con mi opinión.
The instruments of transfer were drawn out: St. John, Diana, Mary, and I, each became possessed of a competency.
Los documentos transmisorios fueron legalizados, y John, Diana y Mary entraron en posesión de sus partes respectivas.
CHAPTER XXXIV
XXXIV
It was near Christmas by the time all was settled: the season of general holiday approached.
Todo quedó arreglado poco antes de las fiestas de Navidad.
I now closed Morton school, taking care that the parting should not be barren on my side.
Abandoné la escuela después de procurar que me sustituyera alguien que no hiciese estériles mis esfuerzos en pro de las alumnas.
I had long felt with pleasure that many of my rustic scholars liked me, and when we parted, that consciousness was confirmed: they manifested their affection plainly and strongly.
La mayoría de ellas, según parecía, me apreciaban, y mi partida lo puso de manifiesto.

Deep was my gratification to find I had really a place in their unsophisticated hearts: I promised them that never a week should pass in future that I did not visit them, and give them an hour's teaching in their school.

Me sentí profundamente emocionada por el lugar que me habían concedido en sus inocentes corazones y les prometí que, en el porvenir, las visitaría todas las semanas y daría una hora de clase en la escuela.

Mr. Rivers came up as, having seen the classes, now numbering sixty girls, file out before me, and locked the door, I stood with the key in my hand, exchanging a few words of special farewell with some half-dozen of my best scholars: as decent, respectable, modest, and well-informed young women as could be found in the ranks of the British peasantry. And that is saying a great deal; for after all, the British peasantry are the best taught, best mannered, most self-respecting of any in Europe: since those days I have seen paysannes and Bauerinnen; and the best of them seemed to me ignorant, coarse, and besotted, compared with my Morton girls.

John Rivers llegó cuando yo, después de haberme despedido de las sesenta muchachas alineadas ante mí, cambiaba nuevos adioses con las mejores de mis discípulas: media docena de muchachas recatadas, modestas e instruidas como no se encontrarían fácilmente en el resto de Inglaterra ni en toda Europa.

"Do you consider you have got your reward for a season of exertion?" asked Mr. Rivers, when they were gone. "Does not the consciousness of having done some real good in your day and generation give pleasure?"
-¿No sientes -dijo John cuando todas hubieron salido- la satisfacción de haber hecho con esas muchachas algo en beneficio de tus semejantes?
"Doubtless."
-Sin duda.
"And you have only toiled a few months! Would not a life devoted to the task of regenerating your race be well spent?"
-Pues si eso ha sido así en pocos meses, ¿no crees que la tarea de dedicar toda la vida a la regeneración humana es hermosa?
"Yes," I said; "but I could not go on for ever so: I want to enjoy my own faculties as well as to cultivate those of other people.
-Sí -dije-, pero yo no puedo dedicarme sólo al bien de los demás.
I must enjoy them now; don't recall either my mind or body to the school; I am out of it and disposed for full holiday."
Deseo gozar de mi propia vida también.
He looked grave. "What now? What sudden eagerness is this you evince? What are you going to do?"
-¿Y qué vas a hacer ahora? -me preguntó gravemente.
"To be active: as active as I can.
-Trabajar en lo que está a mi alcance.
And first I must beg you to set Hannah at liberty, and get somebody else to wait on you."
Deseo que busques a alguien que sustituya a Hannah para que ésta me acompañe.
"Do you want her?"
-¿A dónde?
"Yes, to go with me to Moor House.
-A Moor House.
Diana and Mary will be at home in a week, and I want to have everything in order against their arrival."
Diana y Mary llegarán de aquí a una semana y quiero tenerlo todo arreglado para cuando vengan.
"I understand.
-Comprendo.
I thought you were for flying off on some excursion.
Creí que pensabas hacer algún viaje.
It is better so: Hannah shall go with you."
Sí, vale más que vaya Hannah contigo.
"Tell her to be ready by to-morrow then; and here is the schoolroom key: I will give you the key of my cottage in the morning."
-Bien; pues dile que esté lista para mañana. Toma la llave de la escuela.
He took it.
La de casa mañana te la daré.

"You give it up very gleefully," said he; "I don't quite understand your light-heartedness, because I cannot tell what employment you propose to yourself as a substitute for the one you are relinquishing.
-Quisiera saber -me dijo, mientras tomaba la llave- qué ocupación vas a realizar en lugar de la que dejas.
What aim, what purpose, what ambition in life have you now?"
¿Qué proyectos, qué ambiciones tienes ahora?

"My first aim will be to _clean down_ (do you comprehend the full force of the expression?)--to _clean down_ Moor House from chamber to cellar; my next to rub it up with bees-wax, oil, and an indefinite number of cloths, till it glitters again; my third, to arrange every chair, table, bed, carpet, with mathematical precision; afterwards I shall go near to ruin you in coals and peat to keep up good fires in every room; and lastly, the two days preceding that on which your sisters are expected will be devoted by Hannah and me to such a beating of eggs, sorting of currants, grating of spices, compounding of Christmas cakes, chopping up of materials for mince-pies, and solemnising of other culinary rites, as words can convey but an inadequate notion of to the uninitiated like you.

-Primero, limpiar Moor House de arriba abajo; segundo, encerarla y pulirla cuanto pueda; tercero, colocar todas las mesas, sillas y demás muebles con un orden y precisión matemáticos; cuarto, arruinarme comprando carbón y leña para que en cada cuarto haya un fuego excelente; quinto, dedicar a Hannah, dos días antes de que lleguen Diana y Mary, a batir tantos huevos, amasar tantas empanadas y preparar tantos bollos de Pascua, que no hay palabras en el diccionario para darle idea de la solemnidad de los ritos culinarios a que me entregaré.

My purpose, in short, is to have all things in an absolutely perfect state of readiness for Diana and Mary before next Thursday; and my ambition is to give them a beau-ideal of a welcome when they come."
En resumen: mi ambición consiste en que todo esté listo el próximo jueves para otorgar a mis primas una acogida que constituya el ideal de las acogidas familiares.
St. John smiled slightly: still he was dissatisfied.
John sonrió. No parecía del todo satisfecho.
"It is all very well for the present," said he; "but seriously, I trust that when the first flush of vivacity is over, you will look a little higher than domestic endearments and household joys."
-Eso está muy bien por el momento -dijo-, pero hablando seriamente, creo que después mirarás un poco más alto y no te limitarás a ocuparte de esas cuestiones domésticas.
"The best things the world has!"
-¡Son lo más agradable del mundo! -repuse.
I interrupted.
-No, Jane:
"No, Jane, no: this world is not the scene of fruition; do not attempt to make it so: nor of rest; do not turn slothful."
este mundo no es lugar de placeres, ni hay por qué intentar convertirlo en tal; como no hay tampoco que entregarse a la molicie.
"I mean, on the contrary, to be busy."
-Al contrario; voy a entregarme a la actividad.

"Jane, I excuse you for the present: two months' grace I allow you for the full enjoyment of your new position, and for pleasing yourself with this late-found charm of relationship; but _then_, I hope you will begin to look beyond Moor House and Morton, and sisterly society, and the selfish calm and sensual comfort of civilised affluence.
-Por ahora está bien, Jane. Admito que están bien dos meses para gozar el encanto de tu nueva situación y del cariño de tus nuevos parientes.
I hope your energies will then once more trouble you with their strength."
Pero después supongo que Moor House y Morton, y la compañía de mis hermanas, y la calma egoísta y la comodidad no te parecerán suficientes.
I looked at him with surprise.
Le miré con sorpresa.
"St. John," I said, "I think you are almost wicked to talk so.
-John -dije-: ¿cómo puedes hablar así?
I am disposed to be as content as a queen, and you try to stir me up to restlessness!
Me sentiré tan satisfecha como una reina.
To what end?"
¿En qué cosa mejor puedo pensar?
"To the end of turning to profit the talents which God has committed to your keeping; and of which He will surely one day demand a strict account.
-En aprovechar la inteligencia que Dios te ha concedido y de que, si no la ejercitas como debes, te pedirá algún día estrecha cuenta.
Jane, I shall watch you closely and anxiously--I warn you of that.
Te observo con mucho interés, Jane,
And try to restrain the disproportionate fervour with which you throw yourself into commonplace home pleasures.
y extraño el desmesurado interés que pones en los placeres vulgares del hogar.
Don't cling so tenaciously to ties of the flesh; save your constancy and ardour for an adequate cause; forbear to waste them on trite transient objects.
No te aferres tan tenazmente a las debilidades materiales. Reserva tu constancia y tu vehemencia para empresas más elevadas...
Do you hear, Jane?"
¿Entiendes, Jane?
"Yes; just as if you were speaking Greek.
-Tanto como si me hablaras en griego.
I feel I have adequate cause to be happy, and I _will_ be happy.
Para mí ser feliz es una empresa bastante elevada. Y lo seré.
Goodbye!"
¡Adiós!

Happy at Moor House I was, and hard I worked; and so did Hannah: she was charmed to see how jovial I could be amidst the bustle of a house turned topsy-turvy--how I could brush, and dust, and clean, and cook.

Y lo fui, en efecto, en Moor House, y trabajé de firme, con asombro de Hannah, admirada de la jovialidad con que me desenvolvía en el ajetreo de aquellos arreglos, de la energía con que pulía, limpiaba y cocinaba.
And really, after a day or two of confusion worse confounded, it was delightful by degrees to invoke order from the chaos ourselves had made.
Era delicioso, un par de días después, ver cómo iba resurgiendo el orden del caos que nosotras mismas habíamos producido.

I had previously taken a journey to S--- to purchase some new furniture: my cousins having given me _carte blanche_ to effect what alterations I pleased, and a sum having been set aside for that purpose.
Hice antes un viaje a S... para comprar algunos muebles, fin al que habíamos asignado algún dinero y para lo que mis primas me habían dado carta blanca.

The ordinary sitting-room and bedrooms I left much as they were: for I knew Diana and Mary would derive more pleasure from seeing again the old homely tables, and chairs, and beds, than from the spectacle of the smartest innovations. Still some novelty was necessary, to give to their return the piquancy with which I wished it to be invested.

La salita y los dormitorios fueron dejados como estaban, porque comprendí que a Diana y a Mary les placería hallarse en su ambiente acostumbrado, pero en cambio, una alcoba libre y un salón que no se usaba fueron decorados con bellos cortinajes y alfombras nuevas, con adornos de bronce cuidadosamente elegidos.

Dark handsome new carpets and curtains, an arrangement of some carefully selected antique ornaments in porcelain and bronze, new coverings, and mirrors, and dressing-cases, for the toilet tables, answered the end: they looked fresh without being glaring.
En las demás alcobas instalé tocadores y espejos nuevos. Los muebles comprados eran de caoba y las alfombras y cortinas de color carmesí oscuro.
When all was finished, I thought Moor House as complete a model of bright modest snugness within, as it was, at this season, a specimen of wintry waste and desert dreariness without.
Todo terminado, juzgué que Moor House era el modelo perfecto de una casa modesta bien acomodada por dentro, como era el tipo de la desolación invernal por fuera en aquella época del año.
The eventful Thursday at length came.
Llegó, al fin, el anhelado jueves.
They were expected about dark, and ere dusk fires were lit upstairs and below; the kitchen was in perfect trim; Hannah and I were dressed, and all was in readiness.
Esperábamos a las jóvenes al oscurecer. Las chimeneas estaban encendidas, la cocina preparada.
St. John arrived first.
John fue el primero en llegar.

I had entreated him to keep quite clear of the house till everything was arranged: and, indeed, the bare idea of the commotion, at once sordid and trivial, going on within its walls sufficed to scare him to estrangement.
Yo había procurado que no acudiese durante los preparativos, para no darle una impresión desagradable con el espectáculo de la casa revuelta.
He found me in the kitchen, watching the progress of certain cakes for tea, then baking.
Me encontró en la cocina vigilando la operación de amasar pastas para el té.
Approaching the hearth, he asked, "If I was at last satisfied with housemaid's work?" I answered by inviting him to accompany me on a general inspection of the result of my labours.
Me preguntó si estaba satisfecha de mis tareas domésticas y le contesté invitándole a inspeccionar el resultado de mis tareas.
With some difficulty, I got him to make the tour of the house.
No sin dificultad, le convencí de que me acompañase.

He just looked in at the doors I opened; and when he had wandered upstairs and downstairs, he said I must have gone through a great deal of fatigue and trouble to have effected such considerable changes in so short a time: but not a syllable did he utter indicating pleasure in the improved aspect of his abode.

Luego que hubimos recorrido toda la casa y subido y bajado escaleras, comentó que debía haberme tomado mucha molestia para llevar a la práctica aquellos cambios en tan poco tiempo, pero no añadió ni una sílaba que indicase que le placía el nuevo aspecto de la residencia.
This silence damped me. I thought perhaps the alterations had disturbed some old associations he valued.
Me disgustó aquel silencio, pensando que acaso le hubiera contrariado que se alterase el aspecto de la casa paterna.
I inquired whether this was the case: no doubt in a somewhat crest-fallen tone.
Le pregunté si era así.
"Not at all; he had, on the contrary, remarked that I had scrupulously respected every association: he feared, indeed, I must have bestowed more thought on the matter than it was worth.
-Nada de eso. Ya he observado el cuidado que has tenido en respetar cuanto pudiese significar un recuerdo.
How many minutes, for instance, had I devoted to studying the arrangement of this very room?--By-the-bye, could I tell him where such a book was?"
¿Cuántos minutos has dedicado a pensar en el arreglo de esa habitación? Y ¿puedes decirme dónde está colocado...?
I showed him the volume on the shelf: he took it down, and withdrawing to his accustomed window recess, he began to read it.
Se lo mostré, lo cogió y, retirándose a su acostumbrado rincón, junto a la ventana, comenzó a leer.
Now, I did not like this, reader.
Aquello me desagradó.
St. John was a good man; but I began to feel he had spoken truth of himself when he said he was hard and cold.
John, lector, era un hombre bueno, pero yo comenzaba a pensar que había dicho la verdad cuando él mismo afirmara que era frío y duro.
The humanities and amenities of life had no attraction for him--its peaceful enjoyments no charm.
La vida no presentaba atractivos para él.
Literally, he lived only to aspire--after what was good and great, certainly; but still he would never rest, nor approve of others resting round him.
No vivía más que para sus elevadas aspiraciones, y además desaprobaba que no se compartiesen.

As I looked at his lofty forehead, still and pale as a white stone--at his fine lineaments fixed in study--I comprehended all at once that he would hardly make a good husband: that it would be a trying thing to be his wife.

Mientras contemplaba su frente, pálida y serena como el mármol, y las bellas facciones de su rostro absorto en la lectura, comprendí que nunca podría ser un buen marido y que su esposa sería muy desgraciada.
I understood, as by inspiration, the nature of his love for Miss Oliver; I agreed with him that it was but a love of the senses.
Y concordé con él en que su amor por Rosamond era un amor puramente sensual.

I comprehended how he should despise himself for the feverish influence it exercised over him; how he should wish to stifle and destroy it; how he should mistrust its ever conducting permanently to his happiness or hers.
Me hice cargo de que John mismo se despreciaba por aquella emoción que ante ella sentía.

I saw he was of the material from which nature hews her heroes--Christian and Pagan--her lawgivers, her statesmen, her conquerors: a steadfast bulwark for great interests to rest upon; but, at the fireside, too often a cold cumbrous column, gloomy and out of place.

Y, en resumen, advertí que estaba hecho según el modelo de los héroes, cristianos o paganos, que han dado leyes a sus pueblos, que los han llevado a la conquista o los han convertido a una nueva creencia.
"This parlour is not his sphere," I reflected: "the Himalayan ridge or Caffre bush, even the plague-cursed Guinea Coast swamp would suit him better.
«Este salón no es lugar adecuado para él -pensé-. En la cordillera del Himalaya, en las selvas de Cafrería o en las costas de Guinea estaría más en su centro.
Well may he eschew the calm of domestic life; it is not his element: there his faculties stagnate--they cannot develop or appear to advantage.
La calma de la vida doméstica no es su elemento. Aquí sus facultades se enmohecen, faltas de desarrollo.

It is in scenes of strife and danger--where courage is proved, and energy exercised, and fortitude tasked--that he will speak and move, the leader and superior. A merry child would have the advantage of him on this hearth.
Sólo en medio de la lucha y el peligro, allí donde se requiera valor, fortaleza y energía, podrá hablar y actuar, manifestarse superior a los demás.
He is right to choose a missionary's career--I see it now."
Creo que acierta eligiendo la carrera de misionero.»
"They are coming! they are coming!" cried Hannah, throwing open the parlour door.
-¡Ya vienen, ya vienen! -gritó Hannah.
At the same moment old Carlo barked joyfully.
El perro ladró alegremente.
Out I ran.
Salí corriendo.
It was now dark; but a rumbling of wheels was audible.
Se sentía en la oscuridad ruido de ruedas.
Hannah soon had a lantern lit.
Hannah tomó una linterna.
The vehicle had stopped at the wicket; the driver opened the door: first one well-known form, then another, stepped out.
El coche se detuvo ante la verja. El cochero se apeó para abrir la portezuela y dos bien conocidas figuras bajaron del carruaje.
In a minute I had my face under their bonnets, in contact first with Mary's soft cheek, then with Diana's flowing curls.
Un momento después, mi cara se ponía en contacto, primero con las suaves mejillas de Mary y luego con los tirabuzones de Diana.
They laughed--kissed me--then Hannah: patted Carlo, who was half wild with delight; asked eagerly if all was well; and being assured in the affirmative, hastened into the house.
Rieron, me besaron; luego besaron a Hannah, acariciando a Carlo, medio loco de alegría, y entraron en la casa.
They were stiff with their long and jolting drive from Whitcross, and chilled with the frosty night air; but their pleasant countenances expanded to the cheerful firelight.
Aunque estaban heladas de frío después de su largo viaje en aquella inclemente noche, sus agradables facciones irradiaban luz.
While the driver and Hannah brought in the boxes, they demanded St. John. At this moment he advanced from the parlour.
Preguntaron por John quien salía en aquel momento del salón, y le abrazaron las dos a la vez.

They both threw their arms round his neck at once. He gave each one quiet kiss, said in a low tone a few words of welcome, stood a while to be talked to, and then, intimating that he supposed they would soon rejoin him in the parlour, withdrew there as to a place of refuge.
Él las besó con calma, pronunció algunas frases de bienvenida y, tras una breve conversación, suponiendo que ellas irían también al salón a poco, se retiró a su acostumbrado refugio.
I had lit their candles to go upstairs, but Diana had first to give hospitable orders respecting the driver; this done, both followed me.
Encendí bujías para subir al piso superior. Diana dio antes algunas órdenes hospitalarias concernientes al cochero.
They were delighted with the renovation and decorations of their rooms; with the new drapery, and fresh carpets, and rich tinted china vases: they expressed their gratification ungrudgingly.
Luego ambas me siguieron y manifestaron su satisfacción por las reformas introducidas, por las nuevas cortinas y alfombras y los ricos jarrones de China.
I had the pleasure of feeling that my arrangements met their wishes exactly, and that what I had done added a vivid charm to their joyous return home.
Tuve el placer de comprobar que mis modificaciones coincidían exactamente con los gustos de ellas y que constituían un motivo más de alegría a su llegada.
Sweet was that evening.
Aquella velada fue deliciosa.

My cousins, full of exhilaration, were so eloquent in narrative and comment, that their fluency covered St. John's taciturnity: he was sincerely glad to see his sisters; but in their glow of fervour and flow of joy he could not sympathise.

La entusiasta charla de mis primas, sus relatos y sus comentarios hacían olvidar la taciturnidad de John. Él estaba contento de ver a sus hermanas, pero no simpatizaba con las exteriorizaciones de su contento.

The event of the day--that is, the return of Diana and Mary--pleased him; but the accompaniments of that event, the glad tumult, the garrulous glee of reception irked him: I saw he wished the calmer morrow was come.
Su regreso le complacía, mas el tumulto inherente le desagradaba y ansiaba, sin duda, que llegase el día siguiente, menos bullicioso.

In the very meridian of the night's enjoyment, about an hour after tea, a rap was heard at the door. Hannah entered with the intimation that "a poor lad was come, at that unlikely time, to fetch Mr. Rivers to see his mother, who was drawing away."

Cuando estábamos en el momento más grato de aquella noche, una hora después del té, oímos llamar a la puerta, y Hannah entró con la noticia de que estaba allí un pobre muchacho a rogar que Mr. Rivers fuese a visitar a su madre, moribunda.
"Where does she live, Hannah?"
-¿Dónde vive, Hannah?
"Clear up at Whitcross Brow, almost four miles off, and moor and moss all the way."
-En Whitcross Brow, a más de cuatro millas y por un camino lleno de pantanos.
"Tell him I will go."
-Dile que iré.
"I'm sure, sir, you had better not.
-Creo que haría mejor en no ir, señor.
It's the worst road to travel after dark that can be: there's no track at all over the bog.
Es el peor camino para recorrer de noche que pueda imaginarse. No hay carretera.
You had better send word, sir, that you will be there in the morning."
Vale más que diga que irá mañana.
But he was already in the passage, putting on his cloak; and without one objection, one murmur, he departed.
Pero él ya estaba en el pasillo poniéndose el gabán y, sin una palabra, se fue.
It was then nine o'clock: he did not return till midnight.
Eran las nueve y no volvió hasta medianoche.
Starved and tired enough he was: but he looked happier than when he set out.
Se le notaba fatigado, pero parecía más satisfecho que cuando salió.
He had performed an act of duty; made an exertion; felt his own strength to do and deny, and was on better terms with himself.
Había cumplido un deber y realizado un sacrificio y estaba satisfecho de sí mismo.
I am afraid the whole of the ensuing week tried his patience.
La semana siguiente debió agotar su paciencia.
It was Christmas week: we took to no settled employment, but spent it in a sort of merry domestic dissipation.
Era la semana de Navidad y nosotras nos entregamos a una especie de alegre orgía doméstica.
The air of the moors, the freedom of home, the dawn of prosperity, acted on Diana and Mary's spirits like some life-giving elixir: they were gay from morning till noon, and from noon till night.
El aire de las alturas, la libertad de sentirse en su casa, obraban sobre Diana y Mary como estimulantes elixires y estaban contentas de la mañana a la noche y de la noche a la mañana.
They could always talk; and their discourse, witty, pithy, original, had such charms for me, that I preferred listening to, and sharing in it, to doing anything else.
Hablaban sin cesar y sus conversaciones me eran tan agradables, que prefería escucharlas a hablar yo misma.

St. John did not rebuke our vivacity; but he escaped from it: he was seldom in the house; his parish was large, the population scattered, and he found daily business in visiting the sick and poor in its different districts.
La parroquia era grande y la población muy diseminada. Tenía, pues, constantes ocasiones de visitar a los pobres y enfermos de las diferentes zonas.
One morning at breakfast, Diana, after looking a little pensive for some minutes, asked him, "If his plans were yet unchanged."
Una mañana, durante el desayuno, Diana le preguntó si sus planes seguían siendo los mismos.
"Unchanged and unchangeable," was the reply.
-Lo son y lo serán -contestó él.
And he proceeded to inform us that his departure from England was now definitively fixed for the ensuing year.
Y en seguida explicó que su marcha de Inglaterra estaba acordada para el año entrante.
"And Rosamond Oliver?" suggested Mary, the words seeming to escape her lips involuntarily: for no sooner had she uttered them, than she made a gesture as if wishing to recall them.
-¿Y Rosamond...? -insinuó Mary. Debió decir las palabras sin darse cuenta, porque al punto hizo un gesto como si quisiera rectificar.

"Rosamond Oliver," said he, "is about to be married to Mr. Granby, one of the best connected and most estimable residents in S-, grandson and heir to Sir Frederic Granby: I had the intelligence from her father yesterday."
-Rosamond Oliver -repuso John- va a casarse con Mr. Granby, hijo de Sir Frederic Granby y persona muy estimable y bien relacionada en E...
His sisters looked at each other and at me; we all three looked at him: he was serene as glass.
Las tres nos miramos y luego le contemplamos a él. Estaba tan sereno como un cristal.
"The match must have been got up hastily," said Diana: "they cannot have known each other long."
-Muy de prisa han concertado el enlace --comentó Diana-, porque no se deben conocer desde hace mucho tiempo.
"But two months: they met in October at the county ball at S-.
-Hace dos meses. Se conocieron en un baile, en S...

But where there are no obstacles to a union, as in the present case, where the connection is in every point desirable, delays are unnecessary: they will be married as soon as S--- Place, which Sir Frederic gives up to them, can he refitted for their reception."
Pero cuando no hay obstáculos, como en el caso presente, es natural abreviar. Se casarán en cuanto la casa que les regala Sir Frederic esté en condiciones de ser habitada.

The first time I found St. John alone after this communication, I felt tempted to inquire if the event distressed him: but he seemed so little to need sympathy, that, so far from venturing to offer him more, I experienced some shame at the recollection of what I had already hazarded.

La primera vez que vi a John a solas traté de averiguar si estaba disgustado, pero me pareció tan reacio a las manifestaciones de simpatía, que no me aventuré a expresarle lo que sentía por sus supuestos sufrimientos.
Besides, I was out of practice in talking to him: his reserve was again frozen over, and my frankness was congealed beneath it.
Además, su reserva había vuelto a hacerme perder la costumbre de hablarle con sinceridad.

He had not kept his promise of treating me like his sisters; he continually made little chilling differences between us, which did not at all tend to the development of cordiality: in short, now that I was acknowledged his kinswoman, and lived under the same roof with him, I felt the distance between us to be far greater than when he had known me only as the village schoolmistress.

Antes bien, marcaba a cada momento pequeñas y molestas diferencias nada propicias al aumento de una mutua cordialidad. A tal extremo, que ahora que vivíamos bajo el mismo techo me sentía menos unida a él que cuando era maestra de escuela en Morton.
When I remembered how far I had once been admitted to his confidence, I could hardly comprehend his present frigidity.
Recordando hasta qué punto había conseguido su confianza, me resultaba increíble su frialdad presente.
Such being the case, I felt not a little surprised when he raised his head suddenly from the desk over which he was stooping, and said--
Por todo ello, en la mencionada ocasión en que estábamos solos, no fue poco mi asombro cuando le vi alzar súbitamente la cabeza de sobre la mesa y le oí decir:
"You see, Jane, the battle is fought and the victory won."
-¿Ves, Jane? La batalla se ha dado y la victoria se ha conseguido.
Startled at being thus addressed, I did not immediately reply: after a moment's hesitation I answered--
La sorpresa me dejó atónita, pero al fin contesté:
"But are you sure you are not in the position of those conquerors whose triumphs have cost them too dear? Would not such another ruin you?"
-¿Estás seguro de que la victoria no te ha costado demasiado cara, como a muchos conquistadores?
"I think not; and if I were, it does not much signify; I shall never be called upon to contend for such another.
-Creo que no, y aunque fuera así, no importa.
The event of the conflict is decisive: my way is now clear; I thank God for it!"
El desenlace es definitivo y ahora no tengo obstáculos en mi camino, gracias a Dios.
So saying, he returned to his papers and his silence.
Y volvió a sus papeles y a su mutismo.

As our mutual happiness (_i.e._, Diana's, Mary's, and mine) settled into a quieter character, and we resumed our usual habits and regular studies, St. John stayed more at home: he sat with us in the same room, sometimes for hours together.

La felicidad que sentíamos Diana, Mary y yo acabó tomando un carácter más reposado, y entonces John estaba en casa con más frecuencia. Se sentaba en el mismo aposento que nosotras y a veces todos pasábamos varias horas juntos.

While Mary drew, Diana pursued a course of encyclopaedic reading she had (to my awe and amazement) undertaken, and I fagged away at German, he pondered a mystic lore of his own: that of some Eastern tongue, the acquisition of which he thought necessary to his plans.

Mientras Mary dibujaba, Diana seguía un curso de lecturas enciclopédicas que había emprendido con gran asombro mío, y yo me afanaba en el alemán. John estudiaba una lengua oriental, que creía necesaria para el desarrollo de sus planes.

Thus engaged, he appeared, sitting in his own recess, quiet and absorbed enough; but that blue eye of his had a habit of leaving the outlandish- looking grammar, and wandering over, and sometimes fixing upon us, his fellow-students, with a curious intensity of observation: if caught, it would be instantly withdrawn; yet ever and anon, it returned searchingly to our table.

Sentado en su rincón, parecía absorto y sereno, pero a veces sus azules ojos abandonaban los libros y se posaban sobre nosotras, examinándonos con curiosa intensidad. Si se le sorprendía, retiraba la vista inmediatamente, mas de vez en cuando volvía a dirigirla a nuestra mesa.

I wondered what it meant: I wondered, too, at the punctual satisfaction he never failed to exhibit on an occasion that seemed to me of small moment, namely, my weekly visit to Morton school; and still more was I puzzled when, if the day was unfavourable, if there was snow, or rain, or high wind, and his sisters urged me not to go, he would invariably make light of their solicitude, and encourage me to accomplish the task without regard to the elements.

Me asombraba, por otro lado, la satisfacción que nunca dejaba de expresar siempre que yo iba a realizar la prometida visita semanal a la escuela de Morton. Si sus hermanas me querían persuadir, los días de mal tiempo, de que no fuera, él, por el contrario, me excitaba a que acudiese desafiando los elementos adversos.
"Jane is not such a weakling as you would make her," he would say: "she can bear a mountain blast, or a shower, or a few flakes of snow, as well as any of us.
-Jane no es lo débil que suponéis -solía decir- y puede soportar un poco de viento o unos copos de nieve tan bien como el primero.
Her constitution is both sound and elastic;--better calculated to endure variations of climate than many more robust."
Su naturaleza es nerviosa y flexible, más apropiada para adaptarse a los cambios de clima que otras más robustas.

And when I returned, sometimes a good deal tired, and not a little weather-beaten, I never dared complain, because I saw that to murmur would be to vex him: on all occasions fortitude pleased him; the reverse was a special annoyance.

Y cuando yo volvía, muy cansada y a veces víctima de las inclemencias del tiempo, no osaba quejarme por temor a causarle contrariedad. La fortaleza en sufrir tales molestias le placía y lo contrario le disgustaba.
One afternoon, however, I got leave to stay at home, because I really had a cold.
No obstante, una tarde resolví quedarme en casa, porque realmente estaba acatarrada.
His sisters were gone to Morton in my stead: I sat reading Schiller; he, deciphering his crabbed Oriental scrolls.
Sus hermanas habían ido a Morton en mi lugar. Yo estaba sentada leyendo una obra de Schiller y él luchaba por descifrar sus orientales jeroglíficos.
As I exchanged a translation for an exercise, I happened to look his way: there I found myself under the influence of the ever-watchful blue eye.
Se me ocurrió mirarle y hallé que me contemplaba atentamente con sus azules ojos.

How long it had been searching me through and through, and over and over, I cannot tell: so keen was it, and yet so cold, I felt for the moment superstitious--as if I were sitting in the room with something uncanny.
Ignoro cuánto tiempo llevaba así; sólo sé que me sentí desasosegada.
"Jane, what are you doing?"
-¿Qué haces, Jane?
"Learning German."
-Aprender alemán.
"I want you to give up German and learn Hindostanee."
-Preferiría que dejase el alemán y aprendieses el indostaní (lengua del Sur de la India).
"You are not in earnest?"
-¿Hablas en serio?
"In such earnest that I must have it so: and I will tell you why."
-En serio. Me explicaré.

He then went on to explain that Hindostanee was the language he was himself at present studying; that, as he advanced, he was apt to forget the commencement; that it would assist him greatly to have a pupil with whom he might again and again go over the elements, and so fix them thoroughly in his mind; that his choice had hovered for some time between me and his sisters; but that he had fixed on me because he saw I could sit at a task the longest of the three.

La explicación consistió en manifestarme que era indostaní la lengua que él estudiaba, que solía olvidar lo que había aprendido, y que si tuviese una discípula con quien practicar los rudimentos, éstos no se le irían de la memoria, antes bien, quedarían -fijos en su mente. Agregó que me había preferido a mí por juzgarme la más apta de las tres mujeres.
Would I do him this favour?
¿Le haría este favor?
I should not, perhaps, have to make the sacrifice long, as it wanted now barely three months to his departure.
En todo caso, no sería largo el sacrificio, ya que contaba partir antes de tres meses.
St. John was not a man to be lightly refused: you felt that every impression made on him, either for pain or pleasure, was deep-graved and permanent.
No era fácil negar nada a John porque se comprendía que cualquier sensación, grata o ingrata, se grababa profundamente en él.
I consented.
Consentí.

When Diana and Mary returned, the former found her scholar transferred from her to her brother: she laughed, and both she and Mary agreed that St. John should never have persuaded them to such a step.
Cuando Diana y Mary regresaron hallaron a la maestra de Morton transformada en discípula del párroco. Se echaron a reír y opinaron que John no debía haberme metido en aquella aventura.
He answered quietly-- "I know it."
El repuso, tranquilamente: -Ya lo sé.
I found him a very patient, very forbearing, and yet an exacting master: he expected me to do a great deal; and when I fulfilled his expectations, he, in his own way, fully testified his approbation.
Descubrí que era un maestro muy paciente, muy tolerante y muy exigente a la vez. Esperaba mucho de mí, y cuando veía que llenaba sus esperanzas, manifestaba su aprobación a su modo.
By degrees, he acquired a certain influence over me that took away my liberty of mind: his praise and notice were more restraining than his indifference.
Poco a poco fue adquiriendo cierta autoridad sobre mí, y su influencia y atención me parecieron más cohibidores que su indiferencia.
I could no longer talk or laugh freely when he was by, because a tiresomely importunate instinct reminded me that vivacity (at least in me) was distasteful to him.
Ya no me atrevía a hablar ni a reír a mis anchas cuando él estaba presente, porque un espíritu de clarividencia me advertía que eso le disgustaba a él.
I was so fully aware that only serious moods and occupations were acceptable, that in his presence every effort to sustain or follow any other became vain: I fell under a freezing spell.

Yo comprendía muy bien que a John sólo le placían los modales graves y las ocupaciones serias y que era vano tratar de obrar de otro modo en su presencia. Acabé hallándome bajo el efecto de una fría sugestión.
When he said "go," I went; "come," I came; "do this," I did it.
Si él me decía: «vete», me iba; si «ven», iba; si «haz esto», lo hacía.
But I did not love my servitude: I wished, many a time, he had continued to neglect me.
Pero no me agradaba aquella sumisión y hubiera preferido que, como antes, mi primo no se ocupara de mí.
One evening when, at bedtime, his sisters and I stood round him, bidding him good-night, he kissed each of them, as was his custom; and, as was equally his custom, he gave me his hand.
Una noche, al ir a acostarnos, le rodeamos como de costumbre para desearle buenas noches, y como de costumbre también, después de besarle sus hermanas, él y yo nos dimos la mano.
Diana, who chanced to be in a frolicsome humour (_she_ was not painfully controlled by his will; for hers, in another way, was as strong), exclaimed--
Diana, que estaba de buen humor (ella y Mary no experimentaban el influjo de la voluntad de John porque, en su estilo, eran tan fuertes como su hermano), exclamó:
"St. John! you used to call Jane your third sister, but you don't treat her as such: you should kiss her too."
-Vaya, John: tú llamas a Jane tu tercera hermana, pero no te comportas como si lo fuera. Bésala también.
She pushed me towards him.
Y me empujó hacia él.

I thought Diana very provoking, and felt uncomfortably confused; and while I was thus thinking and feeling, St. John bent his head; his Greek face was brought to a level with mine, his eyes questioned my eyes piercingly--he kissed me.
Pensé que Diana era muy imprudente y me sentí desagradablemente turbada. John inclinó la cabeza, hasta poner sus griegas facciones a nivel de las mías.

There are no such things as marble kisses or ice kisses, or I should say my ecclesiastical cousin's salute belonged to one of these classes; but there may be experiment kisses, and his was an experiment kiss.
No creo que exista nada parecido al beso de un mármol o de un trozo de hielo, mas me atrevo, con todo, a decir que el beso de mi eclesiástico pariente pertenecía a un género semejante.
When given, he viewed me to learn the result; it was not striking: I am sure I did not blush; perhaps I might have turned a little pale, for I felt as if this kiss were a seal affixed to my fetters.

En todo caso, tuve la impresión de que me besaba por vía de ensayo, ya que luego me contempló como para comprobar el resultado. Ciertamente, no fue nada impresionante y estoy segura de que no me sonrojé.
He never omitted the ceremony afterwards, and the gravity and quiescence with which I underwent it, seemed to invest it for him with a certain charm.
Desde entonces no prescindió nunca de repetir aquella ceremonia y la tranquila gravedad con que yo recibía su beso parecía tener cierto encanto para él.

As for me, I daily wished more to please him; but to do so, I felt daily more and more that I must disown half my nature, stifle half my faculties, wrest my tastes from their original bent, force myself to the adoption of pursuits for which I had no natural vocation.

Cada vez deseaba más complacerle, pero también cada vez experimentaba más la sensación de que había de cambiar mis gustos, transformar mi naturaleza, modificar mis inclinaciones y forzarme a propósito hacia los que no sentía el menor apego.
He wanted to train me to an elevation I could never reach; it racked me hourly to aspire to the standard he uplifted.
Él deseaba elevarme a una altura que yo no podía alcanzar y hacerme imitar modelos fuera de mis posibilidades.
The thing was as impossible as to mould my irregular features to his correct and classic pattern, to give to my changeable green eyes the sea-blue tint and solemn lustre of his own.
Tan imposible era aquello como igualar mis irregulares facciones a las suyas, perfectas, y sustituir mis ojos, de cambiantes tonalidades verdes, por los suyos, azules como el mar.
Perhaps you think I had forgotten Mr. Rochester, reader, amidst these changes of place and fortune.
Acaso, lector, imagines que yo había olvidado a Rochester en el curso de mi cambio de fortuna.
Not for a moment.
Ni por un momento.

His idea was still with me, because it was not a vapour sunshine could disperse, nor a sand-traced effigy storms could wash away; it was a name graven on a tablet, fated to last as long as the marble it inscribed.

Su recuerdo vivía en mí: no era una nube de estío que el sol disipa, ni una figura trazada en la arena, que borra el viento. No: su recuerdo era como un nombre grabado en un mármol, persistente en él mientras el mármol exista.

The craving to know what had become of him followed me everywhere; when I was at Morton, I re-entered my cottage every evening to think of that; and now at Moor House, I sought my bedroom each night to brood over it.
Si su imagen me perseguía en Morton, también ahora, en mi lecho de Moor House, pensaba en él.

In the course of my necessary correspondence with Mr. Briggs about the will, I had inquired if he knew anything of Mr. Rochester's present residence and state of health; but, as St. John had conjectured, he was quite ignorant of all concerning him.

En el curso de mi correspondencia con Briggs, el procurador, yo le había preguntado sobre la residencia actual y la salud de Rochester, pero Briggs, como John supusiera, ignoraba por completo tales extremos.
I then wrote to Mrs. Fairfax, entreating information on the subject.
Entonces escribí a Mrs.
I had calculated with certainty on this step answering my end: I felt sure it would elicit an early answer.
Fairfax preguntándole lo mismo, y contando con una rápida contestación.
I was astonished when a fortnight passed without reply; but when two months wore away, and day after day the post arrived and brought nothing for me, I fell a prey to the keenest anxiety.

Grande fue mi asombro cuando pasaron quince días sin recibir noticias. Pero cuando las dos semanas se convirtieron en dos meses y el correo continuaba sin traerme carta alguna, me sentí presa de una ansiedad mortal.
I wrote again: there was a chance of my first letter having missed.
Volví a escribir, en la suposición de que mi primera carta no hubiera llegado.
Renewed hope followed renewed effort: it shone like the former for some weeks, then, like it, it faded, flickered: not a line, not a word reached me.
Mi esperanza se mantuvo varias semanas, y luego comenzó la tensión de antes. Ni una línea, ni una palabra.
When half a year wasted in vain expectancy, my hope died out, and then I felt dark indeed.
Cuando hubo transcurrido medio año sin noticias, mi esperanza murió y volví a sentirme entre sombras.
A fine spring shone round me, which I could not enjoy.
No pude, pues, gozar de la magnífica primavera que nos rodeaba.
Summer approached; Diana tried to cheer me: she said I looked ill, and wished to accompany me to the sea-side.
Llegaba el verano. Diana, preocupada por mi salud, quería llevarme a alguna playa.

This St. John opposed; he said I did not want dissipation, I wanted employment; my present life was too purposeless, I required an aim; and, I suppose, by way of supplying deficiencies, he prolonged still further my lessons in Hindostanee, and grew more urgent in requiring their accomplishment: and I, like a fool, never thought of resisting him--I could not resist him.

John se opuso, alegando que yo no necesitaba distracción, sino ocupaciones, ya que mi vida estaba demasiado vacía, de lo cual deduje que se proponía llenar las lagunas que había en ella con más prolongadas sesiones de indostaní. Así era, y no pensé en resistirle ni hubiera conseguido resistir.
One day I had come to my studies in lower spirits than usual; the ebb was occasioned by a poignantly felt disappointment.
Un día acudí a mis lecciones con menos voluntad que de costumbre.

Hannah had told me in the morning there was a letter for me, and when I went down to take it, almost certain that the long-looked for tidings were vouchsafed me at last, I found only an unimportant note from Mr. Briggs on business.
Hannah me había avisado por la mañana que había una carta para mí, y cuando fui a recogerla, cierta de que las noticias esperadas llegaban al fin, me encontré con una insulsa nota de Mr. Briggs.
The bitter check had wrung from me some tears; and now, as I sat poring over the crabbed characters and flourishing tropes of an Indian scribe, my eyes filled again.
La amarga decepción me hizo verter lágrimas y después, mientras luchaba con los indescifrables caracteres y las floridas metáforas de un escritor indio, sentí humedecerse de nuevo mis ojos.
St. John called me to his side to read; in attempting to do this my voice failed me: words were lost in sobs.
John me llamó para que leyera. Al hacerlo se me entrecortaba la voz y los sollozos impedían oír mis palabras.
He and I were the only occupants of the parlour: Diana was practising her music in the drawing-room, Mary was gardening--it was a very fine May day, clear, sunny, and breezy.
Diana estaba tocando en el salón grande y Mary paseaba por el jardín. Hacía un bello, soleado, claro y fresco día de mayo.
My companion expressed no surprise at this emotion, nor did he question me as to its cause; he only said--
Mi primo no pareció extrañar mi emoción, ni me preguntó los motivos, limitándose a decir:
"We will wait a few minutes, Jane, till you are more composed."
-Esperemos unos minutos, Jane, hasta que te tranquilices.

And while I smothered the paroxysm with all haste, he sat calm and patient, leaning on his desk, and looking like a physician watching with the eye of science an expected and fully understood crisis in a patient's malady.
Y mientras yo me entregaba a los paroxismos de mi dolor, él, sentado ante el pupitre, me contemplaba como un médico pueda contemplar las reacciones de un paciente.
Having stifled my sobs, wiped my eyes, and muttered something about not being very well that morning, I resumed my task, and succeeded in completing it.
Después de dominar mis sollozos, enjugar mis lágrimas y murmurar que no me encontraba bien aquella mañana, reanudé la tarea y logré concluirla.
St. John put away my books and his, locked his desk, and said-- "Now, Jane, you shall take a walk; and with me."
John entonces, apartó su libro y el mío y dijo: -Vamos a dar un paseo, Jane. -Bueno.
"I will call Diana and Mary."
Voy a llamar a Diana y a Mary.
"No; I want only one companion this morning, and that must be you.
-No. No quiero que me acompañe nadie más que tú.
Put on your things; go out by the kitchen-door: take the road towards the head of Marsh Glen: I will join you in a moment."
Arréglate, sal por la puerta de la cocina y toma el camino de Marsh Clen. Te alcanzaré enseguida.
I know no medium: I never in my life have known any medium in my dealings with positive, hard characters, antagonistic to my own, between absolute submission and determined revolt.
Durante toda mi vida, yo no había sabido, ante los caracteres enérgicos y duros, tan distintos al mío, optar por el término medio, sino someterme del todo o rebelarme abiertamente.

I have always faithfully observed the one, up to the very moment of bursting, sometimes with volcanic vehemence, into the other; and as neither present circumstances warranted, nor my present mood inclined me to mutiny, I observed careful obedience to St. John's directions; and in ten minutes I was treading the wild track of the glen, side by side with him.

En mis relaciones con John siempre hasta entonces me había sometido, y sin deseo alguno de sublevarme, seguí sus instrucciones y, diez minutos después, caminaba a su lado por el abrupto sendero del valle. Soplaba desde los montes una brisa del Oeste, olorosa a juncos y brezos.

The breeze was from the west: it came over the hills, sweet with scents of heath and rush; the sky was of stainless blue; the stream descending the ravine, swelled with past spring rains, poured along plentiful and clear, catching golden gleams from the sun, and sapphire tints from the firmament.
El cielo era de un inmaculado azul. El río, lleno por las lluvias de primavera, fluía, sereno, en el fondo del valle, reflejando los dorados rayos del sol y los tonos de zafiro del firmamento.

As we advanced and left the track, we trod a soft turf, mossy fine and emerald green, minutely enamelled with a tiny white flower, and spangled with a star-like yellow blossom: the hills, meantime, shut us quite in; for the glen, towards its head, wound to their very core.
Dejamos el camino y avanzamos por un prado de hierba menuda, verde, esmaltada de minúsculas flores amarillas y blancas.

"Let us rest here," said St. John, as we reached the first stragglers of a battalion of rocks, guarding a sort of pass, beyond which the beck rushed down a waterfall; and where, still a little farther, the mountain shook off turf and flower, had only heath for raiment and crag for gem--where it exaggerated the wild to the savage, and exchanged the fresh for the frowning--where it guarded the forlorn hope of solitude, and a last refuge for silence.

-Quedémonos aquí -dijo John cuando alcanzamos la primera hilera de un batallón de rocas que guardaban una especie de paso que desembocaba cerca de una cascada. Más allá, la montaña aparecía desnuda de césped y flores y sólo malezas la vestían y riscos la adornaban.
I took a seat: St. John stood near me.
John tomó también asiento a mi lado.

He looked up the pass and down the hollow; his glance wandered away with the stream, and returned to traverse the unclouded heaven which coloured it: he removed his hat, let the breeze stir his hair and kiss his brow.
Miró más allá del paso, contempló las aguas del río y luego volvió la vista al cielo sereno. Se quitó el sombrero, dejando que la brisa acariciase su cabello y besase sus sienes.
He seemed in communion with the genius of the haunt: with his eye he bade farewell to something.
Por la expresión de sus ojos se comprendía que estaba despidiéndose mentalmente de lo que le circundaba.
"And I shall see it again," he said aloud, "in dreams when I sleep by the Ganges: and again in a more remote hour--when another slumber overcomes me--on the shore of a darker stream!"
-No volveré a ver esto más, sino en sueños -dijo-, cuando duerma a orillas del Ganges o de algún río más remoto aún.
Strange words of a strange love!
¡Extrañas palabras, que testimoniaban un extraño amor a su tierra natal!
An austere patriot's passion for his fatherland!
Durante media hora guardamos mutuo silencio.
He sat down; for half-an-hour we never spoke; neither he to me nor I to him: that interval past, he recommenced--
Al fin, él comenzó:
"Jane, I go in six weeks; I have taken my berth in an East Indiaman which sails on the 20th of June."
-Jane: me voy dentro de seis semanas. Embarco en un navío que zarpa para la India el 20 de junio.
"God will protect you; for you have undertaken His work," I answered.
-Dios te proteja, ya que lo haces a gloria suya -dije.
"Yes," said he, "there is my glory and joy.
-Sí -repuso-; ése es mi orgullo y mi alegría.
I am the servant of an infallible Master.
Soy servidor de un señor infalible.
I am not going out under human guidance, subject to the defective laws and erring control of my feeble fellow-worms: my king, my lawgiver, my captain, is the All-perfect.
No actúa bajo dirección humana, sujeto a las leyes imperfectas y a la errónea dirección de mis flacos semejantes. Mi rey, mi legislador, mi capitán es el Todopoderoso.
It seems strange to me that all round me do not burn to enlist under the same banner,--to join in the same enterprise."
Me asombra que los que me rodean no se alisten bajo el mismo estandarte, no se asocien a la misma empresa.
"All have not your powers, and it would be folly for the feeble to wish to march with the strong."
-Todos no tienen tu energía. Sería una locura en el débil seguir los pasos del fuerte.
"I do not speak to the feeble, or think of them: I address only such as are worthy of the work, and competent to accomplish it."
-No pienso en los débiles: pienso en los que son dignos de la tarea y capaces de realizarla.
"Those are few in number, and difficult to discover."
-Pocos son y difíciles de encontrar. -Tienes razón.

"You say truly; but when found, it is right to stir them up--to urge and exhort them to the effort--to show them what their gifts are, and why they were given--to speak Heaven's message in their ear,--to offer them, direct from God, a place in the ranks of His chosen."
Por eso, cuando se encuentran, debe exhortárseles a que se unan al esfuerzo común, hacerles oír las palabras de Dios, ofrecerles un puesto entre los elegidos.
"If they are really qualified for the task, will not their own hearts be the first to inform them of it?"
-¿No crees que los aptos para esa labor se ofrecerían a ella espontáneamente si les llamara a ella la voz de su corazón?
I felt as if an awful charm was framing round and gathering over me: I trembled to hear some fatal word spoken which would at once declare and rivet the spell.
Sentí la impresión de que un sortilegio se abatía sobre mí y temblé al pensar que iba a oír las palabras fatales que ratificarían el hechizo.
"And what does _your_ heart say?" demanded St. John.
-¿Y qué dice la voz de tu corazón? -preguntó John.
"My heart is mute,--my heart is mute," I answered, struck and thrilled.
-Mi corazón permanece mudo, mudo... -respondí, estremecida.
"Then I must speak for it," continued the deep, relentless voice.
-Yo hablaré entonces por él.
"Jane, come with me to India: come as my helpmeet and fellow-labourer."
Jane: ven conmigo a la India para ser mi compañera y mi colaboradora.
The glen and sky spun round: the hills heaved!
Los campos, el cielo, los montes giraron en torno mío.
It was as if I had heard a summons from Heaven--as if a visionary messenger, like him of Macedonia, had enounced, "Come over and help us!"
Me parecía escuchar una llamada del cielo, las palabras de un iluminado...
But I was no apostle,--I could not behold the herald,--I could not receive his call.
Pero yo no era un apóstol, no podía atender la llamada.
"Oh, St. John!"
-¡John! -exclamé-.
I cried, "have some mercy!"
¡Ten piedad de mí!
I appealed to one who, in the discharge of what he believed his duty, knew neither mercy nor remorse.
Apelaba a la piedad de un hombre que, en cumplimiento de lo que creía su deber, no conocía la piedad ni el remordimiento.
He continued--
Continuó:
"God and nature intended you for a missionary's wife.
-Dios y la naturaleza te han creado para ser la esposa de un misionero.
It is not personal, but mental endowments they have given you: you are formed for labour, not for love.
No te han sido otorgadas dotes físicas, sino espirituales. No estás hecha para el amor, sino para la labor.
A missionary's wife you must--shall be.
Debes ser la esposa de un misionero, y serás la mía.
You shall be mine: I claim you--not for my pleasure, but for my Sovereign's service."
Te reclamo, no en nombre de mi placer personal, sino en el de mi Soberano.
"I am not fit for it: I have no vocation," I said.
-No sirvo para eso. No tengo vocación -dije.
He had calculated on these first objections: he was not irritated by them.
No se irritó. Tenía previstas las primeras objeciones.

Indeed, as he leaned back against the crag behind him, folded his arms on his chest, and fixed his countenance, I saw he was prepared for a long and trying opposition, and had taken in a stock of patience to last him to its close--resolved, however, that that close should be conquest for him.
Se apoyó contra la roca que había a su espalda, cruzó los brazos y me miró con serenidad. Comprendí que estaba preparado para una oposición tenaz y dispuesto a vencerla.
"Humility, Jane," said he, "is the groundwork of Christian virtues: you say right that you are not fit for the work.
-La humildad, Jane, es la principal de las virtudes cristianas --dijo-. En tal sentido, haces bien en contestar que no sirves para eso.
Who is fit for it? Or who, that ever was truly called, believed himself worthy of the summons?
¿Quién de los que realmente han sido llamados por Dios se ha creído digno de la llamada?
I, for instance, am but dust and ashes.
Yo, por ejemplo, no soy sino polvo y ceniza.
With St. Paul, I acknowledge myself the chiefest of sinners; but I do not suffer this sense of my personal vileness to daunt me.
Como San Pablo, me considero el mayor de los pecadores, pero la convicción de mi insignificancia personal no me aparta de la tarea.

I know my Leader: that He is just as well as mighty; and while He has chosen a feeble instrument to perform a great task, He will, from the boundless stores of His providence, supply the inadequacy of the means to the end.
Dios es infinitamente bueno y poderoso y cuando elige un débil instrumento para una labor grandiosa, Él proveerá a lo que falte.
Think like me, Jane--trust like me.
Piensa como yo, Jane, y acertarás.
"I do not understand a missionary life: I have never studied missionary labours."
-No estoy capacitada para una vida misionera. Nunca he estudiado los trabajos de las misiones.
"There I, humble as I am, can give you the aid you want: I can set you your task from hour to hour; stand by you always; help you from moment to moment.
-En eso, por humilde que yo pueda ser, me cabe ayudarte. Te mostraré tu tarea, hora a hora, te ayudaré siempre que lo necesites.
This I could do in the beginning: soon (for I know your powers) you would be as strong and apt as myself, and would not require my help."
Eso sólo al principio, porque conozco tu capacidad y pronto serás tan apta como yo mismo y no necesitarás mi ayuda.
"But my powers--where are they for this undertaking? I do not feel them.
-¿Mi capacidad? ¿Dónde está mi capacidad para tal empresa?
Nothing speaks or stirs in me while you talk. I am sensible of no light kindling--no life quickening--no voice counselling or cheering.
Mientras me hablas, nada en mi interior me aconseja, ninguna luz me alumbra.

Oh, I wish I could make you see how much my mind is at this moment like a rayless dungeon, with one shrinking fear fettered in its depths--the fear of being persuaded by you to attempt what I cannot accomplish!"
Quisiera que comprendieses lo que pasa en mi alma en este momento en que tú me llamas a una tarea que yo no puedo desempeñar.
"I have an answer for you--hear it.
-Escucha.
I have watched you ever since we first met: I have made you my study for ten months.
Te he venido observando desde que nos conocimos, hace diez meses.
I have proved you in that time by sundry tests: and what have I seen and elicited?
Te he sometido a varias pruebas sin que lo notases.

In the village school I found you could perform well, punctually, uprightly, labour uncongenial to your habits and inclinations; I saw you could perform it with capacity and tact: you could win while you controlled.
En la escuela de la aldea he observado que cumplías bien, puntual y eficazmente una tarea que no estaba en tus costumbres ni inclinaciones.
In the calm with which you learnt you had become suddenly rich, I read a mind clear of the vice of Demas:--lucre had no undue power over you.
La serenidad con que recibiste la noticia de que eras rica me hizo ver que no te tienta el afán de lucro.

In the resolute readiness with which you cut your wealth into four shares, keeping but one to yourself, and relinquishing the three others to the claim of abstract justice, I recognised a soul that revelled in the flame and excitement of sacrifice.
En la resuelta facilidad con que espontáneamente dividiste tus bienes en cuatro partes reconocí un alma que arde en la llama de la abnegación y el sacrificio.

In the tractability with which, at my wish, you forsook a study in which you were interested, and adopted another because it interested me; in the untiring assiduity with which you have since persevered in it--in the unflagging energy and unshaken temper with which you have met its difficulties--I acknowledge the complement of the qualities I seek.

En la docilidad con que, al pedírtelo, abandonaste un estudio que te interesaba por otro que me interesaba a mí, en la asiduidad con que lo has seguido, en la energía que has puesto en vencer sus dificultades, he reconocido el complemento de tus méritos, Jane.
Jane, you are docile, diligent, disinterested, faithful, constant, and courageous; very gentle, and very heroic: cease to mistrust yourself--I can trust you unreservedly.
Eres dócil, activa, desinteresada, leal, valerosa, constante, amable y heroica. Sí: puedo decírtelo sin reservas.
As a conductress of Indian schools, and a helper amongst Indian women, your assistance will be to me invaluable."
Serías una insuperable directora de escuelas indias y la ayuda que me prestarías cerca de las mujeres de aquel país sería inapreciable. El círculo de hierro se estrechaba en torno mío.
My iron shroud contracted round me; persuasion advanced with slow sure step.
La persuasión avanzaba, lenta pero segura.
Shut my eyes as I would, these last words of his succeeded in making the way, which had seemed blocked up, comparatively clear.
Las últimas palabras de John comenzaban a hacerme ver como relativamente fácil el camino que antes me pareciera infranqueable.
My work, which had appeared so vague, so hopelessly diffuse, condensed itself as he proceeded, and assumed a definite form under his shaping hand.
Mi tarea, antes difusa y problemática, se me figuraba más sencilla al adquirir una forma definida.
He waited for an answer.
Él esperaba una contestación.
I demanded a quarter of an hour to think, before I again hazarded a reply.
Le pedí que me dejara pensarlo quince minutos antes de arriesgar una respuesta.
"Very willingly," he rejoined; and rising, he strode a little distance up the pass, threw himself down on a swell of heath, and there lay still.
-Muy bien-dijo. Y, levantándose, se alejó a alguna distancia y se tendió sobre la hierba.
"I _can_ do what he wants me to do: I am forced to see and acknowledge that," I meditated,--"that is, if life be spared me.
«Soy capaz de hacer lo que él desea, lo reconozco -pensé-.
But I feel mine is not the existence to be long protracted under an Indian sun.
Creo que mi vida, en el clima de la India, no sería larga. ¿Y entonces?
What then?
Eso no le preocupaba a él.
He does not care for that: when my time came to die, he would resign me, in all serenity and sanctity, to the God who gave me.
Cuando llegara mi hora, me exhortaría a aceptar, con calma y santidad, la voluntad de Dios.
The case is very plain before me.
Eso es indudable.
In leaving England, I should leave a loved but empty land--Mr. Rochester is not there; and if he were, what is, what can that ever be to me?
Yéndome de Inglaterra abandonaría un país que amo, pero vacío para mí, ya que Rochester no está en él, y aunque estuviera, nada variaría en mi vida.
My business is to live without him now: nothing so absurd, so weak as to drag on from day to day, as if I were waiting some impossible change in circumstances, which might reunite me to him.
He de vivir sin Edward. Nada tan absurdo como esperar de día a día un imposible cambio de la situación que me permita reunirme con mi amado.
Of course (as St. John once said) I must seek another interest in life to replace the one lost: is not the occupation he now offers me truly the most glorious man can adopt or God assign?
Como John dice, debo buscarme otro interés y otra ocupación en la vida, y ¿hay alguna más digna que la que él me ofrece?
Is it not, by its noble cares and sublime results, the one best calculated to fill the void left by uptorn affections and demolished hopes?
¿No es por sus nobles propósitos y sus sublimes consecuencias la más apropiada para llenar el vacío que dejan los afectos fracasados y las esperanzas rotas?
I believe I must say, Yes--and yet I shudder. Alas!
Creo que debía decirle que sí y, sin embargo, temo...
If I join St. John, I abandon half myself: if I go to India, I go to premature death.
Al unirme a John, renuncio a la mitad de mí misma, a mi voluntad propia, y al ir a la India me condeno a una muerte prematura.
And how will the interval between leaving England for India, and India for the grave, be filled?
Y ¿cómo se llenará el intervalo entre Inglaterra y la India y la tumba?
Oh, I know well!
¡Me consta muy bien!
That, too, is very clear to my vision.
La perspectiva es clara.
By straining to satisfy St. John till my sinews ache, I _shall_ satisfy him--to the finest central point and farthest outward circle of his expectations.
Me constreñiré a complacer a John hasta que me duelan los huesos y los nervios me estallen, le complaceré hasta el máximo de sus esperanzas.
If I _do_ go with him--if I _do_ make the sacrifice he urges, I will make it absolutely: I will throw all on the altar--heart, vitals, the entire victim.
Si me voy con él haré el sacrificio que desea, lo haré absolutamente, me ofreceré entera en aras de ese sacrificio.
He will never love me; but he shall approve me; I will show him energies he has not yet seen, resources he has never suspected.
Él no me amará nunca, pero me aprobará. Yo le mostraré energías que no conoce, recursos que no sospecha.
Yes, I can work as hard as he can, and with as little grudging.
Sí: me cabe trabajar tanto como él lo haga.

"Consent, then, to his demand is possible: but for one item--one dreadful item. It is--that he asks me to be his wife, and has no more of a husband's heart for me than that frowning giant of a rock, down which the stream is foaming in yonder gorge.

»Puedo, pues, acceder a lo que me pide, pero debo hacerme a mí propia una advertencia, y es que en él no he de esperar encontrar un corazón de esposo más que pudiera encontrarlo en esta roca que me apoyo.
He prizes me as a soldier would a good weapon; and that is all.
Me aprecia como un soldado aprecia una buena espada, y nada más.
Unmarried to him, this would never grieve me; but can I let him complete his calculations--coolly put into practice his plans--go through the wedding ceremony?
No siendo esposa suya, esto me es igual. Pero ¿he de auxiliarle a realizar sus planes y a poner sus cálculos en práctica mediante el matrimonio?
Can I receive from him the bridal ring, endure all the forms of love (which I doubt not he would scrupulously observe) and know that the spirit was quite absent?
¿He de ostentar el anillo de casada, soportar todas las formas del amor, que -estoy segura- él observará escrupulosamente, y saber que el alma está ausente en todo eso?
Can I bear the consciousness that every endearment he bestows is a sacrifice made on principle? No: such a martyrdom would be monstrous.
¿Podría aceptar sus manifestaciones de cariño sabiendo que son sacrificios hechos en aras de sus principios?
I will never undergo it.
No: sería monstruoso aceptar tal marido.
As his sister, I might accompany him--not as his wife: I will tell him so."
Podré acompañarle como su hermana, pero no como su esposa, y así voy a decírselo.
I looked towards the knoll: there he lay, still as a prostrate column; his face turned to me: his eye beaming watchful and keen.
» Le miré. Seguía tendido, como una columna derribada.
He started to his feet and approached me.
Volvió la cabeza, se incorporó y vino a mi lado.
"I am ready to go to India, if I may go free."
-Estoy dispuesta a ir contigo a la India, pero conservando mi libertad.
"Your answer requires a commentary," he said; "it is not clear."
-Esa respuesta requiere aclaración.
"You have hitherto been my adopted brother--I, your adopted sister: let us continue as such: you and I had better not marry."
-Puesto que me has adoptado por hermana, continuaré siéndolo y te acompañaré como tal, sin casarnos.
He shook his head.
Meneó la cabeza.
"Adopted fraternity will not do in this case.
-Una fraternidad adoptiva no es viable en este caso.
If you were my real sister it would be different: I should take you, and seek no wife.
Si se tratase de una hermana de verdad, sí.
But as it is, either our union must be consecrated and sealed by marriage, or it cannot exist: practical obstacles oppose themselves to any other plan.
Pero en nuestras circunstancias, o nuestra unión es consagrada por el matrimonio o no puede existir.
Do you not see it, Jane?
Muchos obstáculos lo impiden.
Consider a moment--your strong sense will guide you."
Considéralo un momento, tú que tienes buen sentido.
I did consider; and still my sense, such as it was, directed me only to the fact that we did not love each other as man and wife should: and therefore it inferred we ought not to marry. I said so.
Mi buen sentido no me decía sino que dos seres que no se aman no deben casarse.
"St. John," I returned, "I regard you as a brother--you, me as a sister: so let us continue."
Se lo manifesté así, agregando: -John: te aprecio como a un hermano y tú a mí como a una hermana. Continuemos como hasta ahora.
"We cannot--we cannot," he answered, with short, sharp determination: "it would not do.
-Imposible -replicó él con energía-.
You have said you will go with me to India: remember--you have said that."
Me has dicho que irás conmigo a la India, no lo olvides.
"Conditionally."
-Condicionalmente.
"Well--well.
-Ya, ya...
To the main point--the departure with me from England, the co-operation with me in my future labours--you do not object.
A lo principal -partir conmigo y cooperar a mis tareas- no objetas nada.
You have already as good as put your hand to the plough: you are too consistent to withdraw it.
Puesto que estás dispuesta a empuñar el arado no debes retirar la mano en virtud de consideraciones pequeñas.

You have but one end to keep in view--how the work you have undertaken can best be done. Simplify your complicated interests, feelings, thoughts, wishes, aims; merge all considerations in one purpose: that of fulfilling with effect--with power--the mission of your great Master.
Sólo has de pensar en la grandiosidad de la labor, prescindiendo de tus deseos, inclinaciones, sentimientos y propósitos para consagrarte enteramente al servicio del Maestro.
To do so, you must have a coadjutor: not a brother--that is a loose tie--but a husband.
Necesitas en ello un colaborador, y ese ha de ser tu marido.
I, too, do not want a sister: a sister might any day be taken from me.
Una hermana no me es necesaria: podría además llegar un día en que dejase de estar a mi lado.
I want a wife: the sole helpmeet I can influence efficiently in life, and retain absolutely till death."
Necesito una mujer en quien yo pueda influir mientras viva y conservar a mi lado hasta la muerte. Me estremecí.
I shuddered as he spoke: I felt his influence in my marrow--his hold on my limbs.
Me parecía ya sentir aquella influencia sobre mí.
"Seek one elsewhere than in me, St. John: seek one fitted to you."
-Busca otra más idónea, John.
Again I tell you it is not the insignificant private individual--the mere man, with the man's selfish senses--I wish to mate: it is the missionary."
-Vuelvo a repetirte que no busco en ti la consorte, sino la misionera.
"And I will give the missionary my energies--it is all he wants--but not myself: that would be only adding the husk and shell to the kernel.
-Y puedes encontrarla en mí. Yo te daré todas mis energías, pero no mi persona.
For them he has no use: I retain them."
Para ti no es útil; déjame conservarla.
"You cannot--you ought not.
-No puedes ni debes.
Do you think God will be satisfied with half an oblation?
¿Crees que sería grato a Dios un sacrificio a medias?
Will He accept a mutilated sacrifice? It is the cause of God I advocate: it is under His standard I enlist you.
Es la causa de Dios por la que abogo y bajo su bandera quiero alistarte.
I cannot accept on His behalf a divided allegiance: it must be entire."
No puedo aceptar un enrolamiento de la mitad de su personalidad; ha de ser completo.
"Oh!
-¡Oh! -contesté-.
I will give my heart to God," I said. "_You_ do not want it."
Dios cuenta ya con mi corazón. Tú no lo necesitas.
I will not swear, reader, that there was not something of repressed sarcasm both in the tone in which I uttered this sentence, and in the feeling that accompanied it.
No te aseguraría, lector, que yo no pusiera algo de reprimido sarcasmo en estas palabras.
I had silently feared St. John till now, because I had not understood him.
Hasta ahora había temido a John porque no acababa de entenderle.

How much of him was saint, how much mortal, I could not heretofore tell: but revelations were being made in this conference: the analysis of his nature was proceeding before my eyes. I saw his fallibilities: I comprehended them.
Pero en el curso de nuestra conversación de hoy había desvelado su carácter: veía sus debilidades y las comprendía.
I understood that, sitting there where I did, on the bank of heath, and with that handsome form before me, I sat at the feet of a man, caring as I. The veil fell from his hardness and despotism.
La arrogante figura que se sentaba ante mí no era sino un hombre cuya intransigencia y despotismo resultaban evidentes.
Having felt in him the presence of these qualities, I felt his imperfection and took courage.
El conocer sus defectos me dio valor.
I was with an equal--one with whom I might argue--one whom, if I saw good, I might resist.
Siendo igual a mí, podía resistirle.
He was silent after I had uttered the last sentence, and I presently risked an upward glance at his countenance. His eye, bent on me, expressed at once stern surprise and keen inquiry.
Al oír mis últimas palabras permaneció silencioso, mirándome, como si quisiera decirme:
"Is she sarcastic, and sarcastic to _me_!" it seemed to say. "What does this signify?"
«Eres sarcástica, y lo eres a mi costa. »
"Do not let us forget that this is a solemn matter," he said ere long; "one of which we may neither think nor talk lightly without sin.
-No debemos olvidar que estamos tratando un asunto grave -dijo al fin-.
I trust, Jane, you are in earnest when you say you will serve your heart to God: it is all I want.
