–Para venir a buscarme es muy pronto, y para que venga gente de fuera, es muy tarde –comentó Kitty. .
'Papers from the office for me, I expect,' said Oblonsky.
–Será que me traen algún documento ––dijo Esteban Arkadievich.

A footman ran up to announce the new arrival, who stood at the foot of the stairs under a lamp. Anna looked down from the landing where she stood and at once recognized Vronsky, and a strange feeling of pleasure mixed with fear suddenly stirred in her heart.

Mientras Ana pasaba ante la escalera principal, el criado subía para anunciar al recién llegado, que estaba en el vestíbulo, bajo la luz de la lámpara. Ana miró abajo y, al reconocer a Vronsky, un extraño sentimiento de alegría y temor invadió su corazón.
He stood in his overcoat, feeling for something in his pockets.
El permanecía con el abrigo puesto, buscándose algo en el bolsillo.
When Anna was half-way up the top flight, he lifted his eyes and saw her, and a look of something like embarrassment and fear came into his face. She bowed slightly and went on.
Al llegar Ana a la mitad de la escalera, Vronsky miró hacia arriba, la vio y una expresión de vergüenza y de confusión se retrató en su semblante.
She heard Oblonsky's loud voice downstairs asking him to come in, and Vronsky's low, soft voice refusing.
Ana siguió su camino, inclinando ligeramente la cabeza.

When Anna returned with her album he had already gone, and Oblonsky was saying that Vronsky had called to inquire about a dinner they were giving next day to a celebrity who was visiting Moscow, but that he could not be induced to come in.

En seguida, sonó la voz de Esteban Arkadievich invitando a Vronsky a que pasara, y la del joven, baja, suave y tranquila, rehusando. Cuando volvió Ana con el álbum, Vronsky ya no estaba allí, y Esteban Arkadievich contaba que su amigo había venido sólo para informarse de los detalles de una comida que se daba al día siguiente en honor de una celebridad extranjera. –Por más que le he rogado, no ha querido entrar –dijo Oblonsky–.
'He seemed so queer,' added Oblonsky.
¡Cosa rara!
Kitty blushed. She thought that she alone understood why he had come to the house and why he would not come in.
Kitty se ruborizó, creyendo haber comprendido los motivos de la llegada de Vronsky y su negativa a pasar.
'He has been to our house,' she thought, 'and not finding me in he guessed that I was here.
«Ha ido a casa y no me ha encontrado», pensó, «y ha venido a ver si me hallaba aquí.
And he would not come in because Anna is here, and he thought it too late.'
Pero no ha querido entrar por lo tarde que es y también por hallarse Ana, que es una extraña para él».
They all glanced at one another and said nothing but began examining Anna's album.
Todos se miraron en silencio. Luego comenzaron a hojear el álbum.

There was nothing extraordinary or strange in the fact that a man had called at half-past nine at a friend's house to ask about a dinner they were planning and that he would not come in; but it seemed strange to all of them. To Anna in particular it seemed strange and not right.

Nada había de extraordinario en que un amigo visitase a otro a las nueve y media de la noche para informarse sobre un banquete que había de celebrarse al día siguiente; pero a todos les pareció muy extraño, y a Ana se lo pareció más que a nadie, y aun le pareció que el proceder de Vronsky no era del todo correcto.
CHAPTER XXII
XXII
THE BALL HAD ONLY JUST BEGUN when Kitty and her mother ascended the broad staircase which was deluged with light, decorated with flowering plants, and occupied by powdered footmen in red liveries.
Se iniciaba el baile cuando Kitty entró con su madre en la gran escalera iluminada, adornada de flores, llena de lacayos de empolvada peluca y rojo caftán.

From the ballroom as from a bee-hive came the regular sound of movement, and while they were arranging their hair and dresses before a mirror on the landing between the plants they heard the accurate measured sounds of the orchestra violins just beginning the first waltz.

De las salas llegaba el frufrú de los vestidos como el apagado zumbido de las abejas en una colmena. Mientras ellas se componían vestidos y peinados ante los espejos del vestíbulo lleno de plantar, sonaron suaves y melodiosos los acordes de los violines de la orquesta comenzando el primer vals.

A little old man, who had smoothed the grey hair on his temples before the mirror and who smelt strongly of scent, happened to jostle them on the stairs, and stepped aside in evident admiration of Kitty, whom he did not know.

Un anciano, vestido con traje civil, que arreglaba sus sienes canosas ante otro espejo, despidiendo en torno suyo un fuerte perfume, se encontró con ellas en la escalera y les cedió el paso, mientras contemplaba a Kitty, a quien no conocía, con evidente placer.

A beardless youth, one of those whom the old Prince Shcherbatsky called puppies, with a very low-cut waistcoat, straightening his white tie as he went along, bowed to them and ran past but returned to ask Kitty for a quadrille.

Un joven imberbe –sin duda uno de los galancetes a quienes el viejo Scherbazky llamaba pisaverdes–, que llevaba un chaleco muy abierto y se arreglaba, andando, la corbata blanca, las saludo y, después de haber dado algunos pasos, retrocedió a invitó a Kitty a danzar.
She had given the first quadrille to Vronsky and had to give the second to this youth.
Como tenía la primera contradanza prometida a Vronsky, Kitty hubo de prometer la segunda a aquel joven.
An officer, buttoning his glove, stood aside at the doorway to make room for them, and smoothing his moustache looked with evident pleasure at the rosy Kitty.
Un militar próximo a la puerta, que se abrochaba los guantes y se atusaba el bigote, miró con admiración a Kitty, resplandeciente en su vestido de color rosa.

Although Kitty's gown and coiffure and all her other adornments had given her much trouble and thought, she now entered the ballroom in her complicated dress of white net over a pink slip, as easily and simply as if these bows and laces and all the details of her toilet had not cost her or her people a moment's attention, as if she had been born in this net and lace and with that high coiffure and the rose and its two leaves on the top.

Aunque el vestido, el peinado y los demás preparativos para el baile habían costado a Kitty mucho trabajo y muchas preocupaciones, ahora el complicado traje de tul le sentaba con tanta naturalidad como si todas las puntillas, bordados y demás detalles de su atavío no hubiesen exigido de ella ni de su familia un solo instante de atención, como si hubiese nacido entre aquel tul y aquellas puntillas, con aquel peinado alto adornado con una rosa y algunas hojas en torno...

When, just before entering the ball-room, her mother wished to put straight a twisted end of her sash, Kitty drew slightly back: she felt that everything on her must be naturally right and graceful and that there was no need to adjust anything.

La vieja princesa, antes de entrar en la sala, trató de arreglar el cinturón de Kitty, pero ella se había separado, como si adivinase que todo le sentaba bien, que todo en ella era gracioso y no necesitaba arreglo alguno. Estaba en uno de sus mejores días.

It was one of Kitty's happy days. Her dress did not feel tight anywhere, the lace around her bodice did not slip, the bows did not crumple or come off, the pink shoes with their high curved heels did not pinch but seemed to make her feet lighter.
Los zapatitos color rosa, de alto tacón, en vez de oprimir, parecían acariciar y hacer más bellos sus piececitos. Los espesos y rubios tirabuzones postizos adornaban con naturalidad su cabecita.

The thick rolls of fair hair kept up as if they had grown naturally so on the little head. All three buttons on each of her long gloves, which fitted without changing the shape of her hand, fastened without coming off.
Los tres botones de cada uno de sus guantes estaban perfectamente abrochados y los guantes se ajustaban a sus manos sin deformarlas en lo más mínimo.
The black velvet ribbon of her locket clasped her neck with unusual softness.
Una cinta de terciopelo negro ceñía suavemente su garganta.
That ribbon was charming, and when Kitty had looked at her neck in the glass at home, she felt that that ribbon was eloquent.
Aquella cintita era una delicia; cada vez que Kitty se miraba en el espejo de su casa, sentía la impresión de que la cinta hablaba.
There might be some possible doubt about anything else, but that ribbon was charming.
Podía caber alguna duda sobre la belleza de lo demás, pero en cuanto a la cinta no cabía.
Kitty smiled, here at the ball, when she caught sight of it again in the mirror.
Al mirarse aquí en el espejo, Kitty sonrió también, complacida.
Her bare shoulders and arms gave her a sensation as of cold marble, a feeling she liked very much.
Sus hombros y brazos desnudos le daban la sensación de una frialdad marmórea que le resultaba agradable.
Her eyes shone and she could not keep her rosy lips from smiling at the consciousness of her attractive appearance.
Sus ojos brillantes y sus labios pintados no pudieron por menos de sonreír al verse tan hermosa.

Before she had reached the light-coloured crowd of women in tulle, ribbons, and lace, who were waiting for partners (Kitty never long formed one of the crowd), she was already asked for the waltz and asked by the best dancer, the leader of the dancing hierarchy, the famous dirigeur and Master of the Ceremonies, a handsome, stately married man, George Korsunsky.

Apenas entró en el salón y se acercó a los grupos de señoras, todas cintas y puntillas, que esperaban el momento de ser invitadas a bailar –Kitty no entraba jamás en aquellos grupos– le pidió ya un vals el mejor de los bailarines, el célebre director de danza, el maestro de ceremonias, un hombre casado, guapo y elegante, Egoruchka Korsunsky, que acababa de dejar a la condesa Bónina, con la que danzara el primer vals.

He had just left the Countess Bonin, with whom he had danced the first round of the waltz, and looking round his domain – that is to say, a few couples who had begun to dance – he noticed Kitty just coming in.
Mientras contemplaba con aire dominador a las parejas que bailaban, vio entrar a Kitty y se dirigió a ella con el paso desenvuelto de los directores de baile.
He approached her at that peculiar free and easy amble natural only to Masters of Ceremonies, bowed, and, without even asking her consent, put his arm round her slim waist.
Se inclinó ante ella y, sin preguntarle siquiera si quería danzar, alargó la mano para tomarla por el delicado talle.
She looked about for some one to hold her fan and the mistress of the house took it from her with a smile.
La joven miró a su alrededor buscando a alguien a quien entregar su abanico y la dueña de la casa lo cogió sonriendo.
'How fine that you have come in good time,' he said with his arm round her waist.
–Celebro mucho que haya llegado usted pronto –dijo él, ciñéndole la cintura–.
'It's wrong of people to come so late.'
No comprendo cómo se puede llegar tarde.
Bending her left arm she put her hand on his shoulder, and her little feet in their pink shoes began moving quickly, lightly, and rhythmically in time with the music, over the smooth parquet floor.
Kitty apoyó la mano izquierda en el hombro de Korsunsky y sus piececitos calzados de rosa se deslizaron ligeros por el encerado pavimento al ritmo de la música.
'It is a rest to waltz with you,' he said as he took the first slow steps of the dance.
–Bailar con usted es un descanso. ¡Qué admirable precisión y qué ligereza! –dijo Korsunsky, mientras giraban a compás del vals.
'What lightness and precision! it's delightful!' he remarked, saying to her what he said to almost all the dancing partners whom he really liked.
Eran, con poca diferencia, las palabras que dirigía a todas las conocidas que apreciaba.
She smiled at his praise, and over his shoulder continued to survey the ball-room.
Ella sonrió y, por encima del hombro de su pareja, miró la sala.

She was not a girl just come out, for whom all faces at a ball blend into one fairy-like vision; nor was she a girl who had been dragged from ball to ball till all the faces were familiar to dullness.

Kitty no era una de esas novicias a quienes la emoción del primer baile les hace confundir todos los rostros que las rodean, ni una de esas muchachas que, a fuerza de frecuentar las salas de danza, acaban conociendo a todos los concurrentes de tal modo que hasta les aburre ya mirarlos.
She was between those two extremes, and though elated was able to control herself sufficiently to be observant.
Kitty estaba en el término medio. Así, pues, pudo contemplar toda la sala con reprimida emoción.
She saw that the elite of the company were grouped in the left-hand corner of the room.
Miró primero a la izquierda, donde se agrupaba la flor de la buena sociedad.

There was the beauty Lida, Korsunsky's wife, in an impossibly low dress, and the hostess, and there shone the bald head of Krivin who was always where the elite were; youths who had not the courage to approach gazed in that direction, and there Kitty's eyes found Stephen, and then the lovely head and beautiful figure of Anna, in a black velvet dress.

Estaba allí la mujer de Korsunsky, la bella Lidy, con un vestido excesivamente descotado; Krivin, con su calva brillante, presente, como siempre, donde se reunía la buena sociedad; más allá, en un grupo que los jóvenes contemplaban sin osar acercarse, Kitty distinguió a Esteban Arkadievich y la arrogante figura y la cabeza de Ana, vestida de terciopelo negro.
And he was there.
También «él» estaba allí.
Kitty had not seen him since the day she had refused Levin.
La muchacha no le había vuelto a ver desde la noche en que rechazara a Levin.
With her far-sighted eyes she recognized him at once and even noticed that he was looking at her.
Kitty le descubrió desde lejos y hasta observó que él también la miraba.
'Shall we have another turn? You are not tired?' asked Korsunsky who was a little out of breath.
–¿Una vueltecita más si no está cansada? –preguntó Korsunsky, un tanto sofocado.
'No more turns, thank you.'
–No; gracias.
'Where may I take you?'
–¿Adónde la acompaño?
'I believe Anna Arkadyevna Karenina is here, take me to her.'
–Me parece que veo a Ana Karenina. Lléveme allí.
'Wherever you please.'
–Como guste.

And Korsunsky waltzed toward the left of the room, gradually diminishing his step and repeating 'Pardon, mesdames, pardon, pardon, mesdames,' as he steered through that sea of lace, tulle and ribbons without touching as much as a feather, and then turned his partner so suddenly that her delicate ankles in the open-work stockings appeared as her train spread out like a fan and covered Krivin's knees. Korsunsky bowed, straightened his broad shirt front, and offered Kitty his arm to conduct her to Anna.

Korsunsky, sin dejar de bailar, pero a paso cada vez más lento, se dirigió hacia el ángulo izquierdo del salón, murmurando constantemente: –Pardon, mesdames, pardon, mesdames... Y, abriéndose así paso entre aquel mar de puntillas, tules y encajes sin haber enganchado una sola cinta, Korsunsky hizo describir una rápida vuelta a su pareja, de modo que las finas piernas de Kitty, envueltas en medias transparentes, quedaron al descubierto y la cola de su vestido se abrió como un abanico, cayendo sobre las rodillas de Krivin.
Kitty flushed and, a little giddy, took her train off Krivin's knees and looked round for Anna.
Luego Korsunsky la saludó, ensanchó el pecho sobre su abierto frac y le ofreció el brazo para conducirla al lado de Ana Arkadievna.

Anna was not in lilac, the colour Kitty was so sure she ought to have worn, but in a low-necked black velvet dress which exposed her full shoulder and bosom that seemed carved out of old ivory, and her rounded arms with the very small hands. Her dress was richly trimmed with Venetian lace.

Kitty, ruborizándose, retiró la cola de su vestido de las rodillas de Krivin y se volvió, algo aturdida, buscando a Ana. Ana no vestía de fila, como supusiera Kitty, sino de negro, con un traje muy descotado, que dejaba ver sus esculturales hombros que parecían tallados en marfil antiguo, su pecho y sus brazos torneados, rematados por finas muñecas.
In her black hair, all her own, she wore a little garland of pansies, and in her girdle, among the lace, a bunch of the same flowers. Her coiffure was very unobtrusive.

Su vestido estaba adornado con encajes de Venecia; una guirnalda de nomeolvides adornaba sus cabellos, peinados sin postizo alguno, y prendido en el talle, entre los negros encajes, llevaba un ramo de las mismas flores.
The only noticeable things about it were the wilful ringlets that always escaped at her temples and on the nape of her neck and added to her beauty.
Su peinado era sencillo y sólo destacaban en él los bucles de sus cabellos rizados, que se escapaban por la nuca y las sienes.
Round her finely chiselled neck she wore a string of pearls.
En el cuello, firme y bien formado, ostentaba un hilo de perlas.

Kitty had been seeing Anna every day and was in love with her and had always imagined her in lilac, but seeing her in black she felt that she had never before realized her full charm. She now saw her in a new and quite unexpected light.

Kitty había visto diariamente a Ana y se había sentido prendada de ella, y la imaginaba siempre con el vestido lila. Sin embargo, al verla vestida de negro, reconoció que no había comprendido todo su encanto.
She now realized that Anna could not have worn lilac, and that her charm lay precisely in the fact that her personality always stood out from her dress, that her dress was never conspicuous on her.
Ahora se le aparecía de una manera nueva a inesperada y reconocía que no podía vestir de lita, porque este color hubiese apagado su personalidad.
And her black velvet with rich lace was not at all conspicuous, but served only as a frame; she alone was noticeable – simple, natural, elegant and at the same time merry and animated.
El traje, negro con su profusión de encajes, no atraía la vista, pero se limitaba a servir de marco y hacía resaltar la figura de Ana, sencilla, natural, elegante, y a la vez animada y alegre.
She was standing among that group, very erect as usual, and was talking to the master of the house with her head slightly turned toward him, when Kitty approached.
Cuando Kitty se acercó al grupo, Ana, muy erguida como siempre, hablaba con el dueño de la casa con la cabeza inclinada ligeramente hacia él.

'No, I am not going to throw the first stone,' she was saying in reply to some question, adding, with a shrug of her shoulders, 'although I cannot understand it'; and at once she turned to Kitty with a tender protecting smile.

–No, no comprendo... pero no seré yo la que lance la primera piedra... –decía, contestando a una pregunta que, sin duda, le había hecho él y encogiéndose de hombros. Y en seguida se dirigió a Kitty con una sonrisa suavemente protectora.
She surveyed Kitty's dress with a rapid feminine glance and with a movement of her head, scarcely perceptible but understood by Kitty, she signified her approval of Kitty's dress and beauty.

Con experta mirada femenina contempló rápidamente el vestido de Kitty a hizo un movimiento de cabeza casi imperceptible, pero en el cual la joven leyó que la felicitaba por su belleza y por su atavío. –Usted –dijo Ana a Korsunsky– hasta entra en el salón y sale de él bailando.
'You even come into the room dancing,' she said. 'She is one of my most faithful helpers,' said Korsunsky, turning to Anna whom he had not yet seen.
–La Princesita es una de mis mejores colaboradoras –dijo Korsunsky, inclinándose ante Ana Karenina, a la que no había sido presentado– Contribuye a que el baile sea animado y alegre.
'The Princess helps to make a ball gay and beautiful. Anna Arkadyevna, shall we have a turn?' he added, stooping toward her.
¿Un vals, Ana Arkadievna? –preguntó.
'Oh, you know one another?' asked the host.
–¿Se conocen ustedes? –inquirió el dueño de la casa.
'Whom do we not know? My wife and I are like white wolves, every one knows us,' answered Korsunsky.
–¿Quién no nos conoce a mi mujer y a mí? –repuso Korsunsky–. Somos como los lobos blancos.
'Anna Arkadyevna, just one turn?'
¿Quiere bailar, Ana Arkadievna? –repitió.
'I don't dance if it is possible not to,' she said.
–Siempre que me es posible, procuro no bailar –respondió Ana Karenina.
'But to-night it is not possible,' he rejoined.
–Pero eso hoy es imposible.
At that moment Vronsky approached.
Vronsky se acercó en aquel momento.
'Well, if it is impossible not to dance to-night, let us dance,' she said taking no notice of Vronsky's bow and quickly putting her hand on Korsunsky's shoulder.
–Pues si es imposible, bailemos –dijo Ana, pareciendo no reparar en el saludo de Vronsky y apresurándose a poner la mano sobre el hombro de Korsunsky.
'Why is she displeased with him?' thought Kitty, noticing that Anna had intentionally taken no notice of Vronsky's bow.
«Acaso estará enfadada con él», pensó Kitty, observando que Ana había fingido no ver el saludo de Vronsky.
He came up to Kitty, reminding her of the first quadrille and regretting that he had not seen her for such a long time.
En cuanto a éste, se acercó a Kitty, recordándole su compromiso de la primera contradanza y diciéndole que sentía mucho no haberla visto hasta entonces.
Kitty, while gazing with admiration at Anna waltzing, listened to him, expecting him to ask her to waltz, but he did not do so and she glanced at him with surprise.
Kitty le escuchaba admirando entre tanto a Ana, que danzaba. Esperaba que Vronsky la invitara al vals, pero el joven no lo hizo.
He blushed and hurriedly asked her to dance, but scarcely had he put his arm round her slim waist and taken one step when the music stopped.
Kitty le miró sorprendida. Él, sonrojándose, la invitó precipitadamente a bailar; pero apenas había enlazado su fino talle y dado el primer paso, la música dejó de tocar.

Kitty looked into his face which was so near her own, and long after – for years after – that look so full of love which she then gave him, and which met with no response from him, cut her to the heart with tormenting shame.
Kitty le miró a los ojos, que tenía tan cerca. Durante varios años había de recordar, llena de vergüenza, aquella mirada amorosa que le dirigiera y a la que él no correspondió.
'Pardon, pardon, a waltz – a waltz,' shouted Korsunsky from the other end of the room, and seizing the first girl within reach he himself began dancing.
¡Vals, vals! –gritó Korsunsky desde el otro extremo de la sala. Y, emparejándose con la primera joven que encontró, comenzó a bailar.
CHAPTER XXIII
XXIII

VRONSKY AND KITTY WALTZED several times round the room and then Kitty went to her mother, but hardly had she exchanged a few words with the Countess Nordston before Vronsky returned to fetch her for the first quadrille.

Kitty y Vronsky dieron algunas vueltas de vals. Luego Kitty se acercó a su madre y tuvo tiempo de cambiar algunas palabras con Nordston antes de que Vronsky fuese a buscarla para la primera contradanza.

Nothing special was said during the quadrille: they talked in snatches about the Korsunskys, husband and wife, whom Vronsky very amusingly described as dear forty-year-old children, and about a proposed Stage Society, and only once did the conversation touch her to the quick – when he asked her about Levin, whether he was still in Moscow, and added that he had liked him very much.

Mientras bailaban no hablaron nada particular. Vronsky hizo un comentario humorístico de los Korsunsky, a los que describía como unos niños cuarentones; luego charlaron del teatro que iba a abrirse al público próximamente.
But Kitty had not expected more from the quadrille, she waited with a clutch at her heart for the mazurka.
Sólo una frase llegó al alma de Kitty, y fue cuando el joven le habló de Levin, asegurándole que había simpatizado mucho con él y preguntándole si continuaba en Moscú.
It seemed to her that the mazurka would settle everything.
De todos modos, Kitty no esperaba más de aquella contradanza.
That he did not ask her for the mazurka while they were dancing the quadrille did not disturb her.
Lo que aguardaba con el corazón palpitante era la mazurca, pensando que todo había de decidirse en ella.

She was sure that she would dance the mazurka with him as at previous balls, and she refused five other partners for that dance, saying that she was already engaged. The whole ball up to the last quadrille was for Kitty an enchanted dream of gay flowers, sounds and movements.

No la inquietó que él durante la contradanza no la invitara para la mazurca. Estaba segura de que bailaría con él, como siempre y en todas partes, y así rehusó cinco invitaciones de otros tantos caballeros diciéndoles que ya la tenía comprometida.

She only stopped dancing when she felt too tired and had to ask to be allowed a rest. But while dancing the last quadrille with one of the youthful bores whom it would not do to refuse, she happened to be vis-à-vis to Anna.

Hasta la última contradanza, el baile transcurrió para ella como un sueño encantador, lleno de brillantes colores, de sones, de movimiento. Danzó sin interrupción, menos cuando se sentía cansada y rogaba que la dejasen descansar.
She had not come across Anna since the beginning of the ball, and now she suddenly saw her again in a different and unexpected light.
Durante la última contradanza con uno de aquellos jóvenes que tanto la aburrían, pero con los que no podía negarse a bailar, se encontró frente a frente con Ana y Vronsky.
She noticed that Anna was elated with success, a feeling Kitty herself knew so well.
No había visto a Ana desde el principio del baile y ahora le pareció otra vez nueva a inesperada.
She saw that Anna was intoxicated by the rapture she had produced.
La veía con aquel punto de excitación, que conocía tan bien, producida por el éxito.

She knew the feeling and knew its symptoms, and recognized them in Anna – she saw the quivering light flashing in her eyes, the smile of happiness and elation that involuntarily curled her lips, and the graceful precision, the exactitude and lightness, of her movements.

Ana estaba ebria del licor del entusiasmo; Kitty lo veía en el fuego que, al bailar, se encendía en sus ojos, en su sonrisa feliz y alegre, que rasgaba ligeramente su boca, en la gracia, la seguridad y la ligereza de sus movimientos.
'Who is the cause?' she asked herself.
–«¿Por qué estará así?», se preguntaba Kitty.

'All or only one?' And without trying to help her youthful partner who was painfully struggling to carry on the conversation the thread of which he had lost, as she mechanically obeyed the merry, loud, and authoritative orders of Korsunsky, who commanded every one to form now a grand rond, now a chaine, she watched, and her heart sank more and more.

«¿Por la admiración general que despierta o por la de uno sólo?» Y sin escuchar al joven, que trataba en vano de reanudar la conversación interrumpida, y obedeciendo maquinalmente a los gritos alegremente imperiosos de Korsunsky a los que bailaban: «Ahora en grand rond, en chaîne», Kitty observaba a la pareja cada vez con el corazón más inquieto.
'No, it is not the admiration of the crowd that intoxicates her, but the rapture of one, and that one is... can it be he?'
«No; Ana no se siente animada por la admiración general, sino por la de uno. ¿Es posible que sea por la de él?»
Every time he spoke to Anna the joyful light kindled in her eyes and a smile of pleasure curved her rosy lips.
Cada vez que Vronsky hablaba con Ana, los ojos de ésta brillaban y una sonrisa feliz se dibujaba en sus labios.
She seemed to make efforts to restrain these signs of joy, but they appeared on her face of their own accord.
Parecía como si se esforzara en reprimir aquellas señales de alegría y como si ellas aparecieran en su rostro contra su voluntad.
'But what of him?' Kitty looked at him and was filled with horror.
Kitty se preguntó qué sentiría él, y al mirarle quedó horrorizada.
What she saw so distinctly in the mirror of Anna's face, she saw in him.
Los sentimientos del rostro de Ana se reflejaban en el de Vronsky.
What had become of his usually quiet and firm manner and the carelessly calm expression of his face?
¿Qué había sido de su aspecto tranquilo y seguro y de la despreocupada serenidad de su semblante?
Every time he turned toward Anna he slightly bowed his head as if he wished to fall down before her, and in his eyes there was an expression of submission and fear.
Cuando ella le hablaba, inclinaba la cabeza como para caer a sus pies y en su mirada había una expresión de temblorosa obediencia.
'I do not wish to offend,' his every look seemed to say, 'I only wish to save myself, but I do not know how.'
«No quiero ofenderla –parecía decirle con aquella mirada–; sólo deseo salvarme, y no sé cómo ...»
His face had an expression which she had never seen before.
El rostro de Vronsky transparentaba una expresión que Kitty no había visto jamás en él.
They talked about their mutual friends, carrying on a most unimportant conversation, but it seemed to Kitty that every word they said was deciding their and her fate.
Aunque su charla era trivial, pues hablaban sólo de sus mutuas amistades, a Kitty le parecía que en ella se estaba decidiendo la suerte de ambos y de sí misma.

And, strange to say, though they were talking about Ivan Ivanich, who made himself so ridiculous with his French, and how Miss Eletskaya could have made a better match, yet these words were important for them and they felt this as well as Kitty. A mist came over the ball and the whole world in Kitty's soul.

Y era el caso que, a pesar de que en realidad hablaban de lo ridículo que resultaba Iván Ivanovich hablando francés o la posibilidad de que la Elezkaya pudiera hallar un partido mejor, Ana y Vronsky tenían, como Kitty, la impresión de que aquellas palabras estaban para ellos llenas de sentido.
Only the thorough training she had had enabled and obliged her to do what was expected of her, that is, to dance, to answer the questions put to her, to talk, and even to smile.
Sólo gracias a su rígida educación, pudo contenerse y proceder según las conveniencias, danzando, hablando, contestando, hasta sonriendo.
But before the mazurka began, when the chairs were already being placed for it, and several couples moved from the small to the large ball-room, Kitty was for a moment seized with despair.
Pero, al empezar la mazurca, cuando empezaron a colocarse en su lugar las sillas y algunas parejas se dirigieron desde las salas pequeñas al salón, Kitty se sintió horrorizada y desesperada.
She had refused five men who had asked for the mazurka and now she had no partner for it.
Después de rehusar cinco invitaciones, ahora se quedaba sin bailar.
She had not even a hope of being asked again just because she had too much success in Society for anyone to think that she was not already engaged for the dance.
Hasta podía ocurrir que no la invitasen, porque dado el éxito que tenía siempre en sociedad, a nadie podía ocurrírsele que careciese de pareja.
She must tell her mother that she was feeling ill, and go home, but she had not the strength to do it.
Era preciso que dijese a su madre que se encontraba mal a irse a casa.
She felt herself quite broken-hearted.
Pero se sentía tan abatida que le faltaban las fuerzas para hacerlo.
She went to the far end of a little drawing-room and sank into an easy chair.
Entró en el saloncito y se dejó caer en una butaca.

Her light skirt stood out like a cloud round her slight body; one thin bare girlish arm dropped listlessly and sank into the pink folds of her tunic, the other hand held a fan with which she rapidly fanned her flushed face.

La vaporosa falda de su vestido se hinchó como una nubecilla rodeándola; su delgado, suave y juvenil brazo desnudo se hundió entre los pliegues del vestido rosa; en la mano que le quedaba libre sostenía un abanico y con movimientos rápidos y breves daba aire a su encendido rostro.
But although she seemed like a butterfly just settled on a blade of grass and ready at any moment to flutter and spread its rainbow wings, her heart was crushed with terrible despair.
A pesar de su aspecto de mariposa posada por un instante en una flor, agitando las alas y pronta a volar, una terrible angustia inundaba su corazón.
'But perhaps I am mistaken, perhaps it was nothing of the kind?' And she again recalled all that she had witnessed.
«¿Y si me equivocase, si no hubiera nada?», se decía, recordando de nuevo lo que había visto.
'Kitty, what does this mean?' asked the Countess Nordston, coming up inaudibly over the carpet. 'I don't understand it.'
–¡Pero Kitty! No comprendo lo que te pasa –dijo la condesa Nordston, que se había acercado caminando sobre la suave alfombra sin hacer ruido.
Kitty's nether lip trembled, and she rose quickly.
A Kitty le tembló el labio inferior y se puso en pie precipitadamente.
'Kitty, are you not dancing the mazurka?'
–¿No bailas la mazurca, Kitty?
'No, no,' said Kitty in a voice tremulous with tears.
–No –repuso con voz trémula de lágrimas.
'He asked her for the mazurka in my presence,' said the Countess, knowing that Kitty would understand whom she meant by 'him' and 'her.'
–Él la invitó ante mí a bailar la mazurca –dijo la Nordston, sabiendo muy bien que a Kitty le constaba a quién se refería–. Y ella le preguntó si no bailaba con la princesita Scherbazky.
'She asked, "Are you not dancing with the Princess Shcherbatsky?"-'
–Me es igual –contestó Kitty.

'Oh! it's all the same to me!' replied Kitty. No one but herself understood her situation, because no one knew that she had only a few days ago refused a man whom she perhaps loved, and refused him because she trusted another.
Nadie comprendía mejor que ella su situación, pues nadie sabía que el día anterior había rechazado al hombre a quien acaso amaba, y lo había rechazado por éste.
The Countess Nordston, who was engaged to Korsunsky for the mazurka, told him to ask Kitty instead.
La Nordston buscó a Korsunsky, con quien tenía comprometida la mazurca, y le rogó que invitase a Kitty en lugar suyo.
Kitty danced in the first pair, and luckily for her she was not obliged to talk, because Korsunsky ran about all the time giving orders in his domain.

Por fortuna, Kitty no hubo de hablar mucho, porque Korsunsky, como director de baile, había de ocuparse continuamente en la distribución de las figuras y correr sin cesar de una parte a otra dando órdenes.
Vronsky and Anna sat almost opposite to her.
Vronsky y Ana estaban sentados casi enfrente de Kitty.
And she saw them with her far-sighted eyes, she saw them close by, too; when they met in the dance, and the more she saw of them the surer she was that the blow had fallen.
Los veía de lejos y los veía de cerca, según se alejaba o se acercaba en las vueltas de la danza, y cuanto más los miraba, más se convencía de que su desdicha era cierta.

She saw that they felt as if they were alone in that crowded ball-room. On Vronsky's face, usually so firm and self-possessed she noticed that expression of bewilderment and submission which had so surprised her – an expression like that of an intelligent dog when it feels guilty.

Kitty notaba que se sentían solos en aquel salón lleno de gente, y en el rostro de Vronsky, siempre tan impasible y seguro, leía ahora aquella expresión de humildad y de temor que tanto la había impresionado, que recordaba la actitud de un perro inteligente que se siente culpable.
Anna smiled – and the smile passed on to him; she became thoughtful – and he became serious.
Ana sonreía y le comunicaba su sonrisa. Si se ponía pensativa, se veía triste a él.
Some supernatural power attracted Kitty's eyes to Anna's face.
Una fuerza sobrenatural hacía que Kitty dirigiese los ojos al rostro de Ana.

She looked charming in her simple black dress; her full arms with the bracelets, her firm neck with the string of pearls round it, her curly hair now disarranged, every graceful movement of her small feet and hands, her handsome, animated face, – everything about her was enchanting, but there was something terrible and cruel in her charm.

Estaba hermosísima en su sencillo vestido negro; hermosos eran sus redondos brazos, que lucían preciosas pulseras, hermoso su cuello firme adornado con un hilo de perlas, bellos los rizados cabellos de su peinado algo desordenado, suaves eran los movimientos llenos de gracia de sus pies y manos diminutos, bella la animación de su hermoso rostro. Pero había algo terrible y cruel en su belleza.
Kitty admired her even more than before, and suffered more and more.
Kitty la miraba más subyugada todavía que antes, y cuanto más la miraba más sufría.
She felt herself crushed and her face expressed it. When Vronsky happened to knock against her as they danced, he did not at once recognize her, so changed was she.

Se sentía anonadada, y en su semblante se dibujaba una expresión tal de abatimiento que cuando Vronsky se encontró con ella en el curso del baile tardó un momento en reconocerla, de tan desfigurada como se le apareció en aquel momento.
'A delightful ball,' he remarked, in order to say something.
–¡Qué espléndido baile! –dijo él, por decir algo.
'Yes,' she replied.
–Sí –contestó Kitty.

In the middle of the mazurka, performing a complicated figure newly-invented by Korsunsky, Anna stepped into the middle of the room and chose two men and two ladies, one of whom was Kitty, to join her.

Durante la mazurca, Ana, al repetir una figura imaginada por Korsunsky, salió al centro del círculo, escogió dcs caballeros y llamó a Kitty y a otra dama. Al acercarse, Kitty levantó los ojos hacia ella asustada.
Kitty, as she moved toward Anna, gazed at her with fear.
Ana la miró y le sonrió cerrando los ojos mientras le apretaba la mano.

Anna half-closed her eyes to look at Kitty, smiled and pressed her hand, but noticing that Kitty only responded to her smile by a look of surprise and despair, she turned away from her and talked cheerfully with the other lady.
Pero al advertir en el rostro de Kitty una expresión de desesperación y de sorpresa por toda respuesta a su sonrisa, Ana se volvió de espaldas a ella y empezó a hablar alegremente con otra señora.
'Yes, there is something strange, satanic, and enchanting about her,' thought Kitty.
«Sí, sí –se dijo Kitty–, hay en ella algo extraño, hermoso y a la vez diabólico.»
Anna did not wish to stay to supper, but the master of the house tried to persuade her to do so.
Ana no quería quedarse a cenar, pero el dueño de la casa insistió.
'Come, Anna Arkadyevna,' began Korsunsky, drawing her bare arm under his, 'I have such a good idea for a cotillion – Un bijou.'
–Ea, Ana Arkadievna –dijo Korsunsky, tomando bajo la manga de su frac el brazo desnudo de Ana–. Tengo una idea magnífica para el cotillón.
And he moved slowly on, trying to draw her with him. Their host smiled approvingly.
Y comenzó a andar, haciendo ademán de llevársela, mientras el dueño de la casa le animaba con su sonrisa.

'No, I won't stay,' answered Anna, smiling, and despite her smile Korsunsky and the host understood from the firm tone of her voice that she would not stay. 'No, as it is I have danced more in Moscow at your one ball than I danced the whole winter in Petersburg,' said Anna, looking round at Vronsky who stood beside her.

–No me quedo –repuso Ana, sonriente. Y, a pesar de su sonrisa, los dos hombres comprendieron en su acento que no se quedaría. –He bailado esta noche en Moscú más que todo el año en San Petersburgo y debo descansar antes de mi viaje –añadió Ana, volviéndose hacia Vronsky, que estaba a su lado.
'So you really are going to-morrow?' said Vronsky.
–¿Se va decididamente mañana? –preguntó Vronsky.
'Yes, I think so,' Anna replied as if surprised at the boldness of his question; but the uncontrollable radiance of her eyes and her smile burnt him as she spoke the words.
–Sí, seguramente –respondió Ana, como sorprendida de la audacia de tal pregunta.
Anna did not stay for supper, but went away.
Su sonrisa y el fuego de su mirada cuando le contestó abrasaron el alma de Vronsky. Ana Arkadievna se fue, pues, sin quedarse a cenar.
CHAPTER XXIV
XXIV
'YES, THERE IS CERTAINLY SOMETHING OBJECTIONABLE and repellent about me,' thought Levin after leaving the Shcherbatskys, as he walked toward his brother's lodgings.
«Sin duda hay en mí algo repugnante, algo que repele a la gente», pensaba Levin al salir de casa de los Scherbazky y dirigirse a la de su hermano.
'I do not get on with other people.
«No sirvo para convivir en sociedad.
They say it is pride! No, I am not even proud.
Dicen que esto es orgullo, pero no soy orgulloso.
If I had any pride, I should not have put myself into such a position.'
Si lo fuera, no me habría puesto en la situación que me he puesto.»
And he pictured to himself Vronsky, happy, kind, clever, calm, and certainly never placing himself in such a terrible position as he, Levin, had been in that evening.
Imaginó a Vronsky dichoso, inteligente, benévolo y, con toda seguridad, sin haberse encontrado jamás en una situación como la suya de esta noche.
'Yes, she was bound to choose him.
«Forzoso es que Kitty haya de preferirle.
It had to be so, and I have no cause to complain of anyone or anything.
Es natural; no tengo que quejarme de nadie ni de nada.
It was my own fault.
Yo sólo tengo la culpa.
What right had I to imagine that she would wish to unite her life with mine?
¿Con qué derecho imaginé que ella había de querer unir su vida a la mía?
Who and what am I?
¿Quién soy yo?
A man of no account, wanted by no one and of no use to anyone.'
Un hombre inútil para sí y para los otros.»
And he remembered his brother Nicholas, and kept his mind gladly on that memory.
Recordó a su hermano Nicolás y se detuvo con satisfacción en su recuerdo.
'Is he not right that everything on earth is evil and horrid?
«¿No tendrá razón cuando dice que todo en el mundo es malo y repugnante?
And have we judged brother Nicholas fairly?
Acaso no hayamos juzgado bien a Nicolás.
Of course, from Prokofy's point of view, who saw him in a ragged coat and tipsy, he is a despicable fellow; but I know him from another side. I know his soul, and know that we resemble one another.
Desde el punto de vista del criado Prokofy, que le vio borracho y con el abrigo roto, es un hombre despreciable; pero yo te conozco de otro modo, conozco su alma y se que nos parecemos.
And yet I, instead of looking him up, dined out and came here.'
Y yo, en vez de buscarle, he ido a comer primero y después al baile en esa casa.»
Levin went up to a lamp-post and read his brother's address which he had in his pocket-book, and then hired a sledge.
Levin se acercó a un farol, leyó la dirección de su hermano, que guardaba en la cartera, y llamó a un coche de punto.
On the long way to his brother's he recalled all the events he knew of Nicholas's life.
Durante el largo camino hacia el domicilio de su hermano, Levin iba evocando lo que conocía de su vida.

He recalled how despite the ridicule of his fellow-students his brother had lived like a monk while at the University and for a year after, strictly observing all the religious rites, attending service, fasting, avoiding all pleasures and especially women; and then how he suddenly broke loose, became intimate with the vilest people and gave himself up to unbridled debauchery. He remembered how his brother had brought a boy from the country to educate, and in a fit of anger had so beaten the lad that proceedings were commenced against him for causing bodily harm.

Recordaba que durante los cursos universitarios y hasta un año después de salir de la universidad, su hermano, a pesar de las burlas de sus compañeros, había hecho vida de fraile, cumpliendo rigurosamente los preceptos religiosos, asistiendo a la iglesia, observando los ayunos y huyendo de los placeres y de la mujer sobre todo.
He remembered an affair with a sharper to whom his brother had lost money, and whom he had first given a promissory note and then prosecuted on a charge of fraud.
Recordó después cómo, de pronto y sin ningún motivo aparente, empezó a tratar a las peores gentes y se lanzó a la vida más desenfrenada.

(That was when his brother Sergius had paid the money for him.) Then he remembered the night which Nicholas had spent in the police cells for disorderly conduct, and the disgraceful proceedings he had instigated against his brother Sergius Ivanich, whom he accused of not having paid out to him his share of his mother's fortune: and lastly, the time when his brother took an official appointment in one of the Western Provinces and was there arrested for assaulting an Elder...

Recordó también que en cierto caso su hermano había tomado a su servicio un mozo del pueblo y en un momento de ira le había golpeado tan brutalmente que había sido llevado a los Tribunales; se acordó aún de cuando su hermano, perdiendo dinero con un fullero, le había aceptado una letra, denunciándole después por engaño (a aquella letra se refería Sergio Ivanovich). Otra vez Nicolás había pasado una noche en la prevención por alboroto.
It was all very disgusting, but to Levin it did not seem nearly so disgusting as it must have seemed to those who did not know Nicholas, nor his whole story, nor his heart.
Y, en fin, había llegado al extremo de pleitear contra su hermano Sergio acusándole de no abonarle la parte que en derecho le correspondía de la herencia materna.

Levin remembered that when Nicholas was passing through his pious stage of fasting, visiting monks, and going to church; when he was seeking in religion for help to curb his passionate nature, not only did no one encourage him, but every one, and Levin among them, made fun of him.

Su última hazaña la realizó en el oeste de Rusia, donde había ido a trabajar, y consistió en maltratar a un alcalde, por lo que fue procesado. Y si bien todo esto era desagradable, a Levin no se lo pareció tanto como a los que desconocían el corazón de Nicolás y su verdadera historia.
He was teased and called 'Noah' and 'monk,' and then when he broke loose no one helped him, but all turned away from him with horror and disgust.

Levin se acordaba de que en aquel período de devoción, ayunos y austeridad, cuando Nicolás buscaba en la religión un freno para sus pasiones, nadie le aprobaba y todos se burlaban de él, incluso el propio Levin. Le apodaban Noé, fraile, etcétera, y, luego, cuando se entregó libremente a sus pasiones, todos le volvieron la espalda, espantados y con repugnancia.
Levin felt that his brother Nicholas, in his soul, in the innermost depths of his soul, despite the depravity of his life, was no worse than those who despised him.
Levin comprendía que, en rigor, Nicolás, a pesar de su vida, no debía encontrarse más culpable que aquellos que le despreciaban.
It was not his fault that he was born with his ungovernable temper, and with a cramped mind. He always wished to do right.
Él no tenía ninguna culpa de haber nacido con su carácter indomable y con su limitada inteligencia.
'I will tell him everything, I will get him to tell me everything.
Por otra parte, su hermano siempre había querido ser bueno.
I will show him that I love and therefore understand him,' Levin decided in his mind, as toward eleven o'clock he drove up to the hotel of which he had the address.

«Le hablaré con el corazón en la mano, le demostraré que le quiero y le comprendo, y le obligaré a descubrirme su alma», decidió Levin cuando, ya cerca de las once, llegaba a la fonda que le indicaran.
'Upstairs, Nos. I2 and I3,' said the hall porter in reply to Levin's question.
–Arriba. Los números 12 y 13 –dijo el conserje, contestando a la pregunta de Levin.
'Is he in?'
–¿Está?
'I expect so.'
–Creo que sí.
The door of No. I2 was ajar, and from within, visible in the streak of light, issued dense fumes of inferior and weak tobacco.
La puerta de la habitación número 12 se hallaba entornada y por ella salía un rayo de luz y un espeso humo de tabaco malo.
Levin heard a stranger's voice, but knew at once that his brother was there, for he heard him coughing.
Sonaba una voz desconocida para Levin, y al lado de ella reconoció la tosecilla peculiar de su hermano.
As he entered the doorway the stranger's voice was saying:
Al entrar Levin, el desconocido decía:
'It all depends on how intelligently and rationally the affair is conducted.'
–Todo depende de la inteligencia y prudencia con que se lleve el asunto.

Constantine Levin glanced into the room, which was beyond a partition, and saw that the speaker was a young man with an enormous head of hair, who wore a workman's coat, and that a young, pock-marked woman in a woollen dress without collar or cuffs [At that time better-class women always wore something white round their necks and wrists.] was sitting on the sofa.

Constantino Levin, desde la puerta, divisó a un joven con el cabello espeso y enmarañado vestido con una poddiovka. Una muchacha pecosa, con un vestido de lana sin cuello ni puños, estaba sentada en el diván.
He could not see his brother, and his heart sank painfully at the thought that Nicholas lived among such strange people.
No se veía a Nicolás, y Levin sintió el corazón oprimido al pensar entre qué clase de gente vivía su hermano.
No one noticed him, and, as he took off his goloshes, he overheard what the man in the workman's coat was saying. He was talking about some commercial enterprise.
Mientras se quitaba los chanclos, Levin, cuya llegada no había notado nadie, oyó al individuo de la poddiovka hablando de una empresa a realizar.
'Oh, let the privileged classes go to the devil,' said his brother's voice, with a cough.
–¡Que el diablo se lleve las clases privilegiadas! –dijo la voz de Nicolás tras un carraspeo–.
'Masha, get us some supper and bring the wine if any is left, or send for some.'
Macha, pide algo de cenar y danos vino si queda. Si no, envía a buscarlo.
The woman rose, came out from behind the partition and saw Constantine.
La mujer se levantó, salió del otro lado del tabique y vio a Levin.
'Here is a gentleman, Nicholas Dmitrich,' she said.
–Nicolás Dmitrievich: aquí hay un señor –dijo.
'Whom do you want?' said Nicholas Levin's voice angrily.
–¿Por quién pregunta? –exclamó la voz irritada de Nicolás.
'It is I,' answered Constantine Levin, coming forward into the lamp-light.
–Soy yo –repuso Constantino Levin, presentándose.
'Who's I?' said the voice of Nicholas Levin still more angrily.
–¿Quién es «yo»? –repitió la voz de Nicolás, con más irritación aún.

Constantine heard how he rose hurriedly and caught against something, and then in the doorway before him he saw the familiar yet ever strange figure of his brother, wild, sickly, gigantic, lean, and round-shouldered, with large, frightened eyes.

Se le oyó levantarse precipitadamente y tropezar, y Levin vio ante sí, en la puerta, la figura que le era tan conocida, la figura delgada y encorvada de su hermano, pero su aspecto salvaje, sucio y enfermizo, la expresión de sus grandes ojos asustados, le aterró.
He was even more emaciated than three years before when Constantine Levin had last seen him.
Nicolás estaba aún más delgado que cuando Levin le viera la última vez, tres años antes.
He was wearing a short coat, and his hands and broad bones appeared more immense than ever.
Llevaba una levita que le estaba corta, con lo que sus brazos y muñecas parecían más largos aún.
His hair was thinner but the same straight moustache covered his lips; and the same eyes with their peculiar, naive gaze looked out at the new-comer.
La cabellera se le había aclarado, sus labios estaban cubiertos por el mismo bigote recto, y la misma mirada extrañada de siempre se posaba en el que había entrado.
'Ah! Kostya!' he said suddenly, recognizing his brother, and his eyes lit up with joy.
–¡Ah, eres tú, Kostia! –dijo, al reconocer a su hermano. Sus ojos brillaron de alegría.

But at the same moment he turned to look at the young man and convulsively jerked his head and neck as if his necktie were strangling him, a movement Levin knew well, and quite another expression – a wild, suffering, and cruel look – settled on his haggard face.

Pero a la vez miró al joven de la poddiovka a hizo un movimiento convulsivo con el cuello y cabeza –como si le apretase la corbata–, que Constantino conocía bien, y una expresión salvaje, dolorida, feroz, se pintó de repente en su rostro.
'I wrote both to you and to Sergius Ivanich that I do not know you and do not wish to know you.
–Ya he escrito a Sergio diciéndole que no quiero nada con ustedes.
What is it? What do you want?'
¿Qué deseas... qué desea usted?
He was not at all as Constantine had imagined him.
Se presentaba bien distinto a como Levin le imaginara.

Constantine when thinking of him had forgotten the most trying and worst part of his character, that which made intercourse with him so difficult, but now when he saw his face, and especially that convulsive movement of his head, he remembered it all.

Constantino olvidaba siempre la parte áspera y difícil de su carácter, la que hacía tan ingrato el tratarle. Sólo ahora, al ver su rostro, al distinguir el movimiento convulsivo de su cabeza, lo recordó.
'I do not want anything of you specially,' he answered meekly; 'I have simply come to see you.'
–No deseaba nada concreto, sino verte –––dijo con timidez.
His brother's timidity obviously softened Nicholas, whose lips quivered.
Nicolás, algo suavizado, al parecer, por la timidez de su hermano, movió los labios.
'Ah! You have come just for that?' he said.
–¿Así que vienes por venir?
'Well, come in, sit down.
Pues entra y siéntate.
Will you have some supper?
¿Quieres cenar?
Masha, get supper for three.
Trae tres raciones, Macha.
No, wait a little.
¡Ah, espera!
Do you know who this is?' he added, turning to his brother and pointing to the man in the workman's coat.
¿Sabes quien es este señor –dijo, indicando al joven de la poddiovka–.
'It is Mr. Kritsky, my friend ever since my Kiev days, a very remarkable fellow. Of course the police are after him, because he is not a scoundrel.'
Se trata de un hombre muy notable: el señor Krizky, amigo mío, de Kiev, a quien persigue la policía porque no es un canalla.
And he glanced round at everybody present as was his way.
Y, según su costumbre, miró a todos los que estaban en la habitación.

Seeing that the woman in the doorway was about to go out he shouted to her: 'Wait, I told you,' and in the awkward and blundering manner familiar to Constantine, he again looked round at everybody, and began to tell his brother about Kritsky: how he had been expelled from the University because he had started a society to help the poorer students, and also Sunday schools, and how he had afterwards taught in an elementary school, and had been turned out from that too, and had then been tried on some charge or other.

Al ver a la mujer, de pie en la puerta y disponiéndose a salir, le gritó: «¡Te he dicho que esperes!». Y con la indecisión y la falta de elocuencia que Constantino conocía de siempre, comenzó, mirando a todos, a contar la historia de Krizky, su expulsión de la universidad por formar una sociedad de ayuda a los estudiantes pobres y a las escuelas dominicales, su ingreso como maestro en un colegio popular y cómo después se le procesó sin saber por qué.
'You were at Kiev University?' Constantine Levin asked Kritsky, in order to break the awkward silence that followed.
–¿,Conque ha estudiado usted en la universidad de Kiev? –dijo Constantino Levin, para romper el embarazoso silencio que siguió a las palabras de su hermano.
'Yes, at Kiev,' Kritsky replied with an angry frown.
–Sí, en Kiev –murmuró Krizky, frunciendo el entrecejo.

'And this woman,' said Nicholas Levin, interrupting him, and pointing to her, 'is my life's companion, Mary Nikolavna; I took her out of a house...' and as he said this he again jerked his neck. 'But I love and respect her and beg all those who wish to know me,' he added, raising his voice and scowling, 'to love and respect her.

–Esta mujer, María Nicolaevna, es mi compañera –interrumpió Nicolás–. La he sacado de una casa de... –movió convulsivamente el cuello y agregó, alzando la voz y arrugando el entrecejo–: Pero la quiero y la respeto y exijo que la respeten cuantos me tratan.
She is just the same to me as a wife, just the same.
Es como si fuera mi mujer, lo mismo.
So now you know whom you have to deal with, and if you fear you will be degraded – there is the door.'
Ahora ya sabes con quiénes te encuentras. Si te sientes rebajado, «por la puerta se va uno con Dios» .
And again his eyes glanced questioningly around.
Y volvió a mirar interrogativamente a todos.
'Why should I be degraded? I don't understand.'
–No veo por qué he de sentirme rebajado.
'Well, Masha, order supper for three, with vodka and wine...
–En ese caso... ¡Macha: encarga tres raciones, vodka y vino!
No, wait.
Espera...
No, never mind... You may go.'
No, nada, nada, ve...
CHAPTER XXV
XXV

'SO YOU SEE...' NICHOLAS LEVIN CONTINUED with an effort, wrinkling his brow and twitching. He evidently found it hard to decide what to say and to do. 'Do you see...' he pointed to a bundle of iron rods tied together with string, in a corner of the room. 'Do you see that? It is the beginning of a new business we are undertaking. The business is to be a Productive Association...'

–Sí, ya ves... –murmuró Nicolás con esfuerzo, arrugando la frente y con movimientos convulsivos. Se notaba que no sabía qué hacer ni qué decir. –¿Ves? –siguió, señalando unas vigas de hierro atadas con cordeles que había en un rincón–. Éste es el principio de una nueva empresa que vamos a realizar, una cooperativa obrera de producción...

Constantine hardly listened. He kept glancing at his brother's sickly, consumptive face, and felt more and more sorry for him, nor could he force himself to pay attention to what Nicholas was telling him about the Association.
Constantino, contemplando el rostro tuberculoso de Nicolás, no conseguía prestar atención a sus palabras.
He realized that this Association was merely an anchor to save his brother from self-contempt.
Comprendía que su hermano buscaba en aquella empresa un áncora de salvación contra el desprecio que sentía hacia sí mismo.
Nicholas Levin continued speaking:
Nicolás Levin continuaba hablando:
'You know that capitalism oppresses the workers.
–Ya sabes que el capital oprime al trabajador.
Our workmen the peasants bear the whole burden of labour, but are so placed that, work as they may, they cannot escape from their degrading condition.
Los obreros y campesinos llevan todo el peso del trabajo y no logran salir, por mucho que se esfuercen, de su situación de bestias de carga.

All the profits on their labour, by which they might better their condition, give themselves some leisure, and consequently gain some education, all this surplus value is taken away by the capitalists.
Todas las ganancias, todo aquello con que pudieran mejorar su estado, descansar a instruirse, lo devoran los dividendos de los capitalistas.
And our society has so shaped itself that the more the people work the richer the merchants and landowners will become, while the people will remain beasts of burden for ever.
La sociedad está organizada de tal modo que, cuanto más trabaja el obrero, más ganan los comerciantes y los propietarios, y el proletario sigue siendo siempre una bestia de carga.
And this system must be changed,' he concluded, with an inquiring look at his brother.
Es preciso cambiar este orden de eosas –terminó, mirando inquisitivamente a su hermano.
'Yes, of course,' said Constantine, looking intently at the hectic flush which had appeared on his brother's face below its prominent cheek bones.
–Claro, claro –dijo Constantino, contemplando con atención las hundidas mejillas de Nicolás.
'And so we are starting a Locksmiths' Association, in which all the products and the profits and, above all, the instruments of production will be common property.'
–Así vamos a formar una cooperativa de cerrajeros en la que la producción y las ganancias, y, sobre todo, las herramientas, que es lo esencial, sean comunes.
'Where will the business be?' asked Constantine.
–¿Dónde la instalaréis?
'In the village of Vozdrema, Kazan Government.'
–En Vosdrema, provincia de Kazán.
'Why in a village?
–¿Por qué en un pueblo?
It seems to me there is plenty of work to do in the country as it is.
No parece que el trabajo falte en los pueblos.
Why start a Locksmiths' Association there?'
No sé para qué puede necesitar un pueblo una cooperativa de cerrajeros.

'Because the peasants are still just as much slaves as they used to be, and that is why you and Sergius Ivanich don't like it when anyone wishes to deliver them from their slavery,' replied Nicholas Levin, irritated by Constantine's objection.
–Es preciso hacerlo porque los aldeanos son ahora tan esclavos como antes, y lo que os desagrada a ti y a Sergio es que quiera sacárseles de esa esclavitud –gruñó Nicolás, irritado por la réplica.
Constantine sighed and at the same time looked round the room which was dismal and dirty.
Constantino Levin suspiró mientras miraba la sucia y destartalada habitación.
The sigh seemed to irritate Nicholas still more.
Aquel suspiro irritó más aún a Nicolás.
'I know your aristocratic outlook and Sergius Ivanich's.
–Conozco las ideas aristocráticas de usted y de Sergio.
I know that he uses all the powers of his mind to justify the existing evils.'
Sé que él emplea toda la capacidad de su cerebro en justificar la organización existente.
'But why talk about Sergius Ivanich?' said Levin with a smile.
–No es cierto... ¿Por qué me hablas de Sergio? –preguntó, sonriendo, Levin.
'Sergius Ivanich?
–¿Por qué?
This is why!' suddenly shouted Nicholas at the mention of the name. 'This is why.
Ahora lo verás –exclamó Nicolás al oír el nombre de su hermano–.
But what is the good of talking?
Pero ¿para qué perder tiempo?
One thing only...
Dime: ¿a qué has venido?
Why have you come here?
Tú desprecias todo esto.
You despise it, well, that is all right – then go away.
Pues bien: ¡vete con Dios!
Go, go in God's name!' he exclaimed, rising from his chair. 'Go, go!'
¡Vete, vete! –gritó, levantándose de la silla.
'I do not despise it at all,' Constantine replied meekly.
–No lo desprecio en lo más mínimo ––dijo Constantino tímidamente–.
'I do not even dispute it.'
Preferiría no tratar de esas cosas.
Meanwhile Mary Nikolavna had come back.
María Nicolaevna entró en aquel momento.
Nicholas gave her an angry look.
Nicolás la miró con irritación.
She hurried up to him and said something in a whisper.
Ella se le acercó y le dijo unas palabras.
'I am not well and have grown irritable,' said Nicholas, breathing heavily and quieting down.
–Me encuentro mal y me he vuelto muy excitable –pronunció Nicolás, calmándose y respirando con dificultad–.
'And you talk to me about Sergius Ivanich and his article.
¡Y vienes hablándome de Sergio y de sus artículos!
It is such rubbish, such humbug, such self-deception.
Todo en ellos son falsedades, deseos de engañarse a sí mismo.
What can a man write about justice, who does not understand it?'
¿Qué puede decir de la justicia un hombre que no la conoce?
'Have you read his article?' he said, turning to Kritsky again, sitting down to the table and clearing away from it a heap of half-filled cigarettes to make room.
¿Ha leído usted su último artículo? –preguntó a Krizky, sentándose otra vez a la mesa y separando los cigarrillos esparcidos sobre ella para dejar un espacio libre.
'I have not read it,' said Kritsky morosely, evidently not wishing to join in the conversation.
–No lo he leído –repuso sombríamente Krizky, que, al parecer, no deseaba intervenir en la conversación.
'Why not?' irritably answered Nicholas, still addressing Kritsky.
–¿Por qué? –preguntó Nicolás, irritado ahora contra Krizky.
'Because I consider it unnecessary to waste time on it.'
–Porque me parece perder el tiempo.

'What do you mean? May I ask how you knew it would waste your time? That article is incomprehensible to many; I mean it is above them. But it is a different matter with me. I see through his thought, and therefore know why it is weak.'

–Perdón, ¿por qué cree usted que es perder el tiempo? –Para mucha gente ese artículo está por encima de su comprensión. –Pero yo no estoy en ese caso. Yo sé leer entre líneas y descubrir sus puntos flacos.
Every one remained silent.
Todos callaron.
Kritsky rose and took up his hat.
Krizky se levantó lentamente y cogió la gorra.
'Don't you want any supper?
–¿No quiere cenar?
Well, good-bye.
Bien.
Come to-morrow and bring the locksmith.'
Venga mañana con el cerrajero,
As soon as Kritsky had gone out, Nicholas smiled and winked.
Cuando Krizky hubo salido, Nicolás sonrió, guiñando el ojo.
'He also is not much good,' he remarked. 'I can see...'
–Tampoco él es muy fuerte; lo veo bien.
But at that moment Kritsky called him from outside the door.
En aquel momento, Krizky le llamó desde la puerta.
'What do you want now?' said Nicholas and went out into the passage.
–¿Qué quiere? –dijo Nicolás saliendo al corredor.
Left alone with Mary Nikolavna, Levin spoke to her.
Constantino, al quedarse solo con María Nicolaevna, le preguntó:
'Have you been long with my brother?' he asked.
–¿Hace mucho que está con mi hermano?
'Yes, it is the second year now.
–Más de un año.
His health is very bad, he drinks too much,' she said.
El señor está muy mal de salud: bebe mucho –––contestó ella.
'Really – what does he drink?'
–¿Qué bebe?
'He drinks vodka, and it is bad for him.'
–Mucho vodka. Y le sienta muy mal.
'Much vodka?' whispered Levin.
–¿Bebe con exceso?
'Yes,' she said looking timidly toward the door, just as Nicholas returned.
–Sí –repuso ella, mirando atemorizada hacia la puerta por la que ya entraba Nicolás.
'What were you talking about?' he asked frowning and looking from one to the other with frightened eyes. 'What was it?'
–¿De qué hablabáis? –preguntó éste con severidad y pasando su mirada asustada de uno a otro, Decídmelo.
'Nothing,' replied Levin in confusion.
–De nada –repuso turbado Constantino.
'If you do not wish to tell me, do as you please.
–Si no lo queréis decir, no lo digáis.
Only you have no business to talk to her.
Pero no tienes por qué hablar con ella de nada.
She's a street girl, and you are a gentleman,' he muttered jerking his neck.
Es una ramera, y tú un señor –exclamó haciendo un movimiento convulsivo con el cuello–.
'You, I see, have examined and weighed everything here, and regard my errors with compassion,' he continued, again raising his voice.
Ya veo que te haces cargo de mi situación y comprendes mis extravíos y me los perdonas. Te lo agradezco –añadió levantando la voz.
'Nicholas Dmitrich, Nicholas Dmitrich,' whispered Mary Nikolavna, again approaching him.
–¡Nicolás Dmitrievich, Nicolás Dmitrievich! –murmuró María Nicolaevna, acercándose a él.
'Well, all right, all right!... and how about supper?
–¡Está bien, está bien!...
Ah, here it is,' he said noticing a waiter who was bringing in a tray. 'Here, here, put it down here,' he said crossly, and at once poured out a wineglass full of vodka and drank it greedily.
¿Y la cena? ¡Ah, ahí viene! –exclamó, viendo subir al camarero con la bandeja, ¡Póngala aquí! –añadió con irritación.
'Have a drink, will you?' he said to his brother, brightening up at once. 'Well, we've had enough of Sergius Ivanich.
Y llenándose un vaso de vodka, lo vació de un trago. –¿Quieres beber? –preguntó a su hermano, animándose al punto–.
I am glad to see you, anyhow. Whatever one may say, after all, we are not strangers.
Bueno, dejémosle correr a Sergio Ivanovich; sea como sea, estoy contento de verte.
Come, have a drink. Tell me what you are doing,' he continued, greedily chewing a crust of bread and filling himself another glass.
Quieras o no, somos de la misma sangre –prosiguió, mascando con avidez una corteza de pan y bebiendo otra copa–. ¿Qué es de tu vida?
'How are you getting on?'
Vamos, bebe. Y dime lo que haces.

'I am living alone in the country, as I did before, and I look after the farming,' answered Constantine, observing with horror how greedily his brother ate and drank, and trying not to let it be seen that he noticed it.
–Vivo solo en el pueblo, como antes, y me ocupo de las tierras –repuso Constantino, mirando disimuladamente, con horror, la avidez con que comía y bebía su hermano.
'Why don't you get married?'
–¿Por qué no te casas?
'I had not the chance,' replied Constantine blushing.
–No se ha presentado aún la ocasión –respondió Constantino poniéndose rojo.
'Why not?
–¿Por qué no?
For me all that is over. I have spoilt my life.
Tú no eres como yo, que estoy acabado y con la vida perdida.
I have said, and still say, that if I had been given my share of the property when I wanted it, everything would have been different.'
He dicho y diré siempre que si se me hubiese dado mi parte de la herencia cuando la necesitaba, mi existencia habría sido diferente.
Constantine hastened to change the subject.
Constantino se apresuró a cambiar de tema.
'Do you know that your Vanyusha is now a clerk in my office at Pokrovsk?' he said.
–¿Sabes que a tu Vaniuchka lo tengo en Pokrovskoe de tenedor de libros?
Nicholas jerked his head and grew thoughtful.
Nicolás movió el cuello y quedó pensativo.
'Yes, tell me what is happening in Pokrovsk Is the house still standing, and the birch trees, and our schoolroom?
–¿Sí? Y dime: ¿qué hay de nuevo en Pokrovskoe?
And is Philip the gardener really still living?
¿Y la casa? ¿Sigue como antes?
How well I remember the garden-house and the sofa!...
¿Y los abedules, y el cuarto donde estudiábamos? ¿Es posible que viva aún Felipe, el jardinero?
Mind, don't change anything in the house, but get married soon and set things going again as they used to be.
¡Cómo me acuerdo del pabellón y el diván! Mira: no cambies nada en la casa, cásate y déjalo todo como estaba.
Then I will come to you if you have a good wife.'
Y si tu mujer es buena, iré a verte...
'I would come if I were sure I should not find Sergius Ivanich there.'
Ya habría ido, pero me contuvo siempre el temor de encontrarme con Sergio.
'You won't find him there.
–No le encontrarías.
I live quite apart from him.'
Vivo independiente de él.
'Still, say what you will, you must choose between him and me,' said Nicholas with a timid look at his brother.
–Bien: sea como sea has de escoger entre Sergio y yo –murmuró Nicolás, mirándole tímidamente.
His timidity touched Constantine.
Aquella timidez conmovió a Constantino.
'If you want my full confession about it, I will tell you that I take no side in your quarrel with Sergius Ivanich.
–Si quieres que te sea franco, no deseo intervenir en vuestra querella.
You are both to blame: You more in external matters and he more in essential ones.'
Tú tienes la culpa en la forma y él la tiene en el fondo.
'Ah, ah! Then you have grasped it, you have grasped it?' joyfully exclaimed Nicholas.
–¡Has comprendido! –exclamó jovialmente Nicolás.
'But personally, if you care to know it, I value your friendship more because...'
–Yo, personalmente, aprecio más tu amistad, porque...
'Why, why?'
–¿Por qué?
Constantine could not tell him that it was because Nicholas was unfortunate and needed friendship.
Constantino no osó decirle que era porque le veía desgraciado y necesitaba más su amistad que Sergio.
But Nicholas understood that he meant just that, and frowning, again took hold of the vodka bottle.
Pero Nicolás comprendió y cogió en silencio la botella de vodka.
'Enough, Nicholas Dmitrich!' said Mary Nikolavna, stretching out her plump arm with its bare wrist to take the bottle.
–Basta ya, Nicolás Dmitrievich –dijo María Nicolaevna, alargando su redondo brazo desnudo hacia la botella.
'Let go! Leave me alone!
–¡Déjame o te pego! –gritó Nicolás.
I'll thrash you!' shouted he. Mary Nikolavna gave a mild, kindly smile, which evoked one from Nicholas, and she took away the bottle.
María Nicolaevna sonrió bondadosamente, de un modo suave, que se contagió a Nicolás, y cogió la botella.
'Do you think she doesn't understand?' said Nicholas.
–¿Te figuras que Macha no es inteligente? –dijo Nicolás–.
'She understands it all better than any of us.
Lo comprende todo mejor que nosotros.
There really is something good and sweet about her.'
¿Verdad que parece buena y simpática?
'You were never in Moscow before?' Constantine asked very politely, just in order to say something.
–¿Nunca había estado usted antes en Moscú? –le preguntó Constantino, por decir algo.
'Don't speak to her in that way.
–No la trates de usted.
It frightens her.
Se asusta.
No one but the magistrate, when she was tried for an attempt to escape from the house of ill fame, ever spoke to her so politely...
Nadie le ha hablado de usted jamas, excepto el juez que la juzgó cuando la llevaron al Tribunal porque trató de huir de aquella casa...
Oh heavens, how senseless everything is in this world!' he suddenly exclaimed.
¡Dios mío! –exclamó Nicolás–. ¡Cuánta falta de sentido hay en el mundo!
'All these new institutions, these magistrates, these Zemstvos...
¿Para qué sirven tantas nuevas instituciones, tantos jueces de paz, tantos zemstvos!
What a confusion it all is!'
¡Qué estupideces!
And he began to relate all his encounters with these new institutions.
Y comenzó a relatar sus luchas con aquellas nuevas instituciones.
Constantine Levin listened to him, and the condemnation of the social institutions, which he shared with him and had often expressed, was unpleasant to him when he heard it from his brother's lips.
Constantino Levin le escuchaba, y las mismas censuras que había expresado él tantas veces le desagradaba oírlas ahora de labios de su hermano.
'We shall understand it better in the next world,' he said playfully.
–Todo eso lo veremos claro en el otro mundo –dijo bromeando.
'In the next world?
–¿El otro mundo?
Ah, I do dislike that next world,' said Nicholas, fixing his wild, frightened eyes on his brother's face.
Ni me interesa ni lo deseo –dijo Nicolás, posando en el semblante de su hermano sus ojos salvajes y asustados–.
'One would think that to leave all these abominations, these muddles (one's own and other people's), would be good, yet I fear death – I fear it terribly.'

Parece que habría de ser motivo de alegría salir de toda la vileza y maldad que nos rodea, de la nuestra y de la de los demás; y, sin embargo, tengo miedo de la muerte, un miedo terrible –y se estremeció–.
He shuddered.
Anda, bebe algo.
'Do drink something.
¿Quieres champaña?
Would you like some champagne?
¿Quieres acaso que salgamos?
Or let us go out somewhere or other.
Podríamos ir a oír a los zíngaros.
Let us go to the Gipsies!
¿Sabes?
Do you know I have become fond of the gipsies and the Russian folk-songs?'
Ahora me gustan mucho los zíngaros y las canciones populares rusas.
His speech began to grow confused and he jumped from one subject to another.
La lengua no le obedecía y su conversación saltaba de un tema a otro.
With Masha's help Constantine succeeded in persuading him not to go out anywhere, and got him into bed quite tipsy.
Constantino, ayudado por Macha, le convenció de no ir a sitio alguno y entre los dos le acostaron completamente bebido.
Masha promised to write to Constantine in case of need, and to try to persuade Nicholas to go and live with him.
Macha prometió escribir a Constantino en caso necesario a intentar convencer a Nicolás de que fuera a vivir con su hermano.
CHAPTER XXVI
XXVI
NEXT MORNING CONSTANTINE LEVIN LEFT MOSCOW and toward evening he reached home.
Constantino Levin salió de Moscú por la mañana y llegó a su casa por la tarde.

On his way back in the train he talked with his fellow-passengers about politics and the new railways, and felt oppressed, just as in Moscow, by the confusion of the views expressed, by discontent with himself and a vague sense of shame.

En el vagón trabó conversación con sus compañeros de viaje y se habló de política, de los nuevos ferrocarriles y, de cómo en Moscú, le desanimaba la confusión de sus ideas, se sentía descontento de sí mismo y avergonzado no sabía de qué.

But when he got out of the train at his station and by the dim light from the station windows saw his one-eyed coachman, Ignat, with his coat-collar turned up, and his sledge with its carpet-lined back, his horses with their tied-up tails, and the harness with its rings and tassels, and when Ignat, while still putting the luggage into the sledge, began telling him the village news: how the contractor had come, and Pava had calved, – Levin felt that the confusion was beginning to clear away and his shame and self-dissatisfaction to pass.

Pero cuando se apeó en la estación y reconoció a Ignacio, su cochero tuerto, con el cuello del caftán levantado, cuando a la débil luz que salía de las ventanas de la estación vio el trineo cubierto de pieles y los caballos con las colas atadas, cuando Ignacio le contó las novedades del pueblo, la llegada de un comprador y que la vaca «Pava» tenía cría, le parecía a Levin que salía del caos de sus ideas y que poco a poco desaparecían de él su vergüenza y su descontento.

He felt this at the mere sight of Ignat and the horses; but when he had put on the sheepskin coat that had been brought for him and, well wrapped up, had seated himself in the sledge and started homeward, turning over in his mind the orders he would give about the work on the estate, and as he watched the side horse (once a saddle-horse that had been overridden, a spirited animal from the Don), he saw what had befallen him in quite a different light. He felt that he was himself and did not wish to be anyone else.

La sola vista de Ignacio y de sus caballos le había supuesto ya un alivio, y, cuando se puso el tulup que le trajeron, cuando se vio acomodado en el trineo, y los caballos comenzaron a trotar, pensó en las órdenes que debía dar a su llegada, examinó a uno de los corceles, muy veloz, pero que comenzaba ya a perder fuerzas y que había sido en otro tiempo caballo de carreras en el Don, y las cosas comenzaron a manifestarse a sus ojos bajo una nueva luz.
He only wished now to be better than he had been formerly.
Cesó entonces de desear ser otro.

First of all he decided that he would no longer hope for the exceptional happiness which marriage was to have given him, and consequently he would not underrate the present as he had done. Secondly, he would never again allow himself to be carried away by passion, the repulsive memory of which had so tormented him when he was making up his mind to propose.

Y, satisfecho de sí mismo, sólo deseó ser mejor, Decidió no pensar en la felicidad inasequible que le ofrecía su imposible matrimonio y contentarse con la que le deparaba la realidad presente; resistiría a las malas pasiones, como aquella que se apoderó de él el día en que se decidió a pedir la mano de Kitty.

Then, remembering his brother Nicholas, he determined that he would never allow himself to forget him again, but would watch over him, keep him in sight, and be ready to help when things went hard with him.
Se acordó, después, de Nicolás, y resolvió velar por él y estar pronto a ayudarle cuando lo necesitara, cosa que presentía para muy pronto.
And he felt that that would be soon. Then his brother's talk about communism, which he had taken lightly at the time, now made him think.
La conversación sobre el comunismo sostenida con su hermano, del que Constantino había tratado muy ligeramente, ahora le hacía reflexionar.
