He considered an entire change of economic conditions nonsense; but he had always felt the injustice of his superfluities compared with the peasant's poverty, and now decided, in order to feel himself quite justified, that though he had always worked hard and lived simply, he would in future work still more and allow himself still less luxury. And it all seemed to him so easy to carry out that he was in a pleasant reverie the whole way home, and it was with cheerful hopes for a new and better life that he reached his house toward nine o'clock in the evening.

El cambio de las condiciones económicas presentes le parecía absurdo, pero comparando la pobreza del pueblo con su abundancia personal, resolvió trabajar más para sentirse más justo y permitirse todavía menos gustos superfluos, aunque ya antes trabajaba bastante y vivía con gran sencillez.
A light fell on the snow-covered space in front of the house from the windows of the room of his old nurse Agatha Mikhaylovna, who now acted as his housekeeper.

Y todo ello se le figuraba ahora tan fácil de hacer que todo el camino se lo pasó sumido en las más gratas meditaciones. Eran las nueve de la noche cuando llegó a su casa, y se sentía animado por un sentimiento nuevo: de la esperanza de una vida mejor.
She had not yet gone to bed, and Kuzma, whom she had roused, came running out barefoot and still half-asleep into the porch.

Una débil claridad salía de las ventanas de la habitación de Agafia Mijailovna, la vieja aya que desempeñaba ahora el cargo de ama de llaves, y caía sobre la nieve de la explanada que se abría frente a la casa.
Laska, a setter bitch, ran out too, almost throwing Kuzma off his feet, and whined and rubbed herself against Levin's knees, jumping up and wishing but not daring to put her front paws on his chest.

Agafia, que no dormía aún, despertó a Kusmá y éste, medio dormido y descalzo, corrió a la puerta. « Laska», la perra, salió también, derribando casi a Kusmá, y se precipitó hacia Levin, frotándose contra sus piernas y con deseos de poner la patas sobre su pecho sin atreverse a hacerlo.
'You have soon come back, sir,' said Agatha Mikhaylovna.
–¡Qué pronto ha vuelto, padrecito! –dijo Agafia Mijailovna.
'I was home-sick, Agatha Mikhaylovna.
–Me aburría, Agafia Mijailovna.
Visiting is all very well, but "there is no place like home,"-' he replied, and went into his study.
Se está bien en casa ajena, pero mejor en la propia –contestó Levin, pasando a su despacho.

A candle just brought in gradually lit up the study and its familiar details became visible: the stag's horns, the book shelves, the looking-glass, the hot-air aperture of the stove with its brass lid, which had long been in need of repair, his father's couch, the large table on which were an open volume, a broken ash-tray, and an exercise-book in his handwriting. When he saw all this, he was overcome by a momentary doubt of the possibility of starting the new life of which he had been dreaming on his way.

En el cuarto, y a la débil luz de una bujía traída por la servidumbre, fueron surgiendo los detalles familiares: las astas de ciervo, las estanterías llenas de libros, el espejo, la estufa con el ventilador hacía tiempo necesitado de arreglo, el diván del padre de Levin, la inmensa mesa y sobre ella un libro abierto, el cenicero roto, un cuaderno escrito con notas de su mano.

All these traces of his old life seemed to seize hold of him and say, 'No, you will not escape us and will not be different, but will remain such as you have been: full of doubts; full of dissatisfaction with yourself, and of vain attempts at improvement followed by failures, and continual hopes of the happiness which has escaped you and is impossible for you.'
Al ver lo que le era tan conocido, Levin dudó un momento de poder organizar su nueva vida como deseara mientras iba por el camino. Todo aquello parecía rodearle y decirle:
That was what the things said, but another voice within his soul was saying that one must not submit to the past and that one can do anything with oneself.

«No te alejarás de nosotros, seguirás siendo lo que eres, con tus dudas, con tu eterno descontento de ti mismo, con tus inútiles intentos de modificarte y tus caídas, con tu constante deseo de una imposible felicidad ...» .

And obeying the latter voice he went to the corner where two thirty-six pound dumb-bells lay and began doing gymnastic exercises with them to invigorate himself. He heard a creaking of steps at the door and hurriedly put down the dumb-bells.

Pero, si así le hablaban aquellos objetos, en su alma otra voz le decía que no hay por qué encadenarse al pasado y que le era imposible cambiar. Obedeciendo a esta voz Levin se acercó a un rincón donde tenía dos pesas de un pud cada una y comenzó a levantarlas, tratando de animarse con aquel ejercicio gimnástico.
His steward entered and said that, 'the Lord be thanked,' everything was all right, but that the buckwheat had burned in the new drying kiln. This news irritated Levin.

Tras la puerta sonaron pasos y Levin dejó las pesas en el suelo precipitadamente. Entró el encargado y le dijo que, gracias a Dios, todo marchaba bien; pero que el alforfón se había quemado algo en la secadora nueva.
The new kiln had been built and partly invented by him.
La noticia le llenó de enojo.
The steward had always been against the new kiln, and now proclaimed with suppressed triumph that the buckwheat had got burnt.
La nueva secadora había sido construida por él mismo.
Levin felt quite certain that if it had been burnt it was only because the precautions about which he had given instructions over and over again had been neglected.
El encargado era enemigo de aquella innovación y ahora anunciaba con cierto aire de triunfo que el alforfón se había quemado.
He was vexed, and he reprimanded the steward. But the steward had one important and pleasant event to report.
Mas Levin estaba seguro de que el quemarse se debía a no haber tomado las precauciones que cien veces recomendara.
Pava, his best and most valuable cow, bought at the cattle-show, had calved.
Molesto, pues, reprendió con severidad al encargado.
'Kuzma, bring me my sheep-skin. And you tell them to bring a lantern. I will go and have a look at her,' he said to the steward.

En cambio, había una buena noticia: la de la cría de la «Pava», la magnífica vaca comprada en la feria. –Dame el tulup, Kusmá –pidió Levin y dijo al encargado–: traiga una linterna; quiero ver la cría.
The sheds where the most valuable cattle were kept were just behind the house.
El establo de las vacas de selección estaba detrás de la casa.
Crossing the yard past the heap of snow by the lilac bush, he reached the shed.
Levin se dirigió a través del patio por delante de un montón de nieve que se levantaba junto a unas lilas.
There was a warm steaming smell of manure when the frozen door opened, and the cows, astonished at the unaccustomed light of the lantern, began moving on their clean straw.
Al abrir la puerta se sintió el caliente vaho del estiércol, y las vacas, sorprendidas por la luz de la linterna, se agitaron sobre la paja fresca.
Levin saw the broad smooth black-mottled back of a Dutch cow.
Destacó en seguida el lomo liso y ancho, negro con manchas blancas, de la vaca holandesa.
The bull, Berkut, with a ring through his nose, was lying down, and almost rose up, but changed his mind and only snorted a couple of times as they passed by.
«Berkut» , el semental, con el anillo en el belfo, estaba tumbado y pareció ir a incorporarse, pero cambió de opinión y se limitó a mugir profundamente dos veces cuando pasaron junto a él.
The red beauty Pava, enormous as a hippopotamus, turned her back,
La magnífica «Pava», grande como un hipopótamo, estaba vuelta de ancas, impidiendo ver la becerra, a la que olfateaba.

hiding her calf from the newcomers and sniffing at it. Levin entered the stall and examined Pava, who, becoming excited, was about to low, but quieted down when Levin moved the calf toward her, and sighing heavily began licking it with her rough tongue.

Levin examinó a la «Pava» y enderezó a la ternera que tenía la piel con manchas blancas, sobre sus débiles patas. La vaca, inquieta, mugió, pero, calmándose cuando Levin le acercó la cría, comenzó a lamerla con su áspera lengua.
The calf fumbled about, pushing its nose under its mother's belly and swinging its little tail.
La becerra metía la cabeza bajo las ingles de la vaca, agitando la minúscula cola.
'Show a light here, Theodore, here,' said Levin, examining the calf.
–Alumbra, Fedor, acerca la linterna –decía Levin contemplando a la ternera–.
'Like its mother,' he said, 'although the colour is its father's; very fine, big-boned and deep-flanked.
Es parecida a su madre, aunque con los colores del padre. ¡Es hermosa!
Vasily Fedorich, isn't she fine?' he said, turning to the steward, and quite forgiving him for the buckwheat under the influence of his satisfaction about the calf.
Es grande y ancha de ancas. ¿Verdad que es muy hermosa, Basilio Fedorich? –dijo Levin al encargado, olvidándose, con la alegría que le causaba el buen aspecto de la ternera, del asunto del alforfón.
'Whom could she take after, not to be good?
–¿Cómo podía ser de otro modo? –repuso el hombre–.
Simon the contractor, came the day after you left.
¡Oh!, he de decirle también que Semen, el mercader, vino al día siguiente de marchar usted.
We shall have to employ him, Constantine Dmitrich,' said the steward.
Tendré que discutir mucho con él, Constantino Dmitrievich.
'I told you about the machine.'
Le decía el otro día, a propósito de la máquina...
This one question led Levin back to all the details of his farming, which was on a large and elaborate scale.
Aquella alusión introdujo a Levin en los pormenores de su economía, que era vasta y complicada.

He went straight from the cow-shed to the office, and after talking things over with the steward and with Simon the contractor, he returned to the house and went directly upstairs to the drawing-room.
Pasó con el encargado al despacho y, tras discutir con él y con Semen, se fue al salón.
CHAPTER XXVII
XXVII
IT WAS A LARGE OLD-FASHIONED HOUSE, and though only Levin was living in it, he used and heated the whole of it.
La casa era grande y antigua, y aunque Levin vivía solo la hacía calentar y la ocupaba toda.
He knew this to be foolish and even wrong, and contrary to his new plans, but this house was a whole world to Levin. It was the world in which his father and mother had lived and died.
Era una casa absurda y errónea que estaba en pugna con sus nuevos planes de vida, lo veía bien; pero en aquella casa se encerraba para él todo un mundo: el mundo donde vivieron y murieron sus padres.
They had lived a life which appeared to him ideally perfect, and which he had dreamed of renewing with a wife and family of his own.
Ellos habían llevado una existencia que a Levin le parecía la ideal y que él anhelaba renovar con su mujer y su familia.
Levin could scarcely remember his mother.
Apenas recordaba a su madre.
His conception of her was to him a sacred memory, and in his imagination his future wife was to be a repetition of the enchanting and holy ideal of womanhood that his mother had been.
La evocaba como algo sagrado, y en sus sueños su esposa había de ser la continuación de aquel ideal de santa mujer que fuera su madre.
He could not imagine the love of woman without marriage, and even pictured to himself a family first and then the woman who would give him the family.
No sólo le era imposible concebir el amor sin el matrimonio, sino que incluso en sus pensamientos imaginaba primero la familia y luego la mujer que le permitiera crear aquella familia.

His views on marriage therefore did not resemble those of most of his acquaintances, for whom marriage was only one of many social affairs; for Levin it was the chief thing in life, on which the whole happiness of life depended.

De aquí que sus opiniones sobre el matrimonio fueran tan diferentes de las de sus conocidos, para quienes el casarse no es sino uno de los asuntos corrientes de la vida. Para Levin, al contrario, era el asunto principal y del que dependía toda su dicha.
And now he had to renounce it.
¡Y ahora debía renunciar a ello!

When he had settled in the arm-chair in the little drawing room where he always had his tea, and Agatha Mikhaylovna had brought it in for him and had sat down at the window with her usual remark, 'I will sit down sir!' he felt that, strange to say, he had not really forgotten his dreams and that he could not live without them.

Se sentó en el saloncito donde tomaba el té. Cuando se acomodó en su butaca con un libro en la mano y Agafia Mijailovna le dijo, como siempre: «Voy a sentarme un rato, padrecito» y se instaló en la silla próxima a la ventana, Levin sintió que, por extraño que pareciera, no podía desprenderse de sus ilusiones ni vivir sin ellas.
With her, or with another, they would come true.
Ya que no con Kitty, había de casarse con otra mujer.

He read his book, and followed what he read, stopping now and then to listen to Agatha Mikhaylovna, who chattered indefatigably; and at the same time various pictures of farming and future family life arose disconnectedly in his mind.
Leía, pensaba en lo que leía, escuchaba la voz del ama de llaves charlando sin parar, y en el fondo de todo esto, los cuadros de su vida familiar futura desfilaban por su pensamiento sin conexión.
He felt that in the depth of his soul something was settling down, adjusting and composing itself.
Comprendía que en lo más profundo de su espíritu se condensaba, se posaba y se formaba algo.

He listened to Agatha Mikhaylovna's talk of how Prokhor had forgotten the Lord, was spending on drink the money Levin had given him to buy a horse with, and had beaten his wife nearly to death; he listened and read, and remembered the whole sequence of thoughts raised by what he was reading.

Oía decir a Agafia Mijailovna que Prójor, con el dinero que le regalara Levin para comprar un caballo, se dedicaba a beber, y que había pegado a su mujer casi hasta matarla. Levin escuchaba y leía, y la lectura reavivaba todos sus pensamientos.
It was a book of Tyndall's on heat.
Era una obra de Tindall sobre el calor.
He recalled his disapproval of Tyndall's self-conceit concerning the cleverness of his experiments and his lack of a philosophic outlook.
Se acordaba de haber censurado a Tindall por la satisfacción con que hablaba del éxito de sus experimentos y por su falta de profundidad filosófica.

And suddenly the joyous thought came uppermost: 'In two years' time I shall have two Dutch cows in my herd and Pava herself may still be alive; there will be twelve cows by Berkut, and these three to crown all – splendid!'

Y de repente le acudió al pensamiento una idea agradable: «Dentro de dos años tendré ya dos vacas holandesas. La misma "Pava" vivirá acaso todavía; y si a las doce crías de "Berkut" se añaden estas tres, ¡será magnífico!».
He returned to his book.
Volvió a coger el libro.
'Well, let us grant that electricity and heat are one and the same, but can we substitute the one quantity for the other in solving an equation?
«Aceptemos que la electricidad y el calor sean lo mismo; pero ¿es posible que baste una ecuación para resolver el problema de sustituir un elemento por otro?
Then what of it?
¿Entonces?
The connection between all the forces of nature can be felt instinctively without all that...
La unidad de origen de todas las fuerzas de la naturaleza se siente siempre por instinto...
It will be especially good when Pava's calf is already a red-mottled cow, and the whole herd in which these three will be...! Splendid!
Será muy agradable ver la cría de "Pava" convertida en una vaca pinta. Luego, cuando se les añadan esas tres, formarán una hermosa vacada.
To go out with my wife and the visitors and meet the herd...
Entonces saldremos mi mujer y yo con los convidados para verlas entrar.
My wife will say: "We, Constantine and I, reared this calf like a baby."
Mi mujer dirá: "Kostia y yo hemos cuidado a esa ternera como a una niña".
"How can you be interested in these things?" the visitor will ask.
"¿Es posible que le interesen estos asuntos?", preguntará el visitante.
"All that interests him interests me.."
"Sí; me interesa todo lo que le interesa a Constantino..."
But who is she?' and he remembered what had happened in Moscow.
Pero, ¿quién será esa mujer?» Y Levin recordó lo ocurrido en Moscú.
'Well, what is to be done?...
«¿Qué hacer?
It is not my fault.
Yo no tengo la culpa.
But now everything will be on new lines.
De aquí en adelante las cosas irán de otro modo.
It is nonsense to say that life will prevent it, that the past prevents it. I must struggle to live a better, a far better, life.'
Es una estupidez dejarse dominar por el pasado; es preciso luchar para vivir mejor, mucho mejor .. »
He lifted his head and pondered.
Levantó la cabeza, pensativo.

Old Laska, who had not yet quite digested her joy at her master's return and had run out to bark in the yard, now came back, bringing a smell of fresh air with her into the room and, wagging her tail, she approached him and putting her head under his hand whined plaintively, asking to be patted.

La vieja «Laska», aún emocionada por el regreso de su dueño, tras recorrer el patio ladrando, volvió, meneando la cola, introdujo la cabeza bajo la mano de Levin y, aullando lastimeramente, insistió en que la acariciase.
'She all but speaks,' said Agatha Mikhaylovna.
–No le falta más que hablar –dijo Agafia Mijailovna–.
'She is only a dog, but she understands that her master has come back feeling depressed.'
Es sólo una perra y sin embargo comprende que el dueño ha vuelto y que está triste.
'Why depressed?'
–¿Triste?
'Oh, don't I see?
–¿Piensa que no lo veo, padrecito?
I ought to understand gentlefolk by this time.
He tenido tiempo de aprender a conocer a los señores.
I have grown up among them from a child.
¿No me he criado acaso entre ellos? Pero ya pasará, padrecito.
Never mind, my dear, as long as you have good health and a clean conscience!'
Con tal que haya salud y la conciencia esté sin mancha, todo lo demás nada importa.
Levin looked at her intently, surprised that she knew so well what was in his mind.
Levin la miraba con fjeza, asombrado de que pudiera adivinar de aquel modo sus pensamientos.
'Shall I bring you a little more tea?' she said and went out with his cup.
–¿Traigo otra taza de té? –dijo la mujer. Cogió el cacharro vacío y salió.
Laska kept on pushing her head under his hand.
Levin acarició a «Laska», que persistía en querer colocar la cabeza bajo su mano.
He patted her a little, and she curled herself up at his feet with her head on her outstretched hind paw.
El animal se enroscó a sus pies, con el hocico apoyado en la pata delantera.
And to show that all was now well and satisfactory, she slightly opened her mouth, smacked her sticky lips, and drawing them more closely over her old teeth lay still in blissful peace.

Y, como en señal de que ahora todo iba bien, abrió la boca ligeramente, movió las fauces y, poniendo sus viejos dientes y sus húmedos labios lo más cómodamente posible, se adormeció en un beatífico reposo.
Levin attentively watched this last movement of hers.
Levin había seguido con interés sus últimos movimientos.
'And it is just the same with me!' he said to himself.
–Debo imitarla –murmuró–.
'It is just the same with me.
Haré lo mismo.
What does it matter...
Todo esto no es nada...
All is well.'
Las cosas marchan como deben...
EARLY IN THE MORNING after the ball Anna sent a telegram to her husband to say that she was leaving Moscow that same evening.
El día siguiente del baile, por la mañana, Ana Karenina envió un telegrama a su marido anunciándole su salida de Moscú para aquel mismo día.

'Really I must, I must go,' she said, explaining her altered plans to her sister-in-law in a tone suggesting that she had suddenly remembered so many things she had to do that it was not even possible to enumerate them all.
He de irme, he de irme ––decía explicando su repentina decisión a su cuñada en un tono en el cual parecía dar a entender que tenía tantos asuntos que le esperaban que no podía enumerarlos–.
'Really I had better go to-day.'
Sí, es preciso que me vaya hoy mismo.
Stephen Oblonsky was not dining at home, but promised to be back at seven to see his sister off.
Esteban Arkadievich no comió en casa, pero prometió ir a las siete para acompañar a su hermana a la estación.
Kitty also had not come, but had sent a note to say that she had a headache.
Kitty no fue; envió un billete excusándose con el pretexto de una fuerte jaqueca.
Dolly and Anna dined alone with the children and their English governess.
Dolly y Ana comieron solas con la inglesa y los niños.

Whether it is that children are inconstant or that they are sensitive and felt that Anna was not the same person to-day as she had been that other day when they had been so fond of her, and that she no longer took any interest in them, at any rate they suddenly left off playing with their aunt and loving her, and were not at all concerned about her leaving.

Éstos, fuese que no tuvieran el carácter constante, fuese que apreciaran en su tía Ana un cambio con respecto a ellos, dejaron de repente de jugar con ella y se desinteresaron en absoluto de su partida. Ana pasó la mañana ocupada en los preparativos del viaje.
Anna spent the whole morning preparing for her departure: writing notes to her Moscow acquaintances, making up accounts, and packing.
Escribía notas a sus amigos de Moscú, anotaba sus gastos y arreglaba su equipaje.

It seemed to Dolly that Anna was not at ease in her mind, but in a state of anxiety that Dolly knew well from her own experience, a state which does not come on without a cause, but generally hides dissatisfaction with oneself. After dinner Anna went to her room to dress and Dolly followed her.

A Dolly le pareció que no estaba tranquila, sino en aquel estado de preocupación, que tan bien conocía por propia experiencia, que rara vez se produce sin motivo y que en la mayoría de los casos indica sólo un profundo disgusto de sí mismo.
'How strange you are to-day!' said Dolly
Después de comer, Ana subió a su cuarto a vestirse y Dolly la siguió. –Te encuentro extraña hoy.
–¿Tú crees?
Do you think so?
No, no estoy extraña.
I am not strange, but wicked.
Lo que pasa es que me siento triste.
It sometimes happens to me.
Esto me sucede de vez en cuando...
I feel ready to cry.
Tengo como ganas de llorar.
It is very silly, but it will pass,' said Anna hurriedly, and she bent her flushed face over the tiny bag into which she was packing a night-cap and some lawn handkerchiefs.

Es una tontería; ya pasará –dijo Ana rápidamente, y ocultó su rostro enrojecido de repente, inclinándose hacia el otro lado para rebuscar en un saquito donde guardaba sus pañuelos y su gorro, de dormir.
Her eyes shone peculiarly and kept filling with tears.
Sus ojos brillaban de lágrimas, que apenas conseguía retener–.
'I did not want to leave Petersburg, and now I do not want to leave here.'
Salí de San Petersburgo de mala gana y ahora, en cambio, me cuesta irme de aquí.
'You came here and did a good action,' said Dolly, scrutinizing her attentively.
–Hiciste bien en venir, porque has realizado una buena obra –repuso Dolly, mirándola con atención.
Anna looked at her with her eyes wet with tears.
Ana volvió hacia ella sus ojos llenos de lágrimas.
'Do not say that, Dolly.
–No digas eso, Dolly.
I have done and could do nothing.
Ni hice ni podía hacer nada.
I often wonder why people conspire to spoil me.
Hay veces en que me pregunto el porqué de que todos se empeñen en mimarme tanto.
What have I done and what could I do?
¿Qué he hecho y qué podía hacer?
There was enough love in your heart to forgive...'
Has tenido bastante amor en tu corazón para perdonar, y eso fue todo.
'But for you, God only knows what would have happened!
–¡Dios sabe lo que habría pasado de no venir tú!
How lucky you are, Anna,' said Dolly.
¡Y es que eres tan feliz, Ana...!
'Everything in your soul is clear and good.'
¡Hay en tu alma tanta claridad y tanta pureza!
'Every one has a skeleton in their cupboard, as the English say.'
–Todos tenemos skeletons en el alma, como dicen los ingleses.
'What skeleton have you?
–¿Qué skeletons puedes tener tú?
Everything about you is so clear.'
¡Todo es tan claro en tu alma! ––exclamó Dolly.
'I have one!' said Anna, and unexpectedly following her tears, a sly, humorous smile puckered her lips.
–No obstante, los tengo –dijo Ana. Y una inesperada sonrisa maliciosa torció sus labios a través de sus lágrimas.
'Well, at least your skeleton is a funny one and not a dismal one,' said Dolly smiling. 'No, it is a dismal one. Do you know why I am going to-day and not to-morrow?
–Tus skeletons se me figuran más divertidos que lúgubres ––opinó Dolly, sonriendo también.
This is a confession of something that oppresses me, and I want to make it to you,' said Anna, determinedly throwing herself back in an arm-chair and looking straight into Dolly's eyes.
¿Sabes por qué me voy hoy en vez de mañana? Es una confesión que me pesa, pero te la quiero hacer ––dijo Ana, sentándose en la butaca y mirando a Dolly a los ojos.
And to her surprise Dolly saw that Anna was blushing to her ears and to the curly black locks on her neck.
Y, con gran sorpresa de Dolly, su cuñada palideció hasta la raíz de sus cabellos rizados.
'Do you know,' continued Anna,' why Kitty did not come to dinner?
–¿Sabes por qué no ha venido Kitty a comer? –preguntó Ana–.
She is jealous of me. I have spoiled...
Tiene celos de mí; he destruido su felicidad.
I mean I was the cause of the ball being a torture instead of a pleasure to her.
Yo he tenido la culpa de que el baile de anoche, del que esperaba tanto, se convirtiese para ella en un tormento.
But really, really I was not to blame, or only a very little,' she said, drawling out the word 'very' in a high-pitched voice.
Pero la verdad es que no soy culpable, o si lo soy, lo soy muy poco... ––dijo recalcando las últimas palabras.
'Oh, how like Steve you said that,' remarked Dolly laughing.
–Hablas lo mismo que Stiva –dijo Dolly, sonriendo.
'Oh no, no, I am not Steve,' she said frowning.
–¡Oh, no, no soy como él!
'The reason I have told you is that I do not even for a moment allow myself to distrust myself.'
Si te cuento esto, es porque no quiero dudar ni un minuto de mí misma.

But at the moment when she uttered these words she knew they were untrue: she not only distrusted herself but was agitated by the thought of Vronsky, and was leaving sooner than she had intended only that she might not meet him again.
Mas al decirlo, Ana tuvo conciencia de su debilidad: no sólo no tenía confianza en sí misma, sino que el recuerdo de Vronsky le causaba tal emoción que decidía huir para no verle más.
'Yes, Steve told me that you danced the mazurka with him, and that he...'
–Oui, Stiva, m'a raconté que has bailado toda la noche con Vronsky y que...
'You cannot think how queerly it came about.
–Es cosa que haría reír el extraño giro que tomaron las cosas.
I only thought of arranging the match, and – suddenly it all came out quite differently...
Me proponía favorecer el matrimonio de Kitty y en lugar de ello...
Perhaps against my own will I...'
Acaso yo contra mi voluntad ....
She blushed and stopped.
Ana se ruborizó y calló.
'Oh, they feel that at once!' said Dolly.
–Los hombres notan esas cosas en seguida ––dijo Dolly.
'But I should be in despair if there were anything serious in it on his side,' Anna interrupted her.
Y yo siento que él lo tomara en serio.
'I am sure that it will all be forgotten, and Kitty will no longer hate me.'
Pero estoy segura de que todo se olvidará en seguida y que Kitty me perdonará –añadió Ana.

'Well, do you know, Anna, to tell you the truth, I am not very anxious that Kitty should marry him: It is much better that it should come to nothing if he, Vronsky, is capable of falling in love with you in a day.'
–Si he de hablarte sinceramente, esa boda no me gusta demasiado para mi hermana. Ya ves que Vronsky es un hombre capaz de enamorarse de una mujer en un día.
'Oh, my goodness!
–¡Oh, Dios mío!

How stupid it would be,' said Anna, and again a deep flush of pleasure suffused her face at hearing the thought that occupied her mind expressed in words. 'So I am going away having made an enemy of Kitty, of whom I am so fond.

¡Sería tan absurdo eso! –exclamó Ana. Pero un rubor que delataba su satisfacción encendió sus mejillas al oír expresado en voz alta su propio pensamiento. –Ahora me voy convertida en enemiga de Kitty, por la que sentía tanta simpatía.
Oh, what a darling she is!
¡Es tan gentil!
But you will put it right? Eh, Dolly?'
Pero tú lo arreglarás, ¿verdad, Dolly?
Dolly could hardly repress a smile.
Dolly apenas pudo contener una sonrisa.
She was fond of Anna, but it was pleasant to find that she too had a weakness.
Estimaba a Ana, pero le complacía descubrir que también ella tenia debilidades.
'An enemy?
–¿Kitty enemiga tuya?
That is impossible.'
¡Es imposible!
'I should so like you all to love me as I love you and now I love you still more,' said Anna with tears in her eyes.
–Me gustaría irme sabiendo que me queréis todos tanto como yo os quiero a vosotros. Ahora os quiero más que antes.
'Oh dear, how silly I am to-day.'
¡Ay, estoy hecha una tonta! –dijo Ana, con los ojos inundados de lágrimas.
She dabbed her face with her handkerchief, and began to dress.
Luego se secó los ojos con el pañuelo y comenzó a arreglarse,
Oblonsky, smelling of wine and cigars, with his face red and happy, came in late, just as she was about to start.
Cuando se disponía ya a salir, se presentó Esteban Arkadievich, muy acalorado, oliendo a vino y a tabaco.
Anna's emotion had spread to Dolly, who as she embraced her sister-in-law for the last time whispered:
Dolly, conmovida por el afecto que Ana le testimoniaba, murmuró a su oído, al abrazarla por última vez:
'Remember that I love and always shall love you as my best friend!'
–Nunca olvidaré lo que has hecho por mí. Te quiero y te querré siempre como a mi mejor amiga.
'I do not know why you should,' said Anna, kissing her and trying to hide her tears.
–¿Por qué? –repuso Ana, conteniendo las lágrimas.
'You understood and understand me.
–Me has comprendido y me comprendes.
Good-bye, my sweet one!'
¡Adiós, querida Ana!
'WELL, THAT'S ALI, OVER, thank Heaven!' was Anna's first thought when she had taken leave of her brother, who stood to the last moment obstructing the entrance to the railway carriage.
«¡Gracias a Dios que ha terminado todo esto! », pensó Ana al separarse de su hermano, quien hasta que resonó la campana permaneció obstruyendo con su figura la portezuela del vagón.
She sat down beside her maid Annushka, and peered round the dimly-lit sleeping compartment.
Ana se acomodó en el asiento junto a Anuchka, su camarera.
'Thank Heaven, to-morrow I shall see Serezha and Alexis Alexandrovich again, and my good accustomed life will go on as of old.'
«¡Gracias a Dios que voy a ver mañana a mi pequeño Sergio y a Alexis Alejandrovich! Al fin mi vida recobrará su ritmo habitual», pensó de nuevo.
With the same preoccupied mind she had had all that day, Anna prepared with pleasure and great deliberation for the journey.
Presa aún de la agitación que la dominaba desde la mañana, empezó a ocuparse de ponerse cómoda.
With her deft little hands she unlocked her red bag, took out a small pillow which she placed on her knees, and locked the bag again; then she carefully wrapped up her feet and sat down comfortably.
Sus manos, pequeñas y hábiles, extrajeron del saco rojo de viaje un almohadón que puso sobre sus rodillas; se envolvió bien los pies y se instaló con comodidad.
An invalid lady was already going to bed.
Una viajera enferma se había tendido ya en el asiento para dormir.
Two other ladies began talking to Anna. One, a fat old woman, while wrapping up her feet, remarked upon the heating of the carriage.
Otras dos dirigieron vanas preguntas a Ana, mientras una mas vieja y gruesa se envolvía las piernas con una manta mientras emitía algunas opiniones sobre la pésima calefacción.

Anna said a few words in answer, but not foreseeing anything interesting from the conversation asked her maid to get out her reading-lamp, fixed it to the arm of her seat, and took a paper-knife and an English novel from her handbag.

Ana contestó a las señoras, pero no hallando interés en su conversación, pidió a su doncella que le diese su farolillo de viaje, lo sujetó al respaldo de su asiento y sacó una plegadera y una novela inglesa.
At first she could not read.
Era difícil abismarse en la lectura.

For a while the bustle of people moving about disturbed her, and when the train had finally started it was impossible not to listen to the noises, then there was the snow, beating against the window on her left, to which it stuck, and the sight of the guard, who passed through the carriage closely wrapped up and covered with snow on one side; also the conversation about the awful snow-storm which was raging outside distracted her attention.

El movimiento en torno suyo, el ruido del tren, la nieve que golpeaba la ventanilla a su izquierda y se pegaba a los vidrios, el revisor que pasaba de vez en cuando muy arropado y cubierto de copos de nieve, las observaciones de sus compañeras de viaje a propósito de la tempestad, todo la distraía.

And so it went on and on: the same jolting and knocking, the same beating of the snow on the windowpane, the same rapid changes from steaming heat to cold, and back again to heat, the gleam of the same faces through the semidarkness, and the same voices, – but at last Anna began to read and to follow what she read.

Pero, por otra parte, todo era monótono: el mismo traqueteo del vagón, la misma nieve en la ventana, los mismos cambios bruscos de temperatura, del calor al frío y otra vez al calor; los mismos rostros entrevistos en la penumbra, las mismas voces, y Ana acabó logrando concentrarse en la lectura y enterándose de lo que leía.
Annushka was already dozing, her broad hands, with a hole in one of the gloves, holding the red bag on her lap.
Anuchka dormitaba ya, sosteniendo sobre sus rodillas el saco rojo de viaje entre sus gruesas manos enguantadas, uno de cuyos guantes estaba roto.
Anna read and understood, but it was unpleasant to read, that is to say, to follow the reflection of other people's lives. She was too eager to live herself.
Ana Karenina leía y se enteraba de lo que leía, pero la lectura, es decir, el hecho de interesarse en la vida de los demás, le era intolerable, tenía demasiado deseo de vivir por sí misma.

When she read how the heroine of the novel nursed a sick man, she wanted to move about the sick-room with noiseless footsteps; when she read of a member of Parliament making a speech, she wished to make that speech; when she read how Lady Mary rode to hounds, teased her sister-in-law, and astonished everybody by her boldness – she wanted to do it herself.

Si la heroína de su novela cuidaba a un enfermo, Ana habría deseado entrar ella misma con pasos suaves en la alcoba del paciente; si un miembro del Parlamento pronunciaba un discurso, Ana habría deseado pronunciarlo ella; si lady Mary galopaba tras su traílla, desesperando a su nuera y sorprendiendo a las gentes con su audacia, Ana habría deseado hallarse en su lugar.
But there was nothing to be done, so she forced herself to read, while her little hand toyed with the smooth paper-knife.
Pero era en vano. Debía contentarse con la lectura, mientras daba vueltas a la plegadera entre sus menudas manos.

The hero of the novel had nearly attained to his English happiness of a baronetcy and an estate, and Anna wanted to go to the estate with him, when she suddenly felt that he must have been ashamed, and that she was ashamed of the same thing, – but what was he ashamed of?

El héroe de su novela empezaba ya a alcanzar la plenitud de su británica felicidad: obtenía un título de baronet y unas propiedades, y Ana sentía deseo de irse con él a aquellas tierras. De pronto la Karenina experimentó la impresión de que su héroe debía de sentirse avergonzado y que ella participaba de su vergüenza.
'What am I ashamed of?' she asked herself with indignant surprise.
Pero ¿por qué? «¿De qué tengo que avergonzarme?», se preguntó con indignación y sorpresa.
She put down her book, leaned back, and clasped the paper-knife tightly in both hands.
Y dejando la lectura, se reclinó en su butaca, oprimiendo la plegadera entre sus manos nerviosas.
There was nothing to be ashamed of.
¿Qué había hecho?
She called up all her Moscow memories. They were all good and pleasant.
Recordó la sucedido en Moscú, donde todo había sido magnífico.
She recalled the ball and Vronsky and his humble, enamoured gaze, and their relations with one another; there was nothing to be ashamed of.
Se acordó del baile, de Vronsky y de su rostro de enamorado enloquecido, de su conducta con respecto a él...
And yet at that very point of her recollections when she remembered Vronsky, the feeling of shame grew stronger and some inner voice seemed to say to her, 'warm, very warm, burning!'
Nada había que la pudiese avergonzar. Y, no obstante, al llegar a este punto de sus recuerdos, volvía a renacer en ella el sentimiento de vergüenza.
'Well, what of it?' she finally said to herself with decision, changing her position on the seat.
Parecía como si en el hecho de recordarle una voz interior le murmurase, a propósito de él: «Tú ardes, tú ardes.
'What does it signify?
Esto es un fuego, es un fuego». Bueno, ¿y qué?
Am I afraid to look straight at it?
«¿Qué significa todo eso?», se preguntó, moviéndose con inquietud en su butaca.
What of it?
«¿Temo mirar ese recuerdo cara a cara?
Just as if there existed, or could exist, between me and this officer-lad any relations differing from those with other acquaintances.'
¿Por ventura, entre ese joven oficial y yo existen otras relaciones que las que puede haber entre dos personas cualesquiera?»
She smiled disdainfully and again took up her book; but now she absolutely could not understand what she was reading.
Sonrió con desdén y volvió a tomar el libro; pero ya no le fue posible comprender nada de su lectura.
She passed her paper-knife over the windowpane, then pressed its cold smooth surface against her cheek and almost laughed aloud, suddenly overcome with unreasoning joy.

Pasó la plegadera por el cristal cubierto de escarcha, luego aplicó a su mejilla la superficie lisa y fría de la hoja, y poco faltó para que estallara a reír de la alegría que súbitamente se habla apoderado de ella.
She felt that her nerves were being stretched like strings drawn tighter and tighter round pegs.
Notaba sus nervios cada vez más tensos, sus ojos cada vez más abiertos, sus manos y pies cada vez más crispados.

She felt her eyes opening wider, her fingers and toes nervously moving, and something inside her stopping her breath, and all the forms and sounds in the swaying semi-darkness around struck her with unusual vividness.

Padecía una especie de sofocación y le parecía que en aquella penumbra las imágenes y los sonidos la impresionaban con un extraordinario vigor. Se preguntaba sin cesar si el tren avanzaba, retrocedía o permanecía inmóvil.
Momentary doubts kept occurring in her mind as to whether the train was moving forwards or backwards or standing still.
¿Era Anuchka, su doncella, la que estaba a su lado o una extraña? «¿Qué es lo que cuelga del asiento: una piel o un animal?
Was it Annushka who was sitting beside her, or a stranger?
¿Soy yo a otra mujer la que va sentada aquí?»
'And am I here, myself?
Abandonarse a aquel estado de inconsciencia le causaba terror.
Am I myself or another?'
Sentía, sin embargo, que aún podía oponer resistencia con la fuerza de su voluntad.
She was afraid of giving way to these delirious thoughts.
Haciendo, pues, un esfuerzo para recobrarse se incorporó, dejó su manta de viaje y su capa y se sintió mejor durante un instante.
Something seemed to draw her to them, but she had the power to give way to them or to resist.
Entró un hombre delgado, con un largo abrigo al que le faltaba un botón. Ana comprendió que era el encargado de la calefacción.
To get over it she rose, threw off her wrap, and took off the cape of her coat.
Le vio consultar el termómetro y observó que el viento y la nieve entraban en el vagón tras él. Luego, todo se volvía confuso de nuevo.

She came to her senses for a moment, and knew that the lean peasant in the long nankin coat with a button missing who had come into the compartment was the carriage stoker and was looking at the thermometer, and that the wind and snow rushed in when he opened the door; but afterwards everything again became confused...

El hombre alto garabateaba algo apoyándose en el tabique, la señora anciana estiró las piernas y el departamento pareció envuelto en una nube negra. Ana escuchó un terrible ruido, como si algo se rasgase en la oscuridad.

The peasant in the long coat started gnawing at something on the wall; the old woman began stretching her legs the whole length of the carriage, which she filled with a black cloud; then something squeaked and clattered in a dreadful manner, as if some one was being torn to pieces; then a blinding red light appeared, and at last everything was hidden by a wall.
Se diría que estaban torturando a alguien. Un rojo resplandor la hizo cerrar los ojos; luego todo quedó envuelto en tinieblas y Ana sintió la impresión de que se hundía en un precipicio.
Anna felt as if she had fallen through the floor. But all this did not seem dreadful, but amusing.
Aquellas sensaciones eran, no obstante, más divertidas que desagradables.
The voice of a man wrapped up and covered with snow shouted something just above her ear.
Un hombre enfundado en un abrigo cubierto de nieve le gritó algunas palabras al oído.
She rose and came to herself, understanding that they had stopped at a station and that this was the guard.
Ana se recobró. Comprendió que llegaban a una estación y que aquel hombre era el revisor.
She asked Annushka to give her the cape she had removed and a shawl, and putting them on she moved to the door.
Pidió a su doncella que le diese el chal y la pelerina y, poniéndoselos, se acercó a la portezuela.
'Are you going out?' asked Annushka.
–¿Desea salir, señora? –preguntó Anuchka.
'Yes, I want a breath of air.
–Sí: necesito moverme un poco.
It is so hot in here.'
Aquí dentro me ahogo.
She opened the carriage door. The snow and wind rushed toward her and had a tussle with her for the door.
Quiso abrir la portezuela, pero el viento y la lluvia se lanzaron contra ella, como si quisieran impedirle abrir, y también esto le pareció divertido.
And this too struck her as amusing.
Consiguió al fin abrir la puerta.

She went out. The wind seemed only to have waited for her: it whistled merrily and tried to seize and carry her off, but she held on to the cold door-post and held down her shawl, then stepping on to the platform she moved away from the carriage.

Parecía como si el viento la hubiese estado esperando afuera para llevársela entre alaridos de alegría. Se asió con fuerza con una mano en la barandilla del estribo y sosteniéndose el vestido con la otra, Ana descendió al andén.
The wind blew boisterously into the little porch of the carriage, but on the platform, sheltered by the train, it was quiet.
E1 viento soplaba con fuerza, pero en el andén, al abrigo de los vagones, había más calma.
With enjoyment she drew in full breaths of the snowy, frosty air as she stood beside her carriage looking round at the platform and the lighted station.
Ana respiró profundamente y con agrado el aire frío de aquella noche tempestuosa y contempló el andén y la estación iluminada por las luces.
A BLUSTERING STORM WAS RUSHING and whistling between the wheels of the train and round the pillars and the corners of the station.
Un remolino de nieve y viento corrió de una puerta a otra de la estación, silbó furiosamente entre las ruedas del tren y lo anegó todo: personas y vagones, amenazando sepultarlos en nieve.
The railway carriages, the pillars, the people, and everything that could be seen, were covered on one side with snow, and that covering became thicker and thicker.
La tempestad, se calmó por un breve instante, para desatarse de nuevo con tal ímpetu que parecía imposible de resistir.

A momentary lull would be followed by such a terrific gust that it seemed hardly possible to stand against it. Yet people, merrily exchanging remarks, ran over the creaking boards of the platform, and the big station doors were constantly being opened and shut.

No obstante, la puerta de la estación se abría y cerraba de vez en cuando, dando paso a gente que corría de un lado a otro, hablando alegremente, deteniéndose en el andén, cuyo pavimento de madera crujía bajo sus pies. La silueta de un hombre encorvado pareció surgir de la sierra a los pies de Ana.
The shadow of a man stooping slipped past her feet and she heard a hammer striking the carriage wheels.
Se oyó el golpe de un martillo contra el hierro; después una voz ronca resonó entre las tinieblas. –Envíen un telegrama –decía la voz.
'Let me have the telegram!' came an angry voice from the other side out of the stormy darkness.
Otras voces replicaron, como un eco: –Haga el favor, por aquí.
'Here, please, No. 28!' cried other voices, while many people muffled up and covered with snow ran hither and thither.
En el número veintiocho –y los empleados pasaron corriendo como llevados por la nieve.
Two gentlemen passed her with glowing cigarettes between their lips.
Dos señores, con sus cigarrillos encendidos, pasaron ante Ana fumando tranquilamente.

She took another deep breath to get her fill of fresh air and had already drawn her hand out of her muff to take hold of the handrail and get into the train when another man wearing a military overcoat came close between her and the wavering light of the lamp.

Respiró otra vez a pleno pulmón el aire frío de la noche, puso la mano en la barandilla del estribo para subir al vagón, cuando en aquel momento, la figura de un hombre vestido con capote militar, que estaba muy cerca de ella, le ocultó la vacilante luz del farol.
She turned round, and instantly recognized Vronsky.
Ana se volvió para mirarle y le reconoció.
With his hand in salute, he bowed and asked if she wanted anything and whether he could be of any service to her.
Era Vronsky. Él se llevó la mano a la visera de la gorra y le preguntó respetuosamente si podía servirla en algo.

For some time she looked into his face without answering, and, though he stood in the shade she noticed, or thought she noticed, the expression of his face and eyes. It was the same expression of respectful ecstasy that had so affected her the night before.

Ana le contempló en silencio durante unos instantes. Aunque Vronsky estaba de espaldas a la luz, la Karenina creyó apreciar en su rostro y en sus ojos la misma expresión de entusiasmo respetuoso que tanto la conmoviera en el baile.

She had assured herself more than once during those last few days, and again a moment ago, that Vronsky in relation to her was only one of the hundreds of everlastingly identical young men she met everywhere, and that she would never allow herself to give him a thought; yet now, at the first moment of seeing him again, she was seized by a feeling of joyful pride.

Hasta entonces Ana se había repetido que Vronsky era uno de los muchos jóvenes, eternamente iguales, que se encuentran en todas partes, y se había prometido no pensar en él. Y he aquí que ahora se sentía poseída por un alegre sentimiento de orgullo.
There was no need for her to ask him why he was there.
No hacía falta preguntar por qué Vronsky estaba allí.
She knew as well as if he had told her, that he was there in order to be where she was.
Era para hallarse más cerca de ella. Lo sabía con tanta certeza como si el propio Vronsky se lo hubiera dicho.
'I did not know that you were going too.
–Ignoraba que usted pensase ir a San Petersburgo.
Why are you going?' she asked, dropping the hand with which she was about to take hold of the handrail.
¿Tiene algún asunto en la capital? –preguntó Ana, separando la mano de la barandilla.
Her face beamed with a joy and animation she could not repress.
Y su semblante resplandecía.
'Why am I going?' he repeated, looking straight into her eyes.
–¿Algún asunto? –repitió Vronsky, clavando su mirada en los ojos de Ana Karenina–.
'You know that I am going in order to be where you are,' said he.
Usted sabe muy bien que voy para estar a su lado.
'I cannot do otherwise.'
No puedo hacer otra cosa.

At that moment the wind, as if it had mastered all obstacles, scattered the snow from the carriage roofs and set a loose sheet of iron clattering, and in front the deep whistle of the engine howled mournfully and dismally.

En aquel momento, el viento, como venciendo un invisible obstáculo, se precipitó contra los vagones, esparció la nieve del techo y agitó triunfalmente una plancha que había logrado arrancar. Con un aullido lúgubre, la locomotora lanzó un silbido.
The awfulness of the storm appeared still more beautiful to her now.
La trágica belleza de la tempestad ahora le parecía a Ana más llena de magnificencia.
He had said just what, her soul desired but her reason dreaded.
Acababa de oír las palabras que temía su razón, pero que su corazón deseaba escuchar. Guardó silencio.
She did not reply and he saw a struggle in her face.
Pero Vronsky, en el rostro de ella, leyó la lucha que sostenía en su interior.
'Forgive me if my words displease you,' he said humbly.
–Perdone si le he dicho algo molesto –murmuró humildemente.
He spoke courteously and respectfully, but so firmly and stubbornly that she was long unable to reply.
Hablaba con respeto, pero en un tono tan resuelto y decidido que Ana en el primer momento no supo qué contestar
'What you are saying is wrong, and if you are a good man, I beg you to forget it, as I will forget it,' she said at last.
–Lo que usted dice no está bien –murmuró Ana, al fin– y, si es usted un caballero, lo olvidará todo, como yo hago.
'Not a word, not a movement of yours will I ever forget, nor can I...'
–No lo olvidaré, ni podré olvidar nunca, ninguno de sus gestos, ninguna de sus palabras.
'Enough, enough!' she cried, vainly trying to give a severe expression to her face, into which he was gazing eagerly.
–¡Basta, basta! –exclamó ella en vano, tratando inútilmente de dar a su rostro una expresión severa.
She took hold of the cold handrail, ascended the steps, and quickly entered the little lobby leading into the carriage.
Y, cogiéndose a la fría barandilla, subió los peldaños del estribo y entró rápidamente en el coche.
But in that little lobby she stopped, going over in her imagination what had just taken place.
Sintió la necesidad de calmarse y se detuvo un momento en la portezuela.

Though she could remember neither his nor her own words, she instinctively felt that that momentary conversation had drawn them terribly near to one another, and this both frightened her and made her happy.
No recordaba bien lo que habían hablado, pero comprendía que aquel momento de conversación les había aproximado el uno al otro de un modo terrible, lo que la horrorizaba y la hacía feliz a la vez.
After standing still for a few seconds she went into the carriage and sat down.
Tras breves instantes, Ana entró en el departamento y se sentó.

The overwrought condition which tormented her before not only returned again, but grew worse and reached such a degree that she feared every moment that something within her would give way under the intolerable strain.
Su tensión nerviosa aumentaba: parecía que sus nervios iban a estallar. No pudo dormir en toda la noche.

She did not sleep at all that night, but the strain and the visions which filled her imagination had nothing unpleasant or dismal about them; on the contrary they seemed joyful, glowing, and stimulating.
Pero en aquella exaltación, en los sueños que llenaban su mente, no había nada doloroso; al contrario, había algo gozoso, excitante y ardiente. Al amanecer se durmió en su butaca.
Toward morning Anna, while still sitting up, fell into a doze; when she woke it was already light and the train was approaching Petersburg.
Era ya de día cuando despertó. Se acercaban a San Petersburgo.
At once thoughts of home, her husband, her son, and the cares of the coming day and of those that would follow, beset her.
Pensó en su hijo, en su marido, en sus ocupaciones domésticas, y aquellos pensamientos la dominaron por completo.
When the train stopped at the Petersburg terminus and she got out, the first face she noticed was that of her husband.
La primera persona a quien vio al apearse del tren fue su marido.

'Great heavens! What has happened to his ears?' she thought, gazing at his cold and commanding figure, and especially at the gristly ears which now so struck her, pressing as they did against the rim of his hat.

«¿Cómo le habrán crecido tanto las orejas en estos días, Dios mío?», pensó al ver aquella figura arrogante, pero fría, con su sombrero redondo que parecía sostenerse en los salientes cartílagos de sus orejas.

When he saw her, he came toward her with his customary ironical smile and looked straight at her with his large tired eyes. An unpleasant feeling weighed on her heart when she felt his fixed and weary gaze, as if she had expected to find him different.

Su esposo se acercaba a ella, mirándola atentamente con sus grandes ojos cansados, con su eterna sonrisa irónica en los labios, y esta vez la mirada inquisitiva de Alexis Alejandrovich la hizo estremecer. ¿Acaso esperaba encontrar a su marido distinto de como era en realidad?
She was particularly struck by the feeling of dissatisfaction with herself which she experienced when she met him.
¿O era que su conciencia le reprochaba toda la hipocresía, toda la falta de naturalidad que había en sus relaciones conyugales?

It was that ordinary well-known feeling, as if she were dissembling, which she experienced in regard to her husband, but formerly she had not noticed it, while now she was clearly and painfully conscious of it.
Aquella impresión dormía hacía largo tiempo en el fondo de su alma, pero sólo ahora se le aparecía en toda su dolorosa claridad.

'Yes, as you see. Here is a devoted husband; devoted as in the first year of married life, – consumed by desire to see you,' said he in his slow, high-pitched voice and in the tone in which he always addressed her, a tone which ridiculed those who could use such words in earnest.

–Como ves, tu enamorado esposo, tan enamorado como el primer día, anhelaba verte de nuevo –dijo Karenin con su voz lenta y seca, empleando el mismo tono levemente burlón que siempre usaba al dirigirle la palabra, como para ridiculizar aquel modo de expresarse.
'Is Serezha well?' she asked.
–¿Cómo está Sergio? –preguntó ella.
'And is this all the reward I get,' he said, 'for my ardour?
–¡Caramba, qué recompensa a mi entusiasmo amoroso!
He is quite well, quite well...'
Pues está bien, muy bien...
VRONSKY DID NOT EVEN TRY TO SLEEP that night.
Vronsky no trató siquiera de dormir.

He sat in his place, his eyes staring straight before him, not observing the people who went in or out, and if previously his appearance of imperturbable calm had struck and annoyed those who did not know him, he now seemed to them even prouder and more self-confident. He looked at people as if they were inanimate things.

Permaneció sentado en su butaca con los ojos abiertos. Ora mirando fijamente ante él, ora contemplando a los que entraban y salían; y si antes impresionaba a los desconocidos con su inalterable tranquilidad, ahora parecía aún más seguro de sí mismo y más lleno de orgullo.
A nervous young man, a Law Court official, who sat opposite, hated him for that look.
Los seres no tenían para él en aquel momento mayor importancia que las cosas.

The young man repeatedly lit his cigarette at Vronsky's, talked to him, and even jostled him to prove that he was not a thing but a man; yet Vronsky still looked at him as at a street lamp, and the young man made grimaces, feeling that he was losing self-control under the stress of this refusal to regard him as human.

Tal actitud le atrajo la enemistad de su vecino de asiento, un joven muy nervioso, empleado en el Ministerio de Justicia, que había hecho todo lo posible para que Vronsky reparara en que él pertenecía al mundo de los vivos. En vano le había pedido fuego, en vano le hablaba o le daba golpecitos en el codo.
Vronsky neither saw nor heard anyone.
Vronsky no manifestó más interés por él que por el farolillo del vagón. Ofendido por su impasibilidad, su compañero de viaje reprimía su enojo a duras penas.

He felt himself a king, not because he believed that he had made an impression on Anna – he did not yet believe that – but because the impression she had made on him filled him with happiness and pride.

Aquella olímpica indiferencia no significaba que Vronsky se sintiera feliz creyendo haber impresionado el corazón de Ana. Aun no se atrevía ni a imaginarlo, pero el solo hecho de pensar en ello le inundaba de orgullo y de alegría.
What would come of it all he did not know and did not even consider.
No sabía ni quería pensar en lo que podría resultar de todo aquello.
He felt that all his powers, hitherto dissipated and scattered, were now concentrated and directed with terrible energy toward one blissful aim. This made him happy.
Sólo presentía que sus fuerzas, desperdiciadas hasta entonces, iban a unirse para empujarle hacia un único y espléndido destino.
He knew only that he had told her the truth: that he would go where she went, that all the happiness of life and the only meaning of life for him now was in seeing and hearing her.
Verla, oírla, estar a su lado, éste era ahora el único objeto de su vida.
When he had got out of the train at Bologoe station to drink a glass of seltzer water and had seen Anna, he had involuntarily at once told her just what he was thinking about it.
Estaba tan poseído por aquel pensamiento que, apenas vio a Ana en la estación de Blagoe, donde él bajara a tomarse un vaso de soda, no pudo menos de manifestárselo.
He was glad he had said it to her, and that she now knew it and was thinking about it.
Estaba satisfecho de habérselo dicho, satisfecho porque ahora ella sabía ya que la amaba y no podría dejar de pensar en él.

He did not sleep at all that night. When he returned to the train, he kept recalling all the positions in which he had seen her, and all her words; and in his imagination, causing his heart to stand still, floated pictures of a possible future.

Ya en el vagón, Vronsky principió a recordar los más nimios detalles de las veces que se habían encontrado: los gestos, las palabras de Ana. Y su corazón palpitó ante las visiones que su imaginación le presentaba para lo porvenir.
When he got out of the train at Petersburg he felt, despite his sleepless night, as fresh and animated as after a cold bath.
Se apeó en San Petersburgo tan fresco y descansado como si saliera de un baño frío, aunque había pasado la noche sin dormir.
He stopped outside the carriage, waiting till she appeared.
Se paró junto a un vagón para ver pasar a Ana.
'I shall see her again,' he thought and smiled involuntarily.
«La volveré a ver», se decía, sonriendo sin darse cuenta.
'I shall see her walk, her face... she will say something, turn her head, look at me, perhaps even smile.'
«Acaso me dirija una palabra, un gesto, algo ...»
But before seeing her he saw her husband, whom the station-master was respectfully conducting through the crowd.
Pero al primero que vio fue a Karenin, a quien el jefe de estación acompañaba con grandes muestras de respeto.
'Dear me! the husband!'
«¡Ah, el marido!», dijo para sí.

Only now did Vronsky for the first time clearly realize that the husband was connected with her. He knew she had a husband, but had not believed in his existence, and only fully believed in him when he saw him there: his head and shoulders, and the black trousers containing his legs, and especially when he saw that husband with an air of ownership quietly take her hand.

Y, al verle erguido ante él, con sus piernas rectas enfundadas en los pantalones negros, al verle tomar el brazo de Ana con la naturalidad de quien ejecuta un acto al que tiene derecho, Vronsky hubo de recordar que aquel ser cuya existencia apenas considerara hasta entonces existía, era de carne y hueso y estaba unido estrechamente a la mujer que él amaba.

When he saw Karenin, with his fresh Petersburg face, his sternly self-confident figure, his round hat and his slightly rounded back, Vronsky believed in his existence, and had such a disagreeable sensation as a man tortured by thirst might feel on reaching a spring and finding a dog, sheep, or pig in it, drinking the water and making it muddy.

Aquel frío rostro de petersburgués, aquel aire indiferente y seguro, aquel sombrero redondo, aquella espalda ligeramente encorvada, aquel conjunto era una realidad y Vronsky había de reconocerlo, pero lo reconocía como un hombre que, muriendo de sed, al encontrarse con una fuente de agua pura descubriera que estaba ensuciada por un perro, un cerdo o una vaca que habían bebido en ella.
Karenin's gait, the swinging of his thighs, and his wide short feet, particularly offended Vronsky, who acknowledged only his own unquestionable right to love Anna.
Lo que sobre todo le desesperaba de Alexis Alejandrovich era su manera de andar, moviendo sus piernas de un modo rápido y balanceando algo el cuerpo.
But she was still the same, and the sight of her still affected him physically, exhilarating and stimulating him and filling him with joy.
A Vronsky le parecía que sólo él tenía derecho a amar a aquella mujer. Afortunadamente, ella seguia siendo la misma, y al verla, su corazón se sintió conmovido.
He ordered his German valet, who had run up from a second-class carriage, to get his luggage and take it home, and he himself went up to her.
El criado de Ana, un alemán que había hecho el viaje en segunda clase, fue a recibir órdenes. El marido le había entregado los equipajes antes de dirigirse resueltamente hacia Ana.
He saw the husband and wife meet, and with the penetration of a lover he noticed the signs of slight embarrassment when she spoke to her husband.
Vronsky asistió al encuentro de los esposos y su sensibilidad de enamorado le permitió percibir el leve ademán de contrariedad que hiciera Ana al encontrar a Alexis Alejandrovich.
'No, she doesn't and can't love him,' he decided mentally.
«No le ama, no puede amarle ...», pensó Vronsky.
While he was approaching her from behind he observed with joy that she became aware of his approach and was about to turn but, on recognizing him, again addressed her husband.
Se sintió feliz al notar que Ana, aunque de espaldas, adivinaba su proximidad. En efecto, ella se volvió, le miró y siguió hablando con su marido.
'Did you have a good night?' he inquired, bowing toward them both, and leaving it to Karenin to take the greeting as meant for himself and to recognize him, or not, as he pleased.
–¿Ha pasado usted la noche bien, señora? –preguntó Vronsky, saludando a la vez a los dos, y dando así ocasión al esposo de que le reconociese si le placía.
'Yes, quite comfortable, thank you,' she replied.
–Muy bien; gracias –repuso ella.

Her face seemed tired and had none of that play which showed now in a smile and now in the animation of her eyes; but just for an instant as she looked at him he saw a gleam in her eyes and, though the spark was at once extinguished, that one instant made him happy.
En su fatigado rostro no se dibujaba la animación de otras veces, pero a Vronsky le bastó para sentirse feliz apreciar que los ojos de Ana, al verle, se iluminaban de alegría.
She glanced at her husband to see whether he knew Vronsky.
Ella alzó la vista hacia su marido, tratando de descubrir si éste recordaba al Conde.
Karenin looked at him with displeasure, absently trying to recall who he might be.
Karenin contemplaba al joven con aire de disgusto y como si apenas le reconociera.
Vronsky's calm self-confidence struck like a scythe on a stone against the cold self-confidence of Karenin.
Vronsky se sintió incomodado. Su calma y su seguridad de siempre chocaban ahora contra aquella actitud glacial.
'Count Vronsky,' said Anna.
–El conde Vronsky –dijo Ana.
'Ah! I believe we have met before,' said Karenin extending his hand with indifference.
–¡Ah, ya; me parece que nos conocemos! –se dignó decir Karenin, dando la mano al joven–.
'You travelled there with the mother and came back with the son,' he said, uttering every word distinctly as though it were something valuable he was giving away.
Por lo que veo, al ir has viajado con la madre y al volver con el hijo –añadió arrastrando lentamente las palabras como si cada una le costara un rublo–. ¿Qué?
'I suppose you are returning from furlough?' he remarked; and without waiting for an answer said to his wife in his playful manner: 'Well, were many tears shed in Moscow over the parting?'
¿Vuelve usted de su temporada de permiso? –y, sin aguardar la respuesta de Vronsky, dijo con ironía, dirigiéndose a su mujer–: ¿Han llorado mucho los de Moscú al separarse de ti?
By addressing himself thus to his wife he conveyed to Vronsky his wish to be alone with her, and turning to Vronsky he touched his hat.
Creía terminar así la charla con el Conde. Y para completar su propósito, se llevó la mano al sombrero.
But Vronsky, addressing Anna, said:
Pero Vronsky interrogó a Ana:
'I hope to have the honour of calling on you.'
–Confío en que podré tener el honor de visitarles.
'I shall be very pleased,' he said coldly. 'We are at home on Mondays.'
–Con mucho gusto. Recibimos los lunes –dijo Alexis Alejandrovich con frialdad.
Then having finally dismissed Vronsky he said to his wife in his usual bantering tone: 'What a good thing it was that I had just half an hour to spare to meet you and was able to show my devotion!'
Y, sin hacerle más caso, prosiguió hablando a su mujer con el mismo tono irónico de antes: –¡Estoy encantado de disponer de media hora de libertad para testimoniarte mis sentimientos!
'You insist too much on your devotion, for me to value it greatly,' she replied in the same playful tone, while she involuntarily listened to the sound of Vronsky's footsteps following them.
–Parece como si me hablaras de ellos para realzar más su valor –repuso Ana, escuchando, involuntariamente, los pasos de Vronsky que caminaba tras ellos.
'But what does he matter to me?' she asked herself, and began inquiring of her husband how Serezha had got on during her absence.
«En realidad no me preocupan nada», pensó para sí. Y luego preguntó a su esposo cómo había pasado Sergio aquellos días.
'Oh, splendidly!
–Muy bien.
Mariette says he was very sweet.
Mariette me dijo que estaba de muy buen humor.
But – I'm sorry to grieve you! – he did not fret after you... like your husband!...
Lamento decirte que no te echó nada de menos. No le sucedía lo mismo a tu amante esposo.
But I must thank you once again, my dear, for having made me the present of a day.
Te agradezco que hayas vuelto un día antes de lo que esperaba.
Our dear samovar will be in ecstasies.'
Nuestro querido samovar se alegrará mucho también.
(He called the celebrated Countess Lydia Ivanovna samovar because she was always getting heated and boiling over about something.) 'She was asking after you.
Karenin aplicaba el apelativo de «samovar» a la condesa Lidia Ivanovna, por su constante estado de vehemencia y agitación.
And, do you know, if I may advise, you should go and see her to-day.
Siguió diciendo: –Me preguntaba diariamente por ti.
Her heart is always aching about somebody.
Te aconsejo que la visites hoy mismo.
At present, in addition to all her other worries, she is concerned about the Oblonskys' reconciliation.'
Ya sabes que su corazón sufre siempre por todo y por todos y ahora está particularmente inquieta con el asunto de la reconciliación de los Oblonsky.
Countess Lydia Ivanovna was Anna's husband's friend and the centre of that set in Petersburg Society with which Anna, through her husband, was most closely connected.
Lidia era una antigua amiga de su marido y el centro de aquel círculo social que, por las relaciones de su esposo, Ana se veía obligada a frecuentar.
'But I wrote to her.'
–Ya le he escrito.
'Yes, but she wants the particulars.
–Pero quiere saber todos los detalles.
Go and see her my dear, if you are not too tired...
Ve, amiga mía, ve a verla, si no estás muy cansada. Ea, te dejo.
Kondraty is here with the carriage for you, and I must be off to the Committee.
Tengo que asistir a una sesión. Kondreti conducirá tu coche.
Now I shan't have to dine alone,' he went on, no longer in a bantering manner. 'You can't think how I used...'
¡Gracias a Dios que al fin voy a comer contigo! –y añadió con seriedad–: ¡no puedes figurarte lo que me cuesta acostumbrarme a hacerlo solo!
and with a long pressure of her hand and a special kind of smile he helped her into the carriage.
Y estrechándole largamente la mano y sonriendo tan afectuosamente como pudo, Karenin la condujo a su coche.

THE FIRST PERSON TO MEET ANNA when she reached home was her son. He ran down the stairs to her regardless of his governess's cries, and with desperate delight called out: 'Mama! Mama!' When he reached her he clung round her neck.
El primer rostro que vio Ana al entrar en su casa fue el de su hijo, quien, sin atender a su institutriz, corrió escaleras abajo, gritando con alegría: –¡Mamá, mamá, mamá!
'I told you it was Mama!' he shouted to the governess.
Y se colgó de su cuello. –¡Ya decía yo que era mamá! ––dijo luego a la institutriz.
Her son, like his father, produced on Anna a feeling akin to disappointment. Her fancy had pictured him nicer than he was in reality.
Pero, como el padre, el hijo causó a Ana una desilusión.
She had to come down to reality in order to enjoy him as he was. But even as he was, he was charming, with his fair curls, blue eyes and plump shapely legs in tight-fitting stockings.

En la ausencia le imaginaba más apuesto de lo que era en realidad; y sin embargo era un niño encantador: un hermoso niño de bucles rubios, ojos azules y piernas muy derechas, con los calcetines bien estirados.
Anna experienced an almost physical pleasure in feeling his proximity and his caresses, and a moral solace when she met his simple, trustful, and loving gaze and heard his naive questions.
Ana sintió un placer casi físico en tenerle a su lado y recibir sus caricias, y experimentó un consuelo moral escuchando sus inocentes preguntas y mirando sus ojos cándidos, confiados y dulces.
She unpacked the presents which Dolly's children had sent him, and told him that there was a girl in Moscow whose name was Tanya, who could read and even teach other children.
Le ofreció los regalos que le enviaban los niños de Dolly y le contó que en Moscú, en casa de los tíos, había una niña llamada Tania que ya sabía escribir y enseñaba a los otros niños.
'And am I worse than she?' asked Serezha.
–Entonces, ¿es que valgo menos que ella? –preguntó Sergio.
'To me, you are the best in the world.'
–Para mí, vida mía, vales más que nadie.
'I know,' he said, smiling.
–Ya lo sabía –dijo Sergio, sonriendo.
Before Anna had time to finish her coffee the Countess Lydia Ivanovna was announced.
Antes de que Ana acabara de tomar el café, le anunciaron la visita de la condesa Lidia Ivanovna.
The Countess was a tall, stout woman with a sickly sallow complexion and beautiful, dreamy, black eyes. Anna was fond of her, but to-day she seemed to see her for the first time with all her defects.
Era una mujer alta y gruesa, de amarillento y enfermizo color y grandes y magníficos ojos negros, algo pensativos.
'Well, my dear! did you take the olive branch?' asked the Countess Lydia Ivanovna as soon as she entered the room.
Ana la quería mucho y, sin embargo, pareció apreciar sus defectos por primera vez. –¿Conque llevó a los Oblonsky el ramo de oliva, querida? –preguntó Lidia Ivanovna.
'Yes, it's all over; but the whole affair was not as serious as we thought,' Anna replied.
–Todo está arreglado –repuso Ana–. Las cosas no andaban tan mal como nos figurábamos.
'My sister-in-law is, in general, too impulsive.'
Ma belle soeur toma sus decisiones con demasiada precipitación y...
But the Countess, who was interested in everything that did not concern her, had a habit of never listening to what interested her, and she interrupted Anna:
Pero la Condesa, que tenía la costumbre de interesarse por cuanto no le importaba, y solía, en cambio, no poner atención alguna en lo que debía interesarle más, interrumpió a su amiga:
'Ah, yes!
–Estoy abatida.
There is much sorrow and evil in the world, and to-day I am terribly worried.'
¡Cuánta maldad y cuánto dolor hay en el mundo!
'Why! What is the matter?' asked Anna, trying to suppress a smile.
–¿Pues qué sucede? –interrogó Ana, dejando de sonreír.
'I am getting tired of breaking lances uselessly in the cause of truth, and sometimes I feel quite unstrung.
–Empiezo a cansarme de luchar en vano por la verdad, y a veces me siento completamente abatida.

That Little Sisters' affair' (this was a philanthropic religio-patriotic society) 'was going splendidly, but to work with those gentlemen is impossible,' continued the Countess Lydia Ivanovna with an ironical air of resignation to fate.

Ya ve usted: la obra de los hermanitos (se trataba de una institución benéfico–patriótico–religiosa) iba por buen camino. ¡Pero no se puede hacer nada con esos señores! –declaró la Condesa en tono de sarcástica resignación–.
'They took the idea and perverted it, and are now discussing it in such a trivial, petty way!
Aceptaron la idea para desvirtuarla y ahora la juzgan de un modo bajo a indigno.
Two or three, your husband among them, understand the full significance of the affair, but the others just drop it.
Sólo dos o tres personas, entre ellas su marido, comprendieron el verdadero alcance de esta empresa. Los demás no hacen más que desacreditarla...
Yesterday I had a letter from Pravdin...'
Ayer recibí carta de Pravdin.
Pravdin was a well-known Panslavist who resided abroad. The Countess told Anna what he had written.
(Se refería al célebre paneslavista Pravlin, que vivía en el extranjero.)

She then went on to tell her of other unpleasantnesses, and of the underhand opposition to the plan for uniting the Churches, and she went away in a hurry, as she had that afternoon to be at a meeting of another society as well as to attend a Slavonic Committee meeting.

La Condesa contó lo que decía en su carta y luego habló de los obstáculos que se oponían a la unión de las iglesias cristianas. Explicado aquello, la Condesa se fue precipitadamente, porque tenía que asistir a dos reuniones, una de ellas la sesión de un Comité eslavista.
'This is all just as it was before, but how is it that I never noticed it before?' said Anna to herself.
«Todo esto no es nuevo para mí. ¿Por qué será que lo veo ahora de otro modo?», pensó Ana.
'Or is it that she is specially irritated this morning?
«Hoy Lidia me ha parecido más nerviosa que otras veces.
But it is really funny; her aim is to do good, she is a Christian and yet she is always angry and always has enemies – all on account of Christianity and philanthropy!'

En el fondo, todo eso es un absurdo: dice ser cristiana y no hace más que enfadarse y censurar; todos son enemigos suyos, aunque estos enemigos se digan también cristianos y persigan los mismos fines que ella.»
After the Countess had left, a friend – a high official's wife – arrived and gave Anna all the Petersburg news. At three she also left, promising to come back to dinner.
Después de la Condesa llegó la esposa de un alto funcionario, que refirió a Ana todas las novedades del momento y se fue a las tres, prometiendo volver otro día a comer con ella.
Karenin was at the Ministry.
Alexis Alejandrovich estaba en el Ministerio.

Anna, left alone, spent part of the time before dinner in seeing her son have his dinner (he dined apart), in putting her things in order, and in reading and answering the notes and letters that had accumulated on her table.
Ana asistió a la comida de su hijo (que siempre comía solo) y luego arregló sus cosas y despachó su correspondencia atrasada.
The feeling of causeless shame she had felt during the journey, and her agitation, had quite vanished.
Nada quedaba en ella de la vergüenza a inquietud que sintiera durante el viaje.
In her accustomed conditions of life she again felt firm and blameless. She thought with wonder of her state the day before.
Ya en su ambiente acostumbrado se sintió ajena a todo temor y por encima de todo reproche sin comprender su estado de ánimo del día anterior.
'What had happened?
«¿Qué sucedió, a fin de cuentas?», pensaba.
Nothing! Vronsky said some silly things, to which it will be easy to put a stop, and I said what was necessary.
«Vronsky me dijo una tontería y yo le contesté como debía. Es inútil hablar de ello a Alexis.
It is unnecessary and impossible to speak of it to my husband.
Parecería que daba demasiada importancia al asunto.»
To speak of it would be to give it an importance that does not belong to it.'
Recordó una vez que un subordinado de su marido le hiciera una declaración amorosa.

She remembered how she had once told her husband about one of his subordinates who very nearly made her a declaration, and how Karenin had answered that every woman living in Society was liable to such things, but that he had full confidence in her tact and would never degrade himself and her by being jealous. 'So there is no need to tell him!

Creyó oportuno contárselo a Karenin y éste le dijo que toda mujer de mundo debía estar preparada a tales eventualidades, y que él confiaba en su tacto, sin dejarse arrastrar por celos que habrían sido humillantes para los dos. «De modo que vale más callar», decidió ahora Ana como remate de sus reflexiones.
Besides; thank Heaven there is nothing to tell!' she said to herself.
«Además, gracias a Dios, nada tengo que decirle.»

KARENIN RETURNED FROM THE MINISTRY at four o'clock, but, as often happened, he had no time to go up and see his wife. He went straight to his study to receive some petitioners and sign a few documents brought by his private secretary.

Alexis Alejandrovich llegó a su casa a las cuatro, pero como le ocurría a menudo, no tuvo tiempo de ver a su esposa y hubo de pasar al despacho para recibir las visitas y firmar los documentos que le llevó su secretario.

At the Karenins' dinners there were usually about three visitors. This time there came an old lady, a cousin of Karenin's; the Director of a Department; the Director's wife; and a young man who had been recommended to Karenin for a post under him.
Como de costumbre, había varios invitados a comer: una anciana prima de Karenin, uno de los los directores de su ministerio, con su mujer, y un joven que le habían recomendado.
Anna went into the drawing-room to entertain them.
Ana bajó al salón para recibirles.

Exactly at five – the bronze clock (style of Peter I) had not finished striking – Karenin entered in evening dress with a white tie and two stars on his coat, as he had to attend an official meeting directly after dinner.

Apenas el gran reloj de bronce de estilo Pedro I dio las cinco, Alexis Alejandrovich apareció vestido de etiqueta, con corbata blanca y dos condecoraciones en la solapa, pues tenía que salir después de comer.
Every moment of his life was filled up and apportioned, and in order to find time to perform all the tasks allotted to each day he observed the strictest regularity.
