'WELL, KAPITONICH?' SAID SEREZHA, as on the day before his birthday he returned rosy and bright from a walk, and gave his overcoat to the tall old hall-porter, who looked smilingly down from his height at the little fellow.
–Kapitonich –dijo Sergio, colorado y alegre, al volver de pasear la víspera del día de su cumpleaños, entregando su poddievska al viejo portero, que le sonreía desde lo alto de su estatura–––.
'Well, has the bandaged official been to-day?
¿Ha venido hoy aquel empleado de la mejilla vendada?
Has Papa seen him?'
¿Le ha recibido papá?
'He has seen him.
–Le recibió, señorito.
As soon as the secretary left, I announced him,' answered the hall-porter with a wink.
En cuanto salió el secretario, le anuncié –dijo el portero, guiñando jovialmente el ojo–.
'Let me take it off for you.'
Déjeme que le ayude a quitarse...
'Serezha!' said his tutor, a Slav, stopping in the doorway that led to the inner rooms, 'take it off yourself.'
–Sergio –dijo el preceptor eslavo, parándose en la puerta que dabs a las habitaciones interiores–. Quítese usted mismo los chanclos.
But Serezha, though he heard his tutor's weak voice, paid no heed to it.
Aunque Sergio oyó la voz débil del preceptor, no le hizo caso.
He stood holding on by the porter's shoulder-strap and looking into his face.
De pie, agarrándose al cinturón del portero agachado, le miraba el rostro.
'Well, and has Papa done what he wanted?'
–¿Y le concedió papá lo que necesitaba?
The hall-porter nodded affirmatively.
Kapitonich hizo con la cabeza una señal afirmativa.
The bandaged official, who had called seven times to petition Karenin about something, interested both Serezha and the hall-porter.
Tanto Sergio como el portero se interesaban por aquel empleado, que había ido allí ya siete veces a pedir no se sabía qué a Alexey Alejandrovich.
Serezha had met him in the hall, and had heard him piteously begging the porter to announce him to Karenin, and saying that he and his children were face to face with death.
El niño le había encontrado en el vestíbulo y oyó cómo suplicaba con voz lastimera al portero que le anunciase, diciendo que a él y a sus hijos no les quedaba otro recurso que dejarse morir.
Since then, having again met the official in the hall, Serezha had become interested in him.
Sergio encontró al funcionario otra vez y, a partir de entonces, se interesó por él.
'And was he very glad?' he asked.
–¿Y estaba muy alegre? –preguntó.
'How could he help being glad?
–Figúrese.
He nearly jumped for joy as he went away.'
Salía casi saltando...
'And has anything been brought?' inquired Serezha, after a pause.
–¿Han traído algo? –preguntó Sergio, después de una pausa.
'Well, sir,' said the porter, shaking his head and whispering, 'there is something from the Countess.'
–Una cosa de la Condesa, señorito –dijo el portero en voz baja.
Serezha knew at once that the hall-porter was speaking of a birthday present for him from the Countess Lydia Ivanovna.
Sergio comprendió en seguida que aquello de que hablaba el portero era el regalo que Lidia Ivanovna le hacía por su cumpleaños.
'You don't say so? Where is it?'
–¿Dónde está?
'Korney has taken it in to your Papa.
–Korney se lo llevó a papá.
I should think it's a fine thing.'
Debe de ser una cosa muy buena.
'What size?
–¿Cómo es de grande?
About so big?'
¿Así?
'Not quite, but a fine thing.'
–Algo menos, pero muy buena...
'A book?'
–¿Un libro?
'No, just a thing.
–No, otra cosa...

Go, go! Vasily Lukich is calling you,' said the hall-porter, hearing the approaching step of the tutor, and gently disengaging the little hand in the half-drawn-off glove which held him by his shoulder-strap, as he nodded and winked toward the tutor.

Ande, ande; le está llamando Basilio Lukich ––dijo el portero, oyendo los pasos del preceptor, que se acercaba, y librándose suavemente de la manita calzada a medias con un guante azul, que se asía a su cinturón, y señalando con la cabeza a Lukich.
'Vasily Lukich, one moment!' said Serezha with that bright and affectionate smile which always overcame the conscientious Vasily Lukich.
–Voy en seguida, Basilio Lukich –dijo Sergio con la sonrisa alegre y afectuosa que desarmaba siempre al severo preceptor.

Serezha was in too high spirits, too happy not to share with his friend the hall-porter another family joy about which he had heard from Lydia Ivanovna's niece whom he met walking in the Summer Gardens.

Sergio estaba demasiado alegre; se sentía demasiado feliz para no compartir con el portero la satisfacción familiar de que le había informado en el jardín de Verano la sobrina de la condesa Lidia Ivanovna.
This joy appeared to him particularly important because it coincided with the satisfaction of the official, and his own happiness that a present had been brought.
Tal alegría le parecía particularmente importante, sobre todo por coincidir con la del humilde funcionario y la que le proporcionaba la idea de los juguetes que le habían traído.
To Serezha it seemed that this day was one on which everybody ought to be happy and gay.
A Sergio le parecía que en este día todos habían de estar alegres y satisfechos.
'Do you know, Papa has received the Order of Alexander Nevsky?'
–¿Sabes que papá ha recibido la condecoración de Alejandro Nevsky?
'Of course I do!
–Sí.
People have already been calling to congratulate him.'
Ya han venido a felicitarle.
'Well, and is he pleased?'
–¿Y está contento?
'How can he help being pleased at the Tsar's favour?
–¡Cómo no va a estar contento recibiendo esa condecoración del Zar?
It shows he's deserved it,' replied the hall-porter sternly and seriously.
Eso significa que lo merece –repuso el portero, severo y grave.

Serezha grew thoughtful as he peered into the hall-porter's face, which he had studied in minute detail – especially the chin which hung beneath the grey whiskers and which no one saw but Serezha, who always looked up at him.

Sergio quedó pensativo y escudriñó el conocido rostro del portero hasta en sus menores detalles, en especial su barbita entre las dos patillas, en la que nadie reparaba excepto Sergio, que la miraba siempre desde abajo.
'And your daughter, has she been here lately?'
–¿Hace mucho que no te visita tu hija?
The hall-porter's daughter was a ballet-dancer.
La hija del portero era bailarina en el Teatro Imperial.
'How can she come on week-days?
–Entre semana no puede venir.
They have to learn too, and so must you, sir!
También ellas estudian. Y usted tiene que estudiar igualmente.
Go along!'
Váyase, señorito.
On entering the schoolroom, instead of sitting down to his lessons, Serezha told his tutor of his guess that the parcel that had been brought must be a railway train. 'What do you think?' he asked.
Entrando en la habitación, Sergio, en vez de sentarse a estudiar, expresó al maestro su suposición de que lo que le habían regalado debía de ser una máquina.
But Vasily Lukich only thought that Serezha must prepare his grammar lesson, as his teacher was coming at two.
–¿Qué piensa usted? –le preguntó. Basilio Lukich sólo pensaba que tenía que estudiar la lección de gramática, porque el profesor llegaba a las dos.
'Oh, but just tell me, Vasily Lukich!' said Serezha, suddenly, after sitting down at the table with a book in his hand. 'What is higher than the Alexander Nevsky?
–Dígame, Basilio Lukich –suplicó el niño, ya sentado a la mesa de estudio, con el libro en la mano–: ¿qué condecoración hay más importante que la de Alejandro Nevsky?
You know Papa has received the Order of Alexander Nevsky?'
¿Sabe usted que se la han otorgado a papá?
Vasily Lukich replied that the Order of Vladimir was higher.
Basilio Lukich contestó que la condecoración superior era la de Vladimiro.
'And higher still?'
–¿Y más que ésa?
'The highest is the St Andrew.'
–La de Andrés Pervosvanny es superior a todas.
'And higher still?'
–¿Y no hay otra más alta?
'I don't know.'
–No lo sé.
'Even you don't know!'
–¿Cómo? ¿Tampoco usted lo sabe?
And Serezha, leaning his elbows on the table, began to reflect.
Sergio, apoyando los codos en la mesa, quedó pensativo.
His reflections were most complex and varied.
Sus pensamientos eran complejos y varios.

He imagined his father suddenly receiving the Orders of Vladimir and Saint Andrew, and how much kinder in consequence he would be to-day at lesson-time, and how he himself when he grew up would receive all the Orders, and that they would invent one higher than the Saint Andrew.

Imaginaba que su padre iba a recibir de repente las condecoraciones de Andrés y Vladimiro y que, en consecuencia, se mostraría mucho más indulgente para la lección de hoy; pensaba que cuando fuera mayor, recibiría él también todas aquellas condecoraciones y asimismo las que se crearan superiores a la de Andrés.
As soon as it was invented he would gain it.
Apenas las crearan, Sergio las merecería.
A yet higher one would be invented, and he would immediately get that one too.
Y si las creaban más altas aún, también él había de obtenerlas al punto.
In these reflections time passed until the teacher arrived. The lesson on the attributes of Time, Place, and Manner of Action had not been learnt.

Pensando así pasó el tiempo y, cuando llegó el profesor, la lección de tiempo, lugar y modo no estaba estudiada, y el profesor quedó, no sólo descontento, sino hasta triste, ya que hizo afligirse al niño.
The teacher was not only dissatisfied but also saddened. His sadness touched Serezha.
No se creía culpable de no haber estudiado la lección, ya que, a pesar de todo su deseo, no había podido hacerlo.

He did not feel guilty for not having learned his lesson, for try as he would he positively could not do it. While the teacher was explaining, he believed him and seemed to understand, but as soon as he was left alone he positively could not remember or understand how so short and simple a word as suddenly could be an attribute of the manner of action; but all the same he was sorry he had grieved his teacher.

Mientras su maestro había estado con él, parecíale comprender; pero en cuanto quedó solo no pudo recordar ni entender más que una frase tan breve y obvia como que «de repente» era un modo adverbial; pero comprendió, en todo caso, que había disgustado al maestro.
He chose a moment when the teacher was looking silently into the book:
Escogió un momento en que el profesor miraba, en silencio, el libro.
'Michael Ivanovich, when is your birthday?' he suddenly asked.
–Mijail Ivanovich, ¿cuándo es su santo? –le preguntó bruscamente.
'You would do better to think of your work.
–Mejor sería que atendiese usted a sus lecciones.
Birthdays do not signify anything to reasonable beings.
El día del santo de uno no tiene importancia para una persona inteligente.
It is just a day like any other, on which we must work.'
Es un día como otro cualquiera en el que hay que trabajar como siempre.

Serezha looked attentively at his teacher, at his thin little beard and his spectacles which had slipped down the bridge of his nose, and became so engrossed in thought that he no longer heard what his teacher was explaining.

Sergio miró atentamente al profesor, examinó su barba rala, sus lentes que descendían más abajo de la señal que le hacían sobre la nariz, y quedó tan hundido en sus reflexiones que no entendió ya nada de lo que le explicaba.
He was aware that the teacher himself did not believe what he was saying; he felt that by the tone in which the words were uttered.
Se hacía cargo de que el profesor no pensaba lo que decía, y lo adivinaba por el tono en que habían sido pronunciadas aquellas palabras.
'But why have they all agreed to speak in the same way about the dullest and most useless things?
«¿Por qué se habrán puesto todos de acuerdo en hablar de un modo aburrido a inútil?
Why does he repulse me?
¿Por qué me rechaza?
Why does he not love me?' he asked himself sadly, and could find no answer.
¿Por qué no me quiere?» Así se preguntaba con tristeza sin hallar contestación.
AFTER THE TEACHER'S LESSON Serezha had a lesson from his father.
A esta lección seguía la de su padre.
Before his father came Serezha sat at the table playing with a pocket-knife and thinking.
Mientras él venía, Sergio se sentó a la mesa, jugueteando con el cortaplumas y pensando.
Among his favourite occupations was keeping a look out for his mother when he went out walking.
En el número de las ocupaciones predilectas de Sergio figuraba la de buscar a su madre en el paseo.

He did not believe in death in general, and especially not in her death, despite what Lydia Ivanovna had told him and his father had confirmed, and therefore even after he had been told she was dead, he went on looking for her when on his walks.

No creía en la muerte en general, ni en particular en la de su madre, aunque Lidia Ivanovna se lo dijera y papá se lo hubiera confirmado. Por eso, aun después de decirle que había muerto, cuantas veces salía a pasear continuaba buscándola.
He imagined that every well-developed and graceful woman with dark hair was his mother.
Toda mujer llena, graciosa, de cabellos oscuros, le parecía su madre.
At the sight of any such woman a feeling of such tenderness awoke in his heart that he grew breathless and tears came to his eyes.
En cuanto veía una mujer así, se elevaba en él un sentimiento tan dulce que se ahogaba, y las lágrimas le acudían a los ojos.
He expected that at any moment she would approach and lift her veil.
Esperaba que ella, en aquel momento, se acercase a él y se levantase el velo.

Then he would see her whole face, she would smile, embrace him, and he would smell her peculiar scent, feel the tenderness of her touch, and cry with joy as he had done one evening when he lay at her feet and she tickled him, while he shook with laughter and bit her white hand with the rings on the fingers.

Vería todo su rostro sonreírle, la abrazaría, percibiría su perfume y la suavidad de su mano y lloraría de dicha, como una noche en que se tendió a sus pies y ella le hacía cosquillas y él reía mordiéndole su blanca mano llena de sortijas.

Later on, when he accidentally heard from his nurse that she was not dead, and his father and Lydia Ivanovna explained that to him she was dead because she was bad (which he could not at all believe, for he loved her), he continued to look out for and wait for her.

Cuando supo casualmente por el aya que su madre no había muerto y que su padre y Lidia Ivanovna se lo habían dicho así porque ella era mala (en lo cual él, como la quería tanto, no creyó en modo alguno), siguió esperándola y buscándola todavía con más ahínco.
There had been a lady with a purple veil in the Summer Garden to-day whom he had watched with a sinking heart as she came toward him along the path.

Hoy, en el Jardín de Verano, había visto una señora alta, con velo lila, a la que había seguido con la mirada, sintiendo el corazón estremecido, pensando que era ella, mientras la estuvo viendo avanzar a su encuentro por el caminito.
The lady did not come up to them and disappeared somewhere.
Pero la señora no llegó a su lado; desapareció no se sabía por dónde.

To-day Serezha was more than ever conscious of a flow of love for his mother in his heart, and now as he sat lost in thought, waiting for his father, he notched the whole edge of the table with his knife, looking before him with shining eyes and thinking about her.

Y hoy Sergio sentía más cariño que nunca hacia su madre y, mientras esperaba a su padre, sin darse cuenta, rayó con el cortaplumas todo el borde de la mesa, mirando ante sí con ojos brillantes y pensando en ella.
Vasily Lukich roused him. 'Your Papa is coming!'
–Ya viene papá –interrumpió Basilio Lukich.
Serezha jumped up, approached his father, kissed his hand, and looked at him attentively, trying to find some sign of his joy at receiving the Order of Alexander Nevsky.

Sergio se levantó de un salto, corrió hacia su padre y, después de besarle la mano, le miró atentamente, esperando descubrir en su rostro señales de alegría relativas a la condecoración de Alejandro Nevsky.
'Have you had a nice walk?' asked Karenin, as he sat down in his arm-chair, drew toward him an Old Testament and opened it.
–¿Te has divertido en el paseo? –preguntó Karenin, sentándose en su butaca, acercando la Biblia y abriéndola.

Although Karenin had more than once told Serezha that every Christian ought to be well acquainted with Bible history, he often in Old Testament history had to consult the book, and Serezha noticed this.
Aunque Alexey Alejandrovich decía a menudo a Sergio que todo cristiano debe conocer bien la Historia Sagrada, él mismo solía consultar la Biblia a menudo, y su hijo no dejaba de observarlo.
'Yes, Papa, it was very amusing,' answered Serezha, sitting down sideways on his chair and beginning to rock it, which was forbidden.
–Sí, me divertí mucho, papá –repuso el niño, sentándose de lado en la silla y balanceándola, lo cual le estaba prohibido–.
'I met Nadenka' (Nadenka was Lydia Ivanovna's niece, who was being educated at her aunt's house). 'She told me you had received another Order, a new one.
He visto a Nadeñka –se refería a una sobrina de Lidia Ivanovna que vivía en casa de ésta– y me ha dicho que le han dado a usted una nueva condecoración.
Are you glad, Papa?'
¿Está usted satisfecho, papá?
'First of all, don't rock your chair,' said Karenin.
–Ante todo, no te balancees así –repuso su padre–.
'Secondly, it's not the reward but the work that is precious.
Y luego, lo que debe agradar es el trabajo y no su recompensa. Desearía que te fijaras mucho en esto.
I wish you understood that.
Si trabajas y estudias tus lecciones sólo por el premio, el trabajo te parecerá muy pesado.

You see, if you take pains and learn in order to get a reward, the work will seem hard; but when you work' (Karenin said this remembering how he had sustained himself that morning by a sense of duty in the dull task of signing a hundred and eighteen papers) – 'if you love your work, you will find your reward in that.'

Pero cuando trabajes por amor al trabajo, hallarás en él la mejor recompensa. Alexey Alejandrovich hablaba así recordando cómo se había sostenido a sí mismo con la idea del deber durante el aburrido trabajo de aquella mañana, consistente en firmar ciento dieciocho documentos.
Serezha's eyes, that had been shining with affection and joy, grew dull and drooped under his father's gaze.
El dulce y alegre brillo de los ojos de Sergio se apagó, y bajó la vista al encontrar la de su padre.
It was the same long-familiar tone in which his father always addressed him, and to which Serezha had already learnt to adapt himself.
Aquel tono, bien conocido, era el que empleaba siempre con él, y Sergio sabía cómo debía acogerlo.
His father always talked to him, Serezha felt, as if he were some imaginary boy out of a book, quite unlike Serezha; and with his father he always tried to pretend to be that boy out of a book.

Su padre le hablaba como dirigiéndose a un niño imaginario –o así le parecía a Sergio–, a un niño como los que se hallan en los libros y a los que Sergio no se parecía en nada. Pero el niño procuraba entonces fingir que era uno de aquellos niños de los libros.
'You understand me, I hope,' said the father.
–Espero que lo comprendas –concluyó su padre.
'Yes, Papa,' answered the boy, pretending to be that imaginary boy.
–Sí, papá –respondió Sergio, fingiendo ser aquel niño imaginario.
The lesson consisted in learning by heart some verses from the Gospels and repeating the beginning of the Old Testament.
La lección consistía en escribir de memoria algunos versículos del Evangelio y en dar un repaso al Antiguo Testamento.

Serezha knew the Gospel verses pretty well, but whilst saying them he became so absorbed in the contemplation of a bone in his father's forehead, which turned very sharply above the temple, that he became confused and put the end of one verse where the same word occurred after the beginning of another.

Sergio conocía bastante bien los versículos del Evangelio, pero ahora, mientras los recitaba, se fijó en el hueso de la frente de su padre, y al observar el ángulo que formaba con la sien, el chiquillo se confundió en los versículos y el final de uno lo colocó en el principio de otro que empezaba con la misma palabra.
It was evident to Karenin that the boy did not understand what he was saying, and this irritated him.
Karenin notó que el niño no comprendía lo que estaba diciendo y se irritó.

He frowned and began an explanation that Serezha had heard many times already and could never remember because he understood it too clearly, just as he could not remember that the word suddenly was an attribute of the manner of action.
Arrugó el entrecejo y empezó a decir lo que Sergio oyera ya cien veces y no podía recordar por comprenderlo demasiado bien, al estilo de la frase «de repente», que era un modo adverbial.

Serezha looked at his father with scared eyes, and could only think of whether his father would make him repeat what he had just said, as he sometimes did. This thought frightened him so much that he no longer understood anything at all.
Miraba, pues, a su padre con asustados ojos pensando sólo en una cosa: en sí le obligaría a repetir lo que decía ahora, como sucedía a veces.

However, his father did not make him repeat it, but went on to the lesson from the Old Testament. Serezha related the events themselves quite well, but when he had to answer questions as to what some of the events symbolized, he knew nothing about it, though he had been punished before for not knowing this lesson.

Pero su padre no le hizo repetir nada y pasó a la lección del Antiguo Testamento, Sergio recitó bien los hechos, pero cuando pasó a explicar la significación profética que tenían algunos, manifestó una total ignorancia, a pesar de que ya había sido otra vez castigado por no saber la misma lección.
The part, however, about which he could not say anything at all but only floundered, cut the table, and rocked his chair, was that about the antediluvian patriarchs.
Y cuando no pudo ya contestar absolutamente nada y quedó parado, rayando la mesa con el cortaplumas, fue al tratar de los patriarcas antediluvianos.
He did not know any of them except Enoch, who was taken up to Heaven alive.
No recordaba a ninguno de ellos, excepto a Enoch, arrebatado vivo a los cielos.

Previously he had remembered the others' names, but now he had quite forgotten them, chiefly because Enoch was his favourite in the whole Old Testament, and attached to Enoch's being taken up to Heaven there was a long string of thought in his head, which now occupied his mind while he looked fixedly at his father's watch-chain and at a half-unfastened button of his waistcoat.

Antes recordaba los nombres, pero ahora los había olvidado completamente, sobre todo porque de todas las figuras del Antiguo Testamento la que prefería era la de Enoch, y porque junto a la idea del rapto del profeta se mezclaba en su cerebro una larga cadena de pensamientos a los que se entregaba también ahora, mientras miraba con ojos extáticos la cadena del reloj y un botón a medio abrochar del chaleco de su padre.
He did not in the least believe in death, which was so often mentioned to him.
Sergio se negaba en redondo a creer en la muerte, de la que le hablaban tan a menudo.
He did not believe that people he loved could die, nor above all that he himself would die.
No creía que pudieran morir las personas a quienes quería, y, sobre todo, él mismo.
That seemed to him quite impossible and incomprehensible.
Le parecía imposible a incomprensible.
But he was told that everybody would die; he had even asked people whom he trusted and they all confirmed it; his nurse too said so, though reluctantly.
Pero como le decían que todos terminaban muriendo, lo preguntó a personas en quienes confiaba y todos se lo confirmaron. El aya decía también que sí, aunque de mal grado.
But Enoch had not died, so not everybody died, 'and why should not anybody deserve the same in God's sight, and be taken up to Heaven alive?' thought Serezha.
Pero Enoch no había muerto, lo que probaba que no todos mueren. «¿Por qué no puede todo el mundo hacerse agradable a Dios para ser llevado vivo a los cielos?», pensaba Sergio.
Bad people, that is to say those he did not like, might die; but the good ones might all be like Enoch.
Los malos, es decir, los que Sergio no quería, sí podían morir, pero los buenos debían ser todos como Enoch.
'Well, who were the patriarchs?'
–A ver: ¿cuáles fueron los patriarcas?
'Enoch, Enos...'
–Enoch, Enoch...
'But you have already mentioned them.
–Ya lo has dicho.
This is bad, Serezha, very bad!
Mal, muy mal, Sergio...
If you do not take pains to know what is most necessary for a Christian, then what can interest you?
Si no tratas de saber lo que más importancia tiene para un cristiano, ¿cómo puede interesarte lo demás? –dijo el padre, levantándose–.
I am displeased with you, and Peter Ignatych' – this was the chief educationalist – 'is also displeased with you...
Estoy descontento de ti y también lo está Pedro Ignatievich –se refería al sabio pedagogo–.
I shall have to punish you.'
Tendré que castigarte.
His father and the educationalist were both displeased with Serezha, and he really learnt badly.
Padre y profesor estaban, en efecto, descontentos de Sergio.
Yet it could not at all be said that he was an incapable boy.
Y, a decir verdad, el niño era bastante desaplicado.
On the contrary he was far more capable than the boys whom the educationalist set before him as models.
Pero no podía decirse que fuera un niño de pocas aptitudes.
His father from his point of view considered that the boy did not try to learn what he was being taught.
Al contrario: era más despejado que otros a los que el profesor le ponía como ejemplo.
As a matter of fact, he could not learn it.
A juicio de su padre, Sergio no quería estudiar lo que le mandaban.
He could not, because there were more urgent demands on his soul than those put forward by his father and the educationalist.
Pero en realidad no podía estudiar porque en su alma había exigencias más apremiantes que las que le imponían su padre y su profesor.
The two kinds of demands were opposed, and he was in direct conflict with his instructors.
Y como aquellas dos clases de exigencias estaban en oposición, Sergio luchaba contra sus educadores abiertamente.
He was nine years old and quite a child, but he knew his soul, it was dear to him, and he guarded it as the eyelid guards the eye, and never let anyone enter his heart without the key of love.
Tenía nueve años, era un niño, pero conocía su alma, la quería y la cuidaba como el párpado cuida del ojo y, sin la llave del afecto, no permitía a nadie penetrar en ella.
His instructors complained that he would not learn, yet his soul was overflowing with longing for knowledge.
Sus educadores se quejaban, pero él no quería estudiar y, sin embargo, su alma rebosaba de ansia de saber.
So he learnt, from Kapitonich, from his nurse, from Nadenka, and from Vasily Lukich, but not from his teachers.
Y aprendía de Kapitorich, del aya, de Nadeñka, de Basilio Lukich, mas no de sus maestros.
The water which his fathers and the educationalists expected would turn their mill-wheels had long since leaked out and was working somewhere else.
El agua con que el padre y el pedagogo trataban de mover las ruedas de su molino, ya goteaba y trabajaba por otro lado.
His father punished Serezha by not letting him go to see Lydia Ivanovna's niece Nadenka, but this punishment turned out luckily for Serezha.
El padre castigó a Sergio prohibiéndole ir a casa de la sobrina de Lidia Ivanovna, pero el castigo más que entristecerle le alegró.
Vasily Lukich was in good spirits and showed him how to make windmills.
Basilio Lukich estaba de buen humor y le enseñó a hacer molinos de viento.
He spent all the evening working, and dreaming how a windmill could be made on which one could ride, either by seizing one of the sails or by tying oneself to it and spinning round.
Pasó, pues, toda la tarde trabajando y meditando en cómo podría hacer un molino en el cual uno pudiese girar asiéndose a las aspas o atándose a ellas.

He did not think about his mother all the evening; but when in bed he suddenly remembered her, and prayed in his own words that tomorrow, on his birthday, she should stop hiding herself and should come to him.
No pensó en su madre en toda la tarde, pero una vez acostado la recordó de pronto y rogó a Dios, a su manera, para que dejara de ocultarse y le visitara al día siguiente, que era el de su cumpleaños.
'Vasily Lukich! Do you know for what I have been praying extra?'
–Basilio Lukich, ¿sabe por lo que he rezado, además de lo de todos los días?
'To learn better?'
–Por estudiar mejor.
'No.'
–No.
'For toys?'
–Por recibir juguetes.
You will never guess!
No lo adivinará.
It's lovely, but a secret!
Es una cosa magnífica... pero es un secreto.
When it comes true, I will tell you.
Cuando llegue, se lo diré...
You have not guessed.'
¿No lo adivina?
'No, I can't guess.
–No, no, no lo adivino.
You'd better tell me,' said Vasily Lukich, smiling, which he rarely did.
Dígamelo... –repuso Basilio Lukich, sonriendo, lo cual ocurría pocas veces–.
'Well, lie down, and I'll put out the candle.'
En fin, duérmase, más valdrá... Voy a apagar la vela.
'But I can see better without a candle what I have been praying for!
–Sin la vela veo mejor lo que quiero ver y por lo que he rezado.
There, I nearly told you the secret!' said Serezha with a merry laugh.
¡Por poco le descubro mi secreto! –exclamó Sergio, riendo alegremente.
When the candle had been taken away he heard and felt his mother.
Cuando se llevaron la vela, Sergio vio y sintió a su madre.
She stood above him and caressed him with a loving look.
Estaba de pie ante él y le acariciaba con su mirada amorosa.
But then windmills appeared, and a knife, and all became confused, and he fell asleep.
Luego había molinos, cortaplumas... En la mente de Sergio todo se fue confundiendo hasta que se durmió.

WHEN VRONSKY AND ANNA REACHED PETERSBURG they put up at one of the best hotels: Vronsky separately on the first floor, and Anna with the baby, the nurse, and a maid, upstairs in a large suite consisting of four rooms.

Vronsky se instaló en el piso bajo, y Ana, con la niña, la nodriza y la doncella, en un departamento de cuatro habitaciones. El mismo día de su llegada, Vronsky visitó a su hermano, y encontró allí a su madre, venida de Moscú para sus asuntos.
On the day they arrived Vronsky went to see his brother. There he met his mother, who had come from Moscow on business.
Su madre y su cuñada le recibieron como siempre, le preguntaron por su viaje al extranjero, hablaron de sus conocidos y no dijeron ni una palabra de sus relaciones con Ana.
His mother and his sister-in-law received him just as usual, asked him about his trip abroad and spoke of mutual acquaintances, but did not say a single word about his union with Anna.
Pero cuando su hermano le visitó al siguiente día, le preguntó por ella.

His brother, however, having come to see him next morning, asked about her, and Alexis Vronsky told him frankly that he regarded his union with her as a marriage, that he hoped to arrange a divorce for her, and would then marry her, and that meanwhile he considered her his wife, just like any other wife, and he asked his brother to say so to their mother and to his own wife.

Alexey Vronsky le declaró francamente que consideraba sus relaciones con Ana como un matrimonio legal y que esperaba arreglar el divorcio y casarse entonces, pero que para él Ana era ya su mujer como cualquier otra, y le rogaba que lo dijese así a su madre y a su cuñada.
'If the world does not approve of it, I don't care,' said Vronsky, 'but if my relatives wish to treat me as a relation, they must adopt a similar attitude toward my wife.'
–Si la buena sociedad no lo aprueba, me da igual –añadió Vronsky–. Pero si mi familia quiere conservar conmigo relaciones de parentesco, debe hacerlas extensivas a mi mujer.

The elder brother, who had always respected his younger brother's opinions, was not sure whether he was right or wrong, until the world had decided the point; but for his own part he had nothing against it and went up with Alexis to see Anna.

Su hermano mayor, que respetaba siempre las ideas del otro, no sabía qué decir, hasta que el mundo sancionara o no esta decisión. Pero, como él personalmente no tenía nada que oponer, entró con Alexey a ver a Ana.

In his brother's presence Vronsky spoke to Anna merely as to a close acquaintance, as he always did in the presence of a third party; but it was assumed that his brother knew of their relations, and they spoke of Anna's going to Vronsky's estate.
Vronsky la trató de usted, como a una amiga íntima. Pero quedaba sobreentendido que el hermano conocía aquellas relaciones y se habló de que Ana fuera a la finca de los Vronsky.
Despite all his experience of the world, Vronsky, in the new position in which he found himself, was making a terrible mistake.
Pese a su tacto mundano, Vronsky, en virtud de la falsa posición en que se encontraba, incurría en un extraño error.

He might have been expected to understand that Society was closed to him and Anna; but some sort of vague notion got into his head that though it used to be so in olden times, yet now, when there was so much progress (without noticing it, he had become an advocate of every kind of progress), public opinion had changed and it was possible that they would be received in Society.

Debía haber comprendido que el mundo estaba cerrado para él y para Ana. Pero actualmente nacía en su cerebro la vaga idea de que, si eso era así antiguamente, ahora, dado el rápido progreso humano (a la sazón era muy partidario de todos los progresos), el punto de vista de la sociedad había cambiado y por tanto la cuestión de si ellos serían recibidos en sociedad o no, no estaba aún decidida.
'Of course they will not receive her at Court, but intimate friends can and should see things the right way,' he thought.
«Claro que los círculos de la Corte no la recibirán», se decía, «pero los allegados deben y pueden comprendernos».

It is possible to sit for some hours with one's legs doubled up without changing one's position if one knows there is nothing to prevent one's doing so, but if a man knows that he must sit with his legs doubled up he will get cramp, and his legs will begin to jerk and strain in the direction in which he would like to stretch them.

Se puede muy bien estar sentado con las piernas encogidas y sin cambiar de posición durante varias horas sabiendo que nada impedirá cambiar de postura. Pero si se sabe que obligatoriamente se ha de permanecer sentado con las piernas encogidas, se sufren calambres y los pies tiemblan y necesitan estirarse.
This was what Vronsky experienced with regard to Society.
Lo mismo sentía Vronsky respecto al gran mundo.
Though in the depths of his soul he knew that Society was closed to them, he tried whether it would not change and whether it would not receive them.
Aunque en el fondo de su alma sabía que estaba cerrado para ellos, quería probar a ver si, con el cambio de las costumbres, los aceptaba.
But he very soon noticed that though the great world was open to him personally, it was closed to Anna.
No tardó en darse cuenta de que el mundo seguía abierto para él personalmente, pero no para Ana.
As in the game of cat and mouse, the arms that were raised to allow him to get inside the circle were at once lowered to prevent Anna from entering.
Como en el juego del gato y el ratón, los brazos que se alzaban para darle paso se bajaban al ir a pasar ella.
One of the first Petersburg Society ladies he met was his cousin Betsy.
Una de las primeras mujeres distinguidas a quienes Vronsky vio, fue a su prima Betsy.
'At last!' she exclaimed joyfully when they met.
–¡Al fin! –exclamó alegremente Betsy–.
'And Anna?
¿Y Ana?
I am so glad!
¡Cuánto me alegro de verle!
Where are you staying?
¿Dónde han estado?
I can imagine how dreadful our Petersburg must appear to you after your delightful journey; I can picture to myself your honeymoon in Rome.
Deben de encontrar muy feo San Petersburgo después de su espléndido viaje. ¡Ya me imagino su luna de miel en Roma!
And the divorce?
¿Y el divorcio?
Is it all arranged? '
¿Lo han obtenido?
He noticed that Betsy's delight cooled down when she learnt that Anna had not yet been divorced.
Vronsky notó que el entusiasmo de Betsy decaía algo cuando le contestó que aún no habían conseguido el divorcio.
'They will throw stones at me, I know,' she said, 'but I shall come and see Anna.
–Van a lapidarme –dijo Betsy–, pero, no obstante, visitaré a Ana.
Yes, I will certainly come.
Sí, iré de todos modos.
You are not staying here long?'
¿Permanecerán aquí por mucho tiempo?
And really she came to see Anna that same day; but her manner was very different from what it had formerly been.
El mismo día, en efecto, visitó a Ana. Pero su tono era totalmente distinto del de antes.
She was evidently proud of her boldness and wished Anna to appreciate the fidelity of her friendship.
Se la notaba orgullosa de su atrevimiento y quería que Ana apreciase la fidelidad de sus sentimientos amistosos.
She did not stay more than ten minutes, chattering Society gossip, and as she was leaving said:
Sólo estuvo unos diez minutos. Habló de las novedades del mundo y al marcharse dijo:
'You have not told me when you will be divorced?
–No me han dicho cuándo obtendrán el divorcio.
Of course I have kicked over the traces, but others, straight-laced people, will give you the cold shoulder until you get married.
Aunque yo me he liado la manta a la cabeza habrá algunas orgullosas que la recibirán fríamente mientras no estén casados.
And it is so simple nowadays! Ça se fait.
Y con lo sencillo que es eso ahora...
[It is a thing that is done.]
Ça se fait...
So you are leaving on Friday?
¿Así que se van el viernes?
I am sorry we shan't see one another again!'
Siento que no nos podamos ver más por ahora...
From Betsy's tone Vronsky might have realized what he had to expect from Society, but he made another attempt with his relations.
Por el acento de Betsy, Vronsky podía comprender lo que debía esperar del gran mundo, pero aun hizo una prueba más con la familia.
Of his mother he had no hopes.
No ponía mucha esperanza en su madre.
He knew that his mother, who had been so delighted with Anna when she first made her acquaintance, was now merciless toward her for having caused the ruin of her son's career.
Sabía que ésta, tan entusiasmada con Ana cuando la conoció, era ahora inflexible con ella pensando que había arruinado la carrera de su hijo.
But he placed great hopes on Varya, his brother's wife.
Pero Vronsky confiaba mucho en su cuñada Varia.
She, he thought, would cast no stones, but would simply and resolutely go and see Anna and receive her at her own house.
Parecíale que ella, incapaz de tirar la primera piedra, resolvería con toda naturalidad ver a Ana y recibirla en su casa.
The day after his arrival Vronsky called on her, and having found her alone, expressed his wish.
Al día siguiente de llegar, fue, pues, a visitarla y, hallándola sola, le expuso francamente su deseo. Varia, después de oírle, le contestó:

'You know how fond I am of you, Alexis,' she replied when she had heard him out, 'and how ready I am to do anything for you; but I have kept silent because I knew I could be of no use to you and Anna Arkadyevna.' She pronounced the formal 'Anna Arkadyevna' with peculiar precision.

–Ya sabes, Alexey, que te aprecio y estoy dispuesta a hacer por ti todo lo que sea. Pero he callado porque en nada puedo seros útil a Ana Arkadievna y a ti –pronunció «Arkadievna» con una entonación particular–.
'Please don't think I am condemning you.
No pienses, te lo ruego –prosiguió– que la censuro.
Not at all!
Eso nunca.
Perhaps in her place I should have done the same.
Quizá yo en su lugar habría hecho lo mismo.
I do not and cannot enter into details,' she added, looking timidly into his gloomy face. 'But we must call things by their real names.
No puedo entrar en detalles –continuó con timidez mirando el rostro grave de Vronsky–; pero las cosas hay que llamarlas por su nombre.
You wish me to go and see her and to receive her, and so rehabilitate her in Society; but please understand that I cannot do it!
Tú quieres que yo vaya a su casa, que lá reciba y que con eso la rehabilite ante el mundo. Pero, compréndelo, esto «no puedo hacerlo».
I have daughters growing up, and I must move in Society, for my husband's sake.
Tengo hijos, debo vivir en sociedad por mi marido.
Suppose I go to see Anna Arkadyevna; she will understand that I cannot ask her to my house, or must do it in such a way that she does not meet those who see things differently. That would offend her.
Si visito a Ana Arkadievna ella comprenderá que no puedo invitarla a casa o que debo hacerlo de manera que no se encuentre aquí con nadie, y eso la ofenderá también No puedo levantarla de...

'But I don't consider that she has fallen lower than hundreds of people whom you do receive!' said Vronsky still more gloomily, and rose in silence, having understood that his sister-in-law's determination was final.
–No creo que Ana haya caído más bajo que cientos de mujeres que vosotros recibís –interrumpió Vronsky con mayor gravedad. Y se levantó, adivinando que la decisión de su cuñada era irrevocable.
'Alexis, don't be angry with me!
–Te ruego, Alexey, que no te enfades conmigo.
Please understand that it is not my fault,' said Varya, looking at him with a timid smile.
Comprende que no tengo la culpa... Y Varia le miraba con tímida sonrisa.
'I am not angry with you,' he said just as gloomily, 'but I am doubly pained. I am pained too because this breaks our friendship.
–No me enfado contigo –repuso él, siempre serio–, pero esto en ti me es doblemente penoso y lo siento porque rompe nuestra amistad.
No, not breaks it, but weakens it. You understand that for me too there can be no other course'.'
Ya comprenderás que para mí no puede ser de otro modo.
With those words he left her.
Y con esto, Vronsky la dejó.

Vronsky understood that it was vain to make any further attempts and that they would have to spend those few days in Petersburg as in a strange town, avoiding contact with their former world in order not to lay themselves open to unpleasantnesses and insults which were so painful to him.

Reconoció, pues, que sus esfuerzos eran vanos y que debía pasar aquellos días en San Petersburgo como en una ciudad desconocida, evitando su relación con el mundo de antes, para no sufrir escenas desagradables y no soportar dolorosas ofensas.
One of the most disagreeable features of his position in Petersburg was that Karenin seemed to be everywhere and his name in every mouth.
Una de las cosas principalmente ingratas en su situación era que su nombre y el de Karenin se oían en todas partes.

It was impossible to start any conversation without its turning upon Karenin, impossible to go anywhere without meeting him. So at least it seemed to Vronsky, as a man with a sore finger feels that he is continually knocking that finger against everything as if on purpose.
Imposible hablar de nada sin que el nombre de Alexey Alejandrovich surgiera en la conversación, imposible ir a parte alguna sin riesgo de encontrarle.
The stay in Petersburg seemed to him still more trying because he noticed all the time in Anna a new and to him incomprehensible mood.
Así, al menos, le parecía a Vronsky, de la misma manera que a un enfermo a quien le duele el dedo se le antoja que todos los golpes van a parar a él.
At one moment she appeared to be in love with him, and at the next would turn cold, irritable, and impenetrable.
A Vronsky la existencia en San Petersburgo le fue todavía más penosa, porque durante todo aquel tiempo advirtió en Ana una actitud incomprensible para él.

Something tormented her and she hid it from him, appearing not to notice the insults that were poisoning his life, and which should have been still more painful to her with her acuteness of perception.

Algo la atormentaba, sin duda, y algo le ocultaba. No mostraba reparar en las afrentas que emponzoñaban la vida de él y que, dada su aguda sensibilidad, debían forzosamente de haberle sido también a ella muy dolorosas.
ONE OF ANNA'S REASONS FOR RETURNING TO RUSSIA was to see her son.
Uno de los fines principales del viaje a Rusia, era, para Ana, ver a su hijo.
From the day she left Italy the thought of that meeting did not cease to agitate her. The nearer they came to Petersburg the greater its joy and importance appeared.

Desde que salió de Italia, la idea de verle no dejó un momento de conmoverla, y, cuanto más se acercaba a San Petersburgo, mayor le parecía el encanto y la transcendencia de aquel encuentro con el niño.
She did not ask herself how she should contrive it. It seemed to her natural and simple that she should see her son when she was in the same town with him.

Figurábasele sencillo y natural ver a su hijo hallándose en la misma ciudad que él; pero, una vez en San Petersburgo, se hizo evidente su situación ante la sociedad y comprendió que no sería nada fácil arreglar aquella entrevista.
But on reaching Petersburg her present social position presented itself clearly to her, and she realized that it would be difficult to arrange the meeting.
Llevaba ya dos días en la ciudad, y aunque la idea de verle no la dejaba un momento, no había adelantado ni un solo paso en aquel camino.
The thought of her son did not leave her for an instant, but she had not yet seen him. She felt she had not the right to go straight to the house where she might encounter Karenin.
Ana reconocía que no tenía derecho a ir abiertamente a casa de Karenin, a riesgo de encontrarle, y que podía muy bien suceder que le prohibieran la entrada, cosa que la habría llenado de vergüenza.
Possibly they might even not admit her. It was painful to her even to think of writing to and coming into contact with her husband: she could be calm only when she did not think of him.
Sólo el pensar en escribir a su marido y cruzar cartas con él, le suponía ya un tormento. únicamente cuando no se acordaba de su marido podía estar tranquila.

To meet her son when he was out for a walk, after finding out when and where he went, was not enough: she had been preparing herself so for that meeting, had so much to say to him, and so much wanted to embrace and kiss him!
Ver a su hijo en el paseo, enterándose de a dónde y cuándo salía el niño, no le bastaba.
Serezha's old nurse might have helped and advised her, but she was no longer in Karenin's household. In this uncertainty, and in searching for the old nurse, two days had gone by.
¡Se preparaba tanto para esa entrevista, tenía tantas cosas que decirle, deseaba tan ardientemente besarle y poderle estrechar entre sus brazos!

Having heard about Karenin's intimate friendship with the Countess Lydia Ivanovna, Anna on the third day resolved to write her a letter, which cost her much effort, and in which she intentionally mentioned that permission to see her son must depend on her husband's magnanimity.
Estas dudas y en la búsqueda del aya, pasaron dos días. Al informarse de las relaciones que unían ahora a Karenin y a Lidia Ivanovna, Ana decidió al tercer día escribir a la Condesa.
She knew that if that letter were shown to him he, continuing his magnanimous role, would not refuse her request.

Aquella carta, que le costó tanto trabajo, y en la que mencionaba intencionadamente la grandeza de alma de su marido, estaba escrita con la esperanza de que la viese él y, continuando en su papel magnánimo, le concediera lo que pedía.
The commissionaire who delivered her letter brought back the most cruel and unexpected reply: that there would be no answer!
El enviado que llevara la carta trajo una respuesta cruel e inesperada: que no había contestación.
Never had she felt so humiliated as when, having called in the commissionaire, she heard from him the full account of how he had waited and had then been told that there would be no answer.
Jamás se sintió tan humillada como en aquel momento en que, llamando al enviado, le oyó detallar cómo le habían hecho esperar y cómo luego le dijeron que no había respuesta.
Anna felt herself humiliated and wounded, but she saw that the Countess Lydia Ivanovna was right from her own point of view.
Ana se sintió humillada y ofendida, pero reconocía que, desde su punto de vista, la condesa Lidia Ivanovna tenía razón.
Her grief was the more poignant because she had to bear it alone.
Su dolor era tanto más hondo, cuanto que había de soportarlo ella sola.
She could not share it with Vronsky and did not wish to.
No podía ni quería compartirlo con Vronsky.
She knew that, though he was the chief cause of her misery, the question of her seeing her son would seem to him quite unimportant.
Sabía que, aunque era él la causa principal de su desventura, la entrevista con su hijo había de parecerle una cosa sin importancia.

She knew he would never be able to appreciate the depth of her anguish, and that his coldness if the matter were mentioned would make her hate him. And she feared that, more than anything else in the world, and therefore hid from him everything concerning her son.

A su juicio, Vronsky no podría comprender nunca toda la intensidad de su sufrimiento, y temía, como nunca había temido, experimentar hacia él un sentimiento hostil al notar el tono frío en que habría, sin duda, de hablarle de aquello.
Having spent all that day at the hotel considering how she might see her son, she resolved to write to her husband.
Ana pasó en casa todo el día, meditando medios para conseguir su propósito, hasta que, al fin, decidió escribir una carta a su marido.
She had already composed the letter when she received Lydia Ivanovna's reply.
Ya la tenía redactada cuando le llevaron la de Lidia Ivanovna.

The Countess's silence had made her feel humble, but the letter and what she read between its lines so irritated her, its malevolence seemed so revolting when compared with her passionate and legitimate love for her son, that she became indignant with others and ceased to blame herself.

El silencio de la Condesa la había hecho conformarse, pero su carta y lo que pudo leer en ella entre líneas la irritaron tanto, le pareció tan excesiva aquella maldad ante su natural cariño a su hijo, que se indignó contra los demás y dejó de inculparse a sí misma.
'That coldness, that pretence of feeling!' she said to herself.
«¡Qué frialdad! ¡Qué fingimiento!», se decía.
'They want to wound me and torture the child, and shall I submit to them?
«Quieren ofenderme y hacer sufrir al niño. ¿Y he de obedecerles?
Not on any account!
¡Jamás!
She is worse than I. Anyhow, I don't lie!'
Ella es peor que yo, que, al menos, no miento.»

And there and then she resolved that next day, Serezha's birthday, she would go straight to her husband's house and would bribe the servants or deceive them, but would at any cost see her son and destroy that monstrous falsehood with which they surrounded the unfortunate child.

Y decidió en seguida que al día siguiente, cumpleaños de Sergio, iría a casa de su marido, sobornaría a los criados, los engañaría; pero vería a su hijo, costara lo que costara, y destruiría el terrible engaño de que rodeaban a la desgraciada criatura. Fue a un almacén de juguetes, compró un sinfín de cosas y estudió un plan.
She drove to a toy shop, purchased a lot of toys, and devised a plan of action. She would go early in the morning, at about eight, when Karenin would certainly not be up.
Temprano, a cosa de las ocho de la mañana, antes de que Alexey Alejandrovich se hubiera levantado, acudiría a la casa.

She would have ready in her hand some money to give to the hall-porter and the footman, in order that they should let her in. Without raising her veil she would say she had been sent by Serezha's godfather to wish him many happy returns of the day and that she was to put the toys by his bedside.

Llevaría en la mano dinero para el portero y el lacayo, a fin de que ellos la dejasen entrar y, sin levantarse el velo, les diría que iba de parte del padrino de Sergio para felicitarle y que le habían encargado que pusiera los juguetes por sí misma junto a la cama del niño.
The only thing she did not prepare was what she would say to her son. Much as she thought about that she could not prepare the words.
Lo único que no preparó fue las palabras que diría a su hijo, pues por más que lo había meditado no se le ocurrió lo que le había de decir.
Next morning Anna went alone, and at eight o'clock got out of the hired carriage and rang the bell at the front door of the house which used to be her home.
Al día siguiente, a las ocho de la mañana, Ana, apeándose de un coche de alquiler, llamó a la puerta principal de la casa que un día fuera suya.
'Go and see what it is.
–Vaya a ver quién es.
It's some lady,' said Kapitonich, who was not yet dressed, and in overcoat and goloshes peeped from the window at the veiled lady standing close to the door.
Parece una señora –dijo Kapitonich aún a medio vestir, con abrigo y chanclos, mirando por la ventana a la mujer que había junto a la puerta.
His assistant, a lad whom Anna did not know, had hardly opened the door when she entered, and taking a three-rouble note from her muff hastily thrust it into his hand.
El ayudante del portero era un hombre desconocido para Ana. Apenas abrió la puerta, ella entró, sacó rápidamente del manguito un billete de tres rublos y se lo deslizó en la mano.
'Serezha...
–Sergio, Sergio Alejandrovich –dijo Ana.
Sergey Alexeyich!' she said, and walked on.
Y continuó rápida su camino.
After examining the note the porter's assistant stopped her at the inner glass door.
El criado, una vez examinado el dinero, la detuvo en la puerta siguiente.
'Whom do you want?' he asked.
–¿A quién desea ver? ––dijo.
Noticing the stranger's confusion, Kapitonich himself came out, admitted her, and inquired what she wanted.
Notando la turbación de la desconocida, salió Kapitonich en persona al encuentro de la desconocida, la hizo pasar y le preguntó qué quería.
'I come from Prince Skorodumov to see Sergey Alexeyich,' said she.
–Vengo de parte del príncipe Skeradumov a ver a Sergio Alejandrovich.
'He is not up yet,' said the hall-porter, carefully scrutinizing her face.
–El señorito no está levantado aún –repuso el portero mirándola con atención.
Anna had not foreseen at all that the totally unaltered appearance of the hall of the house where she had lived for nine years would so deeply affect her.
Ana no esperaba que el aspecto invariable de la casa donde había vivido nueve años pudiera causarle tan vivo efecto.
One memory after another, both joyful and painful, rose in her mind, and for a moment she forgot why she had come.
Recuerdos alegres y penosos se elevaron uno tras otro en su alma, haciéndole olvidar por un momento el objeto de su visita.
'Would you like to wait?' said Kapitonich, helping her off with her cloak.
–¿Desea esperar? –preguntó Kapitonich, ayudándole a quitarse el abrigo de pieles.
Having done so he glanced again at her face and, recognizing her, silently bowed low.
Al hacerlo, la miró al rostro, la reconoció y, sin decirle nada, la saludó con respeto.
'Come in, Your Excellency,' he said.
–Haga el favor de entrar, Excelencia –dijo después.
She wished to speak, but her voice refused to utter a sound; with a look of guilty entreaty at the old man she went with light steps up the stairs.
Ana quiso hablarle, pero la voz se le ahogó en la garganta. Y, mirando al viejo con aire culpable, subió la escalera con pasos leves y rápidos.
Bending forward and catching the steps with his goloshes, Kapitonich ran after her, trying to overtake her.
Kapitonich, inclinándose hacia delante y tropezando con los chanclos en los escalones, la seguía corriendo, tratando de alcanzarla.
'The tutor may be there and not yet dressed.
–Está allí el preceptor. Quizá no se haya vestido.
I will announce you.'
Iré a anunciarla.
Anna continued to ascend the familiar steps without understanding what the old man was saying.
Ana seguía subiendo la escalera tan conocida sin entender lo que le decía el anciano.
'This way, please! To the left!
–Aquí, a la izquierda, haga el favor.
Please excuse its not being quite clean.
Perdone que no esté limpio aún...
He has been moved to the old sitting-room now,' said the hall-porter, panting. 'Allow me!
El señorito duerme ahora en el cuarto del diván –murmuró el portero, esforzándose en recobrar la respiración–.
Please wait a little, Your Excellency.
Perdone, Excelencia, pero conviene esperar un poco.
I'll just look in,' he said, having overtaken her. He opened a big door and vanished behind it.
Iré a mirar.. Y, adelantándose a Ana, abrió a medias una alta puerta y desapareció tras ella.
Anna paused and waited.
Ana esperó.
'He's only just woke up,' said the porter when he came out again.
El portero salió de nuevo. –El señorito acaba de despertar ––dijo.
Just as he spoke Anna heard the sounds of a child yawning; she recognized her son by the sound of the yawn and pictured him vividly before her.
En el mismo momento en que el anciano portero pronunciaba estas palabras, Ana oyó un bostezo infantil. En aquel sonido reconoció a su hijo y le pareció ya verle ante ella.
'Let me in, let me in!' she cried, and entered at the big door.
–¡Déjeme! ¡Déjeme, y váyase! –pronunció Ana, cruzando la alta puerta.
To the right of the door stood a bed on which sat the boy, his nightshirt unbuttoned, bending his little body backward, stretching himself and finishing his yawn.
A la derecha de la entrada había una cama y en ella estaba sentado el niño que, vestido sólo con una camisita, terminaba de desperezarse, inclinando el cuerpo.
At the moment when his lips were closing they extended into a blissful sleepy smile, and with that smile he again fell slowly and sweetly backwards.
En el momento en que sus labios se juntaron de nuevo, se dibujó en ellos una sonrisa feliz, y con aquella sonrisa el niño se dejó caer otra vez en el lecho, vencido por un suave sueño.
'Serezha!' she whispered, drawing nearer with inaudible steps.
–¡Sergio! –llamó Ana, acercándose con paso cauteloso.

During the time they had been parted and under the influence of that gush of love which she had felt for him of late she had always imagined him as a little fellow of four, the age when she had loved him best.
Durante su separación, y más aún en aquellos días en que la inundaba tan viva ternura por su hijo, Ana le imaginaba como un niño de cuatro años, ya que fue a aquella edad cuando más le había querido.
Now he was not even as she had left him; he was still further removed from the four-year-old child; he had grown still more and had got thinner. What did it mean?
Pero ahora no, estaba tal como le dejó. Su aspecto difería mucho del de un niño de cuatro años; había crecido y adelgazado.
How thin his face was! How short his hair!
¡Oh, qué delgado tenía el rostro, qué cortos los cabellos y qué largos los brazos!
How long his arms! How changed since she had left him!
¡Cuán diferente era de cuando ella le había dejado!
But still it was he: the slope of the head was his, the lips were his, the soft neck and the broad shoulders.
Pero era él, con su misma forma de cabeza, con sus labios, con su suave cuello y sus anchos hombros.
'Serezha!' she repeated, just above the child's ear.
–¡Sergio! –repitió al oído mismo del niño.
He raised himself again on his elbow, moved his tousled head from side to side as if seeking for something, and opened his eyes.
Sergio se incorporó sobre un codo, movió la cabeza a ambos lados como buscando algo y abrió los ojos.

Silently and questioningly he gazed for a few moments at his mother, who stood motionless before him, then suddenly smiling blissfully, he closed his heavy eyelids and fell once more, not backward, but forwards into her arms.

Por algunos segundos miró silencioso a interrogativo a su madre, inmóvil ante él. De pronto, rió lleno de dicha y, cerrando de nuevo sus ojos cargados de sueño, se dejó caer otra vez, pero no hacia atrás, sino en los brazos de su madre.
'Serezha, my dear little boy!' she uttered, catching her breath and embracing his plump little body.
–¡Sergio, querido niño mío! –exclamó Ana, sofocada, abrazando el amado cuerpecito.
'Mama!' he muttered, wriggling about in her arms so as to touch them with different parts of his body.
–¡Mamá! –contestó el niño, moviéndose en todas direcciones para que su cuerpo rozara por todas partes los brazos de su madre.

Sleepily smiling with closed eyes, he moved his plump hands from the back of his bed to her shoulders, leaning against her and enveloping her in that sweet scent of sleepiness and warmth which only children possess, and began rubbing himself against her neck and shoulder.

Sonriendo medio dormido, siempre con los ojos cerrados, y apoyándose con sus manos gordezuelas en la cabecera de la cama, se asió a los hombros de su madre y se dejó caer sobre su regazo, exhalando ese agradable olor que sólo tienen los niños en el lecho. En seguida empezó a frotarse el rostro contra el cuello y los hombros de su madre.
'I knew!' he said, opening his eyes.
–Ya sabía ––dijo, abriendo los ojos–, que habías de venir.
'To-day is my birthday.
Hoy es el día de mi cumpleaños...
I knew you would come! I'll get up directly...'
Me he despertado ahora mismo y voy a levantarme...
While saying this he was again falling asleep.
Y, mientras hablaba, se quedó de nuevo dormido.
Anna watched him with greedy eyes. She noticed how he had grown and changed during her absence.
Ana le miraba con afán, viendo cuánto había crecido y cambiado en su ausencia.

She recognized and yet did not quite recognize his bare legs, now so big; which he had freed from the blanket, and his cheeks, now grown thinner, and the short locks of hair at the back of his head where she had so often kissed him.
Reconocía y desconocía a la vez sus piernas desnudas, ahora tan largas, sus mejillas enflaquecidas, los cortos rizos de su nuca, que tantas veces había besado.
She touched it all, and could not speak: tears were choking her.
Estrechaba todo aquello contra su corazón y no podía hablar, ahogada por las lágrimas.
'What are you crying about, Mama?' he asked, now quite awake. 'Mama, what are you crying about?' he exclaimed in a fretful voice.
–¿Por qué lloras, mamá? –preguntó el niño, despertando por completo, ¿Por qué lloras, mamá? –gritó con voz quejumbrosa.
'I won't cry...
–No lloraré más.
I am crying for joy!
Lloro de alegría.
It is so long since I saw you.
¡Hace tanto que no te he visto!
I won't,' she said, swallowing her tears and turning away.
No, no lloraré más, no lloraré... –dijo, devorando sus lágrimas y volviendo la cabeza–.
'But it's time for you to get dressed,' she said after a pause when she had recovered; and without releasing his hands she sat down by his bed on a chair on which his clothes were lying ready.

Ea, ya es hora de vestirte –añadió, recobrando algo de su serenidad, después de un silencio. Y, sin soltar sus manos, se sentó al lado de la cama en una silla, sobre la que estaba la ropa del pequeño.
'How do you dress without me?
–¿Cómo te vistes sin mí?
How do you...' She tried to speak simply and cheerfully, but could not, and turned away again.
¿Cómo ...? –dijo, tratando de expresarse con voz natural y alegre. Pero no pudo terminar y volvió una vez más la cara.
'I don't wash with cold water.
–No me lavo ya con agua fría; papá no me deja.
Papa says I mustn't.
¿Has visto a Basilio Lukich?
You have not seen Vasily Lukich?
Vendrá ahora... ¡Ah, te has sentado sobre mi vestido!
He will come presently.
Sergio rió a carcajadas.
And you are sitting on my clothes!'
Ana le miró, sonriendo.
And Serezha burst out laughing. She looked at him and smiled.
–¡Mamá, querida mamá! –gritó el chiquillo, lanzándose de nuevo a ella y abrazándola.
'Mama! Dearest, darling!' he shouted, again throwing himself upon her, and embracing her, as if he by now, having seen her smile, clearly realized what had happened.
Parecía que sólo ahora, al ver su sonrisa, comprendió lo que pasaba. –Esto no te hace falta –siguió el niño quitándole el sombrero.
'You don't want that,' he said, taking off her bonnet and on seeing her without it, he began kissing her again as though he had only just seen her.
Y cuando Ana estuvo sin él, Sergio como si en aquel momento la viese por primera vez, se precipitó a ella para besarla.
'Well, and what did you think about me?
–¿Qué pensabas de mí?
You did not think I was dead?'
¿Creías que había muerto?
'I never believed it!'
–No lo creí nunca.
'You didn't believe it, my darling?'
–¿No lo creíste, hijito mío?
'I knew! I knew!' he cried, repeating his favourite phrase, and seizing her hand, which was caressing his hair, he pressed her palm to his mouth, covering it with kisses.
–¡Sabía que no, sabía que no! –respondió el niño empleando su frase predilecta. Y cogiendo la mano de su madre, que acariciaba sus cabellos, la oprimió contra sus labios y la besó.

MEANWHILE VASILY LUKICH, who had not at first understood who the lady was, having realized from what he heard that she was the mother who had left her husband and whom he, having come to the house only after she had left it, had never seen, hesitated whether to go in or not, or whether to tell Karenin.

Entre tanto, Basilio Lukich que, al principio no había comprendido quién era aquella señora, suponiendo por la conversación que aquella era la esposa que había abandonado a su marido, y a la que no conocía, por no estar ya en la casa cuando él llegara allí, dudaba si debía entrar o no y si procedía avisar a Karenin.

Having at last concluded that his duty was to get Serezha up at the appointed time, and that therefore he need not consider who was sitting there – the boy's mother or anyone else – but that he must do his duty, he dressed, went up to the door, and opened it.

Pensando, al fin, que su deber era despertar diariamente a Sergio a una hora fija y que para hacerlo no debía preocuparse de quien estuviese allí, fuera su madre o cualquier otra persona, ya que a él sólo le incumbía cumplir su obligación, Basilio Lukich vistióse, se acercó a la puerta y la abrió.
But the caresses of the mother and son, the sound of their voices and what they were saying, made him change his mind.
Pero las caricias de madre a hijo, el tono de su voz y lo que se decían, le forzó a cambiar de decisión.
He shook his head, sighed, and closed the door again.
Movió la cabeza y cerró la puerta, con un suspiro.
'I will be another ten minutes,' he said to himself, coughing and wiping away his tears.
«Esperaré diez minutos más», se dijo, tosiendo y secándose las lágrimas.

They all knew that the mistress had come, that Kapitonich had admitted her, and that she was now in the nursery. But the master always went to the nursery before nine, and they all understood that a meeting between him and his wife was inconceivable and must be prevented.

Entre los criados, mientras tanto, reinaba gran agitación Todos sabían que había llegado la señora, que Kapitonich la había dejado entrar, que ahora estaba en el cuarto del niño, y que el señor entraba a verle todos los días a cosa de las nueve...
Korney, the valet, went down into the hall-porter's room to inquire who had let her in, and hearing that it was Kapitonich who had done so, he reprimanded the old man.
Todos comprendían que el encuentro de los esposos era una cosa imposible, y que debían hacer cuanto estuviese en sus manos para impedirlo.
The hall-porter remained obstinately silent; but when the valet said he 'ought to get the sack,' Kapitonich rushed at Korney and, flourishing his hands about before Korney's face, began to speak out:
Korney, el ayuda de cámara, bajó a la portería para saber quién había dejado pasar a Ana, y al saber que era Kapitonich dirigió al viejo una severa represión.
'Yes, I daresay you would not have let her in! I've been in service here ten years, and have had nothing but kindness: you had better go up and tell her, "You be off, please!"

El portero callaba obstinadamente, pero cuando Korney dijo que merecía que le despidiesen, Kapitonich se acercó al criado y, agitando las manos ante su rostro, le dijo: –¿Acaso tú no la habrías dejado entrar? He servido diez años aquí y sólo he visto en ella bondad.
You're an artful one, you are!
¡Me habría gustado verte a ti decirle que hiciera el favor de marcharse!
You'd better look after yourself and how to fleece the master of fur coats!'
¡Claro, que tú sabes nadar en todas las aguas! Más valdría que pensaras en lo que robas al señor y en los abrigos de castor que le quitas...
'Soldier!' said Korney, contemptuously, and turned to the nurse who had just entered. 'Now, judge for yourself, Mary Efimovna,' he said to her.
–¡Soldado! ––exclamó Korney con desprecio, y se volvió hacia el aya, que entraba en aquel instante. –¿Sabe María Efinovna que la ha dejado entrar sin decir nada a nadie?
'He's let her in without telling anybody; and Alexis Alexandrovich will be ready in a minute and will go to the nursery.'
Y Alexey Alejandrovich va a salir ahora mismo e irá al cuarto del chico...
Dear! What a business!' said the nurse.
–¡Qué cosas, qué cosas! –exclamaba el aya–.
'You must detain him somehow, Korney Vasilich – the master, I mean! And I'll run and get her out of the way.
Podía usted entretener un rato al señor, Korney Vasilievich, mientras yo subo corriendo para hacerla salir..
What a business!'
¡Qué cosas, Dios mío, qué cosas!
When the nurse entered, Serezha was just telling his mother how he and Nadenka fell down together when ice-hilling, and turned three somersaults.
Cuando el aya penetró en el cuarto de Sergio, éste contaba a su madre que él y Nadeñka se habían caído en la montaña rusa y dieron tres volteretas.
She was listening to the sound of his voice, saw his face and the play of his features, felt his hands, but did not understand what he was saying.
Ana escuchaba el sonido de su voz, veía su rostro y el juego de su expresión, sentía su mano, pero no entendía lo que le hablaba.
She must go away, must leave him – that was all she thought and felt.
Tenía que marchar y dejarle. No pensaba ni comprendía otra cosa.
She heard Vasily Lukich's step as he came to the door and coughed, and then the steps of the nurse as she entered; but she sat as if turned to stone, powerless to speak or rise.
Oía los pasos de Basilio Lukich, que se acercaba a la puerta tosiendo, oía los del aya, que llegaba ya, pero continuaba sentada, como convertida en piedra, sin fuerzas para hablar ni para levantarse.
'Madam, dear!' the nurse began, coming up to Anna and kissing her hands and shoulders.
–¡Oh, mi señora! –––dijo el aya, acercándose, y besando sus manos y hombros–.
'What joy God has sent our little one on his birthday!
¡Qué alegría ha dado Dios a nuestro niño el día de su cumpleaños!
And you have not changed at all.'
No ha cambiado usted nada, nada...
'Oh, nurse dear, I did not know you were in the house,' said Anna, rousing herself for a moment.
–No sabía que usted vivía ahora en casa, aya querida ––dijo Ana, serenándose por un momento.
'I don't live here, I live with my daughter, and have only come to wish him many happy returns, Anna Arkadyevna, dear!'
–No vivo aquí, vivo con mi hija. He venido para felicitar a Sergio, mi querida señora Ana Arkadievna.
Suddenly the nurse burst into tears and again began to kiss Anna's hand.
De pronto, rompió a llorar y volvió a besar las manos de Ana.
Serezha, with bright eyes and beaming smile, holding his mother with one hand and his nurse with the other, jumped with his plump bare feet on to the carpet.
Sergio, con ojos y sonrisa radiantes, asiéndose con una mano a su madre y con la otra al aya, pisoteaba el tapiz con sus piernas llenas y descalzas.
The tenderness of his beloved nurse for his mother sent him into raptures.
El efecto conmovedor con que su querida aya trataba a su madre, le colmaba de júbilo.

'Mama! She often comes to see me, and when she comes...' he began, but stopped, noticing that his nurse was whispering something in his mother's ear and that a look of fear and of something like shame, that did not at all suit her face, appeared there.

–Mamá: el aya viene mucho a verme y cuando viene... ––empezó a contar el niño. Pero se detuvo al observar que el aya hablaba en voz baja a Ana, en cuyo rostro se dibujó el terror y algo parecido a la vergüenza, lo cual le sentaba muy mal.
She came up to him and said, 'My darling!'
–Queridito mío... –murmuro.

She could not say good-bye, but the expression of her face said it and he understood. 'Darling, darling Kutik!' she said, calling him by the pet name she used when he was quite little, 'you won't forget me?
No dijo «adiós», pero el niño lo leyó en la expresión de su rostro, –¡Oh querido, queridísimo Kutik! ––continuó Ana, dando al niño el nombre con que le llamaba de pequeño–. ¿No me olvidarás?
You...' but she could say no more.
Tú... No pudo hablar más.
How many things she thought of later that she might have said!
¡Cuántas palabras pensó después que podía haberle dicho en este momento!
But now she did not know what to say and could not speak.
Pero ahora no sabía ni podía decirle nada.
But Serezha understood all she wanted to tell him. He understood that she was unhappy and that she loved him.
Y, sin embargo, Sergio comprendió cuanto ella hubiera querido decirle.

He had even understood what the nurse had said in a whisper. He had caught the words 'always before nine o'clock,' and he understood that they referred to his father and that his mother and father must not meet.

Comprendió que era desgraciada y que le quería, y hasta comprendió que el aya decía en voz baja a su madre: –Siempre viene hacia las nueve... Y adivinó que hablaban de su padre y que ella y él no debían verse.
This he had grasped, but he could not make out why that look of fear and shame appeared on her face...
Todo esto lo comprendía, mas no comprendía el motivo, ni por qué se dibujaba el terror en el semblante de su madre.
She could not have done wrong, and yet seemed afraid and ashamed of something.
Sin duds ella no era culpable de nada, pero temía a su marido y se avergonzaba de algo.
He wanted to ask a question which would clear up his doubts, but dared not; he saw that she suffered and he was sorry for her.
Habría deseado hacer una pregunta que le aclarase aquellas dudas, pero no se atrevía a hacerla porque veía que su madre sufría, y sentía piedad de ella.
He pressed against her in silence, and then whispered:
Apretándose contra su cuerpo, murmuró en voz baja.
'Don't go – he is not coming yet!'
–No te vayas todavía.

His mother moved him away from her, to see whether he really believed what he was saying; and in the frightened look on his face she saw not only that he was speaking about his father, but that he was, as it were, asking her what he ought to think of him.

El tardará algo en venir.. La madre le apartó un poco para ver si el niño se daba cuenta de lo que decía, y en su rostro asustado leyó que el niño no sólo hablaba de su padre, sino que hasta parecía preguntar qué debía pensar de él.
'Serezha, my darling!' she said, 'love him!
–Sergio, querido hijito, ama mucho a tu padre.
He is better and kinder than I, and I am to blame toward him.
Es mejor y más bueno que yo. Yo me he portado mal con él.
When you are grown up you will be able to judge.'
Cuando seas mayor lo comprenderás.
'There is nobody better than you!...' he cried out in desperation through his tears, and seizing her by her shoulders he hugged her with all his might, his arms trembling with the effort.
–¡No hay nadie más bueno que tú! –gritó el niño con desesperación a través de sus lágrimas. Y cogiéndola por los hombros, la apretó con toda su fuerza con sus brazos temblorosos y tensos.
'Darling little one!' said Anna, and began to cry in the same weak and childlike way as he.
–¡Mi pequeño, n–ú querido Sergio! –dijo Ana. Y se puso a llorar débilmente, como un niño, como lloraba él.
At that moment the door opened and Vasily Lukich entered.
En aquel instante se abrió la puerta y apareció Basilio Lukich.
Steps were heard approaching the other door, and the nurse said in a frightened whisper, 'Coming!...' and handed Anna her bonnet.
Próximos a otra puerta sonaron pasos. El aya dijo en voz baja: –Ya viene.
Serezha sank down on his bed and began to sob, hiding his face in his hands.
Y entregó el sombrero a Ana. Sergio se deslizó en la cama y rompió a llorar, cubriéndose el rostro con las manos.
Anna moved the hands away, kissed him again on his wet face, and went rapidly out.
Ana separó aquellas manos, besó una vez más el rostro húmedo de lágrimas y con rápido paso salió de la alcoba.
Karenin was advancing toward her.
Alexey Alejandrovich avanzaba en dirección opuesta.
When he saw her, he stopped and bowed his head.
Al verla, se detuvo a inclinó la cabeza.

Despite what she had just said, – that he was better and kinder than she was – after casting at him a rapid glance which took in his whole figure to the minutest detail, she was seized by a feeling of loathing and anger toward him and of jealousy for her son.

Aunque sólo un momento antes Ana afirmaba que él era mejor y más bueno que ella, en la mirada rápida que le dirigió, al distinguir su figura en todos sus detalles, la invadieron los habituales sentimientos de aversión, de odio y de envidia de que le hubiera quitado a su hijo.
She swiftly let down her veil and with quickened steps almost ran out of the room.
Con rápido ademán se bajó el velo y salió de allí casi a la carrera.
She had not had time even to unwrap the toys she had chosen with so much love and sadness the day before, and she took them back with her.
No había tenido tiempo de desenvolver los paquetes que con tanta ternura y tristeza comprara el día anterior en la tienda para su hijo y se los llevó consigo en el mismo estado.
GREATLY AS ANNA HAD DESIRED TO SEE HER SON, and long as she had thought of and prepared herself for the interview, she had not at all expected that it would affect her so powerfully.
A pesar de su inmenso deseo de ver a su hijo, a pesar del mucho tiempo que hacía que meditaba y preparaba la entrevista, Ana no esperaba que hubiese de impresionarla tan profundamente.
On returning to her lonely suite in the hotel she could not for a long time understand why she was there.
De vuelta a su solitario cuarto del hotel, no pudo comprender durante largo rato por qué estaba allí.
'Yes, it is all ended and I am alone again,' she said to herself; and without taking off her bonnet she sat down in an easy-chair by the fireplace.
«Todo aquello ha terminado y vuelvo a estar sola», se dijo al fin. Y, sin quitarse el sombrero, se dejó caer en una butaca próxima a la chimenea.
With her eyes fixed on a bronze clock, standing on a table between the windows, she began pondering.
Fijó la mirada en el reloj de bronce próximo a la ventana y comenzó a reflexionar.
The French maid, whom she had brought from abroad, came and asked whether she would not dress.
La doncella francesa que trajera del extranjero entró para saber si debía vestirla.
She looked at her in astonishment and replied, 'Later.'
Ana la miró sorprendida y dijo: –Luego.
A waiter offered her coffee. 'Later,' she said.
El criado llevó el café. –Luego –volvió a decir.
The Italian nurse, having smartened up the baby girl, came in and held her out to Anna.
La nodriza italiana, que acababa de vestir a la niña, entró y se la presentó a Ana.

The plump, well-nourished baby, as usual when she saw her mother, turned her little hands – so fat that they looked as if the wrists had threads tied tightly round them – palms downward and, smiling with her toothless mouth, began waving them as a fish moves its fins, making the starched folds of her embroidered frock rustle.
